Benchmark/challenge organisers — stratify or exclude follow-up exams in evaluation sets. Regulators, notified bodies and reviewers applying CLAIM/STARD-AI-style checklists — add a concrete question about report-derived reference standards on follow-up exams. Radiology QA/peer-learning (RADPEER-style) — a per-class carry-forward rate is directly usable as a metric and as the missing effect size for the "read without the prior first" intervention. Model developers — training targets and prior-conditioned inputs. (Leaderboard re-scoring is the least credible limb: see attack 6.)
Significance — fecundity: Is carry-forward a reader-, site- or template-level property (worklist pressure, shift time)? Does it predict care inheritance (repeat imaging, antibiotic continuation, line repositioning)? Do prior-conditioned generation models amplify the rate relative to their training distribution — i.e. is "prior-comparison hallucination" partly faithful reproduction of human behaviour? Does the estimand transplant to pathology addenda, echo and serial dermatological photography (echo and cytology both confirmed unmeasured)? Can carry-forward be detected automatically (prior-report overlap plus image-model disagreement) to triage serial exams at corpus scale? Is the reader-noise floor itself prior-dependent, which would recast "radiologist-level performance" claims generally?
Significance — anchoring: The unexplained magnitude of report-vs-image label disagreement (VisualCheXbert's kappa gaps, Olatunji's 20%, arXiv:2608.10084's near-zero cardiomegaly agreement) — the candidate supplies a testable component whose predicted sign is opposite to the non-mention channel, making the two discriminable. The gap between report-labelled benchmark performance and prospective clinical performance. The "hallucinated priors" problem in report generation, reframed from preprocessing nuisance to possible label-validity defect. The clinical-documentation copy-forward literature, which has no bridge to imaging labels. Qualitative cognitive-bias work on anchoring and prior-report framing, which lacks an outcome measure.
Reason for silence: Three composing mechanisms, none of them "no one thought of it". (a) Unit-of-analysis artifact at a disciplinary boundary: corpora are consumed as flat (image, label) rows; series order is present in the identifiers and absent from the analysis frame of everyone who studies label quality, whose error taxonomy was inherited from NLP extraction (negation, uncertainty, label hierarchy), while the people who own carry-forward as a concept (documentation researchers, radiology QA) do not work on datasets. Evidenced by arXiv:2509.15107's silence. Per adversary 1, the record's wording must be corrected: the category IS in radiology's error list (opposite sign) and absent from the dataset-label list. (b) The fix absorbed the question: the one subfield that noticed reports talk about priors met it as a text-fidelity nuisance and deleted it (arXiv:2210.06340, CXR-PRO, ReXPref-Prior, 2602.23676); a quantity stripped in preprocessing is never estimated. Strongest and evidenced. (c) Incentive gap and ownership vacuum: the finding would retroactively discount the benchmarks the field rests on, no actor owns it, and a blinded multi-reader audit costs radiologist time with no reward for the likely null.

Strongest remaining objection: A blinded single-image panel cannot distinguish "restated but no longer present" from "still present but now below the detection threshold of a supine portable AP film", and the index-exam noise floor does not fix it because index positives are systematically more conspicuous than follow-up residual positives — so the question's own predicted signature (excess report-label false positives in the classes that resolve) is produced just as well by declining conspicuity with no inheritance at all. With (i)–(iv) the two Partials on attacks 2 and 4 become Resolvable and novelty stays Medium with a close but non-duplicating neighbour.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): Establish feasibility and prevalence of the denominator before any reader study — on MIMIC-CXR, pair each study with its immediately preceding study per subject and count carry-forward-eligible positive assertions per finding class, separating pure change-descriptors and hybrid phrasings, to see whether the stratum is large enough to sample and how much of it the hybrid policy decides. Also verify the ">76% of reports reference priors" figure at its primary source (arXiv:2210.06340 / PMLR v193 ramesh22a); it is recorded only as a second-hand citation inside arXiv:2602.23676 and must not be used as established.

ID: UQ-20261016-08
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): Medicine — solid-organ transplantation / organ preservation; transplant outcome epidemiology. Transplanted from pharmaceutical stability science (ICH Q1A mean kinetic temperature) and chemical kinetics.

Question (canonical): In deceased-donor kidney (or liver) grafts with retrievable time-resolved container/perfusate temperature records from cross-clamp to reperfusion, linked to registry outcomes: does adding a pre-specified Arrhenius thermal-dose exposure D = ∫exp(-Ea/RT(t))dt (equivalently duration paired with the ICH-Q1A mean kinetic temperature of the interval), with a pre-specified sub-zero injury penalty, to a risk model already containing cold ischemia time improve discrimination and calibration for delayed graft function and 1-year graft function in a nested comparison — and does the CIT coefficient attenuate when the dose is entered (the proxy/mediation limb)?

Alternative formulations:
- Is preservation injury a function of elapsed time or of an Arrhenius-weighted temperature-time dose, and does risk-adjustment and organ-acceptance practice therefore use the wrong exposure variable?
- How much of the between-graft variation now attributed to cold ischemia time is variation in storage temperature history instead?

Motivating gap: CIT is a time-only exposure presupposing effectively isothermal storage; instrumented studies contradict that in both directions (Villa 2006, n=6 intraparenchymal livers, near 0 °C not 4 °C; Lima 2023, n=39 kidneys, most transport-box readings sub-zero). Pharmaceutical stability science abandoned time-only accounting and encoded MKT in ICH Q1A; transplantation logs temperature for QA and keeps duration for outcome modelling (Adani 2020 logged at 0.1 Hz and regressed on durations only). Full gap, citation corrections and two unverified intake citations: batches/2026-10-16-0233/UQ-20261016-08-record.md.

Presuppositions: 8 enumerated in the record. Binding/contested: (1) time-resolved logs retrievable at scale and linkable to registry outcomes — judged by adversary 2 to be weaker than "contested": what is routinely retrievable is spot readings (Villa n=6 probes; Lima 4 infrared points; Sweet 2023 four timepoints), not traces; (2) container/perfusate tracks parenchyma with characterisable lag — unsupported, gives structured error biased toward the null; (4)/(6) Arrhenius form over 0–10 °C with Ea unidentifiable in observational data, so the test is of a pre-specified dose family, not of the proposition; (5) temperature history may be a marker of logistics quality, leaving the mediation limb unidentifiable. Intake's "CIT is an allocation variable" was withdrawn as overstated. Judge: nothing smuggled (all flagged), but no mechanistic warrant for a single rate-limiting Ea in a system with parallel metabolic, chill, ice and reperfusion-signalling mechanisms.

What would count as an answer: a pre-registered cohort analysis fixing Ea, penalty form and lag model in advance; dose entered alongside CIT with nested discrimination/calibration gain and CIs; reported change in the CIT coefficient under a stated confounding structure; sensitivity across a pre-specified Ea/lag grid. An across-the-grid null is decisive and justifies keeping the time-only exposure; a result positive at only some grid points is a non-answer and must be reported as one.

Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): Gate 2, 11 searches + 5 fetches (2 failed), six vocabularies; Gate 4, 18 further searches + 8 fetches in 15 vocabularies Gate 2 did not try. Full lists: batches/2026-10-16-0233/UQ-20261016-08-record.md, -adversary-1.md, -adversary-2.md. Most informative:
- "mean kinetic temperature" organ preservation transplant cold storage → no transplant-outcome use of MKT; device patents and setpoint reviews only.
- "storage temperature" static cold storage kidney randomized 10 °C vs 4 °C outcome trial → the field is testing the setpoint as an intervention (NCT07385651, record contents unverified), not temperature history as an exposure.
- Europe PMC full-text "mean kinetic temperature" AND graft (adversary 2, F4 — the sweep Gate 2 failed to run) → hitCount 2, both irrelevant: the MKT-for-grafts construct genuinely has no biomedical footprint.
- perfusate temperature independent predictor delayed graft function multivariable cold ischemia time machine perfusion log (adversary 2, q7; adversary 1, q3/q5 independently) → Sweet 2023, the on-point same-organ cohort Gate 2 missed.
- postharvest chilling injury accumulation model logged temperature history "chill units" vs storage duration (adversary 2, q9) → horticulture already runs dynamic chilling-injury accumulation models on logged traces, sub-zero patch included.
- "time out of controlled temperature" red blood cell units transfusion outcome (adversary 2, q2) → transfusion medicine already regulates cumulative out-of-band thermal exposure (the 30-minute rule).

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
P1. Sweet AL, Connelly CR, Dewey EN, Scott DL. "The Effect of Perfusate Temperature on Delayed Graft Function in Deceased Donor Renal Transplantation." Prog Transplant 2023;33(4):341-347, doi:10.1177/15269248231212920, PMID 37964564. 113 machine-perfused deceased-donor kidneys; perfusate temperature logged at 5/15/60/180 min; T5min >10 °C vs ≤10 °C OR 4.5 for DGF; concludes with a QI target. Found independently by both adversaries; verified via OHSU record and PubMed. This displaces all three of the record's priors as nearest.
P2. Villa R et al. "Real-Time Direct Measurement of Human Liver Allograft Temperature from Recovery to Transplantation." Transplantation 2006;81(3):483-486, doi:10.1097/01.tp.0000195903.12999.bc. Nearest prior on measurement; refutes the fixed-4 °C premise.
P3. Kuipers TGJ et al. "Kidney temperature course during living organ procurement and transplantation." Transpl Int 2017;30:162-169, doi:10.1111/tri.12892 (the record's unverified intake citation; opened by adversary 1). Post-storage kidney temperature mean ~1.6 °C, range 0.7–8.4 °C; CIT a non-significant covariate; no temperature-rise/graft-function correlation.
(Lima 2023, Braz J Transplant 26:e0423 and Adani 2020, Ann Transplant 25:e918997 remain real and relevant but are no longer among the three nearest. NCT07385651 unverified.)

Novelty — how this differs from each: vs P1 — Sweet uses four spot readings rather than a trace, computes no cumulative or kinetic dose, runs no nested discrimination/calibration comparison, and no mediation limb; whether CIT entered its multivariable model could not be confirmed by either adversary (named predictors: donor age, KDPI, T5min). The surviving difference is a parameterisation of the exposure plus the mediation limb, in the same organ, for the same outcome, from the same pump-log data stream the record names as its only feasible source. vs P2 — measures the required input, n=6, no exposure variable, no CIT comparison. vs P3 — temperature-course description with CIT as a nuisance covariate; no dose, no mediation.

Novelty confidence: Low (judge-regraded from the record's Medium). Grounds: a single new query in a vocabulary Gate 2 nominally covered surfaced an on-point same-organ, same-outcome, same-data-source cohort study, found independently by both adversaries; the record's central novelty grounds ("no outcome modelling of logged preservation temperature"; Adani as the un-asked question's negative image) do not survive it. Adversary 2's arithmetic further shows the distinctive construct is a reparametrisation: MKT is defined to reproduce the Arrhenius integral, so D is exactly (duration, MKT), and over the realised 0–10 °C band at ICH's Ea = 83.144 kJ/mol the MKT–mean-temperature gap is ~0.3 K at σ=2 K (~3% of dose) — i.e. numerically "duration × mean storage temperature". Not Unverified: 29 documented queries and the Europe PMC full-text sweep were run.

Significance — consequence: if yes, CIT is partly a proxy, historical CIT coefficients partly absorb era- and route-specific thermal variance, and temperature logging becomes worth mandating as a reportable exposure modifiable by containers rather than couriers; if no, duration adequately captures preservation injury over realised histories and the pharmaceutical analogy fails for a multicellular organ. Judge: both consequences attach to the broad "does temperature history matter beyond duration" question, which Sweet 2023 has already opened, not to the kinetic parameterisation.

Significance — audience: OPOs, couriers and container/perfusion-device vendors; registry custodians (SRTR/UNOS, Eurotransplant, NHSBT) facing a schema decision; transplant epidemiologists and DGF/graft-survival model builders; the setpoint-trial community, for whom a dose metric is a natural secondary analysis of its own logs. Judge: the audiences are real but the decision attributed to them is not evidenced — the one group that did find a temperature–outcome association responded with a local QI threshold ("pre-cool below 10 °C at 5 min"), which needs no Arrhenius machinery, and the field's live decision is a setpoint a dose metric does not inform.

Significance — fecundity: whether machine perfusion's benefit partly reduces to thermal stabilisation; the shape of the injury–temperature curve below 4 °C and whether a sub-zero penalty threshold is estimable; organ-specific setpoints as points on a dose-response curve; re-reading the "safe CIT" threshold literature; pre-specified-dose exposures elsewhere (tissue banking, gametes, cell therapy, blood components).

Significance — anchoring: the open optimal-preservation-temperature problem (4 °C vs ~10 °C, in trial); heterogeneity of CIT effect estimates across registries and eras; the DGF prediction plateau on registry fields; the mechanistic dispute over rate-suppressed metabolism vs chill injury vs reperfusion-coupled signalling; the published critique of MKT's validity in its own field.

Reason for silence: claimed as disciplinary boundary (QA/logistics own the temperature, epidemiologists own the outcome model, regulatory kinetics owns the construct) plus a registry-schema data layer plus a mild liability-adjacent incentive to keep excursion logs local. Judge: this does not survive Gate 4. A transplant group asked the temperature–outcome question from pump telemetry and published it in 2023 without a registry field and without liability stopping it, so the data-layer and incentive legs fall. The residual silence to explain is only "nobody integrated the trace", and per attack 1 that has a cheaper non-silence explanation — the integral is near-collinear with duration and nearly identical to duration × mean temperature, so anyone holding the data has an actuarial reason to prefer the simpler variable. A vocabulary boundary (MKT's zero biomedical footprint, Europe PMC hitCount 2) explains the absent jargon, not an absent question. Under the ledger's own rule, a missing credible silence mechanism makes the novelty finding itself suspect — and here it was independently falsified.

ID: UQ-20261016-09
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): Medicine — neuroepidemiology; Alzheimer fluid biomarkers; public-health forecasting. Neighbouring: demographic period-cohort analysis, laboratory pre-analytics, health-technology planning. Source method: new-instrument question.
Question (canonical): Within a single cohort that has published an epoch-to-epoch fall in age-specific dementia incidence and holds archived plasma drawn at a matched age window in each epoch, when all epochs' aliquots are assayed in one lot with bridging controls: (a) what is the age-standardised later/earlier ratio of plasma p-tau217 positivity and the quantile-by-quantile shift in its continuous distribution, (b) what is the ratio of age-specific clinical dementia incidence to biomarker positivity in each epoch, and (c) does a pre-specified within-epoch storage-duration gradient analysis exclude assay drift as the explanation? (Gate 1 reformulation; one reformulation used.)
Alternative formulations:
- (V0, intake) In cohorts documenting a decline in age-specific clinical dementia incidence across calendar epochs and holding archived plasma from comparable age windows, has biomarker-defined Alzheimer pathology prevalence declined in parallel, or has only the probability that a given pathology burden becomes dementia declined?
- (lay) Is the fall in dementia incidence a fall in pathology, or a fall in the expression of pathology as disease?
Motivating gap: The ~20%/decade fall in age-specific dementia incidence (Satizabal et al., NEJM 2016; Alzheimer Cohorts Consortium) is debated in terms of vascular risk, education and reserve, with pathology measured only at autopsy. Plasma p-tau217 (validated from ~2020, clinically cleared 2025) makes the pathology-versus-expression split measurable in archived plasma from the living cohorts that reported the decline. Gate 2 falsified the gap as a *question* gap: the question itself is in print in autopsy vocabulary (Alzforum, "Those Declining Dementia Rates? It's Not the Plaques and Tangles") and is explicitly declared unanswered for the cohorts that documented the decline. What survives is a new answer-route (archived plasma in place of absent post-mortem tissue) plus its falsification test for the storage confound — a method gap on an asked question.
Presuppositions: P1 p-tau217 in long-archived plasma is stable and comparable across storage durations and collection protocols — CONTESTED and central, because storage duration is collinear with epoch; an active pre-analytics literature exists (storage-dependent variability on Lumipulse, differential analyte stability affecting ratios, prospective p-tau217 stability work), so it is testable rather than assumed. P2 sampling frames comparable across epochs — CONTESTED (falling participation, possible selection by cognitive status). P3 an epoch-transportable positivity threshold exists — CONTESTED (threshold and head-to-head assay work still being published 2025-2026), hence the continuous distribution must be reported. P4 the clinical incidence decline is real rather than a diagnostic/ascertainment artefact — CONTESTED in part; modelled, not assumed away. P5 competing mortality and age-window comparability are handleable — established, but it constrains which cohorts qualify. P6 p-tau217 positivity is a valid proxy for the pathology in question — established against PET/autopsy in contemporary samples, weaker for pre-2000 specimens. It is a question, not a thesis: both answers are pre-specified and neither is favoured by the design.
What would count as an answer: archived plasma from two or more epochs of the same cohort (ideally replicated in a second), one assay lot with bridging controls, reporting epoch-specific age-standardised positivity, the full continuous distribution, the prevalence ratio, and the incidence/positivity ratio, each with confidence intervals, plus a storage-duration sensitivity analysis able to exclude assay drift in either direction. Parallel declines answer "pathology"; stable or rising pathology with falling clinical incidence answers "expression"; a failed storage-stability analysis declares the question not yet answerable rather than splitting the difference.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 11 web searches (cap 11) and 5 fetches (cap 5), full budget consumed, none refused; full list in batches/2026-10-16-0233/UQ-20261016-09-record.md. Most informative: (2, answer-directed) `has the decline in dementia incidence been accompanied by a decline in Alzheimer pathology or only in its clinical expression` → the decisive query, returning the Alzforum report of P1 plus JAMA Neurol and trend meta-analyses — the question exists in print, in autopsy form; (5) `CFAS I CFAS II neuropathology comparison time trends amyloid tangles two epochs` → the CFAS review (P3), which states no neuropathology cohort exists for CFAS II and the pathological basis of the decline is therefore unknown; (9) `"resilience to pathology" changed over calendar time probability pathology expressed as dementia birth cohorts` → the same ROSMAP/Grodstein cluster, confirming "resilience" as established vocabulary for the identical question; (3) H70 p-tau217 prevalence query → the H70 fixed-age prevalence/transition paper, single epoch, no epoch comparison; (6) `secular trends amyloid PET positivity prevalence calendar time cognitively unimpaired Mayo Clinic Study of Aging` → cross-sectional-by-age prevalence only, no calendar-epoch contrast; (7) storage-stability query → a real pre-analytics literature, none of it framing an epoch comparison; (10) eligibility-sizing query → anti-amyloid eligibility and wait-time models (USC; Finland ISPOR 2025) all assuming stationary pathology prevalence; (1, 8, 11) archived-plasma/Framingham/historical-specimen queries → p-tau217 as an incident-dementia predictor and assay head-to-heads, no secular or epoch analysis anywhere. Ledger duplicate check: INDEX.md read in full (39 entries, UQ-20261015-01..UQ-20261016-05), grep for dementia/alzheimer/p-tau/amyloid/neuroepidem over unasked-ledger.md returned zero hits — no ledger duplicate. Not opened, hence not cited: PMC9941972 (CAPTCHA); the JAMA Neurology publisher page for P1 (library proxy only — P1's details are as reported by the opened Alzforum item).
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources): P1. Grodstein F, Leurgans SE, Capuano AW, Schneider JA, Bennett DA, "Trends in Postmortem Neurodegenerative and Cerebrovascular Neuropathologies Over 25 Years", JAMA Neurology 2023;80(4):370-376 — verified via the opened Alzforum report https://alzforum.org/node/2689231; 1,554 ROSMAP decedents, four birth epochs 1905-1930, AD pathology flat (tangles slightly higher later), atherosclerosis/arteriolosclerosis down, microinfarcts up; authors conclude resilience rather than less pathology. P2. Merrick R, Matthews FE, "Time trends in neuropathology give clues to dementia risk reduction", Nature Reviews Neurology 2023 — opened at https://hull-repository.worktribe.com/OutputFile/4529335; states the inference outright, the decline coming "courtesy of vascular and resilience pathways". P3. Wharton SB, Simpson JE, Ince PG, Richardson CD, Merrick R, Matthews FE, Brayne C, "Insights into the pathological basis of dementia from population-based neuropathology studies", Neuropathol. Appl. Neurobiol. 2023 — opened at https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10946587; records falling age-specific dementia prevalence and incidence between CFAS I and CFAS II, that no neuropathology cohort was developed for CFAS II, and therefore that the pathological basis of the decline is unknown. Near but not a prior formulation: Dittrich et al., "Prevalence of high-risk plasma p-tau217 levels and 5-year transition of risk status in 70-year-olds", Alz. Dement. 2026;22(6):e71545 (opened via UKDRI) — H70, one birth cohort, 3.6% high-risk at 70 rising to 7.0% at 75-77; no epoch comparison, no link to incidence trends.
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs P1 — same question, different instrument and population: P1 measures decedents of a convenience cohort that has not itself published an incidence decline, so pathology and incidence trends come from different populations and no incidence/positivity ratio can be formed, and burden-among-decedents is not the age-specific population prevalence projections need. The candidate measures living-cohort plasma at matched age inside a decline-documenting cohort. That is a methodological upgrade to an asked question. vs P2 — the same inference stated as a conclusion rather than a design; it does not consider archived plasma or the storage-duration confound, which is where the candidate's genuinely unfound content lies. vs P3 — P3 asks the candidate's question of the right cohort and records it as unanswered for want of epoch-2 tissue; the candidate's contribution is that the missing measurement need not be tissue. A new answer-route to a question P3 poses outright.
Novelty confidence: Low
Significance — consequence: parallel pathology decline → prevention is altering disease, not only its expression; pathology-prevalence inputs to projection models fall with cohort replacement; prevention trials gain a defensible pathology endpoint. Stable or rising pathology with falling clinical incidence → the population is compensating, the population eligible for amyloid- and tau-targeted therapy is undiminished and will not shrink, the decline is contingent on whatever sustains compensation and so reversible (consistent with reports of flattening), and trials powered on pathology endpoints are powered on the wrong quantity. The two answers move the same planning numbers in opposite directions.
Significance — audience: (i) dementia-projection modellers and health-system planners, who would carry an epoch-varying rather than stationary pathology-prevalence term — query 10 shows eligibility-sizing and wait-time models (USC; Finland, ISPOR 2025) assuming stationarity; (ii) prevention trialists choosing between pathology and expression endpoints; (iii) the risk-reduction community, for whether modifiable risk factors prevent pathology or buffer it, which changes the claim behind the 40%-of-cases figure; (iv) anti-amyloid therapeutic planners and payers sizing eligible populations; (v) biobank custodians, whose archived plasma becomes a primary asset needing bridging-aliquot funding. Real and identifiable — but P1-P3 show this audience has already been served a partial answer in autopsy vocabulary and attributes the decline to resilience, so what the candidate offers them is a better measurement, not a new consideration.
Significance — fecundity: whether the incidence/positivity ratio varies by education, APOE, vascular burden or birth cohort (who is compensating); whether epoch shifts sit in the whole p-tau217 distribution or only its upper tail (onset delayed vs pathology attenuated); whether GFAP/NfL move while p-tau217 stays flat, localising the change to the pathology-to-injury rather than injury-to-dementia step; whether storage-duration gradients generalise into a retro-assay calibration method for other archived analytes; what an epoch-varying pathology prevalence does to lead-time and over-diagnosis estimates for population blood-biomarker screening.
Significance — anchoring: the named open problem of the mechanism of the dementia-incidence decline; the flattening/reversal reports in recent trend updates; the cognitive-reserve/resilience construct, which lacks a population-scale pathology denominator; the pathology-prevalence inputs of every anti-amyloid eligibility estimate; and the pre-analytics literature on whether legacy biobank plasma can be assayed for p-tau217 at all, of which this is in part a stress test.
Reason for silence: proposed mechanism is new instrument plus a deterrent confound, with a disciplinary-boundary component — p-tau217 assays are 1-5 years old (clearance 2025; thresholds and head-to-heads still appearing in 2025-2026), so the plasma route has only recently existed; storage duration is perfectly collinear with epoch, so the obvious design looks confounded on its face and is easier not to propose than to defend; and the decline literature is produced by register-based epidemiologists while the assay literature is produced by neurochemistry groups in memory-clinic and single-epoch samples (H70 holds both, published separately). Admissible under the ledger's list — but by its own admission the instrument component is mere recency and carries little evidential weight, and attack 7's converse applies in the other direction: P3 shows the question *was* asked, in tissue vocabulary, and recorded as undoable. The mechanism explains the silence of the method, not of the question, which is exactly the Gate 2 finding.

Strongest remaining objection: the question is asked. Wharton et al. 2023 (P3) poses it of the very cohorts that documented the decline — CFAS I versus CFAS II — and records it as unanswered because no neuropathology cohort was built for CFAS II; Grodstein et al. 2023 (P1) and Merrick & Matthews 2023 (P2) answer the autopsy version in ROSMAP and conclude resilience rather than less pathology. What the searches failed to find is any epoch-to-epoch plasma-biomarker comparison, protocol or preprint; an unused instrument for an asked question is a method gap, not an un-asked question, and substituting archived plasma for absent brain tissue is a new answer-route to an existing question. ID: UQ-20261016-10
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): Medicine / public health (molecular diagnostics, IVD regulatory science, outbreak preparedness); molecular microbiology. Method imported from industrial organisation (concentration indices) and portfolio risk (correlated failure). Source method: silence mapping.
Question (canonical): For a named pathogen and fixed calendar window, over the enumerable fleet of authorised nucleic-acid amplification tests (pre-specified source set: WHO EUL/PQ, FDA EUA and 510(k) summaries, EU IVDR filings, national reference-laboratory protocol registries), with each assay's amplification target localised at the finest resolution the public record supports and weighted by its share of tests actually performed (pre-specified reconstruction hierarchy): (a) what is the volume-weighted concentration of target regions across the genome, as a Herfindahl-Hirschman index and its reciprocal (effective number of independent targets), on pre-specified binning with the unresolved fraction propagated as interval bounds; and (b) under a stated site-specific substitution/recombination arrival model and a per-chemistry mismatch-to-dropout failure model, what is the probability that a single circulating event degrades at least X% of volume-weighted global capacity (X on a pre-specified grid, e.g. 10/25/50%)?
Alternative formulations:
- What is the effective number of independent diagnostic targets in worldwide use for this pathogen, and what systemic single-mutation failure risk does that concentration imply?
- Is the world's molecular testing capacity for a pathogen a monoculture, and what is the measurement that would show it?
- (V0, intake, superseded at Gate 1 for an underdetermined estimand: fleet membership, target resolution, volume reconstruction, binning.)
Motivating gap: Per-assay in-silico primer/probe evaluation against circulating diversity is a dense genre, and multi-target design advice is decades old, but both are scoped to one assay or panel. The fleet-level quantity — how concentrated targets are across the assays actually in use, and the capacity-weighted probability that one event removes a large share at once — is reportedly absent. Every manufacturer can satisfy "use two targets" while the whole fleet converges on the same two, which is the correlated-failure case per-assay advice cannot see. Intake's instances (PMC8597629, PMC3859022) were not verified in either session.
Presuppositions:
1. Deployed assays' target regions knowable at useful resolution — CONTESTED; resolution recorded per assay, unresolvable fraction itself reportable.
2. Per-assay test volumes reconstructible — CONTESTED; fixed reconstruction hierarchy, coverage stated.
3. Site-specific mutation arrival estimable from observed diversity — PARTLY ESTABLISHED; explicitly model-conditional.
4. Assay failure approximately threshold in mismatch number/position — PARTLY ESTABLISHED; per-chemistry failure model required.
5. Capacity substitutable at short notice — CONTESTED; deliberately excluded from the estimand.
6. Nothing presupposed about the answer's direction; low concentration is a closing answer.
7. (Gate 1) A concentration index on genomic bins meaningfully summarises correlated-failure exposure — WEAKLY ESTABLISHED; binning-sensitive.
8. UNFLAGGED AND FALSE FOR THE DOMINANT CASE (found by adversary 1, attack 4): that an assay's volume share maps onto a capacity share per target region. Most deployed assays are multiplex with any-target positive calling, so loss of one target narrows margin rather than removing capacity, and the record states no rule for splitting a multiplex assay's volume across its targets.
What would count as an answer: A reconstructed fleet table (assay -> target region(s) -> volume share) with stated coverage, per-assay resolution and unresolved proprietary fraction; HHI and effective target number as bounds, not a point estimate; and a site-resolved probability that one event degrades at least X% of capacity under stated evolutionary and failure models. Falsification test as specified: the estimator must assign non-negligible prior probability to known dropout episodes (S-gene target failure; ORF1ab dropout). Three outcomes close it: high concentration with quantified systemic risk; defensible low concentration; or a demonstration that the unresolved fractions preclude any bounded estimate, with that bound stated. JUDGE'S NOTE: the named falsification test is incoherent as written — see "Strongest remaining objection".
Novelty — queries run (query -> one-line result): 12 attempted in the generating session, 9 completed (all GitHub code/issue/repository search), 3 refused (1 WebSearch, 2 WebFetch) by a safety classifier acting on prior conversation content. Most informative completed: GitHub repository search "primer/probe mismatch surveillance against variants" -> 8 hits, 1 relevant (hammasbuilds/assay-drift); GitHub repository search "authorised-test target-gene registry / volume-share database" -> 0 hits (no public machine-readable assay-to-target registry surfaced); GitHub issue search (semantic) "Herfindahl index of amplification target regions weighted by test volume" -> 0 hits; GitHub code search "effective number of targets" / "target concentration index" + assay + mutation -> 0 hits. Adversary 1: 7 web attempts (3 WebSearch, 4 WebFetch) all refused or content-free, 0 pages opened; 3 further GitHub queries completed in vocabularies the record had not tried (non-English; procurement/portfolio; aggregated assay-to-gene database) -> 0 hits each. PubMed/Europe PMC, Google Scholar, arXiv and all grey literature were unreachable in both sessions. Gate 2 step 2 is NOT satisfied: 0 literature queries ran, and code hosting is the wrong index for a clinical-microbiology and regulatory-science literature. Full lists: batches/2026-10-16-0233/UQ-20261016-10-record.md and UQ-20261016-10-adversary-1.md.
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources): Gate 2 step 4 NOT satisfiable from this record; stated honestly rather than filled.
1. VERIFIED (search-API metadata only; README unreadable): hammasbuilds/assay-drift, https://github.com/hammasbuilds/assay-drift — per-assay drift of five published PCR assays against 2,765 GenBank genomes; created 2026-09-23, 0 stars. Not a literature prior.
2. NOT VERIFIED: the per-assay in-silico-evaluation genre (intake names PMC8597629). Unreachable in two consecutive sessions.
3. NOT VERIFIED: the multi-target design-recommendation genre (intake names PMC3859022, 2013). Unreachable in two consecutive sessions.
A fourth class, never searched and the most likely home of a near-duplicate: WHO/FIND/Unitaid and reference-laboratory grey literature on diagnostic market concentration and surge capacity, plus post-2021 commentary generalising S-gene target failure to the installed base.
Novelty — how this differs from each: From 1 — same ingredients (published oligos vs observed diversity), different object: assay-drift is per-assay, with no volume weighting, no fleet enumeration, no concentration statistic and no joint one-event probability. From 2 — different unit of analysis: per-assay output is "assay A loses sensitivity against lineage L"; the candidate's output is a distribution over the installed base, whose distinctive content is cross-assay covariance. From 3 — that genre is normative and per-product; the candidate is descriptive and system-level, and the two come apart precisely when every manufacturer complies yet the fleet's effective target number is near 2. CAVEAT: differences 2 and 3 are stated against intake's description, not against any source read.
Novelty confidence: Unverified
Significance — consequence: High concentration (effective targets ~2-4 over most global volume) prices a currently unpriced failure mode and converts target diversity into a procurement and listing variable (disjoint-region award requirements; reserve assays chosen by genomic distance). Low concentration defuses a post-S-gene-target-failure anxiety and shows the existing per-assay regime sufficient, forestalling a costly regulatory addition. Unmeasurable identifies target-region (not sequence) disclosure as the narrow transparency requirement that would make the risk observable. Three outcomes, three different actions, and no one currently knows which obtains.
Significance — audience: WHO PQ/EUL and FIND (a portfolio-level listing criterion and a target-region dossier field); national procurement agencies and diagnostic funders (target-diversity or lot-splitting award criteria); FDA and EU notified bodies under IVDR (the input that would justify a horizontal or post-market diversity requirement, where the review unit is today one assay); reference laboratories and preparedness planners (reserve-assay selection by genomic distance; expected capacity loss); pathogen-genomics surveillance groups (a watchlist of operationally consequential sites, ranked differently from immunological ones). Adversary: real bodies, but no evidence any of them wants the statistic; tenders turn on price, throughput and installed base, and a genomic-distance criterion cuts against standardisation.
Significance — fecundity: Optimal diagnostic-portfolio diversification given concentration, switching cost and lead time; whether fleet concentration itself selects for its own blind spot via non-uniform ascertainment; the same statistic for antigen-epitope and sequencing-primer-scheme fleets; cross-pathogen comparison separating conserved-region scarcity from protocol copying; whether the first-published protocol's target predicts eventual fleet concentration (path dependence in emergency diagnostic markets).
Significance — anchoring: Documented dropout episodes (S-gene target failure, ORF1ab dropout) currently sit as curiosities or surveillance side-effects rather than realisations of a measured risk; the preparedness literature's surge-capacity problem counts tests and instruments but not target architecture; IVD regulation's per-assay/system-level mismatch leaves no body holding the aggregate; and the analogous imports of concentration and correlated-failure modelling into crop monoculture and financial systemic risk both produced policy instruments.
Reason for silence: Claimed mechanism is a disciplinary boundary with no owner: the quantity is an industrial-organisation statistic computed on genome coordinates, and those fluent in the first never hold assay target data while those fluent in the second work at the unit of one assay; reinforced structurally because the review and publication unit is the assay, so no single review can ever contain a fleet statistic. Secondary: an infrastructure/access mechanism (multi-jurisdiction assembly, trade-secret oligo coordinates, no funder whose remit it matches). A third, incentive-gap strand is disowned by the record itself. Adversary 1 wrote that deployed multiplex assays "call a positive on any-target logic". For the flagship assay in the record's own positive control that is not so: Thermo Fisher's own CE-IVD FAQ (https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/GSD/Reference-Materials/69-70del-s-gene-mutation-ceivd-faq.pdf) states the three-target TaqPath COVID-19 kits detect S, N and orf1ab in separate channels and that "a positive result is called if at least two of the three SARS-CoV-2 targets are detected", that "the S gene dropout does not mean a result is negative", and that with only one target left the result is inconclusive rather than falsely negative. The record's own retrospective falsification test remains incoherent for the reason given: S-gene target failure left two targets amplifying and was used across Europe as a *variant-tracking signal* precisely because testing capacity was not lost.

ID: UQ-20261016-11
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Rejected (Gate 2 — asked-but-still-open: the field has named this missing observation in print. Routed. Novelty Unverified and Gate 4 never ran, so Validated was unreachable on two further independent grounds.)
Domain(s): STEM — pharmaceutical solid-state chemistry / crystallization science; measuring disciplines: aerosol single-particle analysis and cleaning-validation surface sampling. Source method: anomaly mining.
Question (canonical): For a compound with a still-preparable metastable form and a stable form, and a panel of rooms stratified by documented handling history of the stable form: (a) what quantity of the stable form, introduced as recovered surface or air residue into a standardised seed-controlled supersaturated crystallisation that otherwise yields the metastable form, flips the outcome to the stable form — the flip threshold; (b) does recovered residue from exposed rooms carry seeding activity at or above that threshold while naive and cleaned rooms do not, with a monotone dose–response; and (c) what is the persistence half-life of that activity after handling ceases and after defined cleaning?
(This is the Gate 1 reformulation, the one permitted, used for well-posedness only. Gate 0 as submitted: "In laboratories and pilot plants with a documented handling history of a compound that has a metastable and a stable polymorph, is crystallographically active seed material of the stable form recoverable from air and surfaces at quantities above the threshold that determines which form crystallizes, and with what persistence after handling stops?" Reason for reformulating: V0 quantified against "the threshold that determines which form crystallizes" as though it were established, and it is not — Bučar, Lancaster & Bernstein 2015 state verbatim that "there is no consensus about the size and range of activity of such seeds." The reformulation makes the threshold something the study establishes rather than assumes.)
Alternative formulations:
1. Is the "disappearing polymorph" phenomenon caused by an ambient seed burden that can be measured directly — swabbed, counted, form-identified and shown to decay — rather than inferred after the fact?
2. For a given compound and room, what is the dose–response between recovered environmental residue (mass and polymorphic form) and the probability that an unseeded crystallisation yields the stable rather than the metastable form?
Motivating gap: disappearing polymorphs are a named, repeatedly reported anomaly — once the thermodynamically stable form has been obtained somewhere, a previously reproducible metastable form often becomes hard or impossible to prepare across unrelated laboratories. The ambient-seeding explanation is asserted in the canonical reviews and, on the evidence opened, never measured. Deliberate seeding is quantitatively engineered in industry and cleaning validation already swabs surfaces for drug residue by HPLC, so both halves of the measurement exist as routine practice; no source opened puts them together to measure the involuntary seed burden of a working room — mass, polymorphic form, seeding activity and decay time.
Presuppositions: 7 enumerated in the record. Binding/contested: (2) seed-free crystallisation reproducibly gives the metastable form in a naive environment — CONTESTED, and the reformulation's main motivation, since historical records are informal and Bučar 2015 notes ritonavir Form I was later obtained even in previously exposed laboratories under controlled conditions; (3) trace environmental material is a real causal route — CONTESTED, with impurity templating a live competitor (Bučar 2015 reports a sulfathiazole byproduct stabilising metastable Form I at 10 mol %); (7) NEW, introduced by the measurement design and the most fragile — the flip threshold lies at or above the recovery-and-quantitation limit of the sampling chain, CONTESTED and possibly false, since deliberate ritonavir seeding was effective "even at amounts as low as 1 ppm" and the review's own arithmetic puts ~1e10 seeds inside one optically invisible particle, so the active quantity may sit orders of magnitude below HPLC LOQ on a swab.
What would count as an answer: a sampling campaign over rooms stratified by documented exposure, with residue quantified by the existing cleaning-validation HPLC chain and assayed functionally for seeding activity in a standardised supersaturated solution that yields the metastable form in naive apparatus; the deliverable is a dose–response from recovered quantity to probability of the stable form, with a threshold, a persistence half-life from re-sampling after handling ceases and after cleaning, and form identification where mass permits. "Uninterpretable" is pre-registered as a real third outcome: rooms indistinguishable *and* a spiked positive-control series showing the flip threshold lies below the sampling chain's detection limit.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): **6 of the required ≥8 executed.** Searches 1–6 ran (verifying the three intake citations; then "environmental seeding" polymorph crystallization; unintentional seeding / cross-contamination polymorph control; cleaning validation surface residue swab nucleation). Search 7 was refused by a conversation-level safety classifier whose message stated the refusal would recur for the rest of the session, and searches 8–10 plus one fetch were refused the same way; per the operating rule the agent recorded the refusals and stopped rather than reworking the queries. **Never queried: the aerosol-science vocabulary ("single-particle Raman", "surface particulate loading", "airborne crystal nuclei") and the occupational / industrial-hygiene neighbouring field** — by the record's own assessment the two most likely places for a killer paper. Most informative of those that ran: the cleaning-validation sweep, an informative negative — that literature is entirely about total residue mass for toxicological carryover limits and addresses neither polymorphic form nor nucleation activity of recovered residue. Full list in `batches/2026-10-16-0433/UQ-20261016-11-record.md`.
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, all opened):
A. **Bučar D-K, Lancaster RW, Bernstein J, "Disappearing Polymorphs Revisited", *Angew Chem Int Ed* 2015;54(24):6972–6993, doi 10.1002/anie.201410356** (PMID 26031248, PMC4479028). Opened in full by the Gate 2 agent and **re-verified independently by the run session**. Asserts the ambient-seed mechanism as the leading explanation — "the working atmosphere inevitably becomes contaminated with seeds of the particular material", quoting Mullin that atmospheric dust "frequently contains particles of the crystalline product itself" — quantifies it by calculation, reports anecdotal persistence and decontamination (the 1960s benzocaine:picric acid case recovered after "washing the equipment and laboratory benches and waiting for 8–12 days"; otherwise "move to another laboratory" or "thoroughly clean the laboratory", neither always successful), and names the 1 ppm deliberate-seeding threshold for ritonavir Form II.
B. Nicoud L, Licordari F, Myerson AS, *CrystEngComm* 2019, doi 10.1039/c8ce01428k (opened). Seeded batch crystallisation of paracetamol targeting metastable form II with online Raman/IR and population-balance modelling; low temperature and low stirring suppress primary cross-nucleation of form I.
C. Nahas L, Haw M, Sefcik J, Lee M (Strathclyde/GSK), "(301b) Does Seeding Always Preserve Solid Form? Cross-Nucleation Study of α- and γ-Glycine", AIChE Annual Meeting 2025 (opened). Seed-on-a-stick isolation of fluid-shear effects on secondary nucleation; fluid shear alone can drive secondary nucleation.
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs A — A poses the mechanism, asserts the atmosphere is contaminated, offers a seed-quantity calculation, and reports anecdotal persistence and decontamination, but contains and cites no *measurement*: no room sampled, no form identification of recovered particles, no quantity-to-outcome dose–response, no measured decay time. That difference is real, and it is also exactly why this entry is rejected rather than banked (see below). vs B — same underlying physics and the same instruments, but B's seeds are deliberately weighed into a crystalliser and its contaminants are inside the vessel; the candidate's estimand is a property of the *room*. B also supplies an argument for the design, since trace unwanted form is causally potent at unweighably small loadings. vs C — the most serious technical threat to the readout rather than a competitor for the question: if seeding with one form can cross-nucleate the other, a functional seeding assay may misreport which form the room's residue causes.
Novelty confidence: **Unverified** — on two independent grounds, either sufficient: 6 of the required ≥8 searches ran before the tool was refused, and the vocabularies most likely to contain a near-duplicate were never queried. This is a tool-availability outcome and carries no information either way about whether the question has been asked.
Asked-but-open: **Yes, and this is the ground of rejection.** Prior A states in print, quoting the 1995 Dunitz & Bernstein review, that such seeds "have never actually been directly observed" and that "there is no consensus about the size and range of activity of such seeds." The field has therefore named the missing observation and left it standing for thirty years. Under the LEDGER's own Definitions an asked-but-unanswered question is an open problem and belongs in the routing handoff, not in this ledger — and that determination does not depend on any of the refused searches, since the missing searches bear only on whether the question is *un-asked*, which is moot once it is established as asked-and-open. The candidate's real contribution is a measurement design for an acknowledged gap, which is a research proposal rather than an un-asked question.
Significance — consequence: if yes, polymorph control becomes partly a facility-engineering problem with measurable specifications — a surface-loading limit, a decay time, a demonstrated cleaning efficacy — in place of the folklore remedies the review itself documents (discard everything, wash the benches, wait 8–12 days, or move building), and disappearing polymorphs become preventable and in principle reversible on a measured schedule. If no, with positive controls demonstrating adequate sensitivity, the mechanism asserted as well established in the canonical review of the phenomenon is unsupported at the quantities actually present, redirecting causal attention to impurity templating, humidity and scale. Asymmetry, stated against the candidate: a "yes" largely confirms received wisdom, so the expected information sits disproportionately in the "no" and "uninterpretable" branches.
Significance — audience: pharmaceutical solid-form development and CMC groups (manufacturability of a metastable target form in a given suite); **cleaning-validation and QA analysts — the strongest would-actually-act argument in the record**, because that community already swabs surfaces and quantifies drug residue by HPLC on a mandated schedule, exclusively against toxicological carryover limits, so the marginal ask is an added endpoint rather than a new programme; facility and HVAC/containment engineers; regulators drafting cross-contamination expectations, who have no quantitative basis for form-specific carryover; and academic crystallisation laboratories, for the reproducibility of published metastable-form preparations.
Significance — fecundity: decay kinetics of surface seeding activity against humidity and surface material; whether seeding activity survives dissolution-and-drying cycles, i.e. whether cleaning redistributes rather than removes it; whether HVAC filtration class predicts room seed burden; whether documented irreproducibility of specific metastable preparations correlates with institutional handling history.
Significance — anchoring: the disappearing-polymorph anomaly; the explicit "no consensus about the size and range of activity of such seeds" gap stated in Prior A; reproducibility of metastable-form preparation; cross-nucleation as a live 2025 research front (Prior C); and the unexamined boundary between cleaning validation as a toxicology exercise and as a crystallisation control.
Reason for silence: a disciplinary boundary plus a specific incentive gap. The measurement needs three communities sharing neither journals, instruments, personnel nor regulatory endpoints — solid-state chemists own the polymorph question but treat the room as background (the canonical review's response to the missing observation was to calculate how many seeds *would* be in a dust particle rather than to sample one), while cleaning-validation analysts own the swab infrastructure and have no reason to ask about form. The incentive gap is concrete rather than generic: documenting that your rooms carry crystallographically active seed of a particular form creates a discoverable record that cannot be un-known at the next inspection, and the informative "no" requires demonstrating your own assay's detection limit against the active threshold.
Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status):
1. Triviality | not run | no adversary was spawned: the candidate failed Gate 2 (asked-but-open, on a prior opened and independently re-verified) and ended before Gate 4 | Not run
2. Disguise | not run | **Disguise is UNVERIFIED.** No adversarial sweep ran, and Gate 2 itself was cut off at 6 queries with the aerosol-science and industrial-hygiene vocabularies never tried, so on this ground alone the entry could not have been Validated even had the routing determination not settled it. The specific unverified risk the record names: a measurement of environmental API seed burden may exist in occupational-hygiene, containment-engineering or single-particle-aerosol literature that neither Gate 2 nor any adversary searched | Not run
3.–8. | not run | same reason | Not run
Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3
Well-posedness 2/3: the core measurement is specifiable end to end and the reformulation removed the undefined-threshold defect. Deductions: a genuinely naive room is close to unobtainable for any compound ever handled, so a negative can be attributed to insufficient naivety unless naivety is defined by assay rather than by history; Prior C's cross-nucleation result undermines the functional readout; and presupposition 7 may be false, in which case the study returns "uninterpretable" by construction.
Significance 2/3: consequence is real and the anchoring is to a named anomaly with an explicitly acknowledged evidential hole, with an unusually concrete audience argument since the cleaning-validation community already owns the instruments, the access and the schedule. Held below 3 by the information asymmetry — a "yes" confirms the textbook account.
Strongest remaining objection: the one that rejected it. Prior A does not merely leave this question open by accident; it states the gap in terms, in the canonical review of the phenomenon, and has done since 1995 in its predecessor. A question whose own literature says "this has never been directly observed and there is no consensus on it" is an open problem with a standing invitation, not a question nobody asked. The candidate's contribution is a design for answering it, and the ledger's job is to find questions nobody has posed.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): not applicable; rejected and routed. The design question a taker would have to settle first is presupposition 7 — whether the flip threshold lies above the sampling chain's limit of quantitation — because if it does not, the campaign returns "uninterpretable" regardless of what the rooms contain. That is a bench calibration on spiked swabs, not a sampling campaign, and it is cheap.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): **Yes** — appended to `ledger/routed-open-problems.md` with Prior A as the source showing it is open and explicitly acknowledged as unobserved.
Run-environment note, recorded rather than smoothed over: this candidate's Gates 0–3 agent was terminated three times by a model-level safeguard returning `[bio]` — a false positive on a question about crystal nucleation in pharmaceutical manufacturing rooms, which concerns no living organism. The first two attempts died before producing anything; the third wrote this record in full and then failed on its closing call, which is why the record exists while the agent is logged as errored. The candidate's text was never reworded to get past the filter. Gate 4 was not attempted, since the Gate 2 routing determination was by then established on a verified source and an adversary could not change it.

ID: UQ-20261016-12
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): AI — evaluation methodology; inference/serving practice; secondary: empirical software engineering (model-hub mining)
Question (canonical): For the N most-downloaded open-weight instruct repositories on the Hugging Face hub, (a) what fraction carry at least one commit landing after the last weight-shard commit that modifies a behaviour-determining non-weight artifact (`tokenizer*`, `*template*`/`chat_template`, `generation_config.json`, `special_tokens_map.json`, `added_tokens.json`), where "behaviour-determining" is decided empirically by rendering a fixed prompt set under both revisions and diffing token-ID sequences and stop/EOS configuration rather than by diffing files; and (b) with weight files verified identical and harness, seeds, runtime and decoding pinned, what is the paired score-delta distribution between the earliest and latest such revision on a suite spanning format-sensitive and format-robust tasks, measured against a same-revision repeat-run noise floor obtained in the same study, and what fraction of those deltas exceed both that floor and the empirical distribution of improvement margins claimed as evidence in a sampled set of model-comparison papers?
Alternative formulations: (i) Does naming a model, rather than a model plus a revision hash, identify the system under test, or is a published "Model A vs Model B" comparison underdetermined by config drift? (ii) With weights identical, how large is the benchmark-score distribution induced by a repository's own history of tokenizer/template/generation-config commits?
Motivating gap: The field cites open-weight releases by name and treats the weights as the artifact, with tokenizer files, chat template, generation config and special-token map as inert metadata. They are mutable files in a git repo, routinely patched after release, and they decide prompt formatting, EOS/stop behaviour and default sampling. The hazard is handled in tooling, not measured in the literature: `huggingface/lighteval` carries unit tests against the hub fixture `lighteval/different-chat-templates-per-revision` (verified; `tests/unit/models/vllm/test_vllm_model.py`, `tests/unit/models/test_transformers_model.py`), and lm-evaluation-harness issue #4396 (opened 2026-10-16) asks a backend to record tokenizer identity and chat-template metadata. No study measures how often this happens in the wild or what it does to scores.
Presuppositions: 1. Hub commit histories permit distinguishing weight-freeze from later config-only commits — FLAGGED; adversary #2 shows the stated operative definition fails, because safetensors conversion, re-sharding, index rewrites and dtype re-uploads reset "last weight-shard commit" without changing tensor values, and file-byte SHA is the wrong invariant (a `.safetensors` file's SHA differs from the `.bin` it replaces at identical tensors). Mitigable by tensor-value hashing; not in the record. 2. Config-only changes are applicable to fixed weights in isolation — established in principle, needs pinned harness/runtime. 3. Scores are reproducible to within less than the drift effect — CONTESTED (cf. UQ-20261016-06); converted into an in-study measured noise floor rather than assumed. 4. Published comparisons cite bare names often enough for the hazard to bite — asserted in the record; partly corroborated by adversary #2 (arXiv:2609.08765 presents recording resolved commit hashes as a contribution; Ajibode et al. find 40.87% of weight-file changes invisible to name-based versioning). 5. A config-induced shift is an evidence defect rather than a legitimate improvement — CONTESTED, deliberately narrowed to "two papers citing one name may have measured different systems". Additionally unflagged in the record and raised by adversary #1: hub repos are uploaded privately and flipped public later, so pre-publication fixups are indistinguishable in git history from post-release drift, inflating the census.
What would count as an answer: Two-part study. (1) Census: enumerate post-weight-freeze commits to the artifact set across the top-N instruct repositories and classify each behaviour-affecting or cosmetic by rendered token-ID sequences, stop sets and generation defaults; report the affected fraction, per-artifact breakdown, time-to-first-such-commit. (2) Experiment: with weights verified identical and harness/seeds/runtime/decoding pinned, evaluate earliest vs latest behaviour-affecting revision and report the paired delta distribution and its tail against the in-study same-revision noise floor. "Yes, it matters" if a non-trivial share of repositories show deltas exceeding both the floor and measured claimed-margin sizes, concentrated as predicted on format-sensitive tasks; "no" if deltas are indistinguishable from the floor across the suite, which would positively license bare-name citation.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 11 web queries at Gate 2 (+2 GitHub code searches, 2 null GitHub issue searches, 4 fetches); 9 further queries and 4 fetches per adversary in vocabularies Gate 2 did not try (9 and 9 Disguise queries, both above the 8 minimum). Full lists: batches/2026-10-16-0433/UQ-20261016-12-record.md and UQ-20261016-12-adversary-1.md / -2.md. Most informative: own-field obvious-title form "Towards Semantic Versioning of Open Pre-trained Language Model Releases on Hugging Face" → Ajibode et al. arXiv:2409.10472; "effect of chat template version on LLM benchmark accuracy open-weight models" → arXiv:2607.02587 "The Moving Target"; Japanese "チャットテンプレート トークナイザ設定 変更 同じ重み ベンチマーク スコア 差 再現性 評価" → arXiv:2609.08765 "Benchmark Scores Are Pipeline-Dependent" (the run's strongest hit, missed by Gate 2); MSR evolution vocabulary → Castaño et al. arXiv:2411.09645 (680k commits, no benchmark); audit vocabulary → arXiv:2605.25492 "SafetyRepro" (abstract only; full text never opened); reproducible-eval canon → EleutherAI arXiv:2405.14782 (surfaced, not opened); GitHub code search `"different-chat-templates-per-revision"` → 24 hits, lighteval fixture verified. Gate 2's record is therefore incomplete: three on-point own-field items (2609.08765, 2405.14782, 2411.09645) were found only by the adversaries.
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources): 1. "Benchmark Scores Are Pipeline-Dependent: A Reliability Audit of Cybersecurity LLM Benchmarks", arXiv:2609.08765 (PDF opened by adversary #2) — weights fixed; varies prompt template/chat formatting, decoding, stop sequences, backend-inherited generation-config defaults, extraction and aggregation; single-factor effects include an 85.9 pp stop-sequence effect and 40 pp decoding drift; standardisation moves means +1.3 to +32.9 and shifts 9/10 models by ≥3 ranks. 2. Fan et al., "The Moving Target: A Longitudinal Audit of Trust-Benchmark Score Drift Across Open-Source Chat LLM Release Lines", arXiv:2607.02587 (abs opened twice, independently corroborated) — four families, three successive public generations each, three researcher-chosen templates; concludes a trust score belongs to a checkpoint, not a release line. 3. Sclar et al., FormatSpread, arXiv:2310.11324 (ICLR 2024) — researcher-constructed semantically equivalent format perturbations, up to 76-point accuracy spreads. Also near, verified real: Ajibode et al. arXiv:2409.10472 (census side, weight files only, no benchmark); Castaño et al. arXiv:2411.09645; unopened and unexcluded: arXiv:2605.25492 (SafetyRepro, same group as #2, "commit-stamped evaluation protocol"), arXiv:2405.14782.
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs 1 — same experimental shape (weights fixed, formatting/stop/generation-config varied) but the perturbations are benchmark-author and harness choices, not a repository's own successive shipped revisions; it never varies revisions or tokenizer files, never estimates repeat-run variability (explicitly declines), never compares to claimed paper margins, and does no census. It bounds what is achievable, not what was realised. vs 2 — unit is a new public generation, so weights change and drift is confounded with retraining; never mentions tokenizer files, templates, generation configs or special-token maps; no census, no identical-weights condition, no noise floor. vs 3 — synthetic, synchronous, researcher-generated perturbation space with no notion of revision or provenance; cannot bound the realised drift from the handful of edits maintainers actually committed.
Novelty confidence: Medium
Significance — consequence: If yes, a published by-name comparison is underdetermined: two papers can report different numbers for identical weights and both be correct, and a gap of the size routinely treated as evidence can be an artifact of clone date — making revision reporting a requirement rather than a nicety, and predicting an upward creep in by-name scores over time (post-release commits are mostly fixes) that confounds longitudinal progress claims. If no, the field gains a measured licence for bare-name citation. Adversary #2 fairly notes the "no" branch is partly foreclosed by 2609.08765's magnitudes, so the decision-relevant unknown is prevalence and location rather than existence.
Significance — audience: Evaluation-harness maintainers (lighteval's per-revision fixture; lm-eval-harness #4396 and #1841 show the audience is live and the matter unresolved) — whether to record and report resolved artifact SHAs alongside scores; leaderboard operators — whether to re-run entries after a template commit, and how many; venue reproducibility checklists and reviewers — a one-line requirement with a measured justification; model releasers — whether a post-release template/EOS fix warrants a new tag and a note that prior numbers are stale; serving teams — whether a cached tokenizer snapshot is a CI-gated risk.
Significance — fecundity: Makes askable: the right unit of model identity for evaluation (name, revision, or rendered-prompt-plus-stop-config fingerprint); whether a behaviour-affecting/cosmetic classifier can ship as a release-time CI gate; whether drift concentrates on format-sensitive task families, giving a cheap triage rule; whether the upward-fix bias inflates year-over-year progress curves; and jointly with UQ-20261016-06, how a benchmark number's total error budget decomposes across nondeterminism, harness version, runtime and artifact revision.
Significance — anchoring: UQ-20261016-06 (residual nondeterminism; supplies the noise floor and the reason presupposition 3 is contested); the harness-version confound in leaderboard scores, of which this is the artifact-side analogue; Ajibode et al.'s semantic-versioning gap, extended across the weight/non-weight boundary; the closed-API silent-change problem (Gao et al., recorded unverified) as its public, file-attributable complement; the prompt-format-sensitivity line, to which it would supply the realised-perturbation distribution. Adversary #2 adds a cross-field precedent for the question shape: Gene Ontology annotation-version drift changing downstream biological conclusions with data fixed (PMC5865181) — an in-scope transplant, not a disguise.
Reason for silence: A perturbation-set-provenance gap plus a fix-not-publish incentive. The census half is MSR work that has mined hundreds of thousands of hub commits (Ajibode 52k models; Castaño 680k commits; PeaTMOSS) without running a single benchmark; the experiment half is evaluation work that does run fixed-weight configuration audits (2609.08765) but sources its perturbations from benchmark and harness choices because a researcher-constructed space is cheap, unbounded and publishable, whereas a repository's commit history yields a small, messy, non-i.i.d. set requiring provenance archaeology. Adversary #2 correctly shows the record's stronger claim — "neither community owns the join" — is too strong and must be narrowed to this provenance gap. The incentive half survives: 2609.08765 impugns benchmark authors' pipelines, whereas this candidate would impugn the comparability of its own audience's published numbers, so a closed bug is cheaper for everyone who sees the hazard (lighteval's fixture). Minor new-instrument component: cheap earliest-vs-latest sweeps across dozens of repositories only recently became affordable.

Judge's note on scores: the record self-scored 3/3 · 3/3. Well-posedness is reduced to 2/3 because the central operative term — "weights frozen" as the last weight-shard commit, with byte-SHA verification — is demonstrably the wrong invariant on the hub (conversion and re-sharding commits), and because the private→public flip makes "post-release" unidentifiable from git history alone; both are nameable and mitigable, which is why this is not an ill-posedness rejection. Significance is reduced to 2/3 because 2609.08765's magnitudes largely foreclose the "no" branch, so the claim that either answer is equally actionable does not hold; prevalence and location remain decision-relevant.
Strongest remaining objection: arXiv:2609.08765 "Benchmark Scores Are Pipeline-Dependent" already publishes the candidate's headline result in its own field — weights fixed, chat formatting, stop sequences and generation-config defaults varied, with an 85.9 pp single-factor stop-sequence effect and whole-pipeline mean shifts up to +32.9 — so what remains un-asked is the narrower pair of the prevalence census and the provenance of the perturbation set, and Gate 2 missed this paper entirely, which is the ledger's own documented failure signature.
