| 4 | Presupposition failure | The unlisted load-bearing presupposition. V2 centres the band at the cadence frequency 1/T (1 h -> 2.8e-4 Hz; 2 h -> 1.4e-4 Hz), i.e. period = the loop's own sampling interval. A controller updating every T cannot express an oscillation of period T — that component sits at its sampling frequency and aliases to DC; the loop's Nyquist limit is 1/(2T), and the intermittent-control and relay/deadband literatures the candidate borrows from give minimum limit-cycle period 2T or longer. So the pre-registered primary band is centred on the one frequency at which a clinician-sampled loop cannot cycle, and whatever power sits there is the step-train comb of Attack 1. Worse, the theory-predicted 1-h signature 1/(2x3600) = 1.4e-4 Hz is numerically identical to the claimed 2-h signature, so the cadence-tracking contrast that identifies the whole question is degenerate — a 1-h unit cycling as predicted scores as a 2-h unit. P1's "4x resolution" criterion reasons about the resolution of the data and never about the Nyquist frequency of the loop. | Re-centring at 1/(2T) would preserve the question in recognisable form, but the one permitted reformulation was already spent on V2, the 1-h/2-h collision requires the identifying variation to be respecified rather than relabelled, and a question whose pre-registered primary band is in the wrong place under its own borrowed mechanism is not 3/3 well-posed. | Unresolved |
| 5 | Vagueness | The primary test is null by construction: a phase-randomised surrogate preserves the amplitude spectrum exactly, so it cannot be a floor for excess power at a named frequency, and block-shuffling in cadence-commensurate blocks preserves the same comb. The headline comparison is set by the method, not the data. | The coherence/phase requirement and the cadence contrast carry real information and are not vulnerable this way — but the power-excess limb is the record's stated primary. | Unresolved |
| 6 | Significance inflation | Cadence-setters act on staffing economics; device groups will proceed regardless — both conceded in the record. | Audiences are real and named with live trial identifiers, and the neonatal precedent shows a field does change practice once the operator-interval link is demonstrated. Magnitude of consequence remains asserted. | Partial |
| 7 | Reason for silence | The premise was asked, qualitatively, by prior 3; the operator-interval question was asked and answered in neonatal oxygen; mechanism (iii) is speculative, and "you act when you look" being obvious is a more parsimonious account. | Mechanisms (i) and (ii) survive 9 further queries: no clinical loop-identification study exists and the method sits one field away uncited, which is a genuine boundary account of why the quantitative version was never posed. | Partial |
| 8 | Dissolution | The question splits into trivial actuation quantisation, a textbook sampled-data stability question of known sign, and competing cadence-locked generators (syringe changeover, care clusters, the measurement act itself) that occupy the same band and co-vary with unit routine — so limb (b)'s exogenous contrast is unclean even in principle. | Limb (c) survives every decomposition as a real empirical question, and a respecified loop-identification question would be worth asking. | Partial |

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3
(Judge's downgrade from the record's self-assessed 3/3, re-grounded after verification: V2 mis-assigns one of its two named nulls and leaves block length, band width, segment length and the numeric meaning of "loop-consistent phase" unspecified — a real specification gap, which is what costs the third point. The earlier basis for the downgrade, a "1/T-vs-1/(2T) collision", is withdrawn: it does not exist. Significance 2/3 stands as recorded and was not what failed.)

**Judge's post-Gate-4 corrections to attacks 4 and 5 (2026-10-16), each verified at source:**

- **A1's fatal argument is refuted, not merely unproven.** A1 rejected the candidate on the claim that a controller sampling every T cannot host an oscillation of period T, so the pre-registered band at 1/T measures only the actuation step-train comb. All three legs fail. (i) The intermittent-control literature the candidate transplants from derives a limit cycle of period *exactly* one intermittent interval — Gawthrop, arXiv:1705.08228 §3.3, λ_crit = +1: "there is a limit-cycle with period Δ_crit"; 2Δ is the λ = −1 case, not a floor. No source states a 2T minimum. (ii) The Nyquist-style 2T bound is a property of a once-per-T observation *record*, not of the loop: a period-T physical oscillation is permitted and is merely aliased to DC when sampled once per interval. (iii) The step-train-comb leg is inverted for the stationary case: the zero-order-hold envelope |H(f)| = |sin(πfT)/(πf)| has its exact *nulls* at f = k/T, so a staircase of hold steps carries a spectral **minimum** at period T, not a peak (verified numerically: comb/background 0.099 at k = 1 for stationary held levels). Sampling in the human intermittent-control models is also aperiodic (Loram et al., IEEE TBME 2022), so there is no single T to collide with.
- **But one half of that leg survives in a form that matters, and is logged as a confound rather than a kill.** If the held level drifts monotonically — which is exactly what steady weaning is — the hold error is a sawtooth of period T whose Fourier series puts lines at exactly k/T with 1/k amplitudes; a simple zero of the sinc cannot cancel a ramp's dipole image (verified: comb/background 6.8e9 at k = 1 for a drifting staircase, against 0.099 stationary). So f = 1/T cannot be used as a built-in negative control: a successor analysis must detrend or high-pass the commanded-dose series before leaning on the null, and must treat k/T as potentially contaminated. A1's intuition was right for weaning trajectories and wrong in general, and its stated mechanism was wrong either way.
- **Attack 5's surrogate objection is locally valid and does not generalise, so attack 4 and attack 5 both stand at Partial, not Unresolved.** A Fourier-phase-randomised surrogate reproduces the periodogram by construction (Theiler et al. 1992 §§2.2.3 and 2.4.1, read in full; verified to 4.5e−13 relative error), so the band-power limb has literally zero power against *that* null — and that floor was the headline methodological addition V2 was credited with, which is a genuine defect. It reaches no further. The **block-shuffled** surrogate V2 also names preserves only the marginal distribution and the total power, and the spectral shape only as a ~1/L-smoothed, O(1/L)-biased version (Künsch 1989; Lahiri 1999; Politis & Romano 1994; Zhang et al. 2006/2007 on bucket permutations); measured, a narrowband line 25× above 1/L retained only 0.074 of its bin power, so band-limited power *does* have power against the block floor. And **magnitude-squared coherence** — the other half of V2's primary test — is normalised by both auto-spectra, so its no-coupling density depends only on the degrees of freedom, p(C²) ∝ (1−C²)^(K−2) (Hannan 1970; Thomson & Chave 1991; Carter 1987); independently randomising each series' phases randomises precisely the phase differences that *are* the cross-spectrum (Prichard & Theiler 1994, Eq. 4), driving coherence to that null while leaving both amplitude spectra exact. Faes et al., IEEE TBME 2004;51(7):1156–1166 is the dedicated primary source and *recommends* spectrum-preserving surrogates as the coherence floor. Measured: data MSC 0.985 versus independent-FT-surrogate mean 0.040 (≈ 1/K) and 95th percentile 0.727. Naming both floors and both statistics is therefore a well-founded design that mis-assigns one pairing, not a self-defeating one.
- **A2, which had none of the above and reached its own view, independently found the FT-surrogate defect at source and also graded it Partial**, on the same reasoning: phase randomisation is the correct null for the coherence-and-phase criterion, while the block surrogate and the control band carry the band-power limb. It also answered A1's and its own staircase objection the way the methods check does — a stepped monotone ramp and a cycling loop differ in the dose–MAP cross-spectrum, not in dose-series band power.
- **A2's new objection is now the strongest one on the record** and is stated below; it is not a signal-processing error but a confounding structure, and it is why this entry is Provisional rather than higher.

Strongest remaining objection: **The exposure and its one frequency-matched confound are collinear by construction, and limb (b) does not break them apart.** ICU nursing care is bundled onto the same hourly or two-hourly rhythm as charting, so procedure-driven dose change and cadence-driven controller cycling occupy the same band; van der Eijk et al. (Acta Paediatrica 2012;101:E97–E104) evidences that procedures dominate large manual titration steps in the closest analogous loop (126 of 136 adjustments of 15% or more were procedure-associated). Entering procedure periodicity as a covariate cannot fix a covariate sitting at the exposure's own frequency, and limb (b)'s cadence contrast does not rescue it, because a unit that changes its documented assessment interval moves its care-round rhythm with it — shifting the hypothesised cause and the confound together. The one real separation left is the *sign* of the dose–MAP phase relation (disturbance rejection has pressure leading dose; controller cycling has dose leading pressure), and that rests on a phase estimate which P5 and P7 independently threaten, charting-time bias on one side and line dead-volume and carrier-flow lag on the other. Secondary, and the reason well-posedness stays at 2/3: band width, block length, segment length, detrending and the numeric meaning of "loop-consistent phase" are named as categories but not as numbers, while each of them determines whether a 1/T peak is resolvable or removed.
[Superseded, retained for the record: this field previously read that V2 pre-registers its primary band at period T, the one frequency at which a controller sampling every T cannot oscillate ("minimum limit-cycle period 2T"), so the band captures the actuation step-train comb rather than loop dynamics, and the theory-predicted 1-h signature coincides exactly with the claimed 2-h signature, collapsing the cadence contrast that identifies limbs (b) and (c). — **withdrawn on verification; see the judge's corrections above.**]

Provisional at: Gate 5. No attack stands Unresolved on 1, 2 or 4, so the fatal rule does not fire: A1's Unresolved on attack 4 rested on an argument refuted at source (see the judge's corrections), and attack 5 — Unresolved for A1, Partial for A2 — is a non-fatal attack, which caps this entry at Provisional. Gate 1 well-posedness 2/3 caps it there independently of Gate 4. **What would promote it:** (i) reassign the nulls — the phase-randomised surrogate to the coherence-and-phase criterion, where it is the field's recommended floor, and the block-shuffled surrogate (with a stated block length short relative to the hypothesised period) plus the control band to the band-power limb; (ii) state band width, segment length, detrending and "loop-consistent phase" as numbers, with the commanded-dose series detrended before 1/T is used, since a drifting hold regenerates a line comb there; (iii) exhibit at least one candidate pair of institutions whose documented assessment-cadence contrast is not also a care-bundle contrast, or an alternative identifying contrast that is not; and (iv) open the three records Gate 2 still owes. With (i)–(iii) in hand and well-posedness at 3/3 this would meet the Validated bar on the present novelty and significance findings; without (iii) it stays Provisional however well specified, because the collinearity is the substantive objection and not a drafting one. Novelty (Medium-minus, not refuted across 12 own-field and 26 adversary queries in fresh vocabularies) and significance (2/3) were never what was in question.

Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): The cheapest decisive check is the one that decides whether limb (b) can identify anything: before any spectral analysis, establish on documents alone whether any two reachable units differ in documented assessment cadence *without* differing in care-round bundling — i.e. whether the cadence contrast exists free of the care-bundle contrast. If it does not, the question as posed is unidentifiable whatever the logs show, and the successor is the phase-sign version (does dose lead pressure or follow it) on a single unit. Separately, Gate 2 still owes full text of PMID 30513357, PMID 26706983 ("Quicker response results in better SpO2 control") and PMC12567164 / PMC4840124 (catecholamine syringe changeover), all currently attested by abstract or title only, and the neonatal automated-oxygen trial corpus (NCT06622161, NCT05508308, NCT04223258, NCT03785899) was read at registration level only and is the likeliest remaining holder of an unwitting partial prior.

Routing (if rejected as already-asked): Not applicable — not rejected. Nothing is routed to ledger/routed-open-problems.md: novelty was not refuted and no prior formulation of the three-limb question was found in 38 queries across two gates and three fresh contexts, so there is no asked-but-open problem to hand to the research workstream.

ID: UQ-20261016-19
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): Biology/biomedicine — research methods and metascience; shared-facility instrument telemetry
Question (canonical): In a corpus of shared-facility assay records (iLab/PPMS/LIMS, per-run time stamps, user, fund code, sample count) restricted to linked (laboratory, project, assay, sample class) cells whose runs fall in a project window ending at the submission date of a facility-attributed paper, what is the distribution of the attempt-to-publication ratio R = runs logged / runs traceable to a published figure panel (denominator read off the paper's stated n of independent experiments); how does R partition between-laboratory versus between-project; is R associated with the direction of the linked published result; and does any association survive a negative control of calibration/QC assays?
Alternative formulations:
- What is the file-drawer ratio inside the laboratory — how many times was the experiment run before the version that appears in the paper?
- Can billing-grade facility logs reconstruct the unreported attempt count behind a published figure, and is that count associated with whether the finding is positive?
Motivating gap: New-instrument candidate. Selective reporting is claimed to have been measured only from published artefacts (p-curves, excess significance) or self-report, while facility management systems now hold per-run, per-user, time-stamped records for years because finance requires them for cost recovery. Neves & Amaral (eLife 2020;9:e56626) state that detecting unreported experiments "requires information readers don't have" and propose prevention rather than measurement. NOTE: this gap statement was falsified at Gate 4 — see adversarial log, attacks 2 and 4.
Presuppositions: P1 facility records are retrievable and linkable to projects then papers (contested); P2 a logged run is attributable to a published figure (contested); P3 crux — rerun count carries reporting content, with optimisation/faults independent of result direction (contested); P4 an ethics/consent path exists for billing records identifying individuals (contested); P5 facility-mediated assays represent the lab's experimental work (contested; benchtop work leaves no telemetry); P6 retention windows reach back past the publication lag (contested, checkable per facility). Not enumerated by the record and added at Gate 4: P7 the billed unit and the paper's "n independent experiments" are the same kind of thing.
What would count as an answer: A distribution of R over a defined corpus (N linked project-assay cells and matched papers), per assay type, with a within-laboratory variance component, plus the pre-specified result-direction test and the calibration-assay negative control. R near one for most assays is as informative as a large mean. A quantified demonstration that the linkage cannot be made at acceptable error rates is a feasibility verdict, not an answer, and must be reported as such.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): Gate 2: 11 queries (cap), 6 fetches (one over cap, recorded as overage) across lay, metascience, provenance, survey-methodology, manufacturing, pharma-regulatory and facility-management vocabularies — full list in batches/2026-10-16-0633/UQ-20261016-19-record.md. Most informative: "how many experiments were run per published figure unreported attempts biology selective reporting" (mandatory own-field query) → Neves & Amaral 2020, prevention essay, no data; "electronic laboratory notebook records reveal unpublished experiments ratio performed to reported" → Magas, ICML 2026 ELN attempt-dataset proposal (closest hit); "'testing into compliance' instrument audit trail unreported repeat runs" → FDA data-integrity warning letters, the measurement already done per-firm under inspection authority; "iLab PPMS core facility booking billing data mining meta-research" → vendor/admin cost-recovery material only. Gate 4 added 18 further queries in 18 vocabularies Gate 2 did not try (9 per adversary; batches/2026-10-16-0633/UQ-20261016-19-adversary-1.md and -adversary-2.md); the decisive ones were animal-ethics/licence approval records linked to publications, and telescope time-allocation non-publication bibliometrics — both of which returned on-point priors Gate 2 had missed.
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
1. van der Naald et al. 2020, BMJ Open Science (PMC8647586; primary blocked by reCAPTCHA for both adversaries, reported via eurogroupforanimals.org/news/millions-animals-may-be-missing-scientific-studies): three UMC Utrecht departments, animal numbers in 2008-09 ethics-committee protocols linked to resulting papers — 1,471 of 5,590 animals (~26%) acknowledged in publications, 46% of approved studies published as full text, species breakdown. Administrative process records joined to publications to count unreported experiments, in the candidate's own field. Companion: Wieschowski et al. 2019, "Publication rates in animal research" (PMC6879110), two German university medical centres.
2. ESO Survey of Non-Publishing Programmes, arXiv 1802.03272 (opened by adversary #2): 2,716 A-ranked programmes matched against the telbib publication database, 1,278 (47.1%) with no refereed paper, ~37% of allocated time, PI-level breakdown, PI survey in which "null or inconclusive results" accounted for 12.2% of reasons; authors raise a possible "cultural problem" favouring appealing results. Facility allocation records joined to papers with null results already catalogued as a cause. Related: arXiv 1611.09625 (ALMA/ESO archive delivery records, ~90% publication fraction).
3. Magas D (2026), "Experimental Attempts in Electronic Lab Notebooks: A Dataset Proposal for Scientific Debugging," ICML 2026 AI-for-Science workshop poster, https://icml.cc/virtual/2026/73447 (verified independently by both adversaries): run-level attempt records from lab notebooks, for AI scientific debugging; no ratio, no facility records, no publication linkage.
Also in the record and not displaced: Neves & Amaral 2020 (eLife 9:e56626, essay, no data); Kos-Braun et al. 2020 (eLife 9:e62212, core-facility self-report survey); FDA Mylan Nashik warning letter 2017 (instrument audit trails read for unreported runs under inspection authority).
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs Utrecht/Wieschowski — same move (process records → publications), different granularity and conditioning: approved-study-level and unconditional on publication, versus run-level inside published projects. vs ESO — same move at facility-allocation level with the null-result cause already surveyed, versus a per-panel attempt ratio with a pre-registered direction test. vs Magas 2026 — same interest in run-level attempts, different source (self-curated notebooks vs mandatory billing telemetry), no ratio and no publication linkage. The differences are real but they are refinements of a live tradition, not a gap: priors 1 and 2 were found only at Gate 4, and they falsify the "only ever measured from published artefacts or self-report" premise the candidate was built on.
Novelty confidence: Medium (ceiling, with an incomplete search record: 11 of the planned ~15 queries, two blocked fetches, four flagged vocabularies unsearched, and two on-point priors in the candidate's own and a neighbouring literature missed — so Medium is not a Validatable Medium)
Significance — consequence: If R is near one for instrument-mediated assays, experiment-stage selection is small where it can be seen and the reform case shifts to analysis-stage selection and benchtop work; if heavy-tailed in named assays, the file drawer localises to specific techniques and reporting rules can be targeted; if R tracks published result direction, that is process-side evidence of experiment-level selection independent of the published artefact and of self-report, and would calibrate p-curve and excess-significance estimates. A quantified feasibility failure is also consequential. Attenuated at Gate 4: the two closest analogues (26% of approved animals unpublished, 47% non-publishing ESO programmes) produced no reporting-rule change.
Significance — audience: Core-facility directors and shared-resource managers (hold the records, already run acknowledgement/citation tracking and publication KPIs); research-integrity and research-quality offices, which have no process-side metric; journals and funders setting replicate-reporting rules, who would gain an auditable denominator for the "n independent experiments" line; meta-researchers confined to artefact-side inference; facility-funding bodies. Real (ABRF research groups already run inter-facility rigour studies; meta-researchers demonstrably use administrative records when they can get them), but facility directors have a direct incentive against publishing a surveillance-flavoured statistic about their own paying users.
Significance — fecundity: Calibration of artefact-side selective-reporting estimates against a process-side measurement; research-waste accounting with a real denominator; whether attempt count predicts replication failure or retraction; whether a facility-issued "runs performed" provenance line changes how reviewers weigh a figure; whether R responds to preregistration or predefined exclusion criteria; facility-mediated versus benchtop comparison as the limit of telemetry-based metascience.
Significance — anchoring: File-drawer problem and publication bias; the open question of where selection happens (experiment versus analysis stage); the unobservability claim in Neves & Amaral 2020; instrument-PID/RRID-for-core-facility and USEDiT attribution infrastructure; GMP audit-trail practice; research-waste quantification. Gate 4 adds the protocol-to-publication cohort tradition and facility bibliometrics as the actual anchor.
Reason for silence: Claimed: (a) custodianship and incentive boundary — the records sit in finance systems owned by facility managers, were never catalogued as research data, and any analysis reads as surveillance of named colleagues; (b) new instrument — per-run computerised facility records only generalised through the 2010s, so retention windows only now reach past a publication lag. Both adversaries rejected (a): outsiders already obtained institutional records identifying named labs and linked them to publications in biomedicine, and ESO publishes PI-level non-publishing analyses itself; and custodianship explains why answering is hard, not why nobody asked. Only (b) survives, and it explains why the answer is newly obtainable, not the silence.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3
(Well-posedness downgraded from the record's 3/3: the estimand's numerator and denominator are not shown to be the same kind of quantity, which is a definitional defect, not a measurement-error one. Significance 2/3: consequence and fecundity hold; audience uptake is contradicted by the two closest precedents.)
Strongest remaining objection: R is not a well-defined ratio. The numerator is whatever the facility bills — a booked session, a lane, an injection — and the denominator is the paper's count of independent biological replicates; these are different units, related by a price list and a plate layout rather than by anything about the research process, and the relation differs per assay. So R can fall far below or far above 1 for reasons that carry no reporting content, and the per-assay distribution, the cross-assay comparison and the between-laboratory variance decomposition compare quantities of different kinds. Nothing in the Gate 1 reformulation addresses this: P2 covers attribution of runs to figures, never commensurability. Compounding it, the design's inferential load sits on the result-direction test, which is run on a corpus conditioned on publication (a collider that removes exactly the many-runs-then-null cells) and in which legitimate re-replication of nulls predicts the same sign, so even a clean association would not separate selection from ordinary practice.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): Before any corpus is assembled, establish whether a commensurable unit exists at all: for one facility, tabulate what each service actually bills (session, hour, lane, sample, injection) against the "n independent experiments" statements in a hand-audited sample of its acknowledged papers, and see whether any assay class admits a one-billed-unit-to-one-independent-experiment mapping. Separately, redo Gate 2 in the protocol-to-publication cohort and facility-bibliometrics vocabularies the adversaries used, and reposition any surviving question explicitly as the run-level refinement of that family.
**Judge's post-Gate-5 verification (2026-10-16, independent fresh-context sweep, 12 queries, 0 refusals):** the falsification of the motivating gap is CONFIRMED and is stronger than the record states. Prior work links independently created pre-publication process records to the publication record to measure non-reporting in at least three families: animal-ethics protocol cohorts (Wieschowski 2019 — 67% publication; van der Naald 2020 — 26% of animals reported; a French NHP/ALTEX study — 1,751 of 3,649 authorised animals appearing in publications); observatory time-allocation records (ESO non-publishing programmes, 52.9% return and 36.8% of allocated time to non-publishing programmes — mutually confirming the entry's 47.1%/~37% figures; ALMA ~90%; XMM-Newton ObsID linkage — 16% of observations and 13% of observing time never used in any paper); and protocol/registry/grant/regulatory comparisons (the 37 studies tabulated by Li 2018). The sharpest counterexample, which the record does not cite, is **Chan et al. 2004**: it uses ethics-committee protocols rather than published artefacts AND shows self-report failing — 86% of trialists denied unreported outcomes that their own protocols proved existed. So "selective reporting has only ever been measured from published artefacts or self-report" is false and is struck. A narrower gap does survive, and is logged for a successor rather than for this entry: nothing located measures attempts-per-reported-result in the strict sense (runs executed per run reaching a figure). Every existing denominator is either allocated resource (ESO time, animals authorised, XMM observing time) or planned analyses (Boonacker 2011: 69% of prespecified subgroup analyses unreported, 76% of reported analyses post hoc; Kasenda 2014; Chan 2004's outcome-level 50%/65%), never executed experimental attempts, and none is derived from instrument run logs. The XMM reuse factor (5–15x, up to 30x) runs the other way — datasets per paper, not attempts per figure — and the one effort aimed at run-level attempt records (the ICML 2026 ELN dataset proposal) carries no publication linkage and no numbers. None of this disturbs the verdict: the fatal ground is attack 4, the non-commensurability of R, which is independent of the gap question.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): Not routed. The rejection is presupposition failure at Gate 4, not asked-but-still-open; and the parent-family question (process records joined to publications to count unreported work) has been partly answered — van der Naald et al. 2020, Wieschowski et al. 2019, ESO arXiv 1802.03272 — so it is an answered/disguised-adjacent rejection, which the operating rules exclude from routing.

ID: UQ-20261016-20
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): Biology — functional genomics, synthetic biology, oligo-library design. Neighbours: coding theory / DNA data storage, manufacturing engineering (DFM), genome assembly ("dark genome"), CRISPR-library design.

Question (canonical): For a dated, versioned DNA-synthesis manufacturability rule set, implemented per platform (oligo-array pool, column, enzymatic) and calibrated against >=2 publicly queryable vendor feasibility interfaces, applied as a classifier to fixed-length windows tiling GRCh38 plus one non-human control genome: (a) what fraction of bases is classified reject-or-reprice, per platform and date; (b) per pre-specified annotation class (protein-coding exons, promoters and CpG islands, structured-RNA genes, low-complexity sequence and each repeat family, enhancer catalogues), what is the log2 enrichment of excluded bases against a composition-matched shuffled-window null, with CIs; and (c) for a pre-specified set of synthesis-based "genome-wide" screens, what share of each study's nominal target space is in the excluded set, versus the dropout that study's own library-representation QC reports? Pre-committed bands: MANUFACTURING BLIND SPOT / HONEST GENOME-WIDE / NEGLIGIBLE.

Alternative formulations:
- (V0, intake) What fraction of a reference genome's functional annotation classes falls in sequence space current commercial synthesis platforms reject or silently rewrite, and are the most-excluded classes thereby absent from libraries described as genome-wide?
- (lay) Which parts of the genome can we not even manufacture, and does that blind spot coincide with the parts we most want to test?
- (framing) Is "genome-wide" in a synthesis-based MPRA or library screen a biology claim or a vendor-manufacturability claim?
Reformulated once at Gate 1 (V0 -> V1): the "silently rewrite" limb declared out of scope (not observable outside the vendor); platform and date moved into the estimand; shuffle null and pre-committed bands added; non-human control genome added.

Motivating gap: Silence mapping. The how-literature on difficult DNA is dense and largely commercial (vendors score, reject, reprice, "optimise"); the on-point own-field query returned MPRA statistical-method papers plus two vendor pages. Claimed mechanism: the filter acts at ordering, before any data exist, so exclusion appears in no methods or results section. Gate 2 partially falsified the gap: the classifier half exists at least three times (Synthesis Success Calculator 2020; SCP4ssd 2023; DNA Scanner), and SCP4ssd already ran a difficulty classifier over 4,318 E. coli MG1655 sequences (13% difficult). Unlocated: annotation-class enrichment against a null, per-platform dated framing, screen-level audit.

Presuppositions: P1 (contested, load-bearing) vendor rules are implementable as a window classifier — partly relieved by published classifiers/DNA Scanner, but their labels are gene-synthesis turnaround, not an oligo-pool accept/reject. P2 (contested) exclusion is a property of sequence rather than of length/platform/price — not defused, indexed instead. P3 (contested, weakest) published genome-wide screens dropped these regions rather than recovering them from native DNA — untested; genomic-fragment STARR-seq and capture libraries are not synthesis-limited. P4 (asserted ESTABLISHED) annotation classes are defined independently of synthesisability — FAILS at Gate 4 (see below). P5 (out of scope) silent rewriting is frequent and detectable. P6 (contested) reference coordinates are the right frame; double-counting with the dark genome remains. NOT presupposed: that the excluded set is functionally enriched.

What would count as an answer: (i) the per-platform dated classifier applied genome-wide, giving excluded base fraction and per-class log2 enrichment/depletion vs composition-matched shuffles with CIs, scored by the bands, so that "excluded but not enriched" is a real negative; (ii) for de novo synthesised library screens only, measured share of nominal target space in the excluded set against that study's own reported representation dropout, with rule-set sensitivity reported as a quantity.

Novelty — queries run (query -> one-line result): 13 searches + 6 fetches in the Gate 2 record (cap was 11/5 — over cap by 2 and 1, recorded; three fetches returned nothing usable, two curl attempts to Europe PMC refused by the egress proxy), plus 9 new-vocabulary searches and 4 fetches at Gate 4. Full lists: batches/2026-10-16-0633/UQ-20261016-20-record.md and UQ-20261016-20-adversary-1.md. Most informative:
- "synthesis bias limits coverage of regulatory elements in MPRA libraries GC-rich promoters underrepresented" (mandatory own-field obvious title) -> MPRA statistical-method papers plus two Twist pages, one for MPRA oligo synthesis; no census.
- "predicting DNA synthesis difficulty machine learning classifier ... genome-wide application" -> DECISIVE for the classifier half: Synthesis Success Calculator (ACS Synth Biol 2020) and SCP4ssd (Genes 2023).
- "\"dark regions\" of the human genome inaccessible genome annotation overlap fraction genes affected" -> the dark/camouflaged-gene census: the same question already executed at the sequencing boundary.
- "DNA data storage constrained codes homopolymer GC window fraction violating synthesis constraints capacity" -> constraints formalised and capacity computed, but only over designed codewords.

Ledger duplicate check: all 40 INDEX.md entries read; no duplicate or near-duplicate (UQ-20261015-20 opened and confirmed distinct).

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
P1. SCP4ssd, Zhang et al., Genes 14(3):605 (2023), DOI 10.3390/genes14030605 — AutoML easy/difficult synthesis classifier (1,076 labels reused from the Synthesis Success Calculator; 31 of 426 features; test F1 0.930), applied to 4,318 E. coli MG1655 sequences: 87% easy / 13% difficult, ten genes validated. Verified by the adversary, with a correction the record missed: the paper also reports SSC predicting 15.1% difficult on the same set.
P2. Riolo and Steckl, "Comparative analysis of genome code complexity and manufacturability with engineering benchmarks", Sci Rep 12 (Feb 2022), DOI 10.1038/s41598-022-06723-5 — genome scale vs engineering/software benchmarks. Abstract only; NOT re-verified at Gate 4 (crossref check refused by the proxy).
P3. Ebbert et al., "Systematic analysis of dark and camouflaged genes...", Genome Biology 20(1):97 (2019), DOI 10.1186/s13059-019-1707-2 — attribution unverified in the record, CONFIRMED by the adversary: 36,794 dark regions over 6,054 gene bodies, 8.7% wholly dark, dark coding exons in 748 genes.
Also located, title level only, unopened across both gates: DNA Scanner, "a web application comparing DNA synthesis feasibility, price and turnaround time" (JGI; listed at twistbioscience.com/resources/publication/).

Novelty — how this differs from each: vs P1 — gene-length bacterial sequences, not tiled mammalian windows; labels are one 2020 order-history dataset, so no platform or date semantics; no annotation breakdown, no null, no screen limb. P1 nonetheless executes limb (a) in weak form and shows the join is cheap. vs P2 — same manufacturability lens, wrong resolution by orders of magnitude: whole-genome size and throughput, no classifier, windows, annotation, null or screens. vs P3 — same question structure at the reading rather than the writing boundary; sequencing-side exclusion leaves a residual in the data, synthesis-side exclusion leaves nothing; P3 has no study-audit limb. Risk from P3 is double-counting in repeat and segmental-duplication territory, not duplication.

Novelty confidence: **Low for limb (a); Medium for limbs (b) and (c)** — revised down from Medium on the judge's post-Gate-5 verification (2026-10-16, independent fresh-context sweep, 16 queries, 0 refusals). The Disguise caveat is now CLOSED, and not in the candidate's favour. Neither surfaced item is a prior: DNA Scanner is a vendor price/feasibility aggregator with no classifier, no features of its own and no genome-wide analysis; Sc2.0 invokes synthesis difficulty only as qualitative justification for three design rules (homopolymers, intra-CDS repeats, loxPsym spacing), quantifying what it changed and never what could not be made. But the follow-up queries turned up a closer prior that both gates missed: **Halper et al. 2020 already asked and answered limb (a)** — a vendor-trained classifier run over the whole *E. coli* MG1655 genome (~15% of 2.5 kb fragments and 15.5% of CDSs predicted not readily synthesizable) and over 4,474 plasmids (only 34.4% readily synthesizable); SCP4ssd reproduces it (13%) and Zheng et al. 2023 extends whole-chromosome scoring to eukaryotes. Limb (a) is therefore asked and answered for a prokaryotic reference with a predictor, which this entry states rather than claiming the fraction question is open. What is genuinely absent, and belongs to a successor candidate rather than to this one: (i) no published work intersects a synthesis-difficulty call with genome annotation — every existing paper reports sequence determinants (longest repeat, 9-mer density, GC-rich hairpin, Tm) rather than annotation classes; (ii) no such map exists for a eukaryotic or human reference genome at all (the SynHG programme, Wellcome 2025, names human synthesisability as a goal and has published no feasibility map); (iii) no paper of any kind attributes coverage gaps in CRISPR, ORF or oligo-library screens to synthesis failure — the field's own blind-spot literature explains gaps by biology and design instead. Two caveats to carry: the supervised literature's entire empirical base is one 1,076-sequence set containing only 303 real commercial orders (22% failure), so the stratified synthesis-success-versus-GC/repeat/hairpin curves this candidate takes as background do not exist and published fractions are extrapolations from n=303; and the candidate conflates refusal with surcharge, while no published analysis treats the surcharge tier quantitatively at all — the part of the question that most needs vendor data rather than a classifier.

Significance — consequence: If BLIND SPOT, "genome-wide" is partly a procurement claim and pooled MPRA-class reanalyses inherit composition-correlated missingness now modelled as missing-at-random; a synthesis-accessible fraction would be reported alongside nominal coverage and some null results in high-GC and structured-RNA territory reread as non-results. If HONEST GENOME-WIDE, an informative negative that licenses the coverage claim and reassigns dropout to assembly, cloning or sequencing — steps inside the experimenter's control. If NEGLIGIBLE, the question dissolves for current platforms.

Significance — audience: (1) MPRA/STARR-seq/SGE library designers (pre-screen designs, report excluded share); (2) a live standards surface, data.igvf.org's MPRA quality-metric profile, which could absorb a synthesis-accessibility field; (3) groups training sequence-to-function models, who would treat the training distribution as censored by a computable rule; (4) enzymatic/alternative-chemistry vendors, whose capability claims currently have no genome-scale denominator. Discount: audience (1) already routes around difficult sequence as craft knowledge.

Significance — fecundity: whether sequence-to-function models degrade specifically on the synthesis-excluded complement (a by-construction held-out set); whether the synthesis-excluded and sequencing-dark sets intersect or complement (an uncomputed set intersection); whether the literature's "genome-wide" lags synthesis chemistry by vendor generation; whether a benchmark of synthesis-hard functional elements could score new chemistries.

Significance — anchoring: the dark/camouflaged-genome census (same question at the reading boundary, and the methodological template); GC- and length-dependent oligo bias in DNA data storage; constrained-coding capacity results that never ask what share of natural sequence violates the constraints; Riolo and Steckl's manufacturability framing; the inverse-direction Sc2.0 use of synthesis to demonstrate annotation completeness.

Reason for silence: Disciplinary-and-incentive boundary with one structural feature doing the real work — no residual in the data. (1) The rule set lives in vendor order-validation code and, formalised, in coding theory over designed codewords; neither holder has reason to compute its genomic footprint. (2) The rule-holder is the party the census would bound. (3) An unordered molecule leaves nothing behind, so no anomaly ever prompted the question, unlike reads that fail to map. Self-acknowledged weakening: the ingredients are public and cheap and one classifier was already pointed at a genome, so this is nearer "nobody's job" than an instrument or conceptual barrier.

Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status) — adversaries run: 1 (adversary-1, fresh context, 9 new-vocabulary searches, 4 fetches; full log at UQ-20261016-20-adversary-1.md):
1. Triviality | Limb (a) is a threshold on already-published GRCh38 composition statistics, and the sign of limb (b) is textbook (CpG islands and many promoters are GC-rich; GC-rich and repetitive DNA is what phosphoramidite chemistry fails on), so the headline is derivable in a paragraph | Direction is not magnitude: no published per-platform dated base fraction, per-class effect sizes or screen comparison, and SCP4ssd 13% vs SSC 15.1% on one bacterial genome shows the number is not guessable | Partial
2. Disguise | Renamed known? Untried vocabularies: tiling/array probe design, capture-panel design, unclonable/toxic insert, Chinese-language synthetic genomics, enzymatic capability claims, MPRA design attrition, plain composition statistics, Sc2.0 redesign rules | 9 new queries found no renamed duplicate; structural twins all sit at other technology boundaries and stop short of the join (Graf et al. Genome Res 16:271 opened: no uncoverable fraction, no annotation breakdown; toxic-gene censuses are per-gene microbial; Ebbert et al. is the reading boundary; Chinese search returns vendor design guidelines). But Sc2.0 redesign rules and DNA Scanner were surfaced and left unopened for lack of fetch budget — duplication not demonstrated, not excluded | Partial
3. Combinatorial novelty | Vendor rule set x annotation overlay with a shuffle null; the record itself says the join is cheap — is there a problem at the interface or a bedtools job? | One genuine interface problem: vendor labels are per-construct order outcomes, annotation units are genomic windows, and converting an order-level accept/reject into a per-base property of a reference is the actual content — but it is shallow, largely engineering, and the candidate does not pose it as its question | Partial
4. Presupposition failure | Two load-bearing presuppositions fail, one labelled ESTABLISHED. (i) P4 is false for four of six annotation classes: CpG islands are defined by GC fraction and CpG obs/exp, low-complexity by homopolymer and simple-repeat content, repeat families by repetitiveness, structured-RNA genes by secondary structure — exactly the features these classifiers score (SCP4ssd's 31 retained features are composition, k-mer, GC, repeat, Tm, secondary structure, restriction sites). Match the null on the feature and the test can only return no enrichment; fail to match and enrichment is guaranteed. Since the band fires on >=2 annotation classes, the headline verdict can be produced tautologically by the null-matching choice, with only coding exons and enhancer catalogues carrying non-definitional information. (ii) The P1 residual is stronger than admitted: the public rule set is customer-facing design guidelines and SCP4ssd's labels are gene-synthesis turnaround; for array-synthesised pools there may be no reject-or-reprice decision surface at all, so the estimand may measure a decision nobody makes while significance cashes it as absence from libraries | For (ii) limb (c) is the anchor, but it is unevidenced and rests on the record's self-declared weakest limb, whose denominator is admitted undefined before the work starts. For (i) the record offers no response: P4 is asserted as ESTABLISHED on reasoning that is false for three named classes, and its one remedy (the composition-matched null) is what makes those classes uninformative. A repair exists — fire bands only on annotation defined independently of the classifier's features — but that is a rewrite of the scoring rule, not a defence of the question as scored | Unresolved
5. Vagueness | The bands are numeric but the dial is investigator-set: two existing rule sets already differ by 15% relative (13% vs 15.1%) on one bacterial genome, so defensible rule sets can land in different pre-committed bands | Report the rule-set ensemble and treat band instability as the finding; NEGLIGIBLE (<1% on all platforms) is a falsifiable floor. Plausible, unevidenced | Partial
6. Significance inflation | The actionable artefact already exists per-order (SSC, SCP4ssd, DNA Scanner, vendor guidelines), the bench audience already routes around difficult sequence, alternative-chemistry vendors make capability claims in trade press and want no bounding denominator, and perishability caps investment | The real consumers are retrospective — meta-analysts pooling MPRA-class data and sequence-to-function modellers treating computable missingness as at-random — plus one named live standards surface (IGVF MPRA quality metric). Small but genuine | Partial
7. Reason for silence | Ownership and incentive explain vendor silence, not academic silence: guidelines are published as marketing, two classifiers are published, one was already pointed at a genome. The record's own "nobody's job / unglamorous" closing is near-neighbour to "no one thought of it", which the ledger rejects; a competing explanation survives, that practitioners asked, answered informally, and judged it too obvious to publish | "No residual in the data" is a real mechanism and does bear on asking: the reading-side analogue produced a visible artefact that provoked Ebbert et al., whereas an unordered molecule leaves nothing. Acceptable on the ledger's list, but doing less work than intake claimed | Partial
8. Dissolution | Fully indexed, "unmanufacturable" is a property of (platform, length, price tier, date, customer tolerance), not of the genome; what remains risks being an audit of vendor guideline documents crossed with known genome composition, reported as a property of the genome | Limb (c) is the designed stop against self-reference: if predicted exclusion matches independently reported dropout, the classifier measures something outside its own definition. Plausible, unevidenced, and leaning on the weakest limb, which loses genomic-fragment and capture-based screens entirely | Partial

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3

Strongest remaining objection: Definitional circularity in the scoring rule (attack 4(i)). Four of the six pre-specified annotation classes — CpG islands, low-complexity sequence, repeat families, structured-RNA genes — are defined by the very sequence features a synthesis-difficulty classifier scores, so with a composition-matched null they can only return no enrichment and without one they must return enrichment. Because the bands fire on >=2 classes, the headline verdict is set by the null-matching choice rather than by evidence, and the record defends P4 as ESTABLISHED without addressing this. Rejected at Gate 4 (presupposition failure, Unresolved — fatal under the Gate 4 rule). **Second, now-independent ground (judge's post-Gate-5 verification):** limb (a) is asked and answered — Halper et al. 2020 ran a vendor-trained classifier over the whole *E. coli* MG1655 genome and reported the excluded fraction (~15% of 2.5 kb fragments, 15.5% of CDSs), with SCP4ssd (13%) and Zheng et al. 2023 reproducing and extending it; novelty on that limb is Low. The earlier Disguise caveat is withdrawn in the candidate's disfavour: the two unopened items turned out not to be priors, while a closer prior that both gates missed turned out to exist elsewhere. Gate 1 also scored 2/3, below the Validated threshold independently.

Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): Not to be pursued as scored. A V2 resubmission would have to (a) restrict band-triggering to annotation defined independently of the classifier's feature set (protein-coding exons, enhancer catalogues) and report the composition-defined classes as descriptive only, and (b) establish that a reject-or-reprice decision surface exists for array-synthesised pools and not only for clonal gene synthesis — before which the Sc2.0 redesign-rules corpus and the DNA Scanner publication must be opened.

Routing (if rejected as already-asked): None. Rejected for presupposition failure at Gate 4 (fatal), with a second ground added on verification: limb (a) is asked AND ANSWERED (Halper et al. 2020), and answered rejections are excluded from routing by the operating rules. There is accordingly no asked-but-open problem to hand to the research workstream. Not added to routed-open-problems.md.

ID: UQ-20261016-21
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): Medicine — randomised-trial methodology; medical-device regulatory science; measurement/metrology in clinical research

Question (canonical): For a pre-specified frame of completed multicentre RCTs whose primary outcome is generated or titrated by a software-containing measurement device named by model: (i) in what fraction can a firmware or calibration-algorithm revision dated inside the enrolment window be established from a pre-specified ordered route list (manufacturer release notes/service bulletins, FDA recall/MAUDE, EU field-safety notices, direct manufacturer enquiry, the trial report), reported explicitly as a lower bound; and (ii) in the subset with a datable revision and recoverable IPD, what is the treatment-effect-by-device-era interaction on the trial's own effect scale, benchmarked against the trial's own pre-specified MCID (fallback: half-width of its primary 95% CI), with era/calendar-time collinearity reported so non-estimable trials are counted as non-estimable rather than null?
Gate 1 reformulation note: Gate 0 as-submitted version and the single permitted Gate 1 reformulation are both on the record; the above is the reformulation. Full text: batches/2026-10-16-0833/UQ-20261016-21-record.md

Alternative formulations:
 - Do randomised trials silently pool incommensurable measurements because the devices generating their endpoints were re-calibrated by their manufacturers mid-trial?
 - For device-mediated RCTs, is "firmware era" an unmeasured effect modifier large enough to change what the trial concluded?

Motivating gap:
Anchor (both primaries opened at Gate 2): Johnston et al., Arch Dis Child Fetal Neonatal Ed 96(6):F429 (2011) found a Masimo SET calibration-curve artefact ("Values above 87% were elevated by up to 2%"), removed by "board firmware V4.8 or higher", warning it "could affect interpretation of oxygen-targeting trials"; BOOST II, NEJM 2013 (10.1056/NEJMoa1302298): "Halfway through the trials, the oximeter-calibration algorithm was revised", mortality 23.1% vs 15.9% in the revised-algorithm cohort, heterogeneity by algorithm era P = 0.006. The record's gap claim was that no one had asked how often such a revision is establishable across device-mediated RCTs, nor whether the era interaction exceeds an MCID "anywhere other than in the trial that happened to notice". Gate 4 falsified the second limb of that claim and narrowed the first (see adversarial log).

Presuppositions:
 P1 device model and enrolment window retrievable — partly true; non-naming share declared as denominator attrition (measured at 6/22 in wearables by Khattak 2024).
 P2 LOAD-BEARING, CONTESTED: non-recall firmware/calibration revision dates retrievable by third parties; BOOST-II obtained its date because the trialists were also the device investigators, which is not available retrospectively.
 P3 CONTESTED: IPD recoverable for a non-trivial subset — unquantified.
 P4 a software revision changes the RECORDED endpoint value — Gate 4 showed this is mis-stated for the anchor: BOOST-II's endpoint was death/disability, and the revision changed the titration variable, not the recorded endpoint.
 P5 an MCID exists to benchmark against — partly true; CI-half-width fallback declared.
 P6 device era not fully collinear with calendar time — must be checked per trial; NeOProM's software strata are confounded with trial identity (SUPPORT and BOOST NZ wholly original-algorithm).
 UNDECLARED AND NEWLY NAMED BY TWO ADVERSARIES: that a release date identifies a per-patient device era. It does not — fleet roll-out is asynchronous; NeOProM needed trial-internal logs and a 74-infant "mixed exposure" category.
 Not presupposed: that any revision changed any trial's conclusion outside the index case.

What would count as an answer:
A pre-registered census giving per-trial establishability with retrieval route recorded and declared a lower bound, plus era-stratified effect estimates with a pre-specified interaction test, collinearity diagnostic and MCID (or declared fallback) comparison in the recoverable subset. A null would be an equally complete answer. Not an answer: commentary that it "could" happen (Johnston 2011 already is that); a retelling of the oximeter case (BOOST-II 2013 and NeOProM 2018 already are that).

Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result):
38 web searches across 4 independent passes (Gate 2: 11; adversaries 1/2/3: 9 each), 17 fetch attempts of which 9 returned content; ~12 distinct vocabularies (own field, lay, survey methodology, laboratory metrology, device regulatory/PMA, NeOProM cross-trial, imaging scanner-upgrade, ICH-M10 bioanalysis, consumer-wearable firmware, German MDR/legal metrology, IDEAL/surgical innovation, Campbell–Stanley validity theory, misclassification theory). Full lists: batches/2026-10-16-0833/UQ-20261016-21-record.md and -adversary-1/-2/-3.md. Most informative:
 - "NeOProM Askie 2018 JAMA subgroup oximeter calibration software original vs revised" (adv 1) → OPENED PMC6583054: five-trial IPD meta-analysis; "type of oximeter software (original vs revised) were prespecified"; three trials "changed their oximeters to incorporate the revised oximeter software"; death 18–24 mo RR 1.06 (0.91–1.23) original vs 1.38 (1.14–1.68) revised, "P = .03 for interaction"; Discussion asks "whether the change in oximeter software was responsible for this result". DECISIVE.
 - "'Identifying and reporting modifications' surgical innovation systematic review IDEAL/IDEAL-D" (adv 2, adv 3) → OPENED BMJ Open 15(6):e097097: "425 modifications were reported in 76 (73.1%) studies"; hardware/technique taxonomy, no software/firmware/calibration category, no vendor or regulatory records, no outcome comparison; plus the SMART reporting tool.
 - "Khattak Woolley Collins 'Internet of Obscure Medical Things'" (adv 1, adv 3) → OPENED Keele 983776/983777 (BCS HCI 2024): "a complete absence of version reporting" (0/22); 6/22 named no model. The record's flagged unopened lead, now resolved: a reporting fraction is published; occurrence is not.
 - "'The Update Problem of Apps in Medical and Behavioral Research'" (adv 3) → OPENED Shachar et al., Ethics & Human Research 44(2), 2022: IRB-oversight treatment of the "update problem"; no frequency, no effect estimates. The record's other flagged lead; a conceptual near-prior only.
 - FDA DHT-for-remote-data-acquisition guidance (Gate 2 q5, adv 1, adv 3) → OPENED the guidance SNAPSHOT (fda.gov/media/180193): sponsors to consider the "impact of DHT updates and other changes". Full guidance never opened; stronger claims unverified.
 - Gate 2 q6/q7 (survey break-in-series; ISO 17511/JCTLM traceability) and adv 2/3 imaging and ICH-M10 passes → the mid-study instrument-change problem is mature and named in survey methodology, laboratory metrology, bioanalysis (cross-validation/bridging), imaging (scanner-change harmonisation, NeuroImage 184:555–565) and legal metrology (PTB MB06), with no RCT-corpus census in any of them.
 Ledger duplicate check: INDEX.md read in full (45 entries); nearest neighbours UQ-20261016-17, -10, -02 and UQ-20261015-19; no overlap of estimand.

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
 N1. Askie LM et al., "Association Between Oxygen Saturation Targeting and Death or Disability in Extremely Preterm Infants (NeOProM)", JAMA 2018 — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6583054 (opened by adversary 1). [Supersedes the record's N2; BOOST-II NEJM 2013, https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1302298, is the within-trial version of the same analysis.]
 N2. Bristol/IDEAL collaboration, "Identifying and reporting modifications to surgical innovation: a systematic review of IDEAL/IDEAL-D studies", BMJ Open 15(6):e097097, 2025 — https://bmjopen.bmj.com/content/15/6/e097097 (opened by adversary 2), with the SMART reporting tool.
 N3. Khattak KA, Woolley SI, Collins T, "Wearables, Healthcare-Computer Interaction and the Internet of Obscure Medical Things", BCS HCI 2024, doi 10.14236/ewic/BCSHCI2024.22 — https://keele-repository.worktribe.com/output/983777 (opened by adversary 3); protocol at protocols.io/view/version-reporting-of-wearables-in-clinical-trials-dqiw5ufe.
 Also verified and bearing on the gap: Johnston et al. 2011 (https://fn.bmj.com/content/96/6/F429, opened at Gate 2) and Shachar et al. 2022 (opened by adversary 3).

Novelty — how this differs from each:
 vs N1: limb (ii) is the SAME question with the corpus swapped. NeOProM pre-specified device-software era as a subgroup across five trials, three with mid-enrolment revisions, and published the interaction (P = .03). The candidate changes the sampling frame (all device-mediated RCTs rather than the neonatal oxygen-targeting family) and the benchmark (the trial's own MCID rather than an interaction test). It asks no question at the interface that N1 did not already pose and answer.
 vs N2: limb (i) is the SAME question with the modification type and the retrieval source swapped — firmware/calibration instead of hardware and technique, vendor and regulatory records instead of publications and protocols. The census design, the per-study modification count and the "did the study report it" axis already exist, and the community's response to the finding (build SMART) is the practice change the candidate forecasts.
 vs N3: a published reporting census over a trial corpus, swapped from wrist-worn wearables to endpoint-generating clinical devices. Occurrence versus reporting is a real difference and the record's differentiation stands on that axis alone; it does not make the question a new one.
 Residue genuinely unfound after 38 queries: the conjunction — occurrence-from-vendor-records census + MCID-benchmarked era interaction across device classes. No source asks it. Both of its limbs are, individually, an asked question with a swap.

Novelty confidence: **Medium**, restored from the record's Low on the judge's post-Gate-5 verification (2026-10-16; independent fresh-context checker, 11 queries, 0 refusals, log in batches/2026-10-16-0833/UQ-20261016-21-verification.md), and narrowed. The Low grade rested on two priors, and one of them is not what the record took it for. **BMJ Open 2025;15(6):e097097 does not ask limb (i).** It is a thematic synthesis of studies citing IDEAL/IDEAL-D (PROSPERO CRD42023427704; 104 studies, 425 modifications in 76 studies) in which the modifications counted are predominantly SURGICAL — surgical procedure 283 (66.6%), device 94 (22.1%), patient selection 48 (11.3%) — and the device modifications cover "components, number used, size, and how the device is applied", with no mention of software or firmware. Its record source is published reports and protocols only, not manufacturer, regulatory or recall records; it performs no risk-of-bias assessment and does not link modifications to effect estimates (44 studies, 42.3%, merely "described implications"). SMART is the Surgical ModificAtion Reporting Tool, a reporting checklist. **NeOProM is exactly what the record said**, and this is confirmed verbatim: oximeter software era was one of nine PRE-SPECIFIED subgroup factors, tested by a treatment × subgroup interaction term with no adjustment for multiplicity, across five trials of which three changed oximeters mid-enrolment; the interaction attaches to death by corrected age 18–24 months (original software RR 1.06, 95% CI 0.91–1.23; revised RR 1.38, 95% CI 1.14–1.68; "P = .03 for interaction subgroup difference"), not to the primary composite, for which no interaction p-value is given. BOOST II's quoted sentence is also verbatim ("There was heterogeneity for mortality between the original algorithm and the revised algorithm (P=0.006), but not for other outcomes"), with the mechanism being a calibration curve that "caused values ranging from 87 to 96% to read 1 to 2% higher". So limb (ii) IS already asked and answered for the oximeter family, and the record's claim of novelty for it is wrong and is struck. Limb (i) — how often a mid-enrolment manufacturer firmware or calibration revision can be established from manufacturer, regulatory or recall records, across device-mediated RCTs — was not found asked or answered anywhere in 11 further queries, and the nearest neighbour (the Keele wearables version-reporting work) extracts versions from ClinicalTrials.gov records, explicitly does not track change over the enrolment window, uses no manufacturer or regulatory source, and estimates no treatment effects. Medium, therefore, resting on the retrieval census and on device classes other than oximetry.
 Regraded down from the record's Medium on the adversaries' opened primaries. The record's novelty case rested on two claims: that no cross-trial reanalysis existed, and that the era interaction had been examined only in "the trial that happened to notice". N1 falsifies both. With limb (ii) asked and answered over a five-trial corpus and limb (i) asked over a 104-study corpus in another vocabulary, what remains is a corpus/instrument swap whose exact variant is unmeasured — the ledger's disguised-known case.

Significance — consequence:
 Unchanged from the record and not the ground of rejection. Yes → a SPIRIT/CONSORT device-version item (the principle already conceded for AI/ML by CONSORT-AI and DECIDE-AI), a DSMB device-change notification channel with era as a pre-specified interaction, and a device-era covariate in IPD pooling. No → the oximeter episode is bounded as a singular event rather than a general threat.

Significance — audience:
 Real and evidenced to act: reporting-guideline groups (SPIRIT/CONSORT, EQUATOR); trial statisticians and DSMB chairs in neonatology, critical care, diabetes/CGM, cardiology; FDA CDRH and EU MDCG, whose own databases the retrieval-route table would measure; Vivli/YODA; manufacturers' regulatory-affairs functions. Precedents that they act: NeOProM pre-specified software era; the IDEAL community built SMART after a modification census; FDA's DHT snapshot lists "impact of DHT updates".

Significance — fecundity:
 Notification obligations on manufacturers and their cost; whether revision direction (artefact removal vs accuracy tuning) predicts interaction direction; multi-vendor trials as a designable robustness property; how much of the device-trial replication gap is measurement-era drift; extending predetermined change-control plans from AI/ML to conventional endpoint instruments.

Significance — anchoring:
 The NeOProM oxygen-target controversy; pulse-oximeter accuracy/bias and skin-pigmentation calibration work; measurement invariance and break-in-series methods in survey research and laboratory metrology; the locked-vs-adaptive device-software regulatory debate.

Reason for silence:
 Partly stands, partly contradicted. Credible: the records asymmetry and self-sealing limb — vendor change-control records sit behind a proprietary and liability wall, and because no standard ever required version reporting the retrospective corpus is sparse by construction (Khattak: "a complete absence of version reporting"). Contradicted: the record's claim that trialists have no route to instrument-change information and that the anchor's result "was treated as a property of those trials rather than as an instance of a class". Trialists manage mid-study instrument change prospectively as routine in imaging, bioanalysis (ICH M10 cross-validation) and wearables; CONSORT-EHEALTH (2011) already asks whether an application was "frozen" during a trial; and NeOProM treated the anchor precisely as a cross-trial class instance. The silence is narrower than claimed: no one has generalised beyond oximeters and apps to endpoint instruments as a class.

Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status): **Four** fresh-context adversaries ran on this candidate. A1–A3 (the batch's three, including its automatic harder rerun) each returned **Provisional** — no Unresolved on any attack in any of them. A4 was run afterwards at the judge's direction, because the batch's rejection rate had fallen to 40% and LEDGER.md's operating rules treat a low rate as a warning that the adversaries were too gentle: it was held to the new Gate 4 standard (its own technical claims and priors cited to primary sources it opened) and also returned **Provisional** — Triviality, Combinatorial novelty and Reason for silence Resolved; Disguise, Presupposition failure, Vagueness, Significance inflation and Dissolution Partial; 21 Disguise queries, 0 refusals. Rows below are the batch's; A4's findings and the judge's corrections follow.

Adversary 3 ran 9 queries but only 6 in new vocabularies, spending 3 on the record's flagged unopened leads; that shortfall against the 8-new-vocabulary standard is noted and does not affect this verdict, which rests on priors adversaries 1 and 2 opened.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3 (Judge: significance cut from the record's 3/3 on A4's Partial. CONSORT 2025 was published with no device, software, firmware, version or calibration item at all — "software" appears in it only as "statistical code" — after the oximeter case was well known, so the guideline audience has already had the chance to act and has not; and FDA's 2023 DHT guidance §IV.H.4 already requires sponsors to log updates and compare before and after "prior to unblinding", which pre-empts the prospective half of the concern and leaves the census mattering mainly for conventional endpoint devices and the pre-2023 corpus. Against that, the same steering groups did add a version item where device-class evidence existed, in CONSORT-AI and DECIDE-AI, so the audience does act on evidence rather than on anecdote. Well-posedness stays 2/3: see the two specification gaps below.)

Strongest remaining objection:
 **Limb (ii) presupposes a mechanism that cannot operate for the commonest outcome type, and its benchmark is statistically unsound as written.** A4 worked the cases against a primary source and labelled its own arithmetic. Where the device GENERATES a continuous endpoint and the revision is an additive shift, the between-arm difference is identical in both eras — Nab et al. 2019 §2.1.2, "the difference between the two treatment groups is unbiased" — so the interaction is exactly zero and pooling eras is harmless; under a gain change the interaction is (b₁−b₀)·Δ*, which needs a near-100% gain change to reach an MCID. The index case is not an endpoint-generating device at all: BOOST II's revision changed the intervention delivered ("clearer separation between the two target groups"), i.e. a TITRATION device, a different causal structure the question conflates with endpoint generation. So the "incommensurable pooled measurements" framing must be dropped for continuous endpoints, and the mechanism survives only for titration devices and threshold-defined endpoints. Second, within a trial era is a step function of calendar time ("used for all infants who were subsequently enrolled"), so treatment × era is unidentified from treatment × period and the proposed collinearity diagnostic cannot repair it — NeOProM's own authors remain in "considerable debate" over whether the software change caused their result. Third, benchmarking an interaction POINT ESTIMATE against the MCID, when an interaction's standard error is about twice the main effect's (Brookes 2004 inflation factor 4), yields by A4's arithmetic roughly 16% false exceedances under the null at 80% main-effect power, and roughly 33% under the proposed half-CI-width fallback. Compounding all of it, limb (ii) is already published for the index device class (Askie 2018), so the candidate stands or falls on limb (i).

Provisional at: Gate 5.
 No attack reached Unresolved in any of four independent adversaries, so the fatal rule never fires, and the batch's Gate 2 rejection is withdrawn as a novelty regrade that did not survive verification. Well-posedness 2/3 caps it at Provisional independently. **What would promote it:** (i) drop limb (ii)'s claim to novelty for oximetry and cite Askie 2018 and BOOST II as prior art; (ii) partition the frame by device role — titration or intervention-defining, threshold-defined endpoint, and continuous endpoint, the last entering as a pre-registered null interaction and a calibration check rather than as a hypothesis; (iii) replace the point-estimate benchmark with an inferential rule, for example the interaction's 95% CI lying wholly above the MCID, with the expected false-positive rate stated; (iv) classify trials whose rollout was synchronous as period-confounded rather than estimable; and (v) pre-register an enquiry protocol for limb (i) — number of attempts, time limit, who is asked, how refusals are coded — because without it two investigators can reach different fractions from the same corpus with equal diligence, which is the open half of A4's Vagueness objection. With (i)–(v) and well-posedness at 3/3 this would meet the Validated bar on the present novelty and significance findings. Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): establish the retrieval yield on a small, pre-specified sample before anything else, route by route — recall and field-safety databases, manufacturer release notes, direct enquiry — because a near-zero yield is itself the finding (that regulators' databases cannot answer a question trialists need) and it decides whether limb (ii) has any corpus to run on.

Routing (if rejected as already-asked): Not applicable — not rejected. Nothing is routed. Limb (ii) for the oximeter family is asked AND answered (Askie 2018; BOOST II 2013), which the operating rules exclude from routing, and limb (i) was not found asked anywhere, so it is not an asked-but-open problem either.
