ID: UQ-20261016-32
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): Medicine — surgical pathology, cancer staging. Adjacent: registry epidemiology, measurement-error biostatistics, metrology (conformity assessment).
Question (canonical): For organ sites whose T category turns on knife-edge size thresholds, what is the distribution of specimen-handling-induced change in measured tumour size (in situ -> fresh gross -> post-fixation gross -> histologic), and what fraction of staged patients lie within that distribution's width of a threshold, so that their stage, adjuvant therapy and trial eligibility are set by specimen handling rather than by the tumour?
Alternative formulations: (i) How much of T-category assignment is produced by the specimen's journey from patient to paraffin block rather than by the tumour itself? (ii) If size were measured in situ or fresh instead of after fixation, how many patients per year would change T category, and in which direction? Gate 1 reformulation (one permitted, retained in full in the record) split the question into three limbs: (a) per-step shift distribution with observer variance components, protocol held fixed; (b) registry near-threshold probability mass with heaping modelled, as patients per year; (c) head-to-head prognostic discrimination of stage recomputed on fresh versus fixed measurements.
Motivating gap: Presupposition inversion — AJCC/UICC and CAP specify pathologic tumour size to the millimetre and hang categorical thresholds on it, though the tissue measured has been excised, deflated, fixed and sectioned, each step with documented dimensional effect, and the thresholds were calibrated on cohorts of undocumented handling. Gate 2 found the gap does not hold: the framing limb is a published paper's title in the candidate's own field and the fraction limb is a research gap stated in print. Verification overturns the first half of that and re-bases the second: P3's title is about the examination approach, not the specimen's physical state, and P2's stated gap is about terminal-digit preference, not handling. The gap as intaken therefore survives in narrowed form — the per-step dispersion is unpublished even in P1, and the near-threshold fraction is unpublished for any organ.
Presuppositions: 1. Handling changes measured size non-trivially and mostly one-signed [established by Gate 2 — Tran 2015: 4.6% fresh->fixed, 7.1% fixed->microscopic, 11.4% fresh->microscopic; the MEANS are now an input, but the adversary established that the DISPERSION is not: Tran reports P values and bare ranges (0-18.2%, 0-22.7%) with no SD, no CI and no observer-variance analysis at all, so limb (a)'s actual deliverable is unpublished even in the paper said to have executed it]. 2. Threshold crossings are consequential [established]. 3. Near-threshold size densities are retrievable from registries [established]. 4. Terminal-digit heaping is real [established: 34.8-38.7% of diameters end 0/5] but modellable well enough to recover near-threshold mass [contested, load-bearing for limb (b)]. 5. Paired multi-state measurement is feasible without compromising diagnostic material [contested; done once, n=34, one centre]. 6. Handling of the threshold-calibrating cohorts is documentable [contested, no source either way; without it "which measurement is correct" cannot close]. 7. In-situ size is the right measurand at all — the artefact may be baked into the calibration, so correcting it could degrade staging [contested; the dissolution risk, and the only limb with no located prior]. 8. [NEW, Gate 2, load-bearing] Handling-induced dimensional change is separable from grossing-protocol choice; Verbeke 2022's protocol effect (10 mm, 36%) looks larger than the fixation effect, so an unseparated design estimates a mixture. Sharpened at Gate 4: Verbeke's "microscopic corroboration" arm IS a macroscopic-versus-histologic contrast, i.e. one of the candidate's own four states, but varied jointly with plane count — so the published protocol effect sits directly on top of the candidate's gross-to-histologic step and is confounded with it in the only large study of the genre. Separability is now a design requirement, not an assumption.
What would count as an answer: (a) paired-measurement study at >=2 organ sites, protocol fixed, four handling states, reporting the per-step shift distribution with within- and between-observer components; (b) registry computation of probability mass within +/- the measured shift of each cut-point, converted to patients per year with pT handling-determined, heaping modelled; (c) pre-set-margin comparison of prognostic discrimination for stage on fresh versus fixed measurements in an outcome cohort. A small shift relative to threshold spacing, or unchanged discrimination, retires the concern and is equally an answer.
Novelty — queries run (query -> one-line result): 11 distinct web searches (above the 8 minimum) plus 7 WebFetch calls, 4 of which failed on access controls; full list in batches/2026-10-16-1233/UQ-20261016-32-record.md. Most informative: (10) "measurement uncertainty tumour size risk of pT category misclassification staging threshold guard band pathology" -> decisive, surfaced P3, whose title is the candidate's own alternative formulation; (4) "breast cancer tumour diameter measurement error understaging proportion near 20 mm pT1 pT2 threshold" -> the mandatory fraction-already-computed query, no breast near-threshold mass found; (3) heaping/digit-preference query -> P2; (6) cut-point misclassification in epidemiology -> mature named family, limb (c) machinery already standard there; (8) ISO 14253 guard-banding -> metrology owns limb (b)'s structure, no staging application found; (11) shrinkage-corrected size prognostic validation -> pure vocabulary collision with therapy-response "tumour shrinkage". Negatives are "not found", not "absent": no indexed bibliographic (MeSH) search was possible and Kain et al. 2025 (his.15529) was unreadable behind reCAPTCHA, so it is cited but not graded on.
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources): P1 Tran et al., J Cancer 2015;6(8):759-766, doi 10.7150/jca.12094 — n=34 nephrectomies, maximum diameter in four states (radiologic, fresh, fixed, microscopic), fresh as reference, estimand per-step relative change plus correction factors; 2/34 would cross pT1a/pT1b. P2 Tsuruda et al., Acta Oncologica 2020;59(3):260-267, doi 10.1080/0284186X.2019.1669817 — national breast cases (n=13,541 histopathologic), terminal-digit distribution and paired mammographic-minus-histopathologic difference (+1.26 mm, ICC 0.52), histopathologic as reference; states the extent of consequent under-staging remains to be examined. P3 Verbeke, Cancers 2022;14(10):2471, doi 10.3390/cancers14102471 — n=315 pancreatic resections, size and 8th-edition T category under four examination approaches, within-case paired contrast, estimand the fraction changing T category: 142/315 = 45%.
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs P1 — P1 *is* limb (a), executed, at one site, on the same four-state chain; the candidate's increments are design increments (multi-site, pre-registered, variance components rather than means), and P1 even contains a miniature limb (b). vs P2 — P2 establishes presupposition 4 at national scale and then poses limb (b) as its own closing research gap; limb (b) differs in execution but not in having been asked. vs P3 — P3's title paraphrases the candidate's alternative formulation and its endpoint is limb (b)'s endpoint, with the number published; the real difference is the artefact (physical state of the specimen versus grossing protocol, i.e. object measured versus method of measuring), which makes the candidate a sibling study of a published one rather than an un-asked question, and on the published effect sizes the candidate's artefact is the smaller of the two. Surviving residue: limb (c) alone, recorded as not-found rather than absent, since the method-owning field (misclassified discretized covariates in survival models) has standard machinery for it. CORRECTED after verification and Gate 4: the residue is larger than one limb. P3 varies the examination protocol on already-fixed specimens and reports no near-threshold fraction, so it is a sibling aimed at an adjacent object rather than this question published; P1 executes the chain but in one organ, n=34, one surgeon, tumours 5.5 cm or smaller, from a preoperative radiologic rather than an in-situ first state, and publishes no dispersion; and P2's printed gap is about digit preference. What survives unpublished is the shift distribution's width with variance components, the near-threshold fraction for any organ, and limb (c). What the candidate loses instead is methodological novelty: the estimator is named and institutionalised in laboratory medicine as the incremental reclassification rate (Farrell et al. 2026) and in psychometrics as classification accuracy and consistency at cut scores.
Novelty confidence: Medium (Gate 2 graded Low on a ground verification withdrew; re-graded by the late adversary at Medium, which the judge adopts)
Grounds: no publication found states the per-step shift's dispersion with variance components, or the fraction of staged patients within that dispersion of a threshold, for any organ. Not High for two reasons, both sourced: the estimator is a mature named quantity in two sibling fields with published acceptability bands, so only the input and the reference are new; and PMID 29580861, "Breslow thickness measurements of melanomas around AJCC staging cut-off points", pairs imprecision with terminal-digit bias for melanoma and could not be read, so the nearest possible neighbour is uncharacterised. Medium novelty with a close neighbour is the Provisional definition.
Significance — consequence: If the shift is large relative to threshold spacing and discrimination improves on fresh measurements, CAP/AJCC would need a specified measurand state and possibly correction factors, and registry stage distributions become partly an artefact of local practice; if small, the concern retires with a bounded null. Discounted: P3 already published the consequential version for pancreas (45%) and the manuals did not change. Qualified at Gate 4: P3's exposure is a grossing protocol, so acting on it meant mandating a labour-intensive examination method, whereas acting on this finding means specifying the measurand state in a protocol that already specifies source priority — and the sibling field publishes numeric acceptability bands for the same statistic.
Significance — audience: Real and standing — CAP Cancer Protocol committees, AJCC/UICC TNM panels, ICCR dataset authors, NAACCR/SEER standard-setters, and the pancreas and oral-cavity communities already arguing about measurement rules.
Significance — fecundity: Guard-banded staging (reported pT plus stated conformity risk, ISO 14253 terms); measurand definition for every quantitative CAP item carrying a threshold (DOI, margin distance, Ki67); joint threshold recalibration against a specified measurand rather than an inherited one.
Significance — anchoring: Stage migration and the Will Rogers phenomenon; radiology-pathology size discordance; gross-pathology interobserver reproducibility; terminal-digit preference as a registry data-quality defect; measurement uncertainty in laboratory reporting.
Reason for silence: The proposed mechanisms (vocabulary collision, since "tumour shrinkage" means therapy response; and a four-way split between metrology, epidemiology, pathology and registries with nobody owning the composite) are partly dissolved by Gate 2: there was no silence in the candidate's own field, only a thin per-organ literature without synthesis. The honest residual mechanism covers limb (c) only — no single group owns both handling-controlled measurements and long-term outcomes, and the answer could invalidate the measurement its own field reports. Gate 4 added a second mechanism that is better than either, and sourced: a reporting-convention gap. The papers that measured the shift never published the statistic the question needs, because their purpose made it irrelevant — Tran's stated goal is a correction factor "toward standardization of pathological reporting", and a correction factor needs a central estimate where a misclassification risk needs a variance. The field produced the former for a decade and therefore never produced the input the latter requires, and no systematic review that would have pooled the per-organ studies and exposed the omission was found.
Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status): Gate 4 RAN LATE AND SEPARATELY. The batch killed this candidate at Gate 2 and spawned no adversary; when verification withdrew that ground, one fresh-context adversary was given the Gate 0-3 record alone — told the record's Gate 2 and 3 conclusions were a prior finding and not a verdict to inherit — and ran all eight attacks from scratch at the strict standard: 12 searches (cap 12), 5 fetches (cap 5), no overrun, no refusals. Verbatim log at UQ-20261016-32-adversary-1.md. Attack 2 was executed in eight vocabularies neither Gate 2 nor the record had tried, so Disguise is verified rather than unverified.

The quantity asked for is the WIDTH of the shift distribution and it is not in the literature: Tran 2015 reports means with P values and bare ranges (0-18.2%, 0-22.7%), no SD, no CI and no inter- or intra-observer analysis at all, so the variance decomposition cannot be assembled from published numbers. Gate 4 completeness: all eight attacks executed by one adversary at the strict standard, with the Disguise sweep run in eight untried vocabularies. Three Resolved, five Partial, nothing Unresolved, so no fatal objection stands. One item the adversary could not read is recorded as could-not-read rather than absent, and it is the same one the record named: Kain et al., Histopathology 2025, doi 10.1111/his.15529 (PMC12614666) again returned a reCAPTCHA page, so nothing is asserted about it and no attack is graded on it. One partial retrieval: the MDPI page for Verbeke 2022 served abstract, figure legends and tables but not Methods, so the adversary can confirm from the published abstract, figures and tables that specimen physical state is not an exposure, but cannot confirm in the authors' own words that all arms used the same fixed specimens. The adversary recommended Provisional, and with one adversary rather than two the entry could not be Validated on this record in any case.
Verification by the run session (the Gate 2 kill rested on three named priors and no adversary had run, so all three were checked against the papers; independent fresh-context checker, 11 searches and 6 fetches with the fetch budget exhausted, no refusals; full log in batches/2026-10-16-1233/UQ-20261016-32-verification.md). Every number survives; every characterisation needed correcting, and the decisive one is refuted.
(i) P3 REFUTED as the candidate's question already executed. Verbeke's figures are exact — "T-stage assignment differed in 142 (45%) cases between the simple and comprehensive approach", mean absolute size difference 10 mm, mean relative change 36%, 315 cases, 231 head and 84 body/tail, with intermediate contrasts of 57 (18%) and 115 (37%) — but what it varies is the measurement *approach*, not the specimen's physical state: "Compared to the most simple approach (macroscopic measurement in one plane), the comprehensive approach (macroscopic measurement in two planes with microscopic corroboration) resulted in a larger tumour size in 263 (83%) cases", both arms applied to the same already-fixed specimens. Timing is held constant by design, not varied — "As specimen grossing is usually undertaken following fixation" — and the paper uses that to argue formalin shrinkage does not drive its findings; axial slicing versus bivalving appears only as a limitation, never as a compared arm. So P3 is on the other side of the very distinction the record itself added as presupposition 8, it is one organ, and it reports no fraction-near-threshold statistic at all. The claim that the candidate's "headline quantity was computed and published four years ago" does not hold: 45% is a protocol-change fraction, not near-threshold mass under a handling shift.
(ii) P1 CONFIRMED but narrower than described. Tran et al. 2015 does execute a four-state chain with all the quoted numbers (radiologic 12.1% larger than fresh, fresh to fixed -4.6%, fixed to microscopic -7.1%, fresh to microscopic -11.4%, all P<0.01; mean diameters 3.0 / 2.7 / 2.5 / 2.3 cm; conversion factors 1.05, 1.08, 1.13; "Two of our cases would receive a different pT1 classification depending on which measurement was used for staging", 2/34, no CI). But it is renal, n = 34, one surgeon, prospective, and restricted to tumours grossly 5.5 cm or smaller — and its first state is *preoperative* CT/MRI reviewed retrospectively about 2.4 months before surgery, not an in-situ or intraoperative measurement. The chain it executes is radiologic to fresh gross to post-fixation gross to microscopic, which is not the candidate's in-situ-anchored chain.
(iii) P2's quotation CORRECTED and its referent is a different error source. The citation is right, but "remains to be examined" does not appear in the paper; the sentence is "Further studies are needed to investigate the potential extent of under-staging and under-treatment resulting from this measurement error." And "this measurement error" is terminal-digit preference — rounding to 0 or 5 — together with mammographic-versus-histopathologic disagreement, not specimen handling and not fixation (n = 7,792 mammographic and 13,541 histopathologic diameters, 6,865 with both; digit 0 or 5 in 38.7% and 34.8%; ICC 0.52; mammographic mean 1.26 mm larger, the difference growing with size). A registry-limb gap is therefore genuinely posed in print and still open, but about digit preference, and not in the words the record attributed to it.
(iv) The candidate's own limb (b) — distribution width, then the fraction of patients inside that width of a threshold — is NOT FOUND published for any organ. One plausibly closer item could not be read and must be cleared before novelty is graded again: PMID 29580861, "Breslow thickness measurements of melanomas around AJCC staging cut-off points", which pairs imprecision with terminal-digit bias for melanoma and whose PubMed page returned an empty body. A second, the Ewha/Yonsei "Effect of formalin fixation and tumour size in small-sized non-small-cell lung cancer", is also unread. Both are could-not-read, not absent.
Consequence for the Gate 2 verdict: the Low grade rested on the framing limb being a published paper's title in the candidate's own field and the fraction limb being a stated research gap. The first half is refuted — Verbeke is a different axis — and the second half stands but about a different error source, so the ground does not carry a Rejection. Gate 4 therefore ran late and separately, as LEDGER.md requires of a withdrawn Gate 2 ground, and all eight attacks were run from scratch against the Gate 0-3 record by one fresh-context adversary.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3
Well-posedness: the Gate 1 reformulation fixes three limbs, the comparator states, the registry conversion to patients per year and the null that retires the concern — but the window is still "+/- the step shift" with no quantile named, which the adversary confirmed as a live defect even while showing it is nearly inert at the 20 mm cut-point; and presupposition 6, which limb (c)'s comparator depends on, has no source either way. 2/3, and that alone bars Validated.
Significance: argued from documented artefacts and now from a sibling field that has institutionalised the action (Farrell et al.'s fitness-for-purpose bands for an incremental reclassification rate), against the Verbeke precedent that a 45% effect changed no manual. 2/3: the audience is real and operates at this granularity, but whether a pT threshold crossing still changes an adjuvant-therapy recommendation at the named sites could not be evidenced either way within budget.
Strongest remaining objection: Disguise by transposition. The candidate's computational core is a mature, named, already-institutionalised quantity in a field with the same structure — laboratory medicine computes the fraction of a real national population reclassified across a clinical decision limit under a measurement procedure's uncertainty, calls it the incremental reclassification rate, benchmarks it against the procedure the limit was derived on, and has published fitness-for-purpose bands for it (Farrell et al. 2026, doi 10.1515/cclm-2026-0259, abstract opened: optimal <1.5%, desirable <3.0%, minimal <4.7%, with a worked failure at 8.62%); educational measurement has computed classification accuracy and consistency at cut scores as routine software output for years. Once that is on the table, the candidate is one unpublished input (the variance of the handling shift, which the correction-factor literature never reported because correction factors do not need it) plus one measurand-definition choice that both sibling fields dispose of by naming a privileged reference procedure — a reference the candidate cannot yet name, because whether the threshold-calibration cohorts' handling is documentable (presupposition 6) is unchecked. That does not kill it: supplying an unpublished input to a known estimator in a domain where nobody has supplied it, and where registry rules demonstrably specify every measurand dimension except the one at issue, is legitimate and consequential. But it bounds the claim, and the honest form of the question must say so. The earlier objection — that the question was asked in its own field in its own words and its headline quantity published four years ago — is withdrawn: Verbeke varies the examination protocol on already-fixed specimens and reports no near-threshold fraction.
Promotion requires: (i) pre-specifying the window quantile, so that "within the distribution's width" names +/-1 SD, +/-2 SD or a stated interval rather than leaving it to the analyst — this is the well-posedness defect and it is free to fix; (ii) probing presupposition 6 first and cheaply, by establishing whether even one threshold's calibration cohort has documentable specimen handling, since limb (c) has no comparator without it and the question collapses to convention-setting if it is undocumentable; (iii) reading PMID 29580861 and the Ewha/Yonsei lung-fixation study, either of which could close limb (b) for one organ; (iv) restating limb (b) explicitly as a transposition of the incremental-reclassification-rate framework rather than as a new estimator, which shrinks the claim and strengthens it; (v) making variance components, not correction factors, the primary output of limb (a), and holding the grossing protocol fixed by design so the gross-to-histologic step is separated from plane count; (vi) evidencing from a guideline source that a pT size-threshold crossing still changes an adjuvant-therapy recommendation at the named sites. With (i) and (ii) settled and a second adversary run, this could be Validated.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): settle presupposition 6 before anything is measured — find one organ site whose size threshold's calibration cohort has documentable specimen handling, since that single fact decides whether limb (c) has a comparator or the question is convention-setting. Alongside it, an indexed bibliographic search (MeSH, field-restricted), which this run could not run and which is exactly what overturns a null on a prognostic-discrimination phrasing, and reads of Kain et al. 2025 (doi 10.1111/his.15529) and PMID 29580861, the two nearest unread items. Hold the grossing protocol fixed by design, since P3's protocol effect would otherwise swamp the handling effect.
Routing: the entry is Provisional, so none of the candidate's own limbs is routed — the routing file carries problems the ledger found posed in print and still open, and a Provisional candidate is one the ledger is still claiming as un-asked. One row goes in all the same, and it is NOT this candidate's question: Tsuruda et al. 2020 pose, in print and in their own terms, the extent of under-staging and under-treatment resulting from TERMINAL-DIGIT PREFERENCE in reported breast tumour diameter — "Further studies are needed to investigate the potential extent of under-staging and under-treatment resulting from this measurement error." — and defer it. That is a different error source from the specimen-handling chain this candidate asks about, so the two do not collide, and it is routed on Tsuruda's terms with the batch report saying plainly where it came from. The batch's own draft row, which attributed the handling-chain version to Tsuruda on a quotation the paper does not contain, is withdrawn. ID: UQ-20261016-33
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): Medicine — hospital pharmacy / patient safety / drug-diversion surveillance; method from nuclear-safeguards material-balance accountancy (metrology, statistics). Source method: cross-field transplant.

Question (canonical): Computed with safeguards material-balance discipline — an inventory-difference statistic, a propagated measurement-and-documentation variance, and a stated detection probability at a stated false-alarm rate — what is the smallest sustained controlled-substance diversion rate a hospital's reconciliation and analytics can detect per dispensing unit per month, and how does that minimum detectable rate compare with quantities in adjudicated diversion cases?
Question (Gate 1 reformulation, one reformulation used, both versions on the record): For a named ADC-served unit and drug-formulation class, with ID = (beginning inventory + receipts) − (recorded administered + documented waste + returns + ending inventory) and a propagated sigma_ID in which every term is declared either a measured variance or an interval bound (witnessed waste unmeasured by construction), what is the smallest sustained monthly removal M at which each of three named tests — (a) the unit's current discrepancy-review practice, (b) a reproducible vendor alarm rule, (c) a safeguards-style sequential test on cumulative ID (CUMUF/Page-type) — attains Pd = 95% at Pfa = 1 per unit-year; and how does M compare with per-month rates reconstructed from adjudicated cases? (Reformulated because the intake version fixed no test, no (Pd, Pfa) pair and no units.)

Alternative formulations:
- What is the detection limit of hospital drug-diversion surveillance, stated as the smallest diversion detectable at a fixed false-alarm rate, rather than as a classifier's performance on cases already found?
- Can an inventory-difference statistic and its sigma, as used for nuclear material accountancy, be computed for a hospital opioid inventory — and what does it imply about how much can be removed without the accounts noticing?

Motivating gap: Published and marketed diversion detection is classifier performance against already-identified cases. The AJHP 2022 ML study reports 96.6% sensitivity and a 160-day mean earlier-detection gain on 22 known incidents — all of them nursing staff, and the sensitivity measured against 98th-percentile heuristic labels rather than confirmed diversion — and states "Fourth, we tested sensitivity, not specificity"; it reports no alert rate, no diverted quantities and no Pd as a function of quantity. The only published "how much is missed" figures are executive opinion surveys. Hospitals are legally required to keep these accounts with no detection performance specified for them. The interface is not decorative: safeguards assumes bulk material with quantified instrument uncertainty, whereas the hospital balance's dominant error term is documentation error of unknown distribution under partial adversarial control (Epstein 2016: reconciliation error 15.8% baseline, 8.8% -> 5.2%; "Most reconciliation errors are clerical").

Presuppositions: (1) [established at many sites] per-transaction, per-user ADC/administration/waste records are retrievable. (2) [contested — principal feasibility risk] per-month quantities are recoverable for some adjudicated cases (public-record magnitudes exist — a DEA probe's "21 gallons" of missing fentanyl solution, a DOJ/DEA settlement — but neither adversary verified a per-month rate). (3) [contested] administered amounts carry a quantifiable uncertainty; witnessed waste is attestation only, so may enter as a bound not a variance. (4) [contested] a sustained-rate estimand is the right one; burst diversion needs a different statistic. (5) [flagged] safeguards' independence/known-variance assumptions need not hold if the result is a conservative bound. (6) [contested — significance limb] someone would act on a published detection limit. (7) [established] records are partly controlled by the person the statistic is meant to detect. (8) [flagged] a non-degenerate answer exists; "no finite detection limit at the stated Pfa" is pre-declared an admissible, policy-relevant answer. Adversary 2 verified (3) and (7) rather than refuting them: Fan 2019 names "falsifying drug amounts administered or wasted" as an active concealment mode.

What would count as an answer: a computation on real records from at least two institutions giving (i) a term-by-term uncertainty budget separating measured from attested quantities and naming which terms are bounds; (ii) an OC curve — Pd against sustained removal rate at fixed Pfa — for current practice, a reproducible vendor rule, and a safeguards-style sequential test; (iii) that curve placed against per-month adjudicated-case quantities. A demonstration that the attested outflow fraction makes sigma_ID unboundable below some large M is admissible and informative.

Novelty — how this differs from each: vs P1 — same data substrate, opposite direction of inference: P1's estimand is lead time on cases already identified by other means and it has no magnitude axis, so it cannot be placed against adjudicated quantities and cannot bound what is missed (its own limitation: "we tested sensitivity, not specificity"); the candidate's estimand is removal magnitude at a stated Pd and Pfa per unit-month. vs P2 — closest own-field paper and it measures exactly the error term the candidate needs, but its endpoint is documentation discrepancy, not diversion, and its estimand is a before/after change; it forms no inventory difference, propagates no variance, separates no measured from attested terms, computes no detection probability. It is an input to the uncertainty budget, not an answer. vs P3 — unresolved: a validation study is precisely where an alert rate or per-provider detection threshold would live, and neither adversary could read it, so the difference cannot be stated. This is the reason novelty is not promoted.

Novelty confidence: Medium
Grounds: no document in the target field or in nine neighbouring vocabularies (safeguards, auditing, retail loss prevention, UST/pipeline leak detection, SPC, epidemiological capture-recapture, cannabis custody, German BtMVV, defence/police custody) states a minimum detectable diversion rate at a fixed false-alarm rate for hospital controlled-substance accounts; Fan 2019 is field-level evidence that safeguard performance of any kind is unmeasured. Not High for two reasons: P3 is uncharacterised, and the qualitative sign of the answer is already settled inside the method-owning field (safeguards concluded material balance alone cannot meet detection goals at high throughput), so what is new is the question and the quantitative comparison, not the sign.
Asked-but-open status: the strict formulation was not found asked. The adjacent weaker question ("does most diversion go undetected, and how much?") is asked in trade/vendor literature and answered only by belief elicitation — a perception estimand, not this one. Not routed.

Significance — consequence: forces a binary policy conclusion currently undecided by evidence. If the minimum detectable sustained rate for a ward-month exceeds the per-month rate in most adjudicated cases, the legally mandated accounting is a formality with respect to its nominal threat and improvement must come from containment-and-surveillance analogues (blinded counts at randomised cadence, assayed waste sampling, two-person unobservable-step removal) rather than more analytics on the same records, and procurement claims of effective AI detection become unsupportable without a stated Pfa. If it does not, the recurring multi-year undetected cases are organizational failures and the remedy is staffing and workflow, with the detection limit available as an accreditation metric.
Significance — audience: (i) hospital diversion-prevention programmes and pharmacy directors choosing between analytics subscriptions and physical controls with no comparable number for either; (ii) ASHP and diversion-prevention guideline writers, who could specify a target detection limit rather than a practice list; (iii) accreditors and state boards, who audit process compliance with no performance standard — precedent verified in another custody domain (EPA UST SIR: 95% Pd at 5% Pfa for a stated rate); (iv) DEA registrants and plaintiffs' counsel, for whom a published limit is evidence about what an institution could have known; (v) vendors and purchasers of diversion analytics, who would acquire a figure of merit. Both adversaries left this Partial: the audience exists, willingness to act is unevidenced, and Fan 2019's "paucity of controlled trials" is revealed preference against it.
Significance — fecundity: makes askable the safeguards inspection-goal problem for pharmacy (what count cadence, blinded-recount fraction, waste-assay rate and stratification depth meet a target limit at acceptable alarm load); poses the adversarial-attestation partial-identification problem general to any audited account with self-reported consumption (laboratory and veterinary controlled substances, cannabis seed-to-sale, precursor declarations); makes the burst-versus-sustained regime measurable; invites a waste-assay validation experiment that would convert the largest bound into a variance.
Significance — anchoring: the published anomaly that 5-16% of reconciliations are erroneous while diversion is nonetheless said to be caught by these records; the gap between vendor sensitivity claims and P1's untested specificity; repeated accidental discovery of multi-year diversions; and the transferable safeguards finding that material balance alone was inadequate at scale.

Reason for silence: (1) disciplinary boundary with an asymmetry — method owners (safeguards statisticians, metrologists, auditors) have no access to cabinet logs; data owners (pharmacy, nursing, compliance) are not trained in detection-limit formalism, and neither side's indexing terms reach the other. Both adversaries dented this: the computation needs ordinary power/OC statistics, and the data-owning corpus is quantitatively sophisticated, so the boundary does not explain silence inside that corpus. (2) incentive and liability gap — an OC curve is adverse discoverable evidence for a hospital and names what a product misses for a vendor, while recordkeeping is mandated in detail with no performance specified, so the first mover bears the whole cost. No source showing publication was deterred. (3) no sanctioned object to compute, because an outflow term is an attestation rather than a measurement. Dented by adversary 2: cannabis jurisdictions publish inventory-variance reporting thresholds and DLA publishes record-accuracy goals — tolerances, not (Pd, Pfa) specifications, so the claim survives as stated but weakened. Adversary 1's alternative, "considered and set aside" by the Epstein/Dexter group after finding usage and wastage aggregates unlinked to diversion, is inferred from a two-index-case study via a 2023 review, not stated anywhere.

Verification by the run session (the two load-bearing claims of the Triviality kill were checked against primary sources, because neither adversary opened a safeguards text; independent fresh-context checker, 14 searches and 6 fetches, no refusals, one hard fetch failure; full log in batches/2026-10-16-1233/UQ-20261016-33-verification.md). The kill's algebra survives; its characterisation of the method-owning field does not.
(i) CONFIRMED. On the Gate 1 identity a removal concealed inside documented waste or charted administration leaves every term satisfied, so E[ID] = 0, Pd = Pfa at every M, and the declaration-only balance has no minimum detectable rate; Fan 2019's verbatim naming of falsified administered and wasted amounts makes that path real rather than hypothetical.
(ii) CORRECTED, and this is the load-bearing error. A safeguards-style material-balance test is not the balance standing alone. Burr T, Bonner E, Michalak S, Norman C, "An Overview of Statistical Methods used in Nuclear Safeguards" (JSM proceedings 2019, pp. 553-579, read at https://ww2.amstat.org/meetings/proceedings/2019/data/assets/pdf/1199480.pdf) states that "the material balance (MB) is defined as MB = Ibegin + Tin - Tout - Iend", that "these paired data are declarations usually based on measurements by the operator", that falsification "would cause a mean shift between the operator declaration and the corresponding inspector measurement", and that "the D statistic and the one-item-at-a-time tests rely on estimates of operator and inspector measurement error RSDs". Safeguards' answer to exactly this candidate's problem is therefore an independent inspector verification measurement — the MUF+D structure — which the candidate's identity does not contain. So the kill does not void the question, it redirects it: the declaration-only branch has no finite limit, which is the degenerate outcome presupposition 8 pre-declares admissible, and the non-degenerate branch is a verification-augmented balance in which an assay's measurement uncertainty and a verification sampling fraction enter sigma_ID and set a finite limit. The candidate does not say which branch it means; that is added to the promotion conditions below. In the hospital case the inflow side is already instrumented (ADC dispense events, receipts, counts are machine records) and the outflow side is declaration only, so the asymmetry the record locates is real; a verification counterpart for the outflow side exists as an active engineering target (syringe-residual assay, returned-PCA-bag verification) but the checker found only a capstone title and opened no peer-reviewed study of its detection performance, so it is located, not quantified.
(iii) A second obstacle from the same primary, absent from the whole record and arguably more informative than the identity argument: "It is important to recognize that large throughput facilities cannot typically achieve DP >= 0.95", against a stated goal of DP >= 0.95 at a significant quantity of 8 kg Pu. What defeats these tests in the method-owning field is the throughput-to-variance ratio, not the accounting identity — and a dispensing unit is a very high-throughput, high-relative-variance facility. This strengthens the anchoring argument and makes the degenerate answer the prior expectation rather than a surprise.
(iv) P1 corrected against the paper. Knight 2022's timing figures are mean 160 days, median 74, range 7-579, with no confidence intervals; all 22 blinded cases are nursing staff; and the 96.3% accuracy / 95.9% specificity / 96.6% sensitivity triple belongs to the development sample, whose labels came from a 98th-percentile heuristic rather than confirmed diversion outcomes. It is therefore not a specificity against true diversion, and adversary 2's correction to the record needs that qualifier. The paper's own forward-looking sentence is "measure specificity in order to develop analytics that will yield fewer alerts".
(v) The record's universal negative does not hold as written. Vovanese et al. 2018 reports an ROC area, a sensitivity and a qualitative "low false positive rate", so what survives is the narrow claim that nothing opened reports a detection probability as a function of removal magnitude or a specificity measured against confirmed diversion. Three sets of documents remain unread and must be cleared before that narrow claim is relied on: Epstein/Gratch/McNulty/Grunwald, Anesth Analg 2011;113(1):160-4 (highest risk, still metadata-only after a second attempt), the Bluesight Diversion Trends Reports for 2024 and 2025, and the six named US diversion-detection patents.
(vi) The candidate question is NOT FOUND posed in print in either vocabulary — searches for the explicit analogy ("inventory difference", "material balance", MUF applied to hospital controlled substances) returned only ordinary-sense "safeguards" pharmacy literature and unrelated NRC/INMM material. Kept distinct from (v): the question is not found; two named documents could not be read.

Scores: Well-posedness 3/3 · Significance 2/3
Well-posedness: after the Gate 1 reformulation the estimand, accounting identity, unit, test set and (Pd, Pfa) pair are fixed and both outcomes — a finite limit, or a demonstration that the attested term makes it unbounded — are pre-declared admissible, so it cannot be answered either way regardless of evidence. Held at 3/3 rather than reduced because adversary 2's objection is that the answer is a family indexed by concealment path, not that the question lacks an answer; conditioning on path is a sharpening, and it is listed below as a promotion condition.
Significance: argued from documented artefacts (P1's specificity admission, 5-16% reconciliation error, belief-survey-only state of the "how much is missed" question, a verified regulatory precedent for the same performance statement in another custody domain), with concrete fecundity. Not 3/3: presupposition 6 is contested, Fan 2019's "paucity of controlled trials" is revealed preference against the audience acting, and no body has authority to turn a detection limit into a requirement.

Strongest remaining objection: Triviality by degeneracy — on the candidate's own accounting identity, a removal concealed as documented waste or charted administration satisfies every term, so the material-balance test has Pd = Pfa at every magnitude and there is no finite minimum detectable rate on the concealment path that Fan 2019 documents as real; what is left non-degenerate is per-user feature discrimination, which is the field's existing ROC question rather than a material-balance one. Both adversaries left this Partial only because the empirical leg (that quantity aggregates carry no diversion signal) could be sourced only through a 2023 review's summary of a two-index-case 2007 paper; adversary 1 states explicitly that a primary read confirming it moves Triviality to Unresolved and the entry to Rejected. Verification did not clear that leg — Epstein 2011 is still metadata-only after a second independent attempt — and it added a second, sourced ground for the same objection: the method-owning field's own precedent that high-throughput facilities cannot typically reach DP = 0.95.
Promotion requires: (i) opening Epstein/Gratch/McNulty/Grunwald, Anesth Analg 2011 (and Epstein 2007) as primaries and characterising unit, endpoint, comparator and estimand — promotion only if they state no alert rate, per-provider detection threshold or quantity-versus-detection relation; if they confirm that quantity aggregates do not separate diverters, this is Rejected at Gate 4 (Triviality), not promoted; (ii) restating the estimand conditioned on concealment path, so M has a single value per path and attack 5 resolves; (iii) re-opening Epstein 2016 to put measured numbers behind sigma_ID, and verifying one adjudicated case's per-month rate so presupposition 2 stops being contested. (iv) saying which branch of the balance the estimand means — declaration-only, whose answer is now known in advance to be degenerate, or verification-augmented with an assay-sampled outflow term, which is the branch that can have a finite limit. (iv) is the cheapest of the four and the one that decides whether the question has a single answer. With (i)-(iv) done and Triviality and Disguise Resolved, novelty would stand at Medium-to-High with a characterised nearest neighbour and the entry could be Validated.

Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): before any OC curve, obtain one site's twelve-month ADC transaction, administration and waste-attestation extract for a single formulation class and write the term-by-term uncertainty budget, declaring for each term whether it is a measured variance or a bound, stratified by concealment path. The budget decides whether the question has a finite answer at all.

Routing (if rejected as already-asked): Not rejected; nothing routed. Recorded for completeness: the adjacent weaker question ("what fraction of hospital diversion goes undetected?") is asked in trade and vendor literature and answered only by executive belief surveys — a different (perception) estimand, so it is not routed as this candidate's open problem.

ID: UQ-20261016-34
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): Biology — connectomics / systems neuroscience (EM reconstruction metrology)
Question (canonical): In a dense whole-brain connectome whose two hemispheres were reconstructed from a single image volume, how large must a difference in a cell-type-to-cell-type connection weight be before it exceeds the reconstruction-and-proofreading noise floor — i.e. what is the detection limit for any connectome-to-connectome comparison, measured by independent re-reconstruction of the same volume? (Gate 1 reformulation used for Gates 2–3 demotes "independent re-reconstruction" from the question to one candidate estimator, and adds stratification by edge weight, cell type, neurite length and proofreading effort; both versions in the record.)
Alternative formulations: What is the smallest circuit difference a connectome can resolve? · Of the left–right difference in connection weights inside a single fly brain, how much is the pipeline and how much is the animal?
Motivating gap: Claimed at intake that whole-brain connectomes are compared across hemispheres, individuals and sexes with no error model saying which differences are resolvable, and that "the detection limit has not been stated as a number." Gate 2 found every clause contradicted by the flagship papers of the named instrument: the error model, the pipeline/biology decomposition and the number (±30% in edge weight) all exist and are already used to filter between-connectome biological claims. Verification and the late Gate 4 both narrow that: the number exists and is in use, but it is a do-not-interpret-below floor derived from a forward uncertainty budget — not a detection limit at a stated confidence, and not measured by any independent re-reconstruction. On the adversary's arithmetic over two of the paper's own sentences, a 30% band would pass roughly a quarter of pure-noise comparisons at a 30-synapse edge. So the clause that falls is "no error model exists"; the clause that survives is that the limit in use is undocumented, borrowed across volumes, and patched by hand curation.
Presuppositions: (1) two hemispheres from one volume/pipeline, cell-type matchable — established; (2) genuinely independent re-reconstruction achievable, "independent" needs operationalising — contested, unmet by any opened source; (3) true left–right biological variation neither zero nor swamping — established with a number (65% of observed left–right edge-weight variability inside the technical-noise range); (4) per-edge proofreading status/effort retrievable — partly (completion rate is the published proxy, region-specific: mushroom body 46% FlyWire-right vs 77% hemibrain; per-neuron effort unpublished); (5) floor transfers to mouse scale — contested and explicitly denied by the source ("made specifically for the two hemispheres of FlyWire"); (6) THE STAKE: between-connectome differences are used to support biological claims that would need qualifying if below the floor — FALSE as stated, and restated at Gate 4: the 2025 male-CNS connectome already filters dimorphism claims by per-dataset noise thresholds and reports a lower bound, so the stake is not "claims are unfiltered" but "the filters in use differ by about 1.4x between datasets with no stated derivation, and expert curation was required to separate biological signal from cases of technical noise"; (7) synapse count is the right weight unit — flagged, untouched by any opened source; (8) [NEW at the late Gate 4, load-bearing and adverse] that a second pass over the same voxels can measure the dominant error term — CONTESTED and probably false: reconstruction errors are made at image defects (folds, lost sections, poor staining), so any re-reconstruction of the same volume inherits them and fails in the same places, and the male-CNS paper states that technical noise "is more commonly correlated across both sides of one brain" and that "most apparent differences in male-female connectivity were explained by segmentation issues". The candidate's estimator therefore captures the operator-plus-algorithm component and silently sets the common-mode term to zero.
What would count as an answer: (i) edge-weight agreement from an independent re-reconstruction, stratified by weight, cell type, neurite length and effort — partly met by the wrong route (agreement vs weight published: >10-synapse edges reproducible >90%; edges >1.1% of target-type input persist >90%; noise approaches 100% for weak edges — all from a forward noise model, not a second reconstruction, and not stratified by type/length/effort); (ii) decomposition of the within-animal left–right discrepancy — met (65% technical, residual framed as a lower bound on biology; R = 0.96; edge persistence 57%/59%); (iii) a stated minimum resolvable difference at stated confidence — met ("differences in edge weights of +/-30% or less may be entirely due to technical noise and should not be over-interpreted", with a 5–95% envelope and a >40-synapse / 3%-weight strong-edge regime). The significance-settling step (apply the floor to claims in print) is met and already executed.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 11 queries, 5 fetches; full list in batches/2026-10-16-1233/UQ-20261016-34-record.md. Most informative: (2, mandatory own-field own-words title) "FlyWire left right hemisphere connection weight variability within same brain cell type" → direct hit, Schlegel et al. multi-connectome cell typing (biorxiv 2023.06.27.546055); (6, answer-seeking) "Schlegel 2024 Nature technical noise edge weight 30% FlyWire hemibrain biological variability lower bound" → the number and its venue, Nature 634 (2024), doi 10.1038/s41586-024-07968-y; (11) "male Drosophila CNS connectome 2025 sex differences technical noise threshold" → second direct hit, the floor already applied as a filter; (1) the intake's own phrasing ("reconstruction error vs biological variability") → empty, reproducing the intake miss: the field's term of art is "technical noise"; (7) network science, "network inference under edge measurement error" → mature method-owning family (Newman PRX 8:041011 2018; Peixoto arXiv 1806.07956), located not opened; (8) psychometrics generalizability theory and (9) metrology gauge R&R → EM-connectome application genuinely absent, but a method transplant; (10) "two independent segmentations proofreading blinded agreement" → only benchmark-vs-ground-truth (AxonEM), the nearest genuine negative. (2) "Sexual dimorphism in the complete connectome of the Drosophila male central nervous system" (2025), biorxiv 2025.10.09.680999 / PMC12636603 — OPENED (author list unverified from pages opened). Unit: edges across connectomes and hemispheres; endpoint: whether an apparent male–female difference is genuine; comparator: explicit per-dataset noise thresholds (<8 synapses male CNS, <11 FAFB/FlyWire) plus a 30% envelope, FDR correction, expert re-curation; estimand: true dimorphism, explicitly a lower bound ("most apparent differences … were explained by segmentation issues"). (3) Pedigo BD, et al., "Generative network modeling reveals quantitative definitions of bilateral symmetry exhibited by a whole insect brain connectome," eLife (2023), PMC10115445 — NOT opened inside the fetch budget, so its four attributes cannot be stated and it grounds nothing; flagged as the likely home of the hypothesis-testing framing. Also located and not opened: Schneider-Mizell et al., eLife 5:e12059 (two fetches returned JS error pages); Newman (2018) and Peixoto (2018).
Novelty — how this differs from each: From Prior 1, only in the estimator (empirical re-reconstruction vs forward noise model) and in extra stratifiers (cell type, neurite length, effort vs weight alone) — the canonical question's own headline quantity is answered there as ±30% with a 5–95% envelope. From Prior 2, the candidate frames applying the floor to claims in print as the future work that settles significance; Prior 2 has already done it for the field's highest-profile between-connectome claim. From Prior 3, cannot be stated (not opened). Genuine residual, honestly stated: no opened source performs a blinded, independently-proofread second reconstruction of the same sub-volume — but that is a validation study of an existing published number using off-the-shelf machinery (gauge R&R, generalizability theory, network measurement-error estimators), not an un-asked question. CORRECTED after verification and the late Gate 4. Prior 1's comparator is a forward noise model — a fictive ground truth built by scaling observed weights up by the completion rate, subsampled by postsynaptic completion rate, then perturbed at the synapse detector's published false-positive and false-negative rates — compared against the FlyWire left-versus-right hemisphere edge pair. Left and right within one volume are not a technical replicate, since the two hemispheres are different tissue; that is precisely why the authors needed a forward model to partition biological variability from technical noise. So the difference from Prior 1 is not "only the estimator": the published number is a model output and the candidate asks for a measurement, and the forward model does not contain the component the measurement would supply — it perturbs synapse detection but does not model a proofreader attaching a branch to the wrong soma. What the candidate loses instead is methodological novelty: the estimand is mature and named in laboratory medicine (reference change value), imaging metrology (repeatability coefficient, arXiv:2301.11690), cryo-EM (independent half-dataset reconstruction) and diffusion-MRI connectomics, with no EM-connectome instance of any of them found in nine new-vocabulary searches.
Novelty confidence: Medium (Gate 2 graded Low on a ground verification withdrew; re-graded by the late adversary at Medium, which the judge adopts)
Grounds: the question's endpoint — an empirically measured repeatability of a cell-type-to-cell-type edge weight, at a stated confidence, from independent re-reconstruction of the same volume — was found in no opened source, and nine searches across four sibling measurement traditions returned no EM-connectome instance of any of their frameworks. Not High for two reasons: the estimand is a named, mature quantity in those traditions, so what is new is the instrument instance rather than the question's shape; and Prior 1 is a genuinely close neighbour on the same unit, publishing a modelled band that any measurement would be read against. Medium novelty with a close neighbour is the Provisional definition.
Significance — consequence: Weak as graded, because the counterfactual is a modelled ±30% floor rather than no floor. A materially worse empirical result (~±60%) would force re-filtering of the stereotypy and dimorphism claims; a better one would recover resolution. Both branches operate on an existing number. Sharpened at Gate 4: the real counterfactual is not "a floor" but per-dataset cut-offs differing by about 1.4x with no stated derivation, plus "expert curation was required to separate biological signal from cases of technical noise" — hand adjudication of every candidate difference. A worse floor retires a tranche of weak-edge dimorphism claims and redirects proofreading effort to the lowest-completion-rate regions (46% against 77% inside one region); a better one licenses analyses currently declined. The same paper calls a strong quantitative understanding of this variability essential.
Significance — audience: Real and identifiable (FlyWire/Princeton–Cambridge, Janelia FlyEM, MICrONS/Allen proofreading-budget holders), but this audience authored Prior 1, published the threshold and scoped its limits itself. Telling them to validate their own model empirically is a reviewer's comment.
Significance — fecundity: Modest. The downstream questions (transfer to mouse volumes, alternative weight units per presupposition 7, optimal proofreading allocation) are askable now from Prior 1's number.
Significance — anchoring: Touches a real residual anomaly — Prior 1 concedes it "does not correct for other potential confounds such as differences in the synaptic completion rates," and the published completion-rate asymmetry couples error magnitude to region and cell type; anchors to network science's heterogeneous edge-measurement-error family.
Reason for silence: None to explain, and that is the finding. The question was asked by the instrument's own builders in the flagship instrument paper, answered there with a number, and applied as a filter by the next connectome released. The apparent silence was a vocabulary artefact: the field says "technical noise," not "noise floor" / "detection limit" / "reconstruction error versus biological variability." The mechanism that would have been offered — a disciplinary boundary between pipeline engineering and circuit neuroscience — is specifically refuted: they are the same authors on the same paper. The narrow residual (no blinded second reconstruction) has a credible cost-based reason for silence, which makes it an unattractive validation task, not an unposed question. Re-graded Resolved at the late Gate 4, with the mechanism sharpened rather than dismissed: the finding holds for the MODELLED answer and not for the measured one, and the measured one has two mechanisms of the acceptable kind. Cost — a repeatability experiment means paying twice to proofread the same tissue for no new biology, with an expected result that the existing number was about right, and arXiv:2301.11690 notes that real test-retest designs want more subjects and more repeats (its worked example reaches 139 subjects), i.e. many re-proofread sub-volumes. And a disciplinary boundary in vocabulary rather than in personnel: precisely because the error model was written in-house, it was written in the house idiom — forward propagation of detector false-positive and false-negative rates — and never met the traditions that define this quantity by replication.

Record-integrity correction: the record cites Prior 1 as doi 10.1038/s41586-024-07968-y. The quoted numbers are real and the unit is right; the inference that they answer this question fails.
(i) CONFIRMED. Schlegel, Yin, Bates et al., Nature 634:139-152 (2024) does contain the sentences, read twice from independent sources (the bioRxiv full PDF and the Nature HTML): "On average, 65% of the observed variability of edge weight between hemispheres fell within the range expected" and "differences in edge weights of 30% or less may be entirely due to technical noise and should not be overinterpreted" (the preprint renders the latter with "+/-" and a hyphen; the published punctuation could not be settled through the fetch tool's quoting cap). The unit is the one the candidate asks about: "We use the term "edge" to describe the set of connections between two cell types", the weight being "the number of unitary synapses forming that connection", with Fig. 4I reporting the "Fraction of FlyWire left/right edge pairs that fall within the 5-95% quantiles for the modelled technical noise". The record's "approaching 100% for weaker synapses" came back only as paraphrase and is not verified verbatim; it is also a fraction of edge *pairs*, so "weaker edges" rather than "weaker synapses".
(ii) FAILS, and this is the leg the rejection rests on. The comparator is a forward noise model, not an independent re-reconstruction, confirmed verbatim from the Fig. 4H legend, the Results and the Methods: "the impact of technical noise on a fictive ground truth model was assessed", "The raw weight from the connectome for each individual edge is scaled up by the computed completion rate", "This model was randomly subsampled according to postsynaptic completion rate", "synapses were randomly added and deleted according to the false-positive and -negative rates", "Repeated application of this procedure generated a distribution of edge weights between each cell type pair". The observed side of the comparison is the FlyWire left-versus-right hemisphere edge pair, and nowhere is the same image volume re-segmented, re-reconstructed or re-proofread independently and the two results compared. Two consequences the record missed: left versus right within one volume is not a technical replicate, because the two hemispheres are different tissue, which is precisely why the authors needed a forward model to partition biological variability from technical noise; and the 30% figure is therefore a model-derived band rather than a measured repeat-measurement noise floor. The candidate's premise — that the published number is forward-model-derived and that an independent re-reconstruction is what is missing — is correct, and it is exactly what the candidate scopes. "Already answered" does not hold.
(iii) NOT FOUND, with one could-not-read that matters. No published edge-weight detection limit from independent re-reconstruction or repeated independent proofreading of the same volume turned up in 14 searches. The nearest is Schneider-Mizell et al. 2016 (eLife 5:e12059), which has the right design — it compared "iterative reconstruction to the consensus of multiple reconstructions", found "Omission of individual twigs accounted for 96% of errors" and reports that "the robustness of a strong connection to detailed twig anatomy was associated with robustness to reconstruction error" — but its abstract gives a qualitative association and its full text could not be read (elifesciences.org returned a JavaScript-disabled page, PMC a browser interstitial). That is a could-not-read, not an absence, and it is the first thing any re-grading must clear. Two further located-but-unread items: bioRxiv 2025.09.26.678851 on crowdsourced synapse-annotation agreement, and the MICrONS proofreading-and-data-quality tutorial.
Consequence for the Gate 2 verdict: the ground does not carry a Rejection. Gate 4 therefore ran late and separately, as LEDGER.md requires of a withdrawn Gate 2 ground, and all eight attacks were run from scratch against the Gate 0-3 record by one fresh-context adversary.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3
Well-posedness: reduced from 3/3 at the late Gate 4, on two grounds the adversary sourced rather than asserted. The canonical question's "the detection limit for any connectome-to-connectome comparison" asserts a unity that does not hold — Schlegel et al. scope their model to FlyWire's two hemispheres and the male-CNS paper uses different thresholds per dataset — and the question never says which factors are allowed to vary between the two reconstructions, without which the estimand has no value at all, since a deterministic pipeline re-run under genuinely constant conditions has zero variance. Both are wording defects in the canonical sentence that the Gate 1 reformulation partly anticipates; fixing them is cheap and is the first promotion condition.
Significance: 2/3 as graded, but on a better argument than the record's. The counterfactual is not "no floor" versus "a floor"; it is per-dataset cut-offs with no stated derivation plus hand adjudication of every candidate difference, against a measured operator-plus-algorithm variance component. The audience is the same group that built the model, which is the adversary's objection, but it is a group currently substituting expert curation for a measurement and saying in print that a strong quantitative understanding of this variability is essential.
Strongest remaining objection: the candidate's own estimator is structurally blind to the dominant error source, so the measurement it names cannot deliver the quantity its sentence promises. Reconstruction errors are made at image defects — folds, lost sections, poor staining — and the 2025 male-CNS connectome states that technical noise "is more commonly correlated across both sides of one brain" and that "most apparent differences in male-female connectivity were explained by segmentation issues". Any independent second pass over the same voxels inherits those defects and fails in the same places, so the agreement it measures is an optimistic bound: it estimates operator-plus-algorithm variance and silently sets the common-mode term to zero. The candidate therefore cannot displace the modelled floor it is aimed at; it can only contribute one missing variance component beside it. Combined with the residual force of attack 6 — the likeliest empirical result is "about ±30%, as modelled", which moves confidence more than practice — this caps the candidate at a bounded, well-identified metrological increment rather than a new fact about the instrument. The earlier objection, that the disguise is total because the headline quantity is already in print, is withdrawn in substantial part by the adversary that replaced it: the published ±30% is a do-not-interpret-below floor from a forward uncertainty budget and cannot be read as a detection limit at anything like 95% confidence.
Promotion requires: (i) striking "the detection limit for any connectome-to-connectome comparison" and restating the stake as "the thresholds in use are undocumented, borrowed across volumes and patched by hand curation" rather than "no threshold exists"; (ii) stating the replication design explicitly — which of proofreader team, segmentation algorithm, agglomeration threshold, detector version and cell-typing convention is allowed to vary — since a deterministic pipeline re-run under genuinely constant conditions has zero variance; (iii) asking for a variance-components function of edge weight, region and completion rate with confidence bands and a stated specificity, rather than a single number, given that the noise-explained fraction approaches 100% for weaker edges and completion rate ranges from 46% to 77% inside one region; (iv) saying in the question itself that same-volume re-reconstruction bounds only the operator-plus-algorithm component and is blind to image-defect-driven common-mode error, so that the honest claim is a measured component to sit beside the existing modelled budget rather than "the noise floor". With (i), (ii) and (iv) done, well-posedness reaches 3/3 and the entry could be Validated on a second adversary.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): the natural owner is metrology — a gauge R&R or generalizability-theory design over a sub-volume re-proofread by a blinded second team, with variance components for segmentation, proofreading and region, reported against Prior 1's ±30% envelope and stratified on the completion-rate heterogeneity Prior 1 declines to correct for. Decide first, and in writing, which factors vary between the two passes, because the estimand does not exist until that is fixed; and stratify the sub-volume selection on image-defect density, since that is the one way the design can say anything about the common-mode term it otherwise ignores. Open Pedigo et al. (PMC10115445) before anything else: it is the likeliest home of the hypothesis-testing framing and has defeated two fetch attempts.
Routing: not routed. The entry is Provisional, so it is not an already-asked rejection at all, and the candidate's own endpoint — an empirically measured repeatability of an edge weight at a stated confidence — was independently confirmed NOT FOUND posed in print by both the verification checker and the late adversary. Recorded for completeness: the nearest thing in print is the male-CNS paper calling a strong quantitative understanding of this variability essential, which is a statement of need rather than a posed question, and Schneider-Mizell et al. 2016 (eLife 5:e12059), which has the right design but whose full text could not be read from this environment and which is therefore the entry's most important unread item rather than a routing ground.
