Verification by the run session (one fresh-context checker over the whole of arXiv:2504.06219, handed the claims and the identifier but not the reviewer's reasoning; 2 searches, 6 fetches, 2 refusals; full log in batches/2026-10-16-1433/UQ-20261016-38-verification.md). THE KILL SURVIVES, and it is the only one in this batch that survives whole: all four attributes confirmed, the decisive phrase found verbatim, and both absence findings confirmed. That is worth recording in a ledger where verification has withdrawn a kill in every recent batch.
(i) CONFIRMED on all four attributes, and on the two checks that make the Disguise verdict fatal rather than suggestive. The paper does compare the CONTENT of the two strata, not only the volume lost — topic and format composition, token loss, benchmark scores and verbatim-memorization rates are all computed across compliant and non-compliant corpora. And it contains NO missing-data machinery of any kind: no MAR, no MNAR, no ignorability, no selection model, no inverse-probability or propensity reweighting, and no attempt to correct or reweight the retained corpus to stand in for the pre-exclusion one. The record's reading was right on both, which is why deliverable (ii) survives as the candidate's only untouched part while the headline does not.
(ii) THE SIGN OF THE HEADLINE PAIR MUST BE STATED. 42.5 is the NON-COMPLIANT average and 42.8 the COMPLIANT one (Table 2): the compliant model scores HIGHER by 0.3. Written as "42.5 vs 42.8" without naming which is which, it invites the reading that compliance cost 0.3 points, when the sign is the opposite.
(iii) AND THE PAIR CARRIES NO UNCERTAINTY. Tables 2 and 4 report point values with no seeds, standard deviations or confidence intervals, so there is nothing to carry through and the 0.3 gap cannot be distinguished from run-to-run noise at 1.5B parameters and 100B tokens. The defensible statement is "no detectable difference", not "a measured near-zero effect" — a distinction that matters, because the candidate's own nominated answer was that the effect is small, and this paper cannot bound how small.
(iv) Three numbers need qualifying. The 8% token loss cannot be independently recomputed: the paper gives no absolute token counts for the two corpora, the only absolute figure being "the compliant dataset (4.5T tokens)" with no non-compliant counterpart. It must not be conflated with the separate "approximate 4% reduction in total tokens" for the news-removed variant. And the LCCS movement 23.11 -> 21.27 is in a unit the paper never states, over a computation it never describes; the non-integral values imply a mean over the 12,800 articles, which the paper does not label as a mean.
(v) The "minimal" phrase is real and hedged inside its own sentence, which goes on to name a decrease in News Articles and in Science & Tech and an increase in Personal Blogs. Quoting the fragment alone overstates the paper's own claim.
(vi) The comparator set is LARGER than the record states, and the enlargement is where the one positive finding lives. Besides the unfiltered/filtered contrast and the subtractive "-News" row, Table 3 carries three ADDITIVE variants — "Compliant + News", "Compliant + Med", "Compliant + MathSci" — and the medical signal comes from that continual-pretraining arm, not from the from-scratch arm. Relatedly, the estimand exists in two forms the record collapses into one: M1, exact, training from scratch, and M2, an approximation via continual pretraining. The endpoint list also omits Table 1, the percentage of documents with a 50-gram match to nytimes.com, medicalxpress.com and stackexchange.com, which is a fourth cross-strata statistic.
(vii) "Only medical" is partly an artefact of measurement. Appendix A states the authors "are unable to reliably evaluate domain-specific knowledge in Math & Science", so the absence of a signal there is not evidence of its absence.
(viii) Two scope claims are downgraded. "Confined to education-filtered FineWeb-Edu" is unverified for the continual-pretraining arm, which the paper never states is FineWeb-Edu only. And "uses only the most recent robots.txt" is right for the stratification but not for the paper: Figure 1 does use historical robots.txt via the Internet Archive. The consequence the record drew is nonetheless sharpened — because stratification uses today's robots.txt, a document crawled lawfully years ago counts as non-compliant if its domain blocks now, so the strata are a "what if we re-crawled today" counterfactual rather than a record of what any crawler actually took.
(ix) VENUE RESOLVED, and the record's caution was warranted. It is an ICML 2025 WORKSHOP poster (the DataWorld workshop) per icml.cc, not a main-conference paper, and no venue statement appears on the arXiv page, in the paper's header, or in any DOI record. Citing it as "ICML 2025" unqualified would be mis-attribution.
(x) One arithmetic discrepancy found and left open: Table 2's "-News" row prints ten values summing to 427.5, a mean of 42.75, against a printed 42.6 — an unreconciled 0.15. It does not touch the 42.5/42.8 pair the verdict uses.
(xi) Fidelity caveat: raw HTTP to arxiv.org was refused by the egress policy, so the full text was reachable only through a fetch tool that refuses quotations beyond about 125 characters. Quotes are short fragments obtained through a mediating model rather than a local grep, and the absence findings in (i) are tool-reported searches rather than verified greps — strong, but not the same thing.

Gate 4 completeness after verification: complete. The Disguise ground was tested directly rather than taken on trust, and held on every leg, so the fatal status stands without a re-attack.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3
Strongest remaining objection: arXiv:2504.06219 runs the candidate's exact pre-/post-exclusion contrast on FineWeb-Edu ("distribution differences between compliant and non-compliant data are minimal", "8% fewer training tokens", 1.5B models on 100B tokens averaging 42.5 vs 42.8), which is deliverable (iii) in full and both factors of deliverable (i), with the Groves product reducible to arithmetic on published figures — so the candidate as posed is a disguised known, and the one genuinely unexecuted limb (ignorability/MNAR on crawl-observable covariates) is a narrower different question, not a rescue of this one. Independent of novelty, the candidate would still be held off 3/3 well-posedness by P3: "bias" needs a target population the web does not supply, so every figure it yields is frame-relative by stipulation.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): nothing here; the candidate is closed. If the ignorability limb is wanted, re-intake it at Gate 0 as its own narrower question, posed with arXiv:2510.10315's credibility covariate (and its non-crawl-observability) and the P7 snapshot-drift problem in view, and with ToS/CDN exclusion rather than robots.txt as the dominant mechanism to model.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): Not routed. The rejection is a disguised-known/answered one, not asked-but-still-open: arXiv:2504.06219 publishes an answer to the headline. Per the operating rules, answered and disguised-known rejections are not routed to ledger/routed-open-problems.md. (The unexecuted ignorability limb is un-asked, not an open problem, so it is not routable either; it belongs in a fresh Gate 0 intake.)

Status: Rejected
Domain(s): Medicine/STEM — nuclear medicine, PET kinetic modelling, internal dosimetry/radiopharmaceutical therapy. Adjacent vocabularies checked: clinical-pharmacology mass-balance/ADME recovery, metrology closure/adjustment, structural identifiability, process-systems data reconciliation, metabolic flux analysis, ICRP biokinetics, quantitative SPECT/RPT dosimetry.
Question (canonical): In dynamic total-body PET (axial FOV >= ~1.9 m) of N subjects per tracer, for a pre-specified tracer set, does the closure residual R(t) = A_inj(t) − SUM_organs Ahat_organ(t | thetahat) − E(t) − B(t) lie within its propagated uncertainty, where thetahat are per-organ compartmental parameters from the conventional independent per-organ fit, A_inj(t) is decay-corrected injected activity, E(t) is measured excreted/left-FOV activity and B(t) is a pre-registered BOUNDED (not freely fitted) non-segmentable remainder; and for each tracer where R(t) is significantly non-zero, which organ's parameters move when the fit is redone under a global conservation constraint, in which direction, and by how much in Ki, Vt, K1 and organ absorbed dose?
  (This is V2, the one Gate 1 reformulation. V1 as received: "When organ-level compartmental models are fitted independently per organ in the conventional way, do the fitted parameters reproduce the whole-body tracer mass balance that a single total-body PET acquisition now measures directly, and where they do not, which organs' published kinetic parameters are biased and in which direction?" V2 fixes the estimand, the uncertainty denominator, and forbids a free remainder; no scope change.)
Alternative formulations:
- Does total-body PET's simultaneous view of every organ falsify the independence assumption behind decades of single-organ PET kinetic modelling?
- Is injected activity conserved across independently fitted organ compartmental models, and how large is the closure residual by tracer and by time after injection?
- (Metrology register) What is the misclosure of the whole-body activity balance implied by conventional per-organ PET kinetic fits, and which organ's parameters does a constrained adjustment move?
Motivating gap: Total-body scanners (~2 m axial FOV, uEXPLORER class, from 2019) record every organ's TAC and the input function in one dynamic acquisition, so the tracer's whole-body balance is observable while organ kinetics are being fitted. The per-organ independent-fit convention is a fossil of the 15-25 cm FOV and has been carried into total-body data unchanged — three opened instances: Chalampalakis 2024 (eight organs, independent Patlak, never summed), vPET-ABC 2026 (~4.4M voxels fitted independently), Rainio/Knuuti/Klen 2025 (20 structures fitted separately, a joint multi-structure model named only as future work). Internal dosimetry does hold the conservation concept but computes MIRD remainder-of-body as injected minus measured organs, zeroing the residual by construction. Drug development must demonstrate radiolabeled dose recovery; PET never has.
Presuppositions: (1) LAFOV quantification accurate enough at organ level to close to a few percent, incl. FOV extremes — CONTESTED, and undermined by an opened source (Chalampalakis: early-frame underestimation from a fixed 0.75 scatter factor; organ Ki −12%/−16% at 25%/10% counts). (2) Organ volumes segmentable with bounded, propagatable error. (3) The non-segmentable remainder can be BOUNDED rather than freely fitted — KEY DESIGN THREAT, handled by pre-registration; a wide bound makes the test underpowered. (4) Excreted/left-FOV activity accounted for within the window. (5) Decay, dead-time, randoms corrections exact enough not to swamp R(t). (6) The imaged quantity is conserved (labelled metabolites imaged identically or measured) — CONTESTED, tracer-specific; V2 inherits a per-tracer restatement requirement. (7) Independent per-organ fitting is the live convention for total-body data — supported by three opened instances, not by a methods review. (8) Published Ki/Vt/K1 feed decisions at a precision where closure-sized bias matters — only partly established; weakest significance limb. (9) UNFLAGGED BY THE RECORD, added by adversary 2: that a non-zero R(t) is attributable to organ KINETIC parameters. The record supplies no identification argument for this. See strongest objection.
What would count as an answer: Per tracer, in dynamic total-body scans of N subjects, compute R(t) as defined, with uncertainty propagated from segmentation, scanner calibration and input-function error. Answered by (a) the distribution of |R(t)| relative to that uncertainty, per tracer and time window, and (b) for each tracer with R(t) significantly non-zero, which organ's parameters move under a global conservation constraint and by how much (% shift in Ki, Vt, K1, organ absorbed dose). A null — closure within propagated uncertainty for every tracer — is a real result: it licenses the independent-fit convention with evidence for the first time and yields an organ-level bound on LAFOV quantitative accuracy as a by-product.

Estimand: within-subject bias/precision of per-organ SUV/Ki vs count level. Verified absences: no summation across organs, no comparison of any total to injected dose, no compartmental fitting, no conservation constraint.

Gu Q. et al., "vPET-ABC: Fast Voxelwise Approximate Bayesian Inference for Kinetic Modeling in PET," arXiv:2603.14859 (2026) (abstract OPENED and authorship/absences corroborated by adversary 2; public repo confirmed by adversary 1). Unit: voxel (~4.4M, 50-min total-body FDG). Endpoint: parameter log-ratio error, posterior KL, model-selection sensitivity/specificity, runtime, Moran's I. Comparator: NNLS+BIC, SMC, HMC/NUTS, Patlak, SUV. Estimand: voxelwise posterior K1,k2,k3,k4,Vb,Ki. Verified absences: no conservation quantity; every voxel independent; the only cross-voxel object is a post-hoc evaluation, not a constraint.

Unit: whole body, population-level. Endpoint: predicted organ/plasma activities. Comparator: pooled literature biokinetic data. Novelty — how this differs from each: vs 1 — comparator is the crux: Chalampalakis compares a count-reduced scan against itself (per-organ precision); the candidate's comparator is decay-corrected injected activity, an external physical quantity, with the whole subject as unit. A study can pass Prior 1 perfectly and fail the candidate, because self-consistent organs can still sum to the wrong total; Prior 1 is also the strongest evidence FOR presupposition 7. vs 2 — same relation one level finer: an estimator, not a consistency check; nothing in it could detect a closure violation; it is an instance of the convention, not a test of it. vs 3 — Kamp does fit all organs simultaneously under a closed model, so "no coupled whole-body estimator exists" is withdrawn; but its remainder is freely fitted, which imposes closure and zeroes the residual by construction. The candidate's entire content is to bound the remainder and inspect the misclosure instead — the opposite methodological move. vs the clinical-pharmacology recovery standard and the process-systems/MFA reconciliation machinery: both mature, neither applied to PET organ kinetics; the candidate is the transplant, and the PET case adds an input function, decay correction, segmentation and time-resolved rather than steady-state balances.

Would fall to Low if PMC10881693 computes total image activity against injected dose.
  Grounds as regraded: it does. PMC10881693 sums measured activity over the whole subject, decay-corrects it to injection time and sets it against the reported net injected activity, reporting a 14% shortfall and attributing roughly 10 points of it to bladder voiding and the rest to calibration - limb (a) executed, published, numbered and explained, in the candidate's own journal family. The pre-registered condition fires and novelty is Low. What remains un-asked is limb (b) alone: whether INDEPENDENTLY fitted per-organ compartmental models reproduce that balance in TIME, with a bounded remainder, so that a misclosure can be attributed. Target A is a static per-scan total with no kinetics and no organ-level decomposition, and Kamp imposes closure rather than testing it, so limb (b) is untouched by either - but a limb is not a question, and the compound question as posed is answered on its headline.
Significance — consequence: Non-null: published organ parameters carry a bias of identifiable location and sign, and MIRD's remainder-by-subtraction has been absorbing that model error into "remainder of body", misallocating absorbed dose between remainder and offending organ — which propagates to administered activity in radiopharmaceutical therapy. Null: the independent-fit convention gets its first evidential licence in ~four decades, plus an organ-level bound on LAFOV quantitative accuracy across the full 2 m FOV. Either branch yields a usable quantity. Contingency conceded: if R(t) is dominated by calibration, segmentation and the remainder bound, only the quantification figure survives, and harmonisation bodies are already pursuing that by phantom and cross-calibration routes.
Significance — audience: Total-body kinetic-modelling groups (UC Davis/Wang, Sydney/Meikle, Vienna/Beyer, Turku/Knuuti — authors of three priors, and Rainio 2025 names a joint multi-structure model as future work): would add a closure diagnostic and re-derive affected parameters. MIRD and EANM dosimetry committees: a measured residual argues for replacing remainder-by-subtraction with a measured-and-bounded remainder. RPT dosimetry services: organ-dose shifts feed administered-activity decisions. Tracer developers: Vt/Ki drive candidate ranking. EARL/QIBA and LAFOV vendors: the by-product bound is specification-relevant at FOV extremes.
Significance — fecundity: Does a conservation-constrained multi-organ estimator buy identifiability for badly conditioned parameters (k4 in liver, kidney)? Can per-scan closure residual serve as automated QC, as misclosure does in survey adjustment? Can remainder-of-body be measured rather than subtracted, and what does that do to S-value practice? Can closure separate parent from total label without arterial metabolite assay? Does the test transfer to total-body SPECT and 177Lu therapy dosimetry? (Adversary 2: the k4 item is answerable in a paragraph, since a TAC-functional constraint adds nothing in TAC-invariant directions — so part of this list is trivial.)
Significance — anchoring: IDIF validation; the MIRD remainder-of-body convention; structural identifiability of 2TCM; the asymmetry that drug development must demonstrate dose recovery while PET never has; and one concrete opened anomaly — Chalampalakis's early-frame underestimation traced to a fixed 0.75 scatter-scaling factor, exactly the correction error a time-localised non-zero R(t) would surface.
Reason for silence: Strand 2 is the only strand that survives adversarial testing intact: the one community holding the conservation concept defines remainder-of-body as injected minus measured organs, so the residual is zeroed by an accounting identity before anyone could inspect it — confirmed by Kamp 2023's freely fitted "Other". Strand 4 (no regulator requires PET dose recovery, unlike human radiolabeled mass-balance studies) is sound but explains an unforced study rather than an unasked question. Strand 1 (new instrument) is narrowed: multi-bed whole-body PET dosimetry summed organ %IA against injected activity in the 1990s and whole-body retention is measured externally in RPT, so what 2019 made new is early-frame simultaneity, not observability of the balance — and seven years is short for a convention inherited from a 15-25 cm FOV. Strand 3 (method boundary) fails as a non-asking mechanism: no reconciliation machinery is needed to ask whether the organs add up, and SAAM-era closed whole-body models show tracer kinetics already crossed it. A competing mechanism adversary 2 raises and could not source: the answer is widely assumed known and uninteresting (it will not close, because of the unimaged remainder).

Verification by the run session (seven fresh-context checkers ran over this batch's load-bearing kills and priors, each handed a claim and its source but not the reviewer's reasoning; this entry's checker ran 11 searches and 26 fetches with 15 refusals or hard blocks; full log in batches/2026-10-16-1433/UQ-20261016-39-verification.md). This entry's verdict is reversed by it. The access failure that held novelty at Medium was an artefact of the route, not a property of the literature.
(i) THE GATING ITEM IS SETTLED, AGAINST THE CANDIDATE. PMC10881693 is Smith et al., "Mitigating SUV uncertainties using total body PET imaging", Eur J Nucl Med Mol Imaging 51(4):1070-1078 (2024), reached on the first publisher attempt at https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00259-023-06503-x, and it performs limb (a). Its Methods construct the quantity by "counting the total image activity in all voxels" "while applying a correction for radioactive decay toward injection time"; its Eq. 1 sets "ActIMG is the total image-derived 18F-FDG activity (MBq)" against "ActINJ is the reported net injected activity (MBq)"; and its Discussion reports the result: "We found that TB image-derived 18F-FDG activity underestimated reported injected activity by 14%". The mass-balance character is confirmed by the physical account it gives of the shortfall - "Approximately 10% can probably be attributed to activity loss due to emptying the bladder before scanning", with the residual assigned to calibration ("Discrepancies in scanner calibration might explain the resulting percentage difference"). That is a whole-subject sum of measured activity, decay-corrected to injection time, set against the administered dose, with the discrepancy quantified and physically attributed. The record's own pre-registered condition therefore fires: novelty falls to Low and the verdict is Rejected, not Provisional.
(ii) Three qualifications travel with that YES, and none of them saves the candidate. The direction of use is inverted - the paper's aim is image-based QC, deriving injected activity from the image to substitute for an erroneous recorded value, so the dose comparison is the calibration step rather than a validation of the image against the dose. It is a cohort-level regression (a slope fitted on 25 scans, validated on 56 independent scans, 3 phantoms), not a per-subject recovery fraction. And the whole-subject sum holds for the total-body arm only; the half-body arm covers "skull vertex to mid-thigh", which is why its equations carry an extra patient-length term. Limb (a)'s measurement nonetheless exists, sits in the candidate's own journal family, and has a number.
(iii) The number must be carried in the right direction. 14% is ActINJ/ActIMG - 1: the reported dose sits 14% ABOVE the image total, so the image total sits 12.3% below the dose (1/1.14 = 0.877), i.e. the image recovered 87.7% of it, not 86%. The abstract's 4.8% is a post-calibration residual agreement on the 56 validation scans after the fitted coefficients are applied (4.8%/3.2% TB, 4.9%/3.1% HB, 6.7%/4.5% SAFOV), not the raw shortfall; conflating the two understates the raw discrepancy roughly threefold.
(iv) The paper's vocabulary is not the candidate's, and that is the whole trap. Target A contains none of "whole-body activity", "total body activity", "mass balance", "recovery", "accounted for", "sum of", "integral" or "cross-calibration"; its own term is "total image activity in all voxels". The record was right that the closure vocabulary is absent from the field and wrong that the measurement is. That is the exact shape of the Gate 2 error this ledger keeps making - a real paper doing the candidate's thing under other words - caught here by an access route rather than by a reading.
(v) PMC11788250 IS MIS-ATTRIBUTED IN THIS RECORD. It is not a companion total-body PET paper. It is Benitez-Aurioles et al., "Multi-organ kinetic modeling for Na[18F]F pre-clinical total-body PET studies", Medical Physics 52(2):924-937 (2025), doi 10.1002/mp.17499, PMID 39499788 - a pre-clinical MOUSE Na[18F]F study, differing in species, tracer and journal family, sharing only the phrase "total-body PET". Its full text was unreachable on every route tried (Wiley landing page, Wiley PDF and pdfdirect all client errors; PMC reCAPTCHA; Europe PMC REST 429 with an explicit instruction not to retry; europepmc.org robots-disallowed; no OpenAlex record for the PMCID; no repository or preprint mirror found), and even its abstract came back only as a paraphrase, so no text search of it was performed and its absences are NOT a check that passed. Nothing in this verdict rests on it.
(vi) KAMP 2023 IS ONLY PARTLY AS THE RECORD HAS IT. Simultaneous fitting is confirmed verbatim: "The model predictions were fit simultaneously to all available data using the Rosenbrock integrator option of SAAM II". The closed, mass-conserving structure is NOT established by anything readable - the differential-equation system is deferred to Additional file 1, and the nearest phrase, "Activity of 2-[18F]FDG is given in % of administered activity.", is a figure-caption plotting unit, not a constraint. The "Other" compartment is never described as obtained by subtraction and carries no data of its own, so it is functionally a freely fitted remainder, though the paper never says so. And Kamp performs no whole-body-total-versus-injected-activity comparison of its own: it computes TIACs from pooled literature organ TACs and expresses them as a fraction of administered activity, which normalises a fitted model rather than measuring against a dose. Recording Kamp's closed structure as confirmed would have converted an unread supplement into a passed check.
(vii) Process finding, carried forward. The seven prior access failures across three agents were an artefact of routing through PMC and Europe PMC, both hard-blocked for this session. The DOI-to-publisher route settled in one call what seven attempts could not, and belongs first in the sequence rather than last.
(viii) Fidelity caveat on every quotation above: all raw curl egress was refused at the proxy, so nothing could be downloaded and every quote was mediated by a fetch tool whose extraction layer caps verbatim strings at about 125 characters. Fragments marked verbatim were returned in quotation marks under that cap; equation coefficients and full captions are restatements.

Gate 4 completeness after verification: complete, and no late adversary is required. Two independent adversaries ran all sixteen attacks on a record that graded novelty Medium, and neither returned an Unresolved. Verification did not dissolve a fatal ground here; it established a new Gate 2 ground, which the Gate 5 rule lets decide the verdict on its own.

Scores: Well-posedness 3/3 · Significance 2/3 (both stand on the Gate 1-3 record and both are moot for the verdict: Gate 2 novelty is Low, which rejects regardless. Recorded because they are the batch's highest pair and the entry would otherwise have been this ledger's first Validated one - the only thing between it and that grade was a paper nobody could open.)
  Well-posedness 3/3 stands: V2 fixes the estimand, the uncertainty denominator and a pre-registered bounded remainder that defeats the vacuity threat the intake itself identified; both limbs have statable outcomes; the null is informative; the metabolite presupposition is carried as an explicit per-tracer restatement requirement. Neither adversary graded attack 5 above Partial, and both located the real weakness in significance and attribution rather than in posedness.
  Significance 2/3 stands (not raised, not lowered): consequence, audience and fecundity are argued and anchoring includes a concrete opened anomaly, but presupposition 8 is only partly established, presupposition 1 is undermined by an opened source, and both adversaries show the headline consequence is contingent on an attribution step the record never argues.
Strongest remaining objection: R(t), as defined in V2, is built from fitted curves that already reproduce the measured organ curves, so to first order it is independent of the kinetic parameters it is meant to audit — an audit of scanner calibration, segmentation, excretion accounting and the asserted remainder bound — and because a global conservation constraint is a functional of the predicted TACs it carries no information in the parameter directions the TACs already fail to determine. Limb (b) therefore has no identification strategy: which organ "moves" under the constrained refit is a property of the estimator's weighting and conditioning, not a fact about which published parameters are wrong. Two independent adversaries reached this convergently, and it moves attacks 1, 4, 6 and 8 together. It is graded Partial, not fatal, only because neither adversary could cite it to a primary source it opened and because it is scope-limited to the well-specified regime — under organ-model misspecification the summed residual does acquire kinetic content.
What promotion would have required, recorded as written before the answer was known and now moot - item (i) is settled against the candidate, see Verification (i): (i) opening PMC10881693 ("Mitigating SUV uncertainties using total body PET imaging", 2024) and PMC11788250 by a route that has not yet failed — institutional/library access, author request, or the publisher version — and showing that neither computes a whole-body activity total against injected activity (if either does, limb (a) is pre-empted and novelty falls to Low, i.e. Rejected, not promoted); AND (ii) an explicit identification argument for limb (b), restating V2 so the constrained refit separates volume/calibration scale factors from kinetic rate constants, so that a movement can be attributed to one organ's kinetics rather than to calibration, segmentation or the remainder bound; AND (iii) a pre-registered equivalence margin for R(t) in place of "within propagated uncertainty", with the remainder bound B(t) quantified (e.g. CT-segmented muscle/adipose) so a null is not a power artefact. Items (ii) and (iii) are document-level repairs; item (i) is an access problem and is the gating one.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): resolve access to PMC10881693 before any data or design work — the whole verdict hinges on it, and it has defeated seven routes across three agents. After that, and still as design rather than answer, the place to look for the attribution gap is the sensitivity of R(t) to thetahat versus to calibration and volume scale factors, which is a property of the estimator and can be examined before any subject is scanned; the process-systems gross-error-detection and metabolic-flux model-error literatures (BMC Syst Biol 2016; Waterloo generalized-least-squares thesis) are where that machinery already exists.
Verdict reasoning (Gate 5): Rejected at GATE 2 - novelty Low, regraded after verification opened the paper the Gate 2 record could not. Limb (a), the whole-body total of measured activity set against the decay-corrected injected activity, is executed and published in the candidate's own journal family with a quantified result (Smith et al. 2024: a 14% shortfall, ~10 points of it bladder voiding, the rest calibration). The Gate 2 grade was explicitly conditional on that paper and the condition fired. Gate 4 is complete and supports nothing weaker: two independent adversaries ran sixteen attacks and returned no Unresolved, but both converged on the same non-fatal defect - limb (b) has no identification strategy, because a conservation constraint is a functional of the predicted TACs and so carries no information in the directions the TACs already fail to determine. Well-posedness 3/3 and Significance 2/3 both stand and are both moot. Had the paper stayed unread, this entry would have been graded Provisional on the strength of an access failure.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): NOT routed. The rejection is asked-AND-answered on the headline limb, and answered rejections are not routed. Limb (b) - do independently fitted per-organ compartmental models reproduce the whole-body balance in time, against a bounded remainder, and can the misclosure be attributed to an organ rather than to calibration, segmentation or the remainder - is neither asked nor answered by anything opened, so it is not an open problem of record either. It belongs in a fresh Gate 0 intake, carrying the identification defect both adversaries found as a condition of admission rather than as a finding to discover. Recorded so a later run does not re-derive it.

ID: UQ-20261016-40
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): Biology — structural biology; single-particle cryo-EM methodology; structural-data curation (EMPIAR/EMDB). Adjacent vocabularies checked: metrology (operator effect, ring trials), screening epidemiology (verification bias / unverified screen-negatives), quality engineering (accept-reject sampling), astronomy-ML real-bogus artefact rejection, human factors, Chinese-language cryo-EM.
Question (canonical): Over a pre-specified frame of K EMPIAR entries depositing an uncleaned particle stack alongside the published final stack, (a) in what share of entries does a reconstruction from the complement (deposited picks minus final stack) satisfy a pre-registered three-part distinct-state criterion — resolution better than a fixed threshold, map-to-model correspondence above a fixed cutoff, and deviation from the deposited map above the 95th percentile of deviations from size-matched random subsets of the retained stack; and (b) when M curators process the same micrographs independently and blind, what is the Jaccard overlap of their rejected sets, and does any resulting map carry a feature absent from the deposited map? (Gate 1 reformulation, one allowed, and the version graded.)
Alternative formulations:
- Gate 0 intake version: does the rejected complement of a deposited cryo-EM reconstruction support a distinct conformational or compositional state rather than noise, and is the retained/rejected partition a property of the data or of the curator?
- What is in cryo-EM's discard pile, and is the deposited structural record a biased subsample of the molecular ensemble?
Motivating gap: the field is dense with how-answers about discarding (2D/3D classification, vendor "junk cleaning", neural sorters such as ANTIDOTE, bioRxiv 2025.10.06.680814) and validates only the retained map (gold-standard FSC, independent-particle cross-validation), while the "the discard pile is junk" assertion is rarely measured against the alternative that it is enriched in the minority states classification removes. Gate 2 narrowed the gap: the existence limb is already demonstrated in the candidate's own literature and the complement/matched-subset mechanics already exercised; only the pooled corpus-level share and the curator-overlap statistic remain unmeasured.
Presuppositions: (1) enough EMPIAR entries pair raw/uncleaned picks with final lists — partly established (EMPIAR-10930 deposits ~18M uncleaned particles); the archive-wide count is unknown. (2) The deposited picking step is reproducible for entries lacking an uncleaned stack — contested and load-bearing. (3) "Distinct state" admits a non-circular pre-specified criterion — supplied at Gate 1; contested by adversary attack 5. (4) Enough signal in the complement for any reconstruction — ESTABLISHED (P1: 4.38 A from the lowest-scoring 90k of EMPIAR-10093 vs 4.08 A from the top 84k). (5) Rejection is at least partly operator-dependent — contested; supported anecdotally by P2; threatened from the opposite side by run-to-run algorithmic stochasticity (attack 4). (6) Specimens possess minority states at removed frequencies — demonstrated for ALK-ALKAL2 (2:1 beside 2:2). (7) Downstream users treat a deposited map as representative — only partly established; not load-bearing for significance.
What would count as an answer: per-entry pass/fail of the complement against the pre-registered criterion with matched-size random retained subsets as controls; the M-curator Jaccard of rejected sets plus any feature absent from the deposited map; and a pooled share of entries whose discarded material supported a reproducible distinct state. Negative if complement maps are indistinguishable from matched random subsets and curator overlap is high; positive even at a minority share, which would give EMDB/EMPIAR grounds to mandate deposition of the full pick list and rejection record (the analogue of unmerged reflections in crystallography).
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 20 documented queries (11 at Gate 2, cap 11; 9 Disguise queries by adversary 1, cap 9) plus 6 fetches opened. Full lists: batches/2026-10-16-1433/UQ-20261016-40-record.md and UQ-20261016-40-adversary-1.md. Most informative: (i) "rejected/discarded particles reanalysis yielding an additional state from EMPIAR data" → KEY HIT, the ALK reanalysis of EMPIAR-10930 with PDB 9G5I titled "obtained after re-processing of EMPIAR-10930 data"; (ii) "discarded particles + 2D classification + junk + hidden heterogeneity" → bioRxiv 2025.11.12.688030, which reconstructs from the lowest-scoring particles against size-matched random subsets; (iii) MANDATORY fraction-already-computed query on corpus-wide picked-vs-retained attrition → no pooled statistic, re-run independently by the adversary with the same result; (iv) overlap/agreement between independently curated particle sets → REPIC and picker benchmarks only, no rejected-set overlap, and no cryo-EM processing ring trial under metrology vocabulary; (v) practitioner "bad classes rescue" vocabulary → PMC12485487 "How many (distinguishable) classes can we identify?" (2025), unopened; (vi) Chinese-language sweep → PMC6086358 crowdsourcing of cryo-EM (humans as annotators), unopened. PMC10711021 was opened by the adversary and confirmed NOT a prior (CryoSieve operates inside the final stack).
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources): P1 "Automated filtering of particle images in single particle cryoEM", bioRxiv 2025.11.12.688030 — unit: particle images across five EMPIAR entries; endpoint: refinement resolution / B-factor / cryoEF; comparator: RELION class ranker, one expert's manual selection, size-matched random subsets, full set; estimand: whether a score-thresholded retained subset preserves full-set map quality; reconstructs the complement explicitly and states "the filtered-out particles may exhibit different conformation(s) of the molecule, implying heterogeneity" as untested speculation. P2 "Overcoming cryo-EM map anisotropy reveals ALK-cytokine assemblies with distinct stoichiometries", bioRxiv 2024.08.08.607122 / PMC12017499 / PDB 9G5I — unit: particles of EMPIAR-10930's uncleaned ~18M stack; endpoint: recovery of a 2:1 assembly, cFAR/resolution; comparator: the deposited 2:2 map EMD-24095; estimand: that the deposited data contain a population the original did not carry forward (3.2 A), with "6 of the 10 most populated classes after initial 2D classification do not correspond" to the original's. P3 "Cross-validation tests for cryo-EM maps using an independent particle set", arXiv:1908.01054 — unit: the map per refinement iteration; endpoint: BioEM posterior given held-out particles; comparator: gold-standard half-sets; estimand: overfitting, not state identity.
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs P1 — endpoint differs (complement state identity under a pre-registered criterion, pooled over K entries, versus retained-map quality with the complement as an informativeness check); but P1 performs deliverable (a) in degenerate form on two entries with the control the candidate proposes, and names the candidate's hypothesis in print. vs P2 — P2 answers the existence limb affirmatively for one entry and exhibits the curator-divergence phenomenon incidentally; residual novelty over it is quantitative and design-level (how often, and is the partition operator-dependent), not phenomenological. vs P3 — orthogonal estimand; shares only the mechanical act of touching the complement.
Novelty confidence: Low
Significance — consequence: either direction is decidable and useful — a positive pooled share gives EMDB/EMPIAR the expected-yield number needed to justify mandating deposition of full pick lists and rejection records; a negative gives the field's universal "it's junk" assertion its first systematic evidence. Discounted because P2 already supplies the policy argument's existence case (a new PDB entry extracted from someone else's deposited data), leaving the pooled estimate incremental.
Significance — audience: EMDB/EMPIAR and the wwPDB validation task force (live venue: the archiving recommendations, arXiv:2311.17640); sorter developers (P1, ANTIDOTE) who validate only on retained-map quality; reanalysis groups wanting a prior on which entries repay reprocessing. Attack 6 is live against all of them: the Map Challenge documented large processing-to-processing spread and produced no mandate.
Significance — fecundity: per-entry yield function (complement size vs state-recovery probability); predictability of operator-dependence from specimen properties; a rejection record as a validation artefact with its own metric; whether corpus-wide attrition predicts reanalysis success; transfer to cryo-ET subtomogram curation and crystallographic outlier rejection.
Significance — anchoring: cryo-EM validation beyond self-resolution; the processing-reproducibility problem the Map Challenge opened and did not close; archive completeness (arXiv:2311.17640); by analogy, estimation of a false-negative fraction with unverified negatives in screening epidemiology (Begg-Greenes; JRSS-C 2004).
Reason for silence: incentive-and-ownership gap plus a vocabulary effect — a complement map is a worse map of a less interesting thing, so nobody is rewarded for making it and no sorter developer is rewarded for publishing that their sorter discards signal; the work that happens is relabelled "reanalysis" of one biological system (P2), so a corpus-level question never forms. Secondary: an archive gap (uncleaned stacks are recent, so the audit was technically impossible until lately) and map-centric validation culture (no metric whose denominator is the rejected set). The silence is partial, not total — consistent with the Low grade, and it does not explain silence on the curator-overlap limb, which needs only micrographs.
Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status) — one adversary, per the rule that a Gate 2 rejection still gets one adversary on the Gate 0-3 record; its 9 Disguise queries exceed the 8-query floor, so Disguise was executed and verified, not unverified. Verbatim log: UQ-20261016-40-adversary-1.md.
1 | Triviality | The intake version's existence clause is answerable in a page: classification discards alternative conformers, and P2 recovered one at 3.2 A. | The graded version asks a pooled share and a reject-set Jaccard; neither number exists (record query 3 and adversary query 8 both find only per-paper particle tables; query 9 finds no processing ring trial). | Resolved (for the graded version; the intake clause is trivial)

7 | Reason for silence | The incentive/archive/validation mechanisms explain why the work is unrewarded, not why nobody asked — P1's authors did ask it in one sentence and P2 answered it for one entry. | The archive gap is a genuine new-data mechanism for the POOLED question; it does not explain silence on the curator-overlap limb, which the Map Challenge could have computed. | Partial
8 | Dissolution | "Data vs curator" dissolves into "how reproducible is stochastic classification"; "distinct state vs noise" dissolves into the open problem of how many classes are distinguishable (PMC12485487). | Limbs (a)/(c) survive as a concrete archive-level number; limb (b) as framed does partly dissolve. | Partial
Verification by the run session (two fresh-context checkers, one per load-bearing prior, each handed the claim and its source but not the reviewer's reasoning; P2's checker ran 4 searches and 7 fetches with 8 refusals or blocks, P1's ran 14 searches and 6 fetches with 3; full logs in batches/2026-10-16-1433/UQ-20261016-40-verification-alk.md and -filtering.md). The verdict stands and both of its legs change. The leg that carried it is struck; the leg that now carries it is narrower and was previously secondary.
(i) P2 DOES NOT ANSWER THE EXISTENCE LIMB, because the object it works on is not the candidate's. EMPIAR-10930 deposits no curated final particle stack at all: its imagesets are "micrographs - multiframe" (13,618 TIFF) and "micrographs - single frame" (13,618 motion-corrected MRC), and the ~18M figure is picked-particle STAR coordinates, not an accept/reject record. A per-particle accept-or-reject label from the ORIGINAL study is therefore not recoverable from the archive, and the new work could not know which particles the original rejected even in principle. What P2 demonstrates is a distinct state recovered by re-processing the same raw micrographs - not a distinct state recovered from the particles a curator discarded. On the candidate's unit of analysis the two are not comparable, and the record's "affirmative published answer to the existence limb" does not survive. This is the same failure the ledger keeps meeting: a real paper, quoted accurately, aimed at a different object.
(ii) The curator-divergence evidence is weaker than the record states. The "6 of the 10 most populated classes after initial 2D classification do not correspond" comparison is to a published 2D-classification FIGURE in the original paper, not to the original's particle selection. That is a figure-level observation, and the record's wording makes it sound like a particle-level audit.
(iii) P2's own numbers, corrected. The deposited reanalysis is published as "Reanalysis of cryo-EM data reveals ALK-cytokine assemblies with both 2:1 and 2:2 stoichiometries", PLoS Biol 23 (2025), doi 10.1371/journal.pbio.3003124, PMID 40208865 - it reports BOTH states and does not refute the original's 2:2. PDB 9G5I's provenance wording is confirmed ("after re-processing of EMPIAR-10930 data"). The new map at 3.2 A is LOWER in resolution than EMD-24095's 2.27 A (not 2.3); the preprint's "massively improved" is improvement over the authors' own earlier processing stage, not over the original deposition, which is easy to invert on a skim. EMD-51087 prints two particle counts differing by 45 (18,053,750 against 18,053,705) and the archive does not resolve which is the typo. The final count written "142.986" uses a decimal point as a thousands separator and is 142,986, confirmed against EMD-51087. The original's own two archive records disagree on the construct (EMD-24095: residues 673-1025; EMPIAR-10930: 648-1025), and the cytokine is called AUG-alpha in the original archive and ALKAL2 in the new one, so matching the depositions on ligand name fails.
(iv) P1 DOES reconstruct the complement, and that part of the record holds. It builds maps from the particles its own filter rejected, for TWO entries: EMPIAR-10024 (lowest-scoring 12k and 18k, reaching 5.44 A and 4.67 A, with the complement relation arithmetically exact against the stated 43.5k total - 31+12 = 43 and 25+18 = 43) and EMPIAR-10093 (lowest-scoring 90k, 4.38 A). Size-matched random subsets are a real control in the paper, applied in at least three places, with the principle stated: "To compare these metrics meaningfully, the reconstructions need to be performed with similar number of particles."
(v) BUT THE SPECIFIC PAIR THE RECORD LEANS ON IS NOT THE CONTROL IT CLAIMS. The 84k-versus-90k contrast on EMPIAR-10093 is NOT size-matched - the subsets differ by about 7% - and the paper never describes them as size-matched, disjoint or complementary. EMPIAR-10093's stack total is stated nowhere readable, so complementarity could not be established at all: 84,000 + 90,000 = 174,000 would fit a ~174k stack, but that contradicts the same paragraph's "over 80% of the particles must be retained", while a ~105k total would force roughly a 69,000-particle overlap between the "top 84k" and the "lowest 90k". That arithmetic check did not pass; it could not be run. So "the candidate's own control has already been run on this pair" is withdrawn.
(vi) P1 NEVER TESTS THE HYPOTHESIS IT NAMES, and this is what the verdict now rests on. The rejected sets are shown only as map-quality numbers. There is no 3D classification and no heterogeneity analysis of any rejected set, and nowhere a rate, share or count of how often a rejected set holds an identifiable distinct state, under any stated criterion. The hypothesis appears in exactly one hedged sentence closing its section, verbatim: "It is important to note that the filtered-out particles may exhibit different conformation(s) of the molecule, implying heterogeneity." Posed in print, left untested - which is asked-but-open, and still Low.
(vii) P1's four attributes, corrected. cryoEF is not an endpoint but the software used to assess one: the paper's three metrics are resolution, B-factor and ANGULAR DISTRIBUTION ("The angular distribution of a given set of particles was assessed using the software cryoEF"). "One expert's manual selection" over-specifies - the paper says "An expert-selected set of classes was used to obtain a manual selection of particles" and never states how many experts. The unit set is wider than five entries: a separate four-entry EMPIAR test set (10024, 10288, 10547, 10955), 50 eBIC user datasets, and EMPIAR-10812 as training data, with the paper not reconciling its own "four" and "five"; the five codes (10024, 10255, 10097, 10093, 11233) are inferred from running text because every table was unreadable. And the estimand is two-sided rather than pure preservation: the paper also claims improvement over the full set ("better resolution, lower B-factors") and rescue of about 30% of the 50 eBIC datasets past an 11 A threshold.
(viii) The two independent literature questions came back NOT FOUND, which strengthens the un-asked side of the residual. No pooled statistic over many depositions of the share of picked particles surviving to the final reconstruction exists, and no cryo-EM processing ring trial has measured the overlap of independently curated retained or rejected sets. The adversary's own Gate 2 negative on the attrition statistic is independently reproduced, now from a third context.

Gate 4 completeness after verification: complete, and no late adversary is required - the first time in this ledger that a Gate 2 rejection whose ground later moved did not need one. The adversary that the 14:33 runner spawns for Gate 2 kills (LEDGER.md, Gate 5) ran all eight attacks on this record and returned no Unresolved, so when the "already answered" ground fell the log was already there to re-ground the verdict against. Without that change this entry would have needed a cold eight-attack rerun on a separate turn, as two entries in the 12:33 batch did.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3
Strongest remaining objection: Even setting the Gate 2 ground aside, attack 4 stands — the "property of the data or of the curator" dichotomy omits within-curator run-to-run stochasticity of RELION/cryoSPARC classification, so limb (b)'s Jaccard cannot attribute disagreement to curators without a replicate baseline the design does not contain; it is Partial rather than fatal only because the adversary's evidence is three unopened forum-thread titles. (Against the verdict itself, the strongest counter is that P2 answers only the existence limb for one entry and touches neither the pooled share nor the curator overlap; that is why the narrow (b)+(c) residual is routed rather than discarded, but an existence limb with a published affirmative answer in the candidate's own words is an under-quantified question, not an un-asked one.)
Rejection — gate and reason: Gate 2, novelty Low — ground re-based after verification, with the original ground struck.
  STRUCK: "the existence limb has an affirmative published answer (P2)". EMPIAR-10930 deposits micrographs and picked coordinates and no curated final stack, so the original study's accept/reject decisions are not recoverable and P2's 2:1 state came from re-processing the same raw micrographs, not from particles a curator discarded. Different object, different unit — see Verification (i)-(iii).
  STRUCK: "the complement reconstruction scored against size-matched random retained subsets has already been run". P1 does reconstruct complements on two entries, but the 84k-versus-90k pair the record leans on is not size-matched, is never stated disjoint, and could not be shown to be complementary at all — see Verification (iv)-(v).
  STANDS, and now carries the verdict alone: P1 names the candidate's existence hypothesis in print, verbatim — "It is important to note that the filtered-out particles may exhibit different conformation(s) of the molecule, implying heterogeneity." — and leaves it untested, with no 3D classification of any rejected set and no rate, share or count of distinct-state recovery under any criterion. A question posed in print and not answered is asked-but-open, which is Low, which is Rejected. The verdict is unchanged and its basis is narrower: this is no longer a question with a published answer, it is a question somebody wrote down and nobody ran.
  Validated was unreachable regardless, since novelty below Medium bars it; Gate 4 returned no Unresolved attack and a verified Disguise sweep.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): open PMC12485487 and PMC6086358, which adversary 1 could not open within budget, before any re-intake of the (b)+(c) residual; then count how many EMPIAR entries actually deposit an uncleaned stack, since that count bounds whether (c) is a study or a case series.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): Routed, with the scope inverted by verification. The row carries the EXISTENCE question on P1's own terms — whether a filtered-out particle set holds a distinct conformation — because that is the question P1 poses in print and leaves untested, and because it turns out not to be answered by P2 after all. The pooled share and the operator-dependence are NOT routed: no paper poses either, and a quantity nobody has asked for is not an open problem (the ledger's own routing rule (a)). They belong in a fresh Gate 0 intake, carrying attack 4's defect as a condition — a Jaccard across curators cannot attribute disagreement to curators without a within-curator replicate baseline, since RELION/cryoSPARC classification is itself stochastic run to run. The row is appended to ledger/routed-open-problems.md and was checked present there before this line was written.

ID: UQ-20261016-41
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): STEM — numerical computing / scientific software (computer arithmetic, libm implementation); adjacent AI (kernel numerics, GPU fast-math)

Question (canonical): For the elementary functions in deployed math libraries, how do the rate of last-bit disagreement between implementations and the distribution of error against the correctly-rounded result change when measured over the argument distribution that real scientific and machine-learning codes actually generate, rather than over the uniform-over-representable-domain weighting on which published worst-case error figures rest?
(Gate 1 reformulation used, one only, recorded in full in batches/2026-10-16-1633/UQ-20261016-41-record.md: fixed precision, RNE, implementation set I = {glibc, LLVM-libc, a vendor CPU library, a GPU device library + its fast-math variant}, F = {exp, log, pow, sin, cos, tan, erf, exp2, rsqrt, tanh}; per observed argument x the predicates D(x) = "members of I disagree", E(x) = "member differs from the MPFR correctly-rounded value", with ulp error e(x); report Pr[D(x)] and the distribution of e(x) under (i) usage weighting from an instrumented corpus and (ii) uniform weighting over the representable domain, plus the per-function ratio.)

Alternative formulations:
- Are the arguments at which glibc, LLVM-libc, vendor CPU and GPU math libraries disagree reachable by production code at all, or do the documented worst-case ulp errors live in regions real programs never visit?
- What is the usage-weighted, as opposed to domain-weighted, accuracy of deployed libm implementations, measured by interposing on the math-function calls of a pre-specified corpus of instrumented workloads?

Motivating gap: Shipped libraries publish "known maximum error" tables, and the CORE-MATH/Zimmermann accuracy reports (glibc242.pdf, opened) obtain their figures by MPFR reference plus exhaustive binary32 sweeps and recursive black-box worst-case search over the integer encoding above it, with explicitly no function-specific or application-derived test ranges. Every published figure is therefore an extremum or a domain-uniform/adversarial sweep; the argument distribution real codes feed these functions is never the weighting. The regime where this bites is narrow by construction (transformer kernels call exp on max-subtracted logits, rsqrt in normalisation) and worst on GPU fast-math paths, and the LLVM-libc GPU math effort (discourse thread 84570, opened) is choosing its test distribution and oracle now with no application data.

Presuppositions: (1) deployed implementations differ from correct rounding and from each other by >0.5 ulp on some arguments — ESTABLISHED from opened sources (glibc242.pdf; RLIBM-32 Table 1); (2) the argument set a workload feeds a function is a well-defined measurable object — CONTESTED (VPREC-libm finds call-site indices "may not match" across two input sets of one application), so stability is part of the answer condition; (3) calls can be intercepted without changing the computation — PARTLY ESTABLISHED for dynamically linked CPU calls (VPREC-libm LD_PRELOAD, needs -fno-builtin; "not applicable to statically linked programs"; Glatard 2015 independently: "ltrace cannot be used on statically-linked tools"), CONTESTED for inlined intrinsics, vectorised entry points, -ffast-math and GPU device functions; (4) MPFR correct rounding is an adequate oracle — ESTABLISHED; (5) last-bit disagreement matters downstream — CONTESTED and deliberately NOT required ("reachable but inconsequential" is admissible).

What would count as an answer: per function, (a) the fraction of observed calls at which I disagrees and at which a given member differs from the MPFR value, and (b) the e(x) distribution — each under usage weighting and under uniform weighting, with the ratio, intervals, a stability check (reproduces across inputs to one workload and across workloads of a class), and a stated share of calls hidden from interposition. Both directions pre-stated and admissible: usage-weighted rates far below the domain-uniform rate would show the published worst cases are effectively unreachable; comparable or higher rates would show real codes concentrate in the bad regions.

Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 11 in the Gate 2 record + 27 new-vocabulary queries across three adversaries = 38; full lists in batches/2026-10-16-1633/UQ-20261016-41-record.md and UQ-20261016-41-adversary-{1,2,3}.md. Most informative: own-field obvious-title form ("characterizing the use of elementary math functions in HPC applications: argument distributions and required accuracy") → no such paper; software-reliability "operational profile" usage-weighted accuracy → the usage-weighting method is named there and has never been pointed at numerical accuracy (the method-owning-field negative); mandated already-published-fraction query → recorded "no published proportion-of-inputs figure", FALSIFIED by three adversaries on one query each ("RLIBM percentage of inputs where glibc float function produces incorrectly rounded results exhaustive all 2^32 inputs") → RLIBM-32 Table 1; neuroimaging reproducibility ("Glatard reproducibility of neuroimaging analyses across operating systems glibc math functions") → production libm disagreement already demonstrated by call tracing; AI-accelerator softmax vocabulary → approximate-exp evaluations declare a uniform domain and report Top-1, not ulp; dynamic value profiling / FPSpy and Herbgrind/NSan shadow-value vocabularies → mature argument-value profiling whose endpoint is bitwidth or exceptions, never library ulp error (Herbgrind/NSan COULD NOT READ, budget).

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
P1. RLIBM-32, arXiv:2104.04043 (opened and quoted by two adversaries; harness confirmed via rutgers-apl/rlibm-32 README). UNIT: a binary32 input encoding. ENDPOINT: number of inputs with incorrectly rounded results, exhaustive over all 2^32. REFERENCE: MPFR/correct rounding; glibc, Intel libm, CR-LIBM, MetaLibm as the libraries measured. ESTIMAND: the count over the whole format (glibc expf 1.7E5, lnf 4.2E5, sinhf 7.1E7; Intel expf 2.5E5). Samples "proportional to the number of representable values"; does not restrict ranges by profiling real programs.
P2. Chatelain et al., VPREC-libm, arXiv:2005.02732 (opened). UNIT: one libm call site in one binary. ENDPOINT: minimum sufficient output precision per call site, by dichotomic search; operand intervals and call counts as by-products. REFERENCE: internal binary128 via Verificarlo-VPREC. ESTIMAND: smallest per-call-site precision keeping program output within user criteria.
P3. Glatard et al., Front. Neuroinform. 2015, 10.3389/fninf.2015.00012 (opened via publisher). UNIT: a libmath call in an FSL pipeline run. ENDPOINT: call-by-call classification of differences between glibc 2.5 and 2.18; first divergence located (expf ~1.5M calls in, cosf ~43M, sinf ~1.6M). REFERENCE: the other glibc version, no correctness oracle. ESTIMAND: whether and where a production pipeline's calls diverge — no rate, no distribution, no domain-uniform comparator.
Further neighbours, not graded on: Zimmermann glibc242.pdf (maximum over the format, opened); OpTuner arXiv:2107.05761 (opened in part — uses reachability by inspection, "POV-Ray only calls sin and cos with inputs between −π and π", to pick among implementations, with sound bounds over declared ranges); Darulova & Volkova arXiv:1811.10274 (user-declared input intervals, analysis bound); the cross-platform determinism literature (Mozilla 531915, JDK-4345910, Go 20319), which asked the qualitative reachability question and settled it by adopting fdlibm/StrictMath rather than measuring a rate. hal-04399159 "Input-aware accuracy characterization for approximate circuits" COULD NOT READ after three routes across two agents (Anubis denial; no DOI exists in search results) — grounds no grade in either direction.

Novelty — how this differs from each: vs P1 — same predicate and oracle, same libraries, but P1 is arm (ii) of the candidate, not the candidate: its unit is the encoding, its estimand a count over the whole format, and it explicitly disclaims application profiling; it covers binary32 for part of F only (no pow, tan, erf, tanh, rsqrt), its binary64 counts are small non-exhaustive lower bounds, and it has no GPU, vendor fast mode or fast-math member. The candidate's arm (i) and the ratio are not computable from it. vs P2 — the instrument, pointed at a different endpoint: how few bits suffice, against an internal binary128 oracle, so it never measures a deployed library's error, never compares libraries, and spends its argument profile as a search-ordering heuristic rather than reporting it. vs P3 — the reachability demonstration without the measurement: version-vs-version, no MPFR oracle, first-divergence rather than rate, traces truncated at a few million calls, static binaries untraceable. The candidate's distinctive content after Gate 4 is arm (i) — the usage-weighted rate and e(x) distribution for shipped non-correctly-rounded implementations, including GPU and fast-math — and the stability of that estimate.

Novelty confidence: Medium (close neighbours on separate limbs: P1 on arm (ii), P2 on the instrument, P3 on reachability). Not Low: across 38 queries in nine vocabularies nothing computes a usage-weighted per-function ulp-error rate or distribution for deployed libraries, and the three same-shape candidates opened differ in unit, endpoint and estimand. Held at Medium rather than higher because the search record that produced it is falsified on the one limb the protocol most explicitly required, and because hal-04399159, Herbgrind/NSan, Suresh et al. (TACO 2015, which did collect real libm argument streams for memoization hit rate), arXiv 2108.03129, 2107.05761 full text and 2510.13426 remain unread.

Significance — consequence: if usage-weighted rates fall far below the domain-uniform rate, the maximum-error tables are a poor proxy for shipped risk and the honest reporting unit becomes (worst case, usage-weighted rate); if comparable or higher, published worst cases understate exposure and per-function prioritisation changes to the functions whose bad regions coincide with where code lives. Either way it re-prices GPU fast-math variants, where the error is orders of magnitude larger and the argument band is narrow by construction. Discounted by adversary #3: for saturating functions the sign of the ratio appears fixed a priori by encoding-space bookkeeping, so the "factor" clause carries less information than the record claims.

Significance — audience: surviving audiences are GPU kernel authors choosing expf vs __expf, the LLVM-libc GPU math effort choosing its test distribution and oracle on the record now, vendor teams shipping selectable accuracy modes, and the HPC/ML cross-platform reproducibility community (Glatard's group acted on exactly this phenomenon). The CPU audience is deflating fast and on other grounds: LLVM-libc has proven worst-case bounds for all standard univariate double functions at speed parity (Microsoft C++ blog, 2026-09-16, opened), glibc is absorbing CORE-MATH function by function, and Intel announces "the first correctly rounded vector math library, to be available to users in mid-2026" (arXiv:2605.15547 abstract, opened).

Significance — fecundity: makes askable whether a usage-weighted accuracy figure should be a reported library property and over whose corpus; whether measured argument ranges are narrow and stable enough to drive domain-specialised correctly-rounded code generation (Metalibm/RLIBM take the range as declared); what an interposable boundary for GPU device functions would cost; reachability as a prioritisation metric for correctness work generally; and the deliberately separated propagation question.

Significance — anchoring: the standardisation push toward correctly-rounded elementary functions; bitwise irreproducibility in HPC and ML across platforms and libraries, where the mechanism is usually asserted rather than localised to specific calls; and the fast-math-safety argument, currently conducted with worst-case numbers on one side and anecdote on the other.

Reason for silence: a disciplinary boundary plus an incentive asymmetry, with an instrument gap on the newest half. Computer arithmetic's unit of proof is the extremum or an exhaustive count over the format — both auditable and portable, as a corpus-weighted figure is not. The people holding the argument distributions (application and kernel developers) have no reason to produce an accuracy report, and their instruments are aimed at time, bitwidth or memoization hit rate. The one community that built the needed instrument pointed it at a different endpoint and discarded the profile (P2). Adversary #3 adds a belief gap the record omits: the Muller/Lefèvre working heuristic that bits beyond the rounding position behave randomly makes usage weighting look irrelevant a priori. Weakened by RLIBM-32: the discipline does publish counts, so a frequency figure is publishable there and still nobody asked for the usage weighting.

Adversarial log (3 independent adversaries, fresh context, 9 new-vocabulary Disguise queries each = 27; verbatim logs in UQ-20261016-41-adversary-{1,2,3}.md; status shown per adversary A1/A2/A3):
| 1 Triviality | Arm (ii) is a lookup (RLIBM-32 Table 1, exhaustive binary32 counts per library); for correctly-rounded members D(x)=0 by construction; and the ratio may follow from encoding-space bookkeeping with no corpus (A3's arithmetic: ~97% binary64 / ~88% binary32 of uniform mass for exp lands where every implementation is exact). | Where the misrounded inputs lie relative to a logit band is reported nowhere; absolute usage-weighted rates, e(x) histograms, binary64, pow/erf/tanh/rsqrt and the stability check are not available from print; A3's premises are self-labelled unsourced, so Partial at best under the sourcing rule. | Resolved / Resolved / Partial |
| 2 Disguise | Renamed equivalents found on separate limbs: RLIBM's own "how often is a deployed library wrong?" with a different weighting (A1,A2,A3); the reachability form asked and answered in neuroinformatics (Glatard 2015) and in the determinism/desync practitioner literature (A1,A3); OpTuner's POV-Ray range reachability (A3); approximate-circuits "input-aware accuracy characterization" still unread after three routes. | 27 new queries (Chinese own-field, 1970s Cody/ELEFUNT, HPC/climate reproducibility, approximate computing, AI-accelerator softmax, dynamic value profiling, SE reachability, French arithmetic, memoization, shadow-value) surfaced no usage-weighted ulp-error distribution or usage/domain contrast for deployed libm; the same-shape hits differ in unit, endpoint and estimand. | Partial / Partial / Partial |
| 3 Combinatorial novelty | "Operational profile" x "libm accuracy" could be decorative re-weighting of someone else's table; the only real interface problem (observability) is inherited. | RLIBM's counts span ~1 to 7.1E7 inputs within one library, so the misrounding set is wildly non-uniform in function and in domain, which makes the weighting a measurement; and whether usage distributions are stable enough to be a reportable library property is a genuine unknown the answer condition tests. | Resolved / Resolved / Partial |

No Unresolved status on any attack from any adversary, so the fatal-objection rule is not triggered; every adversary independently recommended Provisional. Disguise was executed by all three (9 new-vocabulary queries each), so it is verified-but-Partial, not unverified.

Verification by the run session (one fresh-context checker over both priors and the usage-weighting question; 13 searches, 6 fetches, 2 refusals; full log in batches/2026-10-16-1633/UQ-20261016-41-verification.md). The verdict stands at Provisional. Arm (ii)'s prior art is confirmed, but the record over-reads what that prior art covers, and the single most important correction is that it cannot reach arm (i) at all.
(i) ARM (ii)'s PRIOR ART IS REAL. RLIBM-32 is a complete, format-uniform census of the binary32 domain: every one of the 2^32 input bit-patterns counts the same, each library is scored against the correctly-rounded oracle, and no usage weighting, application profile or empirical argument distribution appears anywhere in the paper. So the candidate's arm (ii) under uniform weighting is prior art for binary32, as the record says.
(ii) BUT TABLE 1 CANNOT GROUND ARM (i), AND THE RECORD IMPLIES IT CAN. Table 1 tabulates COUNTS OF INPUTS WITH WRONG RESULTS per library, each measured against the same oracle. Two libraries can both be wrong on an input and still agree with each other, so wrong-input counts cannot be differenced into a pairwise disagreement count. RLIBM-32 reports no implementation-versus-implementation comparison anywhere, and touches no GPU library and no fast-math variant. The candidate's first arm — how often deployed implementations disagree with EACH OTHER in the last bit — is untouched by it.
(iii) Four corrections to how the record cites RLIBM-32. Table 1's unit is "the number of inputs with wrong results", a count, not a rate; any percentage (0.70% for glibc float log10, say) is the reader's arithmetic, not the paper's. The words "exhaustive" and "exhaustively" never appear in its evaluation text and no sentence says "we evaluated all 2^32 inputs" — the exhaustiveness is carried by the caption's definitions, and the "2^32" sentence in section 4.1 is about something else. The word "sampled" DOES appear, but belongs to the polynomial-generation algorithm and weights by the density of representable values, i.e. by the format, never by program usage, so it must not be read as a usage weighting. And the library set is eight columns, not two: RLibm-32, glibc float, glibc double, Intel float, Intel double, CR-LIBM, MetaLibm float and MetaLibm double, over ten float functions, with posit32 in a separate Table 2.
(iv) Prior 2 confirmed on five of six absences and corrected on two readings. VPREC-libm never evaluates the deployed library's own error, never compares implementations against each other, uses call frequency only as a search-ordering heuristic ("we prioritize the call-site exploration by call frequency as a heuristic") and never as a weight, has no uniform-over-domain comparator, covers one application (SGP4), and has no GPU — all confirmed. Two corrections: its reference is a FAITHFULLY rounded result at precision p derived from a binary128 computation, not certified correct rounding, so it is a weaker guarantee than RLIBM-32's oracle and the two references are not interchangeable; and the application's test suite is not part of the oracle for the precision search — it validates the minimal SGP4 port, while the acceptance predicate is the user-specified correctness criteria.
(v) THE CENTRAL NEGATIVE IS INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED. Thirteen further searches found NO published measurement of elementary-function error, or of cross-implementation disagreement, weighted by an empirically observed argument distribution. The two priors bracket the question without answering it: RLIBM-32 measures error with no usage weighting, VPREC-libm uses real usage but does not measure error. One lead was left unopened when the fetch budget ran out — the LLVM libc GPU math profiling and conformance work — and it should be opened before this grade is relied on.
(vi) Half of one claim is marked unread rather than checked: whether the wider RLIBM project (beyond this paper) reports cross-implementation disagreement could not be established, because the repository read was refused and the companion papers were not opened.

Gate 4 completeness after verification: complete. No fatal ground was dissolved — three adversaries left every attack Partial and none Unresolved — and the Gate 2 correction above narrows the prior art rather than removing it, so the Medium-with-a-close-neighbour cap stands and no re-attack is owed.

Scores: Well-posedness 3/3 · Significance 2/3

Strongest remaining objection, as narrowed by verification: the candidate is one weighting away from an already-answered question on ONE of its two arms — RLIBM-32 publishes, per library and function over the whole binary32 domain, counts of inputs whose result is not correctly rounded, so arm (ii) under uniform weighting is prior art rather than new measurement. The narrowing matters and is recorded in Verification (ii): because every library in that table is scored against the same oracle, two libraries can both be wrong on an input and still agree with each other, so those counts cannot be differenced into a disagreement count, and arm (i) — how often deployed implementations disagree with EACH OTHER — is untouched by it, as are GPU libraries and fast-math variants, which the paper never covers. The rest of the objection stands: the reachability limb was asked and answered qualitatively in two other literatures (Glatard 2015; cross-platform determinism), and the surviving novel content is a corpus-relative number with no sampling frame, on a corpus the record never names, measured by an instrument that is blind precisely where the significance now rests (fused GPU and vectorised kernels that never cross a libm boundary). The Gate 2 record cannot be trusted as written: the one query the protocol most explicitly mandated — whether the fraction had already been computed and published — returned the wrong answer and was overturned by a single query from each of three independent adversaries, so the Medium grade rests on the adversaries' searching, not the record's.
Promotion requires: re-grading novelty with arm (ii) struck FOR UNIFORM WEIGHTING IN BINARY32 ONLY (RLIBM-32 Table 1 added as nearest prior on that arm, Glatard 2015 as second) while arm (i) is retained, since verification established that Table 1 cannot be differenced into the pairwise disagreement count arm (i) asks for; opening the one lead the verification budget did not reach, the LLVM libc GPU math profiling and conformance work, before any grade is relied on; and the implementation set re-scoped to non-correctly-rounded members (vendor fast modes, GPU device libraries, fast-math), the domain-uniform comparator redefined per exponent band or over the non-trivial domain with the "by what factor" headline dropped, the corpus named with its sampling frame and an IR/binary-level argument-capture instrument (e.g. SASS operand capture with off-line replay) specified for inlined and GPU calls, and hal-04399159 read by a working route plus Herbgrind/NSan, Suresh et al. (TACO 2015), arXiv:2108.03129, 2107.05761 full text and 2510.13426 each confirmed to compute no usage-weighted per-function libm error rate — after which Validated also requires a Gate 2 record rerun, since the present one failed its mandated check.

Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): intersect what is already published against where code is known to live — take RLIBM-32's exhaustive binary32 misrounding sets and ask where in the format they sit, then compare against a handful of recorded argument bands from existing traces (VPREC-libm's SGP4 call-site intervals, Glatard's FSL traces) before building any new instrument.

Routing (if rejected as already-asked): n/a — not rejected as already-asked; no row appended to ledger/routed-open-problems.md.
