ID: UQ-20261016-56
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): Biology — evolutionary genomics / cytogenetics / phylogenetic comparative methods (chromosome-number evolution). Method-owning neighbours: metrology (agreement between two imperfect measurement systems), statistics (measurement error in a discrete variable).
Question (canonical): Over the frame of species holding both (a) a chromosome-level assembly in a public archive, pseudo-chromosome count extracted under a pre-declared rule, and (b) a published haploid chromosome number in a compiled karyotype resource (CCDB, coleoguy/karyotypes), matched by accepted name against one backbone: what is the rate, signed direction and taxonomic structure of disagreement between the two counts; and when one chromosome-number evolution model is refitted on one fixed phylogeny per clade using assembly-derived counts in place of cytogenetic counts, by how much do estimated polyploidization, demi-polyploidization, fission and fusion rates move, relative to the movement produced by perturbing cytogenetic counts at the measured error rate and direction alone?
Alternative formulations: (1) How often does a chromosome-level genome assembly contradict the karyotype of record for the same species, and in which direction does it err? (2) Is the chromosome-number data underlying chromosome-evolution models measurement-error-free, and what does realistic count error do to inferred rates of polyploidy and rearrangement?
Motivating gap: EBP/DToL/VGP output makes a pseudo-chromosome count a second, high-throughput realization of haploid number for species already carrying a 20th-century karyotype. ChromEvol-class models treat each compiled count as observed without error; the only literature interrogating them tests model adequacy, not data error (Rice & Mayrose 2021). Hjelmen 2024 states the alignment of scaffold number with haploid count as an expectation in print and then uses the count only as a scaling denominator; Rice & Mayrose name count-collection error in their Discussion as an unexamined candidate cause of adequacy failure.
Presuppositions: (1) the pseudo-chromosome count measures haploid number — CONTESTED, and on adversarial evidence contested in practice, not just in principle (see attack 4); (2) the cytogenetic count of record is retrievable and attributable to a matching species identification — CONTESTED (synonymy, cryptic species, karyotype races); (3) the intersection is large enough, with taxonomic spread, to estimate a clade-wise rate — SUPPORTED at least for Lepidoptera (452 chromosome-level assemblies, >half with light-microscopy counts: Lukhtanov & Pazhenkova 2025); (4) ChromEvol-class inference is sensitive to count error at realistic magnitudes — CONTESTED, untested; (5) neither measurement is a gold standard — CONTESTED by field practice, which treats the karyotype as the validator.
What would count as an answer: (i) a discordance table with explicit denominators by clade, signed direction, and a pre-specified subset adjudicated by a third method (FISH, optical mapping, Hi-C contact-map inspection, fresh meiotic counts); (ii) refits of one model on one fixed phylogeny under cytogenetic versus assembly-derived counts, reporting rate displacement with uncertainty, plus a perturbation simulation at the measured error rate and direction as the internal comparator. A null — discordance rare and rates unmoved — settles it the other way and would license pooling.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 37 recorded queries in total — 11 at Gate 2 (full list and 6 fetch outcomes: batches/2026-10-16-2155/UQ-20261016-56-record.md) plus 26 Disguise queries across three independent adversaries (8 / 9 / 9; full lists in UQ-20261016-56-adversary-1.md, -2.md, -3.md). Most informative: "Genome size and chromosome number are critical metrics for accurate genome assembly assessment in Eukaryota" (own-field own-words title query) → Hjelmen 2024, GENETICS 227(4):iyae099, opened via DOI→publisher: chromosome number enters only as a scaling denominator, no count-vs-karyotype comparison. "'how often' genome assemblies agree with karyotypes chromosome number mismatch audit proportion of species" (mandatory fraction query) → no published fraction at Gate 2. "measurement error in chromosome number data biases ChromEvol estimates" → model-adequacy lineage only. A3-D8 "chromosome numbers derived from chromosome-level genome assemblies compared with cytogenetic records discrepancy assembly-based karyotype Erebia Hymenoptera fishes" → THE KILL: Lukhtanov & Pazhenkova 2025, opened on the publisher site. A3-D9 "'karyotypes versus genomes' … cytogenetics versus genomics chromosome number comparison" → confirms a named per-species genre (Traut et al., "Karyotypes versus Genomes"). A3-D7 → Animal Chromosome Count database (Román-Palacios et al. 2021), an animal karyotype resource the record did not name. A2 curation-vocabulary query → DToL curation teaching material; A1 avian query → Kim et al. 2022 (eight microchromosomes newly recovered on re-assembly). COULD NOT READ, by all four agents: Syst Biol 70(5):1061, never identified; it grounds no grade in either direction.
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources): PRIOR 1 — Lukhtanov VA, Pazhenkova EA (2025), "Cytogenetics of insects in the era of chromosome-level genome assemblies", Vavilovskii Zhurnal Genetiki i Selektsii 29(2):230–237, DOI 10.18699/vjgb-25-26; read on the publisher site (vavilov.elpub.ru). Unit: species within Lepidoptera (452 chromosome-level assemblies as of 15 May 2024, "[f]or more than half of them, there are data on chromosome numbers obtained using light microscopy methods" → >226 compared; that arithmetic is the adversary's own, from the paper's two stated figures). Endpoint: agreement of haploid chromosome number between assembly and light microscopy. Comparator: the other measurement system. Estimand: whether assemblies are a reliable source of karyotype data; reports "complete agreement" and concludes "chromosome level genome assemblies are a reliable source of information on karyotypes", while holding that "[c]lassical cytogenetics is also needed to validate chromosome level genome assemblies". PRIOR 2 — Wright CJ, Stevens L, Mackintosh A, Lawniczak M, Blaxter M (2024), "Comparative genomics reveals the dynamics of chromosome evolution in Lepidoptera", Nat Ecol Evol (PMID 38383850; preprint bioRxiv 2023.05.12.540473, read). Unit: species/assembly within one order plus Merian elements; endpoint: parsimony-reconstructed fusion/fission events; comparator: parsimony reconstructions and a uniform null; estimand: number and phylogenetic distribution of rearrangements. Cytology appears as undenominated narrative corroboration. PRIOR 3 — Rice A, Mayrose I (2021), "Model adequacy tests for probabilistic models of chromosome-number evolution", New Phytol 229:3602–3613, DOI 10.1111/nph.17106 (read). Unit: clade dataset (233 angiosperm datasets); endpoint: four data-based summary statistics plus inference error; comparator: datasets simulated under the fitted model; estimand: model adequacy and inference error from MODEL inadequacy. (Hjelmen 2024, GENETICS 227(4):iyae099, remains the title-nearest paper in the candidate's own field; its comparator is genome size, not the count.)
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs PRIOR 1 — this is the difference that decides the entry, and it is one of scope and downstream analysis, not of question. P1 poses the record's own alternative formulation 1 in the clade the record itself calls densest, supplies a denominator (>226 species) and a match share ("complete agreement"), and answers it. The candidate adds a cross-taxon frame, a signed-direction limb, an adjudication subset and the model-refit limb (ii) — i.e. a corpus swap plus a sensitivity analysis on an asked and answered question, which this ledger grades as a disguised known rather than as un-asked. vs PRIOR 2 — different estimand (events, not between-method discordance), no denominator, no rates fitted, but it touches the same two measurements in the same clade and calls them consistent. vs PRIOR 3 — shares the machinery and the downstream quantities but attributes error to the model against a simulated null; counts are taken from CCDB as given, with no second measurement system and no rate-displacement estimand. Its Discussion names count-collection error as a possible cause, which is a named possibility, not a posed question.
Novelty confidence: Low
(Gate 2 graded this Medium on 11 queries; that grade is superseded. The adversarial sweeps — 26 further queries in vocabularies Gate 2 did not try, including the cytogenetics-review and "karyotypes versus genomes" framings — found limb (i) asked and answered with a denominator in the candidate's own target field. The Gate 2 novelty paragraph had itself conceded that "a reader could reasonably say the qualitative answer is already in print and only the denominator is missing"; the denominator is in print.)
Significance — consequence: If discordance were common and directional (assembly below karyotype, the plausible prior given that under-assembly dominates: Kim et al. 2022 recovered eight previously absent zebra finch microchromosomes; Peona et al. 2018 found 7–42% of expected bird genome missing), the two sources would not be interchangeable and the direction would be a bias mimicking descending dysploidy. If rare and symmetric, pooling would be licensed and count error retired as an explanation for the Rice & Mayrose adequacy failures. Adversarially weakened: under non-independence a near-zero discordance is equally consistent with curation-to-karyotype, so the no-branch does not in fact license pooling — the "a null is a licence, not a shrug" argument fails.
Significance — audience: (a) chromosome-number model developers (Mayrose/Rice, Freyman & Höhna, Blackmon) — would gain or lose a reason to add an observation layer for count error; (b) curators of compiled count resources (CCDB, coleoguy/karyotypes, ACC) — but Blaxter, Leech & Lunt 2024 (Wellcome Open Res 9:55) already record provenance ("[w]hen reporting karyotypes, we have referenced the origin of the data") and already ingest "karyotypes inferred from genome sequencing projects", so this gain is largely already banked; (c) EBP/DToL/VGP curation teams — but curation material shows the karyotype is the target, and a mismatch is investigated regardless of any base rate; (d) the polyploidy/WGD macroevolution community, the only audience whose stake survives intact, and only if limb (ii) is non-null.
Significance — fecundity: Opens the right observation model for a count measured by two instruments with asymmetric failure modes; whether assembly-count error is predictable from repeat content, genome size, heterochromatin or sequencing platform; whether Rice & Mayrose's adequacy failures partition into model-structure and data-error components; the same audit in adjacent compiled-trait literatures (genome size — already done, bioRxiv 2025.11.26.690794; ploidy; sex-determination); and the reflexive question of how often a curated assembly's count is set from the literature karyotype.
Significance — anchoring: (1) Rice & Mayrose's unexplained adequacy failures across 233 angiosperm datasets, for which they list count-collection error among candidate causes; (2) Hjelmen 2024's demonstration that assembly metrics routinely fail against an independent measurement of a different genome quantity, plus its untested scaffold-vs-karyotype expectation; (3) the Lepidoptera finding that fusions concentrate in particular lineages beyond a uniform null.
Reason for silence: Claimed as new instrument (the intersection barely existed before ~2020), disciplinary boundary with no shared key (names versus accessions), and incentive asymmetry (in a genome paper a mismatch is read as an assembly defect and fixed in curation rather than published). The new-instrument mechanism is corroborated. The other two are undercut by the adversarial evidence: cytogeneticists did cross the boundary and did ask limb (i) as soon as the intersection became large (Lukhtanov & Pazhenkova 2025), and DToL built the comparison into its pipeline (Blaxter et al. 2024), so the silence is partly fictitious for limb (i). It remains credible for limb (ii) alone, where comparative modellers inherit counts and have no instrument-level stake in them.
Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status): Three independent fresh-context adversaries ran all eight attacks (logs verbatim in batches/2026-10-16-2155/UQ-20261016-56-adversary-1.md, -2.md, -3.md); each row below carries the worst status across the three.

Judge's note on the fatal row: A3's kill is sourced to a primary publisher-site read with verbatim quotation, in the candidate's actual regime (Lepidoptera, chromosome-level assemblies versus light-microscopy counts), so it meets the standard for Unresolved rather than Partial. A3 flagged that the fetch tool truncated the sentence "Having compared these data, we found complete agreement in the haploid chromosome number calculations made using" and asked the judge to confirm it on the publisher PDF. This judge was barred from searching and did not confirm it. The row stands anyway on two grounds: the paper's conclusion sentence — "chromosome level genome assemblies are a reliable source of information on karyotypes" — was returned un-truncated and independently establishes that the comparison was performed and returned a positive verdict; and the frame figures (452 assemblies, "more than half" with microscopy counts) were likewise un-truncated. A materially qualified agreement would change the answer's content, not the fact that the question was posed and answered with a denominator in that clade, and a corpus swap onto an asked question is Rejected under the operating rules even where the exact variant is unmeasured. If the full sentence turns out not to report a comparison at all, that ground falls and Gate 4 would have to be re-judged on the remaining rows, which are Partial throughout and would support Provisional, never Validated.
Verification (post-batch, fresh-context checker, log UQ-20261016-56-verification.md): the kill's source is real and says what was claimed, on a weaker footing than the batch implied.
DOI 10.18699/vjgb-25-26 resolves to Lukhtanov and Pazhenkova, "Cytogenetics of insects in the era of chromosome-level genome assemblies", Vavilov Journal of Genetics and Breeding 29(2):230-237 (2025). Verified verbatim: "information on chromosome assemblies, including determination of the haploid number of chromosomes, is available for 452 species"; "For more than half of them, there are data on chromosome numbers obtained using light microscopy methods"; "Having compared these data, we found complete agreement in the haploid chromosome number calculations made using the bioinformatics approach and light microscopy methods"; and the conclusion "Examples of such validation reinforce the conclusion that chromosome level genome assemblies are a reliable source of information on karyotypes".
But it is a NARRATIVE REVIEW, and the comparison is a single summary sentence. The compared N is given only as "more than half" of 452, so about 226 or more, with no exact figure. There is no per-species table, no listed exceptions, no statistic, no confidence interval, and no model: the paper fits nothing and estimates no rate of fission, fusion or polyploidization, saying only qualitatively that karyotype change proceeds by simple fusions and fissions in the most parsimonious way. It also says classical cytogenetics is still needed to validate assemblies.
What that does and does not settle. It settles the candidate's premise: in the clade with the densest data, the two instruments have been compared and the reported discordance is zero, so a large discordance rate is not waiting to be found there, and limb (ii) — how far likelihood rate estimates move when assembly counts replace cytogenetic ones — has no signal to propagate in that clade. That is why the rejection stands: what is left is a corpus extension plus a conditional sensitivity analysis. What it does NOT settle is a measured rate with a denominator and CIs, which this review does not contain. One route could revive the line: a per-species audit of the comparison behind that sentence, published as a table, showing whether "complete agreement" conceals mismatches. The kill rests on a review's assertion, not on a table, and this entry says so rather than claiming more.

Scores: Well-posedness 3/3 · Significance 2/3
(Well-posedness upheld: both limbs name their evidence, denominators, stratification, adjudication subset, fixed phylogeny and internal comparator, and a null is pre-stated and informative; attack 5's two missing tie-break rules are a declarable gap, not ill-posedness. Significance downgraded from the record's 3/3 to 2/3: audiences (b) and (c) were shown to hold the practice already, and the pooling-licence branch fails under measurement non-independence, leaving (a) conditional on limb (ii) and (d) intact.)
Strongest remaining objection: Limb (i) is a published result, not an un-asked question — Lukhtanov & Pazhenkova 2025 (DOI 10.18699/vjgb-25-26) compared assembly-derived with light-microscopy haploid counts for more than half of 452 Lepidoptera chromosome-level assemblies, reported complete agreement and concluded that assemblies are a reliable source of karyotype information, which is the candidate's own alternative formulation 1 answered with a denominator in the clade whose data are densest; what remains is a corpus extension plus a downstream sensitivity analysis.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): None for this question as posed. If limb (ii) is ever re-posed on its own — how robust are ChromEvol-class rate estimates to tip-count misclassification at realistic rates and directions — the first step is to read Syst Biol 70(5):1061 (unidentified and unread by all four agents) and the ChromEvol documentation on ambiguous/multiple tip states, either of which may already cover it; that is a Gate 2 check, not a new candidate.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): Not routed. This is a disguised-known / answered rejection, not asked-but-open: limb (i) was asked and answered, so no row is added to ledger/routed-open-problems.md. Where it belongs for a future reader: the cytogenetic-validation literature — Lukhtanov & Pazhenkova 2025 (DOI 10.18699/vjgb-25-26); Traut et al., "Karyotypes versus Genomes" (Lepidoptera); Blaxter, Leech & Lunt 2024, "A catalogue of chromosome counts for Phylum Nematoda" (DOI 10.12688/wellcomeopenres.20550.1) for DToL/GoaT practice. Also noted for future Gate 2 frames: the Animal Chromosome Count database (Román-Palacios et al. 2021, J Evol Biol 34(8):1333), which this record omitted.

ID: UQ-20261016-57
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Rejected
Rejection — gate and reason: Gate 2, novelty Low (disguised known, already answered inside the candidate's own literature). Gate 4 ran late and separately against the Gate 0-3 record (one adversary, per the 14:33-batch rule) and returned Disguise (attack 2) Unresolved, which is independently fatal.
Domain(s): Biology — experimental/microbial evolution (target field, whose literature decides novelty). Method transplanted from community ecology (competitive intransitivity) and paired-comparison/tournament statistics (Bradley-Terry, Elo, Hodge/HHD).

Question (canonical): In a microbial long-term evolution experiment with an archived clone series, does the matrix of pairwise competitive-fitness measurements among archived clones admit a consistent one-dimensional ordering — how often are triples intransitive, and at what magnitudes relative to assay error — and does the published power-law deceleration of fitness gain survive re-estimation under a model that does not assume fitness is a scalar?

Alternative formulations:
- Is "fitness" in an evolution experiment a scalar, or a projection of a competition tournament onto one axis, and what does that projection do to the measured shape of adaptation?
- Transplanting the measurement of competitive intransitivity from community ecology to a frozen fossil record: what share of archived clone triples violate transitivity, and does the fitted trajectory law change when the cyclic component is modelled rather than discarded?
- Gate 1 reformulation (the one permitted; both versions stand): for a pre-registered round-robin of archived LTEE clones (>=1 clone per sampled time point, every pair at >=2 starting frequencies, >=3 replicates, propagated replicate-error model) — (a) what share of C(n,3) triples is cyclic under a pre-specified rule and what is the cycle-magnitude distribution against the error null; (b) what variance share of the pairwise selection-coefficient matrix is skew-symmetric (cyclic) rather than gradient/ranking under a Hodge-style decomposition; (c) what are the pre-registered deltas in fitted exponent and projected asymptote between the standard ancestor-referenced power law and a ranking-plus-cyclic fit.

Motivating gap: Published LTEE trajectories are built from ancestor-referenced head-to-head assays, which presuppose a single scalar fitness axis; non-transitive and frequency-dependent fitness has been reported since Paquin & Adams (1983); a 2025 preprint asserts frequency dependence is the general case. CORRECTED AT GATE 2: the premise that the deceleration has never been re-examined without a scalar/transitive axis is false — de Visser & Lenski (2002), LTEE paper XI, is titled "Rejection of non-transitive interactions as cause of declining rate of adaptation", uses five reference clones from five generations rather than the ancestor alone, and reports the non-transitive model rejected. It was the first hit on the mandatory own-field/own-words query.

Presuppositions:
1. Archived clones revivable and comparable across time points — ESTABLISHED (P1 competed 21 frozen time-point samples).
2. Assay precision finer than the triple-violation magnitudes of interest — CONTESTED and quantified against: P1 residual error ~5% of ln-fitness variance; P2 measurement error ~40% of the frequency-dependence slope variance; adversary F2 finds real archived-clone frequency dependence in Ara-1 at 0.9-5.4%, the same order as P1's residual. Honest deliverable is a bound, not a rate.
3. A tournament model supplies a meaningful alternative target — PARTLY CONTESTED (Bradley-Terry strength is itself scalar, so ranking plus an explicit skew-symmetric term is required); machinery exists and is named outside biology.
4. Intransitivity is not wholly an artefact of a single starting frequency — CONTESTED and substantially undercut: P2 already assays four starting frequencies on LTEE-background strains and reports ~75-80% of competitions frequency-dependent with triad-additivity deviations in that same design.
5. The published trajectory law is sensitive to non-scalar structure at the magnitudes measured — NOT ESTABLISHED, and thinner than intaken: Wiser et al. 2013 itself competed 40k/50k samples of nine populations against marked 40,000-generation clones (adversary F4).

What would count as an answer: A measured distribution of triple-violation magnitudes from a pre-registered round-robin of archived clones within and across populations and time points, against a propagated assay-error null; plus two fits of the same trajectory data (standard ancestor-referenced power law vs transitive-ranking-plus-cyclic decomposition) reporting the cyclic variance share and the resulting change in fitted exponent and projection. A null is as publishable as a positive. This specification is already satisfied in weaker form — limb (b) by P1's model-rejection test, limb (a) by P2's triad-additivity test — which is why the candidate fails at Gate 2, not Gate 1.

Novelty — queries run (query -> one-line result): 20 web searches and 9 fetches in total — 11 searches / 5 fetches at Gate 2, 9 searches / 4 fetches at Gate 4 (8 Disguise sweeps executed, so Disguise is verified, not unverified). Full lists: batches/2026-10-16-2155/UQ-20261016-57-record.md and batches/2026-10-16-2155/UQ-20261016-57-adversary-1.md. Most informative:
- (own field, own words; mandatory) "non-transitive fitness Escherichia coli long-term evolution experiment pairwise competition transitivity" -> FIRST HIT was the kill: de Visser & Lenski 2002, LTEE XI, "Rejection of non-transitive interactions as cause of declining rate of adaptation" (P1).

- "'Frequency-dependent fitness effects are ubiquitous' 2025 doi journal" -> recovered doi:10.1101/2025.08.18.670924 and a bioRxiv PDF route; the paper the intake had recorded COULD NOT READ opened on the first non-PMC attempt and became a near prior (P2).
- (method field's own vocabulary) "Hodge decomposition skew-symmetric cyclic component ranking pairwise comparison matrix ..." and "Bradley-Terry model microbial competition fitness ranking ..." -> tools exist and are named in tournament statistics (arXiv 2011.01825; arXiv 2412.14427) but are unapplied to microbial fitness. Negative recorded; this is the candidate's only residue.
- (Gate 4 Disguise, answer-search inside the LTEE's own later papers) "Wiser Ribeck Lenski 2013 power law ... non-transitive check supplement" -> Wiser et al. 2013 full text opened: 108 competitions of 40k/50k samples "against marked 40,000-generation clones", plus "Frequency-dependent interactions are weak in most populations" and "not expected to amplify gains relative to a distant ancestor, as fitness was measured here".
- (Gate 4 Disguise) "Maddamsetti Lenski Barrick ... clones from different generations Ara-1 competed against each other" -> bioRxiv 10.1101/017020 opened: C1 vs C2 archived clones at three starting frequencies, C2 advantage 5.4% / 2.9% / 0.9% at 10/50/90% start — same order as P1's residual error.
- Negatives in five further vocabularies (Kendall circular triads / coefficient of consistence; cyclic dominance / rock-paper-scissors EGT; pairwise invasibility / adaptive dynamics; network-meta-analysis loop inconsistency; spinning-top game geometry; German and French) -> no non-English or cross-field prior asking the candidate's exact estimand.

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
P1. de Visser & Lenski (2002), BMC Evol Biol 2:19, doi:10.1186/1471-2148-2-19 — https://bmcecolevol.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/1471-2148-2-19 — READ IN FULL at publisher route, twice independently (Gate 2 F1, Gate 4 F1). Unit: 21 whole-population samples of Ara-1, 0-20,000 generations. Endpoint: ln relative fitness from 315 competitions (21 x 5 x 3); sample x reference-clone ANOVA interaction plus cumulative-gain model contrast. Comparator: five marked reference clones from generations 0/5k/10k/15k/20k — deliberately not the ancestor alone. Estimand: whether a non-transitive model accounts for the deceleration. Result: interaction < 2% of variation, P > 0.5, residual ~5%; "the ANOVA tests all forms of non-transitivity"; "the non-transitive model is strongly rejected by the observed cumulative gains".
P2. "Frequency-dependent fitness effects are ubiquitous", bioRxiv doi:10.1101/2025.08.18.670924 (Ascensao et al.) — READ (bioRxiv PDF). Unit: reconstructed single/double mutants on REL606, not archived clones or a time series. Endpoint: per-cycle selection coefficient at four starting frequencies, plus an explicit additive-transitivity test over strain triads (s_ij = s_ik - s_jk, eight definitions). Comparator: REL606 and each panel member. Estimand: prevalence of frequency dependence (~75-80% significant) and magnitude of departure from additive transitivity (~+/-20%); measurement error ~40% of slope variance.
P3. "Adaptive evolution of nontransitive fitness in yeast", bioRxiv doi:10.1101/700302; venue confirmed at Gate 4 as eLife 2020, article 62238 (elifesciences.org/articles/62238 returned a JS shell — COULD NOT READ; authorship never asserted from an opened page, though body text was read via the bioRxiv PDF). Unit: three clones along one yeast lineage. Endpoint: fitness as log-ratio slope in pairwise competitions at various starting ratios. Estimand: whether nontransitive fitness can arise along a single line of descent. Result: yes, one bistable frequency-dependent ordering violation, mechanistically a killer-virus/nuclear-genome interaction.
P4 (method-field prior for the "what fraction" limb). Soliveres et al. (2018), J Ecology 106(3):852-864 — abstract and numbers read via Western Sydney research portal. Unit: species pairs/triplets, five taxa including soil bacteria. Endpoint: competitive outcome over the full pairwise matrix and every triplet. Estimand: share of triplets intransitive. Published number: 5-38% by taxon.
Additionally opened at Gate 4 and load-bearing: Wiser, Ribeck & Lenski (2013), Science 342:1364 (PDF at directory.natsci.msu.edu) and Maddamsetti, Lenski & Barrick, bioRxiv 10.1101/017020.

Novelty — how this differs from each:
vs P1: limb (b) IS P1's question, in the same organism and experiment, asked in P1's own title and answered no. The candidate differs only in era and machinery — the Wiser power-law exponent/projection over 50,000+ generations rather than the hyperbolic deceleration to 20,000, and an explicit ranking-plus-skew-symmetric variance partition rather than an ANOVA interaction term. P1's unit (population samples at a single 1:1 start) cannot in principle yield a per-triple statistic. That is a methodological upgrade of an asked-and-answered question.
vs P2: limb (a) is P2's triad-additivity test, already run on LTEE-background strains at four starting frequencies — including the multi-frequency requirement presupposition 4 was built to motivate. Differs in unit (archived evolved clones across a time series vs reconstructed mutants on the ancestor), statistic (cyclic-triple rate with error-referenced magnitudes vs signed additivity deviation) and deliverable (cyclic variance share plus trajectory re-fit vs a prevalence claim). A reader of P2 would say limb (a) has been asked.
vs P3: P3 asks whether nontransitivity can arise along a lineage and answers yes with one worked case; the candidate asks how often, how large, and whether the trajectory law moves. Genuinely different estimands, but P3 establishes the phenomenon, so the candidate is not opening the topic.
vs P4: P4 already publishes the exact fraction-of-intransitive-triples quantity for microbes among other taxa, so the transplant is not conceptually new — only its destination data set is.
vs Wiser et al. 2013 (surfaced at Gate 4, not at Gate 2): the power-law paper itself ran the non-ancestral-reference check (40k/50k samples of nine populations against marked 40,000-generation clones) and addressed the frequency-dependence objection in text. This narrows presupposition 5 to "the exponent was not itself re-fit", which is an estimator gap, not an unasked question.

Novelty confidence: Low

Significance — consequence: If the cyclic share is large, ancestor-referenced relative fitness is a projection that discards a measurable component and every quantity built on it (power-law exponent, the unbounded-vs-asymptotic argument, cross-population comparisons) carries an unmodelled bias term; if small, the convention is licensed and the field gains a published bound. The asymmetry is weak in practice because P1 already published the null for the trajectory and Wiser's own evolved-reference check pointed the same way — the marginal consequence is a tighter, power-law-era version of a result the field already acts on.

Significance — audience: Experimental-evolution laboratories reporting ancestor-referenced relative fitness (LTEE and descendants, yeast and Pseudomonas groups) would change reporting only if the cyclic share were non-trivial; trajectory-law theorists would gain or lose a nuisance parameter; community ecologists and tournament statisticians gain an application domain. Real audience, but it received the headline answer 23 years ago and has kept the convention since.

Significance — fecundity: Opens whether cyclic structure grows with divergence time, whether it concentrates in the ecologically differentiated populations, and whether the cyclic share predicts within-population coexistence. Reduced, because the most generative version was already asked in 2002.

Significance — anchoring: The unbounded-vs-asymptotic LTEE fitness argument; the macroscopic-epistasis account of deceleration (Good & Desai, arXiv 1408.4108); frequency dependence as the general case (P2); the coexistence role of intransitivity in ecology (P4).

Reason for silence: There was no silence to explain, and that is the finding. The question was asked and answered inside the LTEE's own numbered series in 2002, re-checked with an evolved reference in the 2013 power-law paper, and refreshed in triad-additivity form in 2025. The appearance of silence is an artefact of vocabulary and access routing: the target field writes "non-transitive interactions", never "intransitivity index" or "tournament inconsistency", so a Gate 2 run in the transplant's method vocabulary misses the on-point paper; and the 2025 preprint was recorded COULD NOT READ after PMC blocks but opened on the first bioRxiv attempt. The only genuinely silent part is the estimator transplant (no Bradley-Terry, Elo, Kendall-consistence, NMA-inconsistency or Hodge/HHD treatment of microbial fitness matrices), and there the mechanism is a credible disciplinary boundary — psychometrics, sports ranking and evidence synthesis do not share a readership with the competition-assay literature; three independent negative sweeps at Gate 4 confirm.

Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status) — adversary 1, fresh context, Gate 0-3 record only, run late and separately against a Gate 2 rejection; verbatim log at batches/2026-10-16-2155/UQ-20261016-57-adversary-1.md:
| 1 Triviality | Headline question answerable in a page from P1 (non-transitive model "strongly rejected"; interaction < 2%, P > 0.5) plus Wiser 2013's 108 competitions against marked 40,000-generation clones and its statement that frequency-dependent interactions are "not expected to amplify gains relative to a distant ancestor". | The reformulation's estimands (cyclic-triple rate vs error null, skew-symmetric variance share, exponent delta) are not computable from existing data: no round-robin clone matrix at multiple starting frequencies exists in any opened source. | Partial |
| 2 Disguise | Eight new-vocabulary sweeps (Kendall circular triads, cyclic dominance/EGT, pairwise invasibility, NMA loop inconsistency, spinning-top game geometry, German/French, two answer-searches inside the LTEE's own later papers) found no new paper with the exact estimand — but the answer-searches show the canonical question's main clause is a known question renamed: P1's title IS the question, P1's ANOVA "tests all forms of non-transitivity", and Wiser 2013 re-ran the non-ancestral-reference check. Tournament vocabulary renames "non-transitive model" + "sample x reference-clone interaction". | The residue (explicit cyclic-triple rate with replicate-error null over archived clones, skew-symmetric variance share, power-law exponent refit) appears in no opened source, with negatives recorded in three method vocabularies. | Unresolved (fatal) |
| 3 Combinatorial novelty | The interface problem ("is fitness a scalar") was formulated and tested natively inside the target field without the transplant; tournament statistics contributes an estimator for a problem the field already posed. | The decomposition yields a per-triple statistic and a variance share that P1's unit (population samples) cannot in principle produce. | Partial |
| 4 Presupposition failure | (i) The pre-registered "projected asymptote" delta is undefined for the named model — Wiser: the power law "decelerates ... but fitness has no upper limit"; the asymptote belongs to the rejected hyperbolic model. (ii) Presupposition 5 is over-stated: Wiser 2013 competed 40k/50k samples of nine populations against 40,000-generation clones. (iii) Presupposition 2 further stressed: archived-clone frequency dependence in Ara-1 is 0.9-5.4%, the order of P1's ~5% residual. | (i) repairable by wording (projected fitness at a fixed generation, or exponent alone); (ii) Wiser's check is two time points and one reference generation, not an exponent refit, so limb (c) is not literally done; (iii) already conceded in the record. | Partial |
| 5 Vagueness | Under frequency dependence a triple can be cyclic at one starting ratio and transitive at another, so "share of cyclic triples" is a function of frequency, not a number; the decision rule is unspecified, and the asymptote delta is undefined. | The reformulation already requires >=2 frequencies and a pre-specified rule; "cyclic at every assayed frequency" or per-frequency reporting is a routine pre-registration choice, and a null is admitted as a result, so it cannot be answered regardless of evidence. | Partial |
| 6 Significance inflation | LTEE and descendant labs already hold the answer they would act on and have kept ancestor-referenced reporting for 23 years; a refined null changes no practice and a positive would largely reproduce P2 in new units. | A non-trivial cyclic share at 50,000+ generations would bear on the live unbounded-vs-asymptotic argument; tournament statisticians gain a biological application. | Partial |

| 8 Dissolution | "Is fitness a scalar?" dissolves into the field's existing position that fitness is frequency- and context-dependent; a cyclic share at a fixed starting ratio is a summary of a known phenomenon. | The reformulation is operational (a matrix, a decomposition, two fits), and whether the cyclic share is large is an empirical fact not settled by noting that frequency dependence exists. | Partial |

Verification (post-batch, fresh-context checker, log UQ-20261016-57-verification.md): the quote is real, the estimand is not the candidate's, and the rejection stands on the narrower ground.
Confirmed verbatim in de Visser and Lenski 2002 (BMC Evolutionary Biology 2:19): "the ANOVA tests all forms of non-transitivity", with the interaction term at "< 2% of the overall variation" and P > 0.5, against main effects at P < 0.0001 explaining over 93% and residual error about 5%. A second test compared the cumulative fitness gain predicted under transitivity with the observed gain, with a jackknife interval.
Where the batch's characterisation overreached: the design is ONE evolving population (Ara-1), 21 evenly spaced samples (generations 0, 1,000, ... 20,000) each competed against 5 marked Ara+ clones from generations 0, 5,000, 10,000, 15,000 and 20,000, three-fold replicated — 315 competitions on a fixed 21 x 5 grid, NOT a full round robin among archived clones. And the estimand is a sample-by-clone interaction variance share, i.e. non-parallelism of fitness across reference clones. The checker is explicit that it is not a rate of intransitive triples against an assay-error null: no triple counts are reported anywhere, and the residual term reflects replicate error only. "Tests all forms of non-transitivity" is the authors' own scope claim for their interaction term, not a triple-level measurement.
Why the rejection still holds: the question "is LTEE fitness intransitive, and is that why adaptation decelerates?" was asked and answered negatively inside the LTEE's own numbered series, and the power-law paper this candidate targets re-checked its own curve against marked 40,000-generation clones rather than only the ancestor (Wiser, Ribeck and Lenski 2013: 108 competitions, nine populations at 40k and 50k generations, plus all 12 populations at up to 41 time points against the ancestor — confirmed). What this candidate adds is estimator machinery and a wider design (a cyclic-triple rate with an error null, a Hodge decomposition variance share, an exponent refit) on an answered question, which the ledger does not count as a new question.
Recorded for a future run, since it is genuinely unmeasured: nobody has published a triple-level intransitivity rate against an assay-error null for the LTEE clone archive. If that is ever re-filed it must be posed as an estimator question in its own right, with its own Gate 0, and not as a question about whether fitness is intransitive.

Scores: Well-posedness 3/3 · Significance 2/3
(Scores do not rescue the entry: Gate 2 novelty is Low and attack 2 is Unresolved, each independently fatal. All eight attacks were run from scratch against the Gate 0-3 record, as the rule for a Gate 2 rejection requires, so the log exists whichever way the Gate 2 ground later goes. Only one adversary was run; a second would not change a verdict already fixed by a fatal Unresolved.)

Strongest remaining objection: The candidate is de Visser & Lenski (2002) — LTEE XI, "Rejection of non-transitive interactions as cause of declining rate of adaptation" — restated in tournament vocabulary and re-pointed at a newer curve, in the same organism and the same experiment; its ANOVA "tests all forms of non-transitivity" and returns an interaction term below 2% of variation at P > 0.5, and the 2013 power-law paper then re-checked fitness against marked 40,000-generation clones in nine populations. Both were opened at publisher routes, so the asked-and-answered finding does not depend on which hostname answered. What remains un-asked is estimator machinery, not a question.

Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): None for this candidate; it is rejected as answered. Pointer for the narrower residue, which should be filed and gated as its own candidate rather than inherited from this one: a Hodge/HHD variance partition of a round-robin archived-clone fitness matrix with a replicate-error null, plus the delta in the Wiser et al. power-law exponent — with the adversary's repairs applied (drop "projected asymptote", since the power law has no upper limit; report the cyclic-triple rate per starting frequency; state up front that archived-clone frequency dependence in Ara-1 is 0.9-5.4%, the order of P1's ~5% residual error, so the deliverable is a bound rather than a rate).

Routing (if rejected as already-asked): Not routed. The ledger routes only asked-but-unanswered problems; P1 answers the trajectory limb and P2 the prevalence limb, so this is an answered/disguised-known rejection and gets no row in ledger/routed-open-problems.md.

---
ID: UQ-20261016-58
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): Biology — invertebrate molecular biology / RNA quality metrology; biodiversity-genomics sample QC (EBP, Darwin Tree of Life). Method-owning neighbours: measurement metrology (calibration transfer, commutability), screening-bias epidemiology (verification bias by subgroup), psychometric measurement non-invariance.

Question (canonical): In a defined frame of RNA submissions carrying a recorded integrity score and a documented accept/reject/re-extract decision, with each source taxon assigned a 28S hidden-break status, (a) what is the break-free vs break-bearing difference in recorded integrity score and in per-sample rejection and re-extraction rate, adjusted for preservation route, tissue, protocol, input mass and body size with denominators stated; and (b) in matched RNA from one break-bearing and one break-free species degraded in the same graded series, what is the mapping RIN_break(d) → RIN_free(d) at equal true degradation d measured independently (DV200, spike-in fragment length, library 3' bias), and therefore what numeric correction does a RIN ≥ 7-type gate require in a break-bearing taxon? (c, secondary/exploratory) After conditioning on research effort, body size, collection difficulty and preservation, is break status associated with whether a taxon has any transcriptome at all?
(Gate 1 reformulation; one reformulation used, for well-posedness only. Gate 0 intake wording and the full limb specification are in batches/2026-10-16-2155/UQ-20261016-58-record.md.)

Alternative formulations:
- Has a vertebrate-trained RNA-quality metric been quietly selecting which invertebrates get sequenced?
- What is the mapping between RIN and actual RNA degradation in taxa whose 28S migrates as a single peak, and what has the absence of that mapping cost in rejected samples and missing transcriptomes?
(Adversary 3's attack 8 recommends the first wording NOT be carried as canonical: as a corpus-level causal claim it decomposes into clade-level confounds.)

Motivating gap: Anomaly mining. The hidden break is published and its QC consequence has now been asserted in print at least four times and measured never. Natsidis et al. 2019 (Sci Rep 9:19477) — RIN "will be consistently underestimated in the great majority of animal species with a break", training set "obtained from species without a hidden break", "an alternative to the standard RIN ... would be a valuable development" — computes no RIN value and measures no QC outcome. Casanova Gomez et al. 2026 (PeerJ 14:e20693) recommends "rRNA-aware quality control" with no RIN values, rates or metric. Deleo et al. 2018 (Biol Methods Protoc 3:bpy012) reports RINs "could not be estimated for a majority" of split-28S samples. McCarthy et al. 2015 (PeerJ 3:e1436) uses RIN only as an incidental ">8.0" descriptor. Found late by adversary 2: Agilent application note 5991-7903EN (Fabrick & Hull 2017) — 12 insect species, RIN uncomputable for 5, values 2.4–7.3 for the other 7, "the validity of RIN for insect total RNA was not proven", no break-free arm and RIN not reported on its own degradation series.

Presuppositions:
1. Break status assignable per taxon. ESTABLISHED in silico (Natsidis 2019: break in 17/19 testable protostome phyla); CONTESTED in detail — adversary 3 verified calls are made by eye from coverage drops, several phyla left uncertain, and only for species with ≥1 Gb existing RNA-Seq; Casanova Gomez 2026 (read by adversary 3) confirms graded, not binary, profile classes.
2. QC outcomes recoverable from facility/consortium logs or public submission metadata. REFUTED for the public-metadata fallback: adversary 1 read ERGA sample-manifest SOP v2.5.1 — no RIN/RQN/DV200 field, no rejection or re-collection record. Limb (a) must be a private-LIMS study.
3. Integrity thresholds functioned as accept/reject gates, not advisory numbers. UNESTABLISHED and now with direct counter-evidence: Sanger ToL core-lab paper over ~2,000 species (bioRxiv 2025.04.11.648334, read by adversary 2) names no integrity metric — Qubit/Nanodrop, one numeric gate on yield ("over the 100 ng input requirement"); DToL protocols.io RNA SOP (adversary 3) says only "the required QC"; Cornell TREx (adversary 1) uses RQN<7 as a protocol switch to ribo-depletion, not a gate; Reichel et al. 2026 Mol Ecol Resour 26:e70100 calls RIN ≥ 8 a "rule of thumb" and tells submitters not to apply rigid cut-offs to invertebrates.
4. Confounder-adjusted break-bearing vs break-free comparison possible. CONTESTED and, per adversary 3, near-fatal for limb (c): the break is homologous across protostomes and absent in deuterostomes, so the contrast is close to "protostome vs not" and confounded with body size, tissue, preservation and field logistics.
5. A reference measure of true degradation independent of the 28S peak exists (DV200, spike-in fragment length, 3' bias). ESTABLISHED within one matrix; never run across break status.
6. (Gate 1) Heat/denaturation artefacts can mimic a break-type profile, so denaturing treatment must be held fixed or limb (a) measures protocol, not biology.

What would count as an answer: (i) from facility or consortium QC logs, the integrity-score distribution and the rejection/re-extraction rate for break-bearing vs break-free taxa with denominators stated and preservation/tissue/protocol fixed or adjusted; (ii) a graded-degradation calibration experiment on matched RNA from one break-bearing and one break-free species, RIN regressed on an independent degradation axis, yielding the equivalence mapping and the numeric threshold correction. A credible null — break status unrelated to rejection once effort, preservation and denaturing protocol are accounted for, because facilities already compensate informally — is a real answer, not a failure.

Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 12 WebSearch + 6 WebFetch + 1 GitHub code search at Gate 2 (recorded cap overrun: 12 against a cap of 11; no further searching after the overrun was noticed), plus 27 new adversary queries at Gate 4. Full lists in batches/2026-10-16-2155/UQ-20261016-58-record.md and -adversary-1/-2/-3.md. Most informative:
- "RNA Integrity Number underestimation hidden break 28S rRNA correction calibration invertebrate RIN equivalence" → only Natsidis 2019 and Casanova Gomez 2026; no correction, calibration or equivalence paper exists under this wording.
- [quantity limb] "fraction of eukaryote species with hidden break ... how many species predicted break" → the prevalence HAS been computed and published (Natsidis 2019 Table 1/Fig. 4). That quantity is the candidate's exposure variable, not its estimand.
- [own-field, consequence form] "hidden break 28S rRNA consequences sequencing success rate samples rejected quality control arthropod ... threshold lowered" → surfaced McCarthy 2015; opened; no outcome measurement. The query most likely to have killed the candidate, and it did not.
- [feasibility/answer-search] "mining RNA integrity number values from SRA BioSample submission metadata ..." → no repository-scale mining of deposited RIN values by anyone, for any purpose.
- [method-owning vocabularies] calibration transfer/commutability; differential verification bias by subgroup; (adversary 2) psychometric measurement invariance/DIF → three mature named method families, none ever pointed at a nucleic-acid integrity score.
- [adversary 2, the one real miss] "Drosophila 28S rRNA 28Sa 28Sb two bands bioanalyzer RIN underestimates ..." → Agilent 5991-7903EN, which Gate 2 saw only as a generic vendor overview and never opened.
- [adversary 2 and 3, consortium operations] Sanger ToL core-lab paper and DToL protocols.io SOPs → no published RNA integrity gate in the candidate's own named frame.
- Zero hits in: nematode/C. elegans, mollusc, non-metazoan fragmented-LSU, German, Spanish, Chinese, and public code (GitHub: no break-aware metric implemented anywhere).

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
P1. Natsidis, Schiffer, Salvador-Martínez & Telford 2019, Sci Rep 9:19477, doi 10.1038/s41598-019-55573-1. READ at intake and independently re-read in full by adversary 3. Unit: a eukaryotic species' 28S sequence (in silico). Endpoint: break presence/position predicted from sequence. Comparator: taxa with electrophoretically known status. Estimand: per-taxon break status and its phylogenetic prevalence.
P2. Deleo, Pérez-Moreno, Vázquez-Miranda & Bracken-Grissom 2018, Biol Methods Protoc 3(1):bpy012, doi 10.1093/biomethods/bpy012. OPENED at academic.oup.com. Unit: an arthropod RNA sample plus heated aliquots. Endpoint: qualitative profile class (plus N50/BUSCO for two species). Comparator: heated vs non-heated aliquots of the same sample. Estimand: artefact-vs-real determination per sample; no RIN column, no graded series, no rates, no metric.
P3. Agilent application note 5991-7903EN, Fabrick & Hull 2017 (USDA-ARS copy). NEW PRIOR added by adversary 2; closest to limb (b) and missed by Gate 2. Unit: total RNA from each of 12 insect species. Endpoint: electropherogram profile plus RIN where computable (uncomputable for 5/12; 2.4–7.3 for the rest); separate 0/5/10/30/60-min degradation series in 3 species with actin/GAPDH Cq as readout. Comparator: across insect species and across degradation times — no break-free arm. Estimand: whether RIN is usable for insect RNA (a qualitative verdict), explicitly "not proven"; RIN never reported on the degraded samples, so no mapping.
Also opened and checked, not load-bearing: McCarthy et al. 2015 PeerJ 3:e1436; Winnebeck et al. 2010 J Insect Sci 10:159; Casanova Gomez et al. 2026 PeerJ 14:e20693 (adversaries 1 and 2 COULD NOT READ it — doi.org HTTP 429 / client error; adversary 3 read it at peerj.com and verified every absence the record claimed); Reichel et al. 2026 Mol Ecol Resour 26:e70100 (adversary 1, via escholarship); ERGA manifest SOP v2.5.1; Sanger ToL core-lab paper. NOT OPENED and explicitly not used to grade: the two taxonomic-representation papers (Gate 2 query 6), metagenomic taxon-dependent bias calibration (adversary 3 query 9), Cornell TREx SOP (adversary 3, fetch failed), Schroeder et al. 2006 (adversary 2 declined to press an unsourced attack).

Novelty — how this differs from each:
vs P1: P1's endpoint IS the candidate's exposure variable. P1 establishes who has the break, asserts the RIN consequence in prose, computes no RIN, and leaves the metric as a stated desideratum. The candidate's endpoints — recorded integrity score, rejection/re-extraction rate, transcriptome existence, a RIN↔RIN equivalence function — appear nowhere in it.
vs P2: same exposure, different estimand. P2 asks whether a profile is an artefact; the candidate asks what scoring that profile did to a population of samples with a denominator. P2's "RIN may be impossible or biased" is the hypothesis and its manual-threshold-raising advice is one of the candidate's admissible answers, not a measurement of either limb.
vs P3: P3 shares limb (b)'s exposure and part of its design and still yields neither estimand — no break-free arm, RIN not reported on its own degradation series, no statistics ("a qualitative observation"), no rejection rates. It also falsifies the record's claim that the vendor-recalibration precedent is a plant one, so limb (b) is closer to asked than the record graded it; limb (a)'s rate-with-a-denominator remains untouched by it.
General: across 12 Gate 2 and 27 adversary queries in own-field (several wordings), a second protostome sub-literature, nematode and non-metazoan fragmented-LSU lineages, biodiversity-data metascience, biobank/clinical pre-analytical rejection auditing, library-QC bioinformatics, consortium operations, calibration transfer, verification bias, psychometric non-invariance, three non-English vocabularies and public code, nothing attaches break status to a QC decision with a denominator, regresses an integrity score on an independent degradation axis across break status, or uses break status to explain data availability. The nearest-in-form genre — pre-analytical specimen-rejection-rate auditing — is mature for human specimens and has never been taxon-structured.

Novelty confidence: Medium
Medium, not High: the consequence hypothesis is in print in the candidate's own field with unusual directness, limb (b)'s metric half is an explicitly posed open problem, and adversary 2 found a vendor note (P3) that is closer to limb (b) than anything Gate 2 opened. The un-asked part is the measurement and the quantity. Medium survives all three adversaries' Disguise sweeps; it is not promoted by them.

Significance — consequence: If limb (a) is positive at the size the mechanism implies, a quantifiable share of invertebrate RNA submissions were refused for a property of their ribosomes rather than the condition of their RNA — and these are often field-collected, permit-bound, hard-to-recollect animals, so a rejection converts into another expedition or a dropped taxon. Limb (b)'s deliverable is small and immediately actionable: a number a facility can write into an SOP without new software. A null — the informal compensation Deleo describes is effectively universal — retires a worry four papers have put into print untested and redirects effort to the metric-development problem alone.
Significance — audience: Core facilities and submission portals that publish numeric integrity gates (Gate 2 query 2 found an invertebrate-specific Bioanalyzer advisory in circulation; adversary 2 found a practitioner thread asking how to judge Drosophila RNA quality); vendor algorithm groups (P3 is direct evidence the vendor engages this exposure, and matrix-specific RIN variants already ship); invertebrate transcriptomics labs; biodiversity-genomics funders and sample-logistics planners, for whom a re-extraction differential is a budget line. Relocated by Gate 4: the consortium the record named first (Sanger ToL/ERGA) does not appear to gate on RNA integrity at all, and Reichel et al. 2026 already advises reading the electropherogram instead of the number.
Significance — fecundity: Does a depressed RIN also MIS-PREDICT downstream 3' bias, or merely mislabel it? Do published invertebrate expression estimates carry a break-correlated degradation covariate confounding cross-phylum comparison? Does the gatekeeping argument transfer to DNA-side gates for unusual genome architectures? General form: how many QC instruments in molecular biology are model-organism-trained, and which non-model lineages do they systematically under-score — a form adversary 2 confirms is unasked for bacterial 23S and every other fragmented-rRNA lineage.
Significance — anchoring: P1's stated desideratum; Casanova Gomez et al.'s "rRNA-aware quality control"; the graded exposure within Pancrustacea (verified by adversary 3); the known taxonomic unevenness of genomic data, where break status has never been a candidate explanatory variable; and the mature, unapplied method families of calibration transfer/commutability, verification bias by subgroup and measurement non-invariance.

Reason for silence: A disciplinary boundary plus a self-erasing denominator — amended by Gate 4 to "asked informally and once by a vendor, never posed as a measurable quantity". The anomaly is owned by comparative molecular zoology, which does not hold the outcome data; the outcome data live in core-facility LIMS as operational records, unpublished and unindexed. Gate 4 strengthened this for limb (a) and weakened it for the others: the public consortium standard has no field for either the exposure or the outcome (ERGA SOP), the flagship protocol names no metric, and 1KITE — the one >1,000-species invertebrate RNA programme — published no attrition denominator, so from outside there is no variable for the question to be about, and a rejected sample leaves no INSDC trace. Counting against the candidate: for limb (b) there is no silence to explain (asked-but-open), and for limb (c) both inputs have been public since 2019, so the better explanation of that silence is non-identifiability, not absence of a question.

Verification (post-batch, fresh-context checker, log UQ-20261016-58-verification.md): the cap on this entry is CONFIRMED, from documents rather than from argument, and it tells the candidate which limb to keep.
Of the operational documents opened, NONE mentions RIN or RQN at all. The Sanger Tree of Life core-laboratory paper (bioRxiv 2025.04.11.648334) checks RNA with Qubit and Nanodrop and gates on total yield only (over 100 ng); samples that fail are retried with a different individual, a different tissue, or more input. The Sanger manual TRIzol protocol and the sample-triage protocol contain no RIN, RQN or 28S text at all; their only numeric flags are A230/280 below 1.6 for a partially dissolved pellet and a tissue-weight rule. The EBP standards page reached was an abstract-only landing page with no RNA-integrity text. No programme or core-facility document opened acknowledges the hidden-break problem or tells submitters what to do about it.
So the primary limb — a break-correlated excess of rejections and re-extractions — has no documented decision channel in the very programmes the candidate names: in these documents the integrity score is not the gate, yield is. That is what holds the entry at Provisional, and it is now an evidenced finding rather than an adversary's suspicion. It also points at the limb worth keeping: the equivalence mapping (what RIN in a break-bearing taxon corresponds to the same true degradation state as a given RIN in a break-free taxon) needs no decision channel at all, and nothing opened measures it.
Standing exposure variable, unchanged: Natsidis, Schiffer, Salvador-Martinez and Telford 2019 (Sci Rep 9:19477) computes break status across eukaryotes and leaves the corrected metric as a printed desideratum; Deleo et al. 2018 reports the 28S gap deletion being misread as a degraded profile in about 90% of the species they sampled.
UNVERIFIED and listed as promotion conditions, not as checks that passed: the full EBP standards report (PMC blocked), the Sanger "RNA Decision Making Tree" appendix, the Darwin Tree of Life sample manifests, and generic core-facility submission thresholds. Any one of those carrying a numeric RIN minimum would restore the primary limb; their absence so far is bounded, not settled.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3
Well-posedness 2/3 as graded at Gate 1 and confirmed by Gate 4 rather than lowered: limbs (a) and (b) each have a stated frame, estimand and null and limb (b) is a clean bench design, but the exposure is graded rather than binary, limb (a)(i) is undefined wherever the score does not compute, limb (a)'s frame has lost its public-metadata fallback, and limb (c) remains answerable either way. This alone bars Validated independently of the adversarial statuses.

Strongest remaining objection: No frame has yet been shown to exist in which the exposure could have acted. Every operational document any adversary actually opened shows the integrity score functioning as an advisory number or a protocol switch rather than an accept/reject gate — the Sanger ToL core-lab paper over ~2,000 species names no integrity metric and states a yield-only gate, the DToL RNA SOP names none, the ERGA manifest SOP has no RNA-quality field at all, Cornell routes RQN<7 to ribo-depletion, and Reichel et al. 2026 tells submitters not to apply rigid cut-offs to invertebrates — while for a large share of break-bearing taxa the score is not returned at all (5/12 insect species in Agilent 5991-7903EN; "a majority" of split-28S samples per Deleo). If so, limb (a)'s deficit is zero by construction rather than by measurement, and the question's primary and most novel limb has no decision channel to measure.
Promotion requires: one named, obtainable log frame in which a numeric RNA-integrity value demonstrably triggered an accept/reject or re-extraction decision on invertebrate submissions, with matched break-free comparators at usable volume; limb (a)(i) restated as a composite of score plus non-computability rate; Agilent 5991-7903EN added as the closest prior with limb (b) re-graded against it; and limb (c) dropped or re-specified with an identifiable contrast — which together would take well-posedness to 3/3 and clear the Partials on attacks 4, 5 and 7.

Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): a feasibility probe before any study design — ask whether any single core facility or portal holds LIMS records that pair an integrity value with an accept/reject/re-extract field across both break-bearing and break-free source taxa, and establish the volume of matched records; the answer to that probe decides whether limb (a) is a study or a dead end, and limb (b) can be designed independently of it.

---
ID: UQ-20261016-59
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): Biology — population/conservation genomics of long-lived modular organisms (trees, corals, clonal plants); somatic mutation. Neighbouring: cancer multiregion genomics, survey-sampling variance components, forest/aquaculture clone identity.

Question (canonical): In long-lived modular organisms, how much do standard population-genomic estimands — individual heterozygosity, pairwise relatedness/kinship, allele frequencies and the Ne derived from them — change depending on which module of the same individual was sampled, and is that within-individual sampling variance large relative to the between-individual variance those estimands are meant to measure?
Question (Gate 1 reformulation, carried forward): On a crossed design of N individuals x M >= 3 spatially separated modules per individual in >= 2 taxa (one long-lived tree, one colonial/clonal marine organism), sequenced at matched depth with module provenance recorded, what is the ratio of the between-module-within-individual to the between-individual variance component, with an interval, for each of four pre-specified estimands (per-individual observed heterozygosity; pairwise kinship; per-site allele frequency; one LD-based Ne), after a technical component is estimated from replicate libraries and chimeric individuals are classified and reported separately from mosaics? Target of estimation is the module-conditional estimate plus its between-module variance, not a single per-individual "true" value.

Alternative formulations:
- Does it matter which branch of the tree you sequence?
- Treating within-individual somatic mosaicism as a measurement-error term rather than as biology: how large is the between-module variance component in population-genomic estimates for trees, corals and clonal plants, and which published conclusions are sensitive to it?

Motivating gap: Within-individual somatic variation is now directly measurable and mapped in named organisms (Pando aspen mosaic; per-branch somatic variant counts in oak and Populus), and theory exists for indexing it (Iwasa, Tomimoto & Satake 2024, Quantitative Plant Biology 5:e11, doi 10.1017/qpb.2024.9 — theoretical, three within-tree distance indexes, no estimand). The literature treats mosaicism as biology or as a Discussion-section caveat; no opened source propagates module choice into the estimands the field reports. Gate 2 established the caveat has been voiced explicitly in the coral literature since 2012 and never quantified.

Presuppositions:
1. Somatic variation detectable above sequencing error at population-study depth. CONTESTED — and materially weakened at Gate 4: Schmid-Siegert et al. (oak, 40X WGS) ran 314,865 candidate discordant sites to 17 confirmed; Oury et al. 2024 (46X capture) report IGV counts "extremely sensitive to the threshold defined".
2. Somatic variants reach within-module frequencies high enough to move an individual-level estimand. CONTESTED, the crux, and the ground of the rejection (see Adversarial log, attack 1).
3. Multi-module sampling at matched depth with provenance recorded is feasible. ESTABLISHED (Oury 2024: 93 colonies x 3 nubbins + replicates; Herrera 2022: 15 plants x 5 modules; Pando: 184 samples).
4. The estimands remain defined for a mosaic individual. Dissolution risk, handled by the module-conditional target — but not retired for the Ne limb (Pando: "The unit of effective population size here can be thought of in terms of cellular lineages").
5. Module provenance recoverable in some published datasets. PARTLY CONTESTED; now partly satisfied (Oury 2024 data public, Zenodo 10633675).
6. Chimerism separable from mosaicism. NECESSARY, and shown fragile at Gate 4 (threshold-dependent antimode; mosaic-class discordance density implausible for point mutation).

What would count as an answer: A variance-components analysis on multi-module sequencing in >= 2 taxa partitioning each estimand's variance into between-individual, between-module-within-individual and technical components, with the between-module share and interval per estimand and chimeras reported separately; plus a sensitivity arm re-running a published analysis with modules swapped, reporting how often a conclusion-relevant threshold is crossed. A measured near-zero share answers it in the negative and licenses single-module practice explicitly.

Novelty — queries run (query -> one-line result): Gate 2 ran 11 distinct queries and opened 4 sources; the three adversaries ran a further 26 (9 + 9 + 8) in vocabularies Gate 2 did not use, opening 10 more. Full lists: batches/2026-10-16-2155/UQ-20261016-59-record.md and UQ-20261016-59-adversary-1/-2/-3.md. Most informative:
- "somatic mutation biases estimates of heterozygosity and relatedness in long-lived trees" (own-field own-words title query) -> Iwasa/Satake within-tree index paper (theory) + an oak somatic-variant detection-bias paper; nothing propagating module choice into an estimand.
- "genotyping error effect on relatedness kinship estimates and effective population size bias statistical genetics propagation" (method-owning field) -> mature error-propagation machinery for kinship and LD-Ne; none instantiating module-of-origin as the error term. Grounds the Medium rather than High grade: the machinery is off the shelf, the increment is the measurement.
- "fixed somatic mutations oak tree branches number of SNVs versus heterozygous sites genome per-site heterozygosity negligible" (adversary 3, answer-seeking arithmetic) -> Schmid-Siegert et al. 2017 Napoleon Oak, OPENED at biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/149203v1.full-text. Supplies BOTH terms of the division Gate 2 could not obtain. Decisive.
- exact-title search with PMC blocked (adversary 3 R9; adversary 1 query 9) -> Oury et al. 2024 Sci Rep s41598-024-57136-5 OPENED on the first publisher call, resolving Gate 2's COULD NOT READ.
- "Klekowski genetic mosaicism long-lived plants among-branch allozyme nested variance within individual sampling" (adversary 2) -> Herrera et al. 2021 New Phytol and 2022 J Ecol, both OPENED: the candidate's exact crossed design and variance partition, on methylation.
- "multilocus lineage MLL threshold somatic mutation scoring error ... clonal plants" (adversaries 1-3) -> Arnaud-Haond/RClone clonality tooling (OPENED, archimer 42507.pdf): somatic mutation absorbed into MLL distance thresholds since 2007/2016.
- "mosaicismo somatico intraindividual planta longeva ... sesgo" (Spanish, adversary 2) -> Pando bioRxiv full PDF OPENED, resolving Gate 2's second COULD NOT READ.
COULD NOT READ (grade nothing in either direction): Yu 2022 Zostera dissertation (oceanrep bot challenge; Springer route untried, budget); "Adaptive Potential of Intracolonial Genetic Variability in Coral Populations" (2025 review, PMC-only); Schmid-Siegert journal version (pubmed reCAPTCHA — bioRxiv full text read instead).

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
A. Maier E. et al. (2012) "Intracolonial genetic variation in the scleractinian coral Seriatopora hystrix", Coral Reefs 31:505-517, doi 10.1007/s00338-011-0857-9 (link.springer.com, opened; + Maier 2010 LMU dissertation, edoc.ub.uni-muenchen.de/14906/1/Maier_Elke.pdf, opened). Unit: colony (155 colonies, 2-3 samples, 5-6 microsatellites). Endpoint: within-colony marker discordance, mosaic vs chimera attribution. Comparator: other samples of the same colony. Estimand: PROPORTION of heterogeneous colonies (17%). Abstract: "We discuss the error that mosaicism and chimerism introduce into population genetic analyses"; thesis verifies the error was named and never quantified.
B. Oury Y., Gelin P., Magalon H. et al. (2024) "Investigating the potential roles of intra-colonial genetic variability in Pocillopora corals using genomics", Scientific Reports, doi 10.1038/s41598-024-57136-5 (nature.com, OPENED by adversaries 1 and 3; data Zenodo 10633675). Unit: colony, 93 colonies x 3 apical nubbins, 1,248 UCE + 1,385 exon loci, 59,032 SNPs, mean depth 46.3X, extraction/sequencing replicates included. Endpoint: presence/class of intra-colonial genetic variability. Comparator: nubbins of the same colony. Estimand: IGV prevalence and class (18/93; 7 mosaics, 11 chimeras), with chimeric pairs supplying 58.8% of allelic differences and the counts "extremely sensitive to the threshold defined". VERIFIED ABSENT: no heterozygosity, allele-frequency, Fst, kinship, Ne, AMOVA or nested variance analysis; no re-run with a different nubbin.
C. Herrera C.M., Medrano M., Bazaga P. & Alonso C. (2022) "Ecological significance of intraplant variation...", Journal of Ecology 110:2555-2567, doi 10.1111/1365-2745.13964 (plant-animal.es PDF, OPENED; with Herrera et al. 2021, New Phytologist 231:2065-2076, doi 10.1111/nph.17257, OPENED). Unit: the plant x module cell, 15 shrubs x 5 modules, fully crossed. Endpoint: epigenotype (70 polymorphic MS-AFLP markers) and phenotype. Comparator: modules of the same plant vs other plants. Estimand: the between-module share of total variance — "Intraplant epigenotypic variation accounted for 5.9% of total epigenotypic variance"; 2021 gives within-plant 0.119 (CI 0.015-0.252) vs among-plant 0.100 (CI 0.0056-0.647). States the inverted assumption outright: "In the absence of DNA sequence variation among samples, as expected for leaves from the same plant".

Novelty — how this differs from each:
vs A: same object and design, different estimand — A estimates the prevalence of discordance, the candidate the variance a module draw injects into named estimands. A's 5-6 microsatellites cannot speak to any limb. A's qualitative form is asked-and-unquantified since 2012.
vs B: the crossed genomic design the candidate specifies, already run with replicates and public data, in one of its two named taxon classes; it classifies IGV but computes no estimand. The candidate's increment over B is a re-analysis of B's own data, not a new study.
vs C: the candidate's exact question-form — crossed individual x module design, variance partition, between-module share with interval, in a long-lived modular plant — already executed and published, on epigenetic and phenotypic rather than population-genomic estimands, while explicitly assuming away the sequence variation the candidate asks about. So the FORM is not new; only the four estimands are.

Novelty confidence: Medium (not load-bearing for this verdict). Grounds: 37 distinct queries across the own field in its own words, two answer-seeking forms, seven neighbouring vocabularies and the method-owning field; 14 sources opened. No source computes the four-estimand variance ratio, and the two papers Gate 2 could not read were opened at Gate 4 and verified not to contain it. Capped at Medium because the question-form is published (C), the qualitative form is a voiced 2012 caveat (A), and the identity limb is the MLG/MLL problem renamed. Not Low: the specific ratio is unpublished. The rejection is at Gate 4, not Gate 2.

Significance — consequence: If the between-module share is non-negligible, every single-module study carries an unreported variance term and protocols change cheaply (record provenance; sample >1 module for identity- and threshold-based analyses). Highest-value targets are identity- and threshold-dependent outputs: clone-mate assignment, parentage, "number of genotypes" in a nursery or restoration plot, kinship matrices for broodstock or seed-orchard management, hard-cut conservation indicators. If near zero, the answer licenses single-module sampling explicitly. The record argues, correctly, that the limbs come apart and that the question earns its keep on kinship-near-threshold, allele-frequency-at-variable-sites and coral chimerism rather than on genome-wide heterozygosity.
Significance — audience: (1) conservation genomicists computing GBF genetic-diversity and Ne indicators for trees and corals; (2) coral restoration programmes genotyping nursery fragments against genotypic-diversity targets; (3) forest tree breeders and clonal seed-orchard managers already running ramet clone-verification assays, for whom "mislabelling" and "somatic divergence" are opposite operational responses to the same observation; (4) the somatic-mutation-rate community choosing how many modules per individual to sequence. (3) would act fastest. All four verified to exist and run the relevant assays (adversary 2 query 9: Dendrobiology 81, Silvae Genetica 50, cacao SNP parentage).
Significance — fecundity: module-aware estimators and a design-effect/ICC analogue for modular organisms; whether somatic load tracks module age, height or position so that convenience sampling is non-random rather than merely noisy (Pando: "leaves showing significantly higher mutation loads than roots or branches"); whether mosaicism and chimerism need different corrections; whether the share scales with organism age or size; whether the decomposition transfers to epigenetic estimands, where Herrera 2021/2022 show the within-individual term is already large.
Significance — anchoring: the coral chimerism/unit-of-selection problem; the genet-vs-ramet sampling-unit problem in clonal-plant Ne; the design of somatic mutation-rate studies; Kunming-Montreal GBF genetic-diversity indicators with their hard thresholds; clone-identity verification in breeding.

Reason for silence: As stated in the record — a design incompatibility plus funding ("neither community's grant pays for the other's axis"), plus a genre effect in which the coral caveat lived in Discussion sections since 2012. The design-incompatibility mechanism is FALSIFIED by sources opened at Gate 4: the crossed design has been run, with genomics and replicates, by a coral population-genetics lab (Oury 2024, 93 x 3, data public) and fully crossed in a long-lived plant (Herrera 2022, 15 x 5, with the variance partition). STRUCK. Surviving amendments: (i) the genre effect, which is consistent with Oury's silence but does not explain why a lab holding the crossed design did not compute the ratio; (ii) adversary 2's marker-and-estimand boundary — the groups running crossed designs use marker systems (MS-AFLP, 5-6 microsatellites) that cannot yield the estimands, while the groups with sequence resolution sample one genet; (iii) adversary 3's reading, that for genome-wide estimands the arithmetic is visible to everyone and for identity estimands the field asked and answered via MLL thresholds. (iii) is not a mechanism that supports novelty, and under Gate 4's rule it makes the novelty finding itself suspect.

Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status). Three adversaries, run on the Gate 0-3 record only, logs verbatim in UQ-20261016-59-adversary-1/-2/-3.md. Status given per adversary (A1 | A2 | A3); the worst governs.
1. Triviality | The headline limbs follow in a page from published numbers. A3 supplied both terms of the division Gate 2 and A2 could not obtain, from a source it opened in the candidate's own tree taxon: Schmid-Siegert et al. (Quercus robur, two branches, ~40X WGS, meristems "exposed for 234 years") give "the total number of confirmed SNVs separating the two genomes" as 17, an authors' higher-end total of "46.9 to 113", and "1,832,554 heterozygous sites common to both samples".
