Question (canonical): Within a single model species reared across its viable temperature and nutrition range, is the set of morphological landmark events used to define developmental stage well ordered by one latent axis — that is, does environment only rescale developmental time, as staging series and their temperature-correction formulas assume — or do landmark pairs reverse order, and how much stage-matching error does the measured departure from unidimensionality imply for stage-matched comparative data?
Alternative formulations: (a) Is "developmental stage" a one-dimensional scale, or does the rearing environment change the order of developmental events within a single species? (b) Staging series presuppose uniform rate scaling; how often is that false within one species, and what does the violation do to stage-matched transcriptomic and cell-atlas comparisons? (c) Gate 1 reformulation (one permitted, recorded in full in the record): three separate estimands on a temperature x nutrition grid with a pre-specified landmark set L (|L| >= 10) — E1 fraction of landmark pairs reversing order against a scoring-error null; E2 one-factor vs >=2-factor latent fit under a pre-fixed criterion; E3 variance share contributed by stage-matching error to a named downstream stage-matched contrast.
Motivating gap: Staging was taken as a how-dense/why-empty topic: every model organism has a staging series, the zebrafish index encodes uniform rate scaling explicitly, and scale-validity testing appeared absent, with event-pair/sequence-heterochrony tools pointed between species and unidimensionality testing owned by psychometrics. Intake self-flagged Gate 2 as UNVERIFIED. After Gate 2 the gap is largely absent: the set-level order question was asked and answered within one species, on a morphological landmark set, in developmental biology's own words, in both directions.
Presuppositions: P1 a >=10-event landmark set is scoreable per individual — ESTABLISHED (36 landmarks in D. melanogaster, 9 refined; ~24 zebrafish imaged hourly per temperature). P2 scoring error small relative to inter-landmark intervals — CONTESTED, left genuinely open by the priors (no inter/within-scorer reliability, no scoring-error null); adversary notes continuous single-cell-resolution imaging meets it by instrument choice, so the "needs a manual-scoring null" framing is itself an assumption. What would count as an answer: Per-individual landmark event sequences across a temperature x nutrition grid in one species yielding (i) a pair-reversal rate against a measured scoring-error null, (ii) a one-factor vs >=2-factor latent-scale comparison under a pre-fixed fit criterion, (iii) the variance stage-matching error contributes to a named stage-matched comparison. PRIOR 2 — Kuntz & Eisen, "Oxygen changes drive non-uniform scaling in Drosophila melanogaster embryogenesis", F1000Research 2015, 4:1102, doi 10.12688/f1000research.7221.1; READ IN FULL. Novelty confidence: Low
Significance — consequence: Both branches would change something in principle — stage reported as a vector or model-based estimate if order reverses materially, or an evidential warrant for uniform-rate correction formulas if it does not. But the consequence is substantially discharged: the existence and environment-dependence of the phenomenon is established (uniform under temperature in Drosophila, non-uniform with named order inversion under oxygen, epoch-wise in C. elegans), and the zebrafish correction formula is already reported to misestimate rate with stage-dependent residuals. The decision-relevant remainder is a magnitude, not the question as posed.
Significance — audience: Real and identifiable — staging-series maintainers and users (ZFIN, FlyBase, Carnegie/Kyoto collections), single-embryo and cell-atlas groups that stage-match before contrasting, regulatory ecotoxicology labs with stage-anchored endpoints. Demonstrably acts on findings of this kind (Kuntz & Eisen wrote the stage-matching recommendation into their Discussion; Miller et al. drew an animal-welfare/assay-classification conclusion from a staging-rate result) — which is also why the question did not stay unasked. Discounted by the adversary: transcriptomics already corrects developmental age computationally, and insect thermal biology has long known isomorphy fails in a large minority of populations, so the marginal practice change is small.
Significance — fecundity: Moderate and partly reachable from the priors — whether latent-axis count is itself species- or environment-dependent; whether transcriptomic pseudotime and morphological stage are the same latent variable; whether staging error explains part of the known irreproducibility in stage-matched contrasts; whether a maximally unidimensional landmark subset exists.
Significance — anchoring: Segmentation-clock/gross-rate decoupling; the "Discrepancies in Embryonic Staging: Towards a Gold Standard" problem; the non-linear and overestimating zebrafish temperature correction; Prior 1's own stated boundary that uniform scaling fails at temperature extremes.
Reason for silence: None credible for the question as submitted. The proposed mechanism — a disciplinary boundary, evo-devo pointing heterochrony tools between species while scale theory sits in psychometrics/metrology — was withdrawn in the record and then refuted by the adversary: the uniform-rescaling-versus-order question has been asked and answered within species in at least four literatures without psychometrics (Drosophila landmark timing 2014/2015; insect rate isomorphy 2002, with a diet axis; copepod equiproportional development 2001, temperature x food; C. elegans temporal scaling 2022, per-individual, temperature x diet). The boundary explains at most why nobody used IRT, not why nobody asked. Per the Gate 4 attack-7 rule this feeds back into Gate 2 and corroborates, rather than merely warns about, the Low grade. A residual new-instrument mechanism exists only for a different question (paired landmark scoring and single-embryo sequencing on the same individuals).

Verification (post-batch, fresh-context checker, log UQ-20261016-60-verification.md): the kill is CONFIRMED on both halves.
Kuntz and Eisen 2014 (PLoS Genetics; arXiv 1306.5297) filmed D. melanogaster embryos at seven temperatures from 17.5 to 32.5 C, scoring 36 landmarks per embryo: "while the total time of embryogenesis varies over two fold", "the relative timing of events from cellularization through hatching is constant across all species and temperatures examined here", and the landmarks occur "in the same temporal order", holding across ten further Drosophila species ("go through the same stages in the same order at all viable temperatures", Fig. 4 caption). So within a species, temperature is a uniform rescaling with order preserved — the candidate's first limb, answered.
The companion, "Oxygen changes drive non-uniform scaling in Drosophila melanogaster embryogenesis" (F1000Research 2015, 4:1102), reports that oxygen does NOT rescale uniformly and that "the order of several developmental landmarks is inverted at different oxygen levels": hypoxia has head involution finishing first, hyperoxia has the heart-shaped midgut forming first, with the inversion point shifting with temperature (about 29% O2 at 27.5 C, about 19% at 17.5 C), over more than 800 embryos across 18 oxygen-temperature conditions. So the candidate's second limb — can an environmental change invert landmark order — is answered too, with a named landmark pair.
Qualifications recorded: the evidence is MORPHOLOGICAL, hand-scored landmarks, not transcriptomic, so it should not be cited as transcriptomic evidence; the oxygen quotes are single-sourced through a page summariser (PubMed returned a captcha, so the abstract string was not independently confirmed); and the temperature paper's order-preservation claim sits in the body text and a figure caption rather than the abstract. On the secondary items: RAPToR reports agreement with chronological age as R-squared (above 0.99 for C. elegans and zebrafish, 0.74 for later fly stages, 0.997 for a Drosophila panel) with per-sample bootstrap MAD intervals, and no overall staging error in time units — so the record's "staging error" framing for RAPToR is imprecise; and the C. elegans epoch-wise temporal-scaling paper (bioRxiv 2020.09.21.306423) was surfaced by title only and NOT opened, so that leg of the Disguise finding is unverified and is recorded as such.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3
Strongest remaining objection: The candidate's core interrogative is a disguised known. Its unit of analysis, endpoint, comparator and estimand are those of Kuntz & Eisen 2014/2015 — individual embryos, morphological landmark times, one species across an environmental grid inside the viable range, order preservation under rescaling — and the set-level order claim is stated there in both directions, with the inversion named and threshold-mapped. The two limbs the record still thought open fall to adversary 1's Disguise sweep: E2 is answered epoch-wise in C. elegans and E3 in transcriptomic-staging vocabulary. What remains is a better-instrumented repeat on a particular landmark set — a methods contribution, not an un-asked question. Unresolved on attack 2 is fatal by rule, and it coincides with the independent Gate 2 Low grade rather than resting on it.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): Not applicable — rejected. For a re-intake, the only limb worth scoring from scratch is morphological-landmark stage-matching error propagated into a named stage-matched single-embryo transcriptomic or cell-atlas contrast, which must presuppose Kuntz & Eisen 2014/2015, Filina et al. 2022 and Bulteau & Francesconi 2022 rather than duplicate them, and must distinguish itself from transcriptome-instrument age error.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): None. Rejected as a disguised known / asked-and-answered question, not as asked-but-open, so no row is added to ledger/routed-open-problems.md.

ID: UQ-20261016-61
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): Medicine — rare-disease diagnostics; clinical epidemiology; health-systems performance measurement. Method-owning field: truncated time-to-event biostatistics / back-calculation and nowcasting.
Question (canonical): For a rare-disease population with datable symptom onset, does the reported fall in time-to-diagnosis survive estimation from an incident symptom-onset frame with right truncation and delay-dependent inclusion modelled explicitly — i.e. is the diagnostic odyssey measurably shortening, or is the apparent improvement an artefact of counting only patients who were eventually diagnosed?
Alternative formulations:
- Is the headline rare-disease diagnostic-delay figure (~5 y) and its reported decline identified at all from prevalent diagnosed cohorts, and what does a truncation-corrected back-calculation give for recent onset cohorts?
- Everyone says rare-disease patients wait about five years and that the wait is falling, but the number counts only people who got diagnosed — if the still-undiagnosed are accounted for, is the wait actually falling?
- (Gate 1 reformulation, retained) In one named source enumerating symptom-onset cohorts rather than diagnosed patients, estimate F_c per onset cohort under explicit right truncation with a pre-stated delay-dependent inclusion model, report the naive diagnosed-only estimate beside it on the same records, and decompose any difference into truncation artefact, case-mix change and change in the diagnosis hazard.
Motivating gap: IRDiRC (one year) and Rare 2030 (six months) targets are scored against delay figures computed on already-diagnosed samples — Faye et al., Eur J Hum Genet 2024;32:1116-1126 (4.7 y mean; states the indicator excludes those still waiting and "does not allow to monitor the evolution of TDT over time") and Benito-Lozano et al., Orphanet J Rare Dis 2022 (10.1186/s13023-022-02530-3; −5.1%/yr joinpoint trend, own most-recent segment discarded because recent-onset patients "have not yet had the opportunity to be diagnosed"). Right truncation and advocacy-panel recruitment bias push in opposite directions, so even the sign of the published trend is unestablished. (Both motivating sources were intake-reported, not re-opened at Gate 2; neither was graded as a prior.)
Presuppositions: P1 headline levels/trends come from prevalent diagnosed samples — ESTABLISHED (verified for Perez-Alamino et al., RMD Open 2025;11(1):e004756). P2 still-undiagnosed excluded — ESTABLISHED. P3 onset and diagnosis dates recoverable accurately — CONTESTED (recall bias). P4 "date of diagnosis" a single well-defined event — CONTESTED (Ferrandiz-Espadin et al., J Rheumatol 2025 defined the clock start twice, 761→404 patients). P5 a frame enumerating rare-disease onset cohorts including the never-diagnosed exists or can be built — CONTESTED, UNVERIFIED, LOAD-BEARING. P6 identifiability under right truncation given a stated inclusion model — PARTLY ESTABLISHED, conditional (Seaman/Presanis/Jackson 2022). P7 recruitment probability correlated with delay — CONTESTED, unestimated. P8 case mix not fixed across periods — flagged. P9 someone acts on the number — ESTABLISHED (IRDiRC/Rare 2030).
What would count as an answer: In at least one population with datable onset and an incidence-anchored frame, a pre-registered estimate of (i) the onset-cohort delay distribution with right truncation handled (back-calculation / reporting-delay deconvolution, with a sensitivity band over inclusion models and worst-case delay-dependent-inclusion bounds), reported beside (ii) the naive prevalent-frame estimate on the same records, plus (iii) a decomposition of the published trend into truncation artefact, case-mix change and diagnosis hazard. Agreement vindicates the indicator; a sign flip means the published improvements and the targets scored on them rest on an artefact.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 20 documented web queries (11 at Gate 2, 9 new-vocabulary Disguise queries by adversary 1) plus 9 fetches; full lists in batches/2026-10-16-2337/UQ-20261016-61-record.md and UQ-20261016-61-adversary-1.md. Novelty confidence: Low
Significance — consequence: If the trend survives correction, the indicator is vindicated at the level of sign and the IRDiRC/Rare 2030 targets become assessable with stated identification conditions. If the sign flips, the published declines (Spanish registry −5.1%/yr and the −55%/yr 2018–2021 segment, the ASAS-COMOSPA onset-decade trend, DANBIO, national action-plan dashboards) are frame artefacts and the targets cannot be scored; the decomposition separates "sequencing diffused and the easy diseases got faster" from "the odyssey got shorter."

Correction entered from Gate 4: ARD 74(3):e12 is the original Sørensen & Hetland DANBIO article, not the other half of the correspondence as the Gate 2 record stated; opened in full, it reports the delay decline and names censoring, channelling and immortal-time bias without correcting for right truncation (its 240-month cap is a variance cap, not truncation handling, and its recent-onset sensitivity analyses make the truncation worse). This strengthens, not weakens, the Gate 2 ground: the bias is named in the target paper's own text.
Verification (post-batch, fresh-context checker, log UQ-20261016-61-verification.md): the Gate 2 kill is CONFIRMED verbatim, and the routing ground with it.
All three strings appear in Feldtkeller & Rudwaleit, Ann Rheum Dis 2014;73(12):e77, each checked singly and then jointly: "The authors neglected in their analysis and interpretation all the patients with recent symptom onset who were not yet diagnosed and are therefore not part of their database."; "the average delay in diagnosis found in the DANBIO register seems to be a realistic approximation only for former disease-onset decades, that is, for patients with symptom onset 20-40 years ago"; "However, in order to demonstrate this reduction reliably, we need another 20 years passing by." The letter proposes and applies no correction: it names the missing observations as "diagnoses to be expected in the future", records that Fries et al. called the problem "right censoring", prefers to call it "an incorrect analysis and incorrect data interpretation", and offers waiting as its only remedy. Its unit is individual AS patients grouped by year of symptom onset, its endpoint onset-to-diagnosis time, and the quantity it disputes is the registry's average delay by onset cohort, which it says is biased for recent cohorts. So the question is asked in print and is not answered there, which is the asked-but-open shape exactly; the Gate 2 Low grade and the routed row rest on the same confirmed sentences.
Birrell et al. 2012 (doi 10.1515/1948-4690.1055) is confirmed as a Bayesian back-calculation on England-and-Wales HIV/AIDS diagnosis surveillance "augmented by observed CD4 count levels at diagnosis", jointly estimating incidence, diagnosis rate, time-to-diagnosis trend, time-since-infection and undiagnosed prevalence, and reporting "a decreasing trend in the time to diagnosis and stable levels of incidence in recent years"; its details come from the abstract page only. The CD4 level is what makes that estimator identify both quantities at once, and rare disease has no counterpart clock — which is why P5 survives verification rather than being softened by the precedent, and why the routed row is narrowed to the limb that needs no incidence-anchored frame.
Caveat recorded: the verbatim matches are the page summariser's report, not raw page text.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3
Strongest remaining objection: P5 — no source anywhere in 20 queries enumerates rare-disease symptom-onset cohorts including the never-diagnosed, and onset-cohort membership is not knowable without the diagnosis label or a biomarker clock rare disease does not have; so the question as reformulated presupposes a frame that does not exist and reduces to a demand that one be built.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): settle P5 first — ask whether any single source enumerates rare-disease symptom-onset cohorts including the never-diagnosed (NHS England genomic-medicine-service referral spine, an undiagnosed-diseases programme intake register, or EHR first-symptom coding over a pre-specified disease list); if none does, state the problem as frame construction, not as trend estimation.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): Routed to `ledger/routed-open-problems.md` as asked-but-open. Gate: Rejected at Gate 2 (Low novelty — the canonical question is in print as Feldtkeller & Rudwaleit, ARD 73(12):e77, and the structurally identical question was answered for HIV with the candidate's own estimator), independently fatal at Gate 4 on attack 4 Unresolved (P5 presupposition failure), with attack 7 Unresolved concurring. Disguise was executed (9 queries) and returned Partial, so no check is unverified; only one adversary was run, which is immaterial to a Rejection. The routed limb is narrowed, because the ledger's own attack 4 bears on it. A frame enumerating onset cohorts including the never-diagnosed is what P5 shows unavailable, and the HIV precedent does not transfer: verification confirmed that Birrell et al. 2012 identifies time-to-diagnosis and undiagnosed prevalence jointly only because CD4 at diagnosis supplies a time-since-infection clock, and rare disease has no counterpart to it. So what is routed is the identifiable part only — a right-truncation-corrected onset-cohort delay distribution estimated from registry records carrying both an onset date and a diagnosis date, reported beside the naive diagnosed-only estimate on the same records, with a pre-stated sensitivity band for a delay-dependent never-diagnosed fraction and a truncation/case-mix/hazard decomposition — and the incidence-anchored version is explicitly kept out of the row. Tier B for the routed limb: the estimator family and software exist and the gating step is record-level access to a registry that published a delay decline. The incidence-anchored version stays Tier C and is not routed.

ID: UQ-20261016-62
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): Medicine — clinical microbiology; hospital epidemiology and infection prevention; antimicrobial stewardship. Adjacent/method-owning: measurement reliability and QC, reliability engineering (common-cause failure in a 2-out-of-2 channel), diagnostic biostatistics (conditional dependence between repeated applications of one test).
Question (canonical): Is contamination of the two blood-culture sets drawn in one episode independent between sets, and given the measured within-episode correlation what is the misclassification rate of the standard interpretive convention that one positive set of two indicates contamination while both positive indicates true bacteraemia?
Alternative formulations:
- How much of what is counted as true bacteraemia on the strength of a commensal growing in both of two sets is correlated contamination from a shared draw, operator, skin-prep failure or antiseptic lot rather than bloodstream infection?
- Does the two-set rule for separating contaminants from pathogens rest on an independence assumption that the way blood is actually drawn violates, and by how much?
- (Gate 1 reformulation, retained) In episodes with exactly two sets and retrievable draw-level metadata, with commensal status fixed by a pre-specified organism list and concordance required to be species- (ideally strain-) matched: (a) the ratio of observed both-sets-concordant commensal proportion to the proportion predicted by between-set independence from the same cohort's per-set rate, with a CI and null ratio = 1; (b) variance components of that excess by operator, draw structure, prep protocol and antiseptic lot; (c) the RELATIVE reclassification fraction of the 1-of-2 / 2-of-2 rule against a pre-specified blinded adjudication standard, reported as an interval under stated assumptions rather than as an absolute error rate.
Motivating gap: The convention's stated logic is probabilistic — two contamination events are unlikely to coincide — so it needs between-set independence, while contamination is a clustered process attached to operator, prep and technique, and the two sets are routinely drawn by one person minutes apart. The intake claim that the within-episode correlation is "never reported ... at episode level" is FALSE and the correction is load-bearing: Borad et al., ASHE 5(1), Sept 2025 (opened in full) takes the pair as the unit, reports how often both sets grew commensals, and stratifies that proportion by shared vs separated draw (28.1% single-time-stamp vs 18.5% multiple-time-stamp, P = .11; per-pair commensal recovery 6.3% vs 7.3%) — the candidate's mechanism test in weaker form, in its own field and unit, eight weeks before intake.
Presuppositions: P1 the 1-of-2/2-of-2 multiplicity rule really drives interpretation — UNVERIFIED at Gate 2 (no CLSI/ASM document opened, fetch cap), then EVIDENCED at Gate 4 from a primary source: Yu et al. 2020's own contamination criterion A classifies isolates as "potentially contaminant if they grew in three or fewer of the six bottles"; Beekmann 2005's best algorithm requires ">=2 blood cultures positive for CoNS within 5 days", which is multiplicity across 5 days, not two sets in one episode. P2 within-episode contamination events share causes — PARTLY EVIDENCED (Borad 2025, direction as predicted, underpowered). P3 correlated contamination separable from true bacteraemia retrospectively — CONTESTED. P4 LIS carries linkable draw-level metadata — time stamps VERIFIED (Borad), operator identity and antiseptic lot UNVERIFIED as retrievable at scale; Borad concedes the time-stamp proxy "may not always hold". P5 a reference standard independent of the rule under test — CONTESTED and conceded; every adjudication standard found is unblinded to multiplicity, Yu 2020's being a bottle-count rule outright. P6 downstream costs material — plausible, no source opened. P7 per-set rates estimable in-cohort for the independence benchmark — VERIFIED (Borad publishes both).
What would count as an answer: An episode-level analysis giving (i) within-episode commensal concordance in excess of the independence prediction from the same cohort's per-set rate, with a CI; (ii) variance components for that excess by operator, prep and draw context; (iii) the 2-of-2 rule's PPV and the 1-of-2 rule's NPV under the measured correlation against a pre-specified standard. Strengthened by a prospective arm in which the two sets are deliberately drawn by different operators with independent prep, making the correlation experimentally manipulable. A null would be an informative first defence of a decades-old convention.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 20 documented queries (11 at Gate 2, 9 new-vocabulary Disguise queries by adversary 1, minimum 8 met) plus 9 fetch attempts; full lists in batches/2026-10-16-2337/UQ-20261016-62-record.md and UQ-20261016-62-adversary-1.md. Most informative: `within-episode correlation blood culture contamination independence assumption two sets drawn same phlebotomist` → the decisive hit, Borad et al. ASHE 2025 plus its IDWeek companion P-1582, i.e. the candidate's unit and concordance endpoint in print; `"both sets" OR "two of two" positive blood cultures probability of simultaneous contamination independence multiplication rule questioned` → practice guidance and the same ASHE/IDWeek cluster, nothing framing the rule AS an independence assumption; `Elzi discriminate contamination ... number of positive blood culture sets predictive value` → the 2011 single-venipuncture multi-bottle PPV series (CoNS PPV 3.5% at 1 bottle, 61.1% at 2) plus the then-unread JCM growth-patterns paper; `common cause failure beta factor two-out-of-two redundancy voting correlated failures applied to diagnostic test confirmation` → the method-owning literature is mature and has never been pointed at diagnostic confirmation; (adversary) `single-sampling strategy blood culture contaminant interpretation multiple sets positivity Dargere Lamy single venipuncture` → Yu 2020 and the live single- vs multi-site sampling line the record lacked; (adversary) `"Diagnostic value of blood culture growth patterns ..." doi` → resolves the record's largest declared unread risk to Ben-Chetrit et al. 2025, J Clin Microbiol, doi:10.1128/jcm.01210-25; (adversary) `blood culture contamination rates variation by phlebotomist intraclass correlation clustering nurse-level random effects multilevel` → contamination-reduction trials only, no operator-level ICC reported anywhere, so limb (b)'s object is genuinely unreported. Access routing: Borad 2025 read in full at Cambridge, Yu 2020 at the Frontiers publisher PDF; PMC not attempted (hard-blocked).
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
1. Borad A, Ibrahim A, Boruchoff SE, Kaye KS, Abdul Azim A, "Comparing contamination rates in paired blood culture sets with a single-time stamp vs multiple-time stamps", Antimicrobial Stewardship & Healthcare Epidemiology 5(1), Sept 2025 (Cambridge, full text read) — UNIT: the pair of sets, explicitly the episode (same as candidate). ENDPOINT: pre-defined commensal recovery, reported both as at-least-one-set (6.3% vs 7.3%) and as BOTH sets positive (28.1% STS vs 18.5% MTS, P = .11) — the concordance quantity the intake said was unreported. COMPARATOR: MTS pairs vs STS pairs, an observed draw-structure contrast, not an independence benchmark. ESTIMAND: the STS-minus-MTS difference, not a correlation, ICC or misclassification rate.
2. PubMed 21499970 (2011), interpretive guidelines for positive blood cultures from a single venipuncture; CITATION UNCONFIRMED (abstract read, second fetch hit a reCAPTCHA) — UNIT: the positive six-bottle set from one venipuncture (940 sets), the maximally correlated regime. ENDPOINT: bloodstream infection vs contamination per set. REFERENCE: prospective clinician/bacteriologist/epidemiologist classification, unblinded to bottle count. ESTIMAND: PPV by number of positive bottles (CoNS 3.5% / 61.1% / 78.9% / 100%) — the candidate's "how often does multiplicity mislead" limb already computed in adjacent form, and large.
3. Beekmann SE, Diekema DJ, Doern GV, "Determining the Clinical Significance of Coagulase-Negative Staphylococci Isolated From Blood Cultures", Infect Control Hosp Epidemiol 2005;26(6):559-566, DOI 10.1086/502584 (abstract, metadata and references read; full text "Temporarily unavailable") — UNIT: the episode (405 CoNS-containing of 960). ENDPOINT: significant vs contaminant CoNS. REFERENCE: one experienced reviewer's chart determination. ESTIMAND: sensitivity/specificity of published algorithms (best 62%/91%) — the candidate's limb (c) in weaker form, with no separate PPV for the multiplicity component and no error decomposition.
Added at Gate 4, not one of the three: Ben-Chetrit et al. 2025, "Diagnostic Value of Blood Culture Growth Patterns in Distinguishing Contaminants from Pathogens", J Clin Microbiol, doi:10.1128/jcm.01210-25 — 38,216 peripherally drawn sets, with container concordance as the diagnostic variable (contaminants 71.1% of discordant vs 11.4% of concordant sets; CoNS discordant 98.0% contamination; NPV of a discordant first CoNS culture 98.1%, 95% CI 96.7-98.9). READ ONLY VIA A SECONDARY journal-club summary (rapidmicrobiology, 30 Jan 2026); the primary paper was not opened, so no grade below rests on it alone. Its concordance is between the two bottles of ONE set, one unit down from the candidate.
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs 1 — shares unit and substantially the endpoint (2 of 4 attributes), differs on comparator and estimand; the candidate adds a formal independence benchmark with a CI and a sharp null, species/strain matching, variance components beyond a binary time-stamp proxy, and the rule's PPV/NPV. What it does not add is the question: whether shared-draw structure raises both-sets commensal concordance has been asked, and answered inconclusively. vs 2 — two sets from two draws rather than bottles from one, and a correlation rather than a PPV; but Prior 2 already supplies the order of magnitude of the consequence the candidate reaches for. vs 3 — decomposes the rule's error into between-set correlation where Beekmann reports only overall accuracy; but Beekmann's unblinded single reviewer is exactly the circularity the candidate's own P5 concedes. vs Ben-Chetrit — one unit down (within-set bottle concordance, not between-set), and draw structure unstated; but it is the audience's practical question ("how far should multiplicity of positive containers be trusted?") being answered at scale, in the candidate's own journal, while the candidate was being formulated.
Novelty confidence: Low
Significance — consequence: If the excess concordance is large, the 2-of-2 commensal rule's PPV is materially below what the independence intuition implies, so a quantifiable share of line removals, echocardiograms and multi-week vancomycin courses is triggered by correlated contamination and a share of hospital-onset-bacteraemia counts is an artefact of draw practice. A null licenses a convention that surveillance definitions already rest on without evidence. Actionable either way, since the fix (two independently prepped draws, or draw structure as a covariate) is cheap and partly deployed.
Significance — audience: clinical microbiology laboratories setting commenting rules for commensal isolates; infection prevention and the bodies specifying hospital-onset-bacteraemia metrics (the Borad/Kaye/Abdul Azim group is already publishing here); antimicrobial stewardship, for vancomycin days attributable to concordant commensal pairs; phlebotomy, vascular access and diversion-device vendors, for whom "does the device reduce the correlation or only the rate?" is new and answerable. Real and demonstrably active — two 2025 primary papers, two further IDWeek abstracts, a registered 2026 collection-strategy trial (NCT07751575, record could not be read).
Significance — fecundity: makes askable whether the two-set requirement should be re-specified as two independently prepped draws by different operators; whether interpretive algorithms should weight concordance by draw metadata rather than count sets; whether diversion devices and dedicated phlebotomy teams cut the correlation or only the marginal rate; whether HOB and CLABSI definitions need a draw-structure covariate; and whether every other "confirm on a second specimen" rule in the laboratory carries the same correlated-confirmation problem.
Significance — anchoring: the CoNS-significance problem; the live single-site vs multi-site sampling controversy (Borad 2025, Yu 2020, NCT07751575); the validity of the emerging hospital-onset-bacteraemia quality measure; and, as a transplant target, common-cause failure in a 2-out-of-2 redundant confirmatory channel, mature in reliability engineering and never applied here.
Reason for silence: Offered as a denominator/committee boundary — contamination is owned as a per-set laboratory QC indicator reported to accreditation bodies, interpretation lives in bedside commenting guidance, and the within-episode correlation that links them is in neither document family's required reporting, so no committee must compute it. The adversary accepts that half as a genuine disciplinary-boundary mechanism and rejects the second half (metadata only recently extractable) as a why-answering-was-hard story rather than a why-nobody-asked one. Decisively for the present tense, the silence is already broken: three 2025-2026 primary papers, two abstracts and a trial are asking adjacent versions, which is the situation in which a novelty claim should be presumed stale.

Unread-source note: the adversary's largest residual was identified during verification and read at abstract level — Senger SS, Saccozza ME, Yüce A, Infect Control Hosp Epidemiol 2007;28(8):992-996, doi 10.1086/518753 — and it does test multiple-positive-culture criteria against strain identity, so it is the further prior art the batch flagged as a risk rather than an open residual: CDC surveillance criteria including "the recovery of CoNS from 2 or more successive blood cultures" scored against PFGE, criterion 2a at sensitivity 100% and specificity 31.6%, criterion 2b at 78.9% and 52.6%. Its full text is still COULD NOT READ (resolve.cambridge.org HTTP 403 on URL length; the cambridge.org product page serves abstract and references only, purchase "temporarily unavailable"), so the mapping of 2a to the multiple-culture rule rests on the abstract's own listing rather than on the paper's definitions table. The record's own unread risk (the JCM growth-patterns paper) was closed by adversary query 6.
Verification (post-batch, two fresh-context checkers, logs UQ-20261016-62-verification.md and UQ-20261016-62-verification-2.md): the kill's figures are CONFIRMED as printed, one step of its characterisation is corrected, and the second pass closed the limb this entry had been about to route.
Borad et al., Antimicrob Steward Healthc Epidemiol 5(1), 2025, read through the Cambridge core-reader page (PMC12451794 blocked): 5,296 pairs of blood-culture sets drawn within one hour at a 650-bed academic centre between 1 June 2022 and 15 November 2023, 4,411 single-time-stamp (STS) and 885 multiple-time-stamp (MTS), pairs with non-commensal organisms excluded; commensal growth in "6.3% (278/4,411) of STS and 7.3% (65/885) of MTS"; and, verbatim, "28.1% (78/278) of those STS pairs and 18.5% (12/65) of those MTS pairs grew commensal organisms in both BC sets (P = .11)." The denominator is commensal-positive pairs, not all pairs, and the quantity is a proportion rather than an agreement estimand: no kappa, no intraclass correlation, no concordance odds ratio, no confidence interval, no named test, and no comparison against what independence between sets would predict. The paper nowhere evaluates the one-positive-of-two interpretive rule, and concedes "We also did not adjudicate whether patients had true bacteremia with commensal organisms". Its Discussion poses the consequence instead of measuring it — single-site sampling "may increase the risk of misclassifying patients as having true bacteremia" — and its remark that MTS "may yield higher rates" of two-of-two positivity runs against the direction it reports. So the entry's phrase "reports the candidate's both-sets concordance quantity" is corrected to a descriptive both-sets-positive proportion among commensal-positive pairs. The Gate 2 Low grade is unaffected: the candidate's unit (the pair), endpoint (both sets growing a commensal) and causal variable (shared draw) are Borad's, and the independence excess the candidate wants is one line of arithmetic off their printed counts.
The second pass identified the record's unreadable residual and it does more damage to the candidate than the entry allowed for. It is Senger SS, Saccozza ME, Yüce A, Infect Control Hosp Epidemiol 2007;28(8):992-996, doi 10.1086/518753, and its abstract page reads: "The clinical criteria comprised Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) surveillance definitions" including "the recovery of CoNS from 2 or more successive blood cultures"; "Criterion 2a of the CDC definition for BSI had a sensitivity of 100%" "and a specificity of 31.6% for distinguishing between true bacteremia and contamination."; "CDC criterion 2b had a sensitivity of 78.9% and a specificity of 52.6%." That is the candidate's limb (c) done in 2007 — the operating characteristics of a multiple-positive-culture criterion scored against a reference standard that does not use multiplicity at all, namely PFGE strain identity. It also refutes this entry's own claim that no adjudication standard blinded to multiplicity exists; strain typing is one, and it was used for exactly this purpose.
Two limits on that finding, recorded rather than smoothed over: the full text COULD NOT BE READ (resolve.cambridge.org refused with HTTP 403 on URL length, the cambridge.org product page gives abstract and references only, purchase "temporarily unavailable"), so the mapping of criterion 2a to the two-or-more-cultures rule rests on the abstract's own listing plus general knowledge of the CDC definition rather than on the paper's definitions table; and whether "2 or more successive blood cultures" means separate venipunctures or repeated draws from one is not visible. Neither limit rescues the candidate: on any reading, a multiplicity-based criterion has been scored against strain identity and the numbers are in print.
Consequence for routing: nothing from this entry is routed. The limb the batch had drafted a row for — the misclassification rate of the one-of-two convention against a standard independent of set count — is answered, not open, and an answered rejection is never routed. The independence benchmark is derivable in a page from Borad's printed counts, so it is not open either, and the operator- and antiseptic-lot attribution limb has no source showing the linkage retrievable at scale.
Caveats recorded: the absences at Q2 and Q4 in Borad are the page summariser's report rather than a full-text search, and the paper's table image was unreadable.

Scores: Well-posedness 3/3 (limb (a) sharp null, defined estimand, data shown to exist; limb (b) well defined given metadata; limb (c) made answerable by the V2 relative estimand, and attack 4 Resolved, so no presupposition is false — the generator's self-scored 2/3 understated it, and it does not change the verdict) · Significance 2/3
Strongest remaining objection: The limbs trade off and no choice of limb survives both attacks at once. The only limb immune to the reference-standard circularity and to dissolution — limb (a), excess concordance over an independence benchmark — is the one already asked in the candidate's own field with the candidate's own unit and endpoint (Borad et al. 2025) and derivable to an order of magnitude in a page from that paper's published proportions; the limbs that would be genuinely novel cannot be delivered, since (b) needs operator and antiseptic-lot linkage no opened source shows retrievable at scale and 20 queries found nobody reporting, and (c) was held to need an adjudication standard blinded to multiplicity that does not exist — and verification found one, used for this exact purpose eighteen years before intake: Senger et al. 2007 scored CDC multiple-culture criteria against PFGE strain identity and printed the operating characteristics. So limb (c) is not undeliverable, it is delivered, which is a worse position for the candidate than the batch's own objection described. What remains true in the original objection is the narrower point that Yu et al. 2020's contamination definition is built out of the very multiplicity rule the candidate wants to validate against it, so a clinical-adjudication standard is still circular; the strain-typing standard is not.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): before any new data collection, obtain Borad et al.'s own denominators and recompute the both-sets concordance against an independence benchmark from the same cohort's per-set rate with a CI — that settles whether limb (a) has anything left in it; then settle P4 by asking whether any single site can join set identity, operator and antiseptic lot to results at scale, because limbs (b) and (c) are frame-construction problems until it can.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): None, after verification. Gate: Rejected at Gate 2 (novelty Low — an on-point paper in the candidate's own field and words, published eight weeks before intake, uses the candidate's unit of analysis, reports the candidate's both-sets concordance quantity and tests the candidate's shared-draw mechanism; the intake's central factual claim that this is "not reported anywhere" is refuted by a source opened in full). Gate 4 ran and reached no Unresolved status, so the attack table alone would have permitted Provisional; Low novelty is decided at Gate 2 and is not curable by the adversarial log, and the residual limbs are the next paper in an existing line rather than an un-asked question. Disguise was executed (9 queries, 2 Resolved / 6 Partial overall), so no fatal check is unverified; only one adversary was run, which is immaterial to a Rejection. The batch drafted a row for the misclassification limb and verification withdrew it before it was written: Senger et al. 2007 scored a multiple-positive-culture criterion against PFGE strain identity and reported sensitivity and specificity, so that limb is answered rather than open, and an answered rejection is never routed. Nor is anything else here routable: the independence benchmark is one line of arithmetic off Borad's printed counts (independence on their per-pair commensal rates predicts low single-digit both-sets concordance against the 18.5-28.1% observed), so it is derivable rather than open, and the operator- and antiseptic-lot attribution limb has no source showing that linkage retrievable at scale. ID: UQ-20261016-63
Date: 2026-10-16
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): Medicine / public health — global-health measurement, epidemiology, programme monitoring. Method field: macroeconometrics / official statistics (real-time data and revision analysis). Source method: cross-field transplant.

Question (canonical) — R1, adopted at Gate 1: For a pre-specified set of country-year modelled global-health estimates (primary WUENIC DTP3/MCV1; secondary UN IGME U5MR, MMEIG MMR) and a pre-specified vintage window of annual releases — (a) what are the moments and serial structure of the revision r_{c,t}^{v->v+1}; (b) in the paired regressions of the revision on the prior vintage's level and on the latest value, was the prior vintage an inefficient ("noise-like") estimate of the current one, restated as estimator stability rather than an agency information set; and (c) in a pre-registered sample of published analyses tied to an identifiable earlier vintage, what fraction of headline estimates change sign, cross a pre-declared decision threshold, or gain/lose significance when re-run on the current vintage? (V0 as intaken, and the reason for the single reformulation, in the record.)

Alternative formulations:
1. (lay) Do the annual re-estimations of WHO/UNICEF immunization coverage and comparable series revise history enough to overturn the studies, rankings and target assessments built on the earlier numbers?
2. (infrastructure) Does global health need a vintage ("real-time") database of its headline indicators, and what would a revision-stability audit show?
3. (method field's words) Is the first-release vintage of a modelled global-health indicator an efficient forecast of its later vintages, and how vintage-sensitive are the published results resting on it?

Motivating gap:
As intaken: producers restate history annually (WHO: "Coverage data are reviewed and the estimates updated annually"; 2025 revision released 15 July 2026 with full historical country series) while global health has imported none of macroeconomics' revision apparatus. PARTLY FALSIFIED AT GATE 2: the "no revision statistics" half is untrue of the field's largest modelled series (Prior A, in the candidate's own field and words, seven months before intake). What survived intake was the country-year unit, coverage-type indicators, the efficiency test and the conclusion-reversal rate.

Presuppositions:
P1 historical country-years are re-estimated, not appended — established in kind, unverified in detail (WUENIC 2025-revision notes PDF COULD NOT BE READ by either agent); contested for the primary indicator by one opened aggregator page stating WUENIC "can keep a previous estimate when new information is unavailable". P2 prior vintages retrievable — contested and limiting; no archive found, one aggregator explicitly disclaims vintage status, two coexisting country-profile paths are URL-level evidence only; reconstructible from annual publications (as Wolff et al. and Goes did) but laborious. P3 published analyses tie to an identifiable vintage — contested, untested by anyone; non-identifiability is a reportable stratum. P4 revisions large relative to detectable effects — answered yes for GBD risk-factor burden, unmeasured for coverage. P5 news/noise transfers to model-based estimates — contested; the genuine interface problem, and weakened if the primary series is rule-based carry-forward rather than an annual refit. P6 "headline conclusion" pre-registrable — flagged, operationalised in R1. P7 someone acts on the numbers — established in kind. P8 producer uncertainty does not subsume the question — partly established from the independent side only (revised points outside prior UIs), not from producer documentation.

What would count as an answer:
(i) a vintage matrix with revision moments, serial structure and the share of revisions outside the superseded release's uncertainty interval; (ii) the paired prior-vintage-efficiency regressions per indicator with the P5 caveat carried into interpretation; (iii) a pre-registered re-run of a sampled frame of published analyses reporting sign changes, threshold crossings, significance changes, and the share excluded for unidentifiable vintage; (iv) a specification of a global-health real-time database. Both directions act.

Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result):
20 distinct queries in total — 11 at Gate 2 (plus 5 fetches) and 9 by adversary 1 in four vocabularies Gate 2 had not tried, one of them aimed at the answer rather than the question. Full lists: batches/2026-10-16-2337/UQ-20261016-63-record.md and UQ-20261016-63-adversary-1.md. Most informative:
- [own field, own words] "changes in Global Burden of Disease estimates between successive rounds same country-year revisions GBD 2019 2021 comparison" → Prior A (JAMA Health Forum 2026); the hit that decided the grade.
- [method-owning field] "Penn World Table vintages revisions impact on published growth regression results 'is newer better'" → Prior B, the full template including downstream re-runs.
- [adversary, development economics] "Wolff Chong Auffhammer 'Human Development Index' data error revisions country classification consequences" → NBER WP 16572 / EJ 2011: per-country revision variability of HDI inputs including a UN-modelled health series (life expectancy), HDI vintages reconstructed from annual reports, ~34% of countries misclassified, replicated parameters varying "by up to 100% due to data error".
- [adversary, metascience] "'World Development Indicators' OR 'SDG indicators' data revisions between releases replication vintage reproducibility" → Goes, I4R DP 23 (2023): WDI/PWT/Maddison vintages, country-year unit, 459 articles coded, 2 of 3 replications overturned by vintage swap; World Bank DataBank archive shows the instrument exists for WDI.
- ["what fraction of X", own field] "reanalysis using different release of WHO or UNICEF estimates changed conclusions country ranking SDG target assessment reversed" → nothing but an anecdotal blog on population-denominator revisions; no reversal rate for a health series.
- [adversary, answer-directed] "DTP3 coverage WUENIC '2023 revision' '2024 revision' differences previous revision percentage points same year" → no vintage archive; aggregator page disclaims vintage status and reports carry-forward.
COULD NOT READ: WUENIC 2025-revision notes PDF (both agents; fetch budget, URL not surfaced). IGME annual reports surfaced, not opened — whether they carry a "previous round" comparison is Unverified. No PMC/Europe PMC route attempted.

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
PRIOR A — Zavalis EA, Pezzullo AM, Ioannidis JPA, "Instability of Global Burden of Disease Estimates of Deaths and DALYs From Major Risk Factors", JAMA Health Forum 2026;7(3):e260108, 13 Mar 2026, doi:10.1001/jamahealthforum.2026.0108 (opened by both agents; attributes and numbers confirmed independently). Unit: risk factor × calendar year, global/regional. Endpoint: dispersion across eight GBD iterations (median range-to-mean 0.5 deaths, CV>0.2 for 336/675 death estimates, 96% of SSB estimates outside the GBD 2019 UI, processed meat 8th→13th). Comparator: other iterations and the superseded UI. Estimand: descriptive, exploratory, not pre-registered.
PRIOR B — Johnson S, Larson W, Papageorgiou C, Subramanian A, "Is Newer Better? Penn World Table Revisions and Their Impact on Growth Estimates", 2009 (opened). Unit: country-year PPP GDP levels/growth. Endpoint: revision moments (29-year average growth SD ~1.1pp; annual SD 5.39pp), sign changes in 13% of countries, top/bottom-10 turnover, plus replication of 13 published papers of which 4 change substantively and 35% of sustained-growth cases reclassify. Estimand: the vintage-induced change in a published coefficient — limb (c), for GDP.
PRIOR C — Tang J, Rumack A, Wilder B, Rosenfeld R, "Real-time Forecasting of Data Revisions in Epidemic Surveillance Streams", medRxiv 2025.05.12.25327058 (opened). Unit: location × reference date by reporting lag. Endpoint: quantile forecasts of the finalized value scored by WIS against a flat-line baseline. Mechanism: reporting backfill of counts, not annual re-estimation.
Also: Wolff, Chong & Auffhammer (NBER WP 16572, 2010 / Economic Journal 2011) and Goes (I4R DP 23, 2023), both opened by adversary 1 — two further executed instances of the same template on development indicators, one including a UN-modelled health series; and the rOpenSci `reviser` package (Apr 2026), which makes limbs (a)–(b) off-the-shelf tooling.

Novelty — how this differs from each:
vs A: country-year rather than global risk-factor-year, coverage/mortality series rather than attributable burden, serial structure and an efficiency regression rather than R:M and CV, and limb (c) absent from A — but the same question-type, in the same field, in the field's own words, and it falsifies the stated gap and already does the P8 work. vs B: the same design on another series and field; B supplies the published "what fraction" number (≈4/13 papers, 35% of cases) that limb (c) asks for, so limb (c) is an unexecuted transplant of a documented template, novel only in its target series. vs C: C forecasts the eventual value of a count revised by reporting lag, not an annual model refit, and touches neither (a) nor (c). vs Wolff/Goes: neither targets WUENIC/IGME/MMEIG and neither runs an efficiency regression, but both execute the vintage-sensitivity-of-published-results design on country-year development indicators, Wolff on a UN-modelled health input.

Novelty confidence: Low.

Significance — consequence:
Small unforecastable revisions license current practice with a citable number; large ones not bounded by the superseded interval (already shown for a sibling series by A) plus a non-trivial reversal rate would make vintage citation a reporting item, a vintage archive fundable infrastructure, and target-attainment claims vintage-relative; forecastable revisions would make the first release bias-correctable at publication, a change to producer output.

Significance — audience:
Producers (WUENIC, IGME, MMEIG, IHME) who would publish revision triangles or an as-of API; target monitors (Gavi, IA2030, SDG custodians); impact evaluators and health economists using the series as exposure or outcome; journal editors who could require a release identifier at near-zero cost; the real-time-data community, for whom a modelled rather than reported series is a new regime. Activation is demonstrated for GBD and HDI consumers, not for the named WUENIC/IGME users (adversary attack 6, Partial).

Significance — fecundity:
Whether a revision-corrected first release can be published; whether revision magnitude is a cheap data-system-weakness indicator (B found revisions tracked data-quality grade); vintage-robust panel estimators; whether target-setting against a restated series creates a measurable incentive artefact; what the right null is when the "forecaster" is an estimator.

Significance — anchoring:
The reliability/comparability dispute over modelled global-health estimates (IGME-vs-IHME, A's instability finding, MMEIG round caveats); the reproducibility blind spot that a reproducible script on a restated input is not reproducible in result; measurement error in development statistics (B, Wolff, Goes); and the surveillance-backfill programme (C), which built as-of infrastructure for counts while annual modelled series have none.

Reason for silence:
Disciplinary boundary, credible. The archive-absence ("missing instrument") half of the intake mechanism does not survive: Wolff reconstructed HDI vintages from annual reports with no archive, Goes used the World Bank's own archive, and WUENIC/IGME publish annual country files — so instrument absence explains the cost of answering, not the silence. What stands is that economists and meta-researchers audit the data they use while health researchers import the numbers; every template instance found was produced by the former, including Prior A, which is why the residual limbs are likely to be asked soon by someone else.

Verification (post-batch, two fresh-context checkers, logs UQ-20261016-63-verification.md and UQ-20261016-63-verification-2.md): the first of the two Gate 2 grounds is WITHDRAWN, the second is CONFIRMED and sharpened, and the rejection stands on the second alone.
Ground (i) falls on unit. Prior A is Zavalis EA, Pezzullo AM, Ioannidis JPA, "Instability of Global Burden of Disease Estimates of Deaths and Disability-Adjusted Life-Years From Major Risk Factors: A Meta-Epidemiological Analysis", JAMA Health Forum 2026;7(3):e260108 — and it is not a country-year analysis. Its unit is risk factor crossed with year, reported mostly as GLOBAL totals for 66 harmonised risk factors across eight GBD iterations (2010, 2013, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2019, 2021, 2023), with sex and World Bank region strata only for dietary risks and low physical activity. Its endpoint is absolute annual deaths and DALYs attributable to a risk factor; its estimand is descriptive dispersion across releases (range-to-mean ratio, coefficient of variation, share of point estimates outside the previous iteration's 95% uncertainty interval), reported as median R:M 0.8 for deaths and 0.7 for DALYs, same-year original-versus-revised median R:M 0.4, CV above 0.2 for 336 of 675 death estimates, and GBD 2021 points outside GBD 2019's interval for 70-96% of several dietary risks. It does NOT test whether a revision is predictable from the prior release's value, and it does NOT re-run any published analysis on a later vintage — its own limitation says the analyses "were limited to published GBD estimates rather than primary data or replication of underlying models". So it does not answer limb (a) on the candidate's unit (country-year coverage and mortality indicators), and it does not touch limbs (b) or (c) at all. The entry's earlier claim that Prior A asks and answers limb (a) "in the candidate's own field, in its own words", and that it falsifies the motivating gap as written, is struck. What survives is weaker and still relevant: release-to-release instability in modelled global-health estimates is a live published concern with headline numbers attached, so the gap is not virgin territory even though the candidate's quantity is unmeasured.
Ground (ii) is confirmed, and one leg of it is closer to the candidate's object than the record claimed. Wolff H, Chong H, Auffhammer M, "Classification, Detection and Consequences of Data Error: Evidence from the Human Development Index", Economic Journal 2011;121(553):843-870 (read in the NBER w16572 working-paper version): unit country(-year) HDI components and index; endpoint HDI value, rank and development category; comparator the originally published vintage against the revised one; estimand the size of the revision and its consequences, with "up to 34% of countries are misclassified" and prior-study coefficients shifting by up to 100%. Its components include life expectancy from the "Population Division of the UN Department of Economic and Social Affairs" — so not national accounts and education only, and the record's reading that the components exclude any UN-produced demographic series is wrong — with Table 6 giving country-level standard deviations of that component's revisions and the text reporting, verbatim, "In contrast, life expectancy is revised much less." It also re-runs a published analysis on a later vintage (Noorbakhsh 2006's convergence regression, Table 8), and reports that "key parameters... vary by up to 100%". Two limits on how far it reaches: it is not an efficiency or serial-correlation test, so limb (b) has no precedent even here, and it includes no WHO or UNICEF series, so the candidate's primary indicator is not in its corpus. Goes C, I4R Discussion Paper 23 (2023): 459 International Organization articles 2005-2020, 173 using cross-country macro data, three published studies re-run across WDI, PWT and Maddison vintages (de Soysa & Neumayer 2005; Vreeland 2008; Goldstein, Rivers & Tomz 2007); unit country-year or dyad-year, endpoint the key coefficient's sign and significance, estimand vintage sensitivity of a regression coefficient. So each of the candidate's three limbs is an executed design pointed at a different corpus, and one precedent has already pointed it at a UN-modelled health series.
The object itself remains unmeasured: four further searches here, on top of the record's twenty, found no revision, serial-correlation or efficiency analysis of WUENIC, UN IGME or MMEIG release vintages — only methods-description papers and agency documentation. That is why this entry's rejection is a rule application, not a demonstration that the question has been answered, and it is recorded as such below.
Caveats recorded: Prior A was read through the JAMA article page and the medRxiv preprint 10.1101/2025.11.14.25340145 via a page summariser, with the preprint's authorship confirmed only by initials and a repository URL; Wolff et al. was read in the working-paper version rather than the published Economic Journal text; and absence over four searches is weak evidence of absence.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3
Well-posedness 2/3: limbs (a) and (b) are operational, but limb (c) rests on P2 and P3, which the record cannot discharge, so part of the question could fail to be answerable rather than be answered. Significance 2/3: consequence acts in both directions and the fix is cheap, but Prior A has already delivered much of the available consequence for the field's biggest series.

Status reasoning (Gate 5): Rejected at Gate 2. Novelty is Low, and Low novelty is a rejection at the gate where it failed regardless of what Gate 4 returned. Two independent grounds were given and verification struck the first. Ground (i) as written — limb (a) is asked and answered in the candidate's own field, in its own words, by Prior A, seven months before intake, which also falsifies the motivating gap — is WITHDRAWN: Prior A's unit is risk-factor-year and mostly global rather than country-year, it runs no forecastability test, and it re-runs no published analysis, so it answers no limb of this candidate (see Verification above). The verdict therefore rests on ground (ii) alone: (ii) the surviving limbs are a disguised known under the ledger's rule — the vintage-sensitivity-of-published-results design has been executed three times (Prior B on PWT, Wolff et al. on HDI inputs including a UN-modelled health series, Goes on WDI/PWT/Maddison) and what the candidate changes is the series, i.e. a corpus swap on an asked question, which is Rejected even though the WUENIC/IGME/MMEIG variant is unmeasured. The Disguise sweep was run (9 queries, four new vocabularies), so Disguise is verified, not unverified, and the sweep strengthened rather than weakened the Low grade. Nothing here turns on the two unread sources (WUENIC notes PDF, IGME reports); their absences are not treated as checks that passed, and the adversary's carry-forward claim carries no weight in this verdict. Ground (ii) is confirmed and sharpened by verification: Wolff, Chong & Auffhammer 2011 runs the revision analysis on HDI components including UN Population Division life expectancy, with per-component revision standard deviations in Table 6 and one published regression re-run on a later vintage, and Goes 2023 re-ran three published studies across WDI, PWT and Maddison vintages — so each of the candidate's limbs is an executed design pointed at a new corpus, and one precedent has already pointed it at a UN-produced demographic series. Two things that sharpening does not buy: limb (b)'s efficiency test has no precedent even in Wolff et al., which reports revision variances rather than testing efficiency, and no WHO or UNICEF series is in its corpus. Twenty-four queries in total found nothing measuring vintage revisions for WUENIC, IGME or MMEIG. So this is the disguised-known rule applied to an object nobody has measured, not a finding that the question has been answered, and the entry is recorded that way deliberately.

Strongest remaining objection:
The objection to this rejection is that 20 queries in both fields' vocabularies found limbs (b) and (c) nowhere in global health, so the Low grade rests on template identity rather than object identity: nobody has measured country-year revision structure for coverage indicators, nobody has run an efficiency test on a modelled health estimate, and nobody has a vintage-reversal rate for a health series, while the record shows the answer would act in either direction. It fails anyway under the disguised-known rule — a known design pointed at a new corpus is not an un-asked question — but if that rule were ever relaxed for a demonstrated change of regime (rule-based or Bayesian-refit estimator versus reported counts or national accounts), this is the entry that would be re-judged first, and the P5 interface problem is the place that case would have to be made.

Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it):
Open the WUENIC 2025-revision notes PDF (publisher route, not PMC) to establish whether and how historical country-years move for the primary indicator, and in parallel check on one indicator whether two archived releases can be recovered and whether a non-trivial share of citing papers name a release — the feasibility facts that both P1/P5 and P2/P3 turn on.

Routing (if rejected as already-asked): None. Limb (a) is asked AND answered (Prior A), and the remaining limbs are a disguised known by corpus swap; answered and disguised-known rejections are not routed to the open-questions project. Nothing appended to ledger/routed-open-problems.md.
