ID: UQ-20261017-02
Date: 2026-10-17
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): Other STEM — metrology / measurement science (CIPM MRA key comparisons, degrees of equivalence, traceability-chain uncertainty). Neighbours engaged: proficiency testing / EQA (ISO 13528), collaborative-study statistics (ISO 5725), random-effects meta-analysis and variance components (method-owning field), gravimetry, radionuclide metrology, radiocarbon intercomparison, radiotherapy dosimetry audit.
Question (canonical): Over a pre-declared frame of CIPM and RMO key comparisons, computing per (institute, measurand, comparison, date) a leave-one-out standardised deviation against that comparison's own published reference-value recipe re-run with the assessed participant excluded, and coding documented method-generation changes as a covariate: (i) what share of standardised-deviation variance is attributable to a persistent institute effect, (ii) what is the lag-1 autocorrelation within (institute, measurand), (iii) what is the within-institute cross-measurand correlation of institute effects — each with an interval — and (iv) under a propagation rule stipulated in advance, what multiplicative inflation of a CMC-derived uncertainty follows if that persistent component were carried forward instead of each comparison outcome being treated as an independent draw? (This is R1, the single permitted Gate 1 reformulation, adopted; V0 is in the record.)
Alternative formulations: (1) Does an NMI carry a persistent institute-level offset that successive key comparisons keep re-measuring rather than removing? (2) Is the independence the per-comparison degrees-of-equivalence treatment assumes between one comparison and the next actually present in the published record? (3) Lay: if the same national lab comes out slightly high in one international comparison, does it come out high in the next — and is that extra uncertainty passed to anyone buying a calibration traceable to it?
Motivating gap: Presupposition inversion — that the MRA's per-comparison deliverable carries no participant-level bias term forward, so a user inheriting traceability through one institute's CMC inherits an uncertainty built as if each comparison outcome were an independent draw. Gate 2 already falsified the strong form (Cox & Shirono 2023 model a linking laboratory's common bias across two comparisons, correlation supplied as model input), leaving only the weak form: the persistence is nowhere estimated as a population quantity or propagated into delivered uncertainty. Gate 4 then falsified the inversion itself (see adversarial log, attack 4).
Presuppositions: P1 extractability of participant values, identities, dates and stated uncertainties across comparisons — UNVERIFIED by Gate 2 and by all three adversaries; no final report or linking report was ever opened. P2 enough recurrence per (institute, measurand) for autocorrelation — uncounted; adversary 3's own arithmetic from the stated ~10-year default validity gives chains of <=3 at CC level by 2026. P3 comparator circularity — handled by the mandatory leave-one-out re-running each comparison's own recipe. P4 institute identity across decades — CONTESTED and partly unidentifiable; adversary 3 sourced that the field's unit is the staff/equipment/method configuration, not the institute. P5 no existing participant-level persistence term — PARTLY FALSIFIED at Gate 2 (Cox & Shirono) and further at Gate 4 (CCQM IAWG Record of Participation pools an institute's standardised deviations across >=3 studies / >=10 points over 10 years). P6 propagation into delivered uncertainty — FALSIFIED as stated: CCRI/12-05 says the CMC's expanded uncertainty "should reflect that used in the comparison chosen", i.e. the inherited uncertainty is the NMI's own submitted claim, not a construct over a DoE sequence. Not presupposed: that persistence implies incompetence, or that it is positive (a null was admitted as a complete answer).
What would count as an answer: An extracted tuple set (institute, comparison, measurand, date, leave-one-out deviation, stated uncertainty) with achieved coverage of the declared frame reported, fitted with a variance-component model carrying a persistent institute effect, an institute-by-measurand effect, a method-generation covariate and comparison-level noise; deliverables are (i) the persistent variance share, (ii) lag-1 autocorrelation, (iii) cross-measurand correlation, each with an interval, and (iv) the implied inflation factor under the stipulated rule. A null was pre-declared as a complete answer, as was a documented coverage gap if the extractable subset proves too thin.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 11 Gate 2 searches + 5 fetches, then 27 adversary Disguise searches (9 + 9 + 9) + 12 fetches across three independent adversaries: 38 queries, 17 fetch attempts in total. Full lists in batches/2026-10-17-0059/UQ-20261017-02-record.md and the three adversary files. Biosci. 11:1390079 (opened in full: longitudinal in surveys, not in laboratories — negative for Disguise); (h) adversary 1 q7 `CIPM MRA-G-13 CMC review ... consistency` → MRA-G-13 v1.3 opened: inconsistency triggers reduced range, increased uncertainty, six-month corrective action or grey-out, and no persistence provision anywhere.

Novelty confidence: Medium
Significance — consequence: As posed: YES ⇒ either degrees of equivalence or CMC review acquires a persistence term, the participant-weighted KCRV estimators are implicated through correlated participant errors, and linking's case-by-case correlation input gains an empirical default; NO ⇒ the per-comparison treatment is vindicated with a number. Gate 4 reversed this map: the arrangement presupposes persistence-until-change, so a positive result would vindicate validity windows, supersession and linking's common-bias input, and a null would undermine them. The consequence that survives independent of limb (iv) is the KCRV-contamination limb, which adversary 3 correctly reclassified as a within-comparison cross-participant question, not this candidate's estimand.
Significance — audience: Real and documented from primary sources, not asserted: MRA-G-13 §9 puts monitoring the impact of comparison results on CMC claims on the RMOs and coordination of CMC review on the Consultative Committees, and obliges each RMO to track the continued validity of published CMCs; the CC analysis working groups (CCM, CCL, CCRI, CCQM) own the deliverable; the BIPM/JCGM-adjacent statistical community writes the methodology; downstream calibration laboratories and instrument users bear the consequence. Deflation recorded by two adversaries: their instrument is per-CMC threshold review, and the 2016 MRA Review Key point 8 places stability monitoring outside the remit of comparisons altogether.
Significance — fecundity: Method-generation-indexed rather than institute-indexed systematics as a catalogue; a numerical check of whether linking's assumed common bias matches an empirical estimate; KCRV contamination by shared persistent components; comparison designs that deliberately break the correlation; persistence as a leading indicator of later CMC revision.
Significance — anchoring: KCRV estimator choice and inconsistent comparison data; CIPM–RMO linking and its correlation assumptions; the GUM's treatment of systematic effects and correlated inputs; artefact drift versus comparison error; what a user at the bottom of an ISO 17511-style hierarchy inherits.
Reason for silence: Claimed primary mechanism was a normative/incentive gap — within the MRA a persistent deviation is a defect with a six-month clock, not a parameter to be estimated — with a unit-of-ownership mismatch and PDF data friction as reinforcement. FALSIFIED as the primary mechanism: IAWG-GD-01 requires exactly a per-institute cross-comparison record, and CCRI set its display window on an explicit cross-comparison stability judgement, so the stability question was asked at policy level and answered qualitatively. Adversary 1 and adversary 3 independently supplied the better mechanism, which is not the candidate's: in the GUM frame a stable deviation inside the stated uncertainty is unremarkable, stability monitoring is assigned outside comparisons (2016 MRA Review Key point 8), and supersession strips history from the equivalence record. Verification (post-batch, fresh-context checker, log UQ-20261017-02-verification.md): the kill survives, but not on the legs it was argued from, and one of its three cited documents carries none of the content attributed to it.
Checked leg by leg against the three documents adversary 3 opened. (a) Persistence-until-change: CONFIRMED in CCRI/12-05 only — "This presumes that there have been no significant changes in staff, equipment or measurement methods" — and a change triggers a new comparison. (b) Supersession: CONFIRMED in CCRI/12-05 only — an NMI "may have one result in each comparison, the most recent replacing any earlier participation". (c) Pooling of an institute's deviations across comparisons in CMC review: CCRI/12-05 **forbids** it — "If an NMI has more than one comparison supporting its capability, only one of these should be quoted", and "there is no averaging of results over several qualities" — so the adversary's attribution is wrong for that document. It is confirmed only in CCQM IAWG-GD-01, and there as a participation record rather than an aggregation of deviations: "the NMI/DI should participate in at least three studies" in ten years, at least ten points in the Record of Participation, 90% of points within -1 to +1. (d) Cross-measurand transfer: CONFIRMED in both, by fixed rule — named conversion cases and the Measurement Methods Matrix in CCRI/12-05, analyte-group and matrix-challenge cells of the Core Capability table in IAWG-GD-01. And the third document, the 2016 Recommendations from the Working Group on the CIPM MRA Review, addresses none of (a) to (d): the words supersede, replace, valid and validity do not occur in it, and its nearest content is a Key Point about "comprehensive in-house procedures for monitoring the stability of standards". Citing it for this kill was an error and it is struck.
The finding that matters is one neither the record nor the adversary stated. **No document gives any statistical model of persistence.** Nothing quantifies how well a result persists, how an older result loses weight, or how much uncertainty an extrapolation to another measurand adds; in CCRI/12-05 and IAWG-GD-01 validity and extrapolation are set by fixed time windows and fixed rules (ten years by default, fifteen or twenty for retention or removal from the KCDB). So the candidate's limbs (i) to (iii) — the variance share, the lag-1 autocorrelation and the cross-measurand correlation — are genuinely unmeasured, and the ledger records that rather than letting the rejection imply otherwise.
What the rejection now rests on is limb (iv), and on a sharper presupposition failure than the one argued. The limb asks what "the current per-comparison treatment of degrees of equivalence leaves out of the uncertainty a calibration user inherits" — and the documents show the degrees of equivalence do not feed that uncertainty at all. What a user inherits is the institute's own submitted CMC claim, validated against fixed participation rules. There is therefore no quantity being left out by a per-comparison treatment, because no per-comparison treatment produces the inherited uncertainty. Limb (iv) carries the entry's significance, so attack 4 stays fatal; but the entry's earlier ground, that the field "demonstrably does not hold" the independence presupposition and that the question is therefore already asked in policy, is narrowed to the part that verified, and the "asked and answered in policy" characterisation is struck — a presupposed persistence that nobody has measured is not an answered question.
Recorded for a successor candidate: a question asking only limbs (i) to (iii), without the inherited-uncertainty limb and re-pointed at the staff/equipment/method configuration rather than the institute, would face no prior and no false presupposition. That is a different candidate and is not graded here.
Caveat recorded: the documents were read through the page summariser rather than the raw PDFs; five strings were verbatim-checked on a second pass and the rest are first-pass summariser output.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3
Strongest remaining objection: The candidate's constitutive move is an inversion of a presupposition the field demonstrably does not hold. CCRI/12-05, IAWG-GD-01 and the 2016 CIPM MRA Review Recommendations — opened and quoted at Gate 4, after Gate 2 had graded novelty without opening any MRA or CC guidance — show the arrangement presupposes persistence of an NMI's demonstrated performance for about ten years conditional on no change in staff, equipment or methods, supersedes earlier results with the most recent, pools an institute's standardised deviations across comparisons in CMC review, and extends key-comparison evidence across measurands as policy. The comparator in limb (iv), "each comparison outcome treated as an independent draw", therefore names no actual treatment, and the uncertainty a user inherits is the institute's own submitted claim rather than anything built from a sequence of degrees of equivalence. Repairing this would reverse the question's outcome map and re-point it at the staff/equipment/method configuration rather than the institute — a second reformulation, hence a different candidate.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): Not applicable to this candidate; it is rejected on its presupposition rather than on feasibility. If the object is to be pursued at all, it would be as a new candidate posed as a test of the field's actual presupposition (persistence-until-change, CCRI/12-05), with the staff/equipment/method configuration as the unit and limb (iv) dropped. Pointer only; not taken here.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): Not routed. This is a Gate 4 presupposition-failure rejection, not an asked-but-open problem: Disguise was Partial, not Unresolved, in all three adversary logs, and no prior computes the candidate's estimands. Nor is it asked-but-open in the routable sense: verification established that the MRA documents PRESUPPOSE persistence without measuring it anywhere — no document models how well a result persists, how an older one loses weight, or what an extrapolation across measurands costs in uncertainty — and a quantity nobody has posed is not a routable open problem however unmeasured it is. Nearest in-field prior formulation to log for future Gate 2 runs, missed by this record: the CCQM IAWG Record of Participation (IAWG-GD-01).

ID: UQ-20261017-03
Date: 2026-10-17
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): Other STEM — mathematics (experimental mathematics, automated conjecture generation); method field: statistics (selective inference / FDR).
Question (canonical): For the enumerable corpus of machine-generated numerical conjectures that passed their generator's own numerical-agreement acceptance threshold, what is the realized rate of non-identities among those adjudicated so far, and does it agree with the rate implied by that threshold under an explicit null model of the generator's search volume?
Alternative formulations:
- (Gate 1 reformulation, one permitted, used) Restricted to engines publishing both a per-conjecture acceptance precision d and a recoverable search volume M, and adjudicating accepted conjectures into {proved new, proved but known, disproved, numerically unverifiable, open}: what censored interval covers the non-identity share, and how does it compare with M*10^-d, scoring rediscovery separately?
- What digit threshold would a conjecture engine need at its actual search volume to hold its false-discovery rate below a stated level?
Motivating gap: Intake held that conjecture engines accept on a digit threshold with no null over the search space, hence uncalibrated multiplicity. Gate 2 falsified the central clause in weak form: RM (arXiv:1907.00205) states "the probability of finding a random match for an enumeration space of 10^9 and result accuracy of more than 50 digits, is smaller than 10^-40" (search space carried in the bound); ESMA (arXiv:2212.09470) accepts at 1000 decimals with "the probability for a false positive ... roughly 10^-1000" (per-candidate only). Residue after Gate 2: the realized side has never been tallied; RM's 10-digit first-stage MITM-RF filter; verification-arithmetic failures; threshold-free LLM conjectures.
Presuppositions: (1) dated enumerable corpus with recorded per-conjecture thresholds — PARTLY FALSE (thresholds engine-level/staged only; no dated snapshot verified). (2) search volumes recorded per conjecture — FALSIFIED for RM and ESMA (and for Ramanujan Library, per adversary). (3) resolution status ascertainable — CONTESTED: no aggregate tally, and no disproved conjecture reported in any published corpus, so the numerator is plausibly empty. (4) a null over the search space is specifiable — PARTLY ESTABLISHED, which cuts against the candidate (Odrzywolek's 1/sigma rule). (5) "false discovery" definable — holds only with a pre-specified adjudication rule plus a "numerically unverifiable" class. (6) thresholds stated in papers/code — VERIFIED at engine level. (7) NOT presupposed that any engine claimed calibration — upheld; RM and ESMA both disclaim it ("does not substitute the need for formal proof").
What would count as an answer: per engine, recover d and M (M by instrumenting released code), build an empirical null by re-running against random matched-complexity targets, adjudicate output into the five classes, report the non-identity share as a censored interval, and state the minimum d holding FDR below a stated level at the measured M. "Thresholds are conservative" is a full answer — and for d >= 100 it follows from M*10^-d without steps (i)-(iii), which is the defect that sinks significance.
Novelty — queries run (query -> one-line result): 14 run against a stated cap of 11 (over-run recorded as a protocol breach, not hidden); full list in batches/2026-10-17-0059/UQ-20261017-03-record.md. Most informative: (2) "how many digits suffice for a numerical identity spurious coincidence" -> arXiv:1603.00299, Borwein Zoo 2307.05565, 2112.10873 (mandatory own-field-title query; it hit); (3) and (11) "Ramanujan Machine conjectures ... fraction proved / status proved disproved known" -> no published aggregate resolution tally anywhere (mandatory "what fraction of X" limb); (12) "probability a random formula matches a constant to d digits ... formula space size" -> 1603.00299 and 2002.12690, the two nearest priors; (14) "FDR control for discovered equations symbolic regression multiple testing" -> no FDR framework for formula discovery (method field; the negative holds there). Fetches 5/5: 2002.12690, 1603.00299, 1907.00205, 2212.09470 READ; arXiv:2608.11941 COULD NOT READ (arxiv.org/pdf returned no machine-readable text; no second route, fetch budget) — grounds nothing either way. Adversary #1 added 9 queries (9/9) and 4 fetches; see UQ-20261017-03-adversary-1.md.
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
P1. Odrzywolek, "Criteria for the numerical constant recognition", arXiv:2002.12690 — unit: one target constant z with error sigma plus its enumerated candidate formulas; endpoint: ranked candidate or failure; reference: statistical null for random formula values; estimand: relative likelihood plus the search-size rule "Tested unique formulas count must not exceed 1/sigma", beyond which "probability of random match approaches 1"; explicitly not an FDR.
P2. "Surprises in numerical expressions of physical constants", arXiv:1603.00299 — unit: generated expressions over a 10^5.1 space and the d-digit numbers they produce; endpoint: coverage of d-digit numbers; reference: a random d-digit number; estimand: a priori coincidence probability (~1.2% at 5 digits vs ~2.2% heuristic).
P3. Raayoni et al., Ramanujan Machine, arXiv:1907.00205, read with ESMA arXiv:2212.09470 — unit: one accepted conjecture; endpoint: probability this match is random; reference: random enumeration draw; estimand: per-candidate (RM: space-scaled) false-match probability justifying the threshold. Added by adversary #1: "The Ramanujan Library", arXiv:2412.12361 (ICLR 2025), READ — 118 relations, 43 known, 75 novel, 47 proved, none disproved; RoI>=2 cutoff "decided" from LLL run 100x on uniformly random digits, i.e. an empirical-null control; no M reported.
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs P1 — corpus unit and censored realized share rather than a per-candidate likelihood ranking; but P1 already answers the candidate's own alternative formulation in inverted form (M <= 1/sigma is d >= log10 M, the Bonferroni content), in the candidate's own field under the obvious title, leaving only an FDR-vs-per-comparison distinction with no consequence at the engines' real d. vs P2 — P2 is the nominal limb computed exactly, for a smaller space, over d-digit numbers rather than adjudicated conjectures; the candidate's second limb is P2's estimand transposed. vs P3 — P3 is the object of the question and supplies the nominal side; the candidate adds the realized side, censoring, the rediscovery/non-identity split and an empirical-null rerun, which is unperformed but degenerate at the thresholds in use, and the Library (2412.12361) has since run the empirical-null step for its own cutoff.
Novelty confidence: Low
Significance — consequence: Thin. At d = 100-2000 and any plausible M, M*10^-d is far below 1 (adversary arithmetic, labelled as its own and inheriting the sources' order-of-magnitude status: 10^9 x 10^-50 = 10^-41, matching RM's "<10^-40"; M = 10^20 at 100-1000 digits gives <= 10^-80), so "conservative" is near-certain a priori and obtainable in a paragraph. Non-degenerate residue — RM's 10-digit first stage, verification-arithmetic failures, threshold-free LLM conjectures — is not what the question names.
Significance — audience: Real (Technion RM group, the ICLR 2025 Library authors, graph-conjecture and OEIS-LLM pipelines, referees), but their stated false-positive worry is the precision artefact "cured by sufficient precision", not multiplicity; RM and ESMA already print a bound and disclaim calibration.
Significance — fecundity: Moderate, and displaced: the strongest questions it opens (a non-uniform null over structured near-identity families; whether verification arithmetic rather than coincidence is the real false-discovery channel; search volume as a reporting requirement) are explicitly not the question asked.
Significance — anchoring: Guy's strong law of small numbers (recalled, not opened — folklore only); Borwein "dubious identities" zoo, opened by adversary #1 (a 105-decimal-place near-identity; a further entry "false, although numerically almost satisfied"); integer-relation precision theory (PSLQ/LLL), confirmed to exist but not opened at Gate 2.
Reason for silence: Irrelevance of margin, not a disciplinary boundary: practitioners compute the per-candidate bound, see 10^-40 to 10^-1000, and have no reason to pose a corpus-level question; the Library even runs a random-input control. Credible as a mechanism, but it is a mechanism explaining why the answer is cheap, so it supports the Low grade rather than rescuing it.
Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status): one adversary ran (#1, fresh context, Gate 0-3 record only; 9/9 Disguise queries in 8 vocabularies Gate 2 did not use, so Disguise was executed, not unverified). Verbatim log: UQ-20261017-03-adversary-1.md.
| 1 Triviality | Both limbs answerable in a page: nominal = M*10^-d, which RM itself evaluates as a product; realized = zero disproved across RM, ESMA and the Library. | Only RM's 10-digit stage and the Library's RoI cutoff escape, and neither is the per-conjecture acceptance precision the reformulation restricts to. | Unresolved (fatal) |
| 2 Disguise | Known question renamed? | Not posed verbatim in HEP look-elsewhere, LLL/PSLQ, computer algebra, applied statistics, AI-for-math, French or historical vocabularies; but components are done under other names (P1's 1/sigma rule; the Library's random-input null). | Partial |
| 3 Combinatorial novelty | FDR x conjecture engines with no live interface at operating d; the field's real false positive is a precision artefact. | Interface live only at RM's 10-digit stage, survival rate undocumented — plausible, unevidenced. | Partial |
| 4 Presupposition failure | Presupposes a per-conjecture d with M*10^-d as the right null (false for the Library's empirical RoI cutoff, staged for RM), a recoverable M (falsified for all three engines), and an ascertainable non-identity class (zero disproved, so interval [0, ~3/n] contains any nominal value). | Rerun recovers M and an empty numerator is itself a finding — but a finding forced by the presuppositions is not a test of them. | Unresolved (fatal) |
| 5 Vagueness | With nominal <= 10^-80 and realized in [0, 3/n], "consistent/conservative" is forced; the record counts that as a full answer. | Informative only at the 10-digit stage, which is not the question. | Unresolved |

Verification (post-batch, fresh-context checker, log UQ-20261017-03-verification.md): the Gate 2 "asked and answered" ground is materially weaker than the entry claimed, and the rejection stands on the triviality ground instead.
Odrzywolek (arXiv:2002.12690) carries the quoted rule verbatim — "Tested unique formulas count must not exceed 1/sigma, where sigma is relative numerical error of the target constant" — but he explicitly declines to answer the probability question the candidate asks: "Above criterion do not provide any numerical estimate for probability of successful identification", offering only a relative likelihood ranking, and noting that the "equivalence problem is undecidable in general". So the threshold-versus-search-volume question is asked there and left unanswered in probability terms, not asked and answered. The Ramanujan Machine's 10^-40 is NOT an acceptance threshold: it is a random-match probability for one worked case at an enumeration space of 10^9 and accuracy above 50 digits, and the paper states no minimum digit count for acceptance. Its procedure is staged — a 10-digit first-stage search, then "Every result found by our MITM-RF algorithm is tested numerically to 100 digits", with tests "for up to 2000 digits of accuracy". The Ramanujan Library (arXiv:2412.12361) does calibrate against random inputs, as the entry said, but hedged and without a rate: the PSLQ cutoff "RoI of 2 seems to comfortably separate random results from false positives", with LLL run on inputs "each with d uniformly random binary digits" and a suggested minimum of 1.3. It reports no numeric false-positive rate and no falsified conjecture; all its outputs "are not theorems, but rather conjectures awaiting proofs".
The second ground is confirmed and is now the one the verdict rests on. The acceptance precisions in actual use — 100 digits as the standard validation, up to 2000 — put the nominal false-identity rate so far below any realized rate that could be observed in a corpus of this size that the comparison is decided by the setup. No published report of a disproved machine-generated conjecture was found. That negative is weak and is recorded as such: four searches, few sources opened, titles only for most hits, and the Nature 2021 version of the Ramanujan Machine paper could not be opened at all. It is enough for attack 1 (triviality), which does not need the negative to be exhaustive — it needs only that no engine reports a disproved conjecture, which is what the engines' own papers say.
So the entry's "asked and answered at per-candidate resolution" is corrected to "asked at per-candidate resolution and explicitly not answered in probability terms", and the Gate 2 Low grade is kept for the narrower reason that the candidate's own alternative formulation is Odrzywolek's rule in inverted form, in the candidate's field and words. Routing is unaffected and remains none: a question whose answer the ledger's own Gate 4 shows to be pre-decided is not an open problem, and Odrzywolek's decision not to give a probability is a declaration about his criteria, not a posed question.
Caveat recorded: every quote above was relayed by the page summariser and not checked against raw page text.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 1/3
Strongest remaining objection: The comparison is pre-decided. Three published engines (RM, ESMA, Ramanujan Library) report zero disproved accepted conjectures, and at the 100-1000-digit precisions actually used M*10^-d is below 10^-80 for any conceivable M, so "realized agrees with nominal" is forced by the setup rather than measured; the only regimes where it is not — RM's 10-digit first-stage filter and the Library's RoI cutoff — are not per-conjecture acceptance precisions, and the Library already calibrates its cutoff from random-input controls.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): Not this question. If anything here is worth posing, it is the displaced residue: instrument RM's released MITM-RF to record the first-stage (10-digit) candidate count and survival rate, where M*10^-d can exceed 1 — a different question needing its own Gate 0.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): Not routed. Rejected at Gate 2 as a disguised known on the consequential limb, and at Gate 4 on triviality — the threshold-versus-search-volume question is asked at per-candidate resolution, and explicitly NOT answered in probability terms (verification above) (Odrzywolek arXiv:2002.12690's "Tested unique formulas count must not exceed 1/sigma"; RM arXiv:1907.00205's space-scaled product bound; the Ramanujan Library arXiv:2412.12361's random-input cutoff calibration), so this is not an asked-but-open problem and gets no row in ledger/routed-open-problems.md. Gate 4 ran and independently returns Unresolved on attacks 1 and 4, which is fatal on its own; only one adversary was run, which is sufficient for a Rejection whose fatal grounds stand.

ID: UQ-20261017-04
Date: 2026-10-17
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): Other STEM — crystallography / structure-record validation; computational materials science (lattice dynamics at record scale)

Question (canonical): Over a pre-declared frame of fully ordered experimental inorganic structure entries carrying a reported measurement temperature, with a pre-specified effective-harmonic protocol (named universal MLIP, supercell rule, q-mesh, imaginary-mode threshold, finite-temperature treatment, artefact screen) applied to the deposited geometry WITHOUT relaxation: what are the sensitivity and specificity of the resulting dynamical-instability flag for entries the crystallographic community has independently adjudicated wrong (correction, retraction, redetermination at lower symmetry, or demonstration that the entry is an averaged model of a superstructure, each a distinct outcome class), against controls matched on era, method and chemistry and carrying at least one concordant independent redetermination at the same symmetry; what is the flag's own false-positive rate here, measured by DFT on a stratified subsample; and what incremental discrimination does it add over the alerts an existing automated validation report already issues on the same held-out cases? [Gate 1 reformulation, the version graded; the intake version left the specificity denominator undefined. Both in the record.]
Alternative formulations: (1) Would a lattice-dynamics check, now affordable across the whole experimental structure record, catch bad structures that geometry- and symmetry-based validation misses? (2) Is dynamical instability of a deposited structure a usable diagnostic of a wrong structure determination, and with what sensitivity and false-positive rate?
Motivating gap: Phonons across ~10^5 deposited entries became affordable only with universal MLIPs (arXiv:2407.09674: 86.2% dynamical-stability classification accuracy on a 384-structure held-out subset, but relaxed, unary/binary-weighted, no experimental/hypothetical split, no audit). Every pipeline relaxes first, so the as-deposited-at-reported-temperature frame — the only frame a validation report could see — has no standard workflow.
Presuppositions: P1 adjudicated-wrong set enumerable (CONTESTED, incomplete and prestige-biased; supported by adversary 2's IUCr me0406 / Retraction Watch trail). P2 universal-MLIP effective-harmonic phonons usable on unrelaxed deposited geometries (CONTESTED → CONTRADICTED at Gate 4). P3 artefacts separable from physics (CONTESTED; artefact class "inadequately relaxed structure" is produced by the frame itself). P4 a deposited model can be evaluated at its reported temperature without relaxation (CONTESTED → CONTRADICTED at Gate 4). P5 disorder entries sit in a positive-control stratum. Verification (post-batch, two fresh-context readers: a claim check, log UQ-20261017-04-verification-claim.md, and the eight-vocabulary Disguise sweep adversary 3 could not run, log UQ-20261017-04-verification-sweep.md): the kill is sourced in substance and overstated in form, the gate moves, and the unrun check now has an answer.
The claim check. Half one of the kill holds, with its wording corrected. Pallikara, Kayastha, Skelton & Whalley, "The physical significance of imaginary phonon modes in crystals", Electronic Structure 4, 033002 (2022), arXiv:2203.01244 — the entry's citation named the wrong fourth author and the wrong journal, and both are corrected here — states that "the forces are equal to zero, so that the linear term in u vanishes", that "the forces on the atoms in the initial structure are assumed to be zero", and that "a well-converged geometry optimisation is a prerequisite", adding that force-convergence criteria may need to be tighter than usual. What that supports is that the harmonic interpretation presupposes stationarity and that a converged optimisation is a prerequisite; it does not support the stronger "not well defined", which is struck. Half two holds for the two methods it was checked against, and only as published: TDEP (Hellman & Abrikosov, arXiv:1303.1145) starts from "Guess equilibrium positions, usually the ideal lattice positions" and "These forces are then used to move the atoms in a steepest descent scheme towards equilibrium positions", iterating to convergence; SSCHA (Errea, Calandra & Mauri, arXiv:1311.3083) has a trial Hamiltonian that "contains two group of parameters: the R_eq equilibrium positions and the Phi force-constants matrix" and "The minimization is performed with respect to all the free parameters". So both optimise the reference positions by construction. SCAILD could not be read, and code-level options for holding positions fixed were not checked, so the general claim that NO effective-harmonic method can flag a structure held at its deposited geometry is unsupported and is recorded as such.
What that does to the verdict. Attack 4 drops from Unresolved to Partial, because an impossibility the adversary could not source cannot carry a fatal status — and the adversary that argued it had zero web searches available. But the entry is not thereby promoted, because the same evidence lands on Gate 1 instead, and harder. The reformulation at Gate 1 was already spent, and what verification establishes is that the candidate's index test — an effective-harmonic instability flag, at the reported measurement temperature, on the unrelaxed deposited geometry — is satisfied by no method in the literature: the finite-temperature methods relax the reference positions, and a fixed-geometry Hessian is not the finite-temperature quantity the question names. The question therefore does not pick out one answerable quantity, which is a Gate 1 failure rather than a false presupposition, and the gate recorded for this rejection moves accordingly.
The sweep. Adversary 3's eight Disguise queries were all refused by an exhausted shared budget, so its Disguise status was Unverified, not Unresolved, and grounded nothing. Run here in seven of the eight planned vocabularies (the seventh search exhausted the cap; German-language and generative-model vocabularies were not run), it found NO source that uses a dynamical-stability calculation as a screen over a structure database to flag deposited experimental structures as probably wrong, and none comparing such a flag against checkCIF or PLATON alerts. The closest items, and what they actually do: Mg(BH4)2 (arXiv:1211.6948) is the single-compound version of the idea — "our phonon calculations showed the P42nm structure (delta phase) to be dynamically unstable at ambient pressure", with the authors allowing that "either density functional theory calculations are inaccurate for this system, or experimental structure determination was incorrect" — one compound, not a screen; "Forty years of Marshing" (Acta Cryst. A 2018) audits CSD entries for missed symmetry with PLATON ADDSYM, so database-wide error audits exist but use symmetry tools, not dynamics. Two large-scale phonon studies cut against the index test rather than against novelty: arXiv:2602.07295 reports that "spurious imaginary modes are ubiquitous in MOFs, arising from numerical artifacts such as insufficient structural relaxation", and arXiv:2605.27162 finds "79 compounds (20 % of the total) exhibit imaginary phonon modes" and reads them as possibly "an artifact of the computational setup rather than an indication of true physical dynamic instability". So the question is un-asked, and the reason it is hard is the artefact floor rather than prior art — which is the opposite of what a Gate 2 kill would have said, and is why the rejection is recorded at Gate 1.
Caveats recorded: the sweep ran seven of eight vocabularies, judged several hits from titles only, and could not open one MOF imaginary-mode diagnostic PDF; absence on that basis is weak. SCAILD and the published-workflow question (do any workflows compute force constants at an unrelaxed experimental geometry, and what do they say about the residual forces?) are both unread and are recorded as open.

Scores: Well-posedness 1/3 · Significance 2/3 · Gate of rejection, after verification: Gate 1
[Well-posedness falls from the record's self-assessed 3/3: the reformulation pinned the specificity denominator but left the index test unspecifiable — no protocol satisfies "effective-harmonic at the reported measurement temperature" and "without relaxation" together, so the question does not pick out one answerable quantity. Significance 2/3 stands: consequence and audience are real, the headline actor is mismatched to the frame and the likely answer is the modest one.]
Strongest remaining objection: the frame that carries the entire novelty claim — "the unrelaxed deposited model, effective-harmonic, at its own reported temperature" — cannot be instantiated. Harmonic phonons require a stationary point, and the finite-temperature effective-harmonic machinery that would otherwise rescue specificity relaxes the reference positions to the potential's own equilibrium by construction; so every consistent protocol either relaxes (and is a different, already-ancestored question) or computes a temperature-independent Hessian at a non-stationary point that is artefact class (I) by construction and mostly measures distance from the MLIP minimum — prior A's signal under a new name.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): return to Gate 1 and replace "WITHOUT relaxation" with symmetry-constrained relaxation of internal coordinates at the fixed deposited cell, reporting the deposited-vs-relaxed displacement alongside the flag and adding residual force/stress magnitude and the relaxed-geometry flag as comparators; then re-run Gate 2 (the Disguise sweep adversary 3 could not execute, the lattice-dynamics case-study and polymorphous-network literatures, and the ICSD-derived phonon databases for the base rate), read PRIS (arXiv:2609.01209) in full by a non-arXiv-PDF route, and verify P6 against the full PLATON test list rather than the IUCr category page.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): Not applicable — rejected at Gate 1 on well-posedness, the index test being unspecifiable with any published method, and not as already-asked. Verification moved the gate: attack 4 falls to Partial because the impossibility it asserted could not be sourced beyond TDEP and SSCHA, and the Disguise sweep adversary 3 never ran was run afterwards and found no prior at all. Not an open problem in the ledger's sense, so nothing is routed to ledger/routed-open-problems.md. Note for the record: PRIS (arXiv:2609.01209) and MOFClassifier (arXiv:2506.14845) show the adjacent non-dynamical version of this question is active and being answered, so a relaxed-frame successor candidate would face a genuinely occupied neighbourhood at Gate 2.

ID: UQ-20261017-05
Date: 2026-10-17
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): Other STEM — measurement practice and metrology of fundamental quantities (particle/nuclear physics). Adjacent: metrology (Birge ratio), clinical meta-epidemiology (method-owning field for the contrast).
Question (canonical): Over a declared frame of published measurements of quantities with >=K independent same-quantity determinations and a pre-declared non-circular reference value, each hand-coded for blinding status (hidden signal region / hidden offset or scale factor / salted data / none / non-ascertainable), what is the ratio between blinded and unblinded strata of the uncertainty-calibration factor c that makes per-measurement pulls (x_i - x_ref)/u_i unit-variance, with quantity fixed effects and era and precision controls and a per-stratum tail index; or is the design non-identifiable in this frame? (Gate 1 reformulation, the one permitted, is the operative version; Gate 0 intake version in the record.)
Alternative formulations:
- Does blinding change how well physicists' error bars predict their own later disagreement, as distinct from changing their central values?
- Are blinded analyses' uncertainty budgets systematically more or less realistic than unblinded ones, and by how much?
Motivating gap: The blinding-in-physics literature is dense with HOW and empty of measurement. Klein & Roodman 2005 (opened) is a techniques review whose only meta-measurement is a central-value herding test and whose verdict is "we cannot say conclusively whether bias has influenced measurements in nuclear and particle physics"; Golub arXiv:2311.13542 (opened) argues from anecdote that blinding "can severely inhibit the search for systematic errors". The record therefore conceded the central-value limb as asked-and-open and claimed only the uncertainty limb as unasked.
Presuppositions: (1) blinding status ascertainable and gradable from publications — CONTESTED, leading feasibility risk; (2) enough dated same-quantity repeats — ESTABLISHED (Review of Particle Physics subset: 8,469 measurements of 864 quantities, Bailey 2017); (3) a non-circular reference exists — CONTESTED, such quantities excluded; (4) blinding not perfectly confounded with era and collaboration size — CONTESTED and central; (5) quoted sigmas are comparable ~1-sigma objects — approximately established by convention; (6) the central-value-bias question is already asked and is EXCLUDED here, and that exclusion is what keeps the candidate from being a known open problem renamed — asserted ESTABLISHED, and FOUND FALSE at Gate 4 (see adversarial log row 4); (7) added at Gate 1, reference-availability asymmetry: blinded measurements are the most recent and so least likely to have a decisive later value — CONTESTED, pre-handled; (8) NOT presupposed: that blinding has any effect, or its direction.
What would count as an answer: a declared frame of measurement histories; blinding coded under a pre-specified scheme with the non-ascertainable stratum reported; pulls against the pre-chosen reference, with Bailey-style reference-free pairwise z as sensitivity; c and a tail index per stratum with quantity fixed effects and era and precision controls. Output: a ratio of calibration factors with an interval and a sign, or a demonstration of non-identifiability.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): Gate 2, 11 distinct web searches and 5 fetches, all used, none refused — full list in batches/2026-10-17-0059/UQ-20261017-05-record.md. Significance — consequence: If answered with a sign, it would price blinding's cost in lost precision or give blinding a second justification independent of the unresolved central-value limb; a null would retire the error-budget half of the standing cost argument; non-identifiability would itself constrain what the historical record can settle. Significance — audience: (i) collaborations and internal review bodies choosing blinding depth, currently deciding on a techniques review and anecdote — real, and all three adversaries granted it; (ii) the PDG, claimed because it publishes per-quantity scale factors — judged inflated by two adversaries, since the scale factor is computed from each quantity's own observed scatter and so already absorbs whatever blinding does, and no source was found contemplating protocol-dependent inflation; (iii) metrology, where the statistic is already named (Birge ratio, "dark uncertainty") and blinded inter-laboratory evaluation is an unpriced option.
Significance — fecundity: whether any effect lives in the statistical or systematic component (the split is published); whether calibration scales with blinding depth as a dose; whether blinding predicts the magnitude of a measurement's own later revision; whether the tail index rather than the core width moves; and whether blinding protocol should be recorded as structured metadata in compilations.
Significance — anchoring: Bailey's unexplained almost-Cauchy tails; the PDG scale-factor practice and the live proposal to replace it (arXiv:2004.01219); the neutron-lifetime beam-bottle discrepancy; Klein & Roodman's unresolved herding chi2; Golub's claim that "there is surprisingly little evidence for experimenter bias in physics research".
Reason for silence: The record's primary mechanism — physics treats uncertainty understatement as a nuisance to be corrected, never an outcome to be explained, so no exposure variable is ever sought — was contradicted by all three adversaries from opened sources: Henrion & Fischhoff sought the exposure in a physics journal in 1986 and named the stratified analysis as the next step, and Croft & Dailey stratified calibration by method and era and recommended blinding in 2011. The surviving mechanism is the record's second: the exposure exists in no machine-readable compilation, hand-coding it from hundreds of primary papers with inconsistent pre-2000 reporting has no owner, and blinded measurements are too recent to have decisive later references. That explains why nobody ANSWERED; it does not explain why nobody ASKED, and the Gate 4 finding is that somebody did. The secondary taboo sub-claim is struck: Golub shows that criticising blinding in print is unpunished.
Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status): Three independent fresh-context adversaries ran; logs verbatim in UQ-20261017-05-adversary-1.md, -2.md, -3.md. Statuses below are the worst returned by any adversary, with the adversary noted.
1 | Triviality | Marginal calibration is published (Birge ratios 1.2-3; Bailey nu ~ 2-3; Croft & Dailey factor ~2 pre-2000), and the non-identifiability limb is derivable in a page from the bias-variance identity plus Henrion & Fischhoff's prediction and Klein & Roodman's reference-sensitivity | The stratified number is in no opened source and the two signed mechanisms point opposite ways, so the contrast cannot be looked up; but the disjunction's second limb is foreseeable from existing knowledge | Partial (adv 3; Resolved for adv 1 and 2)
2 | Disguise | Henrion & Fischhoff 1986, in a physics journal, already pose it: exposure = a preexisting recommended value (i.e. unblinded, by definition of blinding), endpoint = Birge ratio and surprise index of normalized residuals against a later recommended value, era control present, direction predicted ("unduly tight confidence intervals"), remedy proposed = scrutiny "blind," before knowing the outcome, and the stratified follow-up named. Only the blinding-coded contrast is missing, because formal blinding post-dates the paper | "No one framed it as a stratified contrast with coded blinding status" — i.e. the candidate supplies a method for an asked question, which is what the ledger defines as a disguised known | **Unresolved** (adv 3, on a primary source opened twice and quoted; adv 1 and 2 ran 9/9 new-vocabulary queries each, found no prior formulation, and graded the same paper Resolved on the opposite reading of the same lines)
3 | Combinatorial novelty | Just clinical meta-epidemiology's within-stratum contrast x physics measurement histories | Real problems at the interface: the reference-availability asymmetry has no clinical analogue, the era main effect is of the same order as any plausible blinding effect, and the estimator choice is itself a research problem | Resolved (all three)
4 | Presupposition failure | Presupposition 6 is not a property the estimand has. For pulls p = (x - x_ref)/u, E[p^2] = (bias/u)^2 + Var(x)/u^2, so any herding displacement enters c; Klein & Roodman's own verified chi2 values put that term at the same order as any plausible blinding effect (c moves 1.26 → 1.75 on the choice of reference alone — adversary's labelled arithmetic from 131.2/83 and 249.7/82), and Henrion & Fischhoff predicted in 1986 that expectation exposure yields deceptively small Birge ratios. Under a shrinkage model of herding the artifact has the SAME SIGN as the hypothesis, so the likely output is a confidently wrong answer, not the clean non-identifiability the question offers itself. Quantity and era fixed effects remove first-moment displacement within a cell, not second-moment shrinkage. The record's non-identifiability clause covers era and collaboration confounding only; this conflation is nowhere flagged | Redefining c as realized-over-quoted error (the PDG scale factor) withdraws presupposition 6 and turns the candidate into a blinding-stratified herding test, i.e. the asked question; a joint two-reference design would be a second reformulation and the one permitted at Gate 1 is spent. Circular with respect to the novelty claim either way | **Unresolved** (adv 3; adv 1 Partial and adv 2 Resolved on different objections — codability, era confounding, commensurability — neither of which reaches this one)
5 | Vagueness | K, "decisive later value", the non-identifiability criterion and the estimator for c are all unspecified, and c is outlier-dominated in exactly this corpus family (27 of 163 H0 points beyond 2.8 sigma; Croft & Dailey's chi2 per point 22.7 → 0.26 on one outlier) | These are frame-declaration parameters a pre-registration fixes, and the per-stratum tail index is the robust limb; plausible but unevidenced | Partial (adv 1, 2, 3)
6 | Significance inflation | The PDG limb is close to circular — the scale factor already absorbs whatever blinding does — and the record misreports Golub, who claims blinding inhibits the systematics search, not that it inflates quoted uncertainties, and uses at least six examples rather than three | Audience (i) and (iii) are real and documented independently; the PDG limb is overstated. Significance survives at 2/3 | Partial (all three)
7 | Reason for silence | Mechanism (1) is refuted from opened sources (Henrion & Fischhoff 1986 sought the exposure and named the follow-up; Croft & Dailey 2011 stratified and recommended blinding), and mechanism (2) explains why nobody answered, not why nobody asked — and somebody asked, so under the Gate 4 rule the novelty finding is suspect and the candidate returns to Gate 2 | Nobody framed it as a stratified contrast with coded blinding status | **Unresolved** (adv 3; Partial for adv 1, Resolved for adv 2, both of which kept mechanism (2) as sufficient)
8 | Dissolution | Expectation bias is one process — a stopping rule on the systematics search — that sets the central value and the quoted budget together, so the "uncertainty limb vs central-value limb" split is a false dichotomy and the question dissolves into the asked one; separately, "blinding" is a bundle with modern large-collaboration practice | A PDG-style realized-over-quoted ratio per stratum remains definable if impure; within-quantity fixed effects and blinding depth as a dose give some leverage against the bundle. Adversary 2 tested the heavy-tail version of this attack, found it inverted on scope-checking (its one opened tail fit is exponential, all moments finite) and declined to press it | Partial (adv 1, 3; Resolved for adv 2 after its own kill failed verification)
Verification (post-batch, fresh-context checker, log UQ-20261017-05-verification.md): the Disguise kill is CONFIRMED on the point that decides the verdict, the second kill's attribution is wrong while its substance survives as the ledger's own algebra, and the routed row is corrected on two counts.
Henrion & Fischhoff 1986 (Am. J. Phys. 54(9):791-798) poses the candidate's uncertainty limb, verbatim: "Having a preexisting recommended value may particularly encourage investigators to discard or adjust unexpected results, and so induce correlated errors in apparently independent experiments", and "The result would be initially small Birge ratios, unduly tight confidence intervals, and the exclusion of discrepant data." And it does not answer it: the mechanism is hypothesised and illustrated qualitatively (the speed-of-light bandwagon, Millikan's notebooks), with no exposed-versus-unexposed or blinded-versus-unblinded arm anywhere. What it measures is pooled calibration — Birge ratio, interquartile index and surprise index over the speed of light (27 values, 1875-1958), G (14 values), the proton magnetic moment, the inverse fine-structure constant, the ohm ratio and 306 Particle Data Group lifetimes and meson masses — concluding "Reported uncertainties are too small." So the candidate's question was asked in a physics journal in 1986 and is still unanswered, which is what makes this an already-asked rejection and what makes the row routable.
One correction to the kill, in the candidate's favour and recorded because it matters for the row rather than for the verdict: the remedy Henrion & Fischhoff propose is NOT analysis blinding. It is referee-blind review — "referees might be asked to scrutinize the account of an experiment 'blind,' before knowing its outcome and whether it affirmed prior expectations." Blinding the analyst to the recommended value is the candidate's operationalisation, not theirs, and the entry's earlier phrasing that they proposed the candidate's remedy is struck.
The second kill's attribution is wrong. Klein & Roodman (2005) report no comparison of uncertainty calibration between blinded and unblinded analyses, and no statement that a central-value bias contributes to the variance of normalised residuals — the terms "pull" and "normalized residual" do not appear in what could be read. What is there is a chi-square check on four historical unblinded series: "the measurements do tend to cluster nearer the prior published averages than the final value", with "the chi2 for the hypothesis that the measurements are normally distributed around the prior averages is 131.2 for 83 degrees of freedom, whereas the chi2 for the hypothesis that they are normally distributed about the final average is 249.7". The substance of the attack survives on those two printed numbers, but as this ledger's own arithmetic and algebra rather than as a cited result: E[p^2] carries the squared bias, so a calibration factor estimated on normalised residuals cannot exclude the central-value limb, and the factor implied by the two printed chi-squares moves from sqrt(131.2/83) = 1.26 to sqrt(249.7/83) = 1.73 on the choice of reference alone. The entry's figure of 1.75 is corrected to 1.73, and the claim is relabelled as the ledger's derivation. Presupposition 6 is still false, so attack 4 stands — on arithmetic the ledger owns rather than on a sentence misattributed to Klein & Roodman.
Routing, corrected and narrowed to one row. The uncertainty limb is routed, with Henrion & Fischhoff's verified posing sentence as the ground and their referee-blind remedy stated as what they actually proposed. The second row the entry proposed — the central-value limb, does blinding de-bias the mean — is NOT added: the two sentences it would rest on ("the size of an experimenter's bias cannot be estimated"; "there is surprisingly little evidence for experimenter bias in physics research") were not among the strings this pass verified, and the ledger's rule is that a row's posing sentence is quoted verbatim from the paper rather than from an adversary's summary. It is recorded here as a candidate row awaiting that check, not appended.
Caveats recorded: Henrion & Fischhoff and Klein & Roodman were both read through the Gwern mirror because the publisher routes were paywalled or rate-limited (Annual Reviews returned HTTP 429), and the Klein & Roodman absences are the page summariser's report rather than a full-text search.

Scores: Well-posedness 3/3 · Significance 2/3
(Well-posedness and significance both survived; neither was the binding gate. The verdict rests on novelty and on presupposition 6.)
Strongest remaining objection: Henrion & Fischhoff 1986 — opened in full and quoted by two independent adversaries, and recorded as COULD NOT READ by the Gate 2 sweep that graded novelty — already poses the uncertainty limb in a physics journal: a preexisting recommended value is predicted to produce correlated errors, small Birge ratios and "unduly tight confidence intervals", with referee-blind scrutiny of an experiment's account proposed as the remedy, which is not the analysis blinding this candidate means and the across-classes stratified analysis named as the next step. The candidate is that asked-and-unanswered question with blinding substituted as the operational exposure, which the ledger's definitions make an already-asked question however unmeasured the exact variant — asked and still unanswered, which is the routable kind of rejection rather than the disguised-known kind the exact variant; and the second kill is independent of how that reading is graded, because the candidate's own estimand cannot exclude the central-value limb it declares excluded (E[p^2] carries the squared bias; Klein & Roodman's verified chi2 values move c from 1.26 to 1.73, this ledger's own arithmetic on the two printed chi-squares rather than a statement of theirs on the choice of reference alone), so presupposition 6 — the presupposition the record says is "what keeps this from being a known open problem in new clothes" — is false.
Note on unrun checks (recorded, grounds nothing): adversary 3 ran 7 of its 8 required Disguise queries; the 8th was refused by the shared search budget, and arXiv listing fallbacks returned ROBOTS_DISALLOWED and PROXY_REJECTED. Its Disguise sweep is therefore short by one query. That shortfall would on its own have made Disguise unverified and barred Validated without producing a rejection; it does not bear on this verdict, because adversary 3's Unresolved rests on a primary source it opened and quoted, and because adversaries 1 and 2 each completed a full 9-query new-vocabulary sweep. Still unread by any agent: Accred. Qual. Assur. doi 10.1007/s00769-016-1191-2 and the IMEKO WC-2015 proficiency-testing items (the one place a blind-vs-open uncertainty contrast could still hide) and Junk & Lyons arXiv:2009.06864; none of these is load-bearing for the rejection.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): not applicable — the question is rejected. For the routed problem below, the pointer is the joint two-reference design on existing public compilations: chi2 against the contemporaneous published average and against the final value, per quantity, as Klein & Roodman did for four quantities, so that herding and calibration are estimated together rather than one excluded by assertion.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): YES — the uncertainty limb is asked-and-unanswered and gets a row in ledger/routed-open-problems.md: does exposure to the expected value degrade the calibration of quoted uncertainties in physics measurement series? Posed by Henrion & Fischhoff 1986 (hypothesis, predicted signature, "blind" remedy, stratified follow-up named), restated as a demand for evidence by Klein & Roodman 2005 and Golub arXiv:2311.13542, and unanswered. Separately, the CENTRAL-VALUE limb — does blinding de-bias the mean of physics measurements? — is asked-and-unanswered on the same two opened sources and should be routed as its own row independently of this entry.

ID: UQ-20261017-06
Date: 2026-10-17
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): AI architecture — sparse mixture-of-experts LM design and pretraining dynamics. Neighbours searched: permutation symmetry / linear mode connectivity and model merging; clustering stability and cluster validity (statistics); label switching and latent-class identifiability (finite mixtures); interpretability universality / convergent learning; vision-MoE representational analysis; expert offloading and serving.

Question (canonical): Train k >= 3 sparse-MoE language models under one recipe differing only in seed (router/expert init and data order), at a scale at which OLMoE's router-saturation curve reproduces; with a pre-declared probe corpus, layer set, top-k and expert matching rule M (Hungarian matching on per-expert activation profiles), measure with CIs (i) A_cross, cross-run agreement of the token-to-expert partition after M (ARI/NMI) at the 1%-of-pretraining checkpoint and at the end; (ii) S, the same agreement within a run between its 1% and final checkpoints (OLMoE's ~60% top-8 saturation); (iii) A_0, nulls from expert label permutation and from matching one run to an unrelated run; and (iv) the share of between-seed variance in terminal held-out loss and downstream scores predictable from 1%-checkpoint routing statistics — reporting A_cross - A_0 and A_cross/S per layer and the sensitivity of all four to the load-balancing auxiliary-loss weight.
(Gate 1 version A, as intaken, recorded not graded: is the token-to-expert partition that saturates in the first ~1% of MoE pretraining canonical — reproduced up to expert relabelling by independent runs of one recipe — or an arbitrary early lottery, and does it predict the run's terminal quality? One reformulation used; Gate 1 budget spent.)

Alternative formulations: (1) Do two MoE runs of one recipe differing only in seed converge, after optimal expert matching, on the same expert specialization, or does each freeze a different arbitrary partition in its first ~20B tokens? (2) How much of the run-to-run variance in a sparse MoE's final quality is already determined by routing fixed in the first 1% of pretraining? (3) Is the router's induced clustering of tokens over experts stable across resamplings of training stochasticity, or a stability-zero partition that only looks structured because it is frozen early?

Motivating gap: Anomaly mining on a quantified, never-cross-checked observation. OLMoE §5.1 (arxiv.org/html/2409.02060v2, read): after 1% of pretraining (5000 steps / 20B tokens) "up to ~60% of routing to the top-8 activated experts has already saturated", rising to ~80% at 40%, against a 8/64 = 12.5% random baseline — but measured WITHIN one run, against its own final checkpoint, with no cross-seed comparison. FLAME-MoE (arXiv:2505.20225, opened) independently reports that "routing behavior stabilizes early in training", likewise within-run and with no seed replicates. So the field holds two reports that MoE routing is effectively decided in the first 1% of training and, on everything opened at Gate 2, no measurement of whether what is decided is the same thing twice. Gate 4 complicated this: OpenMoE (arXiv:2402.01739, title/phrase level only) named "early routing learning" and a token-ID mechanism before OLMoE, so the anchor was interrogated — just not across seeds; and Equifinality (arXiv:2604.14419, abstract + §1-4.3 read) states in its introduction "Cross-seed analysis reveals 500x-above-random functional overlap through entirely different weight parameterizations", method unread. Full record: batches/2026-10-17-0310/UQ-20261017-06-record.md.

Presuppositions: P1 OLMoE-style saturation generalizes beyond OLMoE-1B-7B — partly corroborated (FLAME-MoE, opened); unquantified elsewhere; adversary 1 adds that "Why Routers Freeze" (ICML 2026 HiLD, opened) attributes freezing to Standard-Parameterisation logit divergence and finds muP-MoE soft routing does not specialise at all, so saturation may be parameterisation-specific (fix: add SP vs muP to the sweep). P2 experts in independent runs are identifiably matchable — contested; machinery exists (arXiv:2509.11348), carried by the declared M plus permutation null, not assumed. P3 the partition is a comparable object once tokenizer/top-k/context/probe corpus are fixed — established by construction. P4 independent MoE runs differ measurably in terminal quality — Gate 2 found no published number in one query, adversary 2 confirmed the negative in a second vocabulary, and adversary 3 found the number inside Equifinality (3 seeds, 76-84M: "0.12 PPL avg std", all 15 runs in a 0.79 PPL band), which supports P4's denominator being small. P5 saturation is not merely the aux-loss pinning routing early — contested, negation is a declared outcome of the sweep. P6 k >= 3 runs affordable where the saturation curve reproduces — contested; adversaries 1 and 3 show limb (iv) needs k in the tens, which collides with this. P7 S is the right upper reference — declared descriptive only. P8 (adversary 3, added) between-seed routing differences drive between-seed quality differences — predicted largely absent by Equifinality's hash/random-fixed routing costing only 1.1-2.2 PPL (single-seed).

What would count as an answer: k >= 3 (for limb (iv), tens of) runs identical but for seed, at a scale where the saturation curve has first been verified to reproduce; pre-registered matching rule M, pre-registered reduction of the top-k multi-assignment to a comparable object (top-1 or per-token set overlap — ARI/NMI are undefined on top-8 sets as written), and the two nulls; then A_cross vs A_0 and vs S with CIs, per layer and conditioned on routing mass; the between-seed variance share from 1%-checkpoint routing statistics; and sensitivity to aux-loss weight (and parameterisation). Three reportable outcomes: canonical (A_cross near S, far above A_0), arbitrary (A_cross indistinguishable from A_0), or a measured core with an arbitrary remainder localized by layer and token frequency. Secondary pre-registered endpoint: agreement of the DOMAIN-level routing signature as distinct from the token-level partition.

Novelty — queries run (query -> one-line result): 11 Gate 2 web queries + 2 free GitHub probes (full list and results: batches/2026-10-17-0310/UQ-20261017-06-record.md), plus 27 adversary queries in new vocabularies (9 each; batches/2026-10-17-0310/UQ-20261017-06-adversary-1.md, -2.md, -3.md). Most informative: Q1 own-field own-words title form "do independently trained mixture-of-experts models learn the same expert specialization across random seeds" -> no language-MoE cross-seed partition study; nearest is vision (Prior 2). Q9 the "stability" vocabulary -> StableMoE uses "stability" for within-run router freezing; surfaced Prior 3. Q11 mandatory already-published-quantity query for the variance limb -> no MoE between-seed terminal-loss SD published (dense/fine-tuning variance literature only). Adversary 3 D5 (underspecification/Rashomon vocabulary) -> DECISIVE: Equifinality, arXiv:2604.14419, whose introduction claims a cross-seed 500x-above-random functional-overlap result. Adversary 2 Q7 (neuroscience convergent-learning vocabulary) -> Gurnee et al. "Universal Neurons in GPT2" (arXiv:2401.12181, opened): five same-data GPT-2 seeds, activation-correlation matching, rotation null, "1-5% of neurons are universal" — the dense analogue of the template, run in 2024. Adversary 3 D4 -> OpenMoE's "early routing learning"/"context-independent specialization". Adversary 1 D7 -> "Why Routers Freeze" (ICML 2026 HiLD, opened): under Top-K "finite-width fluctuations determine the selected experts, making Top-K an implicit symmetry-breaking mechanism".

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
Prior 1 — "Equifinality in Mixture of Experts: Routing Topology Does Not Determine Language Modeling Quality", arXiv:2604.14419 (Ternovtsii & Bilak, 15 Apr 2026). OPENED (abs + html §1-4.3). UNIT: 76-84M-param cosine-routing MoE LMs (learned centroids, 1024 rank-1 singleton experts, 3 hops, top-k 4), 62 experiments, 15 runs across 3 seeds (42/137/7), WikiText-103 + OpenWebText. ENDPOINT: perplexity equivalence across routing variants; plus, in one unread introduction-level claim, cross-seed "functional overlap". COMPARATOR: random baseline (for the overlap claim), seed noise 0.12 PPL avg std. ESTIMAND: whether routing topology determines LM quality (answer: no). COULD NOT READ: §5 "Why Routing Topology Converges", §8.4, App. B.3 "Seed Variance", and companion arXiv:2604.14434 (abstract via third-party mirror only) — so what was overlapped, by what matching, against what null, is unverified.
Prior 2 — "Beyond Routing: Characterising Expert Tuning and Representation in Vision Mixture-of-Experts", arXiv:2605.20610 (Tangtartharakul & Storrs, 2026). OPENED. UNIT: (model, expert) pairs over 10 seeds, E in {4,8,16}, vision MoE, final checkpoints. ENDPOINT: cluster structure of a second-order RSA matrix over 1,854 THINGS images; abstract asserts an animate/inanimate distinction "dominates expert partitioning and holds across independently trained models". COMPARATOR: silhouette score; no permutation null. ESTIMAND: recurrence of representational motifs across seeds (experts pooled, no one-to-one matching).
Prior 3 — "The Illusion of Specialization", arXiv:2601.03425v1 (Wang et al., 6 Jan 2026). OPENED. UNIT: expert committees per layer per domain in three published MoEs (OLMoE-1B-7B, Qwen3-30B-A3B, DeepSeek-V2-Lite), inference-only. ENDPOINT: cross-domain top-k Jaccard (mean 0.8735/0.8670/0.8670) and ECI Gini (0.8957/0.9207/0.9465). COMPARATOR: uniform-utilisation baseline. ESTIMAND: how far a domain-invariant expert subset captures routing mass. No seeds, no training dynamics.
Also load-bearing: Prior 0 (anchor) OLMoE §5.1 — within-run temporal self-agreement, 12.5% random null. Prior 4 (instrument) FLAME-MoE arXiv:2505.20225 — 38M-1.7B ladder, all checkpoints public, "routing behavior stabilizes early", no seed replicates. Prior 5 arXiv:2509.11348 "On Linear Mode Connectivity of Mixture-of-Experts Architectures" (Viet-Hoang Tran, Van Hoan Trinh, Khanh Vinh Bui, Tan M. Nguyen; author order corrected from the record) — loss-barrier endpoint, parameter-space LAP matching that "avoids data-dependent computational overhead", fine-tuned 2-8-expert MoE layers. Prior 6 Gurnee et al. arXiv:2401.12181 — the dense cross-seed-universality template, 1-5% universal neurons.

Novelty — how this differs from each: vs Prior 1 — the only source claiming a cross-seed measurement in sparse-MoE LMs, and the reason this entry is not Validated. It differs on architecture (cosine routing against learned centroids, rank-1 singleton experts, 1024 experts, multi-hop, vs OLMoE-style top-8-of-64 learned-logit routing), scale (76-84M on multi-epoch WikiText-103), checkpoint (final only; no 1% checkpoint, no saturation curve), and stated endpoint ("functional overlap" of experts, not token-to-expert partition agreement after a declared activation-profile Hungarian match against a permutation and an unrelated-run null); it has no prediction limb and no aux-loss sweep. But the differentiating attributes sit in sections that could not be read, so this is a claimed difference, not a verified one. vs Prior 2 — same spirit with a stronger replicate count (10 seeds) but vision, representational motifs pooled without one-to-one matching, no null, final checkpoints, no loss prediction; its cross-seed stability conclusion is qualitative. vs Prior 3 — different estimand (cross-domain within one model, not cross-run), and the sharpest discount on significance: with ECI Gini ~0.90-0.95, high A_cross could be produced by a mass-concentrated standing committee rather than canonicity. vs Prior 0 — same instrument, orthogonal comparison; a within-run null is not the null a cross-run question needs. vs Prior 5 — shares only the permutation-symmetry premise; a low loss barrier after weight matching is compatible with either answer here. vs Prior 6 — the template exists inside LM interpretability since 2024 for dense neurons (activation-correlation matching, rotation null, no partition statistic, no MoE, final checkpoints), which weakens the record's "the machinery arrived in 2025" story. Method-owning-field negatives (clustering stability — von Luxburg arXiv:1007.1075, cross-study replicability arXiv:2202.01910; label switching — Stephens 2000) rest on titles only, NOT OPENED, and are not checks that passed; consensus/co-association, VQ-codebook, 1990s HME, modular-networks, hash-routing, merging/upcycling and Chinese-language sweeps (adversaries 1-3) returned no instance of the estimand.

Novelty confidence: Medium (at the floor, with one unverified close neighbour). Nothing fully read measures cross-run token-to-expert partition agreement in MoE LMs at any checkpoint against a declared null. Not High: Prior 2 asks the same spirit of question with 10 seeds in vision, and Prior 1 claims a cross-seed overlap result in sparse-MoE LMs whose method is unread. Not Low: an unread section grounds no grade in either direction (LEDGER operating rule), so Prior 1 cannot carry a Low grade or an already-asked rejection until §5 / §8.4 / App. B.3 and arXiv:2604.14434 are read — and three of Gate 2's negatives still rest on unopened results.

Significance — consequence: If canonical, the early-frozen partition is a property of the recipe, which licenses three things now done on faith — expert-level interpretability as a claim about the architecture, transfer of expert-targeted surgery (pruning/merging/upcycling) between runs of a recipe, and reading the 1% checkpoint as an early predictor — and gives Prior 5's alignment algorithm the functional validation it lacks. If arbitrary, every published per-expert specialization table (OLMoE's, DeepSeekMoE's, Prior 3's standing committee) becomes a statement about one run, and the reporting unit for specialization becomes the distribution over runs; engineering on a shipped model is unaffected, since it is re-derived per model. If a core plus remainder (likeliest), its size and layer location is the number pruning, merging and interpretability need and nobody has. Discounted by Prior 1's finding that routing topology does not determine quality, which predicts limb (iv) near-null — informative, but it removes the quality stake.
Significance — audience: (1) MoE pretraining teams publishing specialization analyses from single runs with intermediate checkpoints (OLMo/OLMoE, FLAME-MoE, DeepSeek, Qwen) — they would have to change what they claim; (2) the MoE merging/compression and permutation-symmetry line (Prior 5), which ships an alignment algorithm for independently trained MoEs with no functional validation; (3) interpretability groups treating an expert as a unit of analysis, including Prior 3's and Prior 1's companion's authors; (4) expert-offloading/serving work, for whom run-specificity decides whether caching policy can be recipe-level; (5) statisticians who own clustering stability and label switching. Held at 2/3 and not fully secure: engineering consumers act per shipped model, Prior 3 pre-discounts the arbitrary branch's sting, and adversary 2's sharpest point is that a 2026 group holding three same-recipe MoE seeds (Prior 1) printed a validation-loss comparison and no cross-seed routing table.
Significance — fecundity: Does canonicity scale with expert granularity or count, and is there a knee? Is a canonical core computable at 1% of training usable as a pruning criterion? Does the aux-loss weight trade load balance against canonicity? Can independently trained MoEs be merged usefully once alignment is validated functionally? Is the early-frozen partition a lottery in the Frankle-Carbin sense — does initializing a fresh run with run A's 1% router reproduce A's partition and quality? Does the canonical core coincide with Prior 3's standing committee or its complement?
Significance — anchoring: OLMoE §5.1's reported-but-uninterrogated saturation and FLAME-MoE's independent "stabilizes early"; OpenMoE's token-ID "early routing learning"; the dispute over whether expert specialization is semantic (Prior 3 and the "Myth of Expert Specialization" line vs the specialization tables); permutation symmetry and LMC in MoE (Prior 5) and model merging; "Why Routers Freeze" (ICML 2026 HiLD), which derives Top-K selection as finite-width symmetry breaking; routing consistency as a serving problem; the dense early-phase/lottery-ticket literature and interpretability's universality programme (Prior 6); clustering stability and label-switching identifiability in statistics.

Reason for silence: Partly revised by Gate 4. Surviving: (a) cost and instrument — k from-scratch runs at a scale where the saturation curve reproduces are affordable only to labs with no incentive to re-run one recipe at a new seed, and nobody releases two seeds of an OLMoE-scale MoE recipe (adversary 3 narrows this to a SCALE gap: 10-seed vision and 3-seed 76-84M LM studies exist); (c) the anchor's own instrument hides the question — a within-run metric against a 12.5% random null makes 60% read as structure and never prompts "structure of what?"; (d) incentive asymmetry — the canonical outcome publishes as a negative result licensing others' practice, the arbitrary outcome invalidates a popular genre including the authors' own tables, and both cost k pretraining runs. Weakened: (b) "the machinery arrived in 2025" is wrong — cross-seed unit matching with a null is a standard move inside LM interpretability (Prior 6, 2024; Li et al. convergent learning, 2015), so the conceptual bridge was never missing from the object's own field. Net: this is a scale-and-incentive silence, not a conceptual one, and at small scale it is arguably already breaking (Prior 1).
