ID: UQ-20261017-10
Date: 2026-10-17
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): AI architecture — training-objective implementation and token/compute accounting. Neighbour vocabularies swept: survey statistics (design weights, Kish design effect), biostatistics (informative cluster size, cluster- vs observation-level estimands), NMT/speech toolkit normalization, compute-governance metrology. Source method: silence mapping.
Question (canonical): For a declared frame of published training runs and the K training stacks named in them at named versions, define a run's realized per-token weight w_i as the coefficient on token i's next-token NLL inside the single scalar whose gradient the optimizer consumes at one step — after padding, truncation remainders, packing, prompt/label masking, micro-batch loss reduction, gradient accumulation and cross-rank averaging, normalized to Σw_i = 1 — and take the stated objective to be uniform weight over gradient-bearing tokens plus the configured source mixture. Then: (a) what is each stack's implied w_i in closed form as a function of sequence length, masked-token count, micro-batch composition, accumulation window and world size; (b) for runs with public config and data order (or an instrumented replication), what is the realized weight distribution — zero-weight share against the reported token count, Kish effective-to-nominal token ratio (Σw)²/Σw², and induced per-source mixture shift as TV distance from the configured weights; (c) in a matched-FLOPs pair of runs differing only in loss-reduction semantics, is the held-out loss and benchmark gap inside or outside a band pre-registered from published recipe/mixture effect sizes and same-config seed variance? Limbs reported separately for packed pretraining and for SFT/RL; runs whose releases permit no gap definition are counted into a reported unspecifiability share. (V0 at intake asked loosely for "the objective actually optimized" and its "gap from the stated objective"; it failed Gate 1 for naming no estimand, metric or band, and the single permitted reformulation produced V1 above, the assessed version.)
Alternative formulations: (1) What fraction of a run's reported tokens carried gradient signal, and with what weight — is "tokens seen" a comparable unit across stacks at all? (2) If two labs report the same mixture and the same token count, were they optimizing the same objective? (3) (survey-statistics vocabulary) What are a training run's design weights and its design effect, and what reweighting of the corpus does a per-sequence-mean loss over a length-heterogeneous batch induce relative to the claimed sampling design?
Motivating gap: A region dense with how-answers and empty of why-questions. Vendor and framework documentation exists specifically to make the user pick a loss denominator (Cerebras, "Training with number of tokens loss scaling", four doc versions, live 2026-10-17), and the non-equivalence of gradient accumulation to large-batch training under per-micro-batch normalization is a five-year, multi-repository defect family: huggingface/transformers#14638 (2021) → #37474, #41842, #43604, #46731, #47688 (2026-07-31, where the normalization decision is taken by an `inspect.signature` VAR_KEYWORD check, so which objective a run optimizes depends on a model class's signature); huggingface/trl#2604, #5619, #7047, #7569 (MoE aux loss inflated ×2.19 and ×4.88), and #7206 (2026-09-14, open), which states the mechanism verbatim — "independently normalizing each microbatch makes effective token weighting depend on packing" — with a worked two-micro-batch example (1.25 vs 0.65). GitHub code search confirms the per-micro-batch denominator ships in a pretraining stack: `megatron/core/pipeline_parallel/schedules.py`, `loss = torch.sum(losses.view(-1) * loss_mask) / loss_mask.sum()`. Absent in everything opened: any published run reporting its realized weight distribution, zero-weight share or effective-to-nominal token ratio; any scaling-law/recipe/mixture paper carrying loss-reduction semantics as a covariate; and any token accounting in the governance literature — the Frontier Model Forum's "Issue Brief: Measuring Training Compute" (opened) resolves precision, recomputation, discarded branches and a <5% tolerance and never mentions tokens.
Presuppositions: (1) Loss-reduction defaults differ across the stacks used by published runs — PARTLY ESTABLISHED IN SOURCE: Megatron per-micro-batch token-mean (code quoted), HF Trainer by signature check with `loss / gradient_accumulation_steps` fallback, TRL per-micro-batch on at least one path; adversary added torchtitan `components/loss.py` (c9c8626) returning a SUM with the denominator applied in an unlocated trainer path (UNVERIFIED) and Axolotl inheriting HF post-fix semantics with the same signature dependence; Levanter UNVERIFIED. (2) The realized distribution is reconstructable from released config plus data — established only where pipeline and data order are public, else under declared replication. (3) Sequence lengths are heterogeneous enough for the reweighting to be non-negligible — established for SFT/RL and long-document regimes, CONTESTED and, per the adversary's opened source, effectively FALSE for fixed-length-packed pretraining. (4) Recipe/mixture effect sizes are small enough to be commensurable — CONTESTED, measurable from the papers before any experiment. (5) FLOPs and gradient-bearing tokens diverge because padded/masked tokens still consume compute — established arithmetic; shares already published (Krell et al., arXiv:2107.02027: "up to 50% of all tokens can be padding", up to 89% for GLUE-cola at length 128). (6) The stated objective in papers is specific enough for a gap to be defined — CONTESTED, converted into the reported unspecifiability share. (7) (added at Gate 1) A single scalar per step exists whose gradient is consumed, so w_i is well defined — established for the stacks examined, fails for non-linear per-sequence terms (clipped sequence means, group-normalized RL advantages), where w_i is state-dependent; a real limitation on the RL arm.
What would count as an answer: (i) the code-level audit of limb (a) for the K stacks at the versions published runs name; (ii) the limb (b) functionals computed on runs with public config and data order; (iii) the limb (c) matched-FLOPs pair judged against the pre-registered band. YES: ESS ratio well below 1, mixture TV shift of the order of the deltas mixture papers optimize over, loss/benchmark gap outside the band. NO: shift and gap both inside seed noise, which licenses "tokens seen" as a cross-stack unit. A high unspecifiability share answers the accounting limb directly and is a reporting-standards result.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 11 of 11 web queries (minimum 8 met), 4 of 5 fetches completed, plus 3 GitHub issue searches and 2 code searches on free routes; full list in batches/2026-10-17-0310/UQ-20261017-10-record.md. (5) "DAPO Dr. GRPO token-level loss normalization length bias ablation" → arXiv:2605.04077 "Balanced Aggregation" (opened), an active in-field RL aggregation literature. (6, mandatory fraction limb) "what fraction of tokens are padding … measured percentage" → the quantity is already published for reference corpora (Krell et al., arXiv:2107.02027, opened), though never for a named frontier run or as a weight. (3) "sequence packing prompt loss masking changes effective sample weights SFT length bias" → arXiv:2401.13586 (opened). (9, method-owning field) "unequal cluster sizes implicit weighting cluster- versus observation-level analysis changes estimand" → the named family (informative cluster size; Kahan et al. on estimands in cluster trials) exists with zero application to training. Novelty — how this differs from each: vs P1 — closest, and it states the candidate's mechanism in the candidate's own field in nearly the candidate's words, so the mechanism is not un-noticed; it differs on unit (one code path at one commit vs published run × stack version), endpoint (an invariance property on a synthetic example vs the realized weight distribution and its functionals on a real corpus), comparator (the within-library correct denominator vs a published run's own stated objective and configured mixture) and estimand (implementation correctness vs the size of the paper-to-run gap and its commensurability with the recipe literature). vs P2 — occupies limb (c) within RL only: it differs on unit (a group-level rule in one algorithm), endpoint (benchmark scores, not weights or mixture shift), comparator (two GRPO variants) and estimand (which rule wins); it performs no cross-framework audit, reports no effective-to-nominal ratio and makes no comparison to recipe effect sizes, but the candidate must concede the RL arm is partly answered in-field. vs P3 — studies exactly one weighting mechanism (prompt vs completion masking) as a tunable, and describes its own weighting as binary at the token level, i.e. w_i collapsed to {0,1} on one axis; differs on unit, endpoint, comparator and estimand, and touches none of padding, truncation, packing, micro-batch normalization, accumulation or cross-rank averaging, nor mixture weights. Negative stated in the method-owning field's words: the estimand asked for — implied design weights, their design effect, and whether unit- or cluster-level aggregation targets the intended estimand when cluster size is informative — is a mature named family in survey statistics and biostatistics (queries 4 and 9) with zero application to a training run.
Novelty confidence: Medium
Significance — consequence: If the gap is large, a configured mixture is not the realized mixture, so the mixture-optimization literature optimizes a quantity the trainer does not implement, "trained on N tokens of mixture m" ceases to identify an objective, comparisons at matched token counts are not matched, pooling runs across stacks for scaling-law fits carries a stack-dependent nuisance, and part of the recipe literature's non-transfer gains a named candidate confounder. If small, "tokens seen" is established as a comparable cross-stack unit — a licence the field currently assumes. A high unspecifiability share is a reporting-standards finding: it says what a run report would have to contain.
Significance — audience: Framework maintainers, who demonstrably act when this is pointed out (the transformers/trl issue histories and the Oct-2024 HF fix) but have never aggregated the fixes into a cross-stack statement of shipped semantics; pretraining and post-training recipe teams, who would gain an unrecorded covariate; data-mixture researchers (DoReMi/RegMix/Aioli/SampleMix lineage); scaling-law fitters pooling across stacks; reproducibility and metascience-of-ML workers. The compute-governance audience is weaker than the record claims: thresholds are FLOPs, and padded or masked tokens consume FLOPs whatever their weight, so the FMF brief's silence on tokens is not obviously a gap in a live instrument.
Significance — fecundity: Are fitted scaling-law exponents stack-dependent once loss-reduction semantics are a covariate? Should a mixture be specified as a target realized weight vector, and what sampler achieves one under packing? Does the effective-to-nominal ratio predict seed variance, giving a cheap pre-run diagnostic? Is length-dependent reweighting an unintended curriculum bearing on long-context degradation? What minimum model-card fields make the realized weight distribution reconstructable, and what share of releases clear that bar? Does the same accounting reopen "effective epochs" and data-repetition results, which are stated in nominal tokens? For RL, where w_i is state-dependent, what generalizes a design weight?
Significance — anchoring: The five-year gradient-accumulation normalization defect family across two of the most-used stacks (transformers#14638→#47688; trl#2604→#7569); the RL length-bias debate (DAPO vs Dr. GRPO vs Balanced Aggregation arXiv:2605.04077; arXiv:2508.08221); the non-transfer of pretraining recipe results, treated as an anomaly at UQ-20261016-53; compute-threshold accounting under the EU AI Act and the FMF measurement brief; informative cluster size and estimand choice in cluster-randomised trials; Kish's design effect; published padding shares up to 50% from the packing literature, which asserts objective equivalence without measuring weights. Ledger adjacency: UQ-20261016-30 asks whether a run's claimed training set is the realized one under restart semantics (a coverage estimand over document identities) — disjoint from this entry's denominator-and-weighting estimand over the documents consumed.
Reason for silence: A disciplinary and artifact boundary reinforced by notation and incentives — the semantics live in framework source and launch configs, owned by systems engineers who hold them to a correctness criterion rather than treating them as an estimand, while the claim about what was optimized lives in papers whose notation elides the denominator; nobody owns the join. Compounded by the fact that computing the quantity needs the realized data order, the least-released artifact, and by the method's vocabulary sitting in survey statistics and biostatistics so the question has no name in ML. Adversary's competing mechanism, which the record does not address: once the denominator is a token count over the whole accumulation window — the post-Oct-2024 HF default, Axolotl, Cerebras "num tokens" mode — w_i is uniform by construction, so the silence may be the absence of a problem rather than a boundary.

Verification (post-batch, fresh-context checker, log UQ-20261017-10-verification.md): the kill stands in the regime that carries the entry's significance, but two of the three legs it was argued from are mis-sourced, and the entry's own arithmetic was being presented as a published figure.
Leg by leg. **(1) The padding ratio.** The 0.01-0.08% range is real and is Table 1 of arXiv:2407.07495 (bucket pre-training), whose fixed-length rows read 1024: 0.01%, 2048: 0.01%, 4096: 0.02%, 8192: 0.04%, 16384: 0.08%, against the paper's own bucketing method at 0.12% and document-level at 0.0% ("Padding ratio: The proportion of padding tokens in training sequences"). But it is **not a padding ratio published from a large pretraining run**: it is a data-composition statistic computed on "a representative subset consisting of 100B tokens (approximately 98M documents)" of FineWeb-Edu, and that paper's own 1B Llama3.1-architecture experiments report no padding figure. No lab technical report with a published padding figure was found. The entry's phrasing is corrected accordingly: the figure predicts what a fixed-length-packed run's ratio would be, over a realistic 98M-document corpus at exactly the sequence lengths such runs use, and that is what the kill needs — but it is a computed statistic from one 2024 paper, not a reported property of any published run.
**(2) The "uniform by construction" step.** The checker reports plainly that the clause "so essentially every token carries equal weight in the loss" **is stated by no source it read**. That step is therefore the ledger's own algebra, not a sourced claim, and is relabelled here as such: with sequences of equal length, no masking, and a padded share of order 1e-4, per-micro-batch mean normalisation gives per-token weights uniform to within that order, so limb (b)(i)'s zero-weight share is ~0, the Kish effective-to-nominal ratio is ~1 and the induced mixture TV distance is ~0. The arithmetic is elementary and the inputs are sourced; the inference is the ledger's.
**(3) The October 2024 diagnosis.** CONFIRMED and dated: Unsloth's blog of October 15, 2024 and Hugging Face's of October 16, 2024 both identify the gradient-accumulation loss-normalisation defect, quoting "naively averaging over each gradient accumulation step is wrong" and a correct denominator of "the total number of all non padding tokens in those batches". The checker adds the qualification that matters: those posts concern **padded, variable-length** settings, mostly fine-tuning, and are "not about fixed-length packing", so they do not themselves establish that packed pretraining is free of the defect. That is consistent with the entry's regime split rather than against it — the posts answer the SFT/RL limb, the padding ratio answers the packed-pretraining limb — but the entry no longer claims they cover both. The practice premise is separately supported: arXiv:2404.10830 states that "input documents are typically concatenated together and then split into sequences of equal length to avoid padding tokens", with its own best-fit packing leaving a "negligible amount of padding" (no number given).
**What the rejection now rests on.** Triviality and dissolution over the frame's packed-pretraining limb, from a computed padding ratio at the candidate's own sequence lengths plus the ledger's own normalisation algebra; and, for the SFT/RL limb, a mechanism publicly diagnosed in October 2024 whose ESS ratio reduces to the harmonic-to-arithmetic mean of the length histogram. The surviving fragment is unchanged: an SFT-regime limb (c) ablation. Still UNVERIFIED and counted as neither passing nor failing: torchtitan and Levanter denominators (unrun), arXiv:2609.25890 (abstract only), and trl#7206 and arXiv:2605.04077 (not independently re-verified); no library issue or pull request was opened to confirm the fix date. None of these supports the kill.
Caveat recorded: everything above came through the page summariser; Table 1's header was garbled in the PDF and its row values are the summariser's reading, and the table does not name its dataset explicitly — the FineWeb-Edu attribution is the checker's inference from the paper's text.

Scores: Well-posedness 3/3 · Significance 2/3
Strongest remaining objection: In the regime carrying the candidate's significance — fixed-length-packed pretraining — the realized per-token weights are uniform to within a part in 10^4 and the padding ratio at the candidate's own sequence lengths is 0.01–0.08% (arXiv:2407.07495 Table 1, fixed-length rows 1024 through 16384, opened by the adversary), so limbs (b)(i)–(iii) evaluate to ≈0, ≈1 and ≈0 by algebra rather than by measurement — with two provenance corrections from verification: that ratio is a data-composition statistic computed on a 100B-token, ~98M-document FineWeb-Edu subset rather than a figure published from any large pretraining run (none was found), and the step from near-zero padding to uniform weights is the ledger's own arithmetic, stated by no source; and in the regime where the perturbation is real (SFT/RL), the mechanism was publicly diagnosed and fixed in Oct 2024, the ESS ratio collapses to HM/AM of the length histogram, and the "does the aggregation rule change outcomes" ablation has already been run in RL (arXiv:2605.04077) and in speech token LMs (arXiv:2609.25890). The question is therefore answerable in a page over most of its frame, with only an SFT-regime limb (c) ablation left — which is a study to run, not an un-asked question. Novelty was never the binding constraint: Medium novelty and 3/3 well-posedness survive intact, and the entry fails at Gate 4 on triviality and dissolution. Non-binding caveats, recorded because they constrain any re-opening: torchtitan and Levanter denominators remain UNVERIFIED (unrun, so neither passing nor failing), arXiv:2609.25890 was read at abstract level only, and trl#7206 and arXiv:2605.04077 could not be independently re-verified on the free route — none of these supports the kill, which rests on sources the adversary opened and quoted in the candidate's own regime.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): Not applicable at this status. Were the kill withdrawn, the pointer is limb (a) on the two stacks whose denominators are already in hand plus limb (b)(i) on one fully open run (OLMo/Dolma class), to see whether the zero-weight share and ESS ratio are large enough to make limbs (b)(ii)–(c) worth running.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): Not routed. The rejection ground is triviality/dissolution — answerable in a page over most of the frame from sources already in hand — not asked-but-still-open, and routed-open-problems.md takes only asked-and-unanswered rejections. The surviving fragment belongs as an SFT-regime ablation extending arXiv:2401.13586 / arXiv:2609.25890, or as an addendum to the HF "Fixing Gradient Accumulation" lineage, rather than as a problem for the research workstream.

ID: UQ-20261017-11
Date: 2026-10-17
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): Biology — comparative/evolutionary genomics; reference-genome assembly methodology (EBP/VGP-era pipelines). Method-owning neighbours: statistical screening theory (false-rejection rate of a default-on filter); assembly benchmarking (gene-content metrics).
Question (canonical): In reference genome assemblies produced by the standard Earth BioGenome-era pipeline, what fraction of genuine recent gene duplicates is removed by the haplotypic-duplication purging step (purge_dups / purge_haplotigs plus manual curation), and by how much does that removal shift published estimates of gene-family expansion and contraction rates?
Alternative formulations: (i) When an assembly pipeline is tuned to remove false duplications, how many real young duplicate genes go with them, and does the resulting gene-content bias propagate into comparative-genomic rate estimates? (ii) Is the apparent scarcity of very young, near-identical gene duplicates in reference assemblies a biological fact or a residue of duplicate-purging? Gate 1 reformulation (one, retained): same question restricted to assemblies with archived reads and pinned tool versions, inside a pre-declared paralogue identity band (99.0-99.8% CDS identity, instrument floor stated), with limb (b) posed against the published point estimate, its interval, AND the CAFE 3/5 epsilon-corrected estimate.
Motivating gap: The gain direction is quantified gene by gene (Ko et al., Genome Biol 23:205, 2022: 4-24% of coding genes affected pre-VGP, 0.3-2.3% in VGP assemblies); its companion on false losses (Kim et al., 23:204) attributes them to GC- and repeat-rich sequence and names no purging tool; purge_dups' own paper validates only in the gain direction; hifiasm's discussion and FAQ voice "overpurged repetitive regions" / "may collapse repeats or segmental duplications" with no numbers. Gate 2 narrowed this: the loss-direction fraction IS routinely published in weakened, all-causes form (asmgene multi-copy retained/missed). CORRECTED on verification — see the Verification section: the asmgene figures are real, but the metric pools assembler collapse, purge removal and genuine individual-versus-reference copy-number difference and cannot separate them, and hifiasm's Table 2 contains no same-sample purged-versus-unpurged pair, so no published figure answers limb (a) even weakly. Gate 4 narrowed it further and fatally for the gap sentence as written: Guiglielmoni et al. 2021 (BMC Bioinformatics 22:303, 10.1186/s12859-021-04118-3; opened at link.springer.com by adversary 2) is a dedicated with/without-purge benchmark across HaploMerger2, purge_dups and purge_haplotigs that names overpurging and measures it at the heterozygous-k-mer level. "The over-removal error is left unmeasured" is false; what remains unmeasured is gene-level, ground-truthed, zygosity-stratified attribution and rate propagation.
Presuppositions: (1) an orthogonal per-locus copy-number ground truth exists [contested in degree; fails above ~99.9% identity, conceded by the record]; (2) the purge counterfactual is recoverable [partly evidenced — Guiglielmoni re-ran purging on their own assemblies; VGP moves purged haplotype duplications to the deposited alternate assembly (Rhie et al. 2021 Methods, opened at nature.com), so the counterfactual is largely public]; (3) published CAFE-style rates are computed from these annotations [established]; (4) the bias is not already absorbed by annotation filters or rate-side error models [contested; CAFE 3 epsilon is exactly an absorbing device]; (5) young duplicates occur at non-trivial rate [established for vertebrates/plants]; (6) genuine young duplicates and haplotypic duplicates overlap in the statistic the tool thresholds on [FALSIFIED AS WRITTEN for the named tool and the fixed-duplicate class — see adversarial log row 4].
What would count as an answer: two numbers with uncertainties — (a) a purge-attributable over-removal rate for genuine duplicate gene copies in the declared band, pipeline otherwise fixed, reported alongside the all-causes asmgene collapse rate for the same assemblies; (b) a re-estimate of a pre-specified set of published gene-family gain/loss rates and paralogue-age distributions with purged sequence restored, against the published estimate, its interval, and the epsilon-corrected estimate. A bounded null licenses the current default; a heterozygosity-scaling result makes the bias a between-taxon confound.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): Gate 2 ran 11 web searches + 5 fetches; Gate 4 added 27 Disguise queries in new vocabularies (9 per adversary) + 12 fetches + GitHub issue/code search. Full lists: batches/2026-10-17-0522/UQ-20261017-11-record.md and the three adversary files. Most informative: (Gate 2 q10, the mandatory "already computed" query) asmgene multi-copy retained/missed → HIT, an all-causes fraction exists in both hifiasm papers (23-33% of near-identical multi-copy human genes not retained), though verification showed it is not attributable to purging and has no purged-versus-unpurged pair behind it; (Gate 2 q5) "over-purging" haplotype duplication → concluded "the term exists in discussion sections, no dedicated study", which Gate 4 falsified; (A2 q4, historical HaploMerger vocabulary) → HIT Guiglielmoni et al. 2021, the dedicated overpurging benchmark Gate 2 missed; (A2 GitHub, free route) dfguan/purge_dups issues → 87 matching threads, #42 "Optimise purging without losing too many genes" (BUSCO C 97.0→95.3%, M 2.4→3.9%), #43 "~200 of 350 Mb" over-purged, #10 polyploid "might represent true duplications", hifiasm #713 (real homoeologous region purged, restored by -l0), #928 ("Would further purging risk removing true biological copies?"); (A3 F1) journals.plos.org/ploscompbiol 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1008104 — the record's COULD-NOT-READ paper, opened on the first publisher call, no purging content, not a prior; (A3 F2) Rhie et al. 2021 VGP Methods — purged duplications moved to the alternate assembly; (A3 GitHub) purge_dups README verbatim — only contigs with average coverage below the haploid/diploid *mid* transition are tested for haplotypic duplication; hifiasm man page — default -l3, -s 0.55, --purge-max is a coverage UPPER bound (HOM_PEAK_RATE 1.25). Ledger duplicate check: all 109 INDEX.md entries read, no duplicate (design-motif kin UQ-20261016-40/-56/-59). Still unread, grounding nothing: HiCanu main text (Genome Res 30:1291, abstract only), purge_dups Supplementary Note, GBE "Effect of collapsed duplications on diversity estimates" (PMC/UPF both refused), HPRC Flagger supplement.
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources): PRIOR 1 — hifiasm, Cheng et al., Nat Methods 2021 (read at arxiv.org/pdf/2008.01237): unit = reference multi-copy gene (>=99% identity, Ensembl cDNA on GRCh38); endpoint = % remaining multi-copy in the assembly (paftools asmgene -i.99); comparator = GRCh38 annotation on a different individual; estimand = all-causes assembly-level collapse rate; CHM13 (no purging) 76.9% retained, HG00733/HG002 (purged) 67.3/74.8%. PRIOR 2 — hifiasm Hi-C/dual, Cheng et al., Nat Biotech 2022 (arxiv.org/pdf/2109.04785): same unit/endpoint as complement ("multi-copy genes missed", 13.77-40.13% by strategy), per haplotype; purge_dups applied with manually adjusted cutoffs; no with/without-purge contrast anywhere. MIS-ATTRIBUTED in the batch record and struck: the "dropped for badger and black rhino as significantly worse" passage is about **HiCanu**, not hifiasm, sits in Supplementary 1.2 and a Supp Table 3 caption, carries no figures, and the hifiasm Hi-C main text does not mention purge_dups at all. PRIOR 3 — Han, Thomas, Lugo-Martinez, Hahn, MBE 30:1987, 2013 (hahnlab PDF): unit = gene family with error-prone observed size; endpoint = lambda; comparator = CAFE without error model; estimand = true lambda plus symmetric species-level epsilon; corrected lambda ~50-75% of uncorrected on real data. PRIOR 4 (found at Gate 4, missed by Gate 2) — Guiglielmoni, Houtain, Derzelle, Van Doninck, Flot, BMC Bioinformatics 2021 (link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12859-021-04118-3): unit = heterozygous k-mers; endpoint = het-k-mer completeness (explicitly two-sided — "a lower value indicates that too many k-mers were lost (overpurging)") plus size/BUSCO; comparator = the same assembly pre-purge, across three purging tools and five assemblers; estimand = purge-attributable sequence-level overpurging in one 102 Mb rotifer; no ground truth for real duplications, no gene-copy or identity-band limb, no rates.
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs PRIORS 1-2 — same endpoint class, different comparator and estimand: their 23-33% pools assembler collapse, purge removal and real individual-vs-reference CNV, and neither reports a with/without-purge contrast or any gene-family limb; the candidate varies the purge step alone with a same-individual instrument. vs PRIOR 3 — answers limb (b)'s generic form (gene-content error inflates lambda ~2-4x at epsilon 0.1-0.4) with symmetric, species-level, mechanism-agnostic machinery; the candidate's claim is a directional loss concentrated in the youngest identity bin, which a symmetric nuisance parameter cannot absorb without bias. vs PRIOR 4 — same comparator and same purge-attributable direction, but unit (het k-mers vs gene copies), endpoint (k-mer completeness vs genuine-copy removal), ground truth (k-mer expectation vs orthogonal per-locus copy number) and scope (one 102 Mb genome vs a frame of reference assemblies) all differ, and it has no rate limb. So PRIOR 4 is not a duplicate — but it refutes the gap narrative the Medium grade was argued on and shows the Gate 2 record incomplete, which blocks Validated independently of the attack statuses.
Novelty confidence: Medium
Grading note: Medium survives on unit/endpoint/estimand, but on a demonstrably incomplete search record — an on-point, same-field, same-word neighbour (PRIOR 4) was missed by a Gate 2 that reported "no dedicated study", and the practitioner literature poses the loss-direction worry repeatedly with numbers attached. Medium-on-incomplete-record cannot support Validated.
Significance — consequence: If purge-attributable over-removal is material, the default EBP/VGP pipeline imposes a directional, age-structured gene-content bias on the assemblies the comparative-genomics stack treats as ground truth, the youngest bin of published Ks/identity distributions becomes an artefact of known sign, and because purge aggressiveness tracks heterozygosity the bias is a between-taxon confound rather than a common offset. A bounded null licenses the default on evidence. Either way it apportions the published 23-33% asmgene shortfall. Discounted at Gate 4: the consequence as framed presupposes fixed-duplicate removal, which the purge_dups depth gate largely excludes; for hemizygous copies, exclusion from a haploid primary is a representation convention and a segregating CNV has no species-level family size for CAFE to be biased about.
Significance — audience: Real and evidenced, not notional — purge_dups and hifiasm authors voice the worry and decline to quantify it; four+ purge_dups issue threads and hifiasm #713/#928 ask it with numbers; Guiglielmoni et al. built a purpose-made two-sided metric and recommended archiving alternative assemblies; the PLoS Comput Biol 2020 abstract calls for methods to detect local expansion/collapse. Downstream: CAFE/gene-family users, Ensembl/RefSeq annotation, SD/CNV/pharmacogene communities.
Significance — fecundity: Is the youngest Ks peak an artefact across EBP clades and does it track pipeline version? Does purge loss scale with heterozygosity? What is the right loss-direction QC statistic? Does the same over-rejection audit apply to the other default-on cleaning steps (contaminant, NUMT/organellar, adapter screens)? Does restoration move dN/dS and dosage-balance inference?
Significance — anchoring: The empty cell between Genome Biol 23:205 and 23:204; the unquantified "overpurged repetitive regions" line and the --purge-max warning; the unexplained composition of the 23-33% asmgene shortfall; purge_dups' asymmetric validation; CAFE's epsilon as both propagation machinery and absorbing device; the segmental-duplication-collapse problem T2T work addresses.
Reason for silence: As stated — metric asymmetry, epsilon absorption, archiving gap — it does not survive. Mechanism (i) ("no statistic worsens when a real young duplicate is purged; the error has no owner inside assembly QC") is falsified on sources two adversaries opened: Guiglielmoni's het-k-mer completeness was chosen *because* it is two-sided, asmgene's "multi-copy missed" (the record's own priors 1-2) is a loss-direction statistic, Vollger et al. 2022 applies read-depth copy-number comparison in the loss direction, and practitioners watch BUSCO Missing rise and IsoSeq mapping fall after purging. Mechanism (iii) is falsified for VGP, where purged duplications are deposited as the alternate assembly. What survives is (ii) — downstream consumers absorb the signal into a generic error term — plus a real disciplinary boundary (asmgene is unattributed; gene-family analysts do not read assembler benchmarks). That explains why answering is unrewarded, not why the question went unposed, and the issue trackers show it has been posed informally. Per the ledger's own rule, a failed reason-for-silence makes the novelty finding suspect and returns the candidate to Gate 2.

4 | Presupposition failure | FATAL. Presupposition 6 is false for the tool the canonical question names and for the class it is about: purge_dups tests for haplotypic duplication only contigs whose average coverage is below the haploid/diploid *mid* transition (README, verbatim), whereas a fixed young duplicate contributes diploid depth at each assembled copy, so the two populations do not overlap in the depth statistic — only in identity, which purge_dups does not threshold on alone. The class that does overlap is the hemizygous/segregating duplicate, and for it the candidate's dichotomy ("biological fact or residue of purging") and limb (b)'s "bias" are misposed: moving a one-haplotype copy to the alternate assembly is the haploid-reference convention (Rhie et al. 2021 Methods, verbatim), and a segregating CNV has no species-level family size for CAFE to be biased about. The canonical question stratifies by neither zygosity nor purge module | Best rescue relocates the mechanism to hifiasm's built-in purge, which IS the EBP-era default (-l3, -s 0.55) and whose documented coverage limit is an UPPER bound (HOM_PEAK_RATE 1.25), so diploid-depth unitigs are not excluded, with hifiasm #713 an anchoring case of a genuine homoeologous region purged and restored by -l0. A3's own regime-check thus leaves the mechanism live for the actual default module — but that is a different module, a different discriminant and a zygosity-stratified estimand, i.e. a re-posed question, not a defence of the presupposition as written. A1 reached the same depth argument and graded it Partial only because it had opened no source for it; A3 sourced it (README and VGP Methods, both quoted) and the candidate's response concedes re-posing | Unresolved (A3; A1/A2 Partial) — FATAL
5 | Vagueness | "Genuine recent duplicate" is undefined with respect to zygosity, the very variable the purge mechanism keys on, so the same data support a large or a near-zero answer; the CAFE set is a placeholder; and the frame (archived reads + pinned version + orthogonal instrument on the same individual) may admit only 3-5 genomes, making it a case study, not a property of the pipeline | The pre-declared band, instrument floor and three-way null make it non-vacuous and it sharpens if a zygosity stratum is added, but the unpriced small-n frame and the unnamed analyses stand | Partial (A2/A3 Partial, A1 Resolved)
6 | Significance inflation | The headline consequence presupposes fixed-duplicate removal; the restore-or-flag fix partly exists already (VGP alternate assembly); Ks practice already distrusts the youngest bin; epsilon already exists | Audience is evidenced and already acting; magnitude unknown by construction; significance survives at reduced scope for the hemizygous/CNV-gene and hifiasm-module versions | Partial (A1/A3 Partial, A2 Resolved)
7 | Reason for silence | Two of three mechanisms are contradicted by opened sources (two-sided metrics exist; VGP deposits the purged sequence), and the trackers show the question has been asked informally; what remains explains why answering is unrewarded, not why it went unposed | Mechanism (ii) plus the disciplinary boundary is plausible but thin, and by the ledger's rule a failed reason-for-silence makes the novelty finding itself suspect | Unresolved (A2 and A3; A1 Partial) — non-fatal
8 | Dissolution | At the youngest ages the needed dichotomy may not exist: a hemizygous copy is both a genuine duplicate and a haplotype-specific one, so for that class the question becomes a convention about what a primary assembly is for; under analysis it splits into a QC-calibration question (how often are cutoffs mis-set) and a representation question, and haplotype-resolved hap1/hap2 deposition is removing the purged primary as an object | Only part dissolves: fixed duplicates purged by topology-based purging or mis-set cutoffs are errors under any convention, DToL/EBP still ship purged primaries at scale, and the instrument can separate the strata in principle — but the record declares no such split, so the question as written carries a definitional residue | Partial (all three)
Verification (post-batch, four fresh-context checkers, logs UQ-20261017-11-verification-purgedups.md, -guiglielmoni.md, -asmgene.md, -hemizygous.md): **the rejection does not stand.** Both legs of adversary 3's fatal attack-4 objection are unsupported as stated, the Gate 2 ground against it is weaker than claimed, and two of the entry's own prior characterisations were wrong in the candidate's favour. Verdict moves Rejected -> Provisional.
**Leg 1, the purge_dups mechanism.** The kill held that purge_dups only tests contigs below the haploid/diploid coverage transition, so a fixed young duplicate at diploid depth at each copy cannot be purged as a haplotig at all. Coverage gating is real and documented — the README says "Contigs with average coverage below mid coverage are tested for haplotypic duplications", and the paper's heterozygous-overlap path fires only when both contigs fall below the cutoff. But "cannot be removed at all" appears in neither the paper nor the README, and the code as relayed carries an alignment-only haplotig branch (`flt_by_bm_mm`, labelling HAPLOTIG from base-match and mismatch fractions with no coverage test), with the cutoff-index mapping unresolved because `opt.h` was not seen. The tool's own authors concede the failure mode the candidate asks about: dropping `get_seqs -e` "may delete false positive duplications"; of the middle-sequence removals, "Some of them are real, while others may not."; and purge_dups has "only a limited ability to explicitly handle repeats". hifiasm has a coverage ceiling (`--purge-max`: "If the coverage of a contig is higher than this bound, don't apply purge duplication") but its docs warn that a larger value "may collapse repeats or segmental duplications". The checker adds its own mechanism, labelled as its own: near-identical paralogs multi-map, so reads split between copies and each copy shows reduced depth, which can make a genuine duplicate look haplotig-like. purge_haplotigs could not be read. So a diploid-depth fixed duplicate is *unlikely* to be purged on the coverage-gated path, which is a real finding, but the sources do not rule it out and the tool's authors say real duplications can be deleted. A kill that cannot be sourced is Partial at best: **attack 4 drops from Unresolved to Partial.**
**Leg 2, the convention claim, is UNVERIFIED.** The kill also held that hemizygous copies moving to the alternate assembly is the haploid-reference convention rather than an error. Neither primary source could be opened: Rhie et al. 2021 (doi 10.1038/s41586-021-03451-1) failed by DOI and at nature.com, the EBP standards paper was never opened, and the NCBI glossary defines neither "primary assembly" nor "pseudohaplotype" — it defines only "alternate locus" and "linked pseudohaplotype assemblies". The 2020 bioRxiv preprint of Rhie et al. names false duplications as "one of the most common assembly errors" and describes purge_haplotigs removing "retained false duplicated contigs", but the word "hemizygous" does not appear and nothing read defines the relocation either as correct or as a loss. No standard read prescribes a target or acceptable false-removal rate, and no QC statistic is required for over-removal. Per the ledger's own rule this blocks Validated and names a promotion condition; it cannot reject.
**The Gate 2 ground is weaker than the adversary claimed.** Guiglielmoni et al. 2021 (doi 10.1186/s12859-021-04118-3) was indeed missed and is a relevant neighbour, but it is not the dedicated overpurging benchmark that falsifies the gap sentence. It runs on **one genome** (Adineta vaga, ~102 Mb haploid / 204.6 Mb diploid) with 7 assemblers and 3 purging tools, and purging is a near single-factor contrast only within each assembler and read set — the study also varies read filtering, technology and depth. Overpurging is measured **only** as Illumina k-mer completeness (KAT comp; "a lower value indicates that too many k-mers were lost (overpurging)"), with ~50% the target for a well-collapsed haploid assembly and the paper itself conceding that 50% could also come from a mix of missing and uncollapsed regions. There is **no reference genome or ground truth for genuine duplicates**, no annotation, and no gene-family or ortholog analysis; BUSCO is the only gene-content measure. It reports no fraction of genuine gene duplicates lost, and its one overpurging statement is that HaploMerger2 "seemed to overpurge assemblies of the filtered datasets". So it does not supply the candidate's estimand, and the metric-blindness reason for silence survives in narrowed form.
**Two of the entry's own characterisations were wrong, both in the candidate's favour, and are corrected.** First, the record claimed hifiasm's asmgene "publishes the candidate's limb-(a) fraction in weakened form". It does not. The figures are confirmed as printed in Table 2 — CHM13 76.9, HG00733 67.3, HG002 74.8 percent "multi-copy genes retained", against GRCh38 multi-copy cDNAs at >=99% identity — but the metric **pools assembler collapse, purge removal and genuine individual-versus-reference copy-number difference and cannot separate them**, and Table 2 contains **no same-sample purged-versus-unpurged pair**: CHM13 is a different, homozygous sample run without purging, while HG00733 and HG002 are heterozygous and purged. So no published figure answers limb (a) even weakly. Second, the record attributed to hifiasm the claim that purge_dups was dropped for badger and black rhino as "significantly worse". That passage is about **HiCanu**, not hifiasm, sits in Supplementary 1.2 and a Supp Table 3 caption, and carries no figures; the hifiasm Hi-C main text does not mention purge_dups. Both are struck and restated. The purge_dups paper's own evaluation (Guan 2020) scored BUSCO duplicated and complete on four Falcon-unzip assemblies and did not test whether removed sequence was genuine paralogs.
**Where it lands.** A fourth sweep found no publication measuring genuine gene copies lost to a haplotypic-duplication purging step with purging as the only varied factor — a bounded negative over 7 searches with HapSolo, PMC9516828, purge_dups issue 35 and the paftools asmgene source unopened. Novelty stays Medium. The entry is **Provisional**, capped by attack 7 (Reason for silence) Unresolved from two independent adversaries, which is non-fatal, and by well-posedness, which is raised from the judge's 1/3 to 2/3: the "two estimands under one name" charge survives the refutation of leg 2, because limb (a) as written does conflate removal-as-error with relocation-into-the-alternate-set, but that is one pre-registrable disambiguation rather than an unposable question.
**The proposed routing row is withdrawn.** It asked for the false-positive rate of haplotig purging on genuine duplicate gene copies, which is this entry's own limb (a); with the entry Provisional, the ledger is still claiming that question as un-asked, and routing rule (c) keeps a Provisional entry's own question out of the file.
Caveats recorded: every read in this pass went through the page summariser, so the code quotes and Table 2's column assignment (which the checker said it inferred from garbled headers) need checking against raw sources before citation; the arXiv preprints were read rather than the Nature Methods and Nature Biotechnology versions; Guiglielmoni's tables and figures were not seen; and doi.org returned HTTP 429 on one route.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3
Well-posedness 2/3 (the record self-scored 2/3, the batch judge cut it to 1/3 on the fatal attack 4, and verification restores it): the identity band, instrument floor and usable null are declared, and the mechanism presupposition is no longer shown false — "cannot be purged at all" appears in neither the purge_dups paper nor its README, the code carries an alignment-only HAPLOTIG branch with no coverage test, and the tool's authors concede the failure mode the candidate asks about ("may delete false positive duplications"; of the middle-sequence removals, "Some of them are real, while others may not."). What survives is that limb (a) as written does not name one estimand — it conflates purge-attributable error on fixed duplicates with relocation of hemizygous copies into the alternate set, and the canonical question stratifies by neither zygosity nor purge module — but that is one pre-registrable disambiguation, so it costs the third point rather than the second. Significance 2/3: audience evidenced and acting; consequence discounted because limb (b)'s generic answer and its correction are standard, part of the loss direction is already published all-causes and at k-mer level, and the headline framing presupposes the class the kill excludes.
Strongest remaining objection: Two of the three mechanisms the entry offers for the question's silence are contradicted by sources the adversaries opened, and the third does not explain silence. Loss-direction statistics do exist — Guiglielmoni's heterozygous-k-mer completeness was chosen precisely because it is two-sided ("a lower value indicates that too many k-mers were lost (overpurging)"), and asmgene's own "multi-copy genes missed" is a loss-direction metric the record cites as its priors 1–2 — and VGP deposits purged duplications as the alternate assembly instead of discarding them (Rhie et al. 2021 Methods), so the archiving mechanism fails too. Meanwhile purge_dups' issue tracker shows the weaker limb asked repeatedly with numbers attached (#42, literally "Optimise purging without losing too many genes", BUSCO C 97.0→95.3%; #43's "~200 of 350 Mb"; hifiasm #713 and #928). What remains — that answering is unrewarded and that no single discipline owns the statistic — explains neglect, not silence, and by the ledger's own rule a failed reason-for-silence makes the novelty finding itself suspect. Two of three independent adversaries graded this Unresolved, and it caps the entry independently of the attack-4 refutation.
Promotion requires: Validated needs (i) attack 7 resolved — either a reason the question went unposed that survives the two-sided metrics and the VGP alternate-assembly deposition, or an explicit concession that it is asked-but-unanswered in the practitioner literature, which would make it a routing case rather than an un-asked question and would reopen Gate 2; (ii) well-posedness raised to 3/3 by stratifying limb (a) by zygosity and pinning it to one purge module (hifiasm's default -l3/-s 0.55 is the version that survives, its documented coverage limit being an upper bound), and by naming the specific published gene-family analyses limb (b) is to re-estimate; and (iii) the Gate 2 record completed — Gate 4 found an on-point same-vocabulary neighbour (Guiglielmoni et al. 2021) that Gate 2 had reported absent, so Gate 5's "Medium novelty with the complete search record" is not yet satisfied whatever the attack statuses. Independently, the leg-2 convention claim is UNVERIFIED rather than refuted: Rhie et al. 2021 (doi 10.1038/s41586-021-03451-1) failed by DOI and at nature.com and the EBP standards paper was never opened, so whether relocating a hemizygous copy to the alternate assembly is a prescribed convention or an unmeasured loss is still unread, and reading either source could restore the fatal objection.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): re-pose it as the zygosity-stratified, module-specific question — purge-attributable removal of homozygous-duplicated gene copies under hifiasm's default -l3/-s 0.55 — and before any new work read the three unread sources that bear on it: HiCanu's main text and supplement (Genome Res 30:1291), purge_dups' Supplementary Note, and the HPRC Flagger supplement, plus Guiglielmoni et al. 2021 under the four-attribute test as prior 4.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): Not applicable — not rejected. The batch's draft row, for the false-positive rate of haplotig purging on genuine duplicate gene copies, is **withdrawn**: that is this entry's own limb (a), and with the entry Provisional the ledger is still claiming it as un-asked, which routing rule (c) excludes. Nothing from this entry goes to ledger/routed-open-problems.md. If attack 7 later resolves by conceding the question is asked-but-open, the row becomes routable — and that concession would also reopen Gate 2, so the two moves have to be made together, not separately.

ID: UQ-20261017-12
Date: 2026-10-17
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): Biology — preclinical animal behaviour / neuroscience phenotyping methodology (markerless pose estimation, behaviour classification). Method-owning neighbours: epidemiological measurement-error theory; econometrics of ML-generated variables; plant high-throughput phenotyping.

Question (canonical): For pre-declared automated phenotyping pipelines (>=2 pose estimators, >=2 behaviour classifiers) applied to >=3 manipulations that visibly change the animal's image (sedation/ataxia, diet-induced obesity, nerve or spinal injury, a coat-colour- or body-size-divergent line), with blinded multi-rater human labels at pre-registered per-group counts and restricted to behaviour categories with documented inter-rater reliability: (a) does per-group sensitivity/specificity (discrete behaviour calls) or the per-keypoint error distribution (pose) differ between treated and control animals under a pre-specified test of equality; and (b) where it does, how large is the bias in the pipeline's effect estimate after standard differential-misclassification correction, relative to that estimate's published confidence interval and to the assay's typical effect size? [Tightened at Gate 1, reformulation 1 of 1, well-posedness only. Intake version: "is pose and behaviour classification error independent of experimental group, and how large is the differential-measurement-error bias it imposes on reported effect sizes?"]

Alternative formulations:
1. Does an automated behaviour classifier's accuracy depend on the treatment the animal received, and if so, how much of a published behavioural effect is instrument error rather than behaviour?
2. What is the group-stratified error of automated phenotyping pipelines, and what bias does the field's implicit assumption of non-differential error impose on its effect estimates?

Motivating gap: Presupposition inversion on the claim that learned pipelines (DeepLabCut, SLEAP, MoSeq-class, commercial home-cage systems) made behavioural measurement objective. The instrument is a learned function of the animal's image and the manipulations under study change the image, so error may be differential by group — indistinguishable in the output from a real effect and invisible in the pooled accuracy figure the field reports. Gate 2 anchored the negative on Bhola & Yoo 2025 (systematic review, 67 rodent pose studies) reporting no group-stratified accuracy. GATE 4 WITHDREW THAT ANCHOR: two in-field sources reporting group-stratified instrument error were found (see priors P1, P2), so the gap as written ("no group-stratified accuracy anywhere") is false.

Presuppositions:
1. Blinded multi-rater human labels can serve as a per-group reference standard. [CONTESTED — and weakened further at Gate 4: MARS reports human pose annotation error is large and context-dependent ("only 52.3% fell within a 5mm radius of ground truth in front-view frames"; "quality of human pose annotation is a limiting factor"), so a differential reference standard is an identification problem, not only a precision ceiling. An IRR ceiling does not fix it.]
2. Group-stratified ground truth is obtainable at usable precision. [Established; pre-registered per-group label counts plus a power statement.]
3. Published studies do not already report group-stratified classifier error. [FALSE AS WRITTEN — refuted at Gate 4 by Geuther 2019 (coat-colour-stratified tracking error, main text) and MARS (stratified pose/classifier comparison for cabled vs uncabled videos). Survives only if reworded to "no study estimates per-group error for a biological *treatment* grouping of a learned pose/behaviour pipeline against blinded human labels and propagates it into the effect estimate" — a twice-narrowed residue.]
4. The induced bias is computable by standard measurement-error correction. [MISSPECIFIED for this regime — MARS documents classifier precision/recall rising with bout length, so error depends on the realized outcome, not only on group; per-group Se/Sp does not then identify the bias. Pose limb worse: a keypoint error distribution must propagate through a nonlinear feature pipeline into bout/syllable calls.]
5. Pooled training across groups reduces but does not equalise per-group error. [CONTESTED; part of what the question tests.]
6. The scored behaviours are defined well enough that "error" exists. [CONTESTED for soft ethogram categories; restricted to documented-IRR categories.]

What would count as an answer: Per-group sensitivity/specificity or per-keypoint error distributions for the pre-declared pipelines and manipulations on group-stratified blinded multi-rater labels; a pre-specified test of equality; and, where differential, a corrected effect estimate placed against the published estimate and the assay's typical effect size, with the IRR ceiling attached to every figure. Null branch informative: per-group differences bounded below the level that would move estimates beyond their CIs would license current pooled-validation practice.

Novelty — queries run (query -> one-line result): 11 at Gate 2 (web-search cap reached) + 6 WebFetch (cap 5, over-run self-reported, one returning only a doi.org redirect header); plus 26 further Disguise queries and 11 fetches across three Gate 4 adversaries. Full lists: batches/2026-10-17-0522/UQ-20261017-12-record.md and UQ-20261017-12-adversary-{1,2,3}.md. Most informative:
- Q5 (Gate 2) "hidden bias"/"systematic bias" automated behavioural phenotyping treatment-dependent tracking error -> surfaced Bhola & Yoo 2025 (opened; P3) and the eLife 63720 near-hit that Gate 2 then left unread.
- Q8 (Gate 2, mandated own-field own-words title query) automated behaviour classification less accurate in mutant/obese/aged animals than wild-type -> no paper of that form.
- Q7 (Gate 2, method-field) prediction-powered inference / ML-generated outcome variables -> Battaglia et al. arXiv:2402.15585 (opened); Assumption 2(iii) assumes prediction errors orthogonal to covariates and says relaxation is "straightforward" but does not develop it.
- A3-D2 (adversary 3) mouse tracking accuracy coat colour albino piebald strains neural network -> Geuther et al. 2019 (OPENED, bioRxiv 336685): the field's nearest prior, missed by Gate 2's own Q3 on the same axis.
- A2-D6 (adversary 2, Japanese-language) -> MARS / Segalin et al. (OPENED, bioRxiv 2020.07.26.222299 after elifesciences.org failed): the exact near-hit Gate 2 named and could not read, and it is a partial prior.

COULD NOT READ (no route attempted or cap exhausted; ground no grade either way): eLife reviewed preprint 95709; eNeuro ENEURO.0500-23.2024; von Ziegler, Sturman & Bohacek 2021 "Big behavior" (PMC-only link surfaced); Front. Behav. Neurosci. 2014;8:28 "Parameter optimization for automated behavior assessment" (doi.org redirect only); Geuther 2019 Supplementary Note 2 (strain-level breakdown); the spectrum-bias methodological framework.

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
P1. Segalin L, et al. "The Mouse Action Recognition System (MARS)..." eLife 2021;10:e63720. OPENED at https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2020.07.26.222299.full.pdf by adversary 2. Unit: video/frame, partitioned by apparatus (head-mounted microendoscope or fibre-photometry cable vs none). Endpoint: pose error and classifier precision/recall. Reference: blinded-irrelevant but multi-rater human annotation — pose by five individuals, behaviour by eight trained annotators, inter-annotator variability quantified. Estimand: per-partition classifier performance difference; reports "we do not observe a difference on individual videos with vs without cable when controlling for mean bout length", and "with longer behavior bouts leading to higher Precision and Recall values". No propagation into an effect estimate; its own use case 1 reports a BTBR genotype bout-length difference with no stratified check.
P2. Geuther BQ, et al. "Robust mouse tracking in complex environments using neural networks." Commun. Biol. 2019; OPENED at https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/336685v2 by adversaries 1 and 3. Unit: animal/frame grouped by coat colour across 58 strains. Endpoint: distance-travelled relative error. Reference: Ctrax baseline, plus visual inspection for the learned tracker ("visually checked mice from a majority of the strains... observed excellent performance" — no per-strain metric). Estimand: tracker error by coat colour; black/grey/piebald "errors less than 4%", albino 14%, "significantly higher levels of error"; and phenotype-dependent legacy-instrument artefact — waddle gait or hunched posture "led to abnormal beams breaks causing erroneously high total distances traveled"; discarding poorly tracked frames "can lead to biased sampling and skewed biological interpretation". No bias correction computed.
P3. Zhou Y, et al. "Identification and utilization of genetic determinants of trait measurement errors in image-based, high-throughput phenotyping." The Plant Cell 2021;33(8):2562-2582, DOI 10.1093/plcell/koab134. OPENED (publisher route) at https://academic.oup.com/plcell/article/33/8/2562/6279089. Unit: maize/sorghum genotype. Endpoint: automated-minus-manual trait error; downstream, the GWAS trait-associated-SNP set. Reference: single-operator manual measurement. Estimand: genetically controlled measurement bias and its effect on published results — "Trait measurement bias cannot be controlled by increasing population size and/or replication number"; "GDMB in automatically extracted trait values can greatly alter GWAS results", with no shared TASs between manual and automated GWAS. This is limbs (a)+(b) asked and answered affirmatively, one organism over.
Also recorded, not graded on: Bhola S, Yoo J-I. "Does advancement in marker-less pose-estimation mean more quality research? A systematic review." Front. Behav. Neurosci. 2025;19:1663089 (OPENED; corpus description, no meta-analysis, no estimand — the Gate 2 anchor that Gate 4 withdrew). Battaglia, Christensen, Hansen & Sacher, arXiv:2402.15585 (OPENED; the correction machinery, with the orthogonality assumption named and its relaxation declined). "Spectrum bias"/"spectrum effect" in clinical test evaluation (surfaced by all three adversaries, NOT opened).

Novelty — how this differs from each: vs P1 — same field, same instrument class, same multi-rater human reference, stratified equality check actually run, but on an apparatus partition rather than the biology under test, and no propagation; the candidate swaps the grouping covariate (implant/cable -> sedation, obesity, injury, coat colour). vs P2 — same field, one of the candidate's own listed manipulations (coat colour / body size), group-stratified error reported in main text, and a documented phenotype-dependent artefact inflating a behavioural readout, but at the tracking layer against a software baseline rather than a learned pose/classifier pipeline against human labels; the candidate swaps the instrument. vs P3 — the identical logical move with all four attributes different (plant genotype vs animal under randomised manipulation; continuous trait error vs discrete-call Se/Sp; single operator vs multi-rater; allelic effect/TAS set vs treatment effect); the candidate swaps the corpus. The residue genuinely unmeasured is: per-group Se/Sp of learned classifiers under biological treatments, propagated into a corrected effect estimate in rodents.

Novelty confidence: Low
Grounds for the downgrade from the record's Medium: the Medium rested explicitly on the negative being "anchored in an opened source (P2 = Bhola 2025)" rather than in query silence. Gate 4 destroyed that anchor from two opened in-field sources, and the record's own named top residual risk (eLife 63720) turned out on opening to be a partial prior. Each of the three swap types the gate rejects is now instantiated by a source someone opened: covariate swap on an asked-and-answered in-field question (P1), instrument swap on an asked-and-answered in-field question (P2), corpus swap on an asked-and-answered question (P3) — with the concept named and taught one field over ("spectrum bias") and the correction machinery already built (Battaglia et al.). A presupposition that must be narrowed twice, each time after a prior was found, is the signature of a known question being carved down to its unmeasured residue. Not graded Unverified: Disguise was executed (8, 9 and 9 queries by adversaries 1, 2, 3 respectively, all meeting the >=8 minimum), so this is a run check, not an unrun one.

Significance — consequence: Not reached as a verdict input (Rejected at Gate 2), and recorded as argued: if error is differential and correction moves the estimate beyond its CI, pooled keypoint error and pooled per-behaviour F1 stop being sufficient validation and per-group Se/Sp with a group-balanced label budget becomes the minimum claim; P3 shows the stakes are not theoretical (manual vs automated GWAS shared no SNPs). If bounded null, current practice is licensed by evidence and the bound becomes the citable number. Both branches change a practice.
Significance — audience: (i) behavioural-neuroscience and laboratory-animal-science methodologists, who mandate blinding against human observers and have no analogue for machine observers; (ii) tool groups controlling the validation template (DeepLabCut, SLEAP, B-SOiD, keypoint-MoSeq, MARS, BehaviorDEPOT) — evidenced as willing, since MARS already pays this cost for the apparatus partition; (iii) commercial home-cage and gait vendors; (iv) ARRIVE/NC3Rs/NIH rigour bodies; (v) statistical reviewers, who have the correction and nothing to plug into it.
Significance — fecundity: whether pooled training equalises per-group error; whether differential error is flaggable without new labels from per-frame confidence or residual group-predictability; group-balanced label-budget design; transfer to human digital phenotyping and livestock vision; whether some cross-lab behavioural irreproducibility is instrument-differential; the undeveloped relaxation of Battaglia et al.'s Assumption 2(iii).
Significance — anchoring: preclinical reproducibility and blinding; rodent lab-to-lab variability; the pose-estimation "pitfalls" strand (DeepLabCut primer, Horse-10/Horse-C); the plant GDMB precedent; ML-generated-variable inference.

Reason for silence: Mechanism 2 (inherited computer-vision validation culture — pooled held-out accuracy, adopted with the tool) survives and is the strongest, evidenced from opened sources: MARS asks "is my tool robust to my apparatus?" and answers it carefully while never asking whether its error correlates with the biology under test, even while reporting both the bout-length dependence and a genotype bout-length difference; JAABA's ground-truthing guidance recommends held-out pooled accuracy and never mentions condition; Geuther substitutes a visual check for a per-strain metric. Mechanism 3 (label budget flows to improving the model, not to auditing it symmetrically; a per-group breakdown can only make headline accuracy look worse) is corroborated by arXiv 2508.05138, a 2025 chronic-pain classifier paper with no manual annotation at all ("Since sampling time points correspond directly to pain types, no additional manual annotation is required"). Mechanism 1 (disciplinary boundary) should be DOWNGRADED: "spectrum bias" is taught in clinical test evaluation, preclinical neuroscience is adjacent to it, and the field already regulates human-observer blinding, so the conceptual bridge was short. Net: this is non-reporting of a known-about phenomenon, not non-asking — which per Gate 4 attack 7 returns the novelty finding itself to Gate 2, where it failed.

No attack is Unresolved from any adversary, so this is NOT a Gate 4 rejection. Disguise was executed by all three adversaries (8 / 9 / 9 queries, minimum 8), so Disguise is verified, not unverified, and the Rejection rests on a run check. The rejection is at Gate 2, on priors Gate 4 surfaced.

Verification (post-batch, three fresh-context checkers, logs UQ-20261017-12-verification-mars.md, -mars-full.md, -diffmeas.md): **the rejection stands**, and its central in-field claim is now confirmed verbatim rather than asserted — but one of its two supporting figures was mis-described, and what the candidate's second limb asks is confirmed to be done by nobody found.
**The MARS claim is confirmed, on the second attempt.** A first checker could not open the paper at all (elifesciences.org returns a JavaScript "Client Challenge") and found nothing of the kind in the Caltech repository excerpt it did reach, which left the judge's load-bearing claim unverified. The bioRxiv v1 preprint main text carries it for both stages. Pose: "the presence of a microendoscope or other cabled device only marginally affected the performance of pose estimation" (Fig 4B-C). Classifier: "We do not observe a difference on individual videos with vs without cable when controlling for mean bout length" (Extended Data Fig 7, test set 2). So MARS does ask the candidate's limb (i) under an implant-status grouping, against labels from multiple annotators, with bout length controlled — exactly as the Gate 2 regrade said. The support is qualitative: no cable/no-cable values, confidence intervals or p-values came through, and they would sit in Fig 4 and ED Fig 7, which were not read, as were the Methods, the supplements and the published eLife text. The paper's annotator agreement is reported against Human #1 as precision and recall — mounting 96.7+/-0.9 and 96.9+/-0.6, attack 83.7+/-1.3 and 86.2+/-2.5, close investigation 89+/-0.9 and 80.5+/-1.8, per-video F1 from 0.543 to 0.959 — and it states that "the mean annotator F1 score was well predicted by the mean bout duration of annotations in a video", which is the bout-length control's basis. The only other stratification is by view (annotators 86.2% within 5 mm top versus 52.3% front; MARS 92% versus 67%); there is no breakdown by coat colour, strain, lighting, camera or arena.
**The Geuther figures are real but mis-described, and the description is corrected.** The 14% and under-4% numbers are not tracking error by coat colour measured against ground truth. They are **relative error in total distance travelled**, from a comparison of Ctrax against the neural network, and they are confounded with the arena: "higher levels of error were seen in albino mice in the open-field arena with a white floor (14%)" against "showed errors less than 4%" for black, grey and piebald mice in the white open field, with black mice reported at 27% in the 24-hour arena and 10% in the KOMP2 arena. The paper separately reports IoU against hand annotation by environment group. So Geuther evidences group-stratified error in an automated behavioural read-out — which is what the kill needs — but not in the form the entry stated, and coat colour is not cleanly separable from arena.
**What nobody found does, recorded because it is the honest shape of the rejection.** Nine queries across the differential-measurement-error, post-prediction-inference, preclinical-reproducibility and automated-phenotyping vocabularies found **no paper that does both halves** of the candidate: neither MARS nor Geuther propagates a group-dependent error into a treatment-effect estimate, and no animal-behaviour application of the correction machinery was found. The general machinery exists and was read — Gronsbell et al. (arXiv:2411.19908) on inference with machine-learning-imputed data, and Wang, McCormick & Leek's post-prediction inference, which states that "we can no longer assume that the errors are independent of the predicted values" while fitting one observed-to-predicted relationship that does not vary by group — but its examples are structural biology, epidemiology and UK Biobank. An eNeuro 2026 DeepLabCut zebrafish paper varies imaging conditions, not experimental groups. That negative is bounded: about eight leads were unopened and two eLife reviewed preprints could not be read.
**Why the rejection still holds.** The entry is 3/3 well-posed and 3/3 significant, so Gate 2 is the whole of its rejection, and Gate 2's disguised-known rule bites on the structure rather than the exact measurement. Limb (i) is asked and answered in the candidate's own field under two groupings — implant status (MARS, verbatim above) and coat colour crossed with arena (Geuther) — and both limbs together are asked and answered one organism over in plant phenotyping (Zhou et al. 2021, The Plant Cell 33:2562, where genetically determined measurement bias is carried into a GWAS and the manual and automated analyses share no trait-associated SNPs). What remains is the same structure with the grouping swapped to an assigned manipulation, the instrument swapped to rodent pose pipelines and the correction swapped to differential-misclassification formulae. That is the covariate-instrument-corpus swap the gate rejects, and the entry already said so; verification's contribution is that the in-field half is now sourced instead of claimed, and that limb (ii) is confirmed unoccupied in animals, which is why this rejection is recorded as a close one rather than a clear one.
Not routed, unchanged: a disguised-known rejection is never routed. Recorded for a successor rather than routed, since no posing sentence was read at first hand: the second limb alone — given a measured group-dependent classifier error, what does a differential-misclassification correction do to a published preclinical effect size — which no source found addresses in animals and which does not inherit this entry's Gate 2 ground.
Caveats recorded: MARS was read as the bioRxiv v1 preprint main text through the page summariser, with no Methods, figures or supplements, so the two quoted sentences may differ from the published eLife text and no numbers back them; the Geuther figures came through a summariser from the Nature page rather than from the figure itself; and the claim that MARS nowhere discusses bias from group-differing error is "not found in the preprint main text", not established for the whole paper.

Scores: Well-posedness 3/3 · Significance 3/3

Strongest remaining objection: The strongest objection to the rejection itself — that the swap-chain was assembled from partial reads, and that no opened source has the candidate's estimand. P1's partition is an apparatus nuisance variable that MARS controls for rather than estimates an effect of, so it lacks the confounding structure that makes the candidate's question bite; P1 also returned a null, which weakens "already answered" as much as it weakens the candidate's premise. P2 stops at a classical tracker against a software baseline and explicitly substitutes a visual check for a per-strain metric of its learned model. P3 is a different organism, endpoint, reference and estimand. Against that, three plausibly decisive in-field items remain unread (von Ziegler, Sturman & Bohacek 2021 "Big behavior", a perspective piece in exactly this field and the most likely place the question is posed in print; Front. Behav. Neurosci. 2014;8:28 on automated-versus-manual agreement across conditions in the previous instrument generation; and Geuther 2019's Supplementary Note 2 strain-level breakdown), and either direction of their content would move this verdict — toward a firmer Rejection if the question is posed there, or toward Provisional if the swap-chain is all there is. A re-run that opened them, graded novelty afresh with P1 and P2 as nearest in-field priors, and re-specified limb (b) for outcome-dependent error would be a legitimate challenge to this Low.

Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): Not applicable to a rejected candidate. For the residue, if it is ever re-posed: stratify ground truth that already carries a condition tag (CalMS21-class benchmarks, the MARS annotation sets with their five pose and eight behaviour annotators, published B-SOiD and keypoint-MoSeq validation sets, gait and home-cage validation supplements) by condition and test equality at zero labelling cost — and specify the error model as outcome-dependent, not group-dependent, before any propagation.

Routing (if rejected as already-asked): NOT ROUTED. This is a disguised-known / already-answered rejection, not asked-but-open: the structure is asked and answered in the candidate's own field under other groupings (P1 apparatus partition, null; P2 coat colour, positive) and asked and answered in full one organism over (P3, positive), with the concept named in clinical test evaluation and the correction built in econometrics. Per ENVIRONMENT, answered and disguised-known rejections are not routed to ledger/routed-open-problems.md. No open posed question was found in the target field to route.
