PRIOR 2 (found at Gate 4, decisive for limb (a)) — Kato M, Nakagawa K. "Sequential Audit Sampling for Finite Populations with Exact and Simulation-based Guarantee." arXiv:2604.06116 (v1 opened at /abs and /html, the latter truncated at section 4.3 with no appendices; the v2 title cited here, the v2 abstract and the PDF all failed on proxy HTTP 429, so v2 and Appendix D.6 are attested through alphaxiv's summariser only — see Verification). Unit: the audited item in a finite population, binary deviation/nondeviation, sampled without replacement; endpoint: accept/reject against a tolerable deviation count; estimand: exact hypergeometric stopping boundaries with "sup over m<=m_H Pr(delta = K) <= alpha" and "sup over m>=m_K Pr(delta = H) <= beta", and "If no earlier decision is reached, the auditor inspects all n items and the terminal decision follows from the full count" — i.e. the sequential-with-escalation-to-full-count structure limb (a) asks for, with a CMS CERT claims illustration reported in Appendix D.6 (that appendix was never read; its presence rests on a third-party summary). Verified as far as the reading goes: the estimand is a deviation rate over binary indicators, an additive count, with no shrunken or hierarchical estimand anywhere in the material opened. PRIOR 3 — He Y, Selck F, Normand S-LT. "On the accuracy of classifying hospitals on their performance measures." Stat Med 2014;33(7):1081-1103, doi 10.1002/sim.6012 (abstract-level record opened). Unit: hospitals; endpoint: correct assignment to a quality tier; reference: unadjusted averages vs shrinkage and two posterior-probability estimators; estimand: expected classification accuracy under a one-way random-effects model. Supporting, opened at Gate 2: Garza MY et al. BMC Med Res Methodol 2022;22:227, doi 10.1186/s12874-022-01705-7 (unit = data field within a research QC case; endpoint = field-level error against the EHR; fixed 4.93%-per-10,000-fields acceptability threshold, escalation of three further cases, no decision anywhere); HQIP "Detection and management of outliers for national clinical audits" (unit = provider; endpoint = alert at 2SD / alarm at 3SD; no audit-risk estimand); Illinois APORS QC 19:03 re-abstraction report (152 cases, per-field accuracy only); CMS FY27 IQR validation webinar (design verified, above). Nearest in object, verified at intake and not re-opened: Shen, Wadhera, Yeh, JAMA Cardiol 2021.
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs PRIOR 1 (Haviari 2019) — this is the kill. Same unit (hospital), same error source (human re-reading of the record, here coded comorbidities rather than a process-measure numerator), same propagation (documented disagreement carried through to the hospital's position), same decision object (league-table position and a simulated pay-for-performance programme), and a published cohort fraction. The differences are an estimand substitution and a wrapper: Haviari reports the fraction changing rank and the budget misallocated, not the fraction needing >50% re-abstraction to confirm at alpha = 0.05, and Haviari's 30 records per hospital are a fixed sample with no stopping rule and no risk limit [UNVERIFIED on the body: two passes reached the abstract only, and abstract silence is not body silence. The direction is favourable to the kill either way — a stopping rule in the body would pre-empt the candidate further]. Under this ledger's own rule that is a covariate-and-estimand swap on an asked and answered question, not a new question — and it falsifies the two claims the Medium grade rested on (that only sampling noise had been quantified, and that no such fraction was published). vs PRIOR 2 (Kato & Nakagawa 2026) — for any additive measure, limb (a) reduces to instantiating this paper: define a deviation as an adverse re-abstraction flip and the tolerable count as the case margin to threshold, and the exact hypergeometric boundaries plus escalation to the full count give the alpha guarantee directly (the adversary labels this its own derivation, not the source's claim; ignoring favourable flips only makes escalation likelier, so the rule is conservative). SEP-1, the record's own named test case, is such a measure. vs PRIOR 3 (He 2014) — genuinely distinct on reference and estimand (estimator choice under sampling and between-hospital variance, averaged over hospitals; silent on measurement error) and contains no sampling rule; but it no longer matters, because the candidate is killed in front of it. vs Garza 2022, HQIP, Illinois APORS, CMS IQR validation — all remain evidence FOR a gap in audit DESIGN, none is prior art on the question; the gap they evidence is now the method field's, not medicine's. WHAT SURVIVES UNCLAIMED: a margin statistic, and hence an audit, for shrunken non-additive risk-standardised estimators — not held by Haviari, Kato or the RLA literature.
Novelty confidence: Low (downgraded at Gate 4 from the record's Medium; the record's own grounds for not awarding High — "one substitution away from a live literature", and three method-bearing sources unopened — named exactly the configuration in which the miss occurred)
Significance — consequence: Unchanged as argued, and partly realised rather than hypothetical: Haviari 2019 already published the large-fraction result (60-70% of hospitals reordered, 6.5-7.3% of a P4P budget misallocated) and recommended centralised re-coding of random samples. What a stated-risk design would add is an escalation obligation and a defensible appeal, not the finding that abstraction error moves decisions. For the surviving non-additive limb the consequence stands: if no margin statistic exists, threshold payment on shrunken estimates is unauditable in the risk-limiting sense, which bears on measure construction and sharpens the reliability/minimum-volume debate.
Significance — audience: Real and correctly named (CMS IQR/HVBP/HRRP validation contractors; NCQA HEDIS compliance auditors; HQIP and CQC; hospital IRR programmes; health-measurement statisticians; the RLA and audit-sampling community), but their appetite is now evidenced against: CMS validation exists to police submission accuracy for the Annual Payment Update, validates only Sepsis among chart-abstracted measures, is scored at measure level with no link to any payment threshold, and has no provision for expanding a sample (verified); and Haviari's strong numbers plus explicit recommendation produced no risk-limiting audit in seven years. The audience that would act is the audit-sampling/RLA community, on the non-additive residue.
Significance — fecundity: Measure design for auditability (which constructions admit a margin under shrinkage); risk-limiting audit theory for non-additive model-based functionals, including confidence sequences on a shrunken estimator of audited units; margin-based allocation of a fixed national audit budget; audit-deterrence effects on discretionary element entry; the eCQM, clinician-entered and AI-assisted-abstraction versions, where the error model is a model property specifiable in advance. All of these remain open; all of them now sit in the method field.
Significance — anchoring: Shen 2021's misclassification finding; Haviari 2019's audit-and-reorder finding; the reliability and minimum-volume debate in hospital profiling; SEP-1 abstraction variability (Rhee et al.); CMS star-rating methodology controversy; HQIP/CQC outlier management, where the blank is documented in the guidance itself; and, on the method side, risk-limiting audits for social-choice and estimation rules that are not plurality tallies.
Reason for silence: Claimed mechanism was a disciplinary boundary plus an incentive gap plus a technical delay. The boundary and incentive arguments survive for the audit-design WRAPPER — CMS's measure-level fixed-n design and HQIP's calendar escalation are consistent with nobody wanting an escalation obligation, and Kato 2026 shows even the audit-sampling field has only now formalised exact finite-population sequential tests. They do NOT explain silence on the question, because there was no silence: the health field did ask whether record-review disagreement moves hospitals' ranking and P4P status, and answered it (Haviari 2019). Per Gate 4 attack 7, a reason-for-silence that explains only the vocabulary and not the question is a signal that the novelty finding was the artefact.
Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status): One adversary (fresh context, Gate 0-3 record only); verbatim log in batches/2026-10-17-0742/UQ-20261017-18-adversary-1.md. Disguise WAS executed: 8 of 8 required new-vocabulary queries (German external QA, accounting attribute sampling, Medicare Advantage RADV, clinical-coding/registry audit, NCQA HEDIS, clinical-trial risk-based monitoring, finite-population sequential testing, SEP-1 answer-side), plus 1 verification query, so Disguise is verified, not unverified.
1. Triviality | for the record's own named test case SEP-1 — an unadjusted compliance proportion — each chart moves the numerator by at most one case, so the per-case bound the record calls contested holds by construction, and Kato & Nakagawa 2026 (opened) already supply the exact finite-population sequential test with escalation to the full count; adversary's own derivation sets deviation = adverse re-abstraction flip, tolerable count = case margin to threshold | the shrunken risk-standardised measures (HRRP, mortality, star ratings) are not additive, and there neither the margin nor the bound is in Kato or in the RLA literature | Partial — the additive half (which the record proposes to start with) is trivial; the non-additive half is not
2. Disguise | in clinical-coding vocabulary, Haviari et al. 2019 (opened) re-abstracts a random sample per hospital, propagates the documented disagreement through a hierarchical model to hospital ranking and a simulated P4P programme, and reports 70.3%/61.5% of hospitals changing position and 6.5%/7.3% of budget misallocated — limb (b) asked and answered in kind, falsifying both the motivating gap and the mandatory "what fraction" negative; the residue, a sequential finite-population test with escalation, is Kato 2026's object down to a CMS illustration | the canonical estimand (fraction needing >50% re-abstraction at alpha = 0.05) is not Haviari's, Haviari has a fixed 30-record sample with no stopping rule or risk limit [UNVERIFIED on the body; see Verification], and Haviari's elements are risk-model covariates rather than a process-measure numerator | Unresolved — true but reducing the candidate to "Haviari's question + Kato's procedure"; the novelty argument actually made is defeated by an opened paper one vocabulary step away
3. Combinatorial novelty | audit sampling x hospital measures: for additive measures there is no interface problem (Kato illustrates on CMS claims); for shrunken measures the interface problem is real but belongs to sequential-testing theory, as the record's own routing field concedes | the non-additive case is a real open problem and the health programme is the only place it has a decision consequence | Partial
4. Presupposition failure | (i) "only sampling noise has been quantified" is false (Haviari 2019); (ii) bounded per-case perturbation is uncontested for additive measures, so the record overstates; (iii) HVBP/HRRP payment is a continuous function of the score (adversary's recalled claim, explicitly NOT verified, grounds nothing); (iv) the CMS fixed-n agreement-scored pay-for-reporting description is VERIFIED and stands | the canonical form scopes to single-measure thresholds and makes the bounded-perturbation issue part of the question; (i) is a flaw in the motivating gap rather than in the question text | Partial
5. Vagueness | limb (b)'s number is a property of the pre-registered error model, alpha and the arbitrary 50% cutoff as much as of the world, and "no margin statistic exists" lets any outcome count | pre-registration makes it reproducible given the model; the record flags this itself | Partial
6. Significance inflation | CMS validation (verified) polices submission accuracy for the APU, covers only Sepsis among chart-abstracted measures, is measure-level, and cannot expand a sample; and Haviari's 60-70% reordering plus 6.5% misallocation and an explicit recommendation produced no risk-limiting audit | HQIP guidance documents a blank, and HEDIS's "materially biased" determination shows a decision-flavoured audit concept already in use (title-level only) | Partial
7. Reason for silence | the disciplinary boundary explains the wrapper but not the question: the health field asked and answered the substantive limb, so the silence covers only the risk-limit dressing | the incentive-gap argument is coherent and consistent with CMS's measure-level fixed-n design | Partial
8. Dissolution | for additive measures the question dissolves into applying Kato/RLA; for shrunken measures into "define the margin", since a hospital's shrunken estimate depends on the pooled fit and on cut-points set by other hospitals, making the answer a property of the model | the target is definable (re-abstract this hospital, hold the rest fixed, refit); non-additivity is a difficulty, not an incoherence | Partial
Verification (post-batch, three fresh-context checkers, logs UQ-20261017-18-verification-haviari.md, -haviari2.md and -kato.md): **Rejected stands, and the one claim verification could not settle is one whose falsification would only deepen the rejection.**
**Haviari was never read beyond its abstract, by either checker.** Twelve fetch attempts across two passes reached the publisher's abstract page three times and nothing further: the .full suffix gave abstract-level content only, .full.pdf and .full-text errored, the hal.inserm.fr and hal.science records returned an Anubis "Access Denied" bot wall, a library proxy copy and ouci.dntb.gov.ua gave abstract and metadata, and Europe PMC was robots-disallowed. What the abstract carries is confirmed, and it is enough for the kill: 24 hospitals, 70,402 discharge abstracts over the 78 deadliest DRGs in one year, "Thirty random stays per hospital were then recoded by two central reviewers" from full medical records, comorbidity PPV 64.4-96.4% and NPV 88.0-99.9%, 70.3% of hospitals changing league-table position under Elixhauser and 61.5% under Charlson, 6.5% (SD 3.6) and 7.3% (SD 4.0) of the pay-for-performance budget misallocated, and a conclusion recommending correction "using a centralised coding strategy from a random sample of observations". One arithmetic discrepancy is unresolved: 24 hospitals at 30 stays each is 720, and the abstract says 715 were recoded; the body may explain it and the body was not read.
**The claim this entry cannot support is the one that favours the candidate.** This entry twice states that Haviari's 30 records per hospital are a fixed sample with no stopping rule and no risk limit. The second checker insists, correctly, that the abstract's silence on a sequential rule, a risk limit or an audit-depth computation is not evidence that the body is silent, and that a review must not write "the paper is silent" on that basis. The statement is therefore UNVERIFIED on the body, and is marked so where it appears. Note which way it cuts: it is this entry's own *difference* from Haviari, the thing that stops the candidate being a pure duplicate. If the body did contain a stopping rule or a stated risk limit, the candidate would be more thoroughly pre-empted, not less. The rejection is robust to the unread body in both directions, which is why the verdict does not move.
**Kato is confirmed additive-only and must not be cited for the shrunken case — which is what this entry already says.** The arXiv landing page shows only v1 (7 April 2026), titled "Sequential Audit Sampling with Statistical Guarantees"; the v2 abstract and the PDF both failed on proxy HTTP 429, and the HTML rendering of v1 truncated at section 4.3 with no appendices visible. Confirmed in v1's own HTML: "the number of observed deviations follows a hypergeometric law". Attested only through alphaxiv's summariser and not read at first hand: the v2 title this entry cites, the escalation sentence "If no earlier decision is reached, the auditor inspects all n items.", the alpha/beta framing of the two incorrect sampling conclusions, and the CMS CERT illustration this entry places in Appendix D.6 — that appendix's content beyond tables and figures was never read. Decisively, as far as the reading goes: the estimand is a deviation rate over binary indicators, an additive count, and no shrunken or hierarchical estimand appears anywhere in the material opened, while a targeted search for shrinkage or hierarchical treatments in the risk-limiting-audit literature returned titles only. So Kato supports limb (a) for additive measures, as this entry has it, and supplies nothing for the non-additive residue — confirming the residue is genuinely unclaimed.
**Where it lands. Rejected, unchanged, and the residue stays unrouted.** The ground is that limb (b) was asked and answered in clinical-coding vocabulary (Haviari) and that limb (a), for the additive measure the record proposes to start with, instantiates an existing exact finite-population sequential test (Kato). Both rest on material that was read, and verification disturbed neither. The unclaimed non-additive residue is confirmed unclaimed, and it is correctly not routed: routing carries questions somebody has posed and nobody has answered, and no source in this record poses the margin statistic for shrunken risk-standardised estimators. Caveats for anyone citing this entry: every Haviari figure is abstract-level, the 715-versus-720 discrepancy is open, and Kato's v2 title and Appendix D.6 rest on a third-party summary.

Scores: Well-posedness 3/3 · Significance 3/3 as graded at Gate 3 (well-posedness survives Gate 4 — attacks 4, 5 and 8 all closed Partial, not Unresolved; significance is not re-scored because the entry fails on novelty, but attack 6's evidence that a stronger published result moved no programme would support 2/3)
Strongest remaining objection: The question is a disguised known. Its empirical limb was asked and answered in clinical-coding vocabulary by Haviari et al. 2019 — re-abstraction of a random sample per hospital, propagated to risk-adjusted ranking and to a simulated pay-for-performance allocation, with 70.3% of hospitals changing position and 6.5% of the budget misallocated — and its procedural limb, for the additive measure the record itself proposes to start with, is an instantiation of Kato & Nakagawa's exact finite-population sequential audit test with escalation to the full count. Changing the estimand to audit depth at a stated risk limit, and the data elements from coded covariates to a process-measure numerator, is a covariate-and-estimand swap on an asked question, which this ledger rejects even where the exact variant is unmeasured. The strongest case against this verdict, recorded so it is not lost: the residue is genuine and unclaimed — no margin statistic, and hence no risk-limiting audit, exists for shrunken non-additive risk-standardised estimators — but that is a sequential-testing problem in the method field, not an un-asked question in medicine, and it is where the live part of this candidate belongs.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): For the surviving non-additive residue, first obtain and read Haviari 2019's hierarchical correction and Kato & Nakagawa's hypergeometric boundaries side by side — noting that neither full text yielded to any route tried here, so this step starts with document delivery rather than analysis — to establish whether a shrunken risk-standardised estimate admits any assorter-style bounded contribution per audited chart; if it does not, the question to pose is the non-existence one, in the audit-sampling literature.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): NOT routed to routed-open-problems.md — this is an answered / disguised-known rejection, not an asked-but-still-open one, and the LEDGER routes neither. For the record: limb (b) belongs to health-services methodology (the Duclos/Haviari line on data-validation audit and P4P); the unclaimed non-additive limb (a) belongs to audit-sampling / RLA theory (Kato & Nakagawa 2026; SHANGRLA-style assorters for non-additive functionals), and would be a candidate for that field's own open-problem list rather than this ledger's.

---
ID: UQ-20261017-19
Date: 2026-10-17
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): Medicine — clinical pharmacology, pharmaceutical supply/health systems (target field). Adjacent: stability science, regulatory science, supply-chain informatics.

Question (canonical): Using package- and lot-level provenance recorded by serialized drug track-and-trace (GS1/EPCIS under US DSCSA or EU FMD), for a product set pre-specified before any data pull: (i) in a real serialization-to-dispensing linkage held by one large dispenser, wholesaler or regulator, what are the distributions of manufacture-to-dispensing interval, remaining labelled shelf life at dispensing, and custody-path length / cumulative per-step dwell time, by product and dispensing channel (retail, mail-order, hospital, 340B/specialty), and how much of their variance is within product-and-manufacturer rather than between (a pre-registered within-product ICC declared in advance as the gate on limbs ii-iii); (ii) for products passing that gate, does measured potency (assay % label claim and dissolution, USP/Ph.Eur. monograph as reference) in retrieved patient-held or returned units vary with remaining shelf life and cumulative dwell time, with batch identity as a random effect so the estimand is the within-batch provenance slope rather than between-batch quality; (iii) for any product with a named, routinely measured potency-sensitive endpoint pre-specified at protocol stage, what is the cohort association between those provenance variables and that endpoint, channel and patient mix adjusted?
(Gate 1 V2; the single permitted reformulation is spent. V1 and what the reformulation changed: see batches/2026-10-17-0742/UQ-20261017-19-record.md.)

Alternative formulations:
- How old is the medicine when the patient actually gets it, how much does that vary between products and channels, and does the variation matter clinically?
- Treating the distribution chain as an uncontrolled exposure now made visible by serialization, can per-package provenance be linked to potency assays and patient outcomes to test whether "within expiry" is a sufficient statement of product quality?

Motivating gap: Interoperable package-level serialization was built for anticounterfeiting and, as a by-product, makes per-package provenance (manufacture date, custody steps, dwell times) queryable at national scale. Stability testing and expiry dating certify potency under labelled storage for a BATCH; the realised exposure of an individual package was unmeasurable before serialization and is still uncontrolled. Expiry is treated as binary and no body joins provenance to potency or outcome. Status caveat: the record's recalled DSCSA/FMD dates were unverified at Gate 2; adversary 1 then opened FDA's "Waivers and exemptions beyond stabilization period" page — in force for manufacturers, repackagers, wholesalers and non-small dispensers, small dispensers exempt to 27 Nov 2027 — so the data exist at scale, but the page states nothing about data elements.

Presuppositions: (1) serialized provenance retrievable at research scale and linkable to a dispensing record — CONTESTED, the main feasibility risk, and still evidenced only by a vendor page; (2) manufacture date, lot and remaining shelf life captured at dispensing — PARTLY ESTABLISHED (DSCSA ends at dispenser receipt and carries no manufacture date; EU NMVS decommissions packs at supply with no patient link — adversary 1, recall, unsourced); (3) some products' potency varies measurably within labelled shelf life or with realised distribution exposure — CONTESTED, deliberately not assumed; (4) patient-held or returned units retrievable for assay in number — CONTESTED; (5) at least one product has a potency-sensitive endpoint measurable in routine data — CONTESTED and still UNNAMED, the load-bearing weakness; (6) provenance not simply collinear with product, manufacturer and channel — CONTESTED, and converted into limb i's pre-declared gate rather than assumed.

What would count as an answer: Limb i — published distributions (median, IQR, tails) of the three provenance quantities by product and channel from a real serialization-to-dispensing linkage, with a within-product variance component. Limb ii — assay and dissolution of retrieved patient-held/returned units for the pre-specified products, stratified by remaining shelf life and cumulative dwell time, batch as random effect, monograph limits as reference. Limb iii — a cohort estimate of a named potency-sensitive endpoint on those provenance variables. A null answers the question: provenance explaining nothing beyond expiry status would defend current binary expiry practice at population scale and bound what provenance-aware rotation could buy.

Novelty — queries run (query -> one-line result): 29 recorded queries in all (Gate 2: 11 searches + 5 fetches, caps reached; adversary 1: 9 searches + 4 fetches; adversary 2: 9 new-vocabulary searches + 4 fetches). Full lists and per-query results: batches/2026-10-17-0742/UQ-20261017-19-record.md, -adversary-1.md, -adversary-2.md. Most informative:
- "DSCSA serialization data secondary use research analytics product dwell time supply chain visibility pharmaceutical" -> vendor material only (TraceLink, LSPedia); no research-scale analytic study. Confirms the data-holder/method-holder split.
- "EPCIS event data analytics dwell time pharmaceutical supply chain research study traceability patient outcomes linkage" [method-owning field] -> Solanki & Brewster linked pedigrees (prior C); method field builds the plumbing and computes no provenance epidemiology.
- "medicine quality survey assayed API content versus time since manufacture remaining shelf life substandard samples association" -> the medicine-quality survey genre; the record's named open novelty risk (Ghana, Malawi), PMC-blocked at Gate 2. [Closed on verification: the Ghana survey was opened by the UGSpace repository PDF and the Hindawi article page and runs no assay-on-age regression — see Verification.]
- [adv 2, answer-search, publisher route] "antimalarial post-marketing surveillance assay content association time since manufacture months regression sample level Malawi Ghana" -> Malawi PMS opened: manufacture and expiry dates collected, confined to Additional file 1 "not related to the results", no assay-on-age regression. Closes half the record's novelty risk in the candidate's favour.
- [adv 2, DoD stockpile vocabulary] "Shelf Life Extension Program stability profiles ... potency lots testing" -> Lyon et al. 2006 (122 products, 3005 lots, 88% extended >=1 yr, mean 66 months, "highly variable"); the record's unsearched anchor, and now the sharpest pressure on presupposition 3.
- [adv 1, regulatory vaccinology] "vaccine 'time since manufacture' ... immunogenicity seroconversion lot field study" -> NCT05101486, an "end-of-shelf-life" clinical consistency study: limb iii's generic form, asked per product under controlled ageing, with no realised provenance.
- [adv 1 and adv 2, German pharmacy practice] "Restlaufzeit Arzneimittel bei Abgabe Apotheke Studie" -> German practice names the object ("Kurzlaeufer") and regulates minimum remaining shelf life at dispensing, with no measured distribution behind the rule.
Ledger duplicate check: INDEX.md read in full (115 entries); nearest is UQ-20261016-27 (vaccine lot-identity random intercepts -> outcome), which shares limb iii's design idiom but not its exposure. No duplicate or near-duplicate.
Disguise execution: both adversaries ran their sweeps (8 and 9 new vocabularies, 8 publisher/repository pages opened between them). Disguise is verified-as-run, not unverified.

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
A. Gachara G et al., "Potency status of oral polio virus vaccine among retrieved field samples in Kenya," Int J Infect Dis 2014;21(S1):441 — https://ir-library.ku.ac.ke/items/8fc22812-19f7-4dcd-ad7b-c4517edcf1c7 . Unit: vial (23 TOPV vials, 69 serotype samples). Endpoint: log CCID50 titre. Reference: a "standard" mean titre. Estimand: descriptive mean titre by serotype plus an unquantified association with VVM stage. Not re-opened by either adversary; title/venue consistent.
B. "Quality evaluation of selected expired fluoroquinolones medicines ... Jimma zone, Ethiopia," Front Med 2024;11:1420146 — https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/medicine/articles/10.3389/fmed.2024.1420146/full . Unit: batch (7 batches). Endpoint: assay % label claim, 30-min dissolution. Reference: USP limits. Estimand: proportion of expired batches meeting specification. Re-opened and verified by adversary 2: the collection form "was designed to capture the date of manufacturing, and the date of expiration", those dates sit in supplementary files, and no analysis against assay was run.
C. Solanki M, Brewster C, "EPCIS Event-Based traceability in pharmaceutical supply chains via automated generation of linked pedigrees," ISWC 2014, LNCS 8796:82-97 — https://research.aston.ac.uk/en/publications/epcis-event-based-traceability-in-pharmaceutical-supply-chains-vi/ . Unit: EPCIS event/stream window. Endpoint: pedigree-generation efficiency. Estimand: computational throughput. No quality, potency or outcome endpoint.
Added by the adversaries (near-priors, not displacing A-C): Chiumia FK et al., PLOS ONE 2022;17(12):e0279637 (293 Malawi samples, 14.3% substandard; "batch numbers, expiry date, and stated manufacturer were collected from the labeling", none analysed as a time variable); Malawi antimalarial PMS, Malar J 2015 (doi 10.1186/s12936-015-0637-z; "wide variations in API content within batches", failures attributed to "improper handling during storage or distribution" with no provenance variable measured); Lyon RC et al., J Pharm Sci 2006, doi 10.1002/jps.20636 (SLEP, abstract only); Bekker CL et al., Int J Clin Pharm 2018;40(3):704-711 (remaining shelf life only as a ">= 6 months" redispensing threshold; 19.1% eligible); NCT05101486 (end-of-shelf-life immunogenicity).

Novelty — how this differs from each: vs A — same inferential shape (retrieved field units assayed against a distribution-exposure variable) but A's exposure is a thermal indicator with no provenance attached, 23 vials of one thermolabile product, and its estimand is a mean titre, not a within-batch provenance slope; no channel contrast, no dwell time, no serialized linkage. vs B — B is the genre the candidate is posed against: unit = batch, exposure = expiry as a binary, reference = monograph pass/fail; the candidate's exposure is a continuous realised-provenance vector within labelled shelf life at package level, with batch as a random effect. B held the provenance fields and analysed none, which instantiates the claimed silence. vs C — same data object, no epidemiological question: endpoint is pedigree generation, estimand computational throughput. vs the adversaries' additions — SLEP ages whole lots with no provenance variable and no channel contrast (its storage regime is UNVERIFIED: no source read states Lyon 2006's storage conditions, so the "controlled depot storage" characterisation is recall); end-of-shelf-life trials age one lot per product under controlled conditions, so they answer "does aged product work" and not "does realised provenance predict delivered quality"; Malawi/Chiumia attribute to distribution without measuring it; Bekker and procurement minima are binary thresholds, not distributions.

Novelty confidence: Medium. Twenty-nine queries across clinical pharmacology, medicine-quality surveillance, LMIC procurement, cold chain/vaccinology, food-science shelf life, supply-chain informatics, DoD stockpile, operations research/perishable inventory, transfusion medicine, medicines-returns, EPI/eLMIS, German and Turkish national-traceability vocabularies returned nothing joining per-package serialized provenance to potency or outcome, and the method-owning field's own paper (C) states the gap in its own words. Adversary 2's publisher-route open of the Malawi PMS closed the record's single named novelty risk in the candidate's favour. Held below High because one neighbour remains close in logic (cold-chain-exposure-to-potency, A; plus the end-of-shelf-life trial genre the record never considered) and, as graded at Gate 4, because the Ghana children's-medicines survey was then unread — that second ground is discharged on verification: the survey was opened by repository and publisher route and runs no sample-level assay-on-age regression, so the risk that would have moved limb ii to Low does not materialise, and novelty is now held at Medium by the remaining neighbour alone.

Significance — consequence: If provenance predicts potency or a potency-sensitive endpoint within labelled shelf life, expiry dating stands revealed as a lossy summary of a now-measurable per-package quantity, arguing for shortened dating where distribution tails are long, or for managing remaining shelf life at dispensing (FEFO at the patient interface, channel-specific limits), and making serialized provenance the first routinely collected population-scale covariate for product quality. If not, binary expiry practice is defended with direct population-scale evidence rather than batch-level inference, retiring a standing worry (mail-order heat, long dwell, near-expiry dispensing) that currently generates journalism and local policy without measurement. Limb i alone yields a number nobody has, and the opened sources show the decisions it would inform are currently made on bare thresholds (Bekker's ">= 6 months"; German Kurzlaeufer rules; LMIC contract minima).

Significance — audience: regulators setting stability and dating policy (FDA OPQ/CDER, EMA QWP, ICH stability revision); pharmacopoeial bodies (USP, Ph.Eur.) on whether monograph limits should be checked at the patient end; hospital and chain-pharmacy quality units, PBMs and mail-order operators, who set rotation and shipping rules with no quality endpoint to optimise against; WHO prequalification and LMIC procurement, where minimum remaining shelf life at delivery is already a contract term set by convention; serialization data holders and DSCSA governance bodies, for whom this is the first non-compliance use of the asset. A non-null limb ii changes rotation and channel rules; a non-null limb iii is what would move a guideline; a null is usable by the parties already paying for shelf-life terms.

Significance — fecundity: is labelled expiry the most informative single statistic a package can carry, versus a provenance-conditioned remaining-potency estimate? Does channel heterogeneity create a quality inequity (mail-order in hot climates, rural long tails, 340B/specialty)? Can serialized provenance run as a routine quality-surveillance stream with signal detection on dwell-time anomalies? Should stability protocols be re-weighted from label conditions to the measured realised-exposure distribution? Is dwell-time variation an instrument for delivered dose?

Significance — anchoring: expired-drug-potency and SLEP findings (now sourced: Lyon 2006); substandard-and-falsified-medicines burden estimates, where "degraded" is the hardest category to attribute and Malawi/Jimma attribute to distribution without measuring it; lot-to-lot outcome variation (ledger UQ-20261016-27); cold-chain integrity and VVM practice (A); unexplained variance in narrow-therapeutic-index products where delivered content is assumed exact.

Reason for silence: NEW INSTRUMENT crossed with a DISCIPLINARY BOUNDARY and an INCENTIVE GAP — as graded by both adversaries, the boundary limb survives and the new-instrument limb is partly refuted. Boundary (evidenced by three opened papers): investigators who held the variable did not form the question — Jimma designed its form to capture manufacture and expiry dates and analysed neither against assay; Malawi PMS put them in Additional file 1 "not related to the results" while attributing failures to "improper handling during storage or distribution"; Chiumia 2022 collected batch, expiry and manufacturer and tested none as a time variable. The field owning the DATA has tracing and recall questions and no quality-science estimand (C's endpoint is pedigree throughput); the field owning the METHOD has the estimand and no access. Incentive: the data are commercially confidential and an in-expiry subpotency finding implicates a named manufacturer, wholesaler and channel; the reception of the Carter & Heinemann insulin result (immediate contestation, replication funded by third parties) is the visible instance. New instrument: holds for custody path, dwell time and population-scale linkage, but NOT for product age or remaining shelf life, which have been computable from printed carton dates for decades — for that limb the better explanation is presumed irrelevance (within expiry = within specification by construction), which is the dissolution objection rather than a boundary.

Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status) — two independent fresh-context adversaries; status below is the stricter of the two, with each adversary's own grade noted. Verbatim logs: batches/2026-10-17-0742/UQ-20261017-19-adversary-1.md and -adversary-2.md.
1 | Triviality | Limb ii is bounded a priori by stability design (shelf life is set so a batch stays in specification through expiry), and SLEP measured the margin: 122 products / 3005 lots, 88% extended >=1 year, mean 66 months; limb i(b) is readable off the printed expiry date and is already a German dispensing rule. | Limb i is not derivable from any opened source — the nearest published quantities are binary thresholds (Bekker's ">= 6 months", 19.1% eligible; procurement minima), not distributions or variance components; SLEP has no provenance variable and its own abstract calls the extension "highly variable" (its regime, described here as controlled depot storage, is UNVERIFIED — see Verification); the a-priori bound is on expected effect, not realised effect, and a population-scale null is itself the answer claimed. | Partial (adv 1 Partial — the stability-design bound is recall, ICH Q1A/Q1E not opened; adv 2 Resolved)
2 | Disguise | Known question renamed: regulatory vaccinology's "end-of-shelf-life" clinical consistency study (NCT05101486) is limb iii per product; diabetes technology's pharmacy-purchased insulin assay (Carter & Heinemann 2018) is limb ii's premise; medicine-quality surveillance's "factors associated with poor quality" (Chiumia 2022) is the same; transfusion medicine has asked product-age-at-administration vs outcome for decades; OR treats remaining shelf life at issue as its central variable. | 17 new-vocabulary queries across medicine-quality, diabetes technology, EU FMD/NMVS, German, Turkish, Chinese traceability, DoD stockpile, OR/perishable inventory, transfusion medicine, stability-science MKT, medicines-returns and EPI/eLMIS found nothing joining per-package provenance to potency or outcome. The remainder is a database join plus a standard mixed model. | The interface estimand is specific and currently settled by assertion: Malawi PMS reports "wide variations in API content within batches" and attributes them to handling in distribution with no provenance variable — exactly the within-batch/between-batch attribution the candidate is built to separate. No parent field supplies that estimand, and limb i's ICC gate is a real estimability question, not glue. | Partial (adv 1 Partial — the clinically decisive content may already be answered per product by the end-of-shelf-life genre, so the interface may add measurement without adding a decision; adv 2 Resolved)

P3 and P6 are marked contested, P6 is converted into a gate, a null is interpretable, and within-batch content spread is demonstrated somewhere (Malawi, 99/112 outside 90-110%). Verification (post-batch, two fresh-context checkers, logs UQ-20261017-19-verification-ghana.md and -slep.md): **Provisional stands for the reason that was already controlling, and verification does not touch it — but the last open novelty risk is closed in the candidate's favour, the strongest objection is narrowed on one side and weakened on the other, and SLEP must stop being cited for a storage regime.**
**The Ghana survey is read, and it does not run the regression.** It is Frimpong G, Ofori-Kwakye K, Kuntworbe N, Buabeng KO, Osei YA, Boakye-Gyasi ME, Adi-Dako O, "Quality Assessment of Some Essential Children's Medicines Sold in Licensed Outlets in Ashanti Region, Ghana", J Trop Med 2018, Article ID 1494957, doi 10.1155/2018/1494957. PMC returned a captcha, Europe PMC was robots-disallowed and Wiley errored, but the UGSpace repository PDF and the Hindawi article page both opened. Design: 68 samples of 15 essential children's medicines bought June 2014 to August 2016 from hospital dispensaries, community pharmacies and licensed chemical sellers in the Ashanti Region, assayed for API content against label claim by UV or HPLC with pH and microbial limits, reported as pass/fail counts and percentages, with no statistical-analysis section and no tests or intervals (61.8% failed API content, 27.9% pH, 2.9% microbial, 26.5% passed all three). Table 1 records labelled strength, country, batch number, manufacturing date, expiry date and registration number, and none of those dates is analysed. Cross-tabulations run by medicine, by local versus imported (36 local, 63.9% API failure; 32 foreign, 59.4%), by registration status and by country of manufacture — none by outlet type, none carrying custody or dwell time, and nowhere a regression or correlation of per-cent label claim against time since manufacture, package age or remaining shelf life. Two further details tighten the finding rather than loosen it: the design truncates the exposure by its own rule, since "quality assessment studies were conducted at least six months before their expiry dates" while "The shelf lives of the products ranged between 1 and 5 years."; and the only correlation it comments on is a different one, registration status, where there "appeared to be no correlation" with quality. Promotion condition (b) is therefore discharged in the candidate's favour, and the Routing contingency does not fire. Caveats: everything was read through the page summariser rather than verbatim, Table 1 and Section 2.5 were not checked string by string, a summariser-reported outlet count (24+24+35=83 against 68 samples) is unreconciled and probably counts outlets visited rather than products, and this checker used eight fetches against a cap of six, disclosed here as it was in the batch.
**SLEP is confirmed only as far as its abstract, and its storage regime is not established at all.** Lyon et al. 2006 could not be opened at Wiley (client error) or ScienceDirect (robots-disallowed on a guessed PII); a Zenodo record carried the abstract, from which three figures are confirmed verbatim: "This report summarizes extended stability profiles for 122 different drug products (3005 different lots)", "88% of the lots were extended at least 1 year beyond their original expiration date", and "for an average extension of 66 months". What is NOT established: what the analysis actually fits — no evidence of a per-lot degradation-slope model was seen, so the question is undetermined rather than answered — and, decisively for how this entry uses the source, the storage conditions, which no source read states. This entry calls SLEP's regime "controlled depot storage" in three places; that is a recalled characterisation, now marked unverified, and the entry's own strongest objection leans on it. A secondary review (a Wuerzburg thesis) describes the programme generally rather than Lyon's analysis: "Calculation to determine the new expiry date is carried out by means of individual statistical extrapolations." SLEP therefore supports a margin-of-extension claim at lot level and says nothing about within-lot potency against time, which is what limb ii asks.
**Carter & Heinemann is identified and read, and it cuts both ways.** PMC answered for once (PMC6134310): J Diabetes Sci Technol, online 21 December 2017, issue 2018;12(4):839-841, doi 10.1177/1932296817747292. Unit: the individual 10 ml insulin vial, 18 vials from 16 lots and two manufacturers bought from US pharmacies. Endpoint: intact insulin concentration in U/ml by mass spectrometry against the 95 U/ml USP and FDA minimum. Estimand: the descriptive distribution — 13.9 to 94.2 U/ml, mean 40.2, and "No vial met the minimum standard of 95 U/ml." It fits no model of concentration against storage time or temperature, and pre-purchase exposure was never observed. For this entry that is limb ii's premise and not its answer, as the Disguise row already had it, and it narrows the strongest objection, because the shortfall sits inside the serialized US market where that objection places the largest stability margin. It does not dissolve the objection: insulin is the thermolabile class this entry already concedes, and one 18-vial cross-section is not a within-batch provenance slope.
**Where it lands. Provisional, unchanged.** Gate 5 requires Well-posedness 3/3 for Validated and this entry stands at 2/3, because limb iii names no product-endpoint pair and the reformulation allowance is spent; no novelty news moves that. What verification changes is the state of the promotion conditions: (b) is discharged, (a) is untouched, and (c) is still open — the DSCSA primary sources were located (21 USC 360eee-1 at law.cornell.edu and govinfo, fda.gov/media/171666/download, FDA's dispenser compliance-policy guidance) but the fetch pool was spent before any could be opened, so the claim that no package-to-patient event is recorded remains an unchecked prior and is marked as one in attack 4. Novelty stays Medium, now held there by the single remaining close neighbour rather than by an unread survey.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3
Well-posedness 2/3: after the single permitted reformulation, limbs i and ii are fully specified (populations, exposures, endpoints, monograph references, estimands, and a declared gate between them) and a null is interpretable; the deduction is limb iii, where presupposition 5 is open and no product-endpoint pair is named, so the outcome limb has not yet stated what evidence would settle it. Not 1/3: limbs i-ii are settleable and the question survives dropping limb iii. Both adversaries graded vagueness Partial on the same ground. Significance 2/3: consequence argued in both directions with a named decision each side, audience specific and documented to be acting on bare thresholds; held below 3/3 because the clinically decisive limb is the fragile one and limb i alone is an operations statistic of moderate clinical interest.

Strongest remaining objection: the exposure may be large only where the instrument is absent, and negligible where it exists. The only opened setting with substantial within-batch content spread is unserialized LMIC supply (Malawi PMS: 99/112 samples outside 90-110%, "wide variations ... within batches"), while the serialized markets the question depends on (US DSCSA, EU FMD) are exactly where the stability margin is largest on published data (SLEP: 88% of 3005 lots extended >=1 year, mean 66 months) — so after conditioning on batch, as limb ii's estimand requires, there may be too little within-batch provenance spread and too little realised degradation left to estimate any slope; and whatever residual signal exists is a proxy for cumulative thermal excursion, which is already measured directly in the one product class (thermolabile biologics) where it is known to bite. The candidate therefore risks being positive only where it is not news and null everywhere it would be. Neither adversary could source the stability-design bound to an opened primary, and neither could find any MKT-to-dispensed-assay field study, so the objection is unsettled rather than established — which is why it caps rather than kills. Narrowed on verification, in both directions: Carter & Heinemann was opened (PMC6134310) and found 18 pharmacy-purchased vials from 16 lots running 13.9-94.2 U/ml, mean 40.2, with "No vial met the minimum standard of 95 U/ml." — substantial shortfall inside the serialized US market where this objection places the largest margin, though insulin is the thermolabile class already conceded and the study fits no storage-time model; and pulling the other way, SLEP's storage regime, which the objection's "controlled" premise rests on, could not be established from any source read.
Promotion requires: (a) naming at least one product-endpoint pair for limb iii, which lifts Well-posedness to 3/3 — note the reformulation allowance is spent, so this must be a specification inside V2, not a rewrite; (b) DISCHARGED on verification — the Ghana children's-medicines quality assessment was identified as Frimpong et al., J Trop Med 2018, Article ID 1494957, opened by repository and publisher route, and found to tabulate manufacturing and expiry dates without analysing either against assay, with no regression or correlation of per-cent label claim on age anywhere in it; (c) one real serialization-to-dispensing linkage evidenced from a primary source — statute, FDA guidance or a data holder — rather than a vendor marketing page, together with the DSCSA data elements and whether any package-to-patient event is recorded, since that decides what limb i can read rather than infer. Also worth closing, though not blocking: Carter & Heinemann 2018 via the SAGE/DOI route, and the SLEP full text, to establish whether either modelled potency against storage time within lot.

Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): run limb i alone as a variance-components description inside one integrated dispenser or wholesaler that already holds both serialized receipt events and dispensing records, and report the within-product and within-batch ICC of remaining shelf life at dispensing. That one number decides whether limbs ii and iii are estimable, needs no assay and no outcome data, and is the cheapest test of presupposition 6 and of the regime objection above.

Routing (if rejected as already-asked): not applicable. No opened source — across 29 queries and 13 publisher/repository pages — asks any limb as posed, so this is not an asked-but-open problem and nothing is routed to ledger/routed-open-problems.md. Contingency, now resolved: the Ghana survey was opened on verification and runs no such regression, so the contingency does not fire and nothing is routed.

---
ID: UQ-20261017-20
Date: 2026-10-17
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): Medicine — laboratory medicine (pre-analytical quality), patient safety. Adjacent: causal inference (IV), quality engineering, haemovigilance.
Question (canonical): What happens to the patient whose specimen is rejected — among laboratory orders rejected for pre-analytical reasons, what fraction never yields a usable result, what is the delay to the first usable result, and what downstream clinical consequences follow, estimated with a design exploiting the operator- and draw-route-driven component of rejection?
Alternative formulations:
- When the laboratory rejects a haemolysed, clotted or insufficient sample, how often is the test never repeated, and does anyone come to harm?
- Treating pre-analytical specimen rejection as an exposure rather than a quality indicator, what is its causal effect on time-to-result, test abandonment and patient outcome?
- (Gate 1 reformulation V2, graded at Gate 2) In a linked LIS–EHR frame with documented recollection policy, rejected order as exposed unit and a non-rejected order for the same test, window and acuity stratum as comparator: (i) proportion with no usable result at 6 h / 24 h / never; (ii) order-to-first-usable-result distribution; (iii) effect on pre-specified downstream endpoints (time to recognition of a critical result, escalation/ICU transfer, LOS, additional venipunctures) under a declared identification strategy — phlebotomist identity, draw route or shift-level haemolysis propensity as instrument — with the exclusion restriction tested by falsification outcomes.
Motivating gap: Silence mapping — intake asserted the pre-analytical literature is dense with rejection rates and haemolysis indices and empty of patient-side questions. Gate 2 found this false for limbs (i) and (ii): the field has a paper titled almost exactly the question and publishes both headline quantities. Residual genuine gap is limb (iii) only.
Presuppositions:
1. Rejections recorded with reason, order ID and timestamp and linkable to the clinical record — ESTABLISHED.
2. Rejection has an operator-/draw-route-driven component independent of prognosis given acuity, usable as an instrument — CONTESTED; central threat (sicker patients have harder draws and more line draws).
3. "Never re-collected" separable from "deliberately abandoned as no longer needed" — CONTESTED and still open — P1 does not resolve it: its criterion is "failure to recollect or relabel a rejected specimen" with no time cutoff (read at first hand on verification; the "arbitrary six-hour window" this entry first attributed to P1 is not in the paper).
4. A counterfactual usable result exists; rejection is a correct refusal whose cost is delay/abandonment — ESTABLISHED analytically.
5. Downstream endpoints ascertainable at needed granularity — ESTABLISHED.
6. Rejection not already neutralised by reflex auto-recollection — CONTESTED, site-dependent; published abandonment 11.2% vs 48.3%, repeat delay 65 min median vs 121 h mean, so huge between-site spread.
What would count as an answer: (i) proportion with no usable result in pre-specified windows and never; (ii) order-to-first-usable-result distribution vs matched non-rejected orders; (iii) effect estimates on pre-specified downstream endpoints under a declared identification strategy with falsification tests. A null (prompt recollection, nothing downstream) is a clean answer and would strip the patient-safety warrant from rejection-reduction programmes. Criteria (i) and (ii) have already been met by published work.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): Gate 2 ran 11 web searches and 6 fetches (one fetch over its cap of 5, disclosed in the record); adversary 1 ran 9 searches (8 of them Disguise, in vocabularies Gate 2 did not try) and 4 fetches. Full lists in batches/2026-10-17-0742/UQ-20261017-20-record.md (queries 1–11, fetches F1–F6) and UQ-20261017-20-adversary-1.md (queries 1–9). Most informative:
- "clinical impact of specimen rejection on time to result and patient outcomes laboratory medicine" (own-field own-words) → first hit is the Cape Town rejection-and-clinical-impact paper (P2); plus the CAP TODAY review "Specimen rejection: What price for patient care?", which led to P1. Decisive.
- "audit rejected specimens test not repeated cancelled percentage never recollected clinical impact" → P2 again plus publisher PDF route (DOI 10.1515/CCLM.2011.743).
- "phlebotomist as instrumental variable hemolysis draw route causal effect laboratory result" (method-owner vocabulary) → NEGATIVE: no IV or quasi-experimental identification of rejection as exposure.
- "causal effect of specimen rejection repeat blood draw cohort mortality ICU transfer instrumental variable" → NEGATIVE: limb (iii) unanswered.
- Adversary, haemovigilance vocabulary: `"wrong blood in tube" OR mislabelled transfusion sample rejected delay to transfusion patient harm SHOT haemovigilance` → SHOT ADU chapter OPENED: 15 of 94 delayed transfusions caused by sample errors, deaths attributed to repeat-sample delay (Case 7.1: 45–50 min advised delay "contributed to her deterioration"), key message "Delays in transfusion contribute to death and morbidity."
- Adversary, citation spot-check: `Karcher Lehman "Clinical consequences of specimen rejection" Q-Probes 78 clinical laboratories` → GWU repository OPENED, citation verified: Arch Pathol Lab Med 2014;138(8):1003-1008 (PMID 25076290).
- Adversary, econometric vocabulary: `hemolysis index threshold "regression discontinuity" OR "natural experiment" ... patient outcomes` → NEGATIVE: HI cut-off never used as a discontinuity for outcomes.
- Adversary, informatics vocabulary: EHR cohorts of orders "never resulted" → NEGATIVE; that literature covers results that returned and were ignored.
COULD NOT READ at Gate 2: P1's abstract/full text (GWU repository bibliographic only; PubMed fetch error; publisher route not attempted, fetch cap reached), so P1's endpoint detail rested at Gate 2 on the CAP TODAY review of July 2012, which Gate 2 did open — and which verification has since shown carries figures that are not P1's. P1 itself was opened at the publisher on the second verification attempt (see Verification). Title-only, grounding nothing: newborn-screening unsatisfactory-specimen indicators, Valenstein 2006 identification-error Q-Probes, EFLM HIL survey.
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
P1. Karcher DS, Lehman CM. "Clinical consequences of specimen rejection: A College of American Pathologists Q-Probes analysis of 78 clinical laboratories." Arch Pathol Lab Med 2014;138(8):1003-1008 (citation verified at hsrc.himmelfarb.gwu.edu/smhs_path_facpubs/66; endpoints via captodayonline.com/Archives/0712/0712d_specimen_rejection.html, opened). Unit: rejected specimen aggregated to institution. Endpoint: abandonment (no corrected specimen requested or supplied) and processing delay to usable result, stratified by stat/non-stat, specimen type, bed size. Comparator: none vs non-rejected orders; institution-to-institution percentiles. Estimand: descriptive cross-institutional proportions and medians. Publishes overall abandonment 11.2% (median laboratory-attributed 1.3%, provider-attributed 5%); median delay 65 min (88 non-stat, 54 stat, 91 at >450 beds); and one quantified downstream consequence, 86.8% of rejected blood specimens leading to repeated phlebotomy. Its other consequences — inconvenience and discomfort, potential complications, potential transfusion for iatrogenic blood loss — are named, not measured, and the patient-safety link is explicitly "not specifically assessed in this study". Figures read at the publisher on verification; the earlier ones in this entry came from the CAP TODAY review and were not P1's.
P2. Jacobsz LA, Zemlin AE, Roos MJ, Erasmus RT. "Chemistry and haematology sample rejection and clinical impact in a tertiary laboratory in Cape Town." Clin Chem Lab Med 2011;49(12):2047-2050, DOI 10.1515/CCLM.2011.743 (publisher PDF opened). Unit: specimen (481 rejected of 32,910 over 2 weeks) plus 30 patient files. Endpoint: proportion repeated, time for repeat to reach lab, critical-range repeats, files where rejection "had an impact on patient care". Comparator: none. Estimand: descriptive single-site proportions plus unblinded holistic chart judgement. Publishes 1.46% rejection, 51.7% repeated (48.3% not), mean 121 h to repeat, 5.1% critical, 40% of 30 files judged affected.
P3. Phelan MP, Hustey FM, Good DM, Reineks EZ. "Seeing Red: Blood Sample Hemolysis Is Associated with Prolonged Emergency Department Throughput." J Appl Lab Med 2020;5(4):732-737 (OUP page opened). Unit: ED visit (11,228). Endpoint: ED LOS/arrival-to-disposition, not time to usable result, not redraw (authors say their data cannot determine redraws), no clinical outcomes. Comparator: visits with non-haemolysed potassium sample — it does have the comparator the others lack. Estimand: unadjusted mean differences, causality explicitly disclaimed. Publishes 349 vs 287 min overall; 429 vs 337 discharged; 292 vs 264 admitted.
Novelty — how this differs from each:
- vs P1: P1 IS limbs (i) and (ii), under nearly the candidate's own title, across 78 institutions, with both proposed quantities already published. The candidate differs only in frame and estimand (matched comparator rather than internal processing interval; a chart-validated abandonment code rather than P1's untimed recollect-or-relabel criterion) and in extending to limb (iii), which P1 names and does not quantify. These are improvements to an answered question.
- vs P2: P2 IS limbs (i), (ii) and a weak (iii) at one site, in the candidate's own words. The candidate differs by frame size, matched comparator, pre-specified endpoints and identification — i.e. it attacks P2's validity, not its askedness.
- vs P3: different exposure (haemolysis of a potassium sample, not order rejection) and endpoint (total LOS), no abandonment, no clinical events, no identification. P3 does not answer a limb, but it establishes the non-exposed-comparator delay design as already published here, removing the comparator from the novelty claim.
- Residual no opened prior does: limb (iii) as an identified causal estimate with phlebotomist/draw-route instrument and falsification outcomes. That is a new design for an old question; P1's title and the CAP TODAY framing pose the question itself, so it is asked-but-open, not un-asked.
Novelty confidence: Low
Significance — consequence: If limb (iii) is positive, rejection-reduction programmes gain the measured patient-safety warrant they currently assert; if null, the case deflates to cost and throughput (already separately studied). Weaker than intaked: with 11.2% abandonment and a 65-min median delay already published, the remaining decision-relevant uncertainty is only the final link from delay/abandonment to clinical events.
Significance — audience: laboratory quality and accreditation bodies setting rejection-rate targets (CAP, EFLM/IFCC extra-analytical working groups), hospital patient-safety committees, ED operations groups already acting on P3. Real audience — CAP commissioned P1, SHOT reports annually — but the marginal value of an identified estimate over existing descriptive and case-series evidence is asserted rather than demonstrated.
Significance — fecundity: whether reflex auto-recollection standing orders are justified; how to validate a never-recollected code against intent; whether haemolysis-tolerant reporting with an interpretive comment beats rejection on net patient outcome.
Significance — anchoring: EFLM/IFCC quality-indicator programme (rejection rate as numerator with no patient-side denominator); diagnostic-error/test-follow-up literature (which covers results that returned, not specimens that never resulted); iatrogenic phlebotomy-associated anaemia.
Reason for silence: None credible — there is no silence. The question was asked under its own name in 2014 (P1, citation verified) and its harm limb is asked and case-answered annually in haemovigilance (SHOT). The record's disciplinary-ownership/incentive mechanism (exposure data owned by laboratory medicine, outcome ascertainment and IV identification owned by clinical epidemiology) explains why an identified answer has not been produced, not why nobody asked. Per the pipeline, absence of a reason for silence sends the candidate back to Gate 2, whose Low grade stands.

Verification (post-batch, two fresh-context checkers against the same source, logs UQ-20261017-20-verification-karcher.md and -karcher2.md): **the Rejected verdict stands and is now read at first hand, but five of P1's figures as this entry gave them are wrong and P1's harm list is not P1's.** The first checker could not reach P1 at all — GWU record bibliographic only, PubMed client error, Europe PMC robots-disallowed, and a PMC article that turned out to be a different paper behind a captcha — and returned a clean COULD NOT READ, which left every P1 figure UNVERIFIED rather than refuted. The second checker reached the publisher's own article page at meridian.allenpress.com and read abstract plus Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion through the page summariser.
**What P1 actually publishes.** Confirmed as printed: the delay is a "median of 65 minutes", and the long-delay subgroup is "median = 91 minutes" at a "bed size of greater than 450 beds". Corrected: the split is "a median of 54 minutes for stat specimens and 88 minutes for nonstat specimens", not the ~60 and ~90 this entry gave. Refuted: the 21% abandonment figure is not in the paper — checked twice, not found; what the paper prints is "The overall specimen abandonment rate in this study was 11.2%", with a median laboratory-attributed rate of 1.3% and a median provider-attributed rate of 5%. Refuted: the "arbitrary six-hour window" this entry attributed to P1's abandonment definition is not there either — P1's own definition is "Specimen/test abandonment was determined by failure to recollect or relabel a rejected specimen", with no time cutoff, and the only "6" in the text is a six-week observation period. The harm list is wrong too: P1 does not name haematoma, phlebotomy-associated anaemia or nerve injury. It names "inconvenience and discomfort for the patient", "the potential for patient complications", and the "potential need for blood transfusion due to excessive iatrogenic blood loss". The provenance of the bad figures matters: they came from the CAP TODAY review of July 2012, which Gate 2 could open and which predates the 2014 paper by two years, so it describes an earlier Q-Probes cycle or preliminary data — this entry should never have attributed its numbers to P1, and the general lesson is that a trade-press review of a Q-Probes programme is not a substitute for the paper.
**Two findings cut towards the rejection rather than away from it.** P1 does quantify one downstream consequence this entry listed as unquantified: "In this study, 86.8% of rejected blood specimens led to repeated phlebotomy." And P1 names the patient-safety limb itself as not assessed — "Although not specifically assessed in this study, longer delays in test result availability" ... "may have an even greater negative impact on patient safety" — which states limb (iii) as open more sharply than anything the entry had. Confirmed as the entry described it: the comparator is institution-to-institution percentiles and stat/non-stat and bed-size subgroups within rejected specimens, with no non-rejected comparator anywhere in the paper, and every consequence other than repeat phlebotomy is named without being measured.
**Where it lands. Rejected, unchanged.** The Gate 2 ground never rested on the figures: it is that P1 carries the candidate's question as its title across 78 institutions and publishes limbs (i) and (ii), while the harm limb is posed and case-answered annually in haemovigilance. Reading P1 confirms each element of that directly — the question is its subject, abandonment and delay are its published endpoints, and the patient-safety link is its own stated non-finding. The entry's one countervailing point, that P1's endpoints had never been read, is discharged in the verdict's favour, and the routed row gains a first-hand source. Caveat: all of this came through the page summariser on the publisher's HTML, Table 1's definitions were never visible and no PDF was opened, so these figures should be re-checked against the PDF before anyone cites them.

The one countervailing point, that P1's endpoints had never been read at the publisher or in the abstract, has since been discharged in the verdict's favour: P1 was opened on verification, and its subject, its published abandonment and delay endpoints and its own "not specifically assessed" sentence on patient safety establish askedness directly, alongside the independently opened SHOT chapter.

"may have an even greater negative impact on patient safety" (read at the publisher on verification, replacing the CAP TODAY review this entry first cited) as the sources showing it open; tractability is limited by data access (linked LIS–EHR at multiple sites, recollection policy recorded) rather than by method, so tier B.
