ID: UQ-20261017-21
Date: 2026-10-17
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): Other STEM — atmospheric science / NWP data assimilation; satellite-navigation and avionics engineering (secondary: aviation safety regulation). Target field deciding novelty and acting on the answer: operational meteorology / NWP observation monitoring and QC.

Question (canonical): Over a pre-declared window and airspace set, with exposure defined from non-GNSS-derived evidence only (regulator bulletins, NOTAMs, spectrum-monitoring records) and each aircraft report joined to an archived NWP observation-feedback record, do aircraft-derived meteorological observations (AMDAR and Mode-S EHS/ADS-B-derived u/v wind and temperature) differ between exposed and matched unexposed airspace in (i) observation-minus-background bias and standard deviation, stratified by aircraft navigation configuration, (ii) the rate of gross positional misassignment detectable as kinematic inconsistency between successive reports from one airframe, and (iii) the fraction of such reports that survives operational quality control into the analysis and the analysis increments they produce — or are the exposed and unexposed departure statistics indistinguishable inside a pre-declared equivalence band with no excess QC rejection rate?
(V2; reformulated once at Gate 1 from a V1 that left exposure definition, comparator and null unspecified. V1 and the diff are in the record.)

Alternative formulations:
- Has GNSS interference been putting corrupted aircraft weather reports into operational weather analyses, and if so where and how many?
- Treating documented GNSS interference as an exposure, what is its effect on the O-B error statistics of aircraft-derived wind and temperature, stratified by aircraft navigation configuration, and on the analysis increments those observations produce?

Motivating gap: Dated, geolocated GNSS jamming/spoofing has been documented since 2022 (EASA SIB 2022-02R4; ICAO APAC 2025, SAM 2026). An aircraft-derived wind is the ground vector minus the air vector, and the surveillance-sourced stream's position tag is partly GNSS-derived, so interference can corrupt the value and separately mis-place a valid value. Volume at stake ~55M wind + ~32M temperature obs/day over Europe (de Haan et al. 2025), and ECMWF took the global Mode-S stream operational on 8 May 2025. Aviation quantifies the exposure at fleet scale; the meteorological outcome is quantified nowhere. AMENDED at Gate 4: the join is not wholly absent — Ingleby, ECMWF Newsletter 184 (2025) records it qualitatively ("In parts of eastern Europe and the Middle East, there are gaps due to GPS interference ... and also occasional bad data that was not detected"), with no statistics.

Presuppositions (E established / C contested): 1 (C, in degree) aircraft wind depends on a GNSS-informed ground-velocity solution — per-fleet navigation fit must be documented, not assumed; de Haan et al. 2025 does not state BDS 5,0 ground-vector provenance either way, so this stays contested. 2 (CORRECTED at Gate 4, was wrongly graded E) position and time stamps are NOT uniformly GNSS-derived: de Haan et al. 2025 §2.3 — "The timestamp is not generated by the aircraft; instead, it is created by the radar or receiver at the time of reception", and "For ATC radar, the position is determined by ATC radar"; receiver-sourced reports are CPR-decoded from ADS-B and AMDAR positions come from the FMS. 3 (C, load-bearing) exposure can be geolocated/dated independently of the outcome — usual proxies (PIC/NIC, GPSJAM hex severity) are themselves GNSS-derived, so V2 requires a non-GNSS index with Aireon's TDOA Independent Position Check as validation only. 4 (E, per centre) per-report observation-feedback archives with QC flags exist. 5 (C) sufficient exposed sample — traffic collapse/rerouting confounds and censors. 6 (C, and the object of limb (iii)) operational QC is imperfect. 7 (C) the background is usable in exposed regions — break circularity with reanalysis or a denial reference.

What would count as an answer: a matched-exposure analysis on archived observation feedback (ECMWF/Met Office/NOAA) joined to a non-GNSS exposure index, reporting (i) exposed-vs-unexposed O-B bias and sd for u/v and T stratified by navigation configuration, (ii) a gross-misassignment rate from within-airframe kinematic inconsistency, cross-checked against an independent TDOA track, (iii) the QC-survival fraction, resulting increments and a data-denial OSE. A clean null inside a pre-declared equivalence band with no excess rejection rate answers it equally and closes it.

Novelty — queries run (query -> one-line result): 29 distinct web queries and 13 pages opened across three agents — 11 queries / 5 fetches at Gate 2, 9 / 4 by adversary 1, 9 / 4 by adversary 2, in eleven vocabularies (operational meteorology, DA/OSE, satellite-navigation engineering, surveillance/spectrum, aviation-safety regulation, pre-GNSS aircraft nav-error, space-weather/scintillation, military EW, adversarial-ML/cyber-physical security, maritime AIS, German, French, Chinese). Full lists: batches/2026-10-17-0920/UQ-20261017-21-record.md and the two adversary files. Most informative: (a) mandatory own-field obvious-title pass "impact of GNSS interference on aircraft-based observations" -> lands entirely in avionics/navigation engineering, no meteorological hit; (b) mandatory "what fraction" pass -> the exposure quantity is published (>1,500 flights/day affected in 2025; >122,000 flights in Jan-Apr 2025) and no count or fraction of corrupted, rejected or assimilated aircraft *met reports* exists anywhere; (c) WMO ABO report index (37 reports 2013-2024) fetched -> no mention of GNSS, jamming, spoofing or interference in any title; (d) adversary-1 NWP-monitoring query -> ECMWF Newsletter 184 (Ingleby 2025), the only document found joining interference to the met stream, qualitatively; (e) adversary-2 EW query -> Meteorological Technology International Apr 2025 p.41, the same motif for radiosondes, trade-press, no exposure index or statistics; (f) adversary-2 security query -> arXiv 2504.15942 "Adversarial Observations in Weather Forecasting", nearest formal family, different unit/exposure/estimand; (g) adversary-2 maritime query -> the AIS/ship-report analogue is also unasked.

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
P1. de Haan, de Jong, Koutek, Sondij & Strauss (2025), "EMADDC: high-volume, high-quality, and timely wind and temperature observations from aircraft surveillance data (Mode-S EHS)", Atmos. Meas. Tech. 18, 3341-3359. https://amt.copernicus.org/articles/18/3341/2025/ — unit: Mode-S EHS messages processed to wind/T over European airspace; endpoint: pooled bias/sd plus volume and timeliness; comparator: radiosondes, AMDAR, model; estimand: marginal space-time-pooled agreement. FULL TEXT NOW READ by both adversaries (the record's single named unread load-bearing check): contains no jamming, spoofing, RFI, NIC/NACp, gross position error or geographic stratification.
P2. Ingleby, "Assimilation of global Mode-S aircraft winds", ECMWF Newsletter 184 (Summer 2025). https://www.ecmwf.int/en/newsletter/184/news/assimilation-global-mode-s-aircraft-winds — unit: the operational stream; endpoint: a qualitative coverage-and-quality remark; comparator: none; estimand: none.
P3. Aireon (May 2025), "GPS Anomaly Trends". https://aireon.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Aireon-White-Paper-GPS-Anomaly-Trends.pdf — unit: ADS-B report by hour x H3-r3 tile; endpoint: navigation-anomaly indicators; comparator: PIC>=7; estimand: explicitly none, descriptive only. (Not re-verified by either adversary; Inside GNSS 13 Aug 2026 "ADS-B Data Analysis for GNSS Interference Mapping" is the same relation one step less formal.)

Novelty — how this differs from each: vs P1 — same stream, airspace and endpoint family, different estimand: P1 gives a pooled marginal quality, the candidate an exposed-vs-matched contrast stratified by navigation configuration, plus two endpoints P1 has not (misassignment rate; QC-survival fraction with increments and a denial OSE). vs P2 — P2 is the closest formulation in the candidate's own field and states the phenomenon exists and is not fully caught by QC; it gives no contrast, no O-B statistics, no misassignment rate, no survival fraction and no increments, so it establishes the premise rather than answering any limb. vs P3 — exposure instrument, not outcome: unit is the ADS-B report scored for navigation integrity, no denominators, no tests, nothing on wind, temperature or NWP; treating it as prior art would be the adjacent-object error.

Novelty confidence: Medium (close neighbour P2 in the candidate's own field; the record's named blocker to High — P1's unread full text — is now cleared and does not move the grade down; the unresolvable residual is unindexed NWP-centre internal obstat work)

Significance — consequence: if yes, variational QC and blacklisting are organised by platform ID and variable, never by airspace exposure (confirmed: de Haan et al.'s screen is per-airframe 14-day sd plus message-level sanity checks), so the fix is a new kind of exposure-conditioned QC predictor over tens of millions of obs/day in the region containing the exposure; the worst case is a mis-placed but physically valid temperature that passes a departure check at the wrong location. Regulators gain a quantified non-safety cost term they currently lack — evidenced: IFALPA's Dec-2025 "Effects of Manipulated GNSS" enumerates thirteen downstream effect classes and never mentions wind, temperature or meteorological data. If no, the null licenses the ongoing expansion of the Mode-S/ADS-B stream into exactly the airspace where interference is worst.

Significance — audience: NWP observation-monitoring and DA groups (ECMWF, Met Office, DWD, Meteo-France, KNMI, NCEP), who already run the machinery that would change; EUMETNET E-AMDAR/EMADDC and WMO JET-ABO as stream and guidance owners; EASA/ICAO/national CAAs and spectrum regulators; secondarily the ADS-B integrity community, whose products would become inputs to a meteorological QC chain.

Significance — fecundity: how should assimilation QC treat an observation whose position rather than value is in error; should observation error covariances carry a navigation-integrity term for any navigation-dependent platform (ships, buoys, GPS radiosondes, UAS, mobile-phone pressure); should interference exposure be routine archived report metadata; and inverted — can meteorological O-B departures serve as an independent interference detector, since they rest on a non-GNSS physical reference.

Significance — anchoring: the unresolved AMDAR/Mode-S temperature-bias problem; correlated and non-Gaussian observation error in assimilation; the ECMWF aircraft data-denial literature, which priced losing aircraft data but not keeping corrupted aircraft data; the aviation-side open question of interference's full downstream footprint.

Reason for silence: a disciplinary boundary with an asymmetric handoff — the exposure is mapped in aviation/surveillance/spectrum channels whose outputs are not inputs to any meteorological workflow, while the outcome sits in feedback archives keyed by platform, variable and date with no airspace-exposure dimension, so the join nobody has done is the join neither database supports. Supported by IFALPA's omission of the meteorological product. Reinforced by new data (geolocated exposure products from 2022/2025; operational stream volume from 2025) and by a QC incentive gap: QC is judged by whether the analysis is protected, not by characterising what it rejected, so the rejection-rate series that would show this has no owner who reads it by airspace. WEAKENED at Gate 4: the met community does make the interference-to-observation-quality connection in print for radiosondes (Met. Tech. Int. Apr 2025), so the boundary is permeable where one vendor owns instrument and fix; the aircraft stream's lack of such an owner is a coherent but unevidenced extension.

Verification (post-batch, fresh-context checkers reading the cited priors at first hand): four checks ran on this entry's priors and on the one finding that could have taken novelty to Low. No verdict moved; the Provisional is better founded than the batch's version, the novelty-threatening check resolved in the candidate's favour, and one prior closer than anything in the record was found.
- P1 (de Haan, S. et al. 2025, Atmos. Meas. Tech. 18:3341-3359) — READ AT FULL TEXT, with four countable negatives taken from the body rather than the abstract: no stratification of observation quality by navigation configuration; no positional-misassignment rate; no stated QC-survival fraction; and no occurrence of jamming, spoofing or interference anywhere in the paper. The last of those is the check that could have taken novelty to Low, and it resolves the other way.
- Provenance of the stream — CONFIRMED from two sources at FULL TEXT, so the inversion that caps this entry is first-hand rather than an adversary's paraphrase. ADS-B carries "the aircraft's onboard sensed position (through GPS and inertial systems)", but "For ATC radar, the position is determined by ATC radar.", "The timestamp is not generated by the aircraft; instead, it is created by the radar or receiver", and "Temperature is deduced from the Mach number and airspeed". That last string also bounds the temperature limb: a temperature derived from Mach number and airspeed cannot take a GNSS position error into its value, only into where the value is placed.
- Ingleby, ECMWF Newsletter 184 (2025) — CONFIRMED as exactly what the entry claims of it, a one-clause unquantified remark: "In parts of eastern Europe and the Middle East, there are gaps due to GPS interference," and "and also occasional bad data that was not detected." No counts, no affected-versus-unaffected split.
- A CLOSER prior than any in the record, found at this pass: Ingleby's 2025 DA-Workshop / ECMWF@50 talk, carrying a 200 hPa vector-wind O-B RMS map on 1-degree boxes for 15 October 2024 to 31 January 2025 whose caption reads "There are points in Eastern Europe with large RMS due to GPS jamming and intermittent problems south-east of Iceland (now resolved)." This is the nearest anyone has come to limb (i): the effect mapped with the cause named. It still carries no counts, no affected-versus-unaffected comparison and no exposure join, so novelty stays Medium rather than dropping — but the record must cite it, and a successor must assume the figure exists. A journal or technical-memorandum version was searched for twice and not located, which is a search negative and not evidence that none exists.
- Exposure (presupposition 4, which the record treated as the hard limb) — AVAILABLE, but event-based rather than flight-normalised, which is a different shape of problem than the record expected. IATA FDX SRWG/8 WP/12 gives about 402,000 GPS signal-loss events over about 13.1 million flights, roughly 31 per 1,000 globally and about 3.5 per 1,000 in ASPAC, from an airline sample that does not monitor B777/B787 and has internal inconsistencies. EASA's ECR gives 4,689 GNSS events in 2022 and 4,147 in the first half of 2023; Airbus FDM 10,843 events in 2021 against 49,605 in 2022; EVAIR 2024 reports 3,115 GNSS reports of 7,453, 550 of them spoofing. Two figures bear on how exposure must be defined. EANS reports that human reporting captures only 2-10% of ADS-B-detected events. And Skai found that of 397 transatlantic flights spoofed over the Black Sea, about 74% still broadcast NIC >= 7 after leaving the affected area — so integrity flags do not mark the exposure, an exposure index built from them would be largely blind, and the non-GNSS-derived definition the question already insists on is the right one.
- Countable negatives from this pass, recorded as "not found in the texts read" and not as "absent from the literature": no quantified effect of GNSS interference on assimilated aircraft observation quality anywhere; no interference-driven QC rule (the thinning from 44 km at low levels to 95 km at 200 hPa, the heading correction, and the year-long European Mode-S switch-off and reintroduction all have other causes); and no positional-misassignment figure for meteorological reports. Disclosure: the de Haan reader ran 7 fetches against a cap of 6.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 3/3
(Well-posedness reduced from the record's 3/3: presupposition 2 is false as written and miscited to the very paper that contradicts it, and limb (i) has no stated equivalence band and no censoring limb. Significance stands at 3/3 and was independently strengthened at Gate 4.)

Strongest remaining objection: presupposition 2 is inverted — de Haan et al. 2025 §2.3 states the time stamp is created by the radar or receiver at reception and that radar-sourced positions are determined by ATC radar, so aircraft-side GNSS corruption cannot move the time tag at all and cannot move the position of an unquantified share of the ~55M/32M-per-day stream; the Gate 3 headline mechanism (a geographically displaced but physically valid temperature injecting a coherent increment) therefore applies to a fraction of the stream that no opened source quantifies, and both adversaries sustained this on evidence they read.
Promotion requires: (1) presupposition 2 restated from de Haan et al. 2025 §2.2-2.3's actual architecture — ground-side time stamps, radar-determined positions for the radar-sourced subset, CPR-decoded positions for the receiver-sourced subset, FMS positions for AMDAR — and the radar-versus-receiver-sourced share of the assimilated stream quantified from a source that is opened and read (P1's tables are images; the EMADDC/KNMI technical reports or an ECMWF monitoring note are the routes); (2) a numeric pre-declared equivalence band for limb (i) in u/v (m/s) and T (K), stated rather than deferred to protocol; (3) a censoring/report-loss limb added so limb (i) separates degradation from selection into the exposed sample; (4) the motivating gap amended to cite, as the existing qualitative join and nearest own-field prior, both Ingleby, ECMWF Newsletter 184 (2025) and the closer item verification found — Ingleby's 2025 DA-Workshop / ECMWF@50 talk, whose 200 hPa vector-wind O-B RMS map caption reads "There are points in Eastern Europe with large RMS due to GPS jamming and intermittent problems south-east of Iceland (now resolved)." and which still gives no counts and no affected-versus-unaffected split. These are record amendments plus one bounded search; nothing requires re-running Gate 4.

Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): quantify the radar-sourced versus receiver-sourced split of the assimilated Mode-S EHS stream and confirm the ground-vector (BDS 5,0) provenance, since both the scope of limb (ii) and the sign of limb (i) depend on them.

ID: UQ-20261017-22
Date: 2026-10-17
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): Other STEM — electrochemical engineering; battery test metrology / design of experiments. Secondary: data-driven battery prognostics.
Question (canonical): For long-run Li-ion cell-cycling experiments — (a) PROSPECTIVE: under a design in which cells are rotated between channels on a pre-declared schedule (>=3 channels x >=3 cells per group, sham rotations, traceable per-channel current/voltage/temperature calibration, logged chamber position), what are the cell, channel and cell-by-channel variance components, with intervals, of per-interval degradation rate and of pre-declared trajectory features, and what cycle-life variance share do they imply under the declared trajectory model; and (b) ARCHIVAL: in archived protocol-ranking experiments where the same physical channels hosted cells on different protocols across rounds (Severson 2019; Attia 2020), what is the channel-level variance when channel enters as a random effect alongside protocol, and does the top-k protocol set change under channel-shrunken protocol estimates?
(Graded version is V2; V1 — "what share of between-cell variance in cycle life is attributable to the channel" — failed Gate 1 as unidentifiable in the designs it criticises. Both versions in the record.)
Alternative formulations:
- Is what the battery field calls "cell-to-cell variability" partly channel-to-channel variability of the test rig?
- Under a rotation design, what are the cell/channel/cell-by-channel variance components of cycle life, and how do channel-shrunken protocol effects compare with the published rankings?
Motivating gap: Presupposition inversion on a settled claim. Cycle-life spread among nominally identical cells is read as manufacturing tolerance and used to size test matrices, warranty margins and ML benchmarks — but one cell per channel for life makes cell and channel perfectly confounded, so the standard design cannot separate them at all. Per-channel current/voltage accuracy and position-dependent chamber gradients act non-linearly on degradation rate (Arrhenius; plating thresholds). The field names the issue twice without estimating it: Dechent et al. 2021 list "location in a given testing chamber" as an extrinsic source and declare intrinsic-only scope; Devie/Dubarry et al. 2015 assert "calibration across channels" as a control and report no channel component.
Presuppositions: (1) a cell-vs-channel decomposition is identifiable with a feasible design — CONTESTED and hardest (ageing is destructive, so identification needs rotation plus a trajectory model; a pure rate-multiplier channel effect is partly absorbable by the cell's rate parameter); (2) rotation does not itself perturb the cell — FLAGGED, addressed by sham rotations; (3) channel metrological differences large enough to move rate — PARTLY SUPPORTED (P2 summary: 0.5 degC extrinsic deviation -> >1.5% resistance variation; Attia SI: "single temperature chamber for all channels", "cell temperature increase during cycling is significant"); (4) public datasets record channel identity — VERIFIED TRUE at Gate 4 (two independent repos read a per-cell `channel_id` out of the Severson/MATR files); chamber position and calibration history are not recorded; (5) rate sensitive to small T/current offsets — ESTABLISHED; (6) protocol and channel not crossed/randomised in the published experiments — UNVERIFIED (Attia SI describes no assignment scheme; V2's archival limb needs only the weak form); (7) cycle life defined consistently across channels — FLAGGED.
What would count as an answer: (a) the prospective rotation experiment above reporting the three variance components with intervals and the implied cycle-life share; or (b) a re-analysis of an archived protocol-ranking experiment with channel as a random effect, stating whether top-k changes and whether channel variance could have produced the published ranking difference. A null answers it: a channel component indistinguishable from zero at pre-declared precision converts a named confound into a validated assumption and strengthens the archives.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): Gate 2 ran 11 of an 11-query cap (minimum 8 met); Gate 4 added 18 further queries in vocabularies Gate 2 did not try (9 per adversary) plus one GitHub code search. Full lists: batches/2026-10-17-0920/UQ-20261017-22-record.md and the two adversary logs. Most informative:
- "apparent cell-to-cell variability dominated by test equipment measurement error share of variance attributable to cycler" (mandatory already-computed sweep) → the only published quantity of this kind: P2 reports setup-induced temperature inhomogeneity accounting for roughly half of previously reported resistance variation (~0.45% inherent, ~600 cells) — but at BEGINNING OF LIFE, not cycle life or trajectory shape.
- "gauge repeatability reproducibility measurement system analysis variance components battery cycling test equipment" → generic MSA tutorials only; the method-owning field has the vocabulary and no battery-channel instance.
- "re-analysis ranking of fast-charging protocols cell-to-cell variability too few cells per protocol" (answer side) → protocols designed *considering* ctcV (AIChE 2024; Braatz group); nothing re-ranking with channel as a random effect.
- A2 Disguise: German, Chinese, semiconductor ATE/burn-in site-to-site, hierarchical-Bayes equipment random effect, ML equipment-signature, ISO 5725 intermediate precision, ecological pseudoreplication/"tank effect", Dahn-group HPC → every vocabulary exists in its own field; no battery-channel instance in any.
- A2 GitHub code search "channel_id severson battery" → presupposition 4 verified true.
- A1 "Technology Life Verification Test manual ... allocation of cells to test channels" → exclusively semiconductor tester-matching hits; boundary signature, not a renamed solved problem.
Not run (recorded as not run, never as passed): agronomy incomplete-block/plot-effect wording and survey-methodology interviewer-effect wording, by any of the three agents.
COULD NOT READ: P2 full text (mediaTUM Anubis block; Crossref refused by proxy; no DOI/publisher URL obtained by any of three agents) — identified at verification as eTransportation 2021, article 100129, doi 10.1016/j.etran.2021.100129 (closed access), so the DOI is established while the body is not; what has been read is the published abstract plus the authors'-employer summary page. Severson 2019 SI not read. Attia 2020 main text failed twice on nature.com and once on eScholarship; its Supplementary Information WAS read by A2 via the springernature media route.
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
P1. Dechent, Greenbank, Hildenbrand, Jbabdi, Sauer, Howey (2021), "Estimation of Li-ion degradation test sample sizes required to understand cell-to-cell variability", arXiv:2107.07881 — read in full. Unit: individual 18650 cells across five datasets. Endpoint: capacity-trajectory model parameters. Comparator: each dataset's own population; no apparatus comparator. Estimand: cells needed for the POPULATION sd to stabilise (>=9/11/13). States its aim as "intrinsic rather than extrinsic variability" while naming chamber location as an extrinsic source.
P2. Wildfeuer & Lienkamp, "Quantifiability of inherent cell-to-cell variations of commercial lithium-ion batteries" (TWAICE / TU Munich; journal, year, DOI not established) — summary page only; FULL TEXT COULD NOT BE READ. Unit: ~600 commercial cells at beginning of life. Endpoint: static initial capacity/resistance/mass spread. Comparator: uncompensated vs temperature-compensated spread. Estimand: inherent CoV after removing setup-induced temperature bias, by deterministic compensation plus Monte Carlo — not a random-effects decomposition, no channel term.
P3. Devie, Dubarry, Cabanel, Liaw (2015), "Intrinsic degradation variability in commercial lithium-ion batteries", ECS abstract A01-0129 — HNEI slide deck read. Unit: matched 18650s in one batch. Endpoint: degradation trajectories (candidate's endpoint family). Comparator: cells against each other; "calibration across channels" and "neutralization of extrinsic factors" listed as design features. Estimand: intrinsic spread, with extrinsic factors asserted controlled rather than estimated.
Added at Gate 4 by Adversary #2 (nearer in own field than the record found): Geslin et al., "Selecting the appropriate features in battery lifetime predictions", Joule 7 (2023) 1956-1965 — read in full; decomposes protocol-vs-cell variability on the exact Severson corpus and prints "variation arises purely from intrinsic differences between cells", with no apparatus term. Frenander & Thiringer, J. Energy Storage 102 (2024) 114014 — abstract read; "a minimum of 4 replicates", variability attributed to production tolerances alone. Also opened by A1: Beck/Dechent/.../Dubarry, "Inhomogeneities and Cell-to-Cell Variations in Lithium-Ion Batteries, a Review", Energies 14(11):3276 — contains no cycler, channel, test-bench or chamber-position factor at all.
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs P1 — same datasets and endpoint family, orthogonal estimand: P1 asks how many cells pin down ONE lumped variance; the candidate asks for that variance to be PARTITIONED, and adds a factor P1 never enters. If the channel component is non-trivial, P1's replication guidance is wrong in kind, since replication inside fixed channels cannot average a channel effect away. vs P2 — closest in premise and the stated kill condition: it says in print that measured ctcV is inflated by the setup and publishes the correction, but differs in endpoint (beginning-of-life parameters, not ageing rate or trajectory shape), estimand (deterministic temperature-bias compensation, not a channel variance component or interaction), design (no crossing, no rotation, no per-channel calibration traceability) and has no protocol-ranking limb. Unread, so it grounds no grade either way. vs P3 — same endpoint family and community, but treats channel calibration as an asserted design control; the candidate asks for the magnitude of exactly the component P3 assumes away, in a design where it is estimable. vs Geslin 2023 / Frenander 2024 — both are premises rather than answers: they state or assume intrinsic-only variation on this very corpus, which is what the question asks to test, so they sharpen the significance case rather than defeat novelty.
Novelty confidence: Medium
(Distinct across 29 queries in roughly a dozen vocabularies: no source anywhere reports cell/channel/cell-by-channel variance components for cycle life or trajectory shape, and none re-ranks a published protocol comparison with channel as a random effect. Medium, not High: P2 is close in premise and its full text could not be read by any of three agents; Gate 4 found two nearer own-field priors the Gate 2 record missed; two planned neighbouring vocabularies were never run. Not Low: no prior poses the question with an estimand and a design, and the two intrinsic-only papers print the assumption rather than test it. Asked-but-open: NO in the strict sense — acknowledged-and-set-aside in P1, assumed-away in P3 and Geslin 2023, which is a limitation rather than a posed question, so not routed.)
Significance — consequence: If the channel component is material (channel ICC ~0.1-0.2+): published replication guidance (P1; Frenander 2024's "4 replicates") is structurally wrong rather than merely imprecise, because adding cells inside fixed channel assignments cannot shrink a channel-induced component — the fix is a design change, not a sample-size change; published protocol rankings including the closed-loop top-k may be partly apparatus artefacts, and a closed loop that assigned protocols to channels non-randomly was optimising partly over channels; ML lifetime predictors trained on these corpora may be partly learning channel signatures, giving the much-used batch-to-batch generalisation gap a mundane candidate explanation; test standards and dataset schemas gain channel-randomisation, calibration-traceability and position-logging requirements. If indistinguishable from zero: the intrinsic reading and the rankings stand and the archives become stronger evidence than they are currently entitled to be. Usable either way. (A2's sourced discount: pack/warranty margin re-sizing is the weakest limb — within-protocol cycle-life spread is large relative to the few-percent rate effects the named mechanisms imply, so margins would barely move.)
Significance — audience: battery test laboratories and dataset producers (Stanford/MIT/Toyota, HNEI, Oxford/RWTH, Sandia, NASA, JRC) — two metadata fields and a channel-assignment practice change; cycler manufacturers (Arbin, Neware, Maccor, BioLogic) — per-channel rather than per-instrument calibration disclosure, and between-channel variance in place of a full-scale accuracy bound; the prognostics community — train/test splits currently made by batch would need making by channel; standards bodies (IEC 62660, ISO 12405, USABC/DOE manuals) and the existing battery-metrology activity (BIPM CCQM task group on Li-ion batteries, VAMAS); OEM cell-validation and warranty groups; public archives (Battery Archive, BatteryML).
Significance — fecundity: Is the Severson/Attia batch-to-batch shift a channel-and-era effect rather than a cell-population effect, and does cross-batch prediction error shrink when channel is modelled? How much of the apparent gain from closed-loop/active-learning experimental design survives entering the apparatus as a random effect (same question for autonomous labs; adjacent to UQ-20261015-16)? What calibration traceability is the minimum for inter-laboratory comparability of cycle-life claims? Does channel variance explain part of the documented solid-state irreproducibility? Methodologically: what is the efficient rotation design for variance components when the unit degrades irreversibly — a reliability-DoE question with no battery instance.
Significance — anchoring: the intrinsic/extrinsic split left explicitly open by P1; P2's demonstrated setup inflation of beginning-of-life spread, never carried into the ageing-rate domain; P3's asserted-but-unestimated channel control; the intrinsic-only premise printed by Geslin 2023 on this exact corpus; battery-testing reproducibility work (BIPM CCQM, VAMAS, all-solid-state benchmarking); the unexplained batch-to-batch distribution shift used as prognostics' hardest generalisation test.
Reason for silence: Disciplinary boundary plus incentive, with an invisibility-by-construction amplifier. (1) The method belongs to variance-component statistics, industrial MSA, reliability blocking, agronomy's plot effects and ecology's tank effects; battery ageing is run by electrochemists whose replication culture recognises one random factor, the cell — and Gate 4 confirmed every one of those fields owns the vocabulary with no battery instance. A2 weakens this limb: Geslin/Braatz shows the statistical vocabulary sitting inside the group that owns the data, and they still assumed intrinsic-only. (2) The datasheet substitutes for the estimate: a 0.05%-of-full-scale spec reads as a bound that makes the question look answered, and does not describe between-channel variance or the temperature pathway at all. (3) Invisibility by construction (the load-bearing mechanism, and the only one sourced): with one cell per channel for life, no analysis of any existing single-laboratory dataset can reveal a channel effect, so the anomaly that normally prompts a methodological question cannot appear; Attia's SI corroborates the shape of the silence by treating chamber temperature as a nuisance to hold constant rather than a component to estimate. (4) Throughput and incentive: channels are scarce and fully booked, rotation costs channel-months and risks a null, and a positive result devalues the asker's own archived datasets.

Verification sharpened this rather than moving it: the SI sentence is confirmed as printed, while "about 4 cells per channel" is printed nowhere and is this entry's own arithmetic over a 48-channel cycler run in rounds of 48 ("~200 cells for optimization (4×48)") — sound, but an inference. ID: UQ-20261017-23
Date: 2026-10-17
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): Other STEM — structural reliability and code calibration (target field; its committees — JCSS PMC, CEN/TC250/SC3, AISC Specification Committee, AASHTO/MBE raters — would act). Method imported from public economics (bunching/notch estimators). Secondary data domain: steel mill production QC.
Question (canonical): For a pre-declared heat-level mill-certificate frame stratified by grade and by product/thickness class, what fraction of the mean offset (f_y,measured - f_y,specified) and of the lower-tail shape is attributable to the conformance decision rather than to production — identified not by a single-notch density-smoothness argument but by a cross-grade mass balance (mass missing below grade G's minimum must reappear as excess mass in grade G-1's upper tail at a rate consistent across notches) — and what are the resulting latent (pre-selection) 5th percentile and reliability index beta for canonical code-calibration cases, relative to the certificate-based values? (Gate 1 reformulation, one permitted, used; Gate 0 version rested on excess mass at a single notch and is recorded in the record file.)
Alternative formulations:
- Is the extra strength design codes credit to real steel a property of the steel, or an artefact of which heats get called that grade?
- Applying a notch/bunching-style estimator to grade-conformance records, what is the latent pre-selection strength distribution of the material actually in structures, and how far does its 5th percentile differ from the certificate distribution used in reliability calibration?
Motivating gap: The canonical probabilistic model names the selection mechanism and does not model it. JCSS PMC steel chapter: downgrading "produces bi-modal distributions" with higher means and CoVs, no adjustment, constants alpha = 1.05 / C = 20 MPa on 1970-onward European data, "CoV values refer to total steel production". AISC EJ v40 n1: the data "may be truncated at F_y = 50 ksi", then adopts a distribution that "conservatively, neglects any truncation". Melcher et al. 2004 (JCSR): asymmetry attributed to values that "are reclassified to lower tensile strength classes", rate never estimated, adjacent grades fitted independently, its own 8.6%-below-nominal anomaly for S355 left standing.
Presuppositions: (1) heat-level certificate frame obtainable in volume — volume VERIFIED (TxDOT 3,976/1,587/2,030 values; AISC/SSPC ~20,000; Melcher n = 5,493/1,089), but heat-level linkage plus retest/re-certification flags NOT shown to exist anywhere. (2) Downgrading happens at a non-negligible rate — ANCHOR, the central unknown; no published rate found in three independent sweeps. (3) The threshold is a genuine notch — true by specification logic, softened by retest, and multi-notch within a grade by thickness. (4) Latent density smooth across the threshold — CONTESTED, and the stated reason the imported estimator does not transport. (5) Estimand depends on the lower tail — ESTABLISHED. (6) alpha and C fitted to certificate rather than coupon data — NOT VERIFIED; partly counter-evidenced (AISC's parameters are coupon-based, 207 coupons/38 heats). (7) Certificates and in-structure properties differ only by the selection studied — PARTLY UNDERCUT (static-vs-A370-rate offset 55.8 -> 51.4 ksi; flange-vs-web cooling; producer effects). UNSTATED and load-bearing, found by both adversaries: (8) that the cross-grade flow is closed, exclusive and yield-only; and (9) that the latent pre-selection population is the decision-relevant one for code calibration.
What would count as an answer: A fitted selection model on the pre-declared frame reporting (i) conformance-attributable mass at each notch with uncertainty; (ii) a downgrade/re-certification rate consistent across coupled adjacent grades; (iii) implied latent 5th percentile vs the certificate 5th percentile; (iv) recomputed beta for canonical calibration cases under latent vs certificate distributions. A null — no excess mass beyond a fitted aim-point offset, adjacent grades consistent with independent production — answers it and would reduce C = 20 MPa to a pure aim-point offset.

Verification (post-batch, three fresh-context checkers, logs UQ-20261017-23-verification-dualgrade.md, -aisc.md and -filter.md): **Rejected stands, and the fatal attack is better sourced than it was — two of its three counts have gone from unopened search-result titles to first-hand sources, while the third stays unsourced.** This entry's verdict turned on a disagreement between its two adversaries: the first graded attack 4 Unresolved, which is fatal, and the second graded the same attack Partial. Verification went at the first adversary's three counts directly.
**Dual certification is real and the field calls it common.** The first adversary's strongest count, which it was careful to label as supported only by unopened titles, now has primary sources. AISC's own FAQ 1.3.7 states that "Certificates of conformance and material test reports for materials that comply completely with more than one standard will indicate those standards", that "These materials are considered 'multi-certified.'", and — decisively for the mass balance — that "The practice is common and an indication of well-controlled processes." AISC Steel Interchange (May 1994) records a producer making "dual grade" A36/A572 Gr 50 material, where "This 'dual grade' capability was achieved by careful selection and control of steel chemistry", and a current producer datasheet offers material that "Can be dual certified as A572 Grade 50/CSA G40.21 50W upon request". So a heat can sit in two grades at once without any downgrade having occurred.
**Conformance is multivariate, also confirmed at first hand.** A992 carries an upper yield limit as well as a lower one, a tensile minimum, "a specified maximum yield-to-tensile ratio of 0.85" and "a specified maximum carbon equivalent of 0.47%", and A572 Gr 50 adds elongation limits (21% in 2 in., 18% in 8 in.). A heat can therefore fail a grade on something other than yield strength, which is enough on its own to open the yield-space balance the Gate 1 reformulation depends on.
**The third count stays unsourced, and so does the candidate's own premise — which is the finding.** Nothing the checker read establishes a leakage rate (scrap, off-grade sale, re-rolling), and nothing establishes that dual certification removes downgrading: as the checker put it, a heat in the overlap of two specifications is a heat that meets both, and a heat meeting only the lower grade is simply certified to the lower grade. That half of the objection rests on inference, not on a source, and is marked so. But the symmetry matters more than the gap: eight queries found **no published rate** of downgrading, re-certification or off-grade sale, and no source at all describing the re-certification of a failed heat into a lower grade. The candidate's own premise is as undocumented as the objection to it. And the fallback the record offered — heat-level retest and re-certification flags, which would make the balance unnecessary — is confirmed absent from the documented certificate contents: AISC FAQ 1.3.1 points to ASTM A6 Section 14, whose required content "includes but is not limited to the heat number, steel grade, and nominal sizes supplied", with no retest or re-certification field anywhere in what was read. A6's own clause text on "Retests", "Test Reports" and "Retreatment" was not obtained, and EN 10204 could not be read, so that negative is incomplete — but the circularity the first adversary charged is intact: the question is well-posed only if data exist that would make it unnecessary.
**P1 is correctly quoted, and the attack-6 arithmetic is vindicated by P1's own wording rather than by the arithmetic.** Both of this entry's quotations from P1 appear as printed, with the reason the entry omitted: the distribution "may be truncated at Fy = 50 ksi, or ln(Fy) = 3.91," because "the sample Cumulative Distribution Function (CDF) is nearly vertical at that point". The sample (207 coupons, 38 heats, 8 shapes, 3 producers) and the observed-to-certificate ratio (mean 1.002, CoV 0.044) are confirmed. The citation is completed: Bartlett, Dexter, Graeser, Jelinek, Schmidt & Galambos, Engineering Journal 2003;40(1):2-14. Three corrections. The database size is internally inconsistent in P1 itself — about 25,000 mill test reports in the introduction, 20,259 data points in a figure, 20,295 coupons in Tables 3 and 5 — so no single figure should be cited without that caveat. Ellingwood is cited there as Ellingwood, Galambos, MacGregor & Cornell (1980), not as a sole author. And P1's reliability numbers are: beta 2.52 at L/D = 3 under the original calibration, 2.61-2.77 for phi = 0.9 and 2.37-2.54 for phi = 0.95, with the conclusion that "an increase of resistance factor from 0.90 to 0.95 is not recommended without further study". Confirmed on the decisive point: P1's reliability analysis uses A992 alone, models no adjacent grade jointly, and lets no truncation or selection correction enter beta. On direction, the first adversary's illustrative arithmetic — that neglecting the truncation is conservative, the opposite of this record's claim — is its own, unsourced, and is marked so; but P1's own words carry the same direction, since it calls the neglect "conservatively, neglects any truncation", and that is a first-hand source. The record's claim that the neglect understates lower-tail mass is contradicted by the paper it cites.
**The concrete filter effect exists; the steel analogue does not, and that is the batch's most useful by-product.** Confirmed: Caspeele's HERON 59 paper uses the term, where "this filter effect can be quantified using Bayesian updating techniques" (abstract level only), and Lux, Feiri, Schulze-Ardey, Hegger, Classen & Ricker, Scientific Reports 2026;16:8277 (full text) treats "the filtering effect of conformity control in reliability-based assessments" by updating JCSS Probabilistic Model Code priors with an operating-characteristic likelihood and computing beta by FORM, finding beta up by as much as about 10% and sigma falling from 5.81 to 4.89 N/mm2. Four steel-vocabulary searches found **no steel analogue at all** — a countable negative at title and snippet level, since no steel page was opened. No source states a direction in terms for either material, and no source gives an empirical rejection or reclassification rate. Melcher et al. 2004 is verified verbatim in its full PDF on both strings: the S355 distribution "is asymmetrical, evidently due to the exclusion of values not satisfying the requirements of material standards for that tensile strength class, and therefore they are reclassified to lower tensile strength classes", and "the probability of not maintaining the assumed yield strength nominal value, 355 MPa, is about 8.6%", "this being worse than the supposed 5%". It gives no reclassification rate, never shows how the 8.6% was obtained, and fits S235 and S355 separately.
**Where it lands. Rejected, unchanged.** Attack 4 stays Unresolved, now with its dual-certification and multivariate-conformance counts sourced at first hand and its leakage count marked as inference. The entry's accuracy improves in three places and its claim about the direction of the truncation error is withdrawn against its own cited paper. The by-product is worth more than the entry: the forward question — how much conformity control improves the lower tail and the reliability index of a steel grade, the question the first adversary identified as the useful residue — has an established concrete literature with named machinery and **no steel counterpart in anything opened**, while both the JCSS steel chapter's bi-modality remark and Melcher's unexplained 8.6% sit in print unexplained. That is a candidate for a future batch, not a row in the routing file: it is not routed here because this entry was not rejected as already-asked, and because neither source poses the forward question in a sentence that could be quoted as posing it. It is recorded as a carry-over residue in the batch report.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3
Strongest remaining objection: The reformulation's entire identifying content — the cross-grade mass balance — rests on a presupposition the canonical formulation states as a necessity and which is false: the flow between adjacent grades is not closed, exclusive or yield-only (dual certification, multivariate conformance criteria, scrap and off-grade leakage), so neither the presence nor the absence of a notch-consistent rate identifies selection; and the only non-circular fallback, heat-level retest and re-certification flags, is data the record itself concedes nothing opened demonstrates exists — while the latent pre-selection population it would reconstruct is not the population any grade-G structure is built from, leaving deliverable (iv) without a decision it answers.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): Not applicable to this candidate as formulated. If the closed-flow presupposition is ever to be repaired, the pointer is the AISC MTR plate survey's pre-removal dataset (38,575 tensile lines, three producers, grades A36 / A572 Gr 50-65 / A588 / A852 / A514, non-conforming lines deliberately removed before analysis) together with the two unread priors — Dor 1955, Revue de Statistique Appliquee 3(2):123, and the full texts of Caspeele/Sykora/Taerwe 2014 and HERON 59(2/3).
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): Not routed. The rejection ground is Gate 4 presupposition failure, not already-asked, so the Routing rule (route only candidates rejected because already asked and still unanswered) does not apply. Recorded for the record, not as a routed row: the candidate's existence limb is raised and deferred in print in its own field (doi.org/10.62913/engj.v40i1.800; jcss-lc.org/publications/jcsspmc/steelpr.pdf), and the defensible residue both adversaries name — the forward "filter effect of steel conformance on the characteristic value and beta", the steel case that arXiv 2504.09508 itself lists as underexplored — is a different, forward question and would have to enter the pipeline as its own candidate.

ID: UQ-20261017-24
Date: 2026-10-17
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): Other STEM — atmospheric chemistry and aerosol science; cosmochemistry (extraterrestrial mass influx); space-environment science.

Question (canonical): Now that spacecraft-reentry metal input to the stratosphere is comparable to or larger than the cosmic-dust input for several elements, by how much does it bias the tracer-based constraints on cosmic-dust influx to Earth, and can meteoric and spacecraft material still be separated per particle and per snow/ice layer well enough to preserve those constraints as reentry mass grows?
(Gate 1 reformulation V2, used for Gates 2-4: for each published method that constrains extraterrestrial mass influx from metal abundances — per-particle stratospheric aerosol, mesospheric metal layers, meteoric smoke, polar snow/firn/ice — state its tracer elements and compute (a) the fractional bias implied by the published per-element anthropogenic reentry flux and its uncertainty and (b) the reentry mass or date at which that bias exceeds the method's own quoted precision, with the meteoric/spacecraft separation rule declared in advance and its misattribution rate estimated on pre-space-age archived material.)

Alternative formulations:
- Lay: Has space hardware broken the instrument we use to weigh cosmic dust?
- Technical: What is the anthropogenic reentry component of the post-1990 metal-tracer record in stratospheric aerosol, mesospheric layers and polar snow, and what bias does it impose on the inferred extraterrestrial influx?

Motivating gap: Murphy et al., PNAS 120(43) 2023, doi:10.1073/pnas.2313374120 (read in full via the White Rose deposit) finds >20 elements in spacecraft-alloy proportions inside stratospheric sulfuric-acid particles, ~10% (+/-7%) of particles >120 nm carrying reentry metals against ~20% carrying meteoric iron, and reentry Li, Al, Cu and Pb already exceeding the cosmic-dust influx of those metals. Its own stated open items are aerosol properties, oxide persistence, nucleation, optics and novel chemistry; it does not raise the influx-bias limb, and comes nearest with the remark that reentry copper "could possibly double the concentration of copper in Antarctic snow" — framed as deposition, not as bias to a constraint.

Presuppositions: (1) at least one published influx constraint rests on metal abundances in stratospheric aerosol, mesospheric layers, meteoric smoke or polar snow — ESTABLISHED in kind, inventory not assembled. (2) meteoric and spacecraft material are separable per particle by element ratios — ESTABLISHED operationally (Murphy's Al/Fe > 0.1 with Na as discriminator; NASA JSC's C/TCN/TCA/AOS classes) with no published error rate. (3) reentry flux is estimable per element with usable uncertainty — ESTABLISHED (Schulz et al. 2025, 43 elements) but the uncertainty is large and partly judgemental by the authors' own account. (4) pre-space-age archived material exists for the validation the question needs — NOT VERIFIED. (5) FALSIFYING CONDITION: the disputed influx range is sensitive at the magnitude of the anthropogenic input for at least one tracer method — PARTLY ADVERSE: the anthropogenic-dominated elements are the alloy ultratraces (Li, Al, Cu, Pb, Nb, Hf, Ag) while the dominant constraints run on Na, Fe, Mg, Si, Ni, Ir, Pt, Os. Adversary 2 opened one new prior (Egan et al., EGU25-4460) whose element list, as paraphrased, puts Ni and Mn in the already-exceeds-natural set, so (5) is not safe in either direction. (6) tracer bias propagates to influx bias through each method's transport/removal model — NOT VERIFIED, flagged contested; limb (a) is not computable from a flux ratio without it.

What would count as an answer: (i) an enumerated method inventory with tracer elements and a propagated per-method bias; (ii) a measured spacecraft-attributable fraction of the tracer signal under a pre-declared separation rule validated on pre-1960 material, with a stated misattribution rate; (iii) a dated projection of when each method can no longer constrain the natural flux at its own precision. A null — all tracer methods resting on elements where reentry input is small, plus a flat pre/post-1990 contrast — closes it in the negative.

Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 11 in Gate 2, 9 by adversary 1, 9 by adversary 2 (29 total; all in new vocabularies after Gate 2). Full lists in batches/2026-10-17-0920/UQ-20261017-24-record.md and the two adversary files. Most informative: own-field title form "aluminum oxide spheres solid rocket exhaust contamination stratospheric cosmic dust collection flux estimate" → EGU24-14286 "Assessing stratospheric aerosols contamination due to space activities" (Lasue et al.), the nearest prior and the published artificial-share trend; "spacecraft reentry metals bias estimates of cosmic dust influx ... tracer" → only Murphy 2023 and mirrors, no bias paper; "anthropogenic spacecraft reentry contribution to mesospheric metal layers" → Schulz et al. 2025 (arXiv:2510.21328), the published per-element inventory; A1-S1 ice-core vocabulary "anthropogenic osmium platinum iridium Greenland snow contamination ... extraterrestrial flux tracer recent decades" → Gabrielli et al., Chem. Geol. 255:78-86 (2008), read in full, the decisive hit; A1-S3 "Schulz Glassmeier 2021 anthropogenic and natural injection of matter" → arXiv:2008.13032 (2020), the anthropogenic-vs-natural comparison posed five years before P2; A1-S4 Carrillo-Sanchez 2016 → the canonical 43 +/- 14 t/d constraint rests on lidar Na and Fe fluxes and South Pole spherules; A2-F1 French-vocabulary sweep → EGU25-4460 (Egan et al.), a prior the record never saw; A2-D9 own-words answer-side phrasing → EGU26-1032, COULD NOT READ (fetch cap). Mandatory "what fraction of X" query: the quantity is published twice over (Murphy 2023: ~10% +/-7% of >120 nm particles; Lasue et al. 2024: artificial class ~60% in 2010-2020 against ~40% cosmic in 1980-2009).

The paper is "Siderophile metal fallout to Greenland from the 1991 winter eruption of Hekla (Iceland) and during the global atmospheric perturbation of Pinatubo", not a study of anthropogenic contamination of the meteoric-tracer record. Its anthropogenic remark is hedged ("might be also of anthropogenic origin", "One possible anthropogenic source") and runs the other way for the second tracer ("the Ir atmospheric budget does not appear clearly perturbed by catalytic converters"). Absent from the paper: any bias figure, any corrected flux, any influx value, any mention of spacecraft, rockets or reentry, any separation method, any misattribution rate. The quotation the first pass carried is accurate; the characterisation of what the paper was about is not, and that characterisation was the whole disguised-known ground.
- The two published fractions (Murphy et al. 2023, PNAS 120(43), doi:10.1073/pnas.2313374120, FULL TEXT; Lasue et al. EGU24-14286, ABSTRACT ONLY) — CONFIRMED AS REPORTED, REFUTED AS PRIOR ART. Murphy prints "Over 20 elements from reentry were detected." and "spacecraft ablation products are present in 10±7% of stratospheric sulfuric acid particles that are larger than about 120 nm diameter", and separately "about 20% of such particles contained enhanced aluminum from spacecraft reentry" — where "such" means particles that already contain meteoric iron, so the record's "~10% against ~20%" pairing set two differently-based fractions side by side. Murphy's rule is Al/Fe > 0.1 as "probable spacecraft influence", with "there is no corresponding population with enhanced sodium"; its calibration uncertainty is a factor of 1.5-2; it states no false-positive rate; and the ice-core line is explicitly speculative ("possibly double the concentration of copper in Antarctic snow"). Lasue's abstract gives 25 catalogs 1981-2020, 5,071 particles, cosmic particles "typically represent on average 40% of the collection", the terrestrial-contaminant and artificial classes "roughly doubled" to about 60%, "likely due to the overall human space activity", and the whole set "only preliminary characterized". Neither paper propagates either fraction into a bias on an influx constraint; neither holds a pre-space-age baseline (Murphy's earliest data are 1998).
- The misattribution rate — NOT FOUND anywhere, as a countable negative over what was opened rather than an absence of searching. The nearest figure, Taupin et al. EGU25-4490's "at least 20% ambiguously classified", is an ambiguity rate over a collection, not the misattribution rate of a declared separation rule measured against material of known origin.

Strongest remaining objection: Presupposition 6 and the tracer non-overlap — attack 4, graded Partial by all four adversaries that have attacked this candidate. Limb (a) asks for a fractional bias on an inferred influx, and a per-element reentry flux does not become that without each method's transport and removal model; no opened source supplies one for any named method. And the elements where reentry input is comparable to or larger than cosmic input are the alloy ultratraces (Li, Al, Cu, Pb, Nb, Hf, Ag), while every influx constraint any agent on this record could enumerate runs on Na, Fe, Mg, Si, Ni, Ir, Pt or Os (Carrillo-Sanchez et al. 2016: 43 +/- 14 t/d from lidar Na/Fe fluxes and South Pole spherules) or on Holocene ice that excludes modern material by construction. So the probable value of limb (a) is a null for the methods that exist, and the question's force rests on limb (ii), the misattribution rate, which is one number that exists nowhere. The non-overlap is not safe in the other direction either: Egan et al. EGU25-4460 puts Ni and Mn in the already-exceeds-natural set, and that is a paraphrase from an abstract.

Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): open the results and discussion of Schulz et al. 2025 and the text of EGU26-1032 before anything else, since both sit exactly where a prior formulation would be and four agents have failed to reach the former. Then, ahead of any arithmetic, take one named influx constraint and read its transport and removal model to decide whether its tracer is reentry-sensitive at all. That single read either gives limb (a) an object or retires it, and if it retires it, limb (ii) — the misattribution rate of a pre-declared separation rule against pre-space-age archived material — is the question that remains.

Promotion requires: three things, each a read or a sourced statement rather than new research. (1) A sourced statement, from the transport or deposition model of at least one named influx method, of whether its tracer elements are or are not reentry-sensitive at the Schulz et al. 2025 per-element flux. That converts presupposition 6 from contested to settled and makes limb (a) either computable or formally void, which is the cap. (2) The results and discussion of Schulz et al. 2025 and the text of EGU26-1032, both unread by any agent on this record, closing Disguise. (3) A scope decision: limb (ii) alone — the misattribution rate of a pre-declared meteoric/spacecraft separation rule measured against pre-space-age archived material — is a single-number question with no published value and would stand as a narrower candidate in its own right; the bundle as posed is bounded above by whatever (1) returns.

Routing (if rejected as already-asked): n/a — the entry is not rejected. It is Provisional with a stated promotion condition, so there is nothing to route. Nor does the asked-but-open test apply to the 2008 Gabrielli paper that the first pass read as this question's asked-and-answered form: that paper is about volcanic fallout to Greenland and does not pose the candidate's question at all.

ID: UQ-20261017-25
Date: 2026-10-17
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): Other STEM — hydrology, meteorology, coastal and wind engineering (extreme-value statistics as practised); engineering standards and design-value issuance. Method imported from forecast verification / coverage-test backtesting.
Question (canonical): Over a pre-declared frame of (site, issued value, issue date) triples from dated standards and published quantile maps — 50-year wind speeds, 100-year flood discharges, 100-year significant wave heights — restricted to issued values carrying an explicit nominal annual exceedance probability p, what is the pooled realized exceedance rate in the post-issue site-years, estimated under a declared spatial-dependence model and reported as a ratio to nominal p; and under a pre-declared decomposition, how much of any departure is attributable to (a) issue-era estimator bias (issue-era estimator vs modern estimator on the identical issue-era record), (b) parameter and record-length uncertainty at issue, and (c) post-issue trend?
Alternative formulations: Have the 100-year values we published actually been exceeded about once a century? / Treating each issued design value as a probabilistic forecast with a stated exceedance rate, what are its out-of-sample verification statistics, and does the miscalibration sit in the estimator or in the climate?
Motivating gap: Silence mapping. EVA practice is dense with how-answers (estimator choice, regionalisation, nonstationary GEV) and standards are revised by re-estimation, yet the issued product — a dated number for a named site with a stated nominal rate — is never scored against what followed. Gate 2 added two gap exhibits: the Colorado State 100y/24h monitor flags exceedances daily and accumulates no counts, expected counts or rate; Kjeldsen & Prosdocimi (2023) run the field's own annual-exceedance-count machinery on 842 UK gauges but in-sample only, against thresholds fitted on the same record. Intake arrived with NOVELTY CHECK NOT RUN; Gate 2 was the first search.
Presuppositions: (1) issued values retrievable at site level with issue dates — bounds scope; (2) enough post-issue site-years for power — CONTESTED, forces a declared spatial-dependence model (0.4 expected exceedances/site over 40 yr at p=0.01); (3) measurement system stable, or rating-curve / anemometer-height / averaging-time changes enter as covariates — CONTESTED; (4) nominal rate readable as a frequency — CONTESTED, converted by V2 into a reported classification count on the way into the frame; (5) estimator bias at issue and post-issue nonstationarity separable — CONTESTED and load-bearing; (6) record quality adequate in the exceedance tail specifically — CONTESTED, and biases the realized count downward, i.e. toward the reassuring null.
What would count as an answer: A pooled verification over the pre-declared frame reporting the realized exceedance rate with a dependence-aware interval as a ratio to nominal, plus the three-way decomposition, limb (a) recovered by re-running the issue-era estimator on the issue-era record. A clean null is informative, so the question is not answerable identically regardless of evidence.

Anchors hold; a fourth anchor now exists in the seismic testing literature, which is why the question is not new.
Reason for silence: Collapsed on opened primary sources. (1) "A disciplinary boundary runs through the statistic" — refuted: seismologists made the coverage-test transplant inside a hazard field with the same committee/statistician split. (2) "Nobody owns the superseded issue; incentives run the wrong way" — refuted: P2 tests the model "derived for the official French seismic building code" and P1 tests four successive national vintages. (3) "The statistic has no single-site existence, so every institution's unit is too small" — refuted hardest: seismology produced the pooled version from 62 thinned stations at near-zero expected counts, while hydrology has thousands of gauges and ~337 expected exceedances on a P3-scale frame. The replacement offered — that the transplant has not crossed from seismology to hydrology — is "no one carried it across," which the protocol does not accept as a mechanism, and it points the wrong way because the hydrological case is easier. Per the Gate 4 rule a failed reason for silence makes the novelty finding itself suspect and returns the candidate to Gate 2. On the return the novelty finding was re-searched at verification and the Low grade did not survive it, because no opened source states that the decomposition has been done or that it cannot be. The collapse itself stands, as an Unresolved on attack 7 from adversary 2, and under Gate 4 an Unresolved on an attack other than 1, 2 or 4 caps the entry at Provisional rather than rejecting it. The honest position is that the silence is still unexplained: "no one carried it across" is not a mechanism, and it points the wrong way, since the hydrological case is the easier one.

Verification (post-batch, fresh-context checkers reading the cited priors at first hand, then a late Gate 4 of two cold adversaries): three checks ran on the disguised-known kill and the claim that carried it. The nearest prior is confirmed on the rate statistic and absent on the decisive attribute, the not-separable claim is unsourced, and the verdict moved from Rejected to Provisional.
- P1 (Mak, S. & Schorlemmer, D. 2016, BSSA 106(4):1817-1831) — CONFIRMED on five of seven attributes, WEAK on one, ABSENT on the decisive one; read at FULL TEXT. Confirmed: four dated issued NSHM vintages (1996, 2002, 2008, 2014); six nominal return periods from 10 to 400 years; sites-with-exceedance counted against a forecast expectation, with the inconsistency rule printed as "If the observed hazard falls outside this interval, the forecast is judged as inconsistent with the observation."; a stated power limit, discrimination "≤30%" within "0.75–1.5 times the forecasted hazard"; and about fifteen years of observation. WEAK on spatial dependence: the paper states "Because the sites are spatially clustered (Fig. 2a,c), they are not independent" and handles it by declustering at separation distances it concedes "was fundamentally arbitrary", which is not the declared dependence model the candidate asks for. ABSENT on attribute 7, the decomposition: nowhere does the paper separate issue-era estimator bias from post-issue change, and only the 1996 and 2002 vintages were "truly prospective" by its own account. So the artefact class and the rate limb are genuinely prior art, and limb (a) is not.
- "The sibling field's twenty years indicate the split is not separable" — NOT SOURCED, as a countable negative over four papers opened for exactly this claim. Tasan, Beauval et al. 2014 (GJI, read via isterre.fr), Stirling & Petersen 2006 (ABSTRACT ONLY), Stein, Geller & Liu 2011 (SRL 82(5)) and Rey et al. 2018 all lack both a decomposition and any statement that one is impossible. The strongest sentence anyone found pointing that way is Tasan's "the discrepancies between observations and predictions can generally have more than one explanation", which is hedged, was reported by a summarising reader rather than re-checked as a single string in the PDF, and says in any case that attribution was not achieved, not that it cannot be. The first pass's fatal attack turned on reading "not achieved" as "not separable"; nothing opened supports that step.
- Late Gate 4 (run separately and from scratch against the Gate 0-3 record, because the Gate 2 novelty grade had been withdrawn): two cold adversaries, one handed the verified facts above as numbered findings and one without them, neither given any earlier adversary log, both running all eight attacks. Both returned Provisional at novelty Medium with nothing Unresolved, and both refused the not-separable claim — one in terms: "That seismology's twenty years show bias and change are not separable. No opened source says impossible." One restated the candidate as two questions rather than one: "The bundle is two questions: Q1 is a corpus swap, and Q2 is a new estimand whose separability is unestablished but also not shown impossible." Both graded attack 5 Partial on the identification of limb (a), and that is the cap.

Scores: Well-posedness 3/3 · Significance 2/3
Strongest remaining objection: limb (a) is not shown to be identified — attack 5, Partial from both late adversaries as from both first-pass ones. The candidate's whole claim to be more than a corpus swap is the three-way decomposition, and specifically limb (a), recovering issue-era estimator bias by re-running the issue-era estimator on the issue-era record. No opened paper in either field has done it: P1 is absent on the decomposition and P2 declines it. That cuts both ways, because it is also why the first pass's fatal reading fails — nothing opened says the split is impossible — but an unoccupied limb is not yet an identified estimand, and at the near-zero expected counts the frame delivers, the identification has to be argued before the arithmetic. Second cap, independent of the first: attack 7 stands Unresolved from adversary 1's counterpart, because all three of the record's reason-for-silence mechanisms are refuted by opened primary sources and the replacement offered is "no one carried it across", which the protocol does not accept and which points the wrong way given hydrology's easier data. Either of those two holds the entry at Provisional on its own. For the record, the first pass's disguised-known rejection is withdrawn: the identical rate statistic on the identical artefact class is prior art in seismic hazard-map testing, which is why novelty is Medium rather than higher, but Q2 is not that statistic.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): read the hazard-map-testing literature first and on its own terms — P1, P2 and the CSEP/RELM-descended testing programme — and extract from opened text what it has and has not settled about separating model error from catalogue or record artefacts. The rate statistic is that field's and must not be re-derived as new; limb (a) is the part no opened paper in either field has executed, so it is where the question lives. After that, the smallest real frame is a single variable with dense gauging and dated issued values (UK FEH, or FEMA 1%-annual-chance discharges), with the spatial-dependence model and the frequency-reading classification both declared before any count is taken.
Promotion requires: four things. (1) Limb (a) identified in print — a sourced demonstration, on any hazard variable, that re-running an issue-era estimator on the issue-era record recovers the estimator's contribution separately from post-issue change, or a sourced statement that it cannot. Until one of those exists, attack 5 stays Partial and this is the ceiling. (2) The Tasan sentence, or any other posing sentence from the seismic literature, re-checked as a single string in the PDF, since the candidate's whole relation to that field turns on whether the attribution question is posed there as open. (3) A mechanism for the silence that is not "no one carried it across": the record's three mechanisms are refuted by opened sources, and attack 7 stands Unresolved on that account, which is a Provisional ceiling in its own right. (4) A declared spatial-dependence model, stated in advance, since P1's own handling was declustering that P1 itself called "fundamentally arbitrary" and the candidate's power claim rests on doing better than that.

Routing (if rejected as already-asked): n/a — the entry is not rejected, so there is nothing to route. Recorded for the successor: a routing row was considered for the sibling field's open attribution question and deliberately not written, because the best posing sentence available — Tasan's "the discrepancies between observations and predictions can generally have more than one explanation" — is hedged and was summariser-reported rather than re-checked as a single string, and the ledger's routing test requires a source that poses the problem as open in its own words.

ID: UQ-20261017-26
Date: 2026-10-17
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): AI architecture — inference systems and decoding algorithms (secondary: evaluation methodology / auditing)
Question (canonical): For one production serving engine and one open target/draft pair at fixed weights, precision, temperature and engine version, with the engine-level speculative-decoding switch as the treatment and matching defined at the request level (the target pass's tensor shape conceded as part of the treatment): what is the distributional distance D(spec-on, spec-off) on a fixed prompt set against a permutation null, what is the nuisance baseline D(spec-off, spec-off') under varied request composition, what is the excess (i)−(ii) with a CI, and does that excess exceed a pre-declared yardstick (one quantization step on the same instrument; the smallest benchmark difference the field publishes as a result)?
Alternative formulations:
1. Does turning speculative decoding on change what a served model actually samples, over and above the change caused by request/batch composition alone?
2. What is the measured size of the gap between "algorithmically lossless" and "lossless as served" for speculative decoding, as a two-sample distributional distance with a permutation null?
(Gate 1 reformulation used, for well-posedness only: the Gate 0 phrase "batch-composition-matched" named a match the mechanism forbids — the target pass scores K+1 rows, plain decode scores 1 — so matching moved to the request level and the shape difference into the treatment. Both versions in the record.)
Motivating gap: vLLM's spec-decode documentation ships a losslessness claim ("algorithmically validated to be lossless"; "theoretically lossless up to the precision limits of hardware numerics") beside its own statement that floating-point error and batch size may shift output distributions — i.e. it documents the failure of its own premise and asserts the residual is small without measuring it. The intake's further premise, that published spec-decode measurement is of acceptance rate and speedup rather than fidelity, is true of the systems literature (arXiv:2601.11580, opened: speedup, acceptance length, time breakdown, no fidelity endpoint) and false as a claim that the question is unasked.
Presuppositions: P1 target model's own sampling distribution well defined at fixed weights/precision/kernels — CONTESTED, conceded, hence the excess framing. P2 an adequately powered two-sample test for text-generating distributions exists — ESTABLISHED (arXiv:2410.20247, MMD + Hamming string kernel, median 77.4% power). P3 spec and non-spec paths can be run with all else fixed — FALSE as stated; survives only as request-level matching. Confirmed at first hand by adversary 1 from vLLM's own test comment ("verify-path matmul running at seqlen num_speculative_tokens+1 vs 1") and by adversary 2 from vLLM RFC #54506 ("nothing in the current stack guarantees those two produce identical bits"). P4 deployed endpoints evaluated as "the model" do use spec decoding — supported for engine defaults/self-hosted (#54785 calls MTP k=4 with graphs "the shipped default combination for our config"), partial for closed providers. P5 a deviation of this size would matter to someone — Gate 3's burden.
What would count as an answer: Pre-registered measurement on >=2 open target/draft pairs and >=2 engines reporting (a) D(spec-on, spec-off) with a permutation null; (b) D(spec-off, spec-off') with request composition varied; (c) the excess with a CI; (d) the excess against a known-size perturbation (one quantization step on the same instrument) and the smallest published benchmark gap. A null with a tight interval answers it as decisively as a positive. If large, one-at-a-time ablation names the responsible implementation choice.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 11 at Gate 2 + 9 by adversary 1 + 9 by adversary 2 = 29 distinct queries, full lists in batches/2026-10-17-1128/UQ-20261017-26-record.md and the two adversary files. Most informative: (1) "Is speculative decoding really lossless? empirical measurement of output distribution deviation" — the mandatory own-field own-words title query, first query of the run → arXiv:2607.17283, the near-duplicate. (9) "turning on speculative decoding changed model outputs evaluation regression production report quality shift" — the mandatory magnitude query → dev.to practitioner report with the number (1.2% of 2,000 greedy outputs differ on vLLM). (6/8) sampler-testing and Barbarik-lineage queries in the method-owning field's own words → mature machinery, no LLM-decoding application; the negative holds there. Adversary 1 query 2, "speculative decoding bit-exact reproducibility greedy outputs differ from target-only vLLM issue" → arXiv:2510.22876, the decisive hit the Gate 2 sweep missed. Adversary 2 G1/G3, GitHub issue search in the engine-maintainer vocabulary ("batch invariance speculative decoding forward pass M=1") → vLLM RFC #54506, body retrieved verbatim.
