Novelty confidence: Medium (re-graded at the late Gate 4, upward from the Low the first pass set, once every source behind that Low was read at first hand. The Low rested on five sources read as posing the question. MathArena poses retry-until-success against fixed-retries with no drop arm, and the sentence cited as its convention is the option its authors decline. Rollout Cards measures reporting prevalence over scored audit entries, and only one of its score movements is a denominator convention at all. Inspect documents both estimators without naming a default. AMLB settles drop-versus-penalize by argument inside AutoML, with its Section 6.4 unread. The Anthropic post publishes a failure share with no convention and no comparison. Two priors found late are closer than any of those - DeepSWE (arXiv:2607.07946) for the drop rule with a reported excluded share, arXiv:2605.10448 for the post-selection argument under Manski bounds - and neither compares conventions. Medium, not High: three actors take the decision in print and the bias argument is published, so only the cross-evaluation comparison is unoccupied.)
Significance — consequence: On the yes branch, affected published comparisons become uncitable as capability claims until recomputed and operators must publish the share and name the convention; on the no branch, the two estimators are interchangeable at current failure rates — a null worth having. Deflated: C has already shipped the actionable form of the yes branch, so the increment is sharpening a published rule of thumb into a per-comparison reversal list.
Significance — audience: Real and demonstrably acting in print, not a slogan — a lab published an infra-noise study and a configuration-matching rule, a government harness publishes a denominator policy, a JMLR benchmark paper spends a numbered subsection defending its convention on fairness-between-systems grounds, and the reporting-standards line (Rollout Cards, EvalCards, ReproEvalCard) exists for this class of undisclosed choice. Secondary: model developers whose gaps sit inside the failure share, procurement and safety-case readers. This is the strongest argument against novelty and the weakest against significance.
Significance — fecundity: Whether the harness-failure share is itself a model-dependent covariate worth reporting; whether benchmarks should pre-register an analysis population; whether IR incomplete-judgment estimators (bpref, condensed lists) transfer to harness-failure denominators — the one genuinely unexplored transplant surfaced; whether a declared convention changes the measured noise floor.
Significance — anchoring: Retry bias (A); AutoML failure imputation (B); infra noise and configuration matching (C); harness scoring policy (Inspect); convention census (Rollout Cards); disclosure audit (arXiv:2605.21404); failure localisation (arXiv:2607.28802); leaderboard non-orderability (arXiv:2609.17394, unopened); noise floors (arXiv:2608.22331, unopened); sparse-leaderboard rank identifiability (NeurIPS 2026, Kang). In-ledger: nearest are UQ-20261016-06, UQ-20261017-09, UQ-20261015-08, UQ-20261016-48; no near-duplicate.

The intake's disciplinary-boundary mechanism (clinical trials named ITT, evaluation has no analogue) is falsified as a mechanism: the name is absent but the question is posed in the field's own words and in at least two neighbouring fields, once peer-reviewed. The residual venue-and-credit gap (the pieces live in engineering posts, project pages and harness docs where an estimand search will not look) explains why the ANSWER is scattered, not why the question was never asked. Verification (post-batch, fresh-context checkers reading the cited priors at first hand, then a late Gate 4 of two literature surveys): four checks and two surveys ran. BOTH fatal grounds FALL - every source the rejection read as posing the question turns out to be something adjacent, and one was cited against its own authors' stated position - so the entry moves from Rejected to Provisional, capped by a newly sourced attack 5.
- MathArena (matharena.ai/retry) INVERTS the rejection's reading of it. The sentence the record cited as its convention, "If all attempts fail, the solution is marked as incorrect", is verbatim present but sits under the heading "Fixed number of retries:" - the option the authors explicitly decline: "We prefer the first strategy and do not report model performance until a sufficiently stable implementation is available." The choice is posed as TWO options ("There are two commonly used strategies for retrying failed requests:") and dropping the item is not one of them; the only denominator remark is that under a hard cutoff "the denominator may be zero", in which case "accuracy is undefined". So the article poses retry-until-success against fixed-retries, not drop against score-as-failure. The rest is confirmed: "frequent retries can overestimate performance by up to 5 percent on MathArena benchmarks" is verbatim, though percent-versus-percentage-points is never stated and neither "percentage points" nor "pp" occurs anywhere; the reversal is real - "GPT-5.1 outperforms DeepSeek-v3.2 at high stability levels, but the ranking reverses at lower stability" - but holds "under a maximum-time failure model" in simulation; and 8855 model-problem pairs is right (written without a thousands comma, Figure 1 caption). Three absences are now settled by reading rather than assumed: no real-data share of runs hit by a harness failure (the failure arms are simulated, and "our historical data did not record the time taken per request"), no drop-the-item arm, and no count of publications stating their convention.
- Rollout Cards (arXiv:2605.12131) does not census what the record said it censuses. "None of the 50 repositories reports how often rollouts failed alongside the accuracy or score." is verbatim, as are the three counts - "In our audit, 11 scored entries silently absorb catastrophic failures into the reported score,", "31 drop failures with no visible counter", "9 log failures somewhere but do not surface them beside the reported score." - but they are over SCORED AUDIT ENTRIES rather than repositories, which the paper says itself ("Counts are over scored audit entries rather than mutually exclusive repositories;", with simple-evals split across two subsets), and 11 + 31 + 9 = 51 against 50 repositories. It measures what repositories report and do - reporting prevalence - not the share of runs hit by a harness failure. Its score movements come from a separate re-grading study of archived outputs, and only ONE is a denominator convention: SWE-bench Verified with missing patches counted as failures versus excluded, 15.6 against 13.3, a 2.3-point gap. The headline "can change reported scores by 20.9 absolute percentage points" is MLE-Bench under a success-threshold rule, and the 16.9-point tau-bench move that "reverses the GPT-4o versus Claude 3.5 Sonnet ordering" is a grader choice. The paper also imposes no requirement to disclose a failure rate beside a denominator rule. Disclosed: this check used 7 WebFetch calls against a cap of 6, and the paper's appendices were not reached.
- AMLB and Inspect are confirmed as what they are, and one read failed. AMLB (JMLR 25:101, arXiv:2207.12560) Section 5.1.3 is verbatim on both its rule and its reason - "we impute missing values with the constant predictor, or prior.", "a very penalizing imputation strategy", frameworks that fail "may fail on harder tasks or folds and consequently obtain higher average performance estimates", and the aim of being "fairer towards the well-behaved frameworks" - which is AutoML's drop-versus-penalize decision settled by argument, with no sensitivity analysis in any text that could be read. Section 6.4 COULD NOT BE READ: every route caps at 80,389 characters inside Section 6.3 (the JMLR PDF and its offsets, ar5iv, the arXiv PDF), alphaxiv's markdown is a short rendering ending near 74,000 characters inside Section 6.2, arxiv.org/html returned HTTP 429 twice with an instruction not to retry, and the GitHub and curl routes are closed to this session. Only headings 6.1, 6.2 and 6.3 were ever seen, so even the EXISTENCE of a Section 6.4 is unverified here and no absence may be claimed for it, though the abstract does promise a "framework failures" analysis somewhere. Inspect AI's scoring-policy page is confirmed on the column the record cited - the "Counts in denominator?" table, CORRECT 1.0 yes, INCORRECT 0.0 yes, a raised error n/a no, Score.unscored() NaN no, and the worked 1/2 becoming 1/3 once score_on_error is enabled - but it is documentation rather than a study, and it labels NO single policy the default: fail_on_error is True, score_on_error is opt-in, errored samples default to excluded, and INCORRECT and NOANSWER default to 0.0 inside the denominator. Disclosed: this check also used 7 WebFetch calls against a cap of 6, the extra one being a refused offset call that returned nothing.
- The Anthropic infrastructure-noise post is confirmed on its numbers and confirmed NOT to be this question. Infra error rates of 5.8% at strict enforcement, 2.1% at 3x headroom and 0.5% uncapped are present, with "The drop between strict enforcement to 3x headroom (5.8% to 2.1%) was significant at p < 0.001.", "At uncapped resources, the total lift over 1x is +6 percentage points (p < 0.01).", the earlier calibration figure "as many as 6% of tasks were failing because of pod errors," and the advice that "leaderboard differences below 3 percentage points deserve skepticism". But it states no denominator rule of its own and compares no conventions, and one of its findings cuts against the candidate's mechanism: "Most of the tasks that were crashing at 1x would have failed regardless".
- Late Gate 4, survey A - two new priors, both closer than anything in the record, neither doing limb (b). DeepSWE (arXiv:2607.07946) excludes infrastructure-failure rollouts "from both the numerator and the denominator of every metric" and reports the excluded share per configuration, ranging "from 0%" to "5.3% (Gemini 3 Flash)" over 7,174 scored rollouts and 16 configurations, while asserting that "the leaderboard ordering is not sensitive to the rule" with no arm-by-arm comparison shown - which is precisely the claim limb (b) would test. arXiv:2605.10448 applies Manski-style partial identification to records whose outcome it cannot verify, bounding performance as Perf in [P/N, (P+U)/N], keeps them in the denominator ("We therefore keep Unknown records in the same set of completed records"), argues that dropping them "can create agent-dependent post-selection" - limb (d)'s argument, in the clinical-trials vocabulary the record thought was doing no work - and reports Unknown shares of 50.0% on AndroidWorld, 16.7% on AgentDojo, 0.3% on tau3-retail and 0.0% on AppWorld and MiniWoB, about 7.2% overall (92 of 1282). Its object is UNVERIFIABLE outcomes, not harness crashes: "only infrastructure or pre-run failures are excluded from N". So the bias argument and a bounding method are both in print on a different failure class, with no three-way comparison, no reporting standard requiring the disclosure, and no sentence posing the candidate's question.
- Late Gate 4, survey B - attack 5 is now the cap, UNRESOLVED, and non-fatal, so the ceiling is Provisional. The harness-versus-model partition the question rests on does not survive at the edges, and the shipped tooling shows where it breaks. MASEval's default counts AgentError inside the score while excluding EnvironmentError, UserError and TaskTimeoutError, turning a reported 60/100 into 60/92 = 65.22%, and names the boundary it draws ("Validation failures indicate agent-provided bad input", "Execution failures after validation indicate infrastructure issues"). Harbor's trial-result API exposes only ExceptionInfo with exception_type, exception_message, exception_traceback and occurred_at, with no field separating infrastructure from agent failure. Inspect's log format carries a run status of started, success or error plus a per-sample error, and nothing at the harness-versus-model level in the page read. Unparseable output, malformed tool calls, model-caused timeouts, self-triggered rate limits and self-crashed sandboxes all sit on the line. Underneath that is an objection the candidate never answers: it says "holding the estimand fixed" without declaring WHICH estimand, and the two readings disagree about which estimator is correct rather than about its value - under model-only capability a harness failure is missing data and dropping is right, under deployed model-plus-scaffold performance it is a real outcome and scoring it as failure is right. Limb (a) is therefore only partly executable from released logs, and mostly not at the class level a validated taxonomy needs. Both surveys read through a page summariser and most search hits were titles only, so their negatives are bounded.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 3/3 (significance raised from 2/3 at the late Gate 4: three independent actors now take this decision in print, and one of them, DeepSWE, asserts the exact rank-insensitivity limb (b) would measure without showing an arm, over 7,174 rollouts and 16 configurations, while MASEval ships a default that moves a reported 60/100 to 60/92. Well-posedness held at 2/3 and not lowered further: attack 5's gap is an undeclared estimand, repairable by one sentence of pre-registration, not a failure of identification.)
Strongest remaining objection: vagueness, Unresolved and now sourced in shipped tooling. The harness-versus-model partition is not clean at the edges - unparseable output, malformed tool calls, model-caused timeouts, self-triggered rate limits, self-crashed sandboxes - and the harnesses draw it differently where they draw it at all: MASEval excludes EnvironmentError, UserError and TaskTimeoutError while keeping AgentError in the score, Harbor's trial-result API carries no field distinguishing the two, and Inspect records a status and a per-sample error but nothing at that level. Worse, the question says "holding the estimand fixed" without saying which estimand, and the two readings disagree about which estimator is CORRECT rather than merely about its value: if the target is model-only capability, a harness failure is missing data and the drop estimator is right; if the target is deployed model-plus-scaffold performance, it is a real outcome and scoring it as failure is right. Until that is declared, limb (b) measures the distance between two estimators of two different quantities. Two secondary objections stand, both non-fatal. Limb (a) is only partly recoverable from released logs and mostly not at the class level the taxonomy needs. And the reason-for-silence mechanism, restored once attack 2 fell, is thin: an artifact-and-audience boundary (the conventions live in harness manuals, a vendor engineering post and an AutoML journal subsection rather than in the LLM-evaluation literature) plus the recency of released per-item error fields, while "nobody posed it as an estimand across evaluations" still restates the gap instead of explaining it.
Promotion requires: (1) declaring the estimand - model-only capability or deployed model-plus-scaffold performance - and with it whether a harness failure is missing data or an outcome, so limb (b) compares two estimators of one quantity; (2) pre-declaring an equivalence margin and power for the "no reversal survives resampling" endpoint, which the first pass already called repairable; (3) showing on one released log set that the harness-versus-model class is recoverable at all, since MASEval is the only tool read that draws the line in its defaults while Harbor and Inspect expose no such field; and (4) closing AMLB Section 6.4, still unread after six routes and promised a "framework failures" analysis by the paper's own abstract, and reading arXiv:2608.22331, arXiv:2609.17394, arXiv:2511.21695 and arXiv:2609.04298 in full - any of which could move the grade either way.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only - do not take it): declare the estimand in one sentence, then do the cheap half first - take the evaluations that already release per-item error fields, recompute each score under both conventions, and count pairwise rank reversals. DeepSWE is the natural first target, because it reports its excluded share per configuration over 7,174 rollouts and 16 configurations and asserts rank-insensitivity without showing the arms, so the comparison it skipped can be run against its own released numbers.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): WITHDRAWN as moot. The entry is no longer Rejected, and a Provisional entry's own question is not routed, so nothing goes to ledger/routed-open-problems.md. The AMLB Section 6.4 read and the four unread papers belong to this entry's promotion condition, not to the research workstream.

ID: UQ-20261017-31
Date: 2026-10-17
Status: Provisional
Verdict history: Rejected at Gate 2 on novelty Low and confirmed at Gate 4 by adversary 1 grading Disguise Unresolved; moved to Provisional post-batch when verification refuted the prior that carried the kill and a late Gate 4 re-ran all eight attacks. Source method: anomaly mining.
Domain(s): Biology — single-cell genomics methodology, tissue-atlas composition. Adjacent: compositional data analysis; two-phase/destructive-sampling estimation.
Question (canonical): V1 (scored as canonical, retained per Gate 1): in droplet scRNA-seq of dissociated tissue, is the ambient-RNA ("soup") profile a quantitative record of the cell types destroyed during dissociation — does deconvolving it against a pre-declared reference recover the identity and relative mass of the lost populations well enough to correct that run's cell-type composition estimate? V2 (Gate 1 reformulation, well-posedness only): for a tissue block split across modalities, does the soup profile — deconvolved against a pre-declared signature matrix, converted from RNA mass to cell counts via independently measured per-type RNA content and per-type degradation — give a per-type missing-count estimate whose calibration slope on the (in-situ minus droplet) deficit is distinguishable from 0 and from 1, with interval?
Alternative formulations: Can the RNA in the empty droplets tell us which cells the dissociation killed, and in what proportion? / Treating ambient RNA as a destructive-sampling byproduct rather than contamination, how accurate is a soup-based estimator of composition loss against matched snRNA-seq or in-situ counts of the same block?
Motivating gap: Intake joined two routinely reported facts — every droplet run carries soup, and dissociation destroys cell types differentially — and asserted nobody had tested whether the soup matches the profiled cells. Gate 2 found that assertion false: Janssen et al. (Genome Biology 2023) deconvolve the empty-droplet profile against a cell-type reference, report that "the contamination profiles do not always reflect the cell type proportions of the sample", and interpret the shift as PT cells being "more vulnerable to dissociation procedure than other cell types". The gap as written does not exist.
Presuppositions: (1) soup comes predominantly from dissociation lysis — CONTESTED (nuclei-surface adhesion, erythrocyte leakage, pre-existing extracellular RNA); (2) soup indexes WHICH cells were lost, not how much RNA survivors carry — CONTESTED and contradicted in print (Caglayan: ambient profile "primarily from the most abundant cell types"); (3) lysate mRNA degrades in a modellable, type-specific way — CONTESTED nuisance; (4) an orthogonal reference (snRNA-seq, in situ) measures truth more faithfully — CONTESTED, must be pre-declared with its own error; (5) soup well mixed across a run — partly testable; (6) published proportions are load-bearing for atlas and DA claims — established; (7) enough archived datasets retain empty-droplet barcodes for a retrospective limb — CONTESTED and UNQUANTIFIED, no published denominator found.
What would count as an answer: pre-registered benchmark over K tissues, one block measured three ways (droplet scRNA-seq with empty droplets retained; snRNA-seq; orthogonal in-situ count), soup deconvolved against a pre-declared signature matrix. YES = soup-derived missing mass per type tracks the (in-situ minus droplet) deficit above a pre-declared threshold, calibration slope and interval reported, type-dependent degradation modelled. NO = soup statistically indistinguishable from a weighted average of recovered cells once degradation and per-type RNA content are accounted for. Deliverable either way: the shift in published proportions after soup-based correction, with the archival denominator stated.

Nat Commun 2018, the same deconvolve-then-convert-to-cell-equivalents design on cfDNA; adversary Chinese-language sweep → ambient-decontamination benchmark (bioRxiv 2026.01.13.699237), gene-level only. Also opened: DIEM (Alvarez et al., Sci Rep 10:11019, 2020) and Moss et al., Nat Commun 9:5068 (2018).
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs P1 — only in the second limb. P1 performs the candidate's central operation (deconvolve the empty-droplet profile against a cell-type reference, compare with captured-cell composition) and publishes both the mismatch and the differential-destruction reading. Four attributes do differ (estimand: within-profile proportions vs per-type missing count and calibration slope; reference: the run's own cells, which structurally cannot contain unrecovered types, vs a pre-declared signature matrix plus external in-situ truth; unit: pseudobulk per replicate vs a split block measured three ways; endpoint: correlation/fractions vs slope with interval and the induced shift in published proportions), and P1 models neither degradation nor per-type RNA content — but these separate V2 from P1, and V1 and the motivating gap do not survive it. vs P2 — gene-set enrichment, sorted-dataset reference, and an alternative explanation (transcript abundance, not destruction) the candidate's design must defeat rather than a weaker version of it. vs P3 — measures how much soup there is as a QC score; supplies the nuclei-surface-adhesion source that breaks presupposition 1.
Novelty confidence: Medium (re-graded post-verification, upward from Low). The Low rested on P1 running the deconvolution the question names against a cell-type reference; verification shows P1's reference is the run's own recovered cells — "the endogenous single cell allele counts from the respective replicate were used as reference (qcthreshold = 0.6)" — which structurally cannot contain an unrecovered type, so P1 does not perform the candidate's central operation and both adversaries were wrong on the decisive attribute. DIEM's independent-corroboration leg fails too: its cell-type-specific debris claim rests on a supplementary figure that two later passes could not open by any route, and its one named case is attributed to "nuclei isolation or the snRNA-seq assay". Across 46 queries in three passes (11 at Gate 2, 19 across the two adversaries, 16 across the two late surveys), nothing opened deconvolves an ambient profile against an external reference or compares such a composition with an independent measure of what was destroyed. Medium and not High because two widely deployed tools publish modelling assumptions that pre-commit the answer in the NO direction — SoupX's "approximately uniform sampling of the cells in the sequencing batch" with background-to-cell expression correlations of 0.71-0.96 (median 0.86), and CellBender's ambient profile as "a weighted average of total expression" — so the answer is widely assumed rather than unconsidered. The narrowed V2 estimand remains unasked by everything opened.
Significance — consequence: YES would turn the ambient toolchain's discarded quantity into an in-run, retrospective correction for the field's largest known composition bias and give compositional-DA tools a loss term none now has; NO would vindicate SoupX's construction for composition purposes and push composition claims permanently onto orthogonal references. Discounted: P1 made the crude YES observation three years ago and nothing acted on it, so what is unknown is the interpretation, not the mismatch.
Significance — audience: atlas consortia reporting proportions; compositional-DA tool authors (scCODA, DCATS, milo, voomCLR, scDC); ambient-tool authors (SoupX, CellBender, DecontX, scAR), for whom YES inverts the objective from removal to joint estimation; core facilities, who would gain a per-run loss readout from data they already delete. Real but narrow — and it is the same groups that read P1 and did not act.
Significance — fecundity: per-type RNA content and per-type degradation become publishable estimable quantities; soup becomes a cross-protocol QC readout of which populations a dissociation destroys; a deposition standard for unfiltered matrices gains a justification and a computable denominator; the two-phase-sampling framing raises whether the soup's own capture is informative.
Significance — anchoring: the sc/sn and sc/in-situ composition discrepancy; the reference-frame problem in compositional differential abundance; masked rare cell types (P2); the uncomputed archival denominator for raw droplet data.
Reason for silence: offered mechanisms do not hold. Role boundary inside the subfield is refuted by P1 and DIEM, which both crossed it, asked the qualitative question and stopped. "The needed estimator family is absent from the toolkit" is refuted on sourced grounds: deconvolving a free nucleic-acid pool against a pre-declared reference and converting fractions to per-cell equivalents is Moss et al. 2018, inside genomics. What remains is that the calibration limb is expensive and weakly identified — a reason for no answer, not for no asking, which the Gate 4 rule excludes and which makes the novelty finding itself suspect.

Verification (post-batch, three fresh-context checkers reading the cited priors at first hand, then a late Gate 4 of two literature surveys plus two residual reads): seven reads ran. The fatal ground FALLS — the prior the rejection rested on does not do what both adversaries said it does — so the entry moves from Rejected to Provisional, capped by two newly sourced non-fatal attacks.
- P1 (Janssen et al., Genome Biology 24:140) does NOT deconvolve against a cell-type reference in the candidate's sense. Methods, "Comparison of endogenous, contamination, and empty droplet profiles": "we used the deconvolution method implemented in SCDC[16]" and "the endogenous single cell allele counts from the respective replicate were used as reference (qcthreshold = 0.6)". The reference is the run's OWN recovered cells, so by construction it cannot contain a type the run failed to recover — which is the quantity V1 asks about. The record's own P1 description had this right ("reference = the run's own recovered cells"); the Gate 4 kill contradicted it.
- P1's "differential destruction" reading is one hedged side remark, and the paper's other arm points the other way. The sentence is "suggesting that this cell type is more vulnerable to dissociation procedure than other cell types", attached to a SLIGHT proximal-tubule enrichment in empty droplets in the scRNA-seq arm; the snRNA-seq arm shows "a clear shift in cell type composition with a decreased PT fraction". The compositional comparison itself is qualitative — "the cell type compositions inferred for endogenous, contamination and empty counts are by and large similar" — with no correlation coefficients and no per-type proportion table. No missing count, no composition correction, no calibration: sweeps for "missing", "calibrat", "lost", "destroyed", "lysed" and "in situ" returned no occurrences, and the only composition-adjacent statement is that background removal "changes the classification of only very few cells".
- P1's supplement COULD NOT READ, so even the figure cited for the PT shift (Fig. S6) is second-hand. Routes failed: doi.org (HTTP 429, instructed not to refetch), static-content.springer.com MOESM1 (ROBOTS_DISALLOWED), genomebiology.biomedcentral.com (302), link.springer.com article page twice (opened, no Supplementary Information section rendered). The preprint's Fig. 3C legend fixes the output form: "The stacked barplots depict the estimated fraction of each cell type in the profile as inferred by SCDC" — bar charts, no numeric table.
- DIEM's independent-corroboration leg FAILS the same way. Its claim is "we found that the debris clusters formed by all filtering methods exhibited cell type-specific expression (Fig. S12b-e)", resting on a supplementary figure a dedicated second pass could not open by any route (nature.com twice, a pattern-guessed static-content MOESM1 returning ROBOTS_DISALLOWED, the bioRxiv preprint which carries only Supp Figs 1-7, and par.nsf.gov, main text only). Its one named case is hedged and attributed elsewhere: "This suggests that CD14+ macrophages are more susceptible to damage or contamination", which "may imply that nuclei isolation or the snRNA-seq assay may introduce a bias in cell type capture". Its 5.8% and 4.5% are percentages of differentially expressed genes, not of composition.
- P2 (Caglayan et al.) measures gene-set enrichment against a sorted dataset — "Enrichment of ambient cluster markers with annotated cell types were done using Fisher's exact test from GeneOverlap package", with "we utilized a NeuN-sorted snRNA-seq dataset for comparison" — and supplies the candidate's competing explanation in its own words: "This is likely because of transcriptomic abundance of neurons compared to other cell types in brain tissue", and "an ambient RNA profile is primarily from the most abundant cell types". No deconvolution, no per-type missing count, no composition correction.
Late Gate 4 (required once the fatal ground fell; the first pass's adversaries cannot grade a record they are part of). The two cold eight-attack adversaries were expected to die at launch as twelve did across the 09:20 and 11:28 batches, so the pass ran in the documented fallback form: two fresh-context literature surveys asking neutral questions whose ANSWERS decide the attacks, with the judge applying the Gate 4 rule to what came back. That is a disclosed departure from LEDGER.md's adversary form — it keeps cold context and two independent readers and gives up the adversary's own framing. Logs: UQ-20261017-31-lategate4-lit-a.md and -lit-b.md (16 queries, 12 fetches).
- Attack 2 (Disguise) now RESOLVED. Survey a: no study deconvolves an ambient or empty-droplet profile against an EXTERNAL cell-type reference (NOT FOUND over 9 searches and 4 reads); none compares such a composition against independent ground truth; none publishes a per-cell-type dissociation-loss estimate or a composition correction. The closest opened work is Denisenko et al. 2020, which measures per-type proportion SHIFTS across protocols (podocytes 2.78% cold vs 0.03% warm dissociation; immune cells 6.03% sc vs 0.73% sn) using bulk deconvolution as an indirect check and applying no correction, and Andrews et al. 2021, which measures ambient magnitude with SoupX and reports no spatial percentages. Bounded negatives, each stated with what was opened.
- Attack 4 (Presupposition failure) RESOLVED, not fatal. Survey b found the ambient pool's origin ASSERTED and nowhere apportioned — DropletQC's "predominantly caused by lysis of cells during sample preparation", CellBender's "ruptured or degraded cells, residual cytoplasmic debris" — with alternative origins named across the same sources (exogenous contamination and unbound antibody, un-removed extra-nuclear material in snRNA-seq, red blood cells and necrosis in solid tissue), and no source apportioning the pool among them. Presupposition 1 is therefore unmeasured in both directions; and since V1 asks WHETHER the soup records what was destroyed, the exposed presupposition is the candidate's own endpoint rather than a premise it smuggles.
- Attack 6 (Significance inflation) now UNRESOLVED and sourced. Two deployed tools already answer the question in the NO direction, as a modelling assumption: SoupX's soup is "approximately uniform sampling of the cells in the sequencing batch", supported by background-to-cell expression correlations of 0.71-0.96 with a median of 0.86, and CellBender's ambient profile is "a weighted average of total expression", demonstrated on heart data where cardiomyocytes carry "an order of magnitude higher UMI counts than other cell types" and "the top genes in terms of removed fraction are in fact associated mainly with cardiomyocytes". The one published counter-signal is CellBender's own aside that in PBMC "ambient counts might be enriched with granulocyte lysates" although granulocytes are absent from the clusters, with "cell types do not necessarily contribute equally to ambient RNA". So the quantity is live and unmeasured, but the field has already built on an answer, which lowers what measuring it would change.
- Attack 8 (Dissolution) UNRESOLVED and non-fatal, and the harder cap. V1's "quantitative record" needs a per-type conversion from RNA mass to cell counts, and survey a found none available: per-cell-type mRNA content is unmeasured for any solid tissue in anything opened, the one candidate source (Monaco et al. 2019, PBMC immune types) COULD NOT READ after its publisher redirect consumed the fetch budget, and the cell-size-aware deconvolution paper reports no measured per-type content while stating that tissues contain "cell types with substantially different cell sizes, total mRNA expression". Without that conversion the YES and NO arms are not separable from per-type RNA content and per-type degradation — the two quantities the record already concedes P1 does not model. This is UNVERIFIED on the decisive source rather than refuted, so under the standing rule it caps at Provisional and does not reject.
- Attacks 1, 3, 5 and 7 are unchanged from the first pass; nothing in the verification or the two surveys bore on them.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3 (unchanged; both clear the Provisional threshold, and what holds the entry below Validated is the pair of Unresolved non-fatal attacks above together with Medium rather than High novelty)
Strongest remaining objection (rewritten post-verification): the question is unanswered, and the field has already built on an answer to it. SoupX, the most used background tool in this area, rests on the soup being "approximately uniform sampling of the cells in the sequencing batch" and supports that with background-to-cell expression correlations of 0.71-0.96 (median 0.86); CellBender models the ambient profile as "a weighted average of total expression" and demonstrates it on heart data where the top removed genes track the highest-UMI cell type. Measuring the candidate's quantity is therefore testing a deployed modelling assumption rather than opening an unconsidered one, and NO is the direction two toolchains presuppose. Compounding it, the measurement is not yet identified: converting ambient RNA mass to cells destroyed needs per-type mRNA content, published for no solid tissue in anything opened across three passes, so the YES and NO arms stay confounded with per-type RNA content and per-type degradation.
Promotion requires: (1) an independently measured per-type mRNA-content conversion for the tissue under test, or a design that estimates it inside the experiment, so a composition mismatch is attributable to cells rather than to transcripts per cell — and the one candidate source, Monaco et al. 2019, opened and graded, since it covers PBMC immune types and may not transfer to a solid tissue; (2) the two unreadable supplements resolved, DIEM's Fig. S12b-e and Janssen's Additional file 1, because the first is the entire published basis for cell-type-specific debris and the second holds the only numeric form of P1's composition comparison; (3) the archival denominator the record names, the share of deposited droplet datasets retaining empty-droplet barcodes, which bounds the retrospective arm; and (4) a stated position on attack 6 — what a measured answer changes for a field whose two main background tools already assume one. Nothing less promotes it: (1) is what makes the estimand identifiable and (4) is what makes it worth estimating.
SUPERSEDED (kept for the record): Janssen et al., Genome Biology 2023 already does the thing the canonical question asks about — deconvolves the empty-droplet profile against a cell-type reference, finds its composition does not match the sample's, and publishes the differential-dissociation-vulnerability reading — with DIEM 2020 reaching the same qualitative conclusion from debris droplets. V1 is therefore an answered question in its own field's own words, independently of whether V2's calibration slope has ever been measured; adversary 1 graded Disguise Unresolved on exactly that ground, which is fatal on its own.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): relocated by verification, and it is now a reanalysis rather than an experiment. Take a published dataset with both an scRNA-seq and an snRNA-seq arm on the same tissue block, deconvolve the empty-droplet profile against the UNION atlas instead of the run's own recovered cells, and test which of the two published answers the residual follows: abundance times transcript content, as SoupX and CellBender assume, or the types the snRNA-seq arm recovers and the scRNA-seq arm loses, as the candidate supposes. That discriminates the deployed assumption from the candidate's hypothesis on data already in hand, and the archival denominator (share of deposited droplet datasets retaining empty-droplet barcodes) should be computed alongside it, since it bounds the retrospective arm.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): NOT ROUTED, on a changed ground. The Gate 5 reason — an answered, disguised-known rejection — is withdrawn with the kill: verification shows P1 neither performed the measurement nor published the inference as the entry claimed. The entry is now Provisional, and a Provisional entry's own question is not routed, because the ledger is still claiming it as un-asked and filing it in the research queue as an already-asked problem would contradict this entry's own status. The verification residuals above belong to this entry's promotion condition, not to research.

ID: UQ-20261017-32
Date: 2026-10-17
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): Biology — macroecology, comparative physiology, trait-data curation. Method-owning neighbours: evidence synthesis (double counting, unit-of-analysis error), survey methodology (design effect, effective N), bibliometrics, provenance metadata.
Question (canonical): [R1, the single permitted Gate 1 reformulation and the operative form] For D >= 2 species-level trait databases declared in advance (Genoud et al.'s mammal BMR compilation, AnAge, the Amniote Life History Database, PanTHERIA/TetrapodTraits, FishBase, TRY) and M >= 3 pre-registered published allometric or life-history fits on them, with the analysis plan and the written definition of a "primary determination" frozen before tracing: (i) what share of the records entering each fit resolve, under a written citation-chain protocol with a dual-coded subsample and a reported agreement statistic, to a primary determination shared with at least one other record in the same fit, and what share is unresolvable (reported separately); (ii) what design effect and effective sample size does that source-cluster structure imply; (iii) how far do the fitted exponent and its interval move under a provenance-clustered error model (cluster-robust by primary source, or a random effect per primary source) against the published fit; and (iv) how much of that cluster structure is already absorbed by the phylogenetic covariance PGLS assumes? [V0 at intake asked the same with "deduplicated to primary sources and weighted by provenance" and no frozen protocol.]
Alternative formulations: How many independent measurements actually lie behind a comparative dataset of N species, and does the effective sample size change the allometric exponent? · Is comparative biology's degrees-of-freedom count inflated by citation chains converging on one original measurement, and does correcting for that move the exponents the field argues about?
Motivating gap: Comparative fits over species-level compilations treat one row per species as one observation and correct non-independence for phylogeny alone. The untested presupposition is measurement independence: that rows descend from distinct primary determinations rather than from shared handbook or secondary-compilation ancestry. CORRECTION carried from Gate 2: the intake claim that nobody has looked is partly false — Genoud, Isler & Martin (2018) traced 1739 BMR entries for 817 species to 946 original publications (95% read, 57 entries unresolvable) and reported exponent movement across data selections; Farrell-Gray & Gotelli (2005) named shared data as a second, non-phylogenetic non-independence inside the 2/3-vs-3/4 dispute. The residue claimed as un-asked was only the estimand: cluster structure -> design effect -> provenance-clustered refit.
Presuppositions: (1) enough per-record source metadata for primary-source resolution at scale — CONTESTED, partly relieved by Genoud's 3.3% unresolvable; (2) "primary determination" is definable as a reported measurement on specified individuals — CONTESTED, and the gate this entry failed at; (3) shared sources induce correlated error — established as statistics, magnitude unknown here; (4) published exponents are consequential — established; (5) phylogenetic correction does not already absorb the clustering — CONTESTED, limb (iv) measures it; (6) published intervals are narrow enough for a clustered refit to cross a decisive threshold — SUPPORTED for Genoud's SELECT fit only (0.729 +/- 0.010 S.E.; a design effect of 2 readmits 0.75 — judge's and adversaries' arithmetic on his S.E., which he reports instead of CIs).
What would count as an answer: a provenance audit with the plan frozen before tracing, reporting (i) the shared-source share and the unresolvable share separately, (ii) implied design effect and effective N, (iii) refitted exponent and interval under a provenance-clustered error model against the published fit, (iv) congruence between the source-cluster partition and the phylogenetic covariance. Presupposition harmless = effective N within a pre-declared fraction of nominal N with exponents moving less than their published CIs; presupposition fails = exponents moving outside them, or intervals widening past the margins that separate competing scaling predictions. A null is usable: an explicit licence for one-row-per-species independence over the audited relationships.
Novelty — queries run (query -> one-line result): 30 documented distinct queries — 12 at Gate 2 (full list and 5 fetch outcomes in batches/2026-10-17-1421/UQ-20261017-32-record.md), 9 by adversary 1 and 9 by adversary 2 in vocabularies Gate 2 had not tried (full lists in UQ-20261017-32-adversary-1.md and -2.md). Most informative: "non-independence of trait data in comparative analyses shared original sources inflate sample size allometric exponent" -> Farrell-Gray & Gotelli 2005 (opened, decisive); "basal metabolic rate compilation mammals how many values traced to original measurement" -> Genoud et al. 2018 (opened and independently re-verified verbatim by adversary 2); '"design effect" cluster-robust standard errors data source clustering macroecology ... effective sample size' -> survey-statistics machinery only, zero comparative-biology application; "what fraction of records in plant trait database are duplicates of the same original measurement TRY duplicate detection" -> tooling only, and rtry_remove_dup keys on the within-database OrigObsDataID, not on an external primary source (adversary 1 confirmed by code search); ecological-meta-analysis sweep -> Song et al. 2020 Ecology e03184 (opened: fits paper-level random effects over effect sizes but explicitly assumes within-study error independence, i.e. sets aside the shared-data correlation at issue); FishBase MainRef/DataRef sweep, food-composition "borrowed values", evaluated-nuclear-data shared-normalisation covariances, German-language Quellenkritik, Hurlbert pseudoreplication, library-science citation propagation -> all negative. PRIOR 2 Farrell-Gray CC, Gotelli NJ (2005) "Allometric exponents support a 3/4-power scaling law", Ecology 86(8):2083-2087 (opened at uvm.edu; unit = one published exponent, n = 22, endpoint = the exponent, comparator = 2/3 vs 3/4 by likelihood, estimand = the common exponent and its CI; names "a second kind of nonindependence ... because data on the same species are sometimes used in multiple studies"). PRIOR 3 prepR4pcm vignette "Assembling mammal trait databases for phylogenetic comparative models" (opened at a CRAN mirror; unit = one source record per species/trait/database, endpoint = a merged analysis-ready table, no comparator, no estimand; merges by median across source records, counts database names as "sources").
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs PRIOR 1 — same field, corpus type and endpoint, different stratifier and estimand (measurement conditions vs shared origin); Genoud demonstrates the feasibility presupposition, does not report entries per publication (verified in his text by adversary 2), and discards cluster identity by taking "one of them ... chosen randomly". vs PRIOR 2 — the same presupposition at a different unit: FGG's non-independence is one species recurring across pooled studies, remedied by species-disjoint pairing; the candidate's claimed clusters span different species inside one database, which that remedy does not touch, and FGG reports no fraction, design effect or effective N. vs PRIOR 3 — not a study of the question but evidence of the practice it targets. Negative taken in the method-owning field's own words (survey statistics, evidence synthesis): design effect, cluster-robust SEs, double counting of populations, sample-overlap generalized weights all exist and none is applied to species-level trait compilations.
Novelty confidence: Medium — two opened same-field priors come at the presupposition from different angles and neither computes the estimand; 18 further new-vocabulary queries across two adversaries found no provenance-clustered refit of a species-level trait fit, and the record's own named highest kill risk (ecological meta-analysis having fitted source as a random effect over a trait compilation) was searched in that literature's words and not found. Both adversaries executed their Disguise sweeps, so Disguise is verified, not unverified; adversary 1 graded it Partial only because Kattge 2020 could not be opened on either route. Medium is not the reason for this rejection.
Significance — consequence: if shared-source clusters are large and span species, effective N for headline fits falls and intervals widen; Genoud's published claim that SELECT's 95% interval excludes both 3/4 and 2/3 (verified verbatim) rests entirely on interval width, and a design effect of 2 retracts it. A null licenses one-row-per-species independence explicitly for the audited relationships, which nobody can currently issue.
Significance — audience: comparative-methods developers (PGLS / phylogenetic measurement-error line), trait-database curators (AusTraits, FishBase, TRY already store per-record sources), metabolic-scaling theorists. Adversary 2 judged land-surface modellers and conservation prioritisers to be inflation; the concrete, sourced stake is one audience, not five.
Significance — fecundity: provenance-weighted estimators for compiled data; optimal re-measurement targeting (which new determination raises effective N most); whether data papers should report independent-determination counts rather than record counts; whether provenance and phylogenetic covariance are jointly identifiable at all (limb iv).
Significance — anchoring: the 2/3-vs-3/4 dispute and its sample-composition sensitivity; the trait-imputation circularity criticism (Gorne et al. 2025, now read); FishBase parameter-error audits; the non-independence tradition from Felsenstein 1985.
Reason for silence: claimed as a disciplinary boundary (the field's non-independence reflex is phylogenetic; the needed vocabulary sits in survey statistics and evidence synthesis) plus an incentive/labour gap (946 originals read for reliability, cluster structure discarded) with an instrument component (persistent per-record source IDs are recent). Both adversaries found this explains why the question was not ANSWERED, not why it was not ASKED: FGG asked it qualitatively in 2005 and Genoud named compilation-combination noise in 2018 in lines adversary 2 opened and verified.
Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status) — two independent fresh-context adversaries (A1, A2); full logs in UQ-20261017-32-adversary-1.md and -2.md:
1. Triviality | limbs (i)-(ii) are arithmetic on Genoud's published table (1739/946 = 1.84 entries per publication) and the refit is an afternoon's work | defeated from the source itself: Genoud does not report entries per publication, the mean does not bound the design effect (size-weighted mean can give effective cluster size near 9 at the same ratio), and his stated reason for multiple entries per paper is intraspecific, which a species-level fit discards; limbs (iii)-(iv) exist nowhere | Resolved (A1), Resolved (A2)
2. Disguise | renamed "study as a random effect", "duplicate detection", or cross-study "data-set overlap" | 18 new-vocabulary queries across both adversaries, 6 pages opened; nearest new prior Song et al. 2020 explicitly assumes away the shared-data correlation; BAAD is individual-level, TRY duplicates are same-observation, Dodds/FGG are cross-study; negative real but incomplete for A1 because Kattge 2020 could not be opened | Partial (A1), Resolved (A2)

Combinatorial novelty | survey statistics x comparative biology with nothing at the joint: add (1|source) and you are done | limb (iv) is a genuine interface problem — with one row per species a provenance random effect and the phylogenetic covariance compete for the same residual covariance, and no fit found estimates both — but neither adversary could source an identifiability result within budget, so the response is argued, not evidenced | Partial (A1), Partial (A2)

Presupposition failure | the operative formulation slides between two units: presupposition 2 freezes "primary determination" as a measurement on specified individuals (one species), yet limb (i) counts records sharing one with another record in the same one-row-per-species fit and the PRIOR 2 differentiation insists clusters span species, while limb (iii) switches to "cluster-robust by primary source"; under the strict reading the within-fit shared-determination share is near zero by construction, and the motivating-gap mechanism is a cross-fit mechanism | reading the cluster as "primary source publication" rescues coherence but changes the mechanism from duplication to a lab/protocol variance component, retires the "deduplication" framing, and spends a second Gate 1 reformulation the pipeline does not allow; the significance-bearing design effect of about 2 remains unevidenced, and Genoud's 817 species / 946 publications describes a fragmented structure in which most publications contribute one species (A1's inference from his counts, not a computed design effect) | UNRESOLVED (A1), Partial (A2)

Vagueness | thresholds undeclared; a high unresolvable share would leave limbs (ii)-(iv) uninterpretable while still producing a number | mapping names both directions and fixes thresholds before tracing, unresolvable reported separately, feasibility bound evidenced at 3.3%; residual: no metric for limb (iv) congruence, and the design effect is not uniquely defined for a slope | Resolved (A1), Partial (A2)

Significance inflation | the threshold crossing hangs on a ~0.0014 margin; Genoud's own 0.018 shift changed no practice; likely outcome is wider intervals, stable points | one sourced, falsifiable stake (Genoud's "excludes both" claim retracts under a design effect of 2); curator consequence plausible but unevidenced; audiences (3) and (5) are inflation | Partial (A1), Partial (A2)

Reason for silence | the field did ask: FGG 2005 named the mechanism in this dispute, Genoud 2018 wrote that combining previously published data sets adds noise and is "common practice for time-saving convenience", and then resolved duplicates by random choice — someone who had the cluster structure in hand and discarded it | only response available is that the quantitative estimand was never posed, which is the distinction this ledger reserves for ROUTING rather than admission; the record itself concedes "Asked-but-open: YES, in weaker form"; the instrument component is undercut by Genoud's own hand tracing | Partial (A1), UNRESOLVED (A2)
8. Dissolution | splits into known cross-study overlap plus a standard study variance component, leaving an empirical magnitude | a parameter whose value retracts a published "excludes both predictions" is not a dissolution, but under the strict unit reading limb (i) collapses toward a taxonomic-substitution-and-imputation audit | Partial (A1), Partial (A2)
Verification (post-batch, four fresh-context checkers reading the cited priors at first hand, plus two residual reads of the sources the batch could not open): six reads ran. The fatal ground is CONFIRMED and strengthened in the prior's own words, one published well-posedness reason is WRONG and withdrawn, and two sources stay unreadable after a second independent attempt. The entry stays Rejected.
- PRIOR 1 (Genoud et al. 2018) CONFIRMS attack 4's degeneracy, quoted rather than inferred. "A total of 1739 values for the metabolic rate of 817 species of mammals were extracted from published literature"; "Among the 946 original publications involved, 95% were read"; and decisively, of the analysis data sets, "In each only a single entry from the BMR database was used for any species included" — one entry per species, not a species mean, with ties broken by reliability code and then "one of them was chosen randomly" (SELECT N = 549, ALL N = 817, SPOILED N = 549). So under the frozen definition this question declares, two rows of a one-row-per-species fit cannot share a measurement on specified individuals, and the headline quantity is degenerate by construction. The paper reports no per-publication entry counts, no source-clustered model and no design effect.
- PRIOR 2 (Farrell-Gray & Gotelli 2005) CONFIRMED verbatim and bounded. The sentence is FOUND at p. 2084: "The second kind of nonindependence arises because data on the same species are sometimes used in multiple studies." Its unit is 22 published exponents; its remedy is pairing studies that share no species — "Each study was included in only one pair", "this pair wise procedure reduces the sample size", "we used only the most inclusive data set" — with P = 0.2371 / 0.8827 / 0.1441. It reports no fraction, no design effect and no effective N, and it names NO pair of studies that reused data. It poses the problem and supplies neither a magnitude nor an instance. Its ESA data archive (E086-109-A1) was not read.
- Kattge et al. 2020 (TRY) COULD NOT READ, on a second independent attempt. Routes failed: Wiley /doi/ and /pdfdirect/ (client errors), the Leiden open-access PDF download (client error), doi.org (proxy HTTP 429 with an instruction not to retry), and a Bash curl to the Leiden PDF (proxy 403); a GitHub code search found only citation strings in three R packages and no mirror. Only the figshare abstract and the Leiden handle metadata were read, and neither speaks to duplicates, deduplication, provenance or non-independence. The duplicate-record question in the largest database the candidate names is therefore UNVERIFIED, not absent — and adversary 1's Partial grade on Disguise rested on exactly this.
- Genoud's Table S2 COULD NOT READ, on a second independent attempt (Wiley /doi/, /doi/full/ and /doi/suppl/ all errored; doi.org returned 429; BORIS lists only a restricted PDF and states it has no supplementary data; a search for the brv12350-sup file name found nothing). The main text's own references are ambiguous about what the table even is: entries were "entered into the BMR database (see online Tables S1 and S2)" while "References marked with * and/or dagger were used, respectively, as sources for the BMR database (Table S2)". Whether a per-entry source column exists at all is unresolved, so the computable tier of the routing row has no verified input.
- CORRECTION to a published reason, which changes the reason and not the verdict: a design effect for a SLOPE is well defined, so Gate 5's second well-posedness deduction was wrong. The Moulton factor is standard — Cameron & Miller's Eq. (6) gives tau_k approximately equal to 1 + rho_xk * rho_u * (N_g_bar - 1), with "The result (6) is exact if clusters are of equal size", and MacKinnon et al. give 1 + (M - 1) rho_s; it reduces to Kish's mean form only when rho_x = 1, and Skinner & Vieira report that regression-coefficient design effects are "often found to be less than design effects for the mean". What was NOT FOUND in anything opened is an effective SAMPLE SIZE for a slope. The corrected objection is narrower: the slope design effect is not unique across regressors and estimators, and the effective-N restatement limb (ii) leans on has no published definition for a coefficient.
- Net: the rejection stands on attack 4 alone, sourced in PRIOR 1's own sentence; well-posedness stays 2/3 on one ground instead of two; and the routing row is narrowed below to carry the two unreadable items.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 (revised down at Gate 5 from the record's 3/3 on two grounds, of which one survives verification and one does not. SURVIVES and strengthened: limb (i)'s unit is unchosen between "primary determination" and "primary source publication", and PRIOR 1's one-entry-per-species rule is what makes the first reading degenerate. WITHDRAWN: that limb (ii)'s design effect is "undefined for a slope rather than a mean" — the Moulton factor defines it for a coefficient. Corrected and narrower: the slope design effect is not unique across regressors and estimators, and no effective sample size for a slope exists in anything opened; that is a specification gap, not an undefined quantity, so 2/3 now rests mainly on limb (i)) · Significance 2/3 (one sourced stake, three real audiences, likely finding absorbable)
Strongest remaining objection: attack 4, Unresolved from adversary 1 and fatal under Gate 4's rule. Under the frozen definition the question asks for — a primary determination as a reported measurement on specified individuals — two rows of a one-row-per-species fit cannot share one, so the headline quantity is degenerate by construction; the only coherent rescue reads the cluster as the source publication, which is a second Gate 1 reformulation, converts the question from degrees-of-freedom inflation into a lab/protocol variance component, and leaves the design effect that carries the whole significance argument unevidenced. Adversary 2's independently Unresolved attack 7 compounds it: the qualitative question is on the record in this field and dispute, so what remains un-asked is a magnitude, which this ledger routes rather than admits. POST-VERIFICATION: the fatal leg is now quoted rather than inferred — of each analysis data set Genoud et al. 2018 write that "only a single entry from the BMR database was used for any species included" — so the degeneracy holds inside the prior the question is built on. Farrell-Gray & Gotelli's sentence is confirmed verbatim at p. 2084, with the added finding that it names no pair of studies that reused data and reports no fraction, no design effect and no effective N, which is why the magnitude is routed rather than admitted. One leg of the Gate 5 reasoning is withdrawn: the design effect is not "undefined for a slope" (see the Scores note), so the rescue reading is estimable — it remains a second Gate 1 reformulation at a different unit, which is the reason it cannot be admitted here.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): re-pose at a single declared unit — source publication as a second covariance term alongside phylogeny in species-level allometric fits, its variance share and its congruence with the tree — drop the deduplication framing, define variance inflation for a slope rather than a mean, and re-run novelty against phylogenetic-mixed-model practice and against Kattge et al. 2020 on a publisher route before any status above Rejected.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): YES, but only the NARROW limb, and the row is re-stated post-verification. The broad limb the candidate declares — deduplication to shared primary determinations — is non-identifiable at the unit its own priors use, since Genoud et al. put one entry per species into every analysis data set, so it is not routable. The routable limb is the one the sources themselves pose: source publication as a cluster or a second variance component in a species-level allometric fit, with its per-publication entry counts, its design effect for the slope and a source-clustered refit of the published exponent. Farrell-Gray & Gotelli 2005 pose it at p. 2084 ("The second kind of nonindependence arises because data on the same species are sometimes used in multiple studies.", confirmed verbatim) and remedy it only by species-disjoint pairing, which does not touch clusters spanning different species inside one database; Genoud et al. 2018 pose it as combination noise from "common practice for time-saving convenience" and resolve duplicates by random choice. Neither quantifies it. The row carries three bounds the verification pass established: the slope design effect IS defined (the Moulton factor), so the limb is estimable, while no effective sample size for a slope was found in anything opened; Genoud's Table S2, the only plausible input for per-publication entry counts, could not be opened on any of six routes in two independent attempts, so Tier A's feasibility is unverified; and Kattge et al. 2020 could not be opened either, so the duplicate-record question in TRY is unverified rather than open. Tier B for multi-database tracing. Not re-admissible to this ledger without a fresh Gate 1 and a fresh Gate 4 at the chosen unit.

---
ID: UQ-20261017-33
Date: 2026-10-17
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): Biology — computational-biology research methods / metascience (non-clinical analyses only: genomics, phylogenetics, single-cell, image quantification). Method transplanted from software-engineering mutation testing and reliability-engineering fault injection.

Question (canonical): Over a pre-declared frame of published non-clinical biological analyses that re-run end-to-end from archived code and data and reproduce their published headline numbers to a declared tolerance, and over a pre-registered frequency-weighted catalogue of single-point faults, what is the per-fault probability that an injected fault is both SILENT (the run completes and trips no hard failure, flagged threshold or visibly anomalous sanity plot among those the pipeline itself emits, judged by a blinded rubric with inter-rater agreement reported) and CONSEQUENTIAL (the paper's pre-extracted headline claim changes past that paper's own stated threshold), and does that probability partition more into analysis class than into the authors' software practices?
(Gate 1 reformulation V1 adopted; V0 intake text and the full V1 wording in batches/2026-10-17-1421/UQ-20261017-33-record.md.)

Alternative formulations:
(1) If a published biological analysis had one plausible bug — off-by-one coordinate, swapped strand, mis-sorted join, unit mismatch, mis-specified contrast — how often would nothing in the pipeline notice and the conclusion still change?
(2) What is the mutant-kill rate of biology's de facto test suite (its own QC plots and logs), scored against the biological conclusion rather than against the code?

Motivating gap: Software engineering and reliability engineering measure fault sensitivity by injection; computational biology imported only the dual technique (metamorphic testing), which scores a TOOL against invariants the testers authored. The field's evidence on faults in specific published analyses is anecdotal (column swaps, coordinate conventions, Excel gene-symbol corruption, one-line-script retractions) and supports no rate, no fault-class ranking, and no specification for the assertions that would catch them.

Presuppositions: 8 recorded (full text in the record). CONTESTED and flagged: (1) a reproducible corpus large enough for class-level estimates exists — the recoverable fraction is a primary reportable finding; (2) "realistic fault" is specifiable only relative to an evidence-derived, pre-declared catalogue C, so the estimand is explicitly conditional on C; (4) the coupling effect is not assumed — a fault-pair arm tests it; (7) "silent" is partly counterfactual, so it is defined over EMITTED artefacts under a blinded rubric, not over what an author would have noticed; (8) the frame selects on software practice, range-restricting the class-versus-practice limb by construction. DEFENSIBLE: (3) per-paper headline-claim extraction rule; (6) denominator is injected faults, not papers, with both marginals reported.

What would count as an answer: An interval-estimated silent-and-consequential fraction over the pre-declared frame, with catalogue, injection protocol, silence rubric and claim-change rule all registered before the first injection, in a crossed analyses x fault-class design with per-paper random effects; reporting (i) recoverable-corpus fraction, (ii) share of faults killed by existing gates, (iii) the joint fraction with interval, (iv) per-class ranking, (v) the higher-order arm. Pre-committed readings: near zero across classes = a positive result for existing QC; non-trivial = a ranked list of fault classes usable as an assertion specification for nf-core/Galaxy/Bioconductor/GATK-style pipelines; "not estimable" = a reportable finding about the archive.

Novelty — queries run (query -> one-line result): Gate 2 ran 11 WebSearch across seven vocabularies with 5 WebFetch (4 sources opened, 1 COULD NOT READ); adversary #1 ran 9 Disguise queries in new vocabularies with 4 fetches; adversary #2 ran 8 Disguise queries plus 1 verification query with 4 fetches. Full lists: batches/2026-10-17-1421/UQ-20261017-33-record.md, -adversary-1.md, -adversary-2.md. Most informative: (Gate 2 Q10, own words) "inject errors into published analysis scripts re-run archived code data does the result still hold audit" -> nothing on point, the record's strongest negative; (Gate 2 Q6) injected-bug/off-by-one/strand-swap vocabulary -> only blogs and a help-forum thread, confirming the evidence base is anecdotal; (Gate 2 Q11) nf-test/NFTest -> pipeline test frameworks with no mutant score and no claim-level scoring (audience evidence, not prior art); (Gate 2 Q5) surfaced arXiv:2608.27100, which Gate 2 COULD NOT READ via /pdf/ and both adversaries then opened via /abs/; (A2 D7, forensic-bioinformatics vocabulary Gate 2 named but never searched) -> Baggerly & Coombes AOAS 2009, a prior Gate 2 missed; (A2 D8, Chinese-language) -> ORNL metamorphic/differential-testing and INCOB-2014 items, both tool-level; (A1 D8, peer-review vocabulary) -> arXiv:2508.20069 seeded-error detection experiment (human detection, economics) and arXiv:2603.17893 scicode-lint (static patterns, no injection). Negative vocabularies returning nothing on point: error seeding/bebugging, double programming, silent failures/HPC SDC, chaos engineering/fuzzing, R mutation tooling, spreadsheet-audit (Panko), astronomy injection-recovery, epidemiological bias analysis, German, Chinese. Ledger duplicate check: INDEX.md read in full (120 entries — the generated text said 129, corrected post-batch against the committed index); no duplicate; nearest sibling UQ-20261015-23 opened (injects DATA, not code faults).

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources): Re-ordered at Gate 5 after the record's COULD-NOT-READ item was opened by both adversaries.
P1 (NEW, read at abstract depth by both adversaries; Gate 2's /pdf/ route failed, /abs/ answered first call) — Shulepov, "Mutation Testing for Reproducibility Safeguards in Machine Learning Research Software: An Empirical Study", arXiv:2608.27100, 2026-08-27. UNIT: 39 frozen ML research-repository x operator cases. INJECTED OBJECT: four configuration-choice mutation classes (random seed, dependency pin, data split, CV fold count). COMPARATOR/TEST SUITE: each repository's OWN existing validation workflow. ESTIMAND: detection proportion by that workflow — 23 confirmed non-equivalent mutations, 2 detected (8.7%, that sample only); 13 of 39 cases yielded primary outcomes, 24 after a bounded restoration procedure. Does not re-run published results and has no claim-change endpoint.
P2 — Chen, Ho, Liu, Xie, "An innovative approach for testing bioinformatics programs using metamorphic testing", BMC Bioinformatics 2009;10:24, doi:10.1186/1471-2105-10-24, read in full at the publisher. UNIT: two tools (GNLab simulator, SeqMap). INJECTED OBJECT: code mutants, 12 non-equivalent. COMPARATOR: authored metamorphic relations. ESTIMAND: MR kill rate — 9/9 and 3/3 (100%).
P3 (NEW, added at Gate 4 by adversary #2 as a Gate 2 omission; opened) — Baggerly & Coombes, "Deriving chemosensitivity from cell lines: forensic bioinformatics and reproducible research in high-throughput biology", AOAS 2009, arXiv:1010.1092. UNIT: four published analyses, selected because harm was suspected. OBJECT: real, not injected, faults (off-by-one row offsets, sensitive/resistant label reversals, duplicated samples, confounded run dates). ENDPOINT: qualitative demonstration of both silence ("hidden well enough to survive two explicit corrections") and consequentiality (reported AUC 0.943 vs the re-analysts' own approximation of 0.348 — their arithmetic, carried as such). ESTIMAND: none; no denominator, no rate.
Demoted from the record's list but still graded there: Kiar et al., PLOS ONE 2021 (bioRxiv 2020.10.15.341495, read in full) — numerical-noise perturbation, variability endpoint, no QC gate assessed; Hook, Queen's MSc 2009 (landing page read, re-verified by adversary #2) — eight numerical routines, output deviation against oracle uncertainty. Also at abstract depth: arXiv:1904.08007; arXiv:2109.03991 (observed not injected bugs, no detection mechanism, 1/18 significant). Named-only, not graded on: arXiv:2605.17437, arXiv:2608.14527, arXiv:1808.01093, arXiv:1404.5552, ICST-2024 Roker & Kanewala (abstract names no rate), TRANSMUT-Spark (arXiv:2108.02589), nf-test, Ziemann 2016 (~20% figure from secondary coverage only).
On the mandatory "fraction already computed" check: no published estimate of the joint estimand exists. Nearest published fractions are P1's 8.7% (other field, configuration faults, detection-only endpoint), P2's 100% MR kill on 12 mutants in two tools, the ~20% of genetics papers with Excel-corrupted gene lists (share of papers with a corrupted file), and HPC bit-flip silent-corruption rates against numerical tolerance (listings only).

Novelty — how this differs from each: vs P1 — shares the candidate's distinctive silence construction (injected faults scored against the artefact's own existing checks) and is therefore the binding close neighbour; differs on unit (repository vs published analysis), injected object (configuration choices vs evidence-weighted analyst faults), and estimand (detection proportion vs the joint silent-AND-consequential cell against the paper's own threshold, with class decomposition and a fault-pair arm). P1's 8.7% is the candidate's marginal (ii), in another field, on other faults. vs P2 — tool unit, authored MRs as the test suite, invariant-violation endpoint; a mutant killed by an MR may be irrelevant to any claim, and a claim-flipping fault may violate no MR, so the joint cell is exactly what P2 cannot see. vs P3 — same field and same fault classes, and it pre-answers the DIRECTION qualitatively, but n=4 harm-selected papers, real not injected faults, and no rate; it is evidence that the catalogue names the right faults, not an estimate. vs the multi-analyst/multiverse genre — varies competent choices, so nothing is a fault and no silence endpoint exists. vs HPC silent-data-corruption — bit flips in a running application against an experimenter's tolerance, not analyst faults against a published threshold. vs nf-test/NFTest, R muttest/mutator — snapshot and mutation tooling with no mutant score reported and nothing scored against a claim; audience evidence.

Novelty confidence: Medium (with a read close neighbour). Not High: arXiv:2608.27100 publishes the silence construction with a rate, so the residual is the consequentiality limb plus the biology frame, and the candidate is best described as extending an existing design rather than opening a new transplant. POST-VERIFICATION NOTE: reading that paper in full (see the verification block) shows it injects nothing code-level, scores detection by workflow exit status, and gets both of its two kills from dependency-pin mutations while the three statistical-choice operators were detected 0 of 12 — so it is a partial neighbour on the silence construction rather than an instance of it, and this grade would now read High on the search record alone. It is left at Medium because the grade is not what holds the entry at Provisional (well-posedness 2/3 is) and because re-grading novelty upward on a verification read, without a fresh Gate 2 sweep in the vocabularies the weakened neighbour opens up, would be the kind of unearned promotion Gate 5 exists to prevent. Not Low: 28 queries across 17 vocabularies and 12 sources opened found nothing measuring the joint estimand in any field; the strongest own-words query returned nothing at all.

Significance — consequence: Non-trivial fraction -> a ranked list of fault classes no existing gate catches, i.e. a direct specification for assertions (coordinate-convention checks, join-cardinality assertions, strand/orientation invariants, unit and contrast contracts). Near zero -> a positive result for existing QC and a redirection of reproducibility effort. Either way a by-product: how much a successful re-run actually certifies, separating "reproducible" from "correct" with a number. Adversary #2's dent: the near-zero branch is improbable before the first injection given P1's 8.7% and P3's faults surviving two corrections, so the claimed two-sidedness is weaker than the record argues.

Significance — audience: Workflow and toolkit maintainers already investing in test infrastructure (nf-core/nf-test, NFTest, Galaxy, Bioconductor, GATK-style pipelines; R muttest/mutator) — evidenced appetite for pipeline TESTING, inferred for conclusion-level fault metrics. Reproducibility infrastructure (CODECHECK, ReproHack, WorkflowHub), for whom "the re-run succeeded" currently has unquantified evidential value. Funders of research-software engineering. Journals and editors — conceded as inferred, with no maintainer, journal or funder shown to have asked for this number.

Significance — fecundity: Defines a conclusion-scored QC-coverage metric for pipelines, making askable: which single assertion would have caught the largest share of historical corrections; whether fault sensitivity tracks pipeline complexity or tool count; whether class-level sensitivity predicts replication failure; how to price code review against independent re-analysis; whether the coupling effect holds in data-analysis code at all.

Significance — anchoring: The gap between "re-runs" and "is right" in the reproducibility literature; the anecdotal canon of analysis-code errors; the oracle problem in scientific-software testing (reframed by using the paper's own claim as the oracle); the coupling-effect debate; HPC silent data corruption; the multi-analyst/multiverse bounds on variability from defensible choices.

Reason for silence: Three mechanisms, re-weighted at Gate 4. (1) Disciplinary boundary at the instrument — the method's owners score against test suites and a published analysis has none, so they retreat to the object their instruments can grade; CORROBORATED, since P1 scores against a repository's validation workflow and explicitly declines any claim about reproducing results. (3) Feasibility threshold — containerised workflows, archived data and cheap compute are a development of roughly the last five years; CORROBORATED by P1's Aug-2026 date and its 13/39 execution attrition. (2) Incentive/taboo — deliberately breaking named colleagues' published analyses; WEAKENED: both adversaries note that P1 mutated 39 named public repositories and P3 dissected four named published analyses in a leading statistics journal, so adversarial examination of named artefacts is publishable. Mechanism 2 survives only in the narrow form the record itself states (the forensic genre is reserved for harm-suspected cases, and P3 is one).

Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status): Two independent adversaries, each with a fresh context and the Gate 0-3 record only; #2 did not see #1's log. Both ran their Disguise sweeps in full (9 and 8 new-vocabulary queries), so Disguise is verified, not unverified. Status below is the worse of the two readings; verbatim logs in batches/2026-10-17-1421/UQ-20261017-33-adversary-1.md and -adversary-2.md.
