Verification (post-batch, three fresh-context checkers each handed one claim and its source, not the reviewer's reasoning; logs in batches/2026-10-17-1421/): three checks ran. Gate 5's promotion item (1) is DISCHARGED in full, the close neighbour it rested on is WEAKER than the abstract suggested, two attributions are corrected, and one promotion condition gets harder.
- P1 (arXiv:2608.27100) READ IN FULL TEXT via /html/v1 — exactly the read Gate 5 made a promotion condition. Every headline number holds: "We use MLReproMutate in an empirical study of 39 frozen repository—operator cases"; §5.8 "The meaningful detection denominator therefore contains 23 confirmed non-equivalent mutations"; §6.2 "the selected repository validation workflows detected 2 of 23 confirmed non-equivalent reproducibility-relevant mutations"; abstract "corresponding to an observed detection proportion of 8.7%"; "Primary execution yielded outcomes for 13 of 39 cases", rising to 24 under a bounded restoration layer (D027) with 15 still non-evaluable. CONFIRMED: no result-change endpoint anywhere in the paper — §7.2 "It does not imply that the repository is irreproducible, that its published results are incorrect"; §8.1 "A SURVIVED mutation therefore means only that the selected workflow did not detect"; §4 "Neither research question treats mutation survival as evidence that a repository is irreproducible"; "threshold" occurs only as the oracle category metric-threshold, and §5.4 states "no B02 case used a metric-threshold or reference-comparison oracle".
- The full text also WEAKENS P1 as a close neighbour on three attributes the abstract hid. (a) Nothing code-level is injected: §3 "Its mutation targets are instead elements of the surrounding experimental software and configuration"; the data-split operator "replaces the complete stratification expression with None" and changes neither split ratio nor seed; the seed operator "replaces the literal with N+1"; the pin operator "relaxes the equality constraint to package>=version". (b) Detection is workflow EXIT STATUS, not a comparison against any published value: §5.5 KILLED "when the selected validation workflow failed", SURVIVED "when the same workflow completed successfully despite the mutation", and 13 of the 15 oracle-coded cases are completion-only. (c) Both kills are dependency-pin mutations under completion-only oracles (Table 8); random seed 0/5, data split 0/4 and CV fold 0/3 — the three statistical-choice operators were detected 0 of 12. So the 8.7% measures whether a loosened version pin breaks a build, and the candidate's silence construction is LESS occupied than Gate 5 judged, on the one question Gate 5 called binding.
- P3 (Baggerly & Coombes) ATTRIBUTION CORRECTED. The silence quote is verbatim, §2.8 "These problems were hidden well enough to survive two explicit corrections." The AUC pair is not one re-analysis: 0.943 is the ORIGINAL authors' reported figure (Fig. 3 caption "The reported curve has an AUC of 0.943, indicating extremely good prediction"; §4.3 "The ROC curve assembled with the reported predictions (AUC of 0.943) perfectly matches that given by Bonnefoi et al. (2007)"), while 0.348 is the re-analysts' own reconstruction (Fig. 3 caption "Our best approximation has an AUC of 0.348"). The entry's gloss was right about 0.348 and wrong to carry both as the re-analysts' arithmetic. Also: §1.1 reports FIVE case studies and §1.6 "we examine four of the cases listed above in more detail", selected case by case with no sampling rule — so the entry's "no denominator, no rate" is confirmed, and the only literature-level denominator in the paper (Ioannidis et al. 2009, 18 papers, 10 not reproducible) is cited from others.
- Kiar et al. 2021 supplies NO REUSABLE BAND, which makes a promotion condition harder rather than easier. Monte Carlo Arithmetic on every instrumented flop ("All perturbations targeted the least-significant-bit for all data"), endpoints in estimated significant digits and normalised percent deviation against ONE unperturbed reference, 20 MCA simulations per execution. "null distribution", "noise floor" and "quality control" are each NOT FOUND; no published finding is re-tested; the bands that exist are per-edge measures from one pipeline on two datasets. The fault-free re-run null band the candidate needs must therefore be GENERATED inside the study, per paper in the frame, not borrowed from Kiar.
- Read levels: P1 full text (three prompts on /html/v1 through the page summariser; Equation images not readable); P3 full text; Kiar full text at PLOS plus one bioRxiv PDF, Equation 1 unreadable because it is an image. No fetch cap exceeded, no search refused.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3
Well-posedness held at 2/3, not raised: the primary estimand is fully registrable, but "silent" is defined over emitted artefacts under a blinded rubric rather than the counterfactual readers care about and so imports an inter-rater component into the headline number; the class-versus-practice limb is range-restricted by conditioning on re-runnability; and Gate 4 added a third residual the record did not carry — no fault-free re-run null band is specified, so run-to-run numerical variation would be attributed to the injected fault. Significance lowered from the record's 3/3 to 2/3: both outcomes remain actionable and the positive branch yields a specification rather than an observation, but the near-zero branch's probability is dented by P1's 8.7% and P3's documented survival through two corrections, and no maintainer, journal or funder is shown to have asked for a conclusion-level fault metric. Both clear their Validated thresholds; what blocks Validated is well-posedness below 3/3 together with Medium novelty against a now-read close neighbour.

Strongest remaining objection (rewritten post-verification; the objection Gate 5 named has weakened, and what replaces it is the well-posedness residual, now harder than Gate 5 wrote it): the claim-change rule cannot distinguish a fault-induced threshold crossing from ordinary run-to-run numerical variation until a fault-free re-run noise band is pre-declared for each paper in the frame, and verification established that the paper the entry leaned on for that band publishes none — Kiar et al. 2021 reports per-edge significant digits and normalised percent deviation against a single unperturbed reference, with "null distribution" and "noise floor" both absent and no published finding re-tested — so the band is work the study must do N times over, at a cost nothing in the record prices. Second and unmeasured: the frame's non-emptiness. The only evidence on it is the close neighbour's own attrition, 13 of 39 cases executing and 24 after a restoration layer, from a field whose code archiving is better than biology's. SUPERSEDED (kept for the record): arXiv:2608.27100 (read at abstract depth by both adversaries) already publishes the candidate's distinctive construction — single injected faults scored for detection against the research artefact's OWN existing validation workflow, 2 of 23 non-equivalent mutations detected (8.7%) — one field over, which reduces the candidate to adding a consequentiality limb whose direction is already pre-answered qualitatively in biology by Baggerly & Coombes (off-by-one row offsets and label reversals "hidden well enough to survive two explicit corrections", with a reported AUC of 0.943 against the re-analysts' own approximation of 0.348), and that remaining limb is not yet well-posed, because without a pre-declared fault-free re-run noise band the design cannot distinguish a fault-induced threshold crossing from the run-to-run variation Kiar et al. 2021 demonstrated.
Promotion requires: item (1) is DISCHARGED — arXiv:2608.27100 was read in full text post-batch, graded on all four attributes, and confirmed to report no result-change endpoint, with Baggerly & Coombes AOAS 2009 retained as a graded prior and its AUC attribution corrected. What remains is three well-posedness repairs that lift the score to 3/3 — a pre-declared fault-free re-run null band entering the claim-change rule, GENERATED rather than borrowed (verification established that Kiar et al. 2021 publishes no reusable band), a numeric definition of "near zero", and either an unrestricted practice contrast or the demotion of the class-versus-practice limb out of the question; plus a reported count of published biological analyses that actually satisfy the full frame, demonstrating it is non-empty at a size supporting class-level estimates. Nothing less promotes it. The null band is now the binding condition: it was the cheaper of the two Gate 5 items and verification made it the dearer one.

Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): the full-text read of arXiv:2608.27100 is done and recorded above, and it relocates the first step. Before any injection, enumerate how many archived non-clinical biological analyses re-run end-to-end and reproduce their headline numbers to tolerance, and re-run each fault-free N times to establish its claim's own noise band.

ID: UQ-20261017-34
Date: 2026-10-17
Status: Provisional
Verdict history: Rejected at Gate 4 on attack 2, adversary 1 and adversary 2 both grading Disguise Unresolved against Herculano-Houzel et al. 2015; moved to Provisional post-batch when verification showed that prior computes a different statistic on a non-isogenic cohort, and a late Gate 4 re-ran all eight attacks.
Domain(s): Biology — developmental biology / organ-size control; quantitative neuroanatomy. Method-owning fields: morphological/phenotypic integration, variance-component estimation, and (found by adversary 2) ecology's variance-ratio / compensatory-dynamics family and agronomy's yield-component compensation.

Question (canonical): Across genetically identical, identically reared individuals, is the absolute cell number of an organ regulated as a total — with compensatory negative covariance between its constituent regions or cell types — or are the parts regulated independently, so that the variance of the total is the sum of the parts' variances?
(Gate 1 reformulation, the version graded; one reformulation used: in a cohort of n isogenic, identically reared individuals, with a nested technical-replicate layer and a pre-declared partition, does the across-individual covariance matrix of absolute regional cell counts carry negative off-diagonal structure large enough to put Var(total) significantly below SUM Var(parts) once the technical component is subtracted, and does the sign replicate in a second line and under both an atlas and a registration-free marker partition? The reformulation drops the intake's "regulated as a total" mechanism claim, which the intake itself conceded is not identifiable from covariance.)

Alternative formulations:
- When one brain region of an inbred mouse happens to have fewer cells than average, do other regions have more?
- Does the across-individual covariance matrix of whole-organ cell counts carry the negative structure a conserved total implies, and is CV(total) smaller than the CV of any part?

Motivating gap: Intaken as a new-instrument question — classical stereology sampled one or a few regions per animal, so cross-region covariance within individuals was said to be newly measurable. The premise is false and was refuted at Gate 2: the isotropic fractionator counts every dissected structure of one brain, and the covariance was estimated and published in 2015; adversary 1 pushed it back further, finding within-isogenic-strain covariance with a repeat-count technical layer published in 1996.

Presuppositions (status after Gate 2 and Gate 4):
1. Per-animal technical error separable from biological covariance — ESTABLISHED (Elkind 2023 split-hemisphere proxy; Williams 1996 repeat counts; stereology's CV_obs^2 = CV_bio^2 + CE^2 is decades old, adversary 2 Q5/Q6).
2. Partition well defined and identical across individuals — CONTESTED and unrepaired. Var(T) − SUM Var(parts) = 2·SUM_{i<j}Cov(i,j) is not invariant to partition GRANULARITY; the candidate pre-declares two partitions but no granularity. Correction to the Gate 2 record: adversary 2's algebra shows the record stated the direction backwards (splitting a part moves the statistic by +2·Cov of the pieces, so refining makes compensation harder to find, not easier). Direction aside, the non-invariance stands.
3. Isogenic cohort at usable n — ESTABLISHED (369 inbred C57BL/6J brains in one published cohort).
4. Negative covariance identifies regulation — CONTESTED; conceded and dropped by the Gate 1 reformulation.
5. Per-region count phenotypes are interpreted without a total constraint — PARTLY WEAKENED (Elkind 2023 already benchmarks every effect against inter-individual variability).
6. Residual environmental variation among "identically reared" animals (litter, cage, rack) is measurable and blockable — CONTESTED and unaddressed by any prior opened; this is the design's one genuinely novel limb and also its one untested assumption. Adversary 1 weakens it further: Williams 1996 reports within-isogenic residual variance as "developmental noise rather than conventional environmental factors."

What would count as an answer: an across-individual covariance matrix of absolute counts over n isogenic individuals with a nested technical-replicate layer; a pre-declared comparison of Var(total) against SUM Var(parts) with intervals, at a declared granularity or as a curve over granularity; sign replication in a second line or species; reported under both partitions. Three pre-declared outcomes: below the sum = conserved total; indistinguishable = independent parts; positive residual covariance = shared growth factor. Criteria are crisp and pre-declarable — this candidate is NOT rejected for ill-posedness. (Adversary 2: the auxiliary CV(total) < CV(each part) criterion holds automatically under independence and should be struck.)

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
PRIOR 1 — Herculano-Houzel S., Messeder D.J., Fonseca-Azevedo K., Pantoja N.A. (2015), "When larger brains do not have more neurons: increased numbers of cells are compensated by decreased average cell size across mouse individuals," Front. Neuroanat. 9:64, doi 10.3389/fnana.2015.00064 — OPENED AND READ at the publisher by the record and independently re-verified verbatim by adversary 2. Unit: individual mouse (n = 19, one stock, same birth week). Endpoint: absolute neuron and non-neuron number per CNS structure, all structures in the same brain, by isotropic fractionator, plus whole-brain totals. Comparator: across-individual, between-structure, within one commonly reared stock. Estimand: sign structure of between-structure across-individual count covariance — cerebellum-olfactory bulb rho = 0.4734 (p = 0.0071), cortex-spinal cord rho = 0.3796 (p = 0.0321), rest-of-brain-spinal cord rho = -0.4820 (p = 0.0060). Conclusion in print: "numbers of neurons are regulated and allocated independently to different brain structures"; "we found no evidence of compensatory changes in the distribution of neurons across brain structures." Whole brain varies less than any part (1.63x vs 1.77-4.33x), and the paper engages part CVs explicitly.
PRIOR 2 — Elkind D., Hochgerner H., Aloni E., Shental N., Zeisel A. (2023), "Sex, strain, and lateral differences in brain cytoarchitecture across a large mouse population," eLife 12:e82376 — article page blocked (Client Challenge); READ via https://cdn.elifesciences.org/articles/82376/elife-82376-v3.xml by the record and by adversary 2. Unit: individual mouse, 369 inbred C57BL/6J plus 138 outbred, both hemispheres. Endpoint: absolute count per region over 532 atlas regions per animal, plus whole-brain totals (76 ± 11 x 10^6 cells, male C57BL/6J). Technical layer: "Cell count estimates in the right and left hemispheres served as a proxy for technical noise," 33 regions excluded above a 15.5% left-right difference. Estimand: per-region qualifier effects against inter-individual variability; no Var(total) vs SUM Var(parts), no CV(total) vs CV(parts). Correction to the Gate 2 record, from adversary 2's read: the region-to-region structure fed to the tSNE is computed on DENSITY vectors across 204 brains, not on counts, and no regional count CV or SD is published — so the record overstated what Elkind computed, and the candidate's statistic cannot be assembled from the printed summaries, only from the underlying table.
PRIOR 3 — Johansen N., Somasundaram S., Travaglini K.J. et al. (2023), "Interindividual variation in human cortical cell type abundance and expression," Science 382:eadf2359 — PREPRINT READ (bioRxiv 2022.10.07.511366); the published version was NOT opened and a mis-routed fetch returned a different Science paper (adf6812), recorded as a mis-route, not a check. Unit: non-isogenic human donor (n = 75). Endpoint: cell-type PROPORTION on the simplex; no absolute counts. No technical-replicate layer, no total-vs-parts contrast.
(Also read in Gate 4, and load-bearing: Williams R.W., Strom R.C., Rice D.S., Goldowitz D. 1996, J. Neurosci. 16:7193-7205, author edition at nervenet.org — within-isogenic-strain neuron-number variance with a repeat-count technical layer; "the correlation within isogenic strains between these two variables is close to zero (r = 0.14 ± 0.08 SE)"; "environmental factors do not have significant common effects on both ganglion cell number and brain weight"; residual variance attributed to "developmental noise rather than conventional environmental factors." COULD NOT READ, grounding nothing either way: Klingenberg & Zaklan 2000 Evolution 54:1273 (bot challenge), Hager et al. 2012 Nat. Commun. 3:1079 (fetch error).)

Novelty — how this differs from each:
- vs PRIOR 1: it does not differ in the way that matters. Unit, endpoint, comparator and estimand all match, and the paper prints one of the candidate's three pre-declared answers. The candidate's differences are design strengthenings of an answered question: an isogenic line in place of a stock the authors themselves call "non-isogenic"; atlas and marker partitions in place of five dissected structures; a nested technical layer; the variance identity with intervals in place of pairwise rhos; cross-line replication. Adversary 2 grants that the isogenic restriction is a real variance-components distinction — positive genetic covariance could mask negative developmental covariance, so PRIOR 1's null does not strictly entail the candidate's — but the candidate's own canonical sentence asks PRIOR 1's question, not the variance-components question that would make the restriction the point. A covariate swap (isogenic for outbred) and an instrument swap (atlas for dissection) on an asked-and-answered question is a disguised known, which the gate rejects even where the exact variant is unmeasured.
- vs PRIOR 2: the estimand differs, and this was the candidate's only surviving ground. Cohort genetics, partition and technical layer all match the candidate's stated preconditions at an order of magnitude more power than its own argument needs, which refutes the motivating gap and collapses the candidate from a new-instrument question to an unperformed statistic on an existing table.
- vs PRIOR 3: genuinely not prior art — non-isogenic human donors, a proportion endpoint on which negative covariance is a construction artefact and totals are unrecoverable in principle. Checked and cleared.
- Method-owning-field negative: Gate 2 named phenotypic/morphological integration and reported nothing applied to absolute cell counts, but did not open those sources, so that negative grounds nothing. Adversary 2 then found two larger families Gate 2 missed entirely (ecology's variance ratio / compensatory dynamics; agronomy's yield-component compensation), and found that the "subtract the technical component" step is standard stereology. The method side is more crowded than the record claimed, not less.
- Ledger duplicate check: INDEX.md read in full (120 entries — the generated text said 139, corrected post-batch against the committed index). No duplicate or near-duplicate; UQ-20261016-34, UQ-20261015-23, UQ-20261016-36 and UQ-20261017-28 share only a variance-decomposition motif on unrelated objects.

Novelty confidence: Medium (re-graded post-verification, upward from Low). The Low rested on the near-duplicate sharing the candidate's unit, endpoint, comparator and estimand. Verification refutes three of those four: Herculano-Houzel et al. 2015 computes pairwise Spearman correlations and max/min fold ratios rather than a variance of a total against the sum of its parts' variances (Table 1: "Variation refers to the ratio between maximum and minimum values for each parameter"), it runs on "19 male mice of the Swiss variety, a non-isogenic strain" rather than on genetically identical individuals, and its conclusion carries its own exception for the one neuron-count pair that IS negative. Across 46 queries in three passes, nothing opened computes the candidate's statistic on absolute cell or neuron counts in any organism. Medium and not High because the statistic itself is standard one field over, with a published null — codyn's variance ratio after Schluter 1984, and Ulrich & Gotelli's U = V/W on a chi-square null — so what is new is the object, not the instrument.

Significance — consequence: Real but largely discharged. A negative sign would make every per-region count phenotype a compositional readout against a constrained total, mis-powering and mis-interpreting the single-region literature; indistinguishable from the sum would confirm PRIOR 1 at proper power in an isogenic line; positive residual covariance would point at a shared systemic growth factor. The discount: one answer is in print, so the yes-branch's consequence is "overturn an under-powered published negative," not "settle an open question."
Significance — audience: quantitative-neuroanatomy groups building region-resolved count atlases (the Zeisel cohort, CUBIC and ClearMap communities), mouse-phenotyping consortia reporting per-region counts as phenotypes, and organ-size-control labs arguing about progenitor-pool limitation. They would act by modelling the total as a constraint in region-level tests and powering on covariance rather than means. Adversary 2's revealed-preference objection bites: the lab holding the data did not compute the count covariance matrix at all, only a density-based embedding. Adversary 1's counter-evidence that they would benefit is real — Kim et al. 2017 ran n = 3-5 "without replication."
Significance — fecundity: whether any constraint is imposed at the progenitor-pool stage or later; whether the covariance structure itself is heritable across lines; whether a perturbation moves the total or only redistributes it; whether the same structure appears in non-neural organs with clonal lineages.
Significance — anchoring: the concerted-versus-mosaic brain-evolution dispute brought inside one genotype; canalization and developmental stability; Herculano-Houzel's cell-number/cell-size compensation; progenitor-pool limitation in organ-size control.

Reason for silence: None exists, and that is the finding rather than a gap in the record. The question was asked in this field's own words in 2015 and, for one pair with a technical layer, in 1996; both adversaries reached PRIOR 1 independently from vocabularies Gate 2 never used. What the record supplies is a mechanism for UNDER-REPORTING of the statistic — atlases are funded to detect effects, so the covariance matrix is consumed as nuisance structure or embedding input — compounded by a real disciplinary boundary, since the variance-ratio statistic lives in morphometrics, ecology and agronomy, which counting labs do not read. That explains why answering is unrewarded, not why no one asked. Per the ledger's own rule, an under-reporting mechanism with no silence mechanism corroborates the Low grade instead of defending the candidate. POST-VERIFICATION: the first clause is withdrawn — the question was NOT answered in 2015, because that paper computes fold ratios and pairwise rhos on a non-isogenic cohort — and the disciplinary-boundary limb is now the sourced one: the statistic lives in ecology and morphometrics (codyn and Ulrich & Gotelli for the variance ratio; Klingenberg & Zaklan on wing-shape compartment integration, read at abstract level only), and nothing opened applies it to absolute counts. The under-reporting mechanism also survives, strengthened by PRIOR 2 declaring counts a derived quantity and publishing medians and densities instead. What is still missing is any published statement that the question is open, which one targeted search did not find.

Verification (post-batch, four fresh-context checkers reading the cited priors at first hand, then a late Gate 4 of two literature surveys plus two residual reads): eight reads ran. The fatal ground FALLS — the near-duplicate shares neither the candidate's statistic nor its population — so the entry moves from Rejected to Provisional, capped by two Unresolved non-fatal attacks, one of them new.
- PRIOR 1 (Herculano-Houzel et al. 2015) does NOT compute the candidate's estimand. Both quoted conclusions are FOUND in the Discussion, but the paper computes no variance of a total against the sum of its parts' variances and no CV of a whole against the CVs of its parts. Table 1's caption reads "Variation refers to the ratio between maximum and minimum values for each parameter", so the 1.63 the record carried is a max/min FOLD RATIO for whole-brain neurons, against per-structure fold ratios of 1.77x (cortex) to 4.33x (olfactory bulb); the only CV statement in the paper is that neuron counts have "larger coefficients of variation (CV) than structure mass". The "no compensation" inference therefore rests on pairwise Spearman correlations, not on a variance identity.
- And PRIOR 1's conclusion carries its own exception, which the record's quotation dropped: "there is no negative correlation between numbers of neurons in the different brain structures (except between the rest of brain and the spinal cord)". That pair is rho = -0.4820, p = 0.0060 — the ONLY neuron-count-against-neuron-count negative among the coefficients printed, beside positives for cerebellum/olfactory bulb (0.4734, p 0.0071) and cortex/spinal cord (0.3796, p 0.0321). Table 2 prints coefficients only where P < 0.05 and shows "n.s." elsewhere, so the covariance structure cannot be recovered from the published table even for a reanalysis.
- PRIOR 1 is also the wrong POPULATION. Its cohort is "19 male mice of the Swiss variety, a non-isogenic strain", all two months old. The candidate's question is about genetically identical individuals, so the prior cannot answer it even where it computes a comparable statistic.
- PRIOR 2 (Elkind et al. 2023) sets counts aside and publishes medians. "Cell count (N) is the product VxD; therefore, it was not considered an independent variable", and the region-to-region analysis runs on DENSITIES — "each region is characterized by a vector of 204 components, each representing its density across one brain", with the tSNE "based on their density across 204 C57BL/6J brains (451 regions)". There is no per-animal per-region count table: the three source-data files hold per-region medians (one vs Murakami et al. plus diameter and density over all 507 brains, one of medians by sex and strain) and per-mouse VOLUME and body weight only; no Supplementary file 1, no Zenodo, Dryad or figshare deposit, and the data-availability statement is "All data generated or analysed during this study are included in the manuscript and supporting file". Per-region CV or SD of counts: NOT FOUND; the only count SD is whole-brain, "the standard deviation across individuals was ~10 million cells (for C57BL/6J male alone)", against a total of "76 +/- 11 x 10^6 cells". The technical-proxy string the record quoted is FOUND, with the threshold "If the average difference in cell count between hemispheres was higher than 15.5% of the total cell count for that region" and "33 regions were omitted due to right-left differences". Cohort: 507 brains, 369 C57BL/6J and 138 FVB.CD1, over 532 basic AMBA regions.
- PRIOR 3 (Johansen et al. 2023) read at preprint level, and it is a different measurand again: per-donor FRACTIONS, "Fraction of cells from each subclass collected from each donor, scaled to the total number of cells from each class", over 75 neurosurgical human donors whose unrelatedness is NOT FOUND in the text. It reports anticorrelation between abundant types — "astrocytes and oligodendrocytes were strongly anticorrelated and L2/3 IT was anticorrelated with other glutamatergic types" — with NO discussion of the sum-to-one artefact ("composition" and "compensat" both NOT FOUND) and no variance-of-total against sum-of-parts. The published Science version COULD NOT READ (doi.org 429, science.org error, PubMed empty shell), so these absences are bounded to the preprint main text, which carries no Methods section.
Late Gate 4 (required once the fatal ground fell). The two cold eight-attack adversaries were expected to die at launch as twelve did across the 09:20 and 11:28 batches, so the pass ran in the documented fallback form: two fresh-context literature surveys asking neutral questions whose ANSWERS decide the attacks, with the judge applying the Gate 4 rule. Disclosed departure from LEDGER.md's adversary form: cold context and two independent readers are kept, the adversary's own framing is given up. Logs: UQ-20261017-34-lategate4-lit-a.md and -lit-b.md (17 queries, 12 fetches).
- Attack 2 (Disguise) now RESOLVED. No source opened across 29 first-pass queries and 17 late ones computes a total-versus-sum-of-parts variance ratio on absolute cell or neuron counts, in any organism (NOT FOUND, bounded and stated as such). The three priors differ on population, on measurand, or on both: non-isogenic Swiss mice with fold ratios and censored rhos; densities and medians over isogenic mice with counts explicitly set aside; fractions over genetically diverse humans.
- Attack 3 (Combinatorial novelty) now UNRESOLVED and sourced, and it is one of the two caps. The statistic is standard and named one field over, with a stated null: codyn's variance ratio is "the ratio of the variance of aggregate species abundances in a community to the sum of the variances of individual, component species", where "A variance ratio = 1 indicates that species do not covary", "a variance ratio > 1 indicates predominately positive covariance" and "< 1 indicates predominately negative covariance", citing Schluter 1984; Ulrich & Gotelli state "This test compares the variance of row totals V with the sum of the column variances W", "U = V/W", with a chi-square null on n degrees of freedom. So the candidate supplies no new statistic and no new null — only a new object for an existing one, and it reaches that object across a disciplinary boundary the record already names. Schluter's own text was NOT READ (doi.org and the publisher both failed), so the attribution runs through two secondary descriptions.
- Attack 4 and Attack 6 jointly UNRESOLVED and non-fatal, on a ground the first pass did not have: in the one isogenic dataset that publishes both components, the technical variance is the LARGER one. Williams et al. 1996 report a corrected environmental coefficient of variation averaging "4.60% +/- 0.4%" against a technical CV of "5.70% +/- 0.1%", and state that "the dominant source of quantitative variation within isogenic groups in this study is technical error" while elsewhere attributing within-strain variation to "developmental noise rather than ... conventional environmental factors" — an internal tension the checker flagged. No first-hand source was found giving a formula for subtracting a measured counting variance from a between-individual count variance: the stereology help page opened "never mentions biological variation, between-individual CV, or subtraction", and the conventional identity could not be verified in any opened text. The candidate's design does pre-declare a nested technical-replicate layer, which is why this caps rather than kills, but the signal it must separate is smaller than the noise in the only comparable published case.
- Attack 1 (Triviality) RESOLVED, and this is the finding that most changes what the entry is for: the computation cannot be done from published data. Elkind declares counts a derived quantity and publishes medians and densities, PRIOR 1's table censors every non-significant pair, and PRIOR 3 publishes fractions — so no published table supports the statistic at any granularity, and no study was found publishing per-region CVs of absolute counts for a large isogenic cohort (NOT FOUND, bounded by two searches with two unopened candidates). The question needs a new cohort or an unreleased count matrix, not a reanalysis.
- Attack 7 (Reason for silence) PARTIALLY REPAIRED. The record's disciplinary-boundary limb is now sourced rather than asserted: the statistic exists in ecology, in software documentation and in a morphometrics literature whose nearest item (Klingenberg & Zaklan 2000, read at ABSTRACT level only after five routes failed) analyses wing SHAPE covariation in "genetically diverse individuals" and concludes "the anterior and posterior compartments are not separate units of variation" — adjacent reasoning on a different measurand in a different population. No published statement that the question remains undetermined was found (NOT FOUND, bounded by one targeted search), so the silence is still undocumented from the inside.
- Attacks 5 and 8 are unchanged from the first pass.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3 (both unchanged and both clear the Provisional threshold; what holds the entry below Validated is the Unresolved attacks 3, 4 and 6 above together with Medium rather than High novelty. Significance is NOT raised despite the kill falling: the late pass showed the computation cannot be done from any published table, which raises its cost without raising its stake.)
(Well-posedness deduction: the test statistic is not invariant to partition granularity and the candidate pre-declares two partitions but no granularity and no granularity curve. Repairable, and not the rejection ground. Validated additionally requires 3/3, which this does not reach.)

Strongest remaining objection (rewritten post-verification; the original, that the question was already put and answered in 2015, is WITHDRAWN): the instrument is borrowed and the data do not exist. The statistic the candidate proposes is Schluter's variance ratio, standard in community ecology with a published null of 1 and a chi-square test, so the contribution is an application rather than a method; and no published dataset supports that application, because the large isogenic cohort declares cell count a derived quantity and publishes medians and densities ("Cell count (N) is the product VxD; therefore, it was not considered an independent variable"), the 2015 count paper censors every non-significant pair out of its table, and the human cohort publishes fractions. So the question requires a new cohort or an unreleased count matrix, and then it has to separate a biological variance from a technical one that was the LARGER of the two in the only isogenic dataset publishing both (technical CV 5.70% +/- 0.1% against a corrected environmental CV of 4.60% +/- 0.4%), with no formula for the subtraction verifiable in anything opened.
Promotion requires: (1) a per-animal per-region ABSOLUTE count matrix for an isogenic cohort, either obtained from the Elkind et al. authors or generated, since the published source data are medians and per-mouse volumes and the statistic cannot be computed without it; (2) a technical-variance layer demonstrated to be smaller than the between-individual variance it must be subtracted from, with the subtraction formula stated and sourced rather than assumed — Williams et al. 1996 is the warning case and its own internal tension between "developmental noise" and "technical error" should be resolved first; (3) a granularity curve, since the test statistic is not invariant to partition granularity and the candidate declares two partitions and no curve; and (4) a stated position on attack 3: what applying an existing ecological statistic to a new object buys, given that its null and test are already published. Nothing less promotes it, because (1) decides whether the study is a reanalysis or a cohort and (2) decides whether it can see its own effect.
SUPERSEDED (kept for the record): The question was already put and answered in the candidate's own field, words, unit, endpoint, comparator and estimand — Herculano-Houzel et al. 2015, opened and verified verbatim by two independent agents, concluding that "numbers of neurons are regulated and allocated independently to different brain structures" with "no evidence of compensatory changes" — and the isogenic line, atlas partition and technical-replicate layer that distinguish the candidate are a covariate-and-instrument swap on that asked question, already assembled at higher power in Elkind et al. 2023. Nothing in the record is silent except the computation.

Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): relocated by verification, because the step the first pass named is not executable. There is no published Elkind et al. per-animal per-region count table: the source data are per-region medians plus per-mouse volume and body weight, and the paper sets counts aside as V x D. The cheapest decisive move is therefore to request or reconstruct a per-animal per-region count matrix for one isogenic cohort — the 369 C57BL/6J brains are the obvious target, and the authors' published left-right hemisphere differences, thresholded at 15.5% of a region's total count with 33 regions already omitted, give the technical layer — then compute the variance ratio at several granularities with that technical component subtracted, against Schluter's null of 1. Settle whether the technical variance is smaller than the biological one on a handful of regions before asking for the whole matrix.

Routing (if rejected as already-asked): Not routed, on a changed ground. The Gate 5 reason — PRIOR 1 publishes an answer — is withdrawn: it publishes pairwise correlations and fold ratios on a non-isogenic cohort, not the candidate's statistic. The entry is now Provisional, and a Provisional entry's own question is not routed, because the ledger is still claiming it as un-asked. The verification residuals above belong to this entry's promotion condition, not to research.

ID: UQ-20261017-35
Date: 2026-10-17
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): Biology — experimental laboratory methods; metascience of protocol standardisation. Research-biology protocols only; clinical laboratory/diagnostic standards excluded.

Question (canonical): Over a frame of research-biology protocol parameters enumerated BEFORE any tracing by a pre-registered rule (frequency of exact numeric-plus-unit strings in a dated protocols.io + Methods-section corpus, with physically or instrumentally forced parameters flagged in advance), and traced under a written, dual-coded rubric to exactly one of four states — (i) primary optimisation found, conditions still current; (ii) primary optimisation found, conditions superseded; (iii) traced to a non-evidential source (vendor document, textbook, earlier protocol); (iv) chain unresolvable — (a) what are those four rates, with intervals, a coder-agreement statistic, and forced parameters reported separately; and (b) for a random subsample in state (ii), does re-running the original optimisation under current conditions move the optimum beyond a pre-declared margin?
(V1 as intaken, one permitted Gate 1 reformulation: "For the canonical default parameters of experimental biology protocols, what fraction can be traced to a primary determination that actually optimised a measurable endpoint, and among those, what fraction were optimised under conditions no longer in use?" V1 left denominator, coding rule and limb (b) implicit.)

Alternative formulations:
- A1: Where do biology's default numbers come from, and how many were ever optimised at all rather than inherited?
- A2: Treating each ubiquitous protocol constant as a claim, what is the citation-chain depth to its primary evidence, and what share of chains terminate in no evidence? — WEAKEST; P1 occupies most of A2's territory. If the question is reduced to A2 it must be re-graded Low.

Motivating gap: Silence map. Protocol repositories, vendor manuals and Methods sections specify thousands of exact parameters (37 C / 5% CO2, 10% FBS, 4% PFA for 10 min, 1:1000 primary antibody, 12/12 h light, 20-24 C vivarium) and for almost none is there a literature asking what the primary determination was or whether it still holds. Dense in "how", empty of "why". Class demonstrably non-empty: ambient-O2 gas phase (physioxia; Alva et al. 2022) and sub-thermoneutral vivarium temperature were each re-examined one at a time by individual curiosity, never prompted by a survey; the population of defaults has never been enumerated, so nobody can say which default to re-examine next.

Presuppositions: (1) a frame of canonical defaults is enumerable before tracing — DEFENSIBLE, and the rule is itself the first registrable deliverable (wet-lab-protocol NLP, WNUT-2020, makes it constructible). (2) tracing is feasible enough for rates to be estimable — CONTESTED; "chain unresolvable" is its own reported category, never pooled with "no evidence exists". (3) "optimised a measurable endpoint" is reliably codable — CONTESTED; needs rubric, dual coding, agreement statistic. (4) an untraceable or superseded default may be wrong — CONTESTED and EXPLICITLY DISCLAIMED; the audit measures evidential status only. (5) someone would act on a prioritised list — WEAKEST and undefended; PRO-MaP 2024 (opened, keyword-verified by adversary 2) asks for nothing about provenance. (6) parameters are conventional rather than instrument/chemistry-forced — CONTESTED PER PARAMETER; 5% CO2 is forced by the medium's bicarbonate, itself a default, so forcing relocates rather than dissolves conventionality.

What would count as an answer: Two limbs; not well-posed without the second. (A) N defaults enumerated by the pre-registered rule, each coded to one of the four states under the written protocol, dual-coded with an agreement statistic, reported as rates with intervals, forced parameters separate, state (iv) never pooled with "no evidence". (B) For a random subsample of state (ii), re-run the original optimisation under current conditions and report whether the optimum moved beyond the pre-declared margin. "Evidenced" = most trace to current-condition optimisations AND re-determinations reproduce the optima within margin; "not evidenced" = a ranked re-determination worklist. Limb (A) alone answers a bibliometric question, not this one.

Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): Gate 2 ran 11 distinct queries (cap 11) across lay, technical, historical and three method-owning neighbour vocabularies, 5 papers opened via publisher routes; adversaries added 9 + 9 new-vocabulary Disguise queries with 4 + 4 fetches. Full lists: batches/2026-10-17-1421/UQ-20261017-35-record.md and UQ-20261017-35-adversary-1.md / -adversary-2.md. Most informative: (Gate 2 Q9) methods citation-chain tracing / "citation distortion" → found P1, the only close neighbour; (Q10) "legacy" requirement with no recorded rationale / lost "design rationale" → requirements engineering owns this audit design and has never applied it to biology's constants; (Q3) metrology "traceability chain" / "reference conditions" → applies to clinical measurand values only; (Q11, own-field own-words) "Shortcut citations in the methods section" → publisher route to P1, surfaced PRO-MaP. MANDATORY "fraction already computed" query: a published fraction exists for the ADJACENT quantity (>90% of papers carry >=1 methodological shortcut citation; 96/90/92% by field, 815 papers, 10,852 citations) but none for defaults traceable to a primary optimisation, chain depth to primary evidence, or currency of optimising conditions; P1's authors explicitly caution against using their chain frequencies. ACCESS ROUTING: PMC/Europe PMC URLs returned by Gate 2 Q2/Q4/Q7/Q8/Q9 and by adversary queries were not used as routes; the on-point paper opened at journals.plos.org on the first publisher call. One COULD NOT READ (adversary 2, Q8): "From viability to cell death: Claims with insufficient evidence in high-impact cell culture studies" — PMC-only route, fetch budget spent; grounds no grade either way.

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
P1. Standvoss, Kazezian, ... Weissgerber, "Shortcut citations in the methods section: Frequency, problems, and strategies for responsible reuse", PLOS Biology 2024;22(4):e3002562, 10.1371/journal.pbio.3002562 (opened by Gate 2 and re-verified independently by both adversaries at the publisher). UNIT: the methodological citation (10,852 in 815 papers; 15 parent papers for a chain case study; 465 journals for policy). ENDPOINT: whether a citation is a probable/possible shortcut, its purpose (How / Who-what / Why / From-where / formula-value), resources cited, age of cited work. COMPARATOR: cross-field; in the chain study, whether the cited source adequately describes the method. ESTIMAND: descriptive prevalence (96/90/92%; median 2-3 shortcuts/paper; journal-policy proportions 0-2%).
P2. Chen, Teplitskiy, Jurgens, "The Noisy Path from Source to Citation", arXiv:2502.20581v3, 2025. UNIT: ~13.59M citation-sentence pairs over ~42M S2ORC papers. ENDPOINT: 1-5 model-scored fidelity of citing to cited sentence. COMPARATOR: regression reference categories; ~50K matched telephone-condition pairs. ESTIMAND: association coefficients (Biology +0.245; -0.007/year) and a -0.06 mean-fidelity difference.
P3. Alva, Gardner, Liang, Stuart, "Supraphysiological Oxygen Levels in Mammalian Cell Culture", Cells 2022;11(19):3123 (opened; re-verified by adversary 2). UNIT: one culture parameter (gas-phase O2). ENDPOINT: biological consequences of hyperoxic culture. COMPARATOR: in vivo 2-6% O2 vs ~18% incubator headspace. ESTIMAND: none quantitative; a normative conclusion.
Also opened, non-prior but load-bearing: PRO-MaP (Batista Leite et al., PLOS Biology 2024;22(9):e3002835); Klein et al., Front Cell Dev Biol 2022;10:788808 (adversary 1 — enumerates and audits REPORTING of the same environmental setpoints over 688 papers, names no origin for any); biorxiv 10.1101/2022.12.20.521257 (adversary 2 — exhaustive default-vs-optimum search for bioinformatics TOOL parameters; 72% of 3,000 BLAST configurations beat the default; silent on provenance).

Novelty — how this differs from each: vs P1 — unit is the PARAMETER VALUE, not the citation; endpoint is whether a traced source OPTIMISED a measurable endpoint and under what conditions (evidential status), not whether a cited source adequately DESCRIBES a method (implementability); P1 reports no chain-depth statistic, uses citation age only as a currency proxy, and has no limb (B). But both adversaries verified that P1 does carry a formula/value citation purpose and reports such citations "uncommon in all 3 fields" — P1 is closer than the record allowed. vs P2 — measures fidelity of sentence to sentence, never whether a cited claim rests on primary evidence, no chain depth past one intermediary, no terminal "no evidence" class; numeric experimental parameters appear only as its own hyperparameters. vs P3 — exactly one member of the candidate's class, endpoint biological not evidential, N=1, no enumeration rule, rubric, agreement statistic, rate or prioritisation; it is the candidate's motivating evidence, not an answer. Negatives recorded in the METHOD-owning vocabularies with a query spent in each (metrology, guideline/recommendation appraisal, requirements engineering), plus adversary sweeps of history of science/STS, lab ethnography, software configuration-default auditing, pharmacopoeial legacy limits, evidence-based laboratory practice, computational-biology parameter sensitivity, German-language, and incidental-remark phrasing: four adjacent genres each stop short, none traces a value to an optimisation or computes a rate. Residual unqueried vocabulary named by adversary 2: laboratory-animal-science husbandry standards (evidence base for the Guide's housing recommendations), where a partial prior for the vivarium slice may exist.

Novelty confidence: Medium

Significance — consequence: If most defaults trace to current-condition optimisations and limb (B) reproduces the optima within margin, that is a substantive negative against a popular reproducibility narrative and would redirect effort away from parameter provenance. If states (ii) and (iii) dominate, the output is a ranked re-determination worklist — the input to studies that currently start only by accident of individual curiosity. Either way the rate is new: nobody can presently state its order of magnitude.
Significance — audience: protocol repositories (protocols.io, Bio-protocol, STAR Protocols), for whom a provenance field is implementable only once an audit shows the states are codable; reporting-standards bodies (ARRIVE, MDAR, NC3Rs, the PRO-MaP group); metascience funders needing a prioritisation rule; core facilities, cell-culture standards groups and vendors who write the manuals state (iii) traces to. Adversary 1 adds a nameable live claimant: Klein et al. 2022 already enumerate these setpoints, audit their reporting across 688 papers and call for "urgent reconsideration" of nominal setpoints — demand one step short of provenance. Caveat retained: PRO-MaP's verified silence shows the audience is not currently asking for the exact deliverable.
Significance — fecundity: which classes of default are fragile vs robust under re-determination and whether fragility is predictable from the state code; whether obsolescence correlates with replication-failure rates; a typed provenance schema for protocol parameters ("parameter RRID") and its population cost; whether forced parameters relocate conventionality (5% CO2 / bicarbonate); the half-life of a parameter's optimising conditions as a measurable quantity; the same audit in chemistry, materials or clinical practice as the first cross-field comparison of evidential status of method constants.
Significance — anchoring: preclinical reproducibility/generalizability (harmonization vs heterogenization); physioxia; thermoneutrality in laboratory animal science; P1's shortcut-citation finding and PRO-MaP's recommendations; metrology's traceability chain; "recommendations without supporting evidence" in guideline appraisal; lost design rationale in requirements engineering.

Reason for silence: Mechanism 2 is the one that survives adversarial testing and it is asking-side: in experimental biology a parameter is credentialed by working, not by provenance, so the question has no claimant; adversary 2 verified in the primary source that only 0-2% of journals by field require authors to fully describe previously published methods, so the publication system rewards passing a parameter along by reference and nobody is ever obliged to ask where the number came from, and PRO-MaP's keyword-level silence is the same mechanism in the body that would otherwise ask. Mechanism 1 (disciplinary boundary at the method: metrology stops at the clinical measurand, guideline appraisal at the clinical recommendation, requirements engineering at engineering artefacts) stands as a partial asking-side story. Adversary 1 adds a fourth: metascience's toolkit works on citations and P1 shows parameter values are mostly uncited, so there was no object for citation-based metascience to pick up. Mechanism 3 (frame not constructible before protocol-corpus NLP) is downgraded per both adversaries to a feasibility note, not a reason for not asking — hand-picked frames were always askable, and clinical medicine has run hand-framed "what fraction is evidence-based" audits for decades.

Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status) — two independent adversaries, A1 and A2, each handed the Gate 0-3 record only; A2 did not read A1's log. Logs verbatim in UQ-20261017-35-adversary-1.md and UQ-20261017-35-adversary-2.md. Disguise searches EXECUTED by both (9 and 9 new-vocabulary queries, 4 and 4 fetches); no search call refused.
1 | Triviality | Everyone already "knows" the defaults are historical conventions, so the audit quantifies folklore; and in the sibling domain where limb (b) is cheap it is already published (72% of 3,000 BLAST configurations beat the default; >80% of results differ from it) | A1: the three sources that are exactly about these defaults (Klein 2022, Wenger 2014, Kiernan) each state the value and none states its origin or whether it was optimised, and P1 traces no value, so no page yields the order of magnitude of any of the four states; limb (b) is a wet-lab result readable off nothing. A2: direction is not the deliverable, a software knob's beatability does not transfer to a constant whose optimisation may never have existed, and the actionable output is the identity and ranking of fragile parameters | A1 Resolved / A2 Partial
2 | Disguise | A renamed prior exists in history of science/STS, lab ethnography and folklore, analytical/compendial method validation, software configuration-default auditing, computational-biology parameter sensitivity, evidence-based laboratory practice, data provenance, or German-language cell-culture literature | 18 new-vocabulary queries across the two adversaries, 8 pages opened: historical narratives of media and serum with no enumeration or coding; STS on tacit practice with no numeric-default tracing; DoE theory; computational data-provenance; default-rationale auditing in software engineering, where developers can be asked; parameter-sensitivity work measuring effects not origins; and the "what fraction of practice is evidence-based" genre alive but confined to clinical laboratory medicine, which this frame excludes. Closest new neighbours are Klein 2022 (a reporting audit of current setpoints) and the bioRxiv tool-parameter study (software knobs, no provenance claim). No renamed prior. 3 | Combinatorial novelty | Just guideline citation-chain audit x biology protocols; the record itself calls the design a transplant | A2: the interface problem is the one the transplant cannot import — a protocol constant has no measurand for metrology's chain to terminate in and no requirement owner or change record for rationale recovery, so the four-state evidential coding of a VALUE, advance flagging of forced values and presupposition 6's relocation finding are new design work. Verification (post-batch, two fresh-context checkers each handed one claim and its source, not the reviewer's reasoning; logs in batches/2026-10-17-1421/): both checks ran. The load-bearing FIGURE under the strongest objection does not exist as the entry used it, and the residual vocabulary attack 2 named was swept and returned a bounded negative. Status unchanged.
- P1 (Standvoss et al. 2024) CORRECTED. The quoted phrase is in the paper — "Citations specifying the source of data or materials (From where), or referring to a formula or value, were uncommon in all 3 fields." — but it is ONE sentence covering TWO purposes jointly, with no figure, no table row and no rate for either; Table 1 is captioned only "Reasons for citations in the methods section" and the paper has no stand-alone formula-or-value category. "Uncommon" is the authors' unquantified word. The percentages that ARE printed mix units, so no comparable denominator exists even for the categories that have one: How is per CITATION ("53% to 54% of citations in the methods section were used to explain study methods"), Who-or-what per PAPER ("11% to 21% of papers"), with biology reported as 41% Who-or-what, 31% How, 19% Why. Coverage, summed by the checker and NOT printed in the paper: 815 papers and about 10,852 methodological citations across three fields. The citation-chain case study used "15 parent articles (1 article per quintile per field)" and reports NO chain-depth statistic and NO dead-end count; its dead-end definition is documentary, "an inability to locate the cited article or resource" or "an article or resource that did not describe the cited method", not a provenance verdict, and the authors warn that this "small, nonrepresentative sample" cannot support how often each problem occurred. Nothing in it tests whether a cited numeric value rests on primary data.
- Attack 2's NAMED RESIDUAL SWEPT — laboratory-animal husbandry, 5 searches and 6 fetches, none refused, 3 of the 8 allowed searches unrun. No publication traces the Guide's cage-area tables, 20–26 °C range, 12:12 light or 10–15 air changes per hour to primary sources and counts how many rest on measured optimisation. The strongest items criticise the values without tracing them: the NRC 2004 workshop proceedings record "10 to 15 ac/h has historically proven successful in managing most animal thermal and respiration loads" with no primary study and "most data are outdated and date back to the 1950s or 1960s" (referent not stated in what was read); an NIH ORF ventilation summary states "Current ventilation guidelines are based largely on anthropomorphic views and not on scientifically defined animal needs"; Smith et al. 2004 (Comp Med 54(6):656) is quoted through the page summariser as "The recommendations are based on best professional judgment rather than experimental data", and its title and strain count were NOT reconciled against the paper itself. Unread and named: the 2011 Guide's own chapter 3 reference list (the NCBI Bookshelf route returned a reCAPTCHA) and the AALAS p527/p9 and PMC4587617/20/21 items. A bounded negative, not an absence proof — but a second domain showing the same pattern, which is evidence for the frame and against a renamed prior.
- Net: the objection stands in substance and loses its number, so it is rewritten below and promotion item (2) now carries the whole weight of the feasibility question, with no published rate on either side to size a pilot against.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3

Strongest remaining objection (rewritten post-verification; the original leaned on a rate that does not exist): the headline four rates are not a rule-independent estimand — the denominator is whatever the registered enumeration rule admits, "conditions no longer in use" has no criterion applying uniformly across thousands of heterogeneous parameters, and state (iii) has no hop rule — and whether states (i)–(iii) are estimable at all is now unevidenced in BOTH directions. Verification removed the one quantitative prop under the "(iv) will swamp everything" reading: Standvoss et al. 2024 says only that citations "referring to a formula or value, were uncommon in all 3 fields", jointly with a second purpose, with no figure and no stand-alone category, and its own chain case study reports no depth statistic and no dead-end count on 15 hand-picked parent articles. What is left is qualitative and one-directional: every source opened in this batch on a headline default (Klein 2022 on 37 °C / 5% CO2 / 18.6–20.9% O2 / pH 7.4; Wenger 2014 on serum and Eagle-era media; Kiernan on 4% formaldehyde and 24 h fixation) states the value and no origin, and the husbandry sweep found the same shape in a second domain, where 10–15 air changes per hour "has historically proven successful" with no primary study behind it. So the objection is that nobody knows whether the audit's states are estimable, with no published rate on either side to size the pilot that would find out — and limb (b), without which the record itself says the question is not the question, still runs only on the state-(ii) subsample documented well enough to re-run. SUPERSEDED (kept for the record): the original form read — The headline four rates are not a rule-independent estimand, and on P1's independently verified finding that methodological citations referring to a formula or value are "uncommon in all 3 fields" — with every source opened on the headline defaults (Klein 2022 on 37 C / 5% CO2 / 18.6-20.9% O2 / pH 7.4; Wenger 2014 on serum and Eagle-era media; Kiernan on 4% formaldehyde and 24 h fixation) stating the value and no origin — the trail most parameters would be traced along barely exists, so the audit's largest cell is likely "chain unresolvable", which indexes corpus digitisation and citation habit rather than evidential status; meanwhile limb (b), without which the record itself says the question is not the question, is executable only on the subsample of state (ii) whose original optimisation happens to be documented well enough to re-run.
Promotion requires: Validated requires all four of — (1) Well-posedness raised to 3/3 by a rule-independent or explicitly multi-rule estimand and a sharp, uniformly applicable criterion for "conditions no longer in use"; (2) a registered pilot on ~30 frame members reporting a coder-agreement statistic and showing that states (i)-(iii) are estimable rather than swamped by (iv), plus a characterisation of the re-runnable state-(ii) subsample against the full state-(ii) set so limb (b)'s bias is bounded; (3) a rubric revision adding a hop rule for state (iii) and a distinct code for jointly determined / satisficed parameters with no single optimum; (4) one documented instance of a provenance audit of this type changing a reporting standard or repository field, to defend presupposition 5 against PRO-MaP's verified silence. The laboratory-animal-husbandry vocabulary attack 2 named has now been SWEPT post-batch (5 searches, 6 fetches): no audit with a rate exists there, so there is no partial prior for the vivarium slice, and the sweep instead found the same value-without-origin pattern in a second domain. Two reads stay open from it and belong to item (2)'s feasibility case rather than to novelty: the 2011 Guide's own chapter 3 reference list, which the NCBI Bookshelf route could not open, and the AALAS p527/p9 and PMC4587617/20/21 items. Item (2) also carries more weight than Gate 5 gave it, because P1 supplies no rate to size the pilot's power against.

Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): register the enumeration rule and the four-state rubric, then run the ~30-parameter dual-coded pilot described above before any tracing at scale — the pilot is a feasibility measurement, not an answer to the question.

Routing (if rejected as already-asked): n/a — not rejected.

---
ID: UQ-20261017-36
Date: 2026-10-17
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): Medicine — respiratory medicine / clinical pharmacology of inhaled drugs. Adjacent: regulatory science (OINDP bioequivalence); aerosol science; measurement-error epidemiology.

Question (canonical):
In an inhaled-corticosteroid dose-ranging design in which nominal dose is randomised and per-patient delivered lung dose is independently estimated (recorded inhalation profiles plus device-specific in-vitro flow-to-dose characterisation, with actuation counts for adherence), how much do the fitted dose–response curve's maximum slope and ED50 differ when the exposure variable is estimated delivered dose rather than assigned nominal dose; and of the gap, what share is attributable to (a) dispersion of the nominal→delivered multiplier, (b) pharmacodynamic saturation, and (c) between-patient heterogeneity in corticosteroid responsiveness — with a stated test of whether the delivery multiplier is independent of baseline severity?
(V2, the Gate 1 reformulation; the one permitted reformulation was used. V1 asked whether the reported ICS flatness is "partly an artefact" of randomising label dose, and was re-specified because it named classical measurement error as the mechanism, which is wrong under randomisation.)

Alternative formulations:
- Does the ICS therapeutic ceiling reflect receptor/pathway saturation, or dispersion in the exposure variable every inhaled dose-ranging trial has used?
- If published inhaled dose-ranging trials were re-analysed on estimated delivered dose instead of prescribed dose, how far would the apparent plateau move, and what factor separates the two slopes?

Motivating gap:
Two literatures sit side by side and are never joined. The flat ICS dose–response is reported on nominal dose (Powell & Gibson, MJA 2003: "relatively flat, with little difference seen between doses of 100 μg and 1000 μg of fluticasone per day"; Masoli et al. 2004: ~200 μg/d fluticasone gives >=90% of maximal efficacy), and is the stated reason clinical-endpoint BE studies for generic inhalers are insensitive. Delivered dose depends strongly on flow, device and technique, and is characterised in aerosol science with no clinical endpoint attached. Gate 4 sharpened the gap into a demonstrated disciplinary boundary: the extrafine-vs-fine meta-analysis states "The amount of ICS depositing in the lungs determines the clinical efficacy" and then analyses on nominal dose ("Mean prescribed drug doses were calculated in terms of nominal dose"), while Assi/Chrystyn (Int J Pharm 2006) measures per-patient delivered dose in 20 severe asthmatics and reports no clinical endpoint at all.

Presuppositions:
1. Flat dose–response above low nominal doses is real and replicated. ESTABLISHED (two sources opened; corroborated by both adversaries at title/venue level).
2. Per-patient delivered dose is estimable from recorded profiles plus in-vitro flow–dose curves. ESTABLISHED AS A METHOD, but the record's "newly possible" framing is FALSIFIED: Assi et al. 2006 did exactly this with an Electronic Lung twenty years ago. Separately, the instrument/estimand pairing is wrong as written — flow profile x in-vitro flow-to-dose identifies emitted/fine-particle dose, not deposited lung dose (adversary 1, attack 4).
3. Between-patient delivered-dose variance is large relative to the nominal dose steps. CONTRADICTED IN ITS STATED FORM on the only opened measurement: fluticasone/Diskus FPD 20.4% (SD 4.8) of label, CV ~24%, ±1 SD ~1.6-fold against a 4–10-fold ladder (budesonide/Turbuhaler CV ~56%, ~2.8-fold). Escape, plausible but unsourced this run: FPD omits airway deposition, so true lung-dose σ is a lower bound of unknown slackness.
4. Exposure error predominantly non-differential w.r.t. outcome. CONTESTED; retained as an explicit limb of V2, not assumed. Severity-correlated airway geometry makes it differential roughly by construction (adversary 1).
5. Classical measurement error / regression dilution applies. FALSE AS STATED, caught and corrected at Gate 1; randomised nominal dose makes this Berkson-type, and the mechanism is mixture-induced flattening (convolution of log-shifted sigmoids). Adversary 2 independently verified the correction (Young's inequality: smearing can only broaden a transition).
6. Saturation does not fully account for the plateau. CONTESTED; the rival to be weighed.
7. Responsiveness heterogeneity flattens a group-mean curve on its own, by the same mixture mechanism, and is the explanation the field already gives. Hence a three-way apportionment.
8. Nominal dose was dispensed and taken as assigned, so adherence is a separate term. CONTESTED; V2 requires actuation-level data.

What would count as an answer:
Either (i) an analysis — prospective, or re-analysis of an inhaled dose-ranging trial with recorded profiles — reporting the endpoint's curve fitted on estimated delivered dose with a CI alongside the nominal-dose curve, the max-slope and ED50 difference, and the three-way apportionment with uncertainty; or (ii) a quantitative bound showing measured dispersion of the nominal→delivered multiplier is too small to generate the observed flattening, which answers no. Either branch must report whether the multiplier is independent of baseline severity, and must state how (a) and (c) were separated, since both enter the individual curve as a log-dose shift and are not separately identifiable from endpoint data alone.

Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result):
Gate 2: 11 web searches, 5 fetches attempted (1 failed). Gate 4: 13 further searches in new vocabularies (8 by adversary 1, 5 by adversary 2) and 6 fetches. 24 distinct queries total; full lists in batches/2026-10-17-1619/UQ-20261017-36-record.md and the two adversary files. Most informative:
- "flat dose-response inhaled corticosteroids asthma plateau explained by measurement error in delivered dose versus nominal dose" → the flatness literature itself; no exposure-artefact framing.
- Own-field/own-words title query, "group mean curve flattened by between-patient variability ... apparent plateau artefact" → Masoli 2004 and Szefler 2002; the field asks "why flat" and answers "individual variability in response".
- Method-owning-field query (regression calibration / pharmacoepidemiology) → machinery only, never pointed at inhaled dosing; adversary 2's radiation-dosimetry sweep (shared/unshared Berkson dose error) is a second independent negative in the method field.
- "clinical endpoint bioequivalence OINDP insensitive ... FDA guidance" → FDA deck opened; cites "high variability in response data" but does not attribute insensitivity to curve flatness or to delivered dose. Named duplicate risk does not hold.
- "fine particle dose as dose metric ... better predictor than nominal dose" (adversary 2) → Assi/Chrystyn 2006, the candidate's own instrument, opened.
- "extrafine HFA beclomethasone CFC dose equivalence ... equal clinical efficacy lower nominal dose" (adversary 2) → extrafine-vs-fine meta-analysis, a neighbour family Gate 2 missed entirely, opened.
- "population average dose-response curve flatter than individual curves, mixture of sigmoids, apparent Hill slope attenuation" (adversary 1) → Proost/Eleveld/Struys AAPS J 2021, the drug-agnostic mechanism prior Gate 2 missed.
- Gate 2's flagged gap, Clin Pharmacokinet 10.1007/s40262-013-0078-1, was opened by adversary 2 via the publisher route and CLOSED IN THE CANDIDATE'S FAVOUR: Allen 2013 is cortisol suppression on systemic AUC24 and explicitly declines the comparison ("differences in delivered lung dose have no relevance for these analyses").
- Quantity-already-published limb: deposition variance is published in aerosol science, PD slopes in pharmacometrics, but no published nominal-vs-delivered slope ratio or attenuation factor was found in 24 queries.
Searches refused by the environment's safety classifier (persistently, both adversaries): 1 of 9 for adversary 1 (after all 8 Disguise queries ran), and 3 of 8 for adversary 2 (Disguise incomplete at 5 of 8).

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
1. Masoli M, Holt S, Weatherall M, Beasley R. "The dose-response relationship of inhaled corticosteroids in asthma." Curr Allergy Asthma Rep 2004;4(2):144-148, doi 10.1007/s11882-004-0060-y (abstract + reference annotations opened; BODY PAYWALLED, COULD NOT READ via link.springer.com direct). Unit: trial arm/patient in meta-analysis. Endpoint: ICS efficacy composites plus systemic side-effects. Comparator: a lower nominal daily dose. Estimand: shape of mean efficacy vs prescribed nominal dose, and the dose giving >=90% of maximal efficacy.
2. Assi KH, Chrystyn H, Pearson SB, Tarsin W. "Emitted dose estimates from Seretide Diskus and Symbicort Turbuhaler following inhalation by severe asthmatics." Int J Pharm 2006;316(1-2):131-137 (opened via bradscholars.brad.ac.uk). Unit: the individual severe asthmatic (n=20), recorded profile replayed through an Electronic Lung. Endpoint: fine particle dose as % labelled dose (fluticasone 20.4%, SD 4.8). Comparator: device vs device, and FPD-vs-PIFR slope. Estimand: emitted/fine-particle dose and its flow dependence. No clinical endpoint, no dose–response curve.
3. Extrafine versus fine inhaled corticosteroids in relation to asthma control: systematic review and meta-analysis of observational real-life studies (PDF opened at iris.unife.it). Unit: the patient, pooled across observational cohorts; arms are two formulations. Endpoint: asthma control (OR 1.34) and exacerbations (RR 0.84). Comparator: extrafine vs fine formulation at prescribed doses (256 vs 428 μg). Estimand: group-mean effect of formulation on nominal dose — "Mean prescribed drug doses were calculated in terms of nominal dose".
Also weighed, one rung further out: Powell & Gibson, MJA 2003;178(5):223-225 (opened; supplies the premise, explicitly does not discuss delivered dose, technique or exposure error); Proost, Eleveld & Struys, AAPS J 2021;23(1):10, doi 10.1208/s12248-020-00549-7 (abstract/conclusions opened via research.rug.nl, BODY NOT OPENED; drug-agnostic result that population-predicted steepness is less than individuals', with an empirical equation in IIV of C50 and gamma); Rajaraman et al., J Aerosol Sci 2026;194:106784 (nearest on method, but simulated subjects, a bronchodilator, no nominal-dose comparator, neither adversary re-verified it).

Novelty — how this differs from each:
- vs Masoli 2004: same object and same question verb ("why is it flat?"), but the exposure variable is nominal throughout and the answer offered is heterogeneity of pharmacodynamic response. No term for a slope ratio between two exposure definitions. Closest prior; this is what caps the grade at Medium.
- vs Assi 2006: performs the candidate's measurement and stops there — the dependent variable is emitted dose, not a clinical endpoint, and there is no dose ladder and no curve. It supplies the instrument and the magnitude input, and withdraws the record's "new instrument" claim, but poses no apportionment.
- vs the extrafine meta-analysis: the field's own closest question-shape (does response track delivered rather than labelled dose?) with a group-level number, but a different unit and estimand — two formulations' group means on nominal dose, no deposition percentage, no curve on delivered dose, no slope ratio, nothing on error in the dose variable. Adversary 2 checked it as a candidate kill and found it cannot adjudicate the mechanism, since both arms are themselves smeared populations walking along the already-convolved curve.
- vs Proost 2021: the mechanism, stated drug-agnostically and without the clinical object; it predicts marginal flattening and names the (a)/(c) identifiability obstruction, but computes no inhaled-specific apportionment. Its existence is why the triviality and reason-for-silence attacks bite.

Novelty confidence: Medium
(Distinct across 24 queries including two independent sweeps of the method-owning field; but the candidate's own literature asks "why flat" and has settled on a rival answer, and Gate 4 surfaced two neighbour families Gate 2 missed. Not Low: no prior shares the candidate's unit, exposure variable and estimand. The record's claim that "no hit frames the plateau as an exposure-variable question" is too strong and is struck.)

Significance — consequence:
If yes (delivered-dose curve materially steeper, steepening not absorbed by the responsiveness term): the therapeutic ceiling becomes partly a property of the exposure variable, making clinical-endpoint insensitivity for OINDP BE a fixable design problem and making delivery optimisation a quantified alternative to dose escalation. If no (dispersion too small): the saturation/responsiveness account gains a number for the first time, supporting step-down guidance and the regulatory case for in-vitro plus PK surrogates. Both branches move a decision. Adversary 2 narrows the stake: the record's own Masoli datum caps the efficacy available to apportion at <=10% of maximal over 200→1000 μg, and smearing implies the individual ED90 sits below the group ED90, so a "yes" moves the ceiling down, not up.

Significance — audience:
(i) Regulatory inhalation scientists at FDA OGD and EMA, on record (Gate 2 query 4) wanting "the most sensitive dose-response approach", and demonstrably working on sources of variability and power for locally-acting PD equivalence; (ii) respiratory guideline committees whose dose-step tables encode the plateau (and, per adversary 2, the German/Spanish literature encodes it as equivalence tables on label dose); (iii) inhaler and smart-inhaler manufacturers, for whom an attenuation factor is the first efficacy-denominated argument for flow sensing; (iv) pharmacometricians in model-informed development for inhaled products.

Significance — fecundity:
Opens the same apportionment for inhaled bronchodilators, antibiotics and insulin-type products; opens the within-patient between-actuation reproducibility of the multiplier as a floor on any inhaled trial's power; opens randomising delivered rather than label dose, which no inhaled trial has done; opens the symmetric question for the side-effect curve, whose route differs; and, per adversary 2, opens splitting (c) into a potency limb and a responder/Emax limb, which no delivery correction can touch.

Significance — anchoring:
The ICS therapeutic-ceiling anomaly; insensitive clinical endpoints for orally inhaled products; the unresolved in-vitro/in-vivo correlation dispute (presupposition 2 is the same dispute, which is why a "yes" would be contested); and what randomisation does and does not protect when the randomised variable is a proxy for the exposure of interest.

Reason for silence:
Primary mechanism, a three-sided disciplinary boundary, SURVIVES and is better evidenced after Gate 4 than in the record: aerosol science holds per-patient delivered doses with no clinical endpoint (Assi 2006), clinical respiratory medicine holds the endpoints and analyses on nominal dose (extrafine meta-analysis, Powell & Gibson), and the correction machinery sits in measurement-error epidemiology, which has never been pointed at inhaled dosing (two independent negatives, in regression-calibration and in radiation-dosimetry vocabularies). The extrafine meta-analysis states both halves in one paragraph: deposited amount determines efficacy, and the analysis is on prescribed dose. Secondary mechanism, "new instrument", is WITHDRAWN: the capability is twenty years old, and the group that had it published the delivered doses without posing the apportionment. Third mechanism, incentive asymmetry (neither guideline writers nor generic sponsors benefit from reopening the flatness), is independent of the withdrawn leg and untouched.

Adversary 2's arithmetic from the source's mean(SD) gives a true/observed max-slope ratio of ~1.02–1.08x (Diskus) to ~1.10–1.36x (Turbuhaler), ~2.0x only at an implausible CV ~130%. | Only the bound is cheap.
