Novelty — how this differs from each: vs A — A's family is harness configuration (option order, template, scoring), already treated as known-sensitive and not semantics-preserving, with weights and greedy decoding fixed; no numerics arm, no concordance statistic, no null, no margin conditioning, batch size unreported. BUT A publishes the candidate's share-of-score limb as a number for its own family and names the margin-based per-item flip predictor as explicit future work (Section 6). vs B — B's unit is the tool-call / safety decision, not the MCQ item; no nominally-lossless arm and no overlap statistic between its three methods. BUT B delivers, calibrated over 131,758 predictions, exactly the candidate's declared third determinate outcome within the quantization family. vs C — C covers the dtype and hardware arms and even asserts the shared unstable-item stratum, but by manual inspection, with no statistic, no null, no quantization arm in the same design and no batch-size-1 control; the candidate is the measured version of C's unmeasured aside, which makes it asked-but-unquantified rather than un-asked. vs Hu et al. — within the quantization family only, unmatched bit widths, small CV/NLP models, no formal overlap statistic and no null; but it pre-empts the margin mechanism seven years early and refutes the record's reason-for-silence. Genuinely unposed residual in everything opened: the P-way concordance statistic itself, with lossy and nominally-lossless arms crossed on one item frame against a within-type null and a margin-conditioned residual. Adversary 2 cleared the record's highest-risk unread title (2609.04748) and found it episode-level with no concordance statistic, which strengthens that residual rather than closing it.
Novelty confidence: Low (composite). Two of the three limbs are pre-empted for adjacent families: the share-of-score limb is published for harness configuration (A), and margin-predicts-flips is fitted and calibrated for quantization (B); the existence claim is already asserted in print for numerics (C), and the margin mechanism was established for quantized models in 2022 (Hu et al.). Residual-limb novelty (cross-type concordance alone) is Medium on both adversaries' independent reading, but the composite question as posed is Low, and the motivating-gap text materially mis-stated the state of the field.
Significance — consequence: If yes, a benchmark acquires a reportable fragile share, compression-robustness claims become conditional on which stratum a perturbation lands in, and eval releases could ship transferable per-item fragility annotations. If no, fragility is a property of the perturbation and each perturbation must be evaluated on its own — which is current practice, so the no-branch ratifies practice rather than changing it. If margin explains it, fragility is computable from logits alone — the cheapest branch, and the one B has substantially delivered for quantization.
Significance — audience: Real, identified and already active on this exact object — eval-harness maintainers (A is written from inside eval methodology; 2604.03244 argues for standardized item-level releases; 2605.28873 recommends retaining per-example correctness), compression researchers, inference-engine maintainers, release auditors. Discounted because two of three branches already have published partial answers the audience could act on.
Significance — fecundity: Does fragile-stratum membership transfer across checkpoints or model families on the same items? Does rescoring on the robust stratum change rankings (A's Kendall 0.42 suggests it would)? Does the stratum coincide with known-mislabelled items (MMLU-Redux), making numeric fragility a cheap item-defect detector? Is the between-type component itself a reportable model property?
Significance — anchoring: 2407.09141's unanalysed flips metric; numerical nondeterminism and batch invariance (2506.09501, HEAL, vLLM batch-invariance work); config fragility (2608.21382); fidelity-metric choice (2606.19558); prediction churn and predictive multiplicity (2102.03349 and the Rashomon ambiguity measure); untransplanted common-cause-failure machinery (IEC/IAEA, 2204.03717); SE disagreement testing (DiffChaser IJCAI 2019, 2204.04220, DiverGet 2207.06282); ledger entries UQ-20261016-06, UQ-20261017-26, UQ-20261017-30.
Reason for silence: The record's stated mechanism — a disciplinary boundary with no shared unit of analysis, the item being a means rather than an endpoint — is refuted, independently, by both adversaries. The SE DNN-testing field has taken the per-input disagreement as its endpoint since 2019 and compared four quantization configurations on one item frame in 2022 (2204.04220); 2609.04748 already crosses a lossy arm with a nominally lossless one; 2605.28873 already recommends exactly the per-item paired machinery. Two replacement mechanisms are sourced but are the adversaries' constructions, not the record's: (i) differential testing treats the unquantized model as the oracle, so the reference's own numerical nondeterminism is outside the frame by design, and crossing lossy with lossless arms requires giving up that oracle, which only became natural once FP32 anchors and batch-invariant kernels made the "lossless" arm visibly lossy; (ii) data availability — 2605.28873 states "we did not retain the per-example records under our compute budget", and standardized item-level releases are still being argued for. Under the Gate 4 rule a failed reason-for-silence makes the novelty finding suspect and returns the entry to Gate 2, which is where it already fails.
Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status) — two adversaries on the Gate 0-3 record only, adversary 2 blind to adversary 1; status shown is the worse of the two, both logs verbatim in UQ-20261017-46-adversary-1.md and -2.md:
1. Triviality | All four arms perturb the same final logit vector, so small-margin items flip under every arm and the existence limb is a near-corollary; Hu et al. 2022 separate per-input quantization flips by margin at >0.9 AUC-ROC in 23/30 settings and B fits and calibrates the relation for 16 LLMs, so the margin limb is answered; and the top-decile share is bounded by 0.1/accuracy by construction (adversaries' own arithmetic, ~0-15 pp at 67% accuracy). | The post-margin residual is not derivable from a page: margin is measured in one reference configuration that is itself a perturbation, B's own abstract says borrowed constants are wrong by 18-33 points between bit widths of the same family so the relation is not transportable to a dtype cast or kernel swap, and A records margin only as input to a future predictor. The share limb can be re-posed against an absolute pre-registered threshold. | Partial (both)
2. Disguise | Renamed known: SE "disagreement" testing (DiffChaser 2019; Hu et al. 2204.04220, four quantization configurations on one item frame, union-of-disagreements column, margin predicts), DIF and item-parameter drift, flaky tests across configurations, discordant-call concordance in genomics, prediction churn, common-cause failure, ISO 5725 reproducibility conditions. | 17 new-vocabulary queries across both adversaries (8 + 9, none run at Gate 2) found no instance of the question on the candidate's object: Hu et al. stay within the quantization family at unmatched bit widths on small CV/NLP models with no concordance statistic and no null; Genome Research 33:999 is the same shape on variants; 2605.28873 explicitly declines the per-item paired tests; 2609.04748, cleared by adversary 2, is episode-level. No opened source puts a lossy and a nominally-lossless arm on one item frame with Jaccard/kappa/common-factor concordance against a within-type null. | Partial (adversary 1) / Resolved (adversary 2)

Combinatorial novelty | Compression x numerical reproducibility x psychometric concordance, with the item-vs-perturbation interface already settled in principle by the shared logit-margin mechanism both parents name. | A real interface problem exists and it is arithmetic, not rhetorical: the two-level null needs exchangeable instances within type and two of four arms have none, so the transplant does not go through cleanly; A's extraction-rule finding also shows at least one non-margin pathway. | Partial (adversary 1) / Resolved (adversary 2)

Adversary 2's additional hit — prefix/KV-cache state as a second mediator surviving batch size 1 — is repairable but unpinned, and the adversary labelled it unproven in the single-turn MCQ regime. | Partial (both)

Adversary 2 could not open a primary multilevel-estimation source and recorded the two-level-2-units concern at Partial strength, explicitly not as a kill. | Partial (both)

  Fatal-attack check: no Unresolved on attacks 1, 2 or 4 from either adversary, and no Unresolved anywhere; both Disguise sweeps were executed in full, so nothing is Unverified. Gate 4 therefore neither rejects nor rescues. Adversary 1 recommended Rejected, adversary 2 Provisional; the judge takes neither recommendation on Gate 4 grounds, because Low novelty is itself a Gate 2 rejection under the ledger's rule.
Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3
Strongest remaining objection: The question's primary limb is pre-answered by a shared cause the literature already names and measures — the top-1/top-2 logit margin. Hu et al. (2204.04220, 2022) showed per-input quantization flips separate on margin at AUC-ROC above 0.9 in 23 of 30 settings across two toolchains and two bit widths; 2608.06564 (2026) fits and calibrates the same relation across 16 LLMs over 131,758 decisions; HEAL names the mechanism outright. What is left genuinely unposed is a post-margin concordance residual whose companion share-of-score limb is bounded by construction once defined by decile — a narrower question than the one the record asks, and one whose own two-level null rests on roughly two arms with exchangeable instances.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): Not for this ledger; routed below. Were it pursued, the first step belongs to whoever takes the routed problem: restate the estimand as the item random effect common across types under a type-specific p_{i,t} null, drop the kernel arm to a fixed-effect contrast, and read the full texts of 2608.06564, 2609.04748 (OpenReview PDF; the arXiv PDF route returned empty for adversary 1), NeurIPS 2026 178257, 2605.30218, 2607.09999 and 2604.27405 before any measurement.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): Yes — asked-but-still-open, on the residual limb only. Routed to ledger/routed-open-problems.md as an open problem in AI evaluation methodology. Open-ness is sourced to three papers opened at Gate 2 or by the adversaries: 2608.21382 Section 6 names the margin-based per-item flip predictor as future work; 2606.21023 (HEAL) asserts that flips "generally originate from highly unstable questions" on manual inspection with no statistic; 2605.28873 states "We do not run paired McNemar tests on per-example correctness" and "we did not retain the per-example records under our compute budget", recommending the machinery instead. The share-of-score and margin-predictor limbs are NOT routed: they are published for adjacent families (A, B) and are answered, not open. Rough tier: B — tractable on one checkpoint, one MCQ benchmark, batch size 1, a few hundred GPU-hours, but gated on repairing the exchangeability defect in the kernel and dtype arms and on pinning prefix/KV-cache state as a controlled mediator, so it is not shovel-ready.

Verification (post-batch, 2026-10-17): four fresh-context readers, one per prior, each given the claim and its source and none shown the adversaries' reasoning. All four returned. The Gate 2 ground survives first-hand verification on the two priors that carry it; the third leg is materially weaker than this entry states, and one correction enlarges the routed residual. No late Gate 4 was run, and the reason is set out in the last bullet. What changed:
  • Prior A (arXiv:2608.21382) came back confirmed in unusual detail, including every absence this entry rests on. The design is exactly 12 models x 3,679 items x 26 configurations (ARC 1,000 + HellaSwag 1,000 + MMLU 1,000 + TruthfulQA 679 = 3,679; 4 generation templates x 6 option orders = 24, plus 2 cloze stems = 26). All five absence claims are NOT FOUND after a full-document read: no numerics arm of any kind (no quantization, dtype, kernel or decode-seed variation — weights fixed, greedy decoding, seed inert), no overlap or concordance statistic between perturbation types, no per-item null model or permutation test, no conditioning of fragility on the margin, and no stated batch size — the word "batch" does not occur in the document. Section 6 does name a margin-based per-item flip predictor as future work. Three narrowing corrections: 95.7% is an unweighted mean over the 10 adjacent model pairs with a non-zero gap, with the 11th (gap 0.000) excluded, and pooling items instead gives 99.7%; the 0.85 config-lucky fraction is the share of each model's reference-CORRECT answers that flip to wrong under some other configuration, unweighted over the 12 models; and the margin is recorded in the release for the plain-cloze scorer ONLY, not for all 26 configurations, which weakens this entry's "A records the margin" slightly and leaves A's own future-work route narrower than it reads. Kendall 0.42 is the mean over non-reference configurations with a minimum of -0.09 and about 29% of pairwise orderings flipped; the 0.28 correlation is 0.2767 with a 2,000-resample CI of 0.25–0.30. The date conflict this entry already flagged is real and unexplained in the source: arXiv stamp 17 Jul 2026, PDF title page 25 Aug 2026, and a 2608 identifier that fits neither.
  • Prior B (arXiv:2608.06564) was read in FULL for the first time by anyone in this audit — Gate 2 and both adversaries had only its abstract page — and it holds up, with one unit error to correct and one finding that helps the candidate. The unit is the individual paired binary decision (whether to call a tool, which tool, safety refusal), identified by first tokens, not the benchmark item. It does fit P(flip | margin) = Phi(-(c*m+b)*sign(m)/sigma) per cell from margins alone with no flips in the fit, exactly as recorded. CORRECTION: the 0.86 / 0.33 / 0.00 medians at 4 / 3 / 2 bits are medians of the SURVIVING MARGIN FRACTION c, a regression slope, not "median damage" — the paper's abstract glosses them as damage being proportional rather than fixed, and this entry inherited the gloss as the quantity. Their n is not stated; about 20% of roughly 1,300 cells are not slope-estimable. The other figures are exact with their denominators now known: 1.8 points is the median absolute error of the held-out flip-rate forecast over 868 cells (1.2 in-sample; a separate 585-cell forecast gives 1.5), 0.004 is expected calibration error over 131,758 per-item predictions drawn from 1,113 cells, and 18–33 points is the borrowed-constant transfer error at 3 bits and below — at 4 bits it is only 0.2–8.5. "Kinds of decision do not break together" is verbatim in the abstract. FAVOURING THE CANDIDATE: B has no nominally-lossless arm at all, and no concordance statistic — only raw same-item counts (GPTQ w2 and a simulated 3-bit activation-aware quantizer flip the same 77 of 77 should-call and 16 of 16 should-not-call items; plain and Hadamard-rotated match on the same counts). Its Sec 5.1 states that which decision breaks is a property of the ITEM rather than of the algorithm, which is this candidate's premise asserted in print for the quantization family without a cross-type statistic. Its model count is internally inconsistent (16 across 8 families in the abstract; 12, ten and 14 at various body points; Table 3 lists 17 entries), so 16 is the headline and the body counts are unverified.
  • Prior Hu et al. (arXiv:2204.04220) holds on its substance with two description errors. "27 out of 30" and "23 (out of 30)" are both verbatim in Sec 5.3, but the 30 settings are model x TRAINING STRATEGY (six CNNs x four strategies plus two RNNs x three, with no quantization-aware training for the RNNs), not the four quantization configurations this entry implies, and the 27/30 is Margin beating Entropy, Gini and Least Confidence rather than a margin-versus-anything-else result. "In Total" is a ROW, not a column, in Table 6 (Sec 5.4, retraining), whose caption reads "In total: disagreements in a test dataset regardless of the quantization technique" and never says "union". The adversary's arithmetic is nonetheless CORRECT: LeNet1's four configuration rows sum to 25 against an In-total of 15, so at least 10 disagreement events are shared, and NiN's sum to 590 against 540, so at least 50 — and the same gap appears in other rows (ResNet20 698 vs 536, DenseNet 5066 vs 3834). But this holds only if "In total" counts each distinct input once, which the paper never states, and the paper's text never discusses cross-configuration overlap anywhere. No uncertainty is reported on any count; the AUC figures come from a single 9:1 split. Models are small vision and NLP networks, as recorded. A later same-author CAIN 2023 paper carries a different title, so a citation may point at either.
  • Prior C (HEAL, arXiv:2606.21023) is where this entry overstates, in two ways that pull in opposite directions. AGAINST THE ENTRY: 6.2 +/- 0.4 is not a flip count but a PERCENTAGE flip rate with a standard error of the mean (Table 2, BF16 / Qwen3-8B), and the paper never states its denominator. FOR THE CANDIDATE, and more important: HEAL does NOT cross attention implementation. All baselines run TritonAttention because FlashAttention lacks 32-bit support, and Table 1 only profiles the two kernels on an A100; what it crosses is dtype, hardware and batching/request-order. This entry and its record both list attention implementation among C's arms, and that is wrong — so the kernel arm is unoccupied in C as well as in A and B, and the routed residual is one arm larger than recorded. Also narrowing C's reach: the "highly unstable questions" sentence is in Appendix B.1 as two fragments around "a substantial portion of the answer flips", is scoped to relatively high-precision configurations, rests on manual inspection with no statistic or count, and is framed by its authors as a dataset-quality caveat about the model's limited capability on hard questions rather than as a finding about flip concentration. No per-item propensity, no concordance statistic, no null model, and no batch-size-1 control — the paper says a large batch size is strictly required for its flip analysis. The title is longer than recorded ("... : Achieving Reproducible Inference for Mission-Critical Tasks with HEAL"), and while the anchor is FP32 LayerCast on an H100 the MedQA flip analysis ran only on an MI300X.
  • No late Gate 4, and this is the call to check. The rejection is a Gate 2 composite: two of three limbs pre-empted for adjacent families. Both of those two were verified at first hand and both hold — A publishes the share-of-score limb for harness configuration, B fits and calibrates margin-predicts-flips for quantization over 131,758 predictions, and Hu et al. put the margin mechanism in print in 2022. The leg that weakened is the third, C's assertion of a shared unstable-item stratum, which is now a manual-inspection aside rather than an assertion the field has made — and that leg was the one supporting "asked-but-unquantified" rather than the Low grade itself. A decoration fell; the ground did not. So the verdict stands without a cold re-run, the routed residual is strengthened rather than withdrawn, and the two corrections that favour the candidate (no kernel arm anywhere, and B's item-property claim without a cross-type statistic) belong to the routed problem, not to a rescue of this entry.

ID: UQ-20261017-47
Date: 2026-10-17
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): AI architecture — training systems and compute accounting (secondary: compute governance, scaling-law methodology)
Question (canonical): For a frame F of models declared before any data pull (open-recipe releases publishing RL/distillation configurations and hardware-hours; closed models admitted only as interval bounds), and under three boundaries declared in advance — B1 the European Commission's GPAI boundary (C(2025) 5045 ¶119–122), B2 that boundary widened to include RL rollout and verifier inference, distillation-teacher inference and abandoned runs, B3 = B2 denominated in GPU-hours or board energy — what is the distribution of R = (rollout + verifier + synthetic-data + teacher + discarded)/(gradient-step), what is Spearman ρ between reported "training compute" and total production compute, and how many models change 10^25 FLOP status (EU AI Act Art. 51(2)) between boundaries? (V2; the Gate 1 reformulation, scored as canonical. V1 — "under a declared accounting boundary, what is the distribution of R and does ranking by total production compute reorder models?" — is retained in the record.)
Alternative formulations: How much of the compute that made a model was spent on inference rather than on updating weights, and does counting it change which models are the "biggest"? · Is "training compute" an additive quantity for models produced by RL and distillation pipelines, or does its value depend on an accounting boundary nobody has declared?
Motivating gap: Presupposition inversion on the claim that a model is summarised by one additive "training compute" figure, load-bearing both in scaling-law comparisons and in law (AI Act 10^25 FLOP presumption). Two of the intake's load-bearing premises were falsified at Gate 2: a boundary HAS been declared, in detail and twice over, by C(2025) 5045 ¶118–125; and the adjacent literature treats this as an accounting, not an allocation, problem (Epoch, "Three challenges facing compute-based AI policies"). Gate 4 falsified the one gap claim the record said survived — that failed/abandoned runs are the component no declared boundary counts: the Frontier Model Forum's "Measuring Training Compute" brief (2024-05-02) declares that "Discarded versions or branches should not be included."
Presuppositions: (1) enough models decompose over a non-trivial frame — CONTESTED; demonstrated one model at a time (DeepSeek-R1, ~2× sensitivity to the batch-size assumption alone), so a bound, not a distribution, for most of the population. (2) gradient-step and non-gradient-step compute separable under a stated boundary — CONTESTED, and ¶122 settles it by fiat, which shows the boundary is declarable, not discoverable. (3) reported figures are intended as totals — HOLDS; conventions genuinely differ (Epoch documents "total … including pretraining" and is silent on RL/rollouts/synthetic data; ¶118 is parameter-update-only for one threshold, cumulative for the other; Epoch's GPT-5 note folds RL into its headline figure with no published rule). (4) a regulatory threshold is applied to such a figure — ESTABLISHED. (5) discarded/failed runs belong under at least one defensible boundary — CONTESTED, and now contradicted by two declared boundaries (EC ¶122; FMF brief). (6) training and inference FLOP commensurable — CONTESTED; ¶125 answers by fiat, hence B3. (7) a published compute ranking exists to reorder — ESTABLISHED (Epoch, 33 models ≥1e25 FLOP).
What would count as an answer: per-model estimates with stated uncertainty of the five components under B1/B2/B3; the distribution of R; Spearman ρ against reported training compute; the count of models crossing or ceasing to cross 10^25 FLOP per boundary. Decision margin inherited from the regulated text: a boundary choice that moves a figure by more than the 30% estimation error ¶123 tolerates. A small, boundary-insensitive R would license current practice.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 20 searches and 13 fetches in all — Gate 2: 11 searches, 5 fetches (full list: batches/2026-10-17-2046/UQ-20261017-47-record.md); Gate 4: 9 searches + 4 fetches per adversary (UQ-20261017-47-adversary-1.md, -2.md). Most informative: `reported training compute underestimates true compute reinforcement learning synthetic data teacher inference should be counted threshold recalculation study` (answer-seeking, own field, own words) → the on-point prior, Epoch "Three challenges facing compute-based AI policies"; `European Commission GPAI guidelines July 2025 training compute estimation cumulative FLOP definition synthetic data generation` → C(2025) 5045 ANNEX, the intake's own nominated pre-emption, which fired; `how many models exceed 10^25 FLOP EU AI Act systemic risk count` → the count is already published (33 models, one boundary only); `life cycle assessment AI model training system boundary … failed runs hyperparameter search` → LCA owns the method, endpoint is kgCO2e, no FLOP-denominated R; adversary-1 `frontier lab compute budget breakdown … failed runs versus final pretraining run` → arXiv 2605.01158 (Olmo 3), the strongest kill; adversary-2 `think tank report counting rules training compute threshold which models would be covered under alternative definitions` → FMF "Measuring Training Compute" brief (second declared boundary) and Epoch "Model counts and compute thresholds". Disguise sweeps covered LCA/energy, HPC job accounting, composite-indicator sensitivity analysis, compute-verification/audit, compliance-notification, model-card standards, industry-analyst, German and Chinese vocabularies. Ledger duplicate check: INDEX.md read in full (the generated figure said 145 entries; the committed index at batch start held 135 entry rows in 144 lines, so this is neither count and the tally is wrong — corrected after the batch, and the check itself ran against the real file, as the sibling record's correct "144 lines" shows); nearest is UQ-20261016-30 (claimed vs realized training set) — same genre, different object; no duplicate.
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources): P1 — Epoch AI, Somala, Ho & Krier, "Three challenges facing compute-based AI policies", 2025-09-11, https://epoch.ai/gradient-updates/three-issues-undermining-compute-based-ai-policies (opened at Gate 2 and re-read by adversary 2): unit = frontier model and its pipeline; endpoint = whether a reported figure captures capability-driving compute; comparator = pretraining compute, and policy instruments against each other; estimand = informal best guesses (phi-4 synthetic data ~25% of pretraining; R1-Zero RL ~1/5 of base pretraining; DistilBERT 3%; o1-high <10% of GPT-4o pretraining), stating that teacher compute is ignored and reward-model compute "remains entirely unaccounted for". P2 — European Commission, C(2025) 5045 final ANNEX, 18 July 2025, ¶¶118–132 (opened): unit = one GPAI model per provider; endpoint = cumulative training compute as notification trigger; comparator = 10^23 and 10^25 FLOP, one-third-of-original for modifiers; estimand = a provider's point estimate accurate within 30% under a declared inclusion/exclusion list. P3 — Epoch AI, "Final training runs account for a minority of R&D compute spending", https://epoch.ai/gradient-updates/r-and-d-vs-training-compute (opened): unit = company-window (n=3); endpoint = final-run share of R&D compute **spending in USD** (9.6%, 22.6%, 12.3%); estimand = a share with Monte Carlo 90% intervals. Added at Gate 4, both opened: arXiv 2605.01158 "The Hidden Cost of Thinking" (the Olmo 3 7B/32B Instruct/Think family, measured by Morrison, Smith and Strubell rather than reported by its own authors (see the verification block) — per-stage GPU-hours and energy for pretraining, mid-training, SFT, DPO, RLVR split into generator and trainer, synthetic-data generation (in a separate table and a non-comparable hardware unit, outside the 82.2% denominator), and development including failed runs and ablations; "Development costs … account for 82.2% of total compute"; final-run-only reporting understates by ~5×); Frontier Model Forum, "Issue Brief: Measuring Training Compute", 2024-05-02 (a second declared boundary: "Discarded versions or branches should not be included"). Checked and found NOT to be priors: arXiv 2502.00003 (object is compute-reducing loopholes keeping a model under a threshold — the record's named unread tightening source, read by adversary 2, tightens nothing); Shavit 2303.11341 (whether a claimed figure is true, not what it should include). Not opened, grounding nothing: Hooker; Heim & Koessler 2405.10799; JRC143255; arXiv 2502.08606; 2109.01313; Saisana et al. 2005.
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs P1 — differences are of form, not of question: P1 has no declared frame, no uncertainty on its ratios, no boundary factor, no rank correlation, no threshold recount, and never mentions failed runs; the candidate's estimand is a strict superset of P1's five scattered point ratios. But P1 poses, names and partly prices the candidate's question in the candidate's own field and words, which is fatal to novelty rather than to interest. vs P2 — P2's unit and endpoint match the governance limb exactly and P2 declares the boundary the candidate said nobody had declared; P2 is normative and prospective, fixes no quantities, and never tests whether its own exclusions move a figure by more than the 30% it tolerates. Novelty confidence: Low
Significance — consequence: If R is large and boundary-sensitive, the 10^25 trigger is partly a function of a drafting choice and ¶123's 30% margin is not the binding uncertainty — the boundary is; and pooled scaling-law comparisons regress on an x-axis whose boundary silently moved, understating recent compute. If R is small and boundary-insensitive, current practice is licensed — a useful negative. Adversary 2's own arithmetic from P1's figures qualifies the record's illustration: a model at 7e24 FLOP needs R ≥ 0.43 to reach 1e25, so R = 0.2 does not lift it, while P1's projection that reasoning training "could soon constitute the majority of total training compute" implies R > 1.
Significance — audience: EU AI Office (owns ¶119–122; most exposed exclusions are reward/value models, now verifiers, and failed training runs); third-party trackers, Epoch explicitly, whose ≥1e25 count is the number policy cites and whose own threshold-count work declares post-trained variants "out of scope for this work" and needing investigation; scaling-law methodologists; providers drafting systemic-risk notifications under ¶123 with no reference distribution; model-card standards bodies (the FMF convened a brief precisely to fix this convention; the authors of that study — Morrison, Smith and Strubell, not the Olmo 3 report, see the verification block — call for development-compute reporting standards). Significance — fecundity: what denominator is defensible for a legal trigger once arithmetic intensity differs by an order of magnitude between rollouts and gradient steps; whether a boundary-stable capability-per-compute metric exists; whether thresholds should rest on cloud-attestable hardware-hours rather than provider-computed FLOP; how to price a distillation chain whose teacher is excluded by fiat; whether a "discarded run" is auditable after the fact.
Significance — anchoring: the Biden-EO-vs-AI-Act boundary divergence (P1); ¶118's split definitions; the compute-threshold critique literature (Hooker; Heim & Koessler; 2502.00003 — none load-bearing here); distillation scaling laws reported under teacher-included and -excluded accounting; the LCA boundary-setting tradition, which owns the method and now has an AI instance (2605.01158) that still uses energy rather than FLOP as its functional unit.
Reason for silence: Partial silence only, and the mechanism is an incentive-and-purpose split between the two communities that count — a tracker wants the narrowest boundary estimable from public disclosures and excludes ancillary compute by construction; a regulator wants the boundary a provider can evidence within 30% and excludes what it could not. Neither gains from publishing the cross-boundary sensitivity. Plus a data mechanism: per-model rollout decomposition became inferable only with the 2025 open-recipe RL releases. Both are admissible, but since P1 shows the question WAS asked, the silence to be explained is only why the systematic version has not been RUN — cost, and an answer that embarrasses whoever commissions it. That is a reason answering is unattractive, not a reason nobody asked, and it is derived from the very absence it explains.

Verification (post-batch, 2026-10-17): two fresh-context readers, one per load-bearing source, neither shown the adversaries' reasoning. Both returned. Both legs of the rejection hold, the misattribution of one of them is corrected here, and the routed problem comes out of this stronger rather than weaker. What changed:
  • The strongest kill is MISATTRIBUTED, though its content checks out. arXiv:2605.01158 is not the Olmo 3 technical report: it is "The Hidden Cost of Thinking: Energy Use and Environmental Impact of LMs Beyond Pretraining" by Jacob Morrison, Noah A. Smith and Emma Strubell, submitted 1 May 2026 — an environmental-accounting study OF the Olmo 3 family rather than its model report. Every claim this entry draws from it is in it: Table 4 gives per-run energy and emissions for pretraining, mid-training, long context, Thinking SFT, DPO, RLVR trainer and RLVR generator, and the Instruct equivalents; Table 5 splits development from final run per stage; and Sec 4.3 reads "Development accounts for 82.2% of total GPU hours (6.85M of 8.34M)" with the development rows summing to 6,849,711 against a family total of 8,335,040. The recommendation this entry attributes to "Olmo 3's authors" is in fact Morrison, Smith and Strubell's: Sec 5.1 asks developers to report post-training costs alongside pretraining broken down by stage, and Sec 5.2 asks for a development cost multiplier at minimum.
  • Three narrowings of that kill, all of which cut toward the candidate. First, the 82.2% denominator is family-wide GPU-hours and EXCLUDES the 4,866,064 MI250X GCD-hours of synthetic-data generation, which the paper reports separately in Table 3 and notes are not comparable with H100 hours — so the five components are not in one commensurable frame, which is precisely what the candidate's declared accounting boundary demands. Second, there is NO explicit ratio of non-gradient-step to gradient-step compute anywhere: the paper publishes per-stage totals a reader must combine, and its nearest ratios are RLVR generator against trainer (about 2.5x in GPU-hours and about 7x in energy for 32B Think) and a development-to-final multiplier of about 4.6x, neither of which is the candidate's estimand, since development itself contains gradient steps of failed runs. Third, and decisively for the routing, the paper contains NO FLOP figures at all: everything is GPU-hours, kWh, tCO2eq, kL of water and tokens. The candidate's ratio under a FLOP denominator is therefore confirmed unpublished, which is what the routed row claims.
  • The Epoch essay is confirmed on all seven attributed claims, with its byline and date exact — "Three challenges facing compute-based AI policies", Venkat Somala, Anson Ho and Séb Krier, 11 Sep 2025. Verbatim: pre-training at "90-99% of total training compute" when the AI Act was drafted; phi-4 synthetic data at "~25% of its pre-training compute budget"; R1-Zero's RL at "only one-fifth of the base model's pretraining compute"; o1-high's figure as "likely less than 10% of the pre-training compute"; DistilBERT at "merely 3% of the compute budget that went into training the original BERT model"; "current policies typically only count the compute from the student run"; and "the compute invested in building reward models remains entirely unaccounted for".
  • Four corrections to what the essay is taken to pose. DISCARDED AND FAILED RUNS ARE NOT DISCUSSED IN IT AT ALL — the reader checked the whole page and found the topic absent — so this entry's framing that Epoch "prices four of its five components" is right only if the fifth is read as the unpriced one, and the essay does not pose the failed-run limb even informally. Verifier inference is likewise not quantified, and RL rollouts appear only as labs that "might generate millions of model responses to prompts". The o1-high figure is reasoning TRAINING compute, not inference. And the tail of claim (f), "ignoring the upstream teacher compute", was not returned verbatim and should be treated as paraphrase. The essay carries no uncertainty on any component ratio, reports no distribution across models — only GPT-4o, o1-high, R1-Zero, phi-4 and DistilBERT/BERT as individual cases — and performs no reordering or threshold test: the strings 10^25 and 10^26 FLOP do not appear in it.
  • Verdict unchanged, and no late Gate 4. The Gate 2 ground was that the accounting question is asked in the field's own words by Epoch and that the per-model component decomposition is already published for a four-model family. Both survive at first hand. What verification establishes is that the published decomposition is in hardware-hours across two non-comparable accelerator types with one component outside the denominator, computes no ratio, and reports no FLOP — so "asked-but-still-open" is the right rejection rather than "answered", exactly as recorded, and the routed row is sharpened to the FLOP-denominated ratio under one declared boundary with its uncertainty, which is confirmed to exist nowhere.

ID: UQ-20261017-48
Date: 2026-10-17
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): AI architecture — evaluation methodology (TARGET field, deciding novelty and holding the acting community: AI evaluation / AI-progress measurement). Method transplanted from (i) survey and psychometric missing-data theory (ignorability, non-ignorable missingness, trend comparability under a changing response mechanism) and (ii) index-number theory (substitution bias, new-goods bias, chain drift under item turnover).

Question (canonical): For one named, dated model x benchmark score panel published as the basis of a capability trend series — the Epoch Capabilities Index, 179 models x 38 benchmarks, 1324 observed scores — with each cell's observation indicator R_ij and each benchmark's first/last-report dates recovered: (0) does a unidimensional latent model fit the panel well enough for "the trend" to be a defined object (pre-step, not assumed); (a) does Pr(R_ij = 1) depend on fitted latent capability theta_i and fitted benchmark difficulty b_j after conditioning on the pre-declared covariate set Z = {model release date, developer, open/closed weights, benchmark age, benchmark licence/access, citation count, evaluation cost}; (b) under a pre-declared family of MNAR departures — a shared-parameter selection model with sensitivity parameter gamma on theta, and a pattern-mixture alternative indexed by the mean shift delta between observed and unobserved cells — what are the SIGNED changes in the fitted theta-vs-date trend's intercept and slope, expressed as a change in the implied doubling time, with Manski-style worst-case bounds; (c) does that change exceed the series' own reported uncertainty? (R1, the one permitted Gate 1 reformulation; V0 as intaken is recorded alongside it in the record.)

Alternative formulations: 1. Do AI progress curves bend because models improved, or because benchmarks were replaced whenever they stopped discriminating? 2. Is the benchmark panel behind published capability indices missing-at-random, and what does non-ignorable missingness do to the AI timelines extrapolated from it?

Motivating gap: A panel whose items enter because they are hard for current models and stop accumulating scores once saturated is missing-not-at-random ON the quantity being measured — the canonical setting of non-ignorable missingness in test linking and of substitution/new-goods bias in price indices. The ECI stitches ~40 benchmarks across ~200 models under a latent model, motivated because "Most benchmarks saturate too quickly to study long-run AI trends"; its stated limitations name benchmark gaming and comparability, not the entry/exit selection mechanism, and quantify no such bias. Confirmed at Gate 4 against the method paper itself (arXiv:2512.00193): none of missing, missingness, MAR, ignorable, unobserved or imputation appears in its visible text, and a code search of its repository returns 0 hits for "at random" / ignorable / MNAR / "selection bias". Incomplete coverage is handled by a filter ("we further filter out models that have only been evaluated on <=3 of the benchmarks"; "20 of the benchmarks do not have enough data to perform the analysis"), with no observation model anywhere.

Presuppositions (status after Gate 4; the two defects that held well-posedness at 2/3 at Gate 3 were both repaired by evidence, and two new ones took their place): P1/P2 per-cell dated panel retrievable — SUPPORTED: epoch.ai/data/eci_benchmarks.csv is long-format, one row per observed cell, headers model_id,benchmark_id,performance,benchmark,benchmark_release_date,model,model_version,Model,date,source; unobserved cells are absent rows, so R_ij is the complement over the cross product, and last-report is the max model date per benchmark (A2 V2; A1 independently found benchmark_release_date merged in the repo's data_loader.py). The selective-reporting covariate must be hand-coded: "No column flags developer self-report versus independent evaluation." P7 series reports an interval — SUPPORTED, more strongly than Gate 3 hoped: eci-public README "CIs are quantiles of the bootstrap draws", outputs carry eci_ci_low/eci_ci_high, and the method paper reports the SLOPE as "0.55 capability units per year" with "a 95% confidence interval of 0.45 to 0.67 units per year" (A2 V1; A1 F3). P3 entry/exit non-random in the latent — SUPPORTED in Epoch's own words: "the newest benchmarks that we've included also tend to have few data points where models perform well," which "may overestimate their difficulty" (A2 V3; A1 F3). P4 unidimensionality — CONTESTED AND NOW EVIDENCED AGAINST: the method paper says a single number "is of course not the case, but we opt for it nevertheless" and titles §4.3 "AI capabilities cannot be fully described by a single number"; R1 pre-declared this as pre-step (0), and per-benchmark R-squared of 0.71 and 0.81 shows the fit is not degenerate, but no formal dimensionality test exists in the visible text (A2 V7). P5 bounds informative at these sizes — CONTESTED and now quantified against: 1324/(179x38) = 19.5% cell density, i.e. ~80% of the grid unobserved (A1's own arithmetic from the paper's counts, no uncertainty attached). P6 slopes are used for decisions — SUPPORTED: Epoch forecasts off the slope, and METR publishes modelling-assumption sensitivity notes on its own time-horizon slope (A1 F2). CORRECTION CARRIED: V0's "benchmarks leave the panel once they saturate" is false of the ECI, which keeps GSM8k, HellaSwag, MMLU and WinoGrande in; what stops is new models being scored on old benchmarks, which R1's cell-level R_ij states correctly. Both adversaries raised and accepted this correction.

What would count as an answer: Reconstruct the dated panel; test dimensionality; then model the missingness mechanism explicitly — a shared-parameter selection model and a pattern-mixture alternative — and report the fitted trend under MAR against the declared MNAR family, with bounds. Deliverable is the signed change in level and slope (or doubling time) and whether it exceeds the published 0.45-0.67 units/year interval. Three pre-declared determinate outcomes: (i) IGNORABLE — departures within plausible bounds move the slope less than its reported interval, and the "moving goalposts" critique is answered quantitatively; (ii) NON-IGNORABLE with the sign stated — the sign is not predictable a priori, since entry-when-hard depresses each new benchmark's early cells, exit-at-saturation truncates the top of old ones, and selective reporting pushes the other way; (iii) BOUNDS UNINFORMATIVE — the series carries an unquantifiable selection component and should report (point estimate, selection interval). Sharpened at Gate 4: the published interval is itself computed under the assumption in question, since the bootstrap "resamples each model's benchmark results with replacement" over observed cells under exchangeability (A2 V4), so limb (c)'s denominator cannot answer limb (b).

Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 29 documented across the three logs — Gate 2: 11 searches (11-query cap reached) + 5 fetches; Adversary 1: 9 searches, 8 of them in vocabularies Gate 2 did not try, + 4 fetches + free repository code search; Adversary 2: 9 searches, all 9 in untried vocabularies, + 4 fetches. Full lists in batches/2026-10-17-2046/UQ-20261017-48-record.md, -adversary-1.md and -adversary-2.md. Most informative:

- "Flynn effect artifact of test renorming item replacement when items become too easy bias secular trend latent ability" (A2 q3) → Wechsler overlapping-items DIF-over-time paper: a signed bias in a secular latent-ability trend from item change, on humans. No AI instance.

No published recomputation of the slope under a missingness model.
Negative sweeps that returned nothing crossing into AI panels: SPEC CPU suite retirement (A2 q1), TREC pool bias and collection obsolescence (A2 q2), Mislevy/ETS ignorable-likelihood missing-response work (A2 q4), German Itemrotation/Trendschätzung literature (A2 q7), finance survivorship/backfill index bias (A2 q8), item parameter drift / measurement invariance (A1 q4).

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources): reweighted by the judge after Gate 4; Gate 2's Prior 3 (arXiv:2602.16763, "When AI Benchmarks Plateau", abs page only) is demoted to the source of presupposition P3 and is no longer among the three nearest.
PRIOR 1 — Jung Min Kang, "Ranking Under Biased Missingness: When Model Rank Is Not Identifiable from Sparse Leaderboards", NeurIPS 2026, neurips.cc/virtual/2026/178314 (OPENED at Gate 2). UNIT: model x item cell, 162 models x 18 items, 781 scores, 26.8% density, robot-learning benchmarks. ENDPOINT: model ordering — resolvable-pair share, rank intervals under masking. COMPARATOR: average-score vs penalized 2PL ranking; masked vs unmasked. ESTIMAND: identifiability of RANK from a sparse matrix. Measures the candidate's premise directly (coverage negatively correlated with fitted item difficulty, r = -0.639) and states it "doesn't identify the reporting mechanism."
PRIOR 2 — BenchLM Research, "The Missing-Benchmark Problem: How Leaderboards Reward Hiding Weak Scores", benchlm.ai/blog/posts/missing-benchmark-problem, 4 Jul 2026 (updated 22 Sep 2026); OPENED by Adversary 1 as F4; industry post, not peer-reviewed. UNIT: a model's reported/unreported benchmark scores on a public leaderboard, 272 models rescored (170 changed, mostly down 3-5 points). ENDPOINT: the model's composite leaderboard score and its ranking. COMPARATOR: observed-cell average vs a gap-penalized rescoring. ESTIMAND: the sign and size of the LEVEL bias — cites Rubin 1976, classifies leaderboard gaps as missing not at random, "unreported scores are, on average, worse than reported ones," averaging observed cells is "biased upward, and biased most for exactly the models whose gaps are most strategic."
PRIOR 3 — Parker Whitfill, "Note on Selection Bias in Observational Estimates of Algorithmic Progress", arXiv:2508.11033, Aug 2025, arxiv.org/html/2508.11033v1 (OPENED at Gate 2). UNIT: a training run (loss, parameters, data, year); no benchmark dimension. ENDPOINT: cross-entropy loss; derived annual rate of algorithmic progress. COMPARATOR: fixed reference year; experimentally estimated scaling exponents. ESTIMAND: the signed bias in an estimated progress rate from endogenous compute/data choice (Theorem 1: bias sign = -sign Cov(ln D, eps_D)); first-pass claim that progress is overstated by roughly a factor of nine, self-described as "very much a first-pass argument."

Novelty — how this differs from each: vs PRIOR 1 — same genus (biased missingness in a sparse model x benchmark matrix under a latent-trait fit) and it measures the premise, but the endpoint is rank not the LEVEL AND SLOPE of a capability-vs-date trend; it has no time dimension at all, hence no entry/exit dates, no cohorts, no doubling time; the estimand is identifiability of an ordering, not a signed bias magnitude tested against a published interval; and MNAR, selection models, pattern-mixture and bounds are all confirmed absent, with the mechanism step explicitly declined — which is limb (a). vs PRIOR 2 — the closest on the mechanism's reporting half and the strongest single discount: it poses ignorability of LLM leaderboard gaps under Rubin's taxonomy and sign-answers it, so the candidate cannot claim the ignorability question is unasked of LLM panels. But its estimand is the LEVEL of a composite score for a model, with no time axis, no fitted trend, no slope or doubling time, no IRT or latent fit, no benchmark entry/exit, and no declared MNAR departure family or bounds; it estimates no progress rate. The candidate's novelty survives on the trend/slope estimand and the entry-when-hard half of the mechanism. vs PRIOR 3 — closest on estimand TYPE, and it already delivers a signed selection-bias correction to a published AI progress rate in this field, so the question-form is not absent from the literature. But selection acts on the MODEL side (labs choose compute after observing latent quality), the outcome is training loss not benchmark score, there is no item panel, no observation indicator and no missingness at all; the framing is endogeneity/omitted-variables with experiments or instruments as the remedy, not sensitivity analysis under a declared departure family; and no corrected doubling time is reported. Item entry-when-hard and cell-level exit-at-saturation are not reachable from its compute-substitution argument.

Novelty confidence: Medium
Grounds: across 29 queries in roughly a dozen vocabularies — including the method-owning fields (educational measurement, survey statistics, index-number economics) and six negative sweeps that produced no AI crossing at all — nothing opened fits a trend to a dated model x benchmark panel, models the missingness mechanism, or reports a signed level/slope bias under a declared MNAR family, and the audited index's own method paper names no missingness assumption. Not High: Prior 1 measures the premise with the same instrument on the same kind of matrix, Prior 2 poses and sign-answers ignorability for the LEVEL of LLM leaderboard scores, Prior 3 already corrects a published AI progress rate for selection, and Appendix E of the audited paper ("Varying benchmark inclusion", "Random selection", "Detecting Benchmark Gaming") could not be read by either adversary. Not Low: no prior on the candidate's object was found in any vocabulary tried, and this is not a disguised known — the analogues found (Wechsler DIF-over-time, Living Planet Index slope bias, German item-rotation trend work, TREC pool bias, SPEC suite retirement) are the transplanted method's home turf on other objects, not the same question renamed, and Prior 2 differs on estimand (level vs slope) rather than on vocabulary.

Significance — consequence: YES with a sign exceeding the interval — every published capability doubling time derived from a stitched panel acquires a known-sign correction, and the ECI/Rosetta-Stone family needs a missingness model alongside its fitting procedure; upward bias means forecasts built on these slopes are too fast, downward the reverse. NO within plausible bounds — the indices gain a quantitative defence they currently lack. BOUNDS UNINFORMATIVE — the honest reporting unit becomes (point estimate, selection interval). All three change what a user of the series may claim. The stake is concrete: a published 0.55 units/year slope with a 95% CI of 0.45-0.67, read off as a doubling time of around 4-5 months. Discounted because Prior 3 already establishes in this field that selection biases progress estimates and roughly by how much for a different mechanism, so the candidate inherits part of the stakes.
Significance — audience: Named and demonstrably responsive, confirmed at Gate 4. (1) Epoch AI: ships a method paper, a public reproduction repo with bootstrap CIs, its own inclusion-robustness appendix, and forecasts off the slope; it already recommends curated benchmark subsets as a mitigation, which this would make rigorous. (2) METR: publishes slope-sensitivity notes and says "the most important source of uncertainty is the task distribution rather than analysis choices" and that saturation is making results "more sensitive to analysis choices." (3) BenchLM, which rescored 272 models over selective reporting. (4) Stanford HAI AI Index and safety-institute/government readers who cite trend slopes. (5) Forecasters extrapolating doubling times. (6) Educational measurement and index-number economics, whose trend-comparability literatures have no AI instance.
Significance — fecundity: Makes askable the right chaining rule for a capability index (chained benchmark cohorts with overlap links versus one pooled fit) and whether chain drift is measurable in it; whether a new-benchmark bias analogous to new-goods bias is estimable from overlap cohorts; whether selective reporting is strategically responsive to the index itself, making this MNAR-with-feedback (a Goodhart problem with a missing-data formalism); what a multidimensional latent does to the idea of "a" doubling time; and whether a prospective design — pre-registering retirement and reporting rules — could make future panels ignorable by construction.
Significance — anchoring: Benchmark saturation (arXiv:2602.16763, 2203.04592); Prior 3's selection critique of algorithmic-progress estimates; the live public dispute over the METR slope; sparse-leaderboard rank identifiability (Prior 1); selective disclosure on arena leaderboards ("The Leaderboard Illusion", unopened); the absence of any sampling frame for "capabilities"; CPI new-goods and substitution bias after the Boskin commission; trend comparability under changing nonresponse in NAEP/PISA/TIMSS; and the Living Planet Index slope-bias literature.

Reason for silence: A disciplinary boundary running through the middle of one toolkit, plus a timing gap — and only in the weak form, which the record conceded rather than hid. Index builders import latent-ability modelling as a MEASUREMENT device while the missing-data half of the same tradition (non-ignorable nonresponse, trend comparability when the response mechanism changes) lives in educational measurement and survey statistics, which have no AI panel to care about; Adversary 2's queries 4 and 7 confirm that literature talking only to itself. Every LLM-IRT and leaderboard-completion paper surfaced treats missing cells as a computational nuisance to impute, and Prior 1 stops at a correlation. A structural reason now also stands: the ECI is not a likelihood you can hang an observation model on — it is "standard least squares regression" with L2 and a coverage filter — so the machinery has no natural socket. Against this, and conceded: the worry HAS been voiced against this exact artefact (Davidmanheim on benchmark turnover; Luke Emberson of Epoch conceding "we tend to prioritize evaluations on frontier models, so coverage for smaller models is spottier"), Epoch's own appendix is titled "Varying benchmark inclusion," and Prior 2 crossed the boundary in July 2026. So the silence is about the MEASUREMENT not being made, over a window of roughly ten months, not about the thought not occurring. Both adversaries graded this Partial, and the judge agrees it is thin.

UNVERIFIED, recorded as such and not as a check that passed in either direction: Appendix E of arXiv:2512.00193 — headings "Varying benchmark inclusion", "Random selection", "Detecting Benchmark Gaming" — bodies absent from the returned HTML for both adversaries; routes not attempted for want of budget, arxiv.org/pdf/2512.00193 and the epoch.ai publication page. Also unopened: arXiv:2504.20879, 2602.15327, 2607.01254; and whether the real ECI fit censors scores near 0/1 as its synthetic script does.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 3/3
Well-posedness stays at 2/3, though for different reasons than at Gate 3: P1 and P7 were repaired by evidence from two independent adversaries, but two newly sourced defects replaced them — limb (0) states no criterion for "fits well enough," and limb (c)'s denominator is now known to be ambiguous between three published intervals (per-model bootstrap CI, the 0.45-0.67 slope CI, Figure 1 sensitivity error bars), with the paper itself giving two doubling times, around 5 months in text and about 4 in its footnote 10. Both are one-line repairs, and the one permitted Gate 1 reformulation is spent. Significance 3/3: consequence is signed and decision-bearing on all three branches, the audience is named and has acted on neighbouring sensitivity analyses, fecundity opens a chaining/new-goods programme and a prospective design fix, and the anchoring reaches two live disputes.

Strongest remaining objection: The question's informative content, not merely its answer, depends on a choice the record never declares — with ~80% of the grid unobserved the Manski-style bounds are likely vacuous, so pre-declared outcome (iii) is close to foregone, and the determinate (i)/(ii) branch rests entirely on a gamma/delta range and calibration rule that R1 does not pin to numbers, leaving an analyst free to produce either verdict from the same panel. Both adversaries reached this independently (attack 5, Partial in both logs), and it is the one wound with no repair stated anywhere in the record.

(1) OUTSTANDING — pre-declare the numeric gamma/delta sensitivity range and its calibration rule (e.g. fitted from the ECI panel's own coverage-versus-fitted-difficulty relation, Kang-style), plus a stated fit criterion for limb (0); this is a design decision for whoever answers, not something a further read can settle. (2) DONE — Appendix E was opened: its only inclusion check on the slope is uniform random dropout, so limb (b) is hereby narrowed to the MNAR-versus-MCAR distinction explicitly, and the candidate's claim is now that the published 0.43-0.64 across-selection interval bounds the MCAR case only. (3) DONE with a correction — limb (c)'s single denominator is the 0.45-0.67 units/year interval of Sec 3.2.1, which is a FRONTIER-ENVELOPE rate over models state-of-the-art at release, not a panel regression on date, and it must not be confused with E.3.1's 0.43-0.64 or E.5's 0.37-0.46. (4) DONE — none of the three neighbours reports a slope change under a missingness or item-set model.

Routing (if rejected as already-asked): Not applicable — not rejected. Verification (post-batch, 2026-10-17): four fresh-context readers, each given one source and the claim made of it, none shown the adversaries' reasoning. All four returned. Three of the four promotion items are discharged, the Unverified cap on attacks 1 and 2 is lifted, and the verdict is unchanged. What changed:
  • Appendix E of arXiv:2512.00193 was OPENED, which the batch could not do. The paper is "A Rosetta Stone for AI Benchmarks" (Ho, Denain, Atanasov, Albanie, Shah; 28 Nov 2025), and Appendix E is titled "Robustness tests": E.1 varying the overlap, E.2 varying the anchors, E.3 varying benchmark inclusion (E.3.1 Random selection, E.3.2 Detecting Benchmark Gaming), E.4 varying the statistical model, E.5 a longer time period. The decisive finding is that E.3.1 is uniform random dropout — "randomly drop some fraction of the benchmarks and compare the model fits in each case", 100 draws, median slope 0.54 against the main 0.55 and an across-selection interval of 0.43–0.64. That is the MCAR case, and it is the only inclusion check on the slope. E.3.2 splits benchmarks by whether a frontier lab ever published a score on them (9 "optimized-for" against 10 not, created 2024 or later), reports a capability gap of about 0.12 units with permutation p-values from 0.1 to 0.37, and reports NO slopes for the two sets. So limb (b) survives and sharpens: the published robustness interval answers the MCAR question and leaves the MNAR one untouched.
  • The same read settles the entry's other Unverified point. A keyword pass over the whole paper found no "Rubin", no "ignorab", no missing-at-random mechanism and no "selection bias"; missingness is handled by filtering out models evaluated on three or fewer benchmarks, and IRT appears only as a contrast ("Unlike Item Response Theory (IRT), which operates on pass/fail data for individual questions"). The model is a latent capability with sigmoid benchmark curves, which treats the missing cells as ignorable without ever saying so. Attacks 1 and 2 are therefore RESOLVED on evidence rather than capped as Unverified, and the entry's reading of the paper was right.
  • Promotion item (3) is discharged with a correction that matters. The 0.45–0.67 units/year interval is real but sits in Sec 3.2.1, NOT in Appendix E, and it is a frontier-envelope rate — fitted over models that were state of the art at release (Fig 5) — not a regression of capability on date across the panel. Three similar-looking intervals exist and must not be conflated: 0.45–0.67 (Sec 3.2.1, main estimate about 0.55/year), 0.43–0.64 (E.3.1, across random benchmark selections) and 0.37–0.46 (E.5, about 0.42/year over a longer window). Limb (c)'s single denominator is the first of those, and the estimand must be re-anchored to a frontier-envelope rate specifically. The paper's own doubling time is internally inconsistent and unreconciled: about 5 months in the main text against about 4 months implied by footnote 10's 7.6x/year.
  • The panel's dimensions are confirmed exactly — "we fit the statistical model on 179 models and 38 benchmarks, with a total of 1324 performance scores" (Sec 2.2), so about 19% of the 6,802-cell grid is observed, and a cell is one model's aggregate score on one benchmark, not item-level data (Sec 4.4). The entry's premise that the index's authors do not claim a real latent is confirmed at first hand: Sec 2.1 states the single-number assumption and concedes it is not literally true, and Sec 4.3 says capabilities "likely depend on a range of different skills".
  • Promotion item (4) is discharged, and all three unopened neighbours fall away. arXiv:2504.20879 is "The Leaderboard Illusion" (Singh et al., 29 Apr 2025) and documents the selective-disclosure mechanism on Chatbot Arena — 27 private Meta variants, Google and OpenAI at about 19.2% and 20.4% of Arena data against about 29.7% for 83 open-weight models combined — but fits no capability trend; its only time series are of battle volume. arXiv:2602.15327 is NOT a leaderboard paper, as the record assumed: it is "Prescriptive Scaling Reveals the Evolution of Language Model Capabilities" (Zhang, Jin, Syrgkanis, Kakade; 17 Feb 2026), a compute-conditioned quantile-regression capability boundary with a size-time model, and its Table 3 gives only g=0 against g=1 endpoints with no calendar span, so no per-year slope is recoverable and selection is a qualitative caveat. arXiv:2607.01254 is "The Benchmark Ceiling" (Esposito, Zhang; 4 Jun 2026), sign-only theory on validity depreciation with no estimation. None reports a signed bias in a fitted trend's level or slope from non-random inclusion or selective reporting.
  • PRIOR 1 needs a venue correction and a read-level one. Kang's "Ranking Under Biased Missingness" is a poster at the NeurIPS 2026 workshop "Can We Trust AI Evaluation? Robustness, Causality, and Risk in Modern AI Assessment", not a main-track NeurIPS paper, and only its ABSTRACT could be read — the OpenReview forum (id JiCv1bYasi) is behind a browser check and no arXiv or PDF mirror exists. Everything the entry takes from it is abstract-level: all four design numbers check out (162 deduplicated models, 18 benchmark items, 781 observed scores, 26.8% density, on LIBERO, CALVIN, Meta-World and LIBERO-Plus), r = -0.639 is between reporting coverage and fitted item difficulty from a penalized 2PL fit, and the sentence is verbatim — though narrower than the entry implies, since what "does not identify the reporting mechanism" is that correlation specifically, not the work as a whole. Its absence of MNAR machinery is therefore Unverified at body level, not established; that cuts against this entry, and the distinction on the endpoint (rank, with a maximum divergence of 77 and a 58-position rank interval) is unaffected.
  • PRIOR 2 needs a weight correction and carries one fact that undercuts it. The BenchLM post exists at the stated URL with both dates, and it is an industry blog on a commercial leaderboard site that sells advertising and sponsorships, carries an affiliate disclosure and runs a paid data tier — not peer-reviewed work, as the entry says, though the entry should not lean on it as the batch's "strongest single discount" without that weight. Its content checks out: the Rubin 1976 framing is there under the heading "Statisticians named this problem in 1976", "unreported scores are, on average, worse than reported ones" is verbatim, and "We rescored all 272 tracked models on July 4, 2026" with "the final recalculation moved the stored scores of 170 of 272 tracked models" and "Most models moved three to five points down". Two corrections: the second attributed quote reads "averaging observed VALUES", not "observed cells"; and a dated update note of 14 July 2026 says the method behind the 272/170 rescoring has been SUPERSEDED by BenchAlign v5, in which missing results "widen uncertainty instead of receiving a fixed conservative fill". The discount this prior applies is therefore to a retired method. Confirmed absent: any time trend, slope or progress rate, any IRT or latent fit, and any bounded MNAR departure family — so the candidate's trend-and-slope estimand is untouched by it.
  • Verdict unchanged at Provisional, and for the reason the judge gave rather than the one the batch recorded: the Unverified cap on attacks 1 and 2 is now lifted by the Appendix E read, so what holds the entry below Validated is well-posedness at 2/3 alone, which Gate 5 requires at 3/3. Promotion item (1) is undischarged and cannot be discharged by reading — it is a design decision for whoever answers the question.

ID: UQ-20261017-49
Date: 2026-10-17
Status: Provisional
Verdict history: Rejected at Gate 5 in the 20:46 batch (Gate 2 novelty Low, disguised known / asked-and-answered, with Disguise Unresolved from both in-batch adversaries). Post-batch verification withdrew that ground, a late Gate 4 ran cold and separately per LEDGER.md Gate 5, and both late judges returned no Unresolved attack on any of the eight. Now Provisional; Significance 1/3 independently bars Validated. Full reasoning in the two blocks at the end of this entry.
Domain(s): AI architecture — pretraining data layer (model-based quality filtering, corpus construction). Secondary: recursive-training / model-collapse theory. Method imported for the estimator limb only: prevalence estimation under misclassification (Rogan–Gladen, screening epidemiology). Source method: new-instrument question.
Question (canonical): For each published model-based pretraining quality filter F (FineWeb-Edu educational-value classifier; DCLM fastText; Nemotron-CC ensemble) applied at its shipped threshold to a pinned, dated Common Crawl snapshot S, what is the enrichment ratio E(F,S) = [prevalence of machine-generated documents in the kept set] / [prevalence in the source pool], with both prevalences corrected for detector sensitivity and specificity estimated on a hand-labelled, provenance-anchored validation subsample drawn separately from the kept and discarded strata, reported with intervals propagating that correction, across a keep-rate ladder obtained by moving F's own threshold at fixed F and stratified by snapshot date — and is E monotone increasing in stringency? (One permitted Gate 1 reformulation used, for well-posedness only: it added stratum-specific validation sampling, a fixed-filter rather than pipeline-stage ladder, and a documents-vs-tokens unit declaration. Intake version recorded verbatim in the record.)
Alternative formulations:
1. Do the quality filters used to build pretraining corpora select for AI-written text?
2. What is the post-filter, rather than pre-filter, synthetic share of a pretraining corpus, and how much does filtering move the mixing fraction the model-collapse literature treats as given?
Motivating gap: Corpus-scale MGT detectors with documented operating points, released runnable quality classifiers and archived CC snapshots are new together; the collapse literature parameterises risk by a synthetic mixing fraction while models train on the filtered subset. The gap closed 17 days before intake: arXiv:2609.40295 (30 Sep 2026) ran Pangram over dated 2026 crawls, measured retention by provenance through FineWeb v1.4.0's and DCLM's full pipelines, and printed both the differential pass rate and the post-filter AI token share.
Presuppositions: P1 detectors have characterised operating points on heterogeneous web text — partly ESTABLISHED (Pangram 3.3.2 FPR 0.05% / FNR 1.99%, plus a dated 0.062%-on-2021-crawls control, upper bound only). P2 an estimable pool base rate under one coding rule — ESTABLISHED in principle; not printed by the prior (back-solvable only, across a token/document unit mismatch). P3 filters runnable at shipped thresholds on an archived snapshot — ESTABLISHED and demonstrated for two of three. P4 document-level "machine-generated" is a meaningful binary — CONTESTED; the prior itself needs a "Mixed" label. P5 the mixing fraction is meant to be the training-set fraction — ESTABLISHED by the literature's definitions. P6 detector error not confounded with the filter's criterion — CONTESTED and still live; the prior's FPR control is pre-ChatGPT text, not fluency-matched kept-set human documents. Adversary 2 added that P6's sign has already flipped once (Bahri et al. 2020: machine-looking text scored LOW quality), making E a property of a detector-filter-era triple.
What would count as an answer: Per shipped filter, a prevalence-corrected E with intervals propagating stratum-specific Se/Sp, across a keep-rate ladder, stratified by snapshot date. Yes if a lower bound exceeds 1 at a shipped keep rate; no if intervals contain or sit below 1; third determinate outcome — if operating characteristics cannot bound E away from 1, the post-filter mixing fraction is not currently measurable and its quantitative use in the recursive-training literature is unlicensed. Gate 2/4 verdict against this list: the "yes" branch is published in ratio form for two of three filters, and follows from two printed pass rates for ANY base rate.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 30 web searches and 13 fetches across three independent agents — Gate 2: 12 searches (cap 11; one-call overrun recorded as an overrun, not licence) + 5 fetches; adversary 1: 9 Disguise searches + 4 fetches; adversary 2: 9 Disguise searches + 4 fetches. Both adversaries met the ≥8 new-vocabulary Disguise requirement, so Disguise is VERIFIED, not unverified. No call was refused. Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
P1 (THE KILL). Russell, Glickenhaus, Thai, Wieting, Iyyer, Spero, Emi, "How Much Is an AI Token Worth? Scaling Laws for Wild AI-Generated Web Text", arXiv:2609.40295v1, 30 Sep 2026 (Pangram Labs + UMD). Opened at abs and full-text HTML by all three agents; quotes verified verbatim twice independently. Unit: documents/tokens from dated crawls (June 2026, Aug 2026, 2021 control). Endpoint: Pangram 3.3.2 provenance label × survival through each shipped pipeline stage; post-filter AI token share. Comparator: human- vs AI-labelled pass rates through the same pipeline. Estimand: differential pass rate by provenance — "AI-generated texts pass FineWeb's pipeline 2.3× (29.3% vs. 12.8%)", "DCLM's full pipeline 9.8× (14.5% vs. 1.5%)" — plus "Pangram labels 27.5% of the tokens that pass FineWeb's quality filters as AI-generated", rising to 31.1% by August. Stated conclusion: "These filters are insufficient at filtering out AI-generated text, and in fact heavily prefer it."
P2. Nait Saada et al., "Removing Noise, not Finding Gold: Quality Filtering for Large-Scale Pretraining" ("The Data-Quality Illusion"), arXiv:2510.00866v1, ICML 2026. Opened full text. Unit: RedPajama-V2 documents + 350M/1.3B models. Endpoint: downstream accuracy and HQ loss. Comparator: full LQ set, alternative HQ sets, CRISP, Perm(k). Estimand: effect of selection fraction and HQ-set choice. No provenance estimand anywhere.
P3. Klimaszewski & Andruszkiewicz, "Is a Document Educational or Just Wikipedia-Style? — Pitfalls of Classifier-Based Quality Filtering", arXiv:2605.23721, 21 May 2026. Abstract level only (confirmed real and quoted by adversary 2). Unit: paired original vs Wikipedia-style-reformatted documents. Endpoint: FineWeb-Edu CQF keep/reject. Comparator: each document against its reformatted self. Estimand: ~7% of filtering decisions reverse under style-only reformatting.
Also found late, by both adversaries: Bahri, Tay, Zheng, Metzler, Brunk, Tomkins, arXiv:2008.13533 (Google, Aug 2020) — a GPT-2 human-vs-machine detector over ~500M Common Crawl pages, "documents with high P(machine-written) score tend to have low language quality". An inverted-sign ancestor of the detector/quality coupling, missed at Gate 2.
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs P1 — it does not differ where it matters. Same unit, same endpoint, same two of three named filters, same dated-snapshot stratification in miniature, canonical limb answered yes with magnitudes. E and the published RR are mutually determined: E = RR/(1 + p(RR−1)), so RR > 1 ⇒ E > 1 for any base rate and with no new data (adversary 2's derivation, labelled as its own). Back-solving p ≈ 0.142 gives E ≈ 1.9 (FineWeb) and ≈ 4.4 (DCLM), order-of-magnitude only because 27.5% is a token share against document pass rates. The distinguishing methodological demand is numerically inert in this regime: Rogan–Gladen at the paper's cited Se 0.9801 / Sp 0.9995 moves 27.5% to 28.0% and nearly cancels in the ratio (both adversaries' arithmetic, agreeing; adversary 2 checked the regime and found the correction large only at prevalences near the 0.05% FPR, which the ladder runs away from). Surviving residue, all narrower than the headline: no interval propagating detector error; no fixed-filter threshold ladder (Figure 2 is a pipeline-STAGE ladder, confounding stage identity with stringency); no kept-stratum provenance-anchored validation; FineWeb-Edu and Nemotron-CC not named; no per-category (translated/edited/written) ratio. vs P2 — non-duplicate on all four attributes; it never measures authorship of kept documents, so it does not rescue novelty. vs P3 — non-duplicate on all four attributes; it is the strongest published hint at P1's mechanism (the fluency-confound limb without a provenance variable). vs 2008.13533 — non-duplicate (no filter applied, no share reported), but it shows the detector/quality coupling was measured at web scale in 2020 with the opposite sign, which weakens rather than restores the candidate's claim to an un-asked question. Method-owning negative, in that field's own words: Rogan–Gladen / differential misclassification in a selected subsample has not been transplanted to corpus provenance — confirmed in three distinct statistical vocabularies. That is a missing estimator on an answered question.
Novelty confidence: Medium (regraded post-batch; Low at Gate 5). The sign of enrichment is published for two whole PIPELINES at document level, but no published figure isolates a named model-based filter at its own operating point, no pre-filter prevalence is printed anywhere alongside a kept-set rate in the same unit, and no keep-rate ladder exists for machine-generated text. See the late Gate 4 block.
Significance — consequence: Heavily discounted. Sign, two magnitudes, a two-month time series and the recommended action ("We recommend filtering AI text when the target is human text") are all in print, with NVIDIA NeMo Curator already shipping a synthetic-text-detection stage. A corrected re-estimate changes magnitude by under a point, not sign. The only consequential branch is P6 biting — and that is an audit of a published estimate.
Significance — audience: Real and already moving (FineWeb/DCLM/Nemotron builders, the detector vendor, recursive-training theorists), but an audience handed the answer and the recommendation will not act differently on an error bar. The method-owning audience has no stake in corpora.
Significance — fecundity: Moderate and inherited from P1, not created here: provenance vs fluency; monotonicity at fixed filter (not derivable from print — it needs a monotone-likelihood-ratio ordering nobody has established); per-category ratios; re-solving collapse results at post-filter fractions.
Significance — anchoring: Model-collapse / mixing-fraction parameterisation; curated self-consuming loops (arXiv:2407.09499); data-exhaustion forecasts counting filter-retained tokens; MGT-detector reliability in the wild; the style-vs-content critique of CQFs (arXiv:2605.23721, arXiv:2510.00866); IR "source bias" (Perplexity Trap, ICLR 2025 — titles only).
Reason for silence: NOT APPLICABLE — the question was not silent. It was asked and answered on 2026-09-30, 17 days before intake, by the party owning the new instrument: the named new-instrument mechanism, exploited by the instrument's owner. Both adversaries graded this Unresolved on the ground that asking why no one asked is a factual error about the state of the field. Two mechanisms survive for the RESIDUE only — a vendor incentive gradient against publishing a correction that can only shrink its own headline, and a disciplinary boundary with no inward traffic from biostatistics (corroborated in three vocabularies) — and neither rescues the candidate.
Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status): Two independent adversaries, each run on the Gate 0–3 record alone; adversary 2 did not see adversary 1's log. Each ran 9 Disguise queries (≥8 met), so no attack is Unverified. Worst status across the two is shown; full logs in the adversary files.

Mechanism also predictable a priori from published self-preference bias (arXiv:2404.13076). | Monotonicity at fixed filter and the two uncovered filters are confirmed absent from the paper, so the FULL conjunction is not answerable from print. | Partial (both)

The candidate's estimand is the published differential pass rate relabelled into screening vocabulary; the paper states the candidate's hypothesis in the candidate's own field's words, verified verbatim at primary source by both adversaries. Feasibility of provenance anchoring remains unevidenced. | Partial (both)
