Scores: Well-posedness 3/3 · Significance 1/3
Strongest remaining objection (REPLACED post-batch; the Gate 5 version is kept below for the record): The one distinguishing limb — sensitivity and specificity estimated on a hand-labelled, provenance-anchored subsample drawn inside the kept stratum — may be unexecutable rather than merely expensive. There is no provenance gold standard for detector POSITIVES in a wild dated snapshot, prevalence, sensitivity and specificity are not jointly identified from positive counts alone, and pinning a specificity near 99.95% would need thousands to tens of thousands of anchored negatives. Meanwhile the correction is close to inert where it would be applied: at the published operating point it moves 27.5% to about 28.0%, and under nondifferential error the uncorrected ratio is already a valid lower bound on the corrected one, so the corrected ratio buys half a point and a bound that is already available. What is left genuinely new is therefore the keep-rate ladder and the monotonicity test on named filters, not the correction the question is built around — and that is a narrower question than the one this entry asks. Both late judges reached this independently.

Strongest remaining objection as written at Gate 5, superseded: The candidate is un-asked only in the form it was rewritten into. Its verbatim intake question and its own alternative formulation 1 are answered word-for-word in arXiv:2609.40295, verified at primary source by two independent adversaries, and E > 1 follows from two printed pass rates with no base rate and no new data; the one distinguishing demand that could have changed an answer — the prevalence correction — is numerically inert in the regime the candidate occupies, so the Gate 1 tightening bought well-posedness, not novelty. (Against the rejection, honestly: Figure 2's per-stage values and Appendix A/E.1 of 2609.40295 were COULD NOT READ by all three agents — routes tried: abs page, html/v1; the per-stage numbers live in a figure image. The body quotes were nonetheless confirmed verbatim twice independently and corroborated by the abstract and by secondary coverage, which defeats the record's own mis-transcription worry. The residue — kept-stratum differential-misclassification audit, fixed-filter ladder, FineWeb-Edu and Nemotron-CC — is real but is a replication-and-extension agenda on an answered question.)
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): Not the enrichment measurement, which is published in ratio form. Draw a hand-labelled, provenance-anchored validation sample separately from the kept and discarded strata of one shipped filter on one pinned snapshot and test whether the detector's FPR inside the kept stratum exceeds its FPR on the discarded stratum. That is the one check that could convert the published 2.3×/9.8× into an artefact of shared fluency sensitivity — and it belongs to a new candidate's Gate 0, inheriting no status from this entry.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): NOT ROUTED, and the reason has changed. At Gate 5 this was withheld as an answered disguised known. It is now withheld under the standing rule that a PROVISIONAL entry's own question is never routed, because the ledger is still claiming it as un-asked; a row drafted while an entry is Rejected must be withdrawn if verification makes it Provisional, which is what happened here. One residual is recorded rather than routed: Section 7.2.2 of arXiv:2510.25771 (Gaperon), "Impact of Quality Filters on Contamination", could not be opened in the arXiv version by any route tried — /pdf/ and /html/ both truncate before Section 7 and the v3 PDF returned HTTP 429. Its ACL Findings 2026 twin (section 4.1.2) was read and measures benchmark-leakage amplification rather than retention by provenance, so the section is very unlikely to bear on this question, but the arXiv body itself is UNREAD and should be resolved before any later pass treats this area as swept.

Verification (post-batch, 2026-10-17): the whole rejection rested on one paper, so it got two independent readers — one searching by identifier, one by subject only — plus one reader on the inverted-sign ancestor and three more on residuals the late pass flagged. All six returned. The paper is real and is the on-point paper, and almost everything this entry claimed OF it needed narrowing:
  • arXiv:2609.40295 exists and both readers independently identified it as "How Much Is an AI Token Worth? Scaling Laws for Wild AI-Generated Web Text" (Russell, Glickenhaus, Thai, Wieting, Iyyer, Spero, Emi; 30 Sep 2026). It is a SCALING-LAW paper fitted over 800 pretrained models; the filter-survival audit is a motivating section, not its subject.
  • The survival figures are confirmed exactly and their unit is DOCUMENTS, over a 10,000-document raw Common Crawl sample: through the FineWeb pipeline, AI-labelled documents survive at 29.3% against 12.8% for human-labelled (2.3x); through DCLM's full pipeline, 14.5% against 1.5% (9.8x, from unrounded values — 14.5/1.5 is 9.67). The audit section names no labeller.
  • The 27.5% to 31.1% pair is NOT a before-versus-after-filter contrast, which is how this entry used it. Both readers found it to be a June-2026-to-August-2026 TIME TREND among tokens that have already passed FineWeb quality filtering, with no pre-filter token share reported anywhere in the paper. The same series gives 16.1% for June 2025, 10.1% for June 2024 and 0.1% or less for June 2021, and the Figure 1 caption covers documents Pangram labels "AI or Mixed" with an AI-alone figure of 28% for June 2026. Since the survival rates are in documents and the shares are in tokens, the two cannot be combined into an enrichment ratio at all.
  • The paper names NONE of the three filters in this entry's canonical question. It runs a FineWeb v1.4.0 pipeline replication and reports survival through DCLM's full pipeline; FineWeb-Edu, DCLM fastText and Nemotron-CC do not appear. So "already measured for two of the three filters" was wrong: what is measured is two whole pipelines.
  • No keep-rate ladder and no threshold sweep of any kind, found by both readers independently — so the monotonicity limb is untested in print. No prevalence correction either, and none of the terms Rogan-Gladen, sensitivity, specificity or prevalence correction occurs in the paper.
  • The detector figures are confirmed but are vendor-linked: Pangram 3.3.2 at FPR 0.05% and FNR 1.99%, attributed to Glickenhaus et al. 2026 — Glickenhaus is a co-author of this paper — plus a 0.062% label rate on 60,000 pre-2022 documents offered as an FPR upper bound.
  • Bahri et al. (arXiv:2008.13533) is confirmed as recorded, with its quoted sentence verbatim in Sec 3.3 and the sign as stated, over a 500M-document Common Crawl sample. One correction: the detector is not a single GPT-2 model but the OpenAI RoBERTa-large GPT-2 detector plus GLTR on GPT-2 XL. It runs no quality filter and reports no pass rate by provenance, so it remains an inverted-sign ancestor only.
  • Three residuals the late pass flagged were then chased. (1) The Pew Research Center Data Labs methodology note of 20 Aug 2026 is real and is the first published SOURCE-POOL measurement: 10,000 English Common Crawl pages from each of 49 crawls, January 2021 to July 2026, 490,000 pages, scored with Pangram's open editlens_Llama-3.2-3B at 0.2. Its headline 35% applies only to July 2026 pages carrying a detectable post-2022-11-30 date, which Pew says is "not a random subset of the web" and is only 10-15% of pages; the companion article gives about 10% across ALL sampled July 2026 pages. It applies no correction, and its 96% agreement with commercial Pangram 3.3 over 62,370 pages at kappa 0.61 is detector-versus-detector agreement, not accuracy against ground truth — the 0.2 threshold was itself calibrated to match that detector. It says nothing about quality filters. So this entry's P2 is now published-but-uncorrected, in a different sample and unit from the kept-set rates. (2) Gaperon's Section 7.2.2 remains UNREAD in the arXiv version; its ACL twin measures benchmark-leakage amplification, not retention by provenance (see Routing). (3) Gao 2021 is confirmed in detail and is the nearest published ladder; see the late Gate 4 block.

Late Gate 4 (ran late and separately, 2026-10-17, per LEDGER.md Gate 5): the Gate 2 ground above was withdrawn, so Gate 4 was re-run from scratch against the Gate 0-3 record. Form, disclosed: the eight attacks were put as eight neutral literature questions, one per agent, each answered by a fresh-context reader that had not seen the record — the enumerated eight-attack adversary brief does not launch in this environment — and then judged by TWO cold judges, each given the record, the established facts and all eight answers, neither shown the other's reasoning and both told the Low grade was void. All ten agents returned. Worst status across the two judges, per attack:
  1 Triviality — Partial. No prevalence-corrected kept-versus-pool ratio exists for any web-text quality filter in anything opened. But the method is not new to this application: arXiv:2601.17036 already applies a Rogan-Gladen adjustment (p-hat - FPR)/(1 - FPR) to AI-text prevalence in a text corpus, with FPRs measured on pre-LLM 2020-22 CS papers and corrected figures of 21.40% against 13.97%. And the correction sub-limb is near-pre-bounded: under nondifferential error the uncorrected ratio is a valid lower bound on the corrected one.
  2 Disguise — Partial, where the in-batch adversaries had Unresolved. It bites on the sign, which is in print with a rough ceiling, and no second study was found, so the candidate adds no replication value. It is not an answer to the question as posed: no pre-filter prevalence, a unit mismatch between the two published quantities, no ladder, and — the sharpest point either judge made — neither published figure isolates a named model-based filter at its own operating point, since the FineWeb v1.4.0 arm contains no model-based quality classifier at all and the DCLM figure confounds heuristics, deduplication and the fastText stage.
  3 Combinatorial novelty — Partial (one judge said Resolved). The ladder design is published: Gao 2021 (arXiv:2109.00698) varies its filter's own aggressiveness — tau sampled from Pareto(alpha), keep if tau > 1 - score, alpha over the integers 1 to 8 — and reports Table 1 discard fractions of 0.4107, 0.6351, 0.7610, 0.8329, 0.8761, 0.9026, 0.9198 and 0.9315, with kept-set composition along the ladder in Figures 3 and 4 as BookCorpus2-like and PubMed-Abstracts-like fractions. Those values exist only inside figure images and no table lists them; alpha 6 and 7 appear in Table 1 but Section 3 trains sets only for alpha in {1,2,3,4,5,8}; and the paper measures no machine-generated text. So the form is not novel and the instantiation is unoccupied. Against the attack: the one existing measurement returns 2.3x and 9.8x rather than a null, and a published mechanism predicts it — style-only rewrites flip about 7% of FineWeb-Edu keep decisions and NemoCurator Mixtral admits over 7% of rephrased documents that scored two or worse raw (arXiv:2605.23721), so these filters key on surface fluency.
  4 Presupposition failure — Partial. P3 is FALSE as written for one of the three filters: Nemotron-CC has no single shipped threshold, being a MAX over three classifiers' integer scores mapped into twenty roughly 5% buckets and regrouped post hoc into five labels from downstream performance, with FineWeb-Edu excluded from the ensemble for licence reasons. FineWeb-Edu holds (int_score >= 3, Apache-2.0 weights, runnable) and DCLM's shipped operating point is a top-10% percentile rule, which is a threshold in the candidate's own keep-rate parameterisation. P1 is weaker than recorded: no independent in-the-wild false-positive characterisation of any detector was found, only vendor-linked figures and a 200-text curated-benchmark check.
  5 Vagueness — Partial. No coding rule for mixed or AI-edited documents and no detector cutoff are stated, and no study measures how a prevalence estimate moves with that assignment. Ahrefs' own categories imply 2.5% against 74.2% depending on where mixed goes, about 72 points, and because filters may preferentially retain lightly edited HUMAN text the mixed stratum could move not only the magnitude but the direction of monotonicity. A one-line stipulation repairs it.
  6 Significance inflation — Partial. "The collapse literature parameterises risk by a mixing fraction" overstates what is there: Shumailov (2305.17493) and 2402.07712 are indexed by GENERATION COUNT and Gerstgrasser (2404.01413) by replace-versus-accumulate, while only Dohmatob, Feng and Kempe (2410.04840) makes a training-set share an explicit parameter, with Bertrand (2310.00429) at abstract level. Every fraction in the sources read is set by construction, never measured from a filtered corpus.
  7 Reason for silence — Partial. The vendor co-authorship is supported, but the incentive claim is unevidenced — the vendor did publish FPR, FNR and a negative control — and the "no inward traffic from biostatistics" mechanism is REFUTED by arXiv:2601.17036, which crosses that boundary in this exact application. The simplest surviving explanation is recency: the nearest paper is 17 days old.
  8 Dissolution — Partial. The question does not dissolve, but three of its five parts do land: the correction is near-settled as method with the uncorrected ratio a lower bound; the kept-stratum Se and Sp may be unmeasurable, since prevalence, sensitivity and specificity are not jointly identified from positive counts alone and no provenance oracle exists for positives in a wild 2026 snapshot; and the corrected-ratio limb inherits that. The ladder and monotonicity limbs are measurable and are neither settled nor unmeasurable.
  Verdict: NO attack is Unresolved from either judge, so the fatal rule on attacks 1, 2 and 4 is not triggered and the rejection does not survive. Both judges returned Provisional independently. Significance 1/3 bars Validated on its own, and Gate 5 requires at least 2/3.

Promotion requires: all five of — (1) raise significance above 1/3 by restating the consequence against what the collapse literature actually parameterises, which on the late reading is arXiv:2410.04840 alone among the papers opened, or by dropping to the corpus-builder consequence (does a stricter keep rate worsen the mix?) and arguing that one instead; (2) declare the coding rule for mixed and AI-edited documents and the detector cutoff, since the assignment is worth about 72 points on published categories and could reverse the monotonicity direction; (3) narrow the object to a NAMED model-based filter at its own operating point, because neither published survival figure isolates one — the FineWeb v1.4.0 arm carries no model-based classifier and the DCLM figure confounds three pipeline stages — and drop Nemotron-CC from the filter list or restate its operating point as a bucket rule, since it has no shipped threshold; (4) either show that differential misclassification inside the kept stratum is estimable against some obtainable gold standard for POSITIVES in a wild dated snapshot, or re-scope the question to the uncorrected ratio as a lower bound plus the ladder, conceding that the correction moves the published figure about half a point; (5) resolve the unread arXiv Section 7.2.2 of 2510.25771. Items (3) and (4) are the load-bearing ones: with them done the entry is a ladder-and-monotonicity question on one named filter, which is narrower than what it currently asks and is what both late judges identified as the genuinely unoccupied part.

ID: UQ-20261017-50
Date: 2026-10-17
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): AI architecture — training systems and optimization (pretraining recipe engineering; secondary: scaling-law and ablation methodology)

Question (canonical): Restricted to runs declaring clipping of a GLOBAL gradient norm at nominal threshold c (c = 1.0 the index case), with a step CLIPPED when the stack's clip coefficient is < 1: (a) what is the clipped-step fraction as a function of training progress, per run, from released pre-clip gradient-norm series or instrumented reproductions; and (b) under a band pre-declared from seed replicates, are BOTH the clipped-step fraction AND the realized-update deviation (relative L2 and cosine of the applied update from the update that clipping-disabled would have applied, at matched checkpoints) invariant to (i) model scale along a ladder at fixed c and (ii) the parameter grouping over which the stack reduces the norm — and if not, what c'(scale, grouping) reproduces a reference run's two endpoints? (V2; the one permitted Gate 1 reformulation of V1, for well-posedness only — V1 left "actually active" and "same intervention" undefined and let limb (b) rest on gradient-norm scaling.)

Alternative formulations:
- When a recipe says "gradient clipping 1.0", how often does it clip, and does it mean the same thing at 1B and at 70B?
- Is the clipping threshold a hyperparameter that ladders and ablations hold fixed in name while varying in effect?

Motivating gap: Dense-how, empty-why. The clip appears in nearly every published LLM recipe, almost always at 1.0, and the literature is thick with methods for clipping better (ZClip arXiv:2504.02507, AdaGC arXiv:2502.11034, SPAMP arXiv:2510.01578, spectral clipping arXiv:2605.11838), while nothing found characterises what the shipped constant does in the runs using it. AdaGC motivates adaptive clipping by two named mismatches of a single global threshold (temporal: "The optimal global clipping threshold typically decreases over the course of training"; spatial: across tensors) and compares granularities, yet reports no activation rate, no argument about tightness versus parameter count, and does not treat one nominal threshold under different groupings as a comparability problem.

Presuppositions: P1 activation rate archive-recoverable — LARGELY ESTABLISHED from code read at first hand (OLMo optim.py computes total_grad_norm, clip_coef, and logs clipping_rate; verified by adversary 1 against allenai/OLMo canonical repo), residual: gated on collect_param_metrics, and under global fixed clipping clipping_rate degenerates to a 0/1 per-step indicator. P2 recipes expose the grouping — partly contested (stack VERSION decides). P3 gradient norm scales with size — CONTESTED and deliberately removed by V2's move to the realized update; both adversaries endorse that treatment. P4 ladders hold c fixed — DENTED by adversary 2: Marin 32B retrospective, "Max grad norm: initially 1.0, then 0.2 from 56.4K steps", so at least one headline open run retunes mid-flight. P5 varying constraint is a defect for a ladder's purpose. P6 norm- not element-clipping — removed by V2's frame restriction.

What would count as an answer: Per-run clipped-step fraction versus training progress for >= 2 stacks at >= 3 scales under one nominal c; realized-update deviation (relative L2, cosine) against the clipping-disabled counterfactual at matched checkpoints; and an equivalence mapping c'(scale, grouping). "Same intervention" if both endpoints sit inside the pre-declared replicate band — a null that licenses copying the constant across a ladder. Otherwise the mapping is the deliverable. Near-zero activation in some regime answers limb (a) and makes the constant vestigial there. Grouping arm must be run WITHIN one stack (adversary 2's specification note), else grouping is confounded with reduction precision, kernel order and DP sharding.

Novelty — queries run (query -> one-line result): Gate 2: 11 web searches (at cap) + 7 fetches (cap 5; two-fetch overrun self-reported, all three over-cap calls spent failing to reach ZClip's appendix). Most informative: Q1 "how often does gradient clipping actually trigger during LLM pretraining fraction of steps clipped" -> method papers only, no descriptive study of the shipped constant; Q6 "global vs per-layer/per-tensor granularity same threshold different intervention Megatron-LM DeepSpeed comparability" -> granularity studied as a design choice, no cross-stack comparability study; Q9 "does the optimal clipping threshold change with model size ... 1B 7B 70B" -> no measured threshold ladder; Q10 (robust statistics, winsorization) -> informative disanalogy: there the affected FRACTION is set and reported, here the THRESHOLD is set and the fraction left unmeasured; Q11 -> RL post-training routinely logs and publishes a clip fraction for the policy-RATIO clip, never for the gradient-norm clip. COULD NOT READ at Gate 2: ZClip appendix 6.6.1 "Clipping Percentage Analysis" (HTML offsets 0/38000/62000 all missed it) — the single decisive check. Gate 4 added 18 new-vocabulary searches (9 per adversary, none overlapping Gate 2) plus 7 free GitHub code/issue searches and 8 fetches; the decisive check was RESOLVED there via the PDF route (arxiv.org/pdf/2504.02507), which Gate 2 never tried. Full lists: batches/2026-10-17-2046/UQ-20261017-50-record.md, -adversary-1.md, -adversary-2.md. Still unopened by record and both adversaries: arXiv:2212.01539 (DP group-wise clipping), arXiv:2006.15429 (geometric perspective on clipping bias), arXiv:2206.07136 (Automatic Clipping), u-muP appendices A.7-A.9.

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
A. ZClip, arXiv:2504.02507 — OPENED in full by both adversaries, appendix 6.6.1 included. Unit: global gradient L2 norm per step. Endpoint: loss spikes, tokens to baseline loss; 6.6.1 adds proportion-clipped versus training progress. Comparator: no clipping, fixed c = 1.0, AutoClip. Estimand: spike mitigation without manual tuning. Verbatim: "Figure 11 illustrates how the proportion of clipped gradients evolves as training progresses for various z-score thresholds"; thresholds tested are ZClip's own z-score bounds 1.5-4.0, and for fixed c = 1.0 the paper gives NO numeric percentage, only a qualitative remark on "continuous clipping" at lr 5e-3. One scale (1B LLaMA), one stack. Asserts the candidate's limb-(b) conclusion without measuring it: "The optimal threshold c furthermore depends on the particular model and the many hyperparameters in the training recipe."
B. fairseq's logged clip metric (facebookresearch/fairseq issues #250, #416, #503, #1263, #2201; https://github.com/facebookresearch/fairseq/issues/1263) — NOT a paper but a first-hand published-log prior found by adversary 1. Unit: logging interval within a run. Endpoint: percentage of updates whose gradient norm exceeded the threshold, printed on every log line since 2018. Comparator: none. Estimand: none — a diagnostic readout. Published values range 0% (#416, #503) through 2% (#1263) to 100% (#250). In #2201 the user misreads the logged fraction as the nominal threshold. GitHub code search does not index fairseq here, so the symbol could not be quoted from source; the metric is evidenced from the published log lines.
C. AdaGC, arXiv:2502.11034 — read at first hand at intake, not re-opened at Gate 4. Unit: parameter tensor per step. Endpoint: spike counts/scores, final loss. Comparator: GlobalGC at fixed threshold plus granularity variants (Table 2: Global/Element/Unit/Tensor). Estimand: spike incidence and loss difference vs GlobalGC. Supplies the grouping mechanism: "AdaGC only needs an all-reduce within each TP group" whereas GlobalGC "needs all-reduce across DP, TP, and PP groups".
(Also opened at Gate 4 and treated as structural analogues, not priors: Andrew et al., arXiv:1905.03871, DP adaptive clipping to "a value at a specified quantile of the update norm distribution" — the fraction-instead-of-threshold inversion as existing DP method, unit the per-client update under a privacy constraint; Marin 32B retrospective, which publishes an optimizer table, a mid-run threshold change and a spike narrative and explicitly reports no clipped-step fraction; Pascanu et al., arXiv:1211.5063, "for a given task and model size, training is not very sensitive to this hyperparameter".)

Novelty — how this differs from each:
vs A: A's unit is the step within one run and its comparator a rival METHOD; the candidate's unit is the (run, stack, scale) cell and its comparator the SAME nominal c at another scale or grouping — an equivalence estimand absent from A. A's 6.6.1 curve is for its own z-thresholds, not for c = 1.0, and A measures no update deviation against the unclipped counterfactual. The record's stated demotion condition did NOT trigger.
vs B: B emits the number; it does not ask the question. The fraction is per-interval, per-run, never aggregated, never compared across scale or grouping, and attached to no estimand — and it is demonstrably misread by its own users. But B does falsify the record's "computed everywhere, published nowhere" framing of limb (a) for a major stack, which is what caps this entry.
vs C: C treats grouping as a design choice to optimise for stability and communication cost, not as a comparability problem for one nominal number; reports spike counts, not activation rates; makes no claim about tightness versus parameter count.

Novelty confidence: Medium. Distinct from every prior actually opened — no source anywhere reaches the composite estimand (cross-scale and cross-grouping invariance of clipped-step fraction AND realized-update deviation, with c'(scale, grouping) as deliverable). Not High: limb (a) has two close neighbours now read at first hand (ZClip Fig. 11's clipped-proportion trajectory for an adjacent threshold rule; fairseq's clip=N% published since 2018), the quantile/percentile-clipping family already inverts threshold-to-fraction in-field (AutoClip, TF-Privacy QuantileAdaptiveClipSumQuery), and the DP clipping-bias line that studies exactly this entry's two endpoints (grouping: arXiv:2212.01539; realized-update bias: arXiv:2006.15429) is unopened by the record and by both adversaries. Not Low: no near-duplicate was read; per ledger doctrine an unread paper grounds no grade in either direction. Disguise was EXECUTED, not unverified — 9 new-vocabulary searches per adversary, 18 in all, against a required 8.

Significance — consequence: If the fraction is substantial and moves with scale or grouping at fixed c, every ladder and ablation copying "clip = 1.0" across rungs has varied an active constraint along the axis it extrapolates over, and recipes would report realized clipping while ladders equalised it rather than the nominal number. If the clip is near-inactive in some regime the constant is vestigial there, and stability gains attributed to it are misattributed — which bears on what the spike-mitigation family improves upon. If both endpoints sit in the replicate band, that is a useful null licensing current practice. All three change a reporting convention; two change a design practice. Discount (adversary 2): Marin's published verdict that "Gradient clipping and step-skipping heuristics softened the spikes but never removed them" partly pre-empts the misattribution limb.
Significance — audience: (1) Recipe engineers running multi-rung ladders — one extra logged scalar, and equalisation of realized clipping if limb (b) is non-null. (2) Scaling-law and ablation methodology (cf. UQ-20261016-53, UQ-20261017-28). (3) Adaptive-clipping authors — verified at first hand by adversary 2: ZClip plots the clipped proportion for its own threshold and prints nothing for the c = 1.0 baseline it is measured against, so their effect sizes sit on an uncharacterised control. (4) Maintainers of open runs (OLMo, Marin, LLM360, Apertus) — near-zero publication cost. (5) Stack maintainers (Megatron-LM, torchtitan, DeepSpeed, Levanter), for whom the mapping is what makes a recipe portable between groupings. Counter-evidence on the audience: fairseq printed this number for years and nobody wrote it up; Marin's team retuned off eyeballed norms rather than computing a rate.
Significance — fecundity: Whether clip activation explains part of the loss-spike literature's unexplained variance; whether the clip does work attributed to warmup, z-loss or QK-norm; whether "clip = c" belongs inside muP-style hyperparameter transfer, which prescribes no rule for it; whether the right reporting unit for any saturating training-time operator is its realized activation rate rather than its nominal bound (generalising to loss scaling, router capacity factors, RL ratio clipping); whether recipe portability should be certified by matched realized constraints rather than matched config files.
Significance — anchoring: Loss-spike and instability literature; the adaptive-clipping family, motivated by mismatches it never measures for the shipped constant; hyperparameter transfer and its silence on clipping; this ledger's "fixed in name, not in effect" family (UQ-20261016-53, UQ-20261017-28), differing in object; the DP clipping-bias literature, both anchor and principal novelty risk; econometric top-coding, where a fixed nominal threshold's binding share IS reported and nominal-threshold comparability is explicitly a problem (adversary 2's closest structural analogue, different object).

Reason for silence: An incentive gap crossed with an instrumentation-ownership boundary, now instantiated by opened sources rather than asserted. The quantity is a dashboard readout, not a result: fairseq has printed it since 2018 and OLMo computes it, and the fairseq issue threads show it being read, misread and never aggregated. ZClip's authors DID ask it — of their own threshold, in an appendix, with a figure — and not of the fixed baseline they beat. Marin's team, maximally transparent with every log in hand, discussed the threshold, changed it mid-run, reasoned about norms, and still never wrote down an activation rate. Secondary mechanism (adversary 1): settled by fiat, Pascanu et al. 2013 declaring training "not very sensitive to this hyperparameter", which plausibly closed the question before the ladder era. Limb (b) additionally needs two codebases' reduction groupings and a matched ladder — nobody's paper, sitting between the community owning the operator and the community owning the grouping, with no venue rewarding a null.

Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status): Two independent adversaries, fresh context, Gate 0-3 record only; adversary 2 did not see adversary 1's log. Both ran their full Disguise sweeps (9 web searches each in vocabularies Gate 2 did not try, plus GitHub code/issue search and 8 fetches between them). Statuses below are the worse of the two.
1 | Triviality | Limb (a) is a dashboard number already printed: fairseq clip=N% since 2018, OLMo clipping_rate, ZClip Fig. 11; Marin's "grad norms ... about 0.2" against c = 1.0 reads off the qualitative answer for one run; Pascanu already set the threshold from norm statistics and found low sensitivity | Published fairseq values span 0%-100% across runs, so the answer is run-dependent, not a one-page fact; "norms about 0.2" characterises the bulk while the clip fires in the tail, so no fraction and no trajectory follow; no source gathers it for LLM ladders at c = 1.0 across stacks, and none touches the realized-update deviation, cross-scale or cross-grouping invariance. A page gets folklore, not the three deliverables | Partial (A1 Partial, A2 Resolved)

Trust-region/active-set, audio limiting, CFD flux limiters, Chinese-language, log diagnostics, clinical delivered dose, open-run reports: analogues only, differing in object, unit and estimand. But the DP clipping-bias line (2212.01539, 2006.15429, 2206.07136) stays unopened by the record and by both adversaries | Partial (both) — evidenced but incomplete
3 | Combinatorial novelty | Optimization x training systems; the interface is just "log one scalar in each stack" | c'(scale, grouping) is definable only at the interface: the grouping is a stack-implementation property (AdaGC's DP/TP/PP all-reduce asymmetry; Megatron-LM issue #580 shows norm reduction under a parallelism choice is a live concern), ZClip 6.6.1 shows the quantity is cheap and threshold-sensitive, and Marin shows practitioners improvising retunes with no comparability framework | Partial (A1 Partial, resting on the record's quotes plus a title; A2 Resolved)

P4 is partly contradicted by an opened source (Marin, 1.0 then 0.2 from 56.4K steps), which narrows the framing without falsifying the question. No presupposition found false. Checkpoint matching is a protocol choice, not an ambiguity in the estimand | Resolved (both; with the within-stack specification note) 
6 | Significance inflation | fairseq printed this number in every log for years and nobody wrote it up; #2201's user could not identify what clip meant; Marin coped by eyeballing norms and retuning, shrinking the marginal value of a formal convention | Audience (3) is now sourced, not asserted: ZClip plots the proportion for its own threshold and prints nothing for its c = 1.0 baseline. Marin published an optimizer table, a spike narrative and a mid-run threshold change and would plainly have used this. 7 | Reason for silence | Explains why answering is costly, not why nobody asked | Both mechanisms instantiated by opened sources: ZClip asked it of its own threshold and not of the baseline (method-author incentive); Marin, with every log in hand, never wrote the rate down (dashboard-not-result); plus Pascanu's 2013 low-sensitivity declaration as a settled-by-fiat closure. These explain non-asking, not difficulty | Resolved (both)

Even the dissolved residue is measurable: at which scales and groupings a given c sits in the intermittent band, and how wide that band is — the two-endpoint design detects the dissolution instead of assuming it away | Partial (A1 Partial on its own unsourced Adam reasoning; A2 Resolved). Verification sourced that reasoning: arXiv:2206.07136 Theorems 1–2 prove a constant rescaling R is equivalent to R = 1 and cancels outright for adaptive optimizers, so the objection is published, not folklore; it stays Partial because a stability clip fires intermittently rather than constantly, which is the distinction the two-endpoint design measures.
No Unresolved status from either adversary on any attack, so no fatal objection. Gate 2's single decisive unresolved check (ZClip 6.6.1) was closed at Gate 4 by the PDF route and did not trigger the record's demotion condition.

Scores: Well-posedness 3/3 · Significance 2/3

Strongest remaining objection: fairseq has printed the clipped-update percentage (clip=N%) on every training log line since December 2017, with real published values of 94%, 2% and 0% across runs, so the entry's "computed everywhere, published nowhere" framing of limb (a) is false for a major stack and limb (a) is largely a renamed dashboard metric whose folklore answer is cheaply available. (Two parts of this objection as first written did not survive verification: the conceded 0%-to-100% span is not real, because the 100% came from a run with clipping disabled; and OLMo's clipping_rate counts parameter tensors per rank, not steps. The fairseq concession stands and is older than stated.) What survives unfound is limb (b): the cross-scale and cross-grouping equivalence of the realized update. The three DP papers that study its two endpoints have now been opened and none reaches it — but arXiv:2206.07136's Theorems 1 and 2 do publish the constant-rescaling invariance the entry had treated as folklore, which is why novelty stays Medium.
Promotion requires: this clause was rewritten after verification, because the version written at Gate 5 promised Validated on terms Gate 5 does not offer; that superseded version is quoted in the batch file. All three of its items are now discharged — the three DP papers are opened and none reaches the composite estimand, limb (a) is conceded to fairseq's clip=N% and ZClip Fig. 11 as corrected below, and the Adam-invariance argument is sourced to arXiv:2206.07136 Theorems 1–2 and Fact B.1 — and the entry is still Provisional, because Gate 5 makes "Medium novelty with a close neighbor" the Provisional case outright and those neighbours are confirmed, not removed. What would now promote it is therefore a novelty grade of High, which requires showing that fairseq's per-window clipped-update percentage and ZClip's z-score trajectory are not neighbours of the candidate's estimand but of a different one: concretely, (1) that no published run anywhere reports an aggregated clipped-step fraction for a fixed stability threshold at two or more scales in one stack, searched in the vocabulary of the stacks rather than the papers (release notes, run logs, W&B dashboards, OLMo and Marin retrospectives); (2) that the realized-update deviation against the clipping-disabled counterfactual appears in no non-private training paper, searched separately from the DP line now cleared; and (3) that c'(scale, grouping) is not derivable from arXiv:2206.07136's Theorems 1–2 once clipping is intermittent rather than constant — if it IS derivable, the mapping limb is a corollary and the entry drops to Rejected on attack 1.

Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): pointer only — the cheapest entry is the archive side, not a new run: establish for one or two fully open runs whether the released per-step gradient-norm series is pre-clip and whether the metric block was enabled, before any ladder is contemplated.

Routing (if rejected as already-asked): n/a — not rejected.

Verification (post-batch, 2026-10-17): six fresh-context readers, each given one source and the claim made of it, none shown the adversaries' reasoning. All six returned. Every one of the three papers the promotion clause named was opened at PDF level, and none reaches the composite estimand — but the clause's own promise of Validated was wrong on Gate 5, and the entry stays Provisional. What changed:
  • arXiv:2212.01539 (He et al., "Exploring the Limits of Differentially Private Deep Learning with Group-wise Clipping", 3 Dec 2022) does compare clipping over parameter groupings — flat, fixed per-layer with C_k = C/sqrt(K), adaptive per-layer, per-device for GPT-3 — but entirely inside DP fine-tuning. Its "fraction of clipped gradients" (Sec 3.3) is a privately estimated per-EXAMPLE quantile used to adapt thresholds, with target q set to 0.5, 0.75 or 0.85, not a share of optimizer steps. Clipping bias appears only as one qualitative sentence in Sec 3.2; there is no measurement against an unclipped counterfactual, and no mapping of a threshold across model scales. NOT the composite estimand.
  • arXiv:2006.15429 (Chen, Wu, Hong, "Understanding Gradient Clipping in Private SGD: A Geometric Perspective", 27 Jun 2020, NeurIPS 2020 per search listings only) characterises clipping bias in theory (Theorem 2, Corollary 1, Theorem 5) with small-scale MNIST/CIFAR-10 support, at one global c = 1. It reports NO clip-binding fraction — the reader checked twice, including appendices — and no numerical clipped-versus-unclipped comparison on real data; Section 1 mentions the fraction of examples exceeding c only to describe how Zhang et al. 2019 quantify bias. NOT the composite estimand.
  • arXiv:2206.07136 (Bu, Wang, Zha, Karypis, "Automatic Clipping: Differentially Private Deep Learning Made Easier and Stronger", 14 Jun 2022, v3 4 Oct 2023) is the one that bites, and it bites on the mapping rather than on limb (a). Sec 3.1 does carry clipping percentages — "we find in the GPT2 generation experiments in [41] that 100% of per-sample gradients are clipped at all iterations", and about 20–60% on QQP/QNLI/MNLI — but the unit is per-sample gradients, the GPT-2 figure is cited from Li et al. (ICLR 2021), and the setting is DP fine-tuning, so limb (a)'s step-level rate for a stability clip is still unoccupied. Its Theorems 1 and 2, however, establish that any constant R > 0 is equivalent to R = 1 (learning rate eta*R for SGD-type optimizers; R cancels outright for adaptive ones), and Appendix B.3 with Fact B.1 shows per-layer clipping works only "when R is tuned proportionally", with a counterexample when one layer's threshold moves alone.
  • That last result DISCHARGES the promotion clause's third item, and it discharges it in the adversary's favour: rows 4 and 8 rested on the adversary's own unsourced Adam reasoning, and the algebra now has a primary source. It does not make either row fatal — the theorem concerns a CONSTANT rescaling, while a stability clip fires intermittently in the tail, which is exactly the distinction the two-endpoint design is built to measure — but the invariance mechanism is published, in a neighbouring setting, and the entry no longer gets to treat it as folklore. Both rows stay Partial, now with a citation.
  • ZClip (arXiv:2504.02507) came back exact. Section 6.6.1 exists, Figure 11's caption is "Clipping percentage vs. training step for different z-score thresholds", the introducing sentence is verbatim as recorded, the thresholds swept are ZClip's own z-scores 1.5 to 4.0 in steps of 0.5, and there is NO numeric clipped-step percentage anywhere for fixed c = 1.0 — only the qualitative "continuous clipping" remark at lr 5e-3. The "optimal threshold c furthermore depends on the particular model and the many hyperparameters in the training recipe" sentence is verbatim in Sec 2.1. One scale (1B LLaMA-style, 16 layers), one stack (FSDP, HF Transformers 4.47.1, fused AdamW, BF16).
  • The two log-metric priors were checked in the code, and both needed correcting AGAINST this entry's own concession. fairseq's clip field is real and is the share of updates whose gradient norm exceeded the threshold — v0.6.0's meter carries the comment "# % of updates clipped" — but it dates to December 2017, not 2018: issue #79, created 2017-12-12, already prints "clip 94%". And the published range is not the "0% to 100%" this entry conceded: issue #250's clip=100% was logged on a run with --clip-norm 0.0, i.e. clipping DISABLED, which v0.6.0 later guarded with a clip_norm > 0 condition. Real published values are 94% and 0% (#79), 0% (#416, #503), 2% (#1263) and 0 (#1687). Issue #2201 has a user reading the logged fraction as the threshold itself, as recorded.
  • OLMo's clipping_rate is NOT limb (a)'s quantity. In allenai/OLMo's olmo/optim.py it is num_grads_clipped / num_eligible_grads — the per-step fraction of PARAMETER TENSORS clipped within groups carrying max_grad_norm or max_grad_norm_ratio — computed only when collect_param_metrics is on, counted per rank with no all-reduce, and dropped from the console log, which keeps optim/total_grad_norm alone. Under a single global-norm group it degenerates to a per-step indicator, so the quantity is recoverable there; it is not an aggregated clipped-step fraction, and nothing in either stack aggregates it over a run or compares it across scales. This correction moves one of the three conceded neighbours away from the candidate.
  • Verdict unchanged, for a reason the promotion clause got wrong. Gate 5 reads "Provisional — ... or Medium novelty with a close neighbor", and that is this entry: fairseq's per-window clipped-update percentage and ZClip's Figure 11 are close neighbours on limb (a), both now confirmed at first hand, and opening the three DP papers was never going to remove them. Validated additionally needs novelty >= Medium "with the complete search record", which the clause read as satisfied by clearing the DP line. It was not. Well-posedness 3/3 and Significance 2/3 are met; novelty is the sole bar.

ID: UQ-20261017-51
Date: 2026-10-17
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): Biology — comparative physiology and cell biology (cell-size and metabolic allometry); fitting method borrowed from aquatic size-spectrum ecology

Question (canonical): Is the near-equal partition of total cell biomass across logarithmic cell-size classes reported for the human body a general feature of animal bodies, and does the slope of that within-body cell-size spectrum shift with species body mass? (Scored as canonical: V1, because the Gate 2 ground attaches to V1's own words. The single permitted Gate 1 reformulation, V2 — S >= 3 species over >= 10^4-fold body mass, a pre-declared "one cell" rule for erythrocytes/myofibres/adipocytes/neurons, a declared volume protocol, fitted slope with CI, slope-equality tests against -1 and against the human -0.97, a dominant-tissue hold-out, and an equal-energy check — is in the record and does not escape that ground.)

Alternative formulations:
- Do animals other than humans show roughly equal total biomass per logarithmic cell-size class, and is the exponent conserved across a wide range of body mass?
- Is the within-organism distribution of cell biomass over cell size a conserved allometric property, or an incidental consequence of the particular tissue composition of the human body?

Motivating gap:
At intake: Hatton et al. (PNAS 2023) report a whole-body human census in which cell count falls as roughly cell mass^-1, so each logarithmic size class holds similar total biomass; the pattern is numerically reminiscent of the Sheldon spectrum but has no predation cascade inside a body, and was taken to exist for one species with no comparative measurement and no mechanism. READ LEVEL at intake: title/abstract only. Corrected on opening the paper at the publisher: two of three intake claims fail — the comparative question is posed in print, and a cross-mammal cell-size dataset plus fitted cross-species exponents already exist. What survives: no non-human whole-body census by size class exists, the paper makes no size-spectrum comparison, and it states no mechanism and runs no per-cell metabolic analysis.

Presuppositions:
- The human near-invariance is real, not an artefact of pooling literature estimates. CONTESTED; the source concedes >1,500 sources for ~400 cell types, mass "often inferred ... rather than measured directly", up to 4-fold spread in size and 20-fold in count.
- Two further species can be censused to comparable accuracy. CONTESTED and binding: the human number rests on a century of reference-man morphometry with no second-species substrate; adversary sweeps found only organ-level DNA-based rodent totals, self-described as "very approximate".
- "Cell size class" is usable at both geometric tails. CONTESTED; the source itself flags the myonuclear domain as unresolved. V2 exists only to discharge this.
- A whole-body spectrum is more than a statement about three tissues. CONTESTED and partly falsified: biomass is "dominated by muscle and fat", myocytes ~half of cell biomass, and the two visible departures from flatness sit at the dominant-tissue boundaries.
- Spectrum theory yields a body-mass prediction that survives removing the predation cascade. FALSE as stated: the -1 expectation comes from balanced growth with a lower size bound, with no body-mass term, so V1's "predicted direction" has no referent.
- Per-cell metabolic rate is measurable or boundable against cell size. Supported as boundable only (Savage et al. 2007 infer it indirectly).

What would count as an answer:
A cell census by size class for >= 2 further species spanning >= 10^4-fold body mass, under a counting rule and volume protocol declared before collection with propagated uncertainty, giving (i) a fitted slope with CI per species; (ii) slope-equality tests across species and against -1 and -0.97; (iii) a hold-out decomposition excluding each body's two or three dominant tissues; (iv) a test of whether equal-biomass classes are equal-energy classes under bounded per-cell metabolic rates. A clean negative settles it as well as a positive. Gate 1: statable and falsifiable under V2; but V1's predicted-direction clause is empty, and the answer condition names an artefact whose only instance took >1,500 sources with no route offered to a second — well-posed and inert.

Novelty — queries run (query -> one-line result):
Gate 2: 11 web searches, 5 fetches (full list: batches/2026-10-17-2257/UQ-20261017-51-record.md). Most informative:
- Q6 (answer-side, the "already computed?" query) 'whole-body cell count and size distribution mouse census all cell types 2025 following Hatton' -> NOTHING; the published quantity exists for exactly one species (slope -0.97, 95% CI -1.09 to -0.87, 26 octave classes, 70-kg reference male).
- Q4 '"size spectrum" of cells within an organism Sheldon spectrum analogy' -> aquatic size-spectrum theory only; no intra-body transplant by anyone.
- Q9 (metabolic ecology) '"energetic equivalence" per logarithmic size class cells within an organism' -> community-level energetic equivalence only; limb (iv) genuinely unposed.
- Q11 (method-owning field) '"individual size distribution" size spectrum slope estimation comparing slopes' -> Edwards et al., size-spectrum fitting methods; mature toolkit, never pointed at cells in a body (search negative, NOT OPENED).
- F3/F5 https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2303077120 -> OPENED twice at the publisher on the first call; decisive sentences confirmed verbatim. F1 (doi.org) failed; PMC never attempted per the access rule.
Adversary Disguise sweeps, both executed and both over minimum: adversary 1 ran 9 (developmental polyploidy, rodent DNA-cellularity, German allometry, mouse whole-body census, Zipf/Pareto, cross-species cell-type ratios, cited-by, per-cell ATP budget, plant bodies), adversary 2 ran 9 (quantitative stereology, genome-size/C-value evolution, clinical "body cell mass", statistical-physics heavy tails, German, answer-side mouse census, intra-body size-spectrum phrasing, Peto's paradox, citation-chasing). Neither found a disguised prior; both independently reproduced the Q6 negative. Full lists: UQ-20261017-51-adversary-1.md, UQ-20261017-51-adversary-2.md.

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
PRIOR 1 — Hatton I.A. et al., "The human cell count and size distribution", PNAS 2023, 120(39):e2303077120, opened at https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2303077120 by the record (F3/F5) and independently by both adversaries. Unit: one cell group within a single reference human body (1,264 groups, ~400 cell types). Endpoint: log-log slope of count on cell mass (-0.97, CI -1.09 to -0.87) and biomass per logarithmic size class over 26 octave bins. Comparator: the slope -1 (equal biomass per log class). Estimand: whether cellular biomass is constant across logarithmic cell-size classes.
PRIOR 2 — Savage V.M. et al., "Scaling of number, size, and metabolic rate of cells with body size in mammals", PNAS 2007, 104(11):4718-4723, opened in full at https://people.clas.ufl.edu/gillooly/files/cell_size_PNAS_2007.pdf (record F2; adversary 2 F3). Unit: one (species, cell-type) mean, 18 cell types for volume and 7 for number, mouse to elephant. Endpoint: mean cell volume, cell number, indirectly inferred cellular metabolic rate. Comparator: exponent 0 with number ~M^1 versus exponent 0.25 with number ~M^0.75. Estimand: the allometric exponent against body mass with 95% CI (on verification the paper states no "X of 18" count at all: its Fig. 2 caption excepts only alveolar macrophages among the 14 strategy-i types, so 13 of those 14 include zero and the 4 strategy-ii types exclude it; the record's 14 and adversary 2's 13 are both derivations — not load-bearing).
PRIOR 3 — the cross-mammal limb inside PRIOR 1's own Materials and Methods: "a dataset of cell size for 33 cell types across mammal species spanning the size range from mouse to elephant". Unit: one (cell type, species) mean cell size. Endpoint: mean cell size per type, used qualitatively. Comparator: body-mass invariance. Estimand: whether mean cell size is invariant and hence whether "we should expect a similar inverse cell size-count relation to hold in other mammals". No fitted slope, no CI, no per-species spectrum. (Declared as a limb of PRIOR 1 because the fetch budget was exhausted before a third independent on-point source.)
OPENED AND EXCLUDED: Hatton et al., "Linking scaling laws across eukaryotes", PNAS 2019 (record F4) — organism-level metabolism/abundance/growth/mortality only, no cell size, no cell number, no intra-organism distribution.

vs PRIOR 1 — it does not differ where it matters. ID: UQ-20261017-52
Date: 2026-10-17
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): Biology — functional genomics / cell biology (gene essentiality, targeted protein degradation). Method-owning neighbours: chemical-biology target validation; developmental genetics (transcriptional adaptation); systems biology (rate-dependent response).

Question (canonical): Is gene essentiality a property of the gene or of the rate at which its product is removed — for a matched panel of >= 100 genes in one human cell line assayed both by acute degron depletion and by CRISPR knockout, what fraction of pre-declared essentiality calls disagree (V2: conditional on measured residual target protein at the fitness readout, with an RNA-less knockout arm alongside PTC alleles), and does the residual discordance load on measured protein half-life or on the transcriptional-adaptation signature?

Alternative formulations:
- Does the standard essentiality call depend on removal kinetics, so that genes scored non-essential under gradual loss are essential under abrupt depletion, or the reverse?
- How much of a published essentialome is a statement about the dilution timescale of the perturbation rather than about the gene's function?

Motivating gap: Inverts the presupposition behind every essentiality map — that cutting a gene and reading fitness days later measures the gene's requirement. Knockout removes protein by dilution over divisions; degrons remove it in minutes to hours and are now library-scale. At intake the bookkeeping question looked unposed; Gate 2 found it posed and answered at proteome scale in budding yeast (2025).

Presuppositions: (1) degron and knockout depletion can be made comparable in depth — CONTESTED, partly falsified (both yeast papers name incomplete degradation first); V2 measures depth instead of assuming it. (2) degron tagging does not itself perturb function/stability — CONTESTED and now evidenced as a real confound: Nat Commun 13:5495, unread at Gate 2 and opened by both adversaries via doi.org, reports AID2 "led to a small but consistent increase in basal protein levels", poorly expressed fusions, and that "the kinetics of degradation and recovery are highly variable, unpredictable". (3) essentiality as a continuous fitness score with a pre-declared threshold — supported, and load-bearing (yeast answer swings 69% -> 4% with threshold). (4) panel protein half-lives available — plausible but collinear with depletion depth. (5) compensation detectable in window — mis-specified in V1: the demonstrated trigger is mutant-mRNA decay, not slow protein loss (P3). (6) endogenous tagging at scale plus the non-viability of essential-gene knockout clones — stands; the real human-cell barrier. (7) not settled by knockdown-vs-knockout literature — the risk landed from a different direction (degron-vs-deletion in yeast). (8) cell-autonomous fitness in culture acceptable — stands.

What would count as an answer: >= 100 genes in one cell line, each inducibly degradable and separately knocked out, threshold declared before data collection, yielding (i) discordance rate with CIs, (ii) its direction, (iii) regression of discordance on measured half-life and on measured compensatory transcript/protein change after conditioning on measured residual-protein depth, and (iv) a projection of how many public essentiality-map calls the rate would reclassify.

Novelty — queries run (query -> one-line result): 11 at Gate 2 (cap reached; 5 fetches) + 9 adversary-1 + 9 adversary-2 = 29, all logged. Most informative: "comparison of degron-mediated acute protein depletion and CRISPR knockout essentiality calls discordance" (mandatory own-field/own-words title query) -> the two 2025 genome-wide yeast degron-library papers; "auxin-inducible degron library genome-wide acute depletion fitness screen essential genes human cells" -> JCB 224(2) e202409007 and e202409050, both yeast; "protein half-life determines time to phenotype after CRISPR knockout dilution kinetics screen" -> nothing on point, the decisive coefficient appears unmeasured; mandatory "what fraction of X" limb -> the fraction is already published for a reference proteome (~31-45% of knockout-essential genes without a fitness defect on acute degradation). Adversary new-vocabulary sweeps added: historical "phenotypic lag"; CRISPRi-vs-CRISPRn in human cells; Tn-seq-vs-CRISPRi in bacteria; mycobacterial graded-depletion "vulnerability"; morphant-vs-mutant discordance; metabolic-control-analysis titration thresholds; degrader-vs-dependency pharmacology; plus bioRxiv 10.1101/732552v2, opened, "with only 20 to 35% of the genes in disagreement" across modalities. Novelty confidence: Low

Significance — consequence: If a half-life-predicted discordance survives conditioning on depth, removal kinetics becomes a declared parameter of essentiality maps and of target validation; if discordance is fully explained by residual protein, the published 31-45% yeast figures are a technology artefact rather than a fact about essentiality. Both outcomes informative — but the headline number is already in print.

Significance — audience: (a) human functional-genomics and DepMap-type map builders; (b) chemical-biology/pharma target-validation groups choosing between degrader and knockout evidence; (c) the yeast degron-library authors, whose unexplained 38% would be decomposed. Audience (b) is demonstrably real — Nat Commun 13:5495 (2022) is that audience running this comparison "for target validation studies" — but the lever they already act on is degradation extent per target, not kinetics.

Significance — fecundity: per-gene depletion-depth dose-response ("essentiality reserve"); whether transcriptional adaptation has any fitness consequence (untested in P3); prediction of kinetics-sensitive calls from half-life plus paralog structure; whether RNA-less-vs-PTC allele choice changes human fitness calls.

- ROUTING ROW NARROWED, not withdrawn, and the reasoning is worth following because it went both ways. A dedicated reader of both papers' full text, legends and methods found that NEITHER raises protein half-life as an explanation for the essential-gene DISCORDANCE: P1 offers incomplete degradation, conditional essentiality and readout artefact only, so the row's original attribution to P1 is struck. But three independent readers agree that P2 contains, verbatim and untested, "milder depletion could also reflect longer protein half-lives", with half-lives measured for only a handful of proteins by one-phase decay fits (Fig. 1D) and no correlation of half-life with anything reported. The paper therefore poses half-life as a cause of milder DEPLETION, and separately poses incomplete degradation as a cause of the missing fitness defect; it does not pose the composite that joins them. So the composite decomposition is not routed — unposed, and on this entry's own analysis not identified on a stratum selected on degradability — while the posed narrow link is routed on its own terms. A first pass here recorded the row as withdrawn outright, which was too strong: it read the narrow link as a different phenomenon rather than as a narrower one.
- Cutting the other way, and recorded because it matters for anyone re-posing this: P1 reports that protein levels did not differ between essential proteins with and without a fitness defect, which cuts against residual protein as the cause. The explanation for the discordance is genuinely open — but UN-ASKED rather than asked, which is why it is not routable, and the candidate as posed leads with the headline rate that is answered.
- The mammalian-cells absence is NOT established: a second, deliberately wider sweep (7 searches across dTAG, AID, HaloPROTAC, PROTAC, DepMap concordance and half-life vocabularies) read only two pages at abstract level and found no degron-versus-CRISPR essentiality comparison, with the nearest hit a benchmark of degron systems against each other (Xing et al., Nat Commun 2025, s41467-025-61848-1) and the only discussion of the discordance a qualitative review (Joshi, Dey & De 2023, doi 10.37349/etat.2023.00194). Recorded as not found in a thin search, never as a check that passed.

ID: UQ-20261017-53
Date: 2026-10-17
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): Biology — transcriptomics / genome annotation (target field: long-read and reference-annotation community). Method transplanted from statistical ecology (unseen-species richness estimation). Source method: cross-field transplant.

Question (canonical): For a pre-declared gene set and a pre-declared isoform-individuation rule (splice-junction-chain identity at a declared 5'/3' tolerance), treating each of >= 2 independent deep long-read libraries per tissue as an incomplete sample of a gene's distinct spliced-isoform classes: (a) what does a false-positive-aware richness estimator (coverage-based rarefaction/extrapolation, Chao/Good-Turing extended with a contamination term calibrated per read class from spike-ins and technical replicates) give for the number of unobserved REAL isoforms per gene, with intervals; (b) does its prediction of how many new isoforms one further independent library reveals match a held-out library; and (c) is the fitted per-gene asymptote finite and depth-stable across all admissible contamination models, or does no admissible model close the curve — in which case "isoforms per gene" is a depth-indexed quantity, not an estimand? (V2; V1 and the Gate 1 reformulation rationale in batches/2026-10-17-2257/UQ-20261017-53-record.md)

Alternative formulations:
- Is "the number of isoforms of a gene" an estimable quantity with a finite asymptote, or an unbounded function of sequencing depth?
- What is the unseen-isoform richness of a human gene once single-observation reads are partitioned into genuinely rare isoforms and technical artefacts?

Motivating gap: Long-read studies keep adding novel isoforms dominated by single-observation transcripts and the discovery curve does not visibly close; the field's own 2025 review (Monzó, Frankish & Conesa, Genome Research 35:583, opened) documents the instability, reports a SIRV-derived artefact share of "between 10% and 15% of the sequencing output" that "only represents a possible upper limit", and contains no richness estimator, rarefaction, asymptote or unobserved count. Statistical ecology solves the structurally identical problem, but its estimators assume singletons are rare-but-real, which a separately measurable technical process (RT template switching, intrapriming, degraded 5' ends) falsifies here. The transplant was already made in this field at Hill order q=1 (Schertzer et al., per-gene isoform "perplexity") and stopped there.

Presuppositions: (1) isoforms individuable at a declared tolerance — CONTESTED, pre-declared; (2) per-read-class technical FP rate independently estimable from spike-ins/replicates — LOAD-BEARING, only bound-identified in opened sources; (3) reads near-independent after duplicate handling — CONTESTED for cDNA; (4) real per-gene repertoire finite — NOT ASSUMED, it is limb (c); (5) "real" definable without function, operationalised as reproducible across independent libraries and donors — DECLARED, and the point on which Gate 4 killed the entry; (6) richness estimators informative at per-gene sample sizes — SMALL-SAMPLE RISK; (7) enough independent deep libraries per tissue for a held-out test — unverified.

What would count as an answer: fitted coverage curves plus per-gene unobserved-real-isoform counts with intervals under a pre-declared contamination model calibrated from spike-ins and technical replicates, across >= 2 independent deep datasets per tissue, PLUS a held-out library test of the predicted new-isoform count. Answered either by curves that close (finite, depth-stable per-gene asymptote) or by a demonstration that none closes under any admissible contamination model (so annotation must report a depth-indexed quantity). Both branches reportable.

Novelty — queries run (query -> one-line result): 38 distinct web searches — 11 at Gate 2 (own-field saturation words, ecology rarefaction/richness, EST-era capture-recapture, preseq/library complexity, immunogenomics, microbial spurious singletons, annotation completeness, ENCODE4/GTEx) plus 9 per adversary in vocabularies Gate 2 did not try; full lists in batches/2026-10-17-2257/UQ-20261017-53-record.md and -adversary-1/-2/-3.md. Most informative:
- "estimating the total number of transcript isoforms per gene saturation long-read transcriptome" (Gate 2 #1, mandatory own-words title query) -> Schertzer et al. perplexity preprint; no per-gene asymptote paper.
- "species richness estimation in the presence of false positives misidentification erroneous singletons estimator" (Gate 2 #6) -> Willis arXiv 1604.02598 (breakaway); FP-aware richness estimation is a named problem in microbial-ecology words only.
- "stochastic noise splicing machinery number of isoforms predicted from expression level and number of introns EST cDNA library sampling simulation" (A3 #1) -> Melamud & Moult 2009 NAR 37(14):4873, OPENED at OUP: isoform count predicted from sampling + a 1-10% per-gene error rate.
- "EST clustering error spurious singletons effect on estimating number of expressed genes gene capture prediction" (A3 #3) -> Wang, Lindsay et al. 2005 BMC Bioinformatics 6:300, OPENED at Springer: zero-class estimation of sampled cDNA with singleton-inflation correction and next-library capture prediction.
- "noisy splicing drives mRNA isoform diversity ... estimate total number of isoforms noise rate per intron Pickrell" (A3 #8) -> Pickrell et al. 2010 PLoS Genet 6(12):e1001236, OPENED at PLOS: "We see no sign that our identification of isoforms is near saturation".
- "reverse transcriptase template switching false alternative transcripts reproducible direct repeats ..." (A3 #9) -> Houseley & Tollervey 2010 PLoS ONE 5(8):e12271, OPENED: artefactual junctions reproduce across independent RT reactions and enzymes.
- "pan-transcriptome open closed Heaps law isoform repertoire saturation exponent gene" / "Heaps law type-token hapax legomena transcriptome isoform vocabulary growth" (A2 #1-2) -> pangenome-openness and corpus-linguistics machinery, no isoform application.
- "RNA sequencing depth guidelines for the study of alternative splicing" (A2 #5) -> bioRxiv 2024.10.09.617406, OPENED: published extrapolated loss of "up to 7489 genes with AS/114717 alternative junctions" at GTEx mean depth.
COULD NOT READ after four passes (grounds no grade either way, and not a check that passed): Pardo-Palacios et al., LRGASP, Nature Methods 2024 — abstract/metadata only; failed routes nature.com (CLIENT_ERROR), repositori.upf.edu (Access Denied), PMC (hard-blocked). Also unread: Chiu & Chao 2016 PeerJ 4:e1634, Nellore et al. 2016 Genome Biol 17:266, arXiv 2012.07485, arXiv 2602.08769, Nat Genet ng0904-915, Glinos et al. 2022.

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
1. Melamud E, Moult J, "Stochastic noise in splicing machinery", Nucleic Acids Res 37(14):4873 (2009), doi:10.1093/nar/gkp471 — OPENED (OUP). Unit: gene (EST-sampled). Endpoint: number and abundance of isoforms predicted by a stochastic noise model from expression level and intron count, via simulated sampling of virtual cDNA libraries; per-gene error rates 1-10%. Comparator: observed EST counts as expression surrogate. Estimand: the noise rate generating observed isoform multiplicity. States "present EST libraries sample only a small fraction of transcript space, only a fraction of all isoforms have so far been observed".
2. Pickrell JK, Pai AA, Gilad Y, Pritchard JK, "Noisy splicing drives mRNA isoform diversity in human cells", PLoS Genet 6(12):e1001236 (2010) — OPENED (PLOS). Unit: splice site / intron / gene. Endpoint: ~150,000 unannotated junctions, ~0.7% per-intron splicing error rate, 98.4% major form, and depth-subsampling curves. Comparator: annotated junctions, read depth. Estimand: the per-intron error rate. States "We see no sign that our identification of isoforms is near saturation" and Fig S1 "Identification of isoforms is not at saturation".
3. Wang J-PZ, Lindsay BG, et al., "Gene capture prediction and overlap estimation in EST sequencing from one or multiple libraries", BMC Bioinformatics 6:300 (2005) — OPENED (Springer). Unit: gene in a cDNA library. Endpoint: N = observed + zero class n0, and how many new genes a further sample of targeted size captures. Comparator: estimates before/after clustering-error correction (12030 vs 9155; 12085 vs 9492). Estimand: total sampled-population richness with a spurious-singleton correction — "Inflation of the singleton count n1 usually results in inflation of N"; clustering error biases observed counts upward "by 35% - 40%".
(Gate 2's own three nearest priors — Schertzer et al. bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.07.02.662769 at Hill q=1; Monzó, Frankish & Conesa, Genome Research 35:583, verified verbatim by adversary 2 at the publisher; Kaplinsky & Arnaout, Nat Commun 7:11881 — plus supporting priors preseqR/Daley & Smith and Willis arXiv 1604.02598, are set out in full with their four attributes in the record.)

Novelty — how this differs from each: vs Melamud & Moult and Pickrell — the candidate asks for a quantitative per-gene unobserved-real count with intervals and a held-out predictive test, which neither reports; but both pose and answer the candidate's own alternative formulation #1 (isoform count as a function of sampling, discovery not saturated) in the candidate's own field, so the difference is estimator choice, not question. vs Wang & Lindsay — identical method structure (zero-class estimation of sampled cDNA, singleton inflation corrected, prediction for an additional library) at the gene unit rather than the isoform unit, i.e. a unit swap on an asked question; splice forms appear there only as a nuisance inflating gene counts. vs Schertzer — same field, same unit, same ecological framework at adjacent Hill order q=1, explicitly declining unobserved-richness estimation and bias correction.

Novelty confidence: Medium
Graded Medium at Gate 2 (distinctness held across 11 queries in five vocabularies, with the two most dangerous own-field hiding places opened). Regraded Low at Gate 5 on adversary 3's three own-field primary sources, then RESTORED to Medium on verification, which opened all three: Wang, Lindsay et al. 2005 estimates unobserved GENES and not isoforms, Melamud & Moult 2009 names no richness estimator and estimates error rates rather than unobserved classes, and Pickrell et al. 2010's depth analysis is a subsampling graph with no model fitted. Four further literature sweeps found no per-gene unobserved-isoform estimate by any richness estimator, at any unit, with or without a false-positive term, and no paper posing whether per-gene isoform number has a finite asymptote. Medium rather than High because two close neighbours were read only through a summariser and remain the live residue: Kim et al. 2004 (Nat Genet 36:915-916), which adapts an Ewing-and-Green EST gene-counting method to estimate splice variants per gene — a per-gene RATE, not a zero-class estimate — and Garcia-Ortega & Martinez 2015 (PLoS ONE), which notes the gene unit's ambiguity with respect to splice variants and stays at the gene level. Pickrell's non-saturation statement also overlaps the depth-dependence limb of (c) qualitatively.

Significance — consequence: If a finite depth-stable asymptote exists, the field gains a per-gene completeness statistic and a stopping rule, and arbitrary read-count filters (e.g. Schertzer's >= 10 reads across 124 samples, discarding ~7.9M collapsed isoforms, 81% single-read) could be justified against an estimated contamination rate. If none closes, "N isoforms per gene" is not an estimand and annotation resources, benchmarks and cross-tissue diversity comparisons are reporting a function of their own depth. Not weighed in the verdict: adversaries 1 and 3 both note the negative branch is already the field's stated working position.
Significance — audience: reference-annotation consortia (GENCODE/Ensembl, RefSeq); long-read method and benchmark authors (LRGASP, SQANTI, TALON, IsoQuant, bambu, FLAIR); designers of large long-read studies; clinical RNA diagnostics (strength of a negative isoform finding); diversity-estimation methodologists. Evidenced, not asserted: the motivating review is co-authored by Adam Frankish, GENCODE's annotation lead, and is about what to admit — it advocates replication to separate artefacts, warns that strict filtering risks "discarding real biological TD", and reports an artefact bound it declines to convert into an estimate.
Significance — fecundity: per-gene completeness as a covariate on isoform-level quantification and isoform-eQTL irreproducibility; coverage-standardised rather than depth-confounded cross-tissue/species comparison; a principled filter threshold; extension to TSS/TES and allele-specific repertoires; in the negative branch, what the right depth-indexed annotation statistic is.
Significance — anchoring: the splicing-noise vs functional-diversity debate (now a prior rather than an anchor); documented instability of long-read transcript identification; the annotation community's standing decision about what to admit; the unseen-species problem with false positives.

Reason for silence: Gate 2 claimed a disciplinary boundary (transcriptomics frames novel isoforms as a per-transcript precision problem; the estimator-owning field writes in OTU vocabulary), a missing FP-rate-ingesting estimator, the field stopping at Hill q=1, and recent data. Two legs did not survive Gate 4: the field does ask "how much are we missing at depth D?" and publishes extrapolated numbers (bioRxiv 2024.10.09.617406, opened), and zero-class estimation with singleton-inflation correction was applied to cDNA sampling in 2005 (Wang & Lindsay, opened). The surviving explanation is asked-and-dismissed, not un-asked: the field posed the depth question in 2009-2010, attributed the open curve to stochastic splicing noise, and judged the richness of the noise class uninformative. The missing-method and recent-data legs survive, but they explain why this framing has not been executed, not why it was never posed.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3
Well-posedness regraded from the record's 3/3: the falsifier and both answer branches are specified, but presupposition 5 does not survive contact with opened primary sources — the declared "real" admits reproducible artefacts, excludes validated rare real isoforms, and cannot be evaluated on the never-observed classes limb (a) counts, so the estimand is not well defined as declared. Significance 2/3 as recorded (changed reporting rather than changed admission; per-gene estimates may be informative only pooled).

Strongest remaining objection: Presupposition failure, which both cold judges left Partial and both named as the sharpest objection standing. The declared sense of "real" — reproducible across independent libraries and donors — is itself depth-indexed, because Pickrell's own numbers (a major splice form at 98.4%, a per-intron error rate near 0.7%, a splicing code defining a probability distribution over many splice forms) make rare biologically real noise splices recur once depth is large enough; and presupposition 2's transfer of a per-read-class artefact rate from spike-ins to endogenous reads is contested and evidenced nowhere. Limb (c) partly absorbs this by making the depth-indexed outcome one of its two declared answers, but that repair is argued rather than shown. Next behind it: the unread Disguise residue named under Novelty confidence, and the general non-identifiability of unseen-class richness without parametric assumptions, which could leave (c) ending in "not identifiable". Recorded and not weighed as support: LRGASP was never opened across four passes, so its contents remain unknown in both directions.

Promotion requires: all four of — (1) Kim et al. 2004 (Nat Genet 36:915-916) and Garcia-Ortega & Martinez 2015 (PLoS ONE, "How Many Genes Are Expressed in a Transcriptome? Estimation and Results for RNA-Seq") opened at first hand rather than through a summariser, with the grade restated from papers in hand, since these are the two surviving close neighbours and either could carry the estimand; (2) a pre-declared admissibility class for contamination models and a stated depth-stability tolerance, fixed before any data are seen, which is what would move well-posedness from 2/3 to 3/3; (3) evidence that a spike-in-calibrated per-read-class artefact rate transfers to endogenous reads, or the presupposition restated as a reproducible-across-chemistries criterion with the consequence for limb (a)'s estimand accepted in writing; (4) LRGASP's full text and supplement opened at a working route, to settle whether an identity-error-aware richness estimator and per-read-class false-positive rates already exist off the shelf.

Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): not applicable to the rejected question. For anyone pursuing the surviving residue as a methods question rather than a ledger candidate: open LRGASP full text and supplement at a working route, and Chiu & Chao 2016 (PeerJ 4:e1634) and arXiv 2012.07485, to establish whether a measured-identity-error richness estimator and per-read-class spike-in FP rates already exist off the shelf; then test whether the per-gene frequency spectrum is predictable from a per-intron error rate and depth alone, since only its failure as a generative model would make limb (a) a new question.
