ID: UQ-20261018-01
Date: 2026-10-18
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): Medicine — primary care / general internal medicine; clinical informatics; diagnostic safety. Adjacent: pharmacoepidemiology (code-based phenotype validity).
Question (canonical): For label/result pairs with a consensus disconfirming rule computable from routine data — (a) COPD code + post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC >= 0.7, (b) hypothyroidism code + normal TSH >= 6 weeks after last levothyroxine supply, (c) coeliac code + negative serology and negative biopsy on a documented gluten-containing diet — what is the 24-month cause-specific hazard and cumulative incidence of a recorded retraction event (problem-list removal, "resolved"/inactivated status, exclusion code; pre-declared fallback, reported separately: >= 180 days without disease-specific prescribing) after the first disconfirming result, against matched person-time in labelled patients with no such result, and what share of each group is still on disease-specific therapy at 12 and 24 months? (V2, the Gate 1 reformulation; asthma + negative challenge and heart failure + normal natriuretic peptide are pre-specified secondary pairs; penicillin allergy + negative challenge is the positive control.)
Alternative formulations:
- Are clinical diagnoses falsifiable in practice — what is the hazard of a label being removed once the test that defines it comes back against it?
- When the chart already contains the result that rules a condition out, how long does the condition stay on the problem list and on the prescription?
- V1 (intake, failed Gate 1: "objectively disconfirming evidence" undefined for two of five pairs; outcome stated without naming the data model that emits it): In routine care records, once a chronic-disease diagnosis has been entered, what is the rate at which it is retracted after objectively disconfirming evidence appears in the same record, and does retraction change the disease-specific treatment the patient goes on receiving?
Motivating gap: Repeated studies find a large minority of chronic-disease labels unsupported by their defining criteria (Aaron 2017 ruled out current asthma in 33.1%, 95% CI 29.4-36.8, of 613 completers), but de-labelling there was a research intervention. The intake's framing — nobody asks what routine care does when the disconfirming result is already filed — was falsified at Gate 2 for the index pair: Fortis 2016 asked exactly that for COPD and reported both limbs. What survived was narrower (multi-pair, time-to-event, comparator-controlled, recorded-removal-event endpoint) and did not survive Gate 4's independent sweeps.
Presuppositions: P1 dated diagnosis histories retrievable INCLUDING removal events — recorded as the weakest point at Gate 2; both adversaries EVIDENCED it instead (Jones 2024 built a 16,023-patient CPRD GOLD cohort indexed on first "resolved asthma" code; NHS Digital publishes a QOF "COPD resolved" refset). P2 a computable disconfirming rule per pair — holds for COPD by GOLD's definitional convention; adversary 2 found the hypothyroid rule mis-specified (fires while the patient is still supplied, since ">= 6 weeks after last supply" ignores days'-supply) and the coeliac rule effectively uncomputable (gluten intake lives in free text; labelled patients are gluten-free by default). P3 the result was visible to a clinician — contested; Rimawi 2013 records "no attempt to convey the result" outside the index system. P4 labels are intended to be falsifiable — contested; partly rebutted (a register carrying resolved codes is by construction a register of current disease). P5 retraction is not scored as the good outcome — descriptive only. P6 confounding by record continuity is a design problem (prevalent-user and immortal-time structure), not a covariate problem.
What would count as an answer: A pre-registered multi-database cohort (CPRD/OpenSAFELY, a US EHR network, a Nordic registry) reporting per pair the 24-month cumulative incidence of recorded retraction after the first disconfirming result against matched no-result person-time, the share still on disease-specific therapy at 12 and 24 months in each arm, penicillin allergy as positive control, and the prescribing-cessation analysis where removal events are not emitted. A hazard indistinguishable from comparator with therapy continuing answers it one way; a materially raised hazard with therapy stopping answers it the other. Removals never being recorded would falsify P1 and return the question to Gate 1.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 29 documented queries (11 Gate 2, 9 adversary 1, 9 adversary 2) plus 12 fetches; full lists in batches/2026-10-18-0130/UQ-20261018-01-record.md and the two adversary files. Most informative: (i) Gate 2 own-field own-words title query, "'persistent empiric COPD diagnosis and treatment after pulmonary function testing' study" → THE HIT, Fortis et al., Respir Care 2016;61(9):1192-1200, DOI 10.4187/respcare.04647, asking the candidate's question for the index pair with both limbs; (ii) adversary 2, "'resolved' diagnosis code CPRD time to removal ... 'asthma resolved' incidence of de-labelling primary care" → SECOND HIT missed by Gate 2, Jones et al., Br J Gen Pract 2024;74(743):e364-e370, DOI 10.3399/BJGP.2023.0271, a national matched cohort indexed on the retraction event itself; (iii) adversary 1, "'COPD resolved' OR 'asthma resolved' Read code primary care register removal after spirometry frequency" → the NHS Digital copdres_cod QOF refset, i.e. the removal event is routine operational practice; (iv) adversary 1, penicillin-allergy record query → Rimawi et al., J Hosp Med 2013;8(11):615-618 (opened), 20/55 (36%) relabelled within a year, beta-lactam receipt 22/35 vs 0/20 by record status; (v) Gate 2 "what fraction" query on problem-list deletion rates → completeness and duplication fractions only, no deletion-as-event fraction; (vi) Gate 2 method-owning-field query → Spoto et al., arXiv:2506.14669, where the measured "decay" is loss of code SPECIFICITY and not code removal (verified 2026-10-18), and in any case never conditional on a disconfirming result. Negative sweeps that found nothing: psychiatric diagnostic stability, de-implementation, epilepsy telemetry de-labelling, EHR audit-log metadata, CKD and diabetes register coding, German and Spanish and Dutch primary-care vocabularies.
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
A. Fortis SP, Corazalla EO, Jacobs DR Jr, Kim HJ. "Persistent Empiric COPD Diagnosis and Treatment After Pulmonary Function Test Showed No Obstruction." Respir Care 2016;61(9):1192-1200, DOI 10.4187/respcare.04647. Unit: patient with one non-obstructive PFT session in one academic lab, 855 of 1,805 screened (473 normal, 382 restrictive). Endpoint: COPD diagnosis still in place, and bronchodilator/inhaled-glucocorticoid treatment still given, despite the non-obstructive PFT. Comparator: none external (internal covariate ORs only; current smoking 44.7, empiric diagnosis 24.6 for treatment). Estimand: cross-sectional prevalence of persistence, 60/855 (7%) diagnosis and 208/855 (24%) treatment. FULL TEXT COULD NOT READ — routes failed: rc.rcjournal.com/content/61/9/1192 (CLIENT_ERROR), doi.org → journals.sagepub.com (paywalled, "You currently have no access to this content", tried independently by both adversaries), UMN experts and Iowa Esploro repositories (abstract only); and, on the 2026-10-18 residual pass, CORE search, Google Scholar (robots-disallowed), ResearchGate (no page), springermedicine.com (JavaScript challenge) and PubMed Central (reCAPTCHA) — five independent attempts, about 26 routes, full log in UQ-20261018-01-residual-fortis.md. Abstract read at the publisher by both adversaries, numbers concordant; follow-up window, pre-PFT label denominator and comparator NOT VISIBLE in any route.
B. Jones H, Cumins B, Cannings-John R, Ahmed H. "Adverse respiratory outcomes among patients with resolved asthma: matched retrospective cohort study." Br J Gen Pract 2024;74(743):e364-e370, DOI 10.3399/BJGP.2023.0271. OPENED at https://bjgp.org/content/74/743/e364 by both adversaries independently. Unit: CPRD GOLD patient with >= 1 "resolved asthma" code, index = first such code, 16,023 per cohort. Comparators: 1:1 matched active-asthma and CPRD-generated non-asthma cohorts. Endpoint: asthma/RTI admissions and consultations. Estimand: adjusted IRRs, mixed-effects negative binomial. Found by adversary 2 and absent from the Gate 2 record.
C. Aaron SD, Vandemheen KL, FitzGerald JM, et al. "Reevaluation of Diagnosis in Adults With Physician-Diagnosed Asthma." JAMA 2017;317(3):269-279. OPENED at https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2598265. Unit: adult with a physician asthma diagnosis, 613 completers. Endpoint: whether current asthma can be ruled out under a protocolised taper with repeat spirometry and challenge. Reference: the study's own algorithm, not routine care. Estimand: prevalence (stock) of unsupported labels, 33.1%.
(Also located, not opened, grading nothing: medRxiv 2025 "Diagnostic Reversion in Dementia Care" 10.1101/2025.07.16.25331678; Pavia/Rome coeliac re-evaluation records; Spoto et al. arXiv:2506.14669, opened at Gate 2; its "decay" is loss of code specificity rather than code removal, and is unconditioned on any result.)
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs A — same question, same direction, same two limbs, on one of the candidate's pairs, in routine care, with the result already filed; differences are methodological only (whole-population unit vs one PFT lab; dated retraction EVENT vs persistence at an unstated point; matched no-result person-time vs no comparator; hazard and 24-month cumulative incidence vs one prevalence; conditional on holding a prior label vs a denominator of all 855 non-obstructive attendees). That makes the candidate a better-designed replication and extension, not a new question. vs B — same database, same retraction event, arrow reversed: Jones treats resolution as EXPOSURE and asks what follows; the candidate treats it as OUTCOME and asks what brings it about. An un-chosen direction of an asked relation. vs C — stock not flow, researcher-performed de-labelling, no record-side endpoint; C is the motivating anomaly, not a prior.
Novelty confidence: Low
Significance — consequence: If the hazard is indistinguishable from matched no-result person-time and therapy continues, every code-defined chronic-disease denominator (QOF-style registers, phenotype libraries, HCC-style risk adjustment, code-based trial recruitment) carries a false-positive fraction that is absorbing rather than transient, and de-labelling trials need a maintenance arm. If the hazard is raised and therapy stops, the one-third prevalence figures measure a queue being cleared and the overdiagnosis reading weakens. Deflated: for COPD the direction is already published.
Significance — audience: EHR-phenotyping and pharmacoepidemiology methodologists; primary-care quality bodies that already own resolved/exclusion coding (NHS Digital copdres_cod; vendor inhaler alerts keyed to "dormant or resolved coding"); de-labelling trialists in respiratory, endocrine and allergy medicine; diagnostic-safety researchers; payers using diagnosis-based risk adjustment. Judged real by both adversaries (attack 6 Resolved twice).
Significance — fecundity: whether the hazard varies by who filed the result (own practice vs external lab) makes result-acknowledgement auditing an exposure and tests P3; whether retraction is faster where the EHR emits a removal event turns the data model into a treatment; whether "history of" conversion rather than deletion dominates creates a measurable intermediate category.
Significance — anchoring: the misdiagnosis-prevalence anomaly (Aaron 2017; the COPD spirometry series); the problem-list literature's asymmetry between additions and deletions; penicillin-allergy delabelling and relabelling; code-based phenotype validity and chronic-flag persistence in claims.
Reason for silence: Claimed: a disciplinary boundary plus an incentive and data-model gap — the stock is paid for by clinical epidemiology, the flow belongs to informatics, whose published quantities are presence-side, and claims emit no removal event. FALSIFIED twice from opened sources: Fortis 2016 asked it in clinical pulmonology, the register the mechanism says would not fund it; Jones 2024 built a national matched cohort on the removal event in CPRD GOLD, the candidate's own primary data source, so neither data model nor boundary nor incentive kept anyone from the variable. What remains is that researchers holding the event chose the other direction — a preference, not a mechanism, i.e. the "no one thought of it" the LEDGER rules out. Under the LEDGER's own rule this is a signal to distrust the novelty claim, which is where the entry lands.
Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status) — two independent adversaries, A1 and A2; A2 did not see A1's log. Both ran their Disguise sweeps (9 queries each, cap 9, requirement 8), so Disguise is verified-as-run, not unverified; both independently re-verified the Fortis ground at the publisher and both record its full text as COULD NOT READ.
1 | Triviality — Fortis's 7%/24% and Rimawi's 36% relabelling make it a page of existing knowledge | Fortis's percentages are unconditional over all 855 non-obstructive attendees with no stated window and no restriction to prior label-holders, so they cannot be converted into a conditional retraction rate; Rimawi measures redocumentation after a removal the study team performed (inverse flow); Jones reports no time-to-event analysis and no proportion of the source population carrying a resolved code | Resolved (A1) / Resolved (A2)
2 | Disguise — a renaming of resolved-coding, "diagnostic reversion", psychiatric diagnostic stability, de-implementation, allergy redocumentation, coeliac re-evaluation | 18 new-vocabulary queries across 10+ vocabularies and two non-English; each named family owns one piece pointed elsewhere (stability compares successive assessments with no disconfirming index result; de-implementation's unit is a test or treatment, never a label; CKD/diabetes register work is about missing or true-state-change codes). Not a disguised known. BUT Fortis stands as the asked-in-own-words near-duplicate for the index pair, A2's sweep added a fourth near-prior in the candidate's own database that Gate 2 missed, and three promising hits (medRxiv reversion, Pavia coeliac, Dutch H&W) went unopened for budget | Partial (A1) / Partial (A2)
3 | Combinatorial novelty — clinical epidemiology x informatics with nothing at the seam | The seam has content and the field names it: Jones concedes resolved-code "usage and interpretation ... are likely to vary between clinicians and practices" while building a 16,023-patient cohort on it, places patients with both resolved and active periods in the resolved cohort, and censors at re-prescription — outcome and exposure contaminate each other; the NHS Digital refset subtracts patients from the QOF register with no published account of what results precede the code | Resolved (A1) / Resolved (A2)
4 | Presupposition failure — P1 (removal events retrievable), P2 (computable rule), P4 (labels meant to be falsifiable) | P1 is now EVIDENCED, against the record's own pessimism (Jones's dated 16,023-patient cohort; the QOF resolved refset); claims data still lack it, which the declared fallback covers. P2 holds for COPD by GOLD convention. Two real defects remain, both unsourced and so Partial: the hypothyroid rule fires while the patient is still supplied, and the coeliac rule is effectively uncomputable from coded data — repair (b) and drop (c) and the primary analysis collapses onto the COPD pair Fortis already asked about, removing the multi-pair generalisation that was the surviving novelty | Partial (A1) / Partial (A2)
5 | Vagueness — a null is pre-declared ambiguous, so any result "answers" it | Estimands are numeric and falsifiable and the fallback is declared before any data pull, which is the right discipline; but the most probable result (a null hazard) is uninterpretable between inertia, deliberate "history of" convention, and a third reading the record does not anticipate — that the code tracks prescribing rather than testing | Resolved (A1) / Partial (A2)
6 | Significance inflation — the audience is notional | Demonstrably already acting on the adjacent object: Jones 2024 in a general-practice journal calling resolved-asthma patients a "middle group" who "may benefit from a more comprehensive respiratory assessment"; a CPRD-approved study on resolved asthma; AAAAI 2023 on pharmacy records not updated after delabelling; Rimawi's 63% vs 0% beta-lactam receipt by record status | Resolved (A1) / Resolved (A2)
7 | Reason for silence — the claimed mechanism must explain why nobody ASKED | A1: database epidemiologists treat coding as measurement rather than as behaviour with a hazard, so the resolved code is used as exposure or exclusion but never as outcome — plausible, consistent with what was opened, but stated by no source. A2: falsified twice from opened sources (Fortis asked it in the register the mechanism excludes; Jones built a national cohort on the event in the candidate's own database), leaving only an un-chosen direction, which is the excluded "no one thought of it" | Partial (A1) / Unresolved (A2)
8 | Dissolution — "retraction" is not one object (deletion, inactivation, resolved code, episode-type change, "history of"), it is reversible, and the primary endpoint may collapse into the fallback | Jones confirms fragmentation and reversibility empirically (both resolved and active periods in one patient; censoring at re-prescription; resolution conventionally requiring >12 months without asthma medication, while 5,333/16,023 = 33.3% of the resolved cohort were medicated in the prior year), so the candidate's "first retraction event" treats a reversible clerical annotation as a decision, and its two endpoints are sequentially dependent in the opposite order from the one it assumes. The proposed repair (report routes separately; treat "history of" as an intermediate category) is plausible but is listed only under fecundity and is not operationalised in V2 | Partial (A1) / Partial (A2)
Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3
Strongest remaining objection: Fortis 2016 asked the candidate's question for its index pair, in the candidate's own field and its own words, and reported both of its limbs (7% diagnosis persistence, 24% treatment persistence) — and Jones 2024 then built a 16,023-patient resolved cohort (one of three 1:1:1-matched cohorts, 48,069 patients in all) on the candidate's own primary endpoint in the candidate's own primary database, pointing the arrow the other way. So the data model, the disciplinary boundary and the incentive gap that were offered as the reason for silence are all falsified from opened sources, and what is left is an un-chosen direction of an asked question rather than an un-asked one. The conditional, comparator-controlled, event-level quantity is genuinely unpublished (attack 1 Resolved by both adversaries), which is why this routes as an open problem rather than as an answered or disguised known — but that is a design upgrade on an asked question, not novelty, and A2's Unresolved on attack 7 would in any case cap it at Provisional.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): obtain Fortis et al.'s full text by a non-paywalled route (author request or interlibrary loan; rc.rcjournal.com and Sage both failed) to establish whether a windowed, label-conditional persistence rate was reported, and open the three hits left unopened for budget (medRxiv 10.1101/2025.07.16.25331678; the Pavia and Rome coeliac re-evaluation records; the Huisarts en Wetenschap items) before any further work on this question.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): ASKED and only PARTLY ANSWERED — routed. Row appended to ledger/routed-open-problems.md with Fortis et al., Respir Care 2016;61(9):1192-1200 (DOI 10.4187/respcare.04647, full text unread by anyone on this record) and Jones et al., Br J Gen Pract 2024;74(743):e364-e370 (DOI 10.3399/BJGP.2023.0271) as the sources showing the question live and the answer partial. Tier C: the estimand is crisp but nothing is computable from public sources — it needs licensed EHR data (CPRD/OpenSAFELY or a US EHR network), so the research run cannot attack it without a data application.

Verification (post-batch, 2026-10-18; full log in batches/2026-10-18-0130/VERIFICATION.md): six fresh-context readers on this entry's priors, each given one source and no reviewer reasoning. VERDICT UNCHANGED. The kill's two legs both survive, and one is better supported than it was.
- FORTIS 2016 is now unread at full text after FIVE independent attempts (two adversaries, two verifiers, one residual reader) across about 26 distinct routes, logged in VERIFICATION.md and in UQ-20261018-01-residual-fortis.md so no later pass repeats them. What the abstract does carry is both limbs verbatim: 60 of 855 (7%) persistent empiric COPD diagnosis and 208 of 855 (24%) persistent empiric treatment with bronchodilators and/or inhaled glucocorticoids. An earlier split between two readers over whether the 24% is in the abstract resolved in favour of the reader who found it. The decisive question — whether the 855 is restricted to patients already labelled COPD before the test — remains COULD NOT READ, but the abstract's inclusion wording LEANS AGAINST it: the 855 are described as all subjects with a normal PFT (473) or a restrictive defect (382), drawn from 1,805 reviewed sessions, with no stated requirement of a prior label. That lean supports this entry's own attack-1 response rather than undermining it: an unconditional denominator cannot yield the candidate's conditional retraction rate. So Gate 2 Low rests, as the entry says, on Fortis having ASKED the question and reported both limbs, not on having answered it.
- JONES 2024 verified at PDF level, with one number restated: 16,023 is the size of EACH of three 1:1:1-matched cohorts (resolved, active asthma, non-asthma), 48,069 patients in all. Resolution is the EXPOSURE, cohort-defining with the first code as index date; no rate, hazard or proportion of the asthma population coded resolved is reported, and there is no time-to-event analysis of the resolution event. The 33.3% is 5,333 of the resolved cohort EXCLUDED in a sensitivity analysis for carrying an asthma prescription in the 12 months before index; the 12-month criterion appears both as the authors' own cohort description and as the cited QOF remission definition. The endpoint dependency this entry found at Gate 4 therefore holds in a sharper form: a third of the resolved cohort fails the prescribing criterion the code is meant to follow.
- AARON 2017 verified at full text: 203 of 613 completers, 33.1% (95% CI 29.4-36.8), de-labelling by the study team under protocol, no routine-care follow-up of label or medication. One internal inconsistency in the source: its discussion is reported to say more than 90% of those ruled out stayed off medication for a year, where 181 of 203 is about 89%.
- RIMAWI 2013 verified at PDF level and this entry's denominator is right as written (20 of 55 readmitted, not of the 150 tested; only 55 of 150 returned within a year). Caution for a later reader: the paper's own tables disagree with its text twice, including on beta-lactam receipt (40% against 63%), and this entry's 63% matches one of the two inconsistent figures.
- SPOTO, arXiv:2506.14669 verified at PDF level, and "code decay" in that paper does not mean what the phrase suggests: it is loss of diagnostic SPECIFICITY (specific codes giving way to non-specific ones) plus low county-to-national similarity of code-correlation matrices. Code REMOVAL is not analysed at all and no hazard or cumulative incidence is reported. It must not be cited for a code-removal hazard.
- INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION of attack 1, from three directions. A subject-first reader that started from the topic and not from any identifier found no paper measuring the rate of code removal after a disconfirming result as a time-to-event quantity with a comparator, for COPD or any other disease pair. A residual reader opened the nearest candidate — a SHEA Spring 2022 two-page conference abstract reporting penicillin-allergy reinstatement in 19 of 81 (23%) de-labelled patients over 8-16 months — and found it a single proportion with no comparator and no time-to-event analysis. Both adversaries had already graded attack 1 Resolved. The conditional, comparator-controlled, event-level quantity is unpublished.
- TWO PRIORS NOBODY HAD FOUND, both added to the routing row. Arnold NR et al., "Inhaled Medication Use in Smokers With Normal Spirometry", Respir Care 2021;66(4):652-660, doi 10.4187/respcare.08016, in COPDGene: 541 of 4,303 (12.6%) on inhaled medication at enrolment, about five years of follow-up, a no-medication reference group, and it cites Fortis 2016 — the nearest longitudinal design in this literature, but its population is smokers with normal spirometry rather than patients carrying a label, and its main text reports neither diagnosis nor inhaler persistence. And Fortis 2013, BMC Pulm Med 13:68: 155 obese patients, 33.9% (21 of 62) with normal spirometry kept obstructive-disease medications — the same manoeuvre by the same author three years earlier, in a different population.

---
ID: UQ-20261018-02
Date: 2026-10-18
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): Medicine — obstetrics / intrapartum care (target field, whose literature decides novelty and whose guideline bodies would act). Method-owning neighbours: measurement-error biostatistics (coarsened/heaped-data likelihoods), longitudinal methodology (informative observation processes), metrology.

Question (canonical): In a labour-curve dataset with per-examination dilatation records (Consortium on Safe Labor, WHO BOLD, or LaPS), under (i) an error model for digital cervical dilatation estimated from paired same-time-point measurements — replicate independent examiners primary, an instrumented/ultrasound reference secondary — comprising an error variance (as a function of true dilatation), examiner random effects and an explicit whole-centimetre coarsening process, and (ii) a jointly fitted informative-observation-time model for the examination schedule: (a) what is the shift in the median and 95th-centile dilatation-versus-time curves and in the implied action line, stated relative to the published naive fit and to that fit's own confidence bands; (b) what proportion of recorded labour-dystocia / failure-to-progress diagnoses change classification under the error-corrected curve at the published threshold, applied mechanically as written; and (c) how do (a) and (b) decompose between the measurement-error and observation-timing components? Measurand declaration is load-bearing: true dilatation is defined procedurally as the maximal internal os diameter an examiner using a stated standardised technique and examination pressure would obtain. (V1 intake form and the reasoning for the one permitted Gate 1 reformulation: batches/2026-10-18-0130/UQ-20261018-02-record.md.)

Alternative formulations: (1) If cervical dilatation were measured without examiner error, would the partogram's action line and the diagnosis of failure to progress move, and for how many women? (2) Is "slow labour" partly an artefact of how dilatation is measured rather than of how labour proceeds?

Motivating gap: Presupposition inversion. Modern labour curves (Zhang/CSL; WHO Labour Care Guide) and the dystocia thresholds read off them are built entirely from digital estimates of dilatation. The untested presupposition is that digital assessment is a measurement whose error is small relative to the between-woman variation the curves describe. Error magnitudes have been published since 1995 and are routinely cited as a limitation; nothing found propagates an error model back into a labour-curve dataset. Two features make the error non-classical: records are almost exclusively whole centimetres (coarsening, not Gaussian noise) and examinations are more frequent when progress is doubted (informative observation times). Anchors to a live anomaly — the partograph's alert/action lines have near-null diagnostic accuracy for severe adverse birth outcomes, with no accepted explanation.

Presuppositions: (1) A reference substantially more accurate than digital examination exists — CONTESTED; load-bearing for the secondary route only, since replicate examiners are primary. (2) The error distribution is estimable — CONTESTED; rounding toward decision-relevant values (9 cm, "fully") is differential and only weakly identified, declared as a bounded sensitivity analysis, not a fitted term. (3) Examination times are accurately recorded and the schedule conditionally ignorable — CONTESTED and probably false; modelled explicitly, which is why limb (c) exists. (4) Whole-centimetre digit preference is present and measurable in the source data — NOT VERIFIED by Gate 2 or by either adversary; a step-0 data check. (5) Dystocia thresholds are applied as written, so reclassification counts mean something clinically — CONTESTED; limb (b) narrowed to a mechanical count, clinical meaning declared a separate interpretive step. (6) "True dilatation" is well defined at a time point for a deformable cervix — handled by the procedural measurand declaration.

What would count as an answer: Two linked deliverables under a pre-declared plan. (i) An error model for digital dilatation fitted to paired same-time-point measurements in labouring women — replicate examiners (primary) or digital versus reference instrument (secondary) — large enough to estimate error variance as a function of true dilatation, examiner random effects and the coarsening process, with the measurand stated. (ii) Re-estimation of a published labour-curve dataset under that error model and under an informative-observation-time model, reporting the curve and action-line shifts, the dystocia reclassification proportion, and the decomposition between the two artefacts. A negative answer is pre-committed as a result: movement entirely within the published fit's own confidence bands answers the question negatively and retires the field's commonest standing objection to partogram-based dystocia diagnosis.

Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 29 distinct queries across three independent agents — 11 at Gate 2, 8 new Disguise queries by adversary 1, 9 new queries by adversary 2; full lists with per-query results in batches/2026-10-18-0130/UQ-20261018-02-record.md, -adversary-1.md and -adversary-2.md. Most informative: "measurement error in cervical dilatation assessment effect on labor curve dystocia diagnosis" (mandatory own-field obvious title) → no methodological paper; dilatation-meter patents, a cervicometry trade piece, a vendor white paper, the Phelps phantom record. "proportion of 'failure to progress' diagnoses misclassified due to cervical examination error reclassified caesarean" (mandatory fraction limb) → two overdiagnosis-of-dystocia items, both quantifying overdiagnosis against CLINICAL criteria, both NOT OPENED by Gate 2 or by either adversary — recorded as an unrun check, not as a check that passed. "errors-in-variables ... rounded heaped longitudinal measurements informative observation process" (method-owning field) → the method family is mature and named (informative-visiting-process mixed models; Bayesian heaping mixtures) with no obstetric application. "'cervical dilatation' digit preference rounding whole centimetre heaping" and adversary 2's Whipple-index sweep → no obstetric heaping analysis of dilatation records anywhere; presupposition 4 unverified by all three agents. "two independent examiners paired simultaneous vaginal examination labour cervical dilatation agreement" (adversary 1) → no study found in which two examiners independently digitally examine the same labouring woman at the same time point. "state-space hidden Markov latent cervical dilatation noisy observations labour progress" (adversary 2) → empty; the vocabulary a disguised version would most likely inhabit. "sonopartogram labour curve ... compared digital examination" (adversary 1) → sonopartogram validation and an Ain Shams comparison (opened: dilatation VE vs transperineal US r = 0.8601); agreement only, no curve, no reclassification count. Adversary 1's French sweep surfaced Hanidu et al. 2024 Acta Obstet Gynecol Scand (OPENED): 147 paired DVE/TPUS observations in labouring women, 80.3% within 1 cm, mean difference -0.925 cm, ICC 0.85, DVE "not standardized in respect of anteroposterior or transverse measurements", no propagation into any curve or diagnosis. Both adversaries' P1-hunt queries surfaced a BJOG 2022 letter exchange on P1 that Gate 2 missed (Zhang, Troendle, Souza, Oladapo, doi:10.1111/1471-0528.17221, and a de Vries reply); all mirror routes returned metadata only, bodies COULD NOT READ. Access routing: publisher-first; no PMC or Europe PMC route attempted. P1's full text COULD NOT READ by any agent (doi.org and Wiley routes CLIENT_ERROR).

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources): P1 — de Vries BS, McDonald S, Joseph FA, Morton R, Hyett JA, Phipps H, McGeechan K. "Impact of analysis technique on our understanding of the natural history of labour: a simulation study." BJOG 2021;128(11):1833-1842, doi:10.1111/1471-0528.16719 (abstract record opened at researchers.westernsydney.edu.au; full text COULD NOT READ). Unit: one simulated labour (500,000 per dataset). Endpoint: recovered summary curve, median and 95th-centile transit times. Comparator: the simulation's own known generating truth. Estimand: bias of each ANALYSIS METHOD, and its dependence on examination frequency. P2 — Mulatya CM. "Novel Methods for Analyzing Longitudinal Data with Measurement Error in the Time Variable." PhD dissertation, University of South Carolina, 2016, scholarcommons.sc.edu/etd/3496 (opened). Unit: one labouring woman in CSL. Endpoint: transit times, prospective labour curve. Comparator: naive models taking hospital arrival as true labour onset. Estimand: curve parameters corrected for measurement error in the TIME axis. P3 — Phelps JY, Higby K, Smyth MH, Ward JA, Arredondo F, Mayer AR. "Accuracy and intraobserver variability of simulated cervical dilatation measurements." Am J Obstet Gynecol 1995;173(3 Pt 1):942-945, doi:10.1016/0002-9378(95)90371-2 (opened; independently re-surfaced by adversary 2). Unit: one measurement by one examiner (1,574 measurements, 102 providers). Endpoint: 56.3% exact, 89.5% within ±1 cm; intraobserver variability. Comparator: known inner diameter of PVC pipes. Estimand: digital-examination accuracy and reliability against a physical gold standard. Supporting, opened, not graded as nearest: Roper JC et al., Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol 2023;280:154-159, doi:10.1016/j.ejogrb.2022.11.026 (369 clinicians, known-size circles; Discussion states a 1.4 cm error "could change the decision-making process" — verified verbatim 2026-10-18 — and computes nothing downstream. Verification adds that the 1.4 cm is 20% of the study's mean index-finger length of 7.2 cm, defined as an accuracy threshold in the Methods and applied to dilatation as a HYPOTHETICAL, not a measured dilatation error; the paper's own measured figures are 7 cm circle 17.1% exact and 60.4% within 1 cm, mean -1.24 cm, and 9 cm circle 29.6% and 81.3%, mean -0.57 cm); Hanidu et al. 2024 Acta Obstet Gynecol Scand (adversary 1, opened; 147 paired in-labour DVE/TPUS observations, states imprecise assessment "can contribute to variable clinical decisions", models nothing).

Novelty — how this differs from each: vs P1 (the closest, and the reason this is not High) — P1's artefact is the ESTIMATOR, the candidate's is the MEASUREMENT: P1 feeds error-free simulated dilatations to two curve-fitting methods and asks how the methods distort a known truth; the candidate feeds error-laden real dilatations to a model that represents the error. Differs on all four attributes (unit: simulated labour vs real woman in CSL/BOLD/LaPS; endpoint: method bias vs curve shift against the published fit's bands plus a reclassification count; comparator: simulation truth vs the published naive fit; estimand: analysis-method bias vs measurement- and observation-process-attributable share, decomposed). P1 varies examination FREQUENCY, a design parameter, not an INFORMATIVE observation process, a dependence between schedule and latent state — only the latter biases the curve at fixed frequency. Residual risk, named not hidden: P1's methods are unread by all three agents, so whether its simulation injects a dilatation-error term is unverified; if it does, limb (a) becomes a real-data instance of a simulated result and only (b) and (c) remain novel. vs P2 — same dataset family and same correction-technique family, ORTHOGONAL AXIS: P2 corrects error in time (unknown onset), the candidate corrects error in dilatation; P2 has no examiner error, no coarsening process, no informative visit process and no action-line or reclassification output. P2 is evidence of feasibility, not a kill — and its death in an unpublished dissertation is the silence mechanism's best exhibit. vs P3 — supplies an input the candidate needs and stops one step short: a phantom study, not a labouring cervix, reporting categorical accuracy rates rather than an error distribution conditional on true dilatation, with no examiner random effects and no fitted rounding process, so it cannot be propagated as it stands. Its own conclusion flags relevance "when evaluating dysfunctional labor" and computes nothing downstream.

Novelty confidence: Medium
Grounds: 29 distinct queries across eight vocabulary families including both mandatory queries, three nearest priors opened with all four attributes stated, and two independent adversarial sweeps (French, Spanish, German, Nordic, psychophysics, quantitative bias analysis, centile deconvolution, demographic heaping, state-space/latent-variable, sonopartogram, BJOG correspondence) that found no formulation fitting an error model to paired dilatation measurements and propagating it into a labour-curve dataset — including in the method-owning field's own words. Not High: P1 occupies the same question-shape in the same field and journal, and a reasonable reader could regard the candidate as P1's next instalment. Not Low: no prior does the limb on any of the four attributes. Asked-but-open on the strict reading: NO for the quantitative form, but the implication is voiced and declined three times across 29 years (Phelps 1995, Roper 2023, Hanidu 2024) — the noted-but-not-asked border, and the ground of the surviving objection below.

Significance — consequence: If YES (error and informative timing account for a large share), the published 95th centiles are inflated and the shape partly flattened by examiner noise and coarsening, so the Labour Care Guide's per-centimetre expected durations and any action line derived from them are calibrated partly to the instrument rather than to labour; the implied response is not a recalibrated threshold but a different measurement or a decision rule robust to ±1 cm, and a share of caesareans for dystocia becomes attributable to examination error — a quantity no one has. If NO (movement inside the published fit's own bands), the commonest standing objection to partogram-based dystocia diagnosis is quantitatively retired, attention is redirected to the real source of the alert/action lines' near-null accuracy, and the clinical case for instrumented cervicometry — currently resting on agreement statistics alone — is substantially weakened. Both directions change a decision.

Significance — audience: (1) WHO's intrapartum-care guideline group and the national bodies setting dystocia criteria against these curves (NICE; ACOG/SMFM) — they would learn whether their thresholds are calibrated to examiner noise, and the answer decides whether the fix is a threshold, a measurement or a robust rule. (2) The CSL, BOLD and LaPS analysis teams, who hold the data and already run interval-censored and threshold-regression machinery (P2 proves access and feasibility). (3) Manufacturers and regulators of instrumented cervicometry — an active device trial (DilaCheck, NCT03440723) and the sonopartogram programmes are validated on agreement statistics alone, which is exactly the evidence the candidate would replace or refute. (4) Measurement-error and informative-visit biostatisticians. Audience reality is evidenced, not asserted: both adversaries independently found that Zhang, Troendle, Souza and Oladapo — the CSL/BOLD/WHO-LCG author set, i.e. audiences 1 and 2 — published a signed BJOG letter (2022;129(11):1939-1940) answering a correspondence attack on exactly this question-shape, with a de Vries reply, inside a year. Attack 6 is Resolved by both adversaries.

Significance — fecundity: Newly askable — the minimum dilatation measurement precision at which a given action line retains its stated operating characteristics, i.e. a performance specification for cervicometry devices, which currently have none; whether EXAMINER IDENTITY is an exposure in dystocia diagnosis and caesarean risk; whether part of the Friedman-versus-Zhang difference is a measurement-PRACTICE difference (examiner continuity, examination frequency, rounding convention) rather than a population or practice difference, reopening a settled historical dispute on new grounds; and whether station, effacement and position carry the same artefact into the decisions resting on them.

Significance — anchoring: The partograph's alert and action lines have near-null diagnostic accuracy for severe adverse birth outcomes and dilatation over time is a poor predictor of them, with no accepted explanation; measurement error is an obvious candidate nobody has quantified. Also anchors to unexplained inter-unit variation in caesarean-for-dystocia rates, and to P1's standing and unanswered claim that these regression methods "should not be routinely used to define labour progress", which left the field with a criticism and no replacement.

Reason for silence: Offered mechanism — a disciplinary boundary with an incentive gap on top: three communities hold the three pieces and none owns the junction (error data with phantom-study, simulation-training and device-validation groups; curve datasets with consortium epidemiology; the coarsened-error-plus-informative-visit technique with biostatistics, where it is a mature named family with no obstetric application), and the incentives run the wrong way (curve datasets' value is their descriptive authority; vendors want an agreement statistic; guideline bodies have just rebuilt their thresholds on these curves). P2 is the diagnostic case. JUDGE'S FINDING: this mechanism accounts for the missing ANSWER, not the missing QUESTION, and the ledger does not accept a non-execution mechanism. Both adversaries pressed it and neither accepted it — adversary 1 Partial, adversary 2 Unresolved — on evidence in the record's own hands plus a BJOG 2021-22 exchange showing the artefact question actively contested in the candidate's own journal. This is the reason the entry is capped.

Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status): Two independent fresh-context adversaries, each handed the Gate 0-3 record only; adversary 2 did not see adversary 1's log. Disguise was EXECUTED by both (8 new queries by A1, 9 by A2), so Disguise is not unverified for want of searching — but A1 records an Unverified residual inside it (P1's methods and the two BJOG 2022 letter bodies, COULD NOT READ by both agents), which independently blocks Validated. Full logs: batches/2026-10-18-0130/UQ-20261018-02-adversary-1.md and -adversary-2.md.

Judge's note on scores: 3/3 on V2 only (V1 scores 1/3); neither adversary found a vagueness or presupposition kill, and significance is the one dimension carried by opened evidence rather than argument. Verdict: Provisional, not Validated — adversary 2 returns Unresolved on attack 7, which is non-fatal and caps the entry at Provisional; independently, the Unverified residual inside attack 2 (P1's methods and the BJOG 2022 letter bodies, COULD NOT READ by all three agents) blocks Validated on its own. No Unresolved on attacks 1, 2 or 4 from either adversary, so this is not a Rejection; novelty is Medium with a complete and doubly-swept search record, so Gate 2 does not reject it; and no prior was found that does the limb, so it is not a disguised known.

Strongest remaining objection: The un-asked claim fails on the "un-asked" limb rather than the "unanswered" limb. The question is voiced in the field's own words three times across 29 years (Phelps 1995, Roper 2023, Hanidu 2024 — each stating a decision-making implication and declining to compute it; verification 2026-10-18 confirms all three papers exist and state such an implication, corrects two of the three attributed quotations to the papers' own wording, and establishes that NONE of the three measures digital-examination error against a labouring woman's true dilatation, comparing instead with PVC pipes, paper circles and an ultrasound comparator respectively) and the wider "how much of our picture of normal labour is a picture of how we produced it" question is actively contested in the candidate's own journal (P1 BJOG 2021, a letter from the curve authors, a reply, within a year). The only mechanism on offer for the silence explains non-execution, which this ledger expressly does not accept; on the ledger's own definitions that is the signature of an open problem — asked, unanswered, routable — rather than an un-asked question.
Promotion requires: REWRITTEN 2026-10-18 after verification showed item (1) unreachable by search and item (3) misdescribed. (1) a sourced mechanism for why the QUESTION went unasked rather than merely unanswered — a positive demonstration that the quantitative form, with an estimand, a dataset and a comparator, is absent from the field's own discourse and not merely uncomputed, which must include reading the Zhang/Troendle/Souza/Oladapo letter (doi:10.1111/1471-0528.17221, BJOG 2022;129(11):1939-1940) and the de Vries reply (no published citation established; only located identifier is the Authorea preprint doi:10.22541/au.164970189.91525293/v1) and showing neither poses it. SIX independent route-sweeps across two passes have reached nothing but landing metadata on both documents, so this item needs an interlibrary request or a subscription, not another search, and until then the cap rests on an Unverified residual — which is where it belongs; AND (2) closure of the three Unverified checks — P1's methods on a working publisher route, confirming no dilatation-measurement-error term is injected; the two overdiagnosis-of-dystocia papers from Gate 2 query 6, confirming no measurement-attributable fraction is already published; and the sonopartogram comparison papers, confirming no instrument-versus-digital progress CURVE has been built; AND (3) a replicate-measurement design that actually exists — NOT "the instrumented Hanidu-type paired-data route", which verification showed to be 147 observation pairs in 110 women taken up to 60 minutes apart (median 27.2) with digital examination as the comparator and no independent reference, so it yields no digital-examination error against truth and cannot serve as the primary route. Either same-time-point replicate digital examinations in a labouring cohort at usable scale, or a design carrying an instrumented reference standard measured simultaneously, must be demonstrated. If (1) fails, or if any check in (2) shows the question posed with an estimand or the quantity already computed, the entry is Rejected as asked-but-open (or as a disguised known) and routed to ledger/routed-open-problems.md, not promoted.

Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): Read P1's methods on a working publisher route and settle whether any dilatation-error term is present, and read the BJOG 2022 letter pair; then verify presupposition 4 by tabulating recorded dilatation values in one labour-curve dataset to confirm whole-centimetre coarsening and look for heaping at 9 cm.

UQ-20261016-32, UQ-20261017-18, UQ-20261016-42, UQ-20261017-39); no single entry duplicates this one, but the family-level redundancy warrants a curator decision.

Verification (post-batch, 2026-10-18; full log in batches/2026-10-18-0130/VERIFICATION.md): eight fresh-context readers across three passes. VERDICT UNCHANGED — Validated stays barred independently by Gate 5's "Medium novelty with a close neighbor" (P1, whose methods are unread) and by the Unverified residual inside attack 2, so the entry is at its floor and no late Gate 4 is owed.
- A CORRECTION TO THIS PASS, NOT TO THE RECORD. My first three briefs for this entry's priors were written from the labels in the adversarial log rather than from the full citations the entry carries, and each asked whether its paper states an implication for "labour-progress curves or dystocia thresholds", which is not what this entry claims of any of them. The resulting finding that "Roper 2023" could not be located is VOID: it exists, exactly as cited — Roper JC, Naidu M, Thakar R, Sultan AH, "Getting the size right: Are clinicians ready for it?", Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol 2023;280:154-159, doi 10.1016/j.ejogrb.2022.11.026 — and the first reader simply had no identifier to start from. It is NOT a fourth unlocatable citation on this ledger. A re-check against the real identifiers produced the findings below.
- TWO OF THE THREE ATTRIBUTED QUOTATIONS ARE PARAPHRASES PRESENTED AS QUOTATIONS. Phelps: the abstract's conclusion reads "Intraobserver variability is >50% and is an important consideration when evaluating dysfunctional labor", not "relevant when evaluating dysfunctional labor". Hanidu: the Discussion reads "An imprecise evaluation of cervical dilatation can contribute to variability in clinical decisions within obstetrics", not "can contribute to variable clinical decisions". Both are corrected in place above. The substance of attack 7's point survives in both cases — each paper does state a decision-making implication and compute nothing downstream — but a quotation mark is a claim about wording, and these two were not the papers' wording. Roper's quote IS verbatim, found once in the Comment section.
- ROPER'S 1.4 cm IS NOT A MEASURED DILATATION ERROR. It is 20% of the mean index-finger length in the study (7.2 cm), defined as an accuracy threshold in the Methods and then applied to dilatation in the Comment as a hypothetical. The paper's own measured dilatation figures, which this record did not have, are worth carrying: for the 7 cm circle 17.1% exactly correct (63 of 369), 60.4% within 1 cm, mean signed difference -1.24 cm (95% CI -1.37 to -1.13); for the 9 cm circle 29.6% (109 of 369), 81.3% within 1 cm, mean -0.57 cm (-0.69 to -0.45). No women were examined: the materials were paper tape, a 3.5 cm sphincter model and paper-cut circles.
- HANIDU'S PAIRS ARE NOT SAME-TIME-POINT, AND THIS IS A REAL DEMOTION. The Methods exclude data where "the interval between the DVE and TPUS assessments exceeded 60 min", and TPUS followed DVE at a median of 27.2 minutes (range 4-50). This entry's attack-4 response offered those 147 pairs as the instrumented route "already instantiated with real data", on the strength of their being same-time-point; over a window of up to an hour, cervical dilatation can genuinely change, so the pairs conflate measurement discrepancy with real progression and the instrumented route is less evidenced than the response claimed. Presupposition 4 is correspondingly weaker, not stronger. What the record got right: the intra-observer spread it cites (LOA -0.29 to 0.30 cm, ICC 0.995) is indeed instrument repeat-measurement — one observer re-measuring saved 2D cine-loops about ten days apart — and the paper reports a second reading too (LOA -0.31 to 0.28, ICC 0.996).
- THE PATTERN ACROSS ALL THREE VOICINGS, which is the most useful thing this pass found. None of the three papers measures digital-examination error against a labouring woman's TRUE dilatation: Phelps compares examiners' proprioception with the inner diameter of PVC pipes (1,574 measurements, 102 examiners, 56.3% exact and 89.5% within 1 cm, exactly as recorded), Roper compares estimates with paper-cut circles, and Hanidu uses digital examination as the COMPARATOR for ultrasound and never validates it against anything. Hanidu reports no digital-examination reproducibility figure of its own. So the field has repeatedly characterised the instrument against surrogate references and never against the quantity the curves are built from — which is the candidate's point, and also the reason its primary identification route stays unevidenced.
- THE SECOND LEG OF THE CAP IS UNREAD AFTER SIX ROUTE-SWEEPS. Not one word of either BJOG 2022 letter body has been read by anyone: Authorea, ESSOAr and a third mirror expose landing metadata only, and doi.org, Wiley and PubMed failed in every pass. The de Vries reply has no established published citation; its only located identifier is the Authorea preprint doi 10.22541/au.164970189.91525293/v1. So "actively contested in the candidate's own journal" rests on titles and metadata, which is an Unverified residual and caps at Provisional in its own right.
- P1 REMAINS UNREAD AT FULL TEXT after five attempts, and OpenAlex reports no open-access copy anywhere. But the Crossref structured abstract, reached on the residual pass, settles the paper's own framing, which is what this entry's novelty distinction turns on: it tests whether polynomial and interval-censored regression can detect an ACCELERATION PHASE, and what it manipulates is the data-generating model (Friedman parameters against a progressively increasing rate), the analysis method, the examination frequency and the dilatation level at which results are read. Its reported bias is method-against-truth — a two-fold overestimation of the mean 4-6 cm dilatation rate by the polynomial method — not a measurement-attributable share, and a ResearchGate summary adds that it found no description of simulated measurement error. The distinction "P1's artefact is the ESTIMATOR, the candidate's is the MEASUREMENT" is therefore evidenced from the paper's own abstract rather than assumed, while remaining formally unverified. Routes left untried: the Wiley PDF and full-xml URLs Crossref lists, and a Western Sydney record labelled "authors reply 5".

Domain(s): Medicine — procedural specialties (surgery, interventional cardiology, endoscopy); credentialing/privileging; health systems. Source method: cross-field transplant from aviation currency rules. Method-owning neighbours: health economics (human-capital depreciation), operations management (organizational forgetting), surgical education (skill decay).

Question (canonical): In ONE named registry with operator identifiers and dated per-operator case histories, fitting patient outcome on a pre-declared recency exposure (log days since that operator's previous case of the same procedure; counts in the preceding 30 and 90 days) with operator fixed effects and adjustment for trailing-365-day and cumulative volume, case mix and calendar time: (a) is the recency coefficient distinguishable from zero, and (b) taking the fitted outcome at the shortest pre-declared gap stratum as each operator's own reference, at what gap length (with CI) does fitted expected outcome degrade by a pre-stated absolute risk difference, or is no such gap identified within observed support? (V2; V1 — which referenced "that operator's own best performance" and left registry, outcome and margin unnamed — is in the record, the one permitted Gate 1 reformulation.)

Alternative formulations:
- Do proceduralists lose measurable skill between cases, and how fast — is there an empirical half-life of procedural competence visible in patient outcomes?
- Is "currency" (recency of practice), the quantity aviation licenses on, an identifiable determinant of patient outcome in procedural medicine, separable from case volume?

Motivating gap: Aviation licenses on recency (landings in 90 days, rolling instrument approaches) regardless of lifetime hours; medicine privileges on cumulative/annual volume and time-limited certification. The submitted claim that medicine "contains no recency term anywhere" is FALSE as stated — Ahpra/Medical Board of Australia operate a generic *Recency of practice* registration standard (under review 2025-12-05). Surviving gap: existing recency instruments are generic, hours-based, multi-year, not procedure-specific, and not calibrated to any outcome curve. Adversary 2 added the symmetric deflation: query 4 found no published calibration of aviation's own 90-day rule to accident risk either, so the donor field does not demonstrably possess the outcome-calibrated object the transplant proposes to copy.

Presuppositions:
1. A registry holds operator IDs with dated per-operator case histories — ESTABLISHED and demonstrated in use (PHC4 Pennsylvania: surgeon licence number plus a days-since-last-procedure field, P1).
2. Operator FE plus an unrelated-procedure negative control identifies a procedure-specific recency effect — CONTESTED and evidenced against, but in a weaker form than the record claimed. The record's ground was that P1's pre-declared placebo (recency of any inpatient procedure) is non-null and LARGER than the treatment (+0.067 vs +0.032 pp/day in-hospital mortality). CORRECTION, from adversary 2's own labelled arithmetic on the record's quoted SEs: the two differ by 0.035 pp/day with SE at most sqrt(0.025^2 + 0.015^2) = 0.029 if independent, so they are NOT statistically distinguishable and the "twice the coefficient" framing is a point-estimate comparison the stated uncertainty does not support. What survives and is still load-bearing: the placebo is itself non-null (+0.067, SE 0.025), so the design as written still cannot interpret its own falsification test. Adversary 2 graded attack 4 Resolved on this correction; adversary 1, which did not re-open P1, graded it Partial.
3. Outcome measured on a timescale over which recency could act — CONTESTED for long-horizon endpoints; unproblematic for 1-day, in-hospital and 30-day mortality.
4. Case-mix adjustment adequate at operator-episode level — CONTESTED (the standing weakness of volume-outcome work; P1's checks are balance checks, not placebos).
5. Skill is the mechanism — explicitly NOT presupposed.
6. A credentialing body could act on a recency parameter — ASSUMPTION, weakly contradicted by eleven years of non-response to P1 and nine to P4, and by adversary 2's query 7 (ACCF/AHA/SCAI competence statements and privileging criteria express competence as cases/year, never as a maximum interval) and query 6 (German Mindestmengen, the world's only hard volume-threshold regime, contains no Zeitabstand term).

What would count as an answer: the V2 estimation, pre-registered, giving (i) the recency coefficient and CI conditional on volume, (ii) a negative control and falsification test whose expected-null status is defensible given P1's non-null placebo, (iii) inversion of the fitted curve into the gap length at the pre-stated margin with CI, or a demonstration that no such gap exists within observed support. A CI excluding a material effect answers negatively and is usable: it tells privileging committees not to write recency rules.

Novelty confidence: Low

Significance — consequence: if yes, a recency term enters privileging on an existing lever (volume-conditioned privileges, Ahpra's generic recency standard, state-board re-entry rules keyed to months away), and rota, locum, part-time and leave policy follow; it would also partly reinterpret the volume-outcome literature, annual volume being a smeared proxy for a rate whose recency structure nobody adjusts for. If no, a pre-stated CI excluding a material effect retires the transplant — the cheaper answer to act on. If P1's pattern holds (general activity mattering at least as much as procedure-specific activity), the implication inverts: currency would have to be defined over a bundle of activity, which no privileging form can currently express.
Significance — audience: credentialing and privileging committees, specialty boards setting volume thresholds, Ahpra/Joint Commission-type regulators, payers with volume requirements, registry custodians (NCDR, STS, NJR, GIQuIC). Deflated, and by both adversaries: P1 has sat in J Health Econ since 2014 with an 11.4% relative mortality effect in its sharpest subsample, P4 added a second positive registry in 2017, military medicine has run a "medical currency" programme since at least 2012, and the target field's own 2025 review cites neither P1 nor P2. Adversary 2 adds that the estimand the audience needs is counterfactual (what happens if a gap is prevented) while the question delivers an observational within-operator association over gaps the operator and hospital chose. The audience is real; the evidence it would act on a number is weak.
Significance — fecundity: the functional form of competence decay (P3's unanswered half-life); whether the depreciating asset is procedure-specific or general; whether team recency dominates operator recency, relocating the fix from licensing to rostering; whether recency mediates part of the volume-outcome gradient; a recency analogue for cognitive specialties; and how a regulator sets a threshold on a continuous exposure whose nearest placebo is non-null.
Significance — anchoring: the volume-outcome literature and its unexplained heterogeneity; minimum-volume credentialing and payer volume requirements; skill-decay and retraining-interval research (P3); organizational forgetting and interruption in operations management; physician re-entry regulation, a recency rule already in force with no empirical calibration.

Reason for silence: none to explain for limb (a) — it was asked twice in 2014, again in TAVI in 2017 and in hip-device duration in 2018. For the target field's ignorance, a dated disciplinary-boundary mechanism holds (filed as "human capital depreciation", "organizational forgetting", "skill decay" and "recency of practice" at each hop; Gate 2 q6 returns P1 in the method-owning field's words and q8 does not return it in the target field's; P3 cites neither P1 nor P2). For limb (b), the record's liability mechanism — a published interval becomes a discoverable standard of care — is plausible but unsourced, and both adversaries offer a simpler competing explanation: P1's precision does not support an interval (roughly 8 to 250 days at an illustrative 0.5 pp margin carrying P1's SE, adversary 1's own labelled arithmetic), which is "answering is hard", not "no one asked". Adversary 2 sharpens it to a mechanism that cuts against the candidate: competent analysts do not ask for a regulatory threshold off a non-identified exposure. Neither mechanism explains why the health economists who did ask (a) never inverted their own curve.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3
Strongest remaining objection: the question was asked and executed. P1 is limb (a) run in a named registry with operator identifiers and dated case histories, matching the candidate on unit of analysis (the patient case with operator-assigned exposure), endpoint (short-term mortality), comparator (within-operator, net of trailing annual volume) and estimand (conditional association per extra day away), and P4 was read as performing the registry-and-specialty swap the candidate proposes. CORRECTED ON VERIFICATION, 2026-10-18: P4's exposures are defined per HOSPITAL, with hospital fixed effects and operator identity apparently not observed, so it is a centre-level analogue of P1 rather than the operator-level swap, and it falsifies "no replication in another specialty" only at a different level of aggregation. P1 alone now carries the operator-level claim — and it carries it, having survived first-hand verification of its own coefficients, sample and adjustments. What is left un-asked is the inversion of a curve whose own placebo is non-null — so even the design increments may be aimed at a procedure-specific quantity that does not exist in the form the transplant assumes, and both adversaries independently graded that a disguised known rather than a new question.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): read P4 in full by the Wiley publisher route (doi:10.1002/hec.3505) to settle whether its gap exposure is per operator or per centre and whether operator fixed effects were used — the one fact that decides how much of the swap limb was already done — and then reconcile P1 against P2 before any new registry work. That reconciliation, not a fresh transplant, is where the open question sits.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): YES — asked-and-still-open on the core limb, and routed. Rejected at Gate 2 (novelty Low: the near-duplicate P1 was opened and read in full, and P4 is a registry/specialty swap of it), independently confirmed by Gate 4 attack 2 Unresolved from BOTH adversaries, which is fatal under the Gate 4 rule; the two-adversary requirement is satisfied and the second log does not disturb the Gate 2 grade. Row appended to ledger/routed-open-problems.md as: "Is the within-operator recency-outcome association real, procedure-specific rather than general, and transportable — and does any fitted curve support an interval?", open because P1 (positive per-day within-surgeon mortality association in PA CABG, no interval derived, scheduling flagged endogenous) and P2 (null on in-hospital and 30-day mortality in CA CABG) have never been reconciled, P4 adds a second positive registry, now confirmed on a working-paper read to be CENTRE-level rather than operator-level; no source derives an outcome-calibrated action interval, though Hockenberry et al. 2008 (J Human Capital 2(3):303-335, doi 10.1086/593064, read 2026-10-18) estimates 1-month mortality for CATEGORICAL day-bins of operator recency with surgeon fixed effects (CABG 3-14 days 0.008562 and 15+ 0.013499 against a 0-2 day reference on 5.03% baseline mortality; PTCA in five bins) and recommends no threshold, which is the nearest published approach to limb (b) and must be read before any attempt; and the 2025 target-field review cites neither 2014 paper. Tier B: the method is standard once the data exist, and the binding constraint is protocol-approved registry access carrying operator identifiers and dated per-operator case histories (a PHC4-style restricted extract, or NCDR/STS/NJR/GIQuIC); nothing in it is computable from public data, so the cross-registry transportability arm is nearer C.

Verification (post-batch, 2026-10-18; full log in batches/2026-10-18-0130/VERIFICATION.md): five fresh-context readers on this entry's priors, each given one source and no reviewer reasoning. VERDICT UNCHANGED, and the reason is the pass's own rule: the GROUND survived first-hand verification of its own sources while a DECORATION fell, so the objection is rewritten and no late Gate 4 is owed.
- P1 HOLDS. Every coefficient this entry quotes exists in NBER WP 20017 Table 2, full-sample column, in percentage points per day (the table note says coefficients were multiplied by 100), with surgeon, hospital and year fixed effects and log surgeon and hospital CABG volume over the 365 days to each procedure. The published abstract agrees on 188 surgeons, 56,315 CABG surgeries, Pennsylvania 2006-2010, 0.067 pp/day (2.4% relative) and 0.398 pp (11.4%) in the high-volume emergent subsample. Endogenous scheduling is flagged in two places and the findings are framed as "consistent with" rather than causal. Two qualifications: the PUBLISHED body could not be read (the Elsevier landing page returns empty, ScienceDirect blocks fetching by robots rule), so this entry's "read in full" is true of the working paper only; and the source contradicts itself on the CABG coefficient, which Table 2 flags at 5% while section 4.2 is reported to call it not statistically significant for the full sample. No interval or break-point is estimated anywhere, confirming the record.
- P4 FALLS AS THE SWAP, which is what the entry's own "Suggested first step" said would decide it. Van Gestel 2017 read at PDF level in the HEDG WP 16/27 and Bern DP 17-10 versions: TAVI, the first 860 Belgian procedures across 23 centres, 2007-2012, with days since the last TAVI genuinely an exposure (minimum 0, mean about 26, median 14), "depreciation of human capital" the paper's own term, the 0.12 and 0.07 percentage-point-per-day figures in Table 3 as 0.0012 and 0.0007, and Hockenberry and Helmchen 2014 cited. But THE EXPOSURES ARE DEFINED PER HOSPITAL and the models carry hospital fixed effects — "the 30th patient for a provider (hospital)" — with operator identity apparently not observed and no operator fixed effects. So P4 is a CENTRE-LEVEL analogue of P1, not the operator-level registry-and-specialty swap this entry called decisive, and it falsifies "no replication in another specialty" only at a different level of aggregation. One finding that cuts the candidate's way and was not in the record: the paper's Table 8 remarks that stroke risk is strongly increased once about 100 days separate procedures, which it reads as non-linearity.
- A PRIOR NOBODY HAD READ, and it bears directly on limb (b). Hockenberry JM, Lien H-M, Chou S-Y, "The Impacts of Task Repetition and Temporal Breaks in Production on Human Capital and Productivity", Journal of Human Capital 2008;2(3):303-335, doi 10.1086/593064 — cited as reference 15 of P2 and discussed in WP 20017. Taiwan National Health Insurance, PTCA n = 107,747 and CABG n = 20,798, 1-month mortality, with year, county, hospital AND SURGEON fixed effects and log 12-month surgeon and hospital volume. IT ESTIMATES MORTALITY FOR CATEGORICAL BINS OF DAYS SINCE THE SURGEON'S LAST PROCEDURE: CABG 0-2 days as reference against 3-14 and 15+; PTCA 0-2 against 3-7, 8-14, 15-21 and 22+. Full-fixed-effects coefficients on 1-month mortality: CABG 3-14 = 0.008562 (5%), CABG 15+ = 0.013499 (5%), PTCA 15-21 = 0.006477 (5%), PTCA 22+ = 0.008565 (1%), against reference mortality of 5.03% (CABG) and 1.66% (PTCA). It recommends no day threshold. This is not an outcome-calibrated action interval — bins with coefficients are not a threshold with a confidence interval — but it is far closer to limb (b) than this entry allowed, and the claim that no source derives an interval is narrowed accordingly in the routing row.
- A CITATION-NUMBER DEFECT IN THE CHAIN. WP 20017 attributes to Hockenberry 2008 "a break from performing CABG of 3-14 days raised mortality by 11-14%", and 22% for breaks over 15 days. Neither figure appears in the extract of the 2008 paper, whose own coefficients imply about 17% for CABG 3-14 days (0.008562/0.0503) and about 27% for 15+; WP 20017 also describes the bins as 2-14 and 15+ where the 2008 tables show 3-14 and 15+. A 2014 paper misquotes its own first author's 2008 numbers. Read at summariser level from a ResearchGate copy, so the discrepancy is unreconciled rather than settled against either paper.
- P2 EXISTS; THE DETAIL THIS ENTRY QUOTES IS UNVERIFIED. Huesch 2014 confirmed at abstract level on all 56,956 isolated-CABG patients in California 2003-2005, no significant difference in hospital or 30-day mortality, about 0.5 day longer stay not robust to statistical corrections. The p = .037 and the specific skew-and-clustering wording are NOT FOUND at abstract level, and whether surgeon fixed effects were used COULD NOT BE READ. Its reference list cites Hockenberry 2008, not Hockenberry and Helmchen 2014, alongside Sfekas 2009, Carey 2008, Edelman 2010, Sinha 2008 and Blasier 2009.
- P3 VERIFIED EXACTLY AS RECORDED. de Andres Crespo 2025 read at PDF level from UCL Discovery: a narrative review of 41 articles, endpoints simulated or assessed technical performance with no included study whose endpoint is a patient outcome, "no precise timeframe for skill decay has been found" present in the retention-interval section, and a term search of the 52-entry reference list finding no Hockenberry, Helmchen or Huesch entry. The reason-for-silence mechanism built on this paper is intact.
- ADVERSARY 1'S ARITHMETIC CHECKED DIRECTLY, not taken on trust: its "roughly 8 to 250 days at an illustrative 0.5 pp margin" reproduces exactly on P1's CABG coefficient at plus or minus 2 SE, where the interval [0.002, 0.062] pp/day gives [8.1, 250.0] days; at 1.96 SE it would be [8.1, 192]. The figure is sound and its looseness is the point. If section 4.2's reading is the authors' own, the exposure is less identified still, which strengthens the adversary.
