ID: UQ-20261018-04
Date: 2026-10-18
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): Medicine — perioperative care, infection prevention, sterile processing. Method-owning neighbours: reliability engineering (usage-based service life), hospital asset/clinical engineering.
Question (canonical): In hospital systems whose instrument-tracking system records per-ITEM cumulative reprocessing-cycle counts and per-item-to-case linkage, what are the three separately-estimated associations between an item's cycle count (and calendar age) at the moment of use and (i) intraoperative malfunction or exchange of that item (item-use level); (ii) sterilisation-process failure of the load or tray containing it (load/tray level); and (iii) NHSN-defined surgical-site infection at 30 and 90 days in the case it served (case level, exposure = case max or mean item cycle count) — each adjusted for service line, surgeon, case complexity and tray type, each with a pre-declared negative-control exposure and stated minimum detectable effect? (V2; the one Gate 1 reformulation. V1 asked whether cycle count and age "predict" malfunction, sterilisation failure and SSI — one verb over three units of analysis. Novelty finding applies to both.)
Alternative formulations:
- Do reusable surgical instruments have a measurable service life in clinical use, and is current practice — retire on visible damage, or at a bench-validated cycle limit — consistent with it?
- Is the number of times an instrument set has been through decontamination a risk factor for anything that happens to the patient it is used on?
Motivating gap: Per-item cycle histories linked to cases are a by-product of barcode/RFID tracking claimed to be unused as an exposure, with contamination research concentrated on flexible endoscopes by outbreak pressure and rigid-instrument life governed by bench cycle simulations. LOAD-BEARING CORRECTION (Gate 2, extended by both adversaries): the premise is false. Yoshikawa 2019 took per-item cumulative use counts out of an RFID instrument-management-system log (34,390 operations, 2013–2017) and used them as the exposure against instrument failure; Homma 2023 compared cleaning counts and age across 69 in-use endoscopic devices; Pitschner 2007 read each catheter's reprocessing count off its barcode, joined it to the patient and blinded it to the operator.
Presuppositions: (1) item-level cycle data with per-case linkage retrievable for research — CONTESTED; item-to-operation linkage exists in at least one deployment, item-to-patient-outcome linkage unevidenced (P1's team held the key and used no patient data). (2) cycles are a meaningful wear exposure — CONTESTED and evidenced against: positive but negligible (P1, OR 1.026/use, R² 0.032), null (Homma 2023: cleanings 281 vs 261 P=0.27; age 7 vs 7 y P=0.90), inverted in the scope literature (P2, aOR 0.80). (3) intraoperative malfunction usably recorded — CONTESTED, and adversary 2 found direct evidence against: Nichol 2024 put 24 observers into 7 ORs because instrument errors are logged by manual database entry not linked to the EMR; both device-side priors used proxies (repair request; IF detector). (4) confounding by tray type, service line, surgeon addressable — CONTESTED, unresolved. (5) manufacturers' limits bench-derived — VERIFIED (reprocessing-validation lab's own end-of-life cycle-series simulation under ISO 10993-1/-15). (6) SSI attributable at individual-item level — WEAK; no prior attempts it, and limb (ii)'s wear-to-load-failure mechanism has no source on the record.
What would count as an answer: A pre-registered cohort in one or more item-level-tracking systems, cases linked to the specific trays and items used, estimating pre-declared exposures (cycle count at use; item age; cycles since inspection) against three pre-declared endpoints — OR-recorded malfunction/exchange; load or tray sterilisation-process failure (BI failure, wet pack, load recall); NHSN SSI at 30/90 days — adjusted as above, with a negative-control exposure (cycle count of an instrument type not used in that procedure) and a stated MDE per limb. Gate 1: well-posed in V2 (3/3); the OR-record endpoint is a feasibility defect in the answer-criterion, not an ill-posedness.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 29 across three agents — Gate 2 11 (cap 11, 5 fetches), adversary 1 9 (cap 9), adversary 2 9 (cap 9); both Disguise sweeps ran in full. Full lists: batches/2026-10-18-0130/UQ-20261018-04-record.md, -adversary-1.md, -adversary-2.md. Most informative: "RFID barcode surgical instrument tracking data secondary analysis research cohort usage counts hospital informatics" → P1, the decisive hit; "reusable laparoscopic instruments insulation failure number of uses instrument age association study" → Homma 2023, Sci Rep 13 (new prior, opened via DOAJ); "reprocessed single-use device number of reprocessing cycles clinical outcomes patients electrophysiology catheter reuse count safety" → Pitschner 2007 (barcode reprocessing count joined to patients, opened); "predictors of biological indicator failure wet packs sterilization load failure retrospective analysis hospital tray" → process-control events only, limb (ii) unoccupied; "'surgical site infection' risk factor instrument tray reuse history number of prior uses case-control linked instrument tracking" → nothing on point, limb (iii) unoccupied; "surgical site infection outbreak traced to specific instrument set case-control analysis which tray used in which case" → outbreak work implicates processes and episodes, never mileage. COULD NOT READ at Gate 2 (BMC Surgery 2024, 10.1186/s12893-024-02407-1) was RESOLVED by adversary 2 at doaj.org/article/bca1a96b966a4193addc9efbf323ae12: Nichol et al., observed rates of surgical instrument errors; no cycle counts, no patient outcomes; publisher full text COULD NOT READ at Gate 4 (link.springer.com/article, doi.org, bmcsurg.biomedcentral.com/articles all client-errored); READ AT FULL TEXT on verification 2026-10-18, confirming the manual-entry-not-linked-to-EMR characterisation and supplying the 1.11% notice-filing rate against a 26.16% directly observed error rate.
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
P1 (near-duplicate). Yoshikawa T et al. "Prediction of the service life of surgical instruments from the surgical instrument management system log using radio frequency identification." BMC Health Serv Res 2019;19:695. https://link.springer.com/doi/10.1186/s12913-019-4540-0 — OPENED by Gate 2 and re-verified verbatim by adversary 1. Unit: individual instrument. Exposure: per-item cumulative usage count from the RFID management-system log. Endpoint: instrument failure = issuance of a repair request. Comparator: instrument type, pairwise log-rank; no comparator arm in the logistic model. Estimand: 1.026 per additional use (verified 2026-10-18: the paper words this as a RISK, not an odds ratio, and "odds ratio" does not appear in it; 0.032 is a "coefficient of determination" of unspecified pseudo-R-squared type; Hosmer–Lemeshow p=0.117); predicted-failure thresholds 169 and 224 uses, which verification establishes are the usage counts at which the MODEL-PREDICTED failure probability passes 0.5 and 0.8 for COOPER SCISSORS specifically, from a logistic model fitted on 136 Cooper scissors for which repairs had been requested — not observed rates, not retirement limits, and not across instrument types; no instrument age or calendar time in service is modelled anywhere in the paper; Kaplan–Meier against usage count. No patient data, no SSI, no load limb.
P2. van der Ploeg K et al. "Impact of duodenoscope reprocessing factors on duodenoscope contamination." J Hosp Infect 2024;154:88–94. https://pure.eur.nl/en/publications/impact-of-duodenoscope-reprocessing-factors-on-duodenoscope-conta/ — OPENED by Gate 2 (abstract-level), not re-verified by either adversary. Unit: surveillance culture clustered by scope (307 cultures, 1,296 cycles). Exposure: reprocessing-process factors plus "usage" whose definition is UNREAD (verification 2026-10-18 reached the abstract only, where usage is not among the listed exposures; absence from an abstract is not absence from the paper, so the record's "undefined" is withdrawn). Endpoint: scope contamination. Comparator: opposite category of each dichotomised factor. Estimand: aORs — manual cleaning ≤5 min 1.61 (1.10–2.34); increased usage 0.80 (0.64–0.995).
P3. Pitschner HF et al. "Using reprocessed devices does not impair patient safety nor does it affect course of ablation." Eur Cardiovasc Dis 2007;3(1):83–8. https://www.ecrjournal.com/articles/using-reprocessed-devices-does-not-impair-patient-safety-nor-does-it-affect-course — OPENED by adversary 2. Unit: patient (202 ablations; 241 reprocessed vs 231 new catheters). Exposure: per-item reprocessing turns (1–6) "read from the barcode of the catheter", blinded to operator — but collapsed to binary new-vs-reprocessed in analysis. Endpoint: procedure and fluoroscopy time, RF deliveries, severe complications, 6-month recurrence. Comparator: new device. Estimand: none per cycle count; differences by arm only. Reprocessor was a registry partner (conflict on the record); the article's own recurrence percentages do not reconcile. (The record's third prior, Global Spine J 2019 pedicle screws, is retained in the record as an unquantified bench study with no estimand; it is displaced here by P3, which is materially closer.)
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs P1 — same exposure, same data substrate, same unit for limb (i), same policy target; differs only in endpoint (OR-recorded malfunction vs repair request) and in having limbs (ii) and (iii). Alternative formulation 1 is substantially P1's title, so P1 is a near-duplicate of a recorded formulation and a direct falsifier of the motivating gap, not an adjacent-object miss. vs P2 — different device class, unit (culture) and endpoint (post-reprocessing contamination), and the usage covariate runs the other way; matters as evidence against presupposition 2's sign and as proof that usage is already a routine covariate next door. vs P3 — the candidate's exact data manoeuvre (per-item barcode reprocessing history joined to the patient) executed in 2007 in another device class; differs in estimand (binary arm, no cycle-count exposure–response) and endpoint (procedural complications, recurrence; not SSI, not load failure). The surviving residue is an ENDPOINT swap on an asked question, not a new question.
Novelty confidence: Low
Significance — consequence: Positive limb (i) at the OR-record endpoint would index retirement to usage rather than to visible damage or a bench ceiling; positive limb (ii) would put tray history into ST79-governed process control; positive limb (iii) would be the first patient-level consequence attached to an individual item's biography; a tight null on (iii) would be the first measured counter to single-use advocacy argued from mechanism. Discounted by P1 and Homma: limb (i)'s direction is already known to be positive-but-negligible or null, so its consequence is generalisation and re-endpointing, not establishment.
Significance — audience: Real and identifiable — sterile-processing departments and tracking-system vendors; AAMI ST79 and AORN committees; manufacturers and their reprocessing-validation laboratories, whose maximum-lifetime claims are set by simulated cycle series and would gain a field comparator; infection preventioners and NHSN teams for limb (iii); value-analysis committees. Costed decision on the record (Nichol 2024's own estimate of lost charges from instrument errors), and the sustainability literature is independently measuring lifespan in uses (ESCRS 2025). Discount: their current lever is inspection, not usage-indexed retirement, and limb (iii)'s audience is the weakest.
Significance — fecundity: Is cycles-since-inspection a better exposure than lifetime cycles (is the hazard reset by maintenance)? Does the wear hazard differ by instrument class (hinged, lumened, powered, robotic)? Can usage-indexed retirement be cost-compared against single-use conversion on the same data? Does the tracking system's own definition of a "cycle" (scan at decontamination vs assembly vs issue) move the estimate?
Significance — anchoring: Single-use-versus-reusable debate (argued on mechanism and cost, not per-item outcomes); duodenoscope reprocessing literature where usage is already a covariate with a surprising sign; the unexplained residual in SSI risk models; the reliability-engineering question of whether a reprocessed instrument is a repairable system whose hazard is reset by maintenance.
Reason for silence: Fails for the question as graded. For limb (i) there was no silence: it was asked and answered in 2019 from the candidate's own named data, and again in 2023. For limbs (ii)/(iii) the offered mechanism — separate custodians for the tracking log and for the EHR/NHSN surveillance, no routine item-to-patient join key, plus outbreak-driven attention to endoscopes — explains why answering is hard rather than why nobody asked, and adversary 2 falsified it by example: Pitschner crossed that boundary in 2007 by hand, with a barcode and a data-collection sheet, where a commercial-regulatory controversy made it worth asking. The honest residue (no reprocessing industry whose licence depends on the answer for rigid instruments, sterilisation treated as a validated kill step) sits close to "the field believes the answer is known", which Gate 4 disallows.

Strongest remaining objection: The candidate is a disguised known. Its load-bearing premise — that a tracking system's per-item cumulative reprocessing count has never been used as an exposure — was read at Gate 2 as falsified three times in the candidate's own and neighbouring device literatures. CORRECTED ON VERIFICATION, 2026-10-18: only ONE of the three actually does it. Yoshikawa 2019 does use a tracking-system per-item count as an exposure, but for Cooper scissors alone and with no age limb; Homma 2023 never says its cleaning counts came from a tracking system and is 69 instruments with 8 events, univariate, with no effect size; and Pitschner 2007 recorded the per-item count off the barcode and then collapsed it to two arms with no per-cycle estimate anywhere. Gate 2 Low does not turn on the count of falsifications — the candidate's own alternative formulation 1 is substantially Yoshikawa's title, and that is what carries it — but the premise is falsified once, not three times. Originally stated as falsified in (Yoshikawa 2019, verified on the publisher page by two agents, which is also substantially alternative formulation 1 in its title; Homma 2023; Pitschner 2007, which joined per-item barcode reprocessing counts to patient outcomes nineteen years before intake), and the residue limbs (ii) and (iii) are an endpoint swap on that asked question rather than a new question. Novelty is Low, which rejects at Gate 2 irrespective of the Gate 4 table; independently, adversary 2's Unresolved on attack 7 would have capped the entry at Provisional, which Low novelty does not support. Secondary, non-decisive: limb (i)'s named endpoint (OR-recorded malfunction) is not reliably captured — Nichol 2024, read at full text on verification 2026-10-18, says that the historical reporting database is not integrated into the electronic medical record and that staff reporting is frequently incomplete, delayed and underreporting, with Patient Safety Notices filed on 368 of about 33,000 cases (1.11%) against a directly observed 147 of 562 cases (26.16%) carrying at least one instrument error; "not routinely recorded" was this entry's shorthand and is looser than its source, so the answer-criterion would have to be manufactured prospectively.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): Not for this ledger as formulated. If re-intaken, it must be narrowed to limbs (ii) and (iii) alone, with the "newly measurable, never used as an exposure" premise removed, a stated wear-to-cleanability or wear-to-load-failure mechanism, a real power calculation for the SSI limb, and an endpoint that exists in records; that narrowed question needs a fresh Gate 2, not this verdict. Pointer for whoever runs it: open BMC Surgery 2024 10.1186/s12893-024-02407-1 at the publisher (three routes failed; counter/pdf and link.springer.com/10.1186/... untried) and re-verify P2 independently, which neither adversary did.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): Not routed. This is a disguised-known/answered rejection, not asked-but-still-open: the service-life limb was asked AND answered (P1 reports the estimate and the retirement thresholds), so it is not an open problem for the research workstream. No row appended to ledger/routed-open-problems.md.

Verification (post-batch, 2026-10-18; full log in batches/2026-10-18-0130/VERIFICATION.md): five fresh-context readers on this entry's priors. VERDICT UNCHANGED — Gate 2 Low holds, because the candidate's own alternative formulation 1 is substantially Yoshikawa's title and the service-life question was asked and answered in the candidate's own named data substrate. But ONE LEG CARRIES IT WHERE THIS ENTRY CLAIMED THREE.
- P1 VERIFIED AT FULL TEXT, and narrower than the record implies. Yoshikawa 2019 confirmed on every bibliographic element, with the unit the individual RFID-identified instrument, the exposure a per-item usage count from the system's use and repair-request records, and failure the issuance of a repair request. All four figures exist. Three qualifications: the paper words 1.026 as a RISK per additional use and the phrase "odds ratio" does not appear in it; 0.032 is a "coefficient of determination" whose pseudo-R-squared type is unspecified; and 169 and 224 are the usage counts at which the MODEL-PREDICTED failure probability passes 0.5 and 0.8, FOR COOPER SCISSORS SPECIFICALLY — not observed rates, not retirement limits, and not across instrument types. The logistic model's sample is described as 136 Cooper scissors for which repairs had been requested, leaving it unclear how non-failed items enter. And NO instrument age or calendar time in service is modelled anywhere, so this candidate's age limb has no counterpart in P1 at all. Kaplan-Meier with pairwise log-rank across five types (n = 35, 28, 20, 58, 28) confirmed.
- HOMMA 2023 VERIFIED, and it is far weaker than a near-duplicate. Both p-values are real as recorded (cleanings median 281, IQR 261-323, in failed against 261, IQR 179-320, in intact, P = 0.27; period of use 7 years, IQR 6-8, against 7, IQR 4-8, P = 0.90). But the whole study is 69 instruments with 8 insulation failures (11.6%), tested univariately by Wilcoxon rank-sum with NO effect size, NO confidence interval and NO multivariable model; the variable is "period of use" in years rather than instrument age as such; and THE PAPER NEVER SAYS THE CLEANING COUNTS CAME FROM A TRACKING SYSTEM — no barcode, log or system is mentioned. No instrument is linked to any patient or case.
- PITSCHNER 2007 VERIFIED AT FULL TEXT, and it confirms this entry's own careful reading rather than the stronger claim made of it elsewhere in the entry. The per-item reprocessing count of 1 to 6 WAS recorded and read from the catheter's barcode. But it was NEVER USED AS AN EXPOSURE: the analysis is new against reprocessed as two arms by t-test and Fisher's exact, with no per-cycle estimate, regression or trend anywhere, and the only cycle-indexed data are the reprocessor's own scrap rates. 202 interventions, 241 reprocessed and 231 new catheters, six-month follow-up, all as recorded. The internal inconsistency the record noticed is confirmed: the reprocessed arm is printed at 6.9% where its stated counts give 6 of 102, or 5.9%. And the conflict of interest is worse than the record said — the article page carries NO formal conflict-of-interest or funding statement at all, while the reprocessor is Remed GmbH of the VANGUARD group, the register is jointly VANGUARD and Kerckhoff-Klinik Bad Nauheim, and the article is reproduced with permission from the European Association for Medical Device Reprocessing.
- SO THE THREE-FOLD FALSIFICATION IS ONE DIRECT INSTANCE PLUS TWO WEAKER NEIGHBOURS, corrected in place above. Only Yoshikawa actually uses a tracking-system per-item count as an exposure, for one instrument type, with no age limb; Homma's count provenance is unstated and its study is 8 events; Pitschner captured the per-item count and then collapsed it. Gate 2 Low does not turn on the count of falsifications, so the verdict is unaffected.
- NICHOL 2024 WAS READ AT FULL TEXT HERE, which the batch could not do (it records link.springer.com, doi.org and bmcsurg.biomedcentral.com all client-errored). This entry's load-bearing characterisation is CONFIRMED essentially verbatim: the paper says the historical reporting database is not integrated into the electronic medical record, and that staff reporting is frequently incomplete, delayed and underreporting. What the paper does not say in these words is that malfunction "is not routinely recorded", which was this entry's shorthand at one point and is corrected in place above. Two figures worth carrying: Patient Safety Notices were filed on 368 of about 33,000 cases (1.11%), against a directly observed 147 of 562 cases (26.16%) with at least one instrument error, 44 of the 236 errors being broken or poorly functioning instruments — so an observed malfunction rate does exist, from trained observers rather than from records. Table 6 (232 errors) disagrees with Table 2 and the text (236).
- P2 FIGURES CONFIRMED, ONE CHARACTERISATION SOFTENED. van der Ploeg 2024 read at abstract level (the Erasmus Pure PDF, the Elsevier route and the journal site all failed). Both adjusted odds ratios are in the abstract exactly as recorded, with 307 cultures of which 58 (18.9%) were contaminated, over 1,296 reprocessing cycles from February 2022 to December 2023. But "usage" is not among the abstract's listed exposures and ITS DEFINITION COULD NOT BE READ, so the record's "undefined usage" is corrected to "definition unread" — absence from an abstract is not absence from a paper. The grouping variable of the logistic mixed-effects model is not stated either, so clustering by scope is unconfirmed.

ID: UQ-20261018-05
Date: 2026-10-18
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): Medicine — infusion therapy and vascular access; hospital pharmacy (injectable admixture characterisation); nursing/patient safety. Method owner: survival biostatistics (nested/shared frailty, variance partition) and prediction-model calibration.
Question (canonical): In hospital systems where infusate history is attributable to a SPECIFIC peripheral IV catheter (line-level administration documentation or validated pump-to-line association), fitting a cause-specific nested frailty survival model for catheter failure with random effects for patient, inserter, ward and device lot plus a per-admixture infusate term: (a) on the log-hazard scale, what is the variance partition coefficient of the infusate component for each failure mode (phlebitis, infiltration/extravasation, occlusion, dislodgement, infection), with an interval — a declared DESCRIPTIVE decomposition, any causal reading of "attributable" demoted to a secondary analysis under a stated identification strategy for confounding by acuity; and (b) does the incumbent binary access rule (osmolarity above ~600 mOsm/L, or pH outside ~5–9, implying central access) discriminate and calibrate against (i) the fitted infusate-attributable hazard and (ii) extravasation injury as a co-primary endpoint, as well as an index estimated from the same data under internal–external cross-validation across systems? (V2; the one Gate 1 reformulation. V1 and the reason for reformulation are in batches/2026-10-18-0130/UQ-20261018-05-record.md.)
Alternative formulations: (1) Is the peripheral-versus-central access decision rule calibrated against the catheter failures it exists to prevent? (2) How much of peripheral IV failure is caused by what was put through the line rather than by the line, the patient, the inserter or the ward?
Motivating gap: Silence mapping. PIVC insertion is the commonest invasive hospital procedure and ~a third to a half of catheters fail before therapy completes; the literature is dense with "how" (securement, dressings, replacement policy, insertion technique) and thin on the EXPOSURE, while the rule gating which drugs may enter a peripheral vein is a pair of fixed numeric thresholds reproduced across standards without field calibration against failure. Manrique-Rodríguez et al. 2021 (read in full) apply those thresholds to 307 admixtures, place 40% in the high-risk tier, and state that "human tolerance of pH and osmolarity has not been well studied" and the osmolarity threshold is "not well defined". CORRECTION at Gate 4: the record's claim that the field is "close to silent on what the exposure is" is false — Ryder et al. 2020 ran a randomised, blinded ovine trial on exactly that exposure. The gap is narrower than the record states and concerns the estimand, not the topic.
Presuppositions: (1) line-level infusate attribution — was CONTESTED, now ESTABLISHED in at least the regime V2 conditions on (Yasuda et al. 2025 attribute noradrenaline dose to specific PIVCs, 3,410 catheters, 23 ICUs); generalisation beyond critical care unevidenced. (2) failure modes recorded and distinguishable — CONTESTED; subjective phlebitis grading and reason-less removals push ascertainment error into the residual and bias the infusate VPC downward. (3) per-product pH/osmolarity retrievable — ESTABLISHED (307 measured admixtures; values move with diluent and concentration). (4) thresholds intended as failure predictions rather than conventions encoding extravasation-injury severity — was the strongest reframing available to a critic, now CORROBORATED twice from opened text (Bahl 2022: the INS list is "based on infusate osmolarity thresholds that increase the likelihood of these complications"; Ryder 2020 frames osmolarity and pH as "risk factors for midline catheter failure"); but the rule actually operationalised in practice is the INS vesicant/irritant LIST plus MAGIC compatibility, not the numeric pair, so limb (b) is partly mis-aimed as written. (5) lot and inserter recoverable as variance components — CONTESTED for lot. (6) catheter failure patient-relevant — ESTABLISHED. (7) infusate assignment not wholly confounded by acuity — CONTESTED; handled by making the primary estimand descriptive.
What would count as an answer: Pre-registered analysis in ≥2 systems with line-level attribution reporting (a) the log-hazard variance partition with the infusate share and interval, by failure mode; (b) discrimination and calibration of the incumbent rule against the infusate component and, separately, against extravasation injury; (c) an empirically derived per-admixture peripheral-vein-burden index under internal–external cross-validation; (d) the count and direction of access decisions that would flip. A small infusate share, or thresholds that already capture what there is to capture, answers it negatively — the more useful direction for standards panels.
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 29 documented queries (Gate 2: 11 + 5 fetches; adversary 1: 9 Disguise + 4 fetches; adversary 2: 9 Disguise + 5 fetches), full lists in batches/2026-10-18-0130/UQ-20261018-05-record.md and -adversary-1.md, -adversary-2.md. Most informative: "osmolarity pH thresholds predict peripheral intravenous catheter failure phlebitis validation study" (own field, mandatory title form) → risk-factor genre only, no threshold-validation study; "variance partition coefficient frailty model random effects operator ward device attributable share catheter failure" (method-owning field) → nested/shared frailty and VPC mature and named, never pointed at this object; "proportion of PIVC failures attributable to infused medications ... attributable risk estimate" (mandatory fraction query) → no published attributable share; "population attributable fraction phlebitis infused drug ... variance components nurse effect intraclass correlation catheter" (pharmacoepi, A2) → still no published share or ICC decomposition; "midline catheter osmolarity 600 mOsm pH restriction evidence outcome study catheter failure challenged" (device-class, A2) → Ryder et al. 2020 ovine midline trial, the closest prior on the exposure, MISSED by Gate 2; "静脈炎 発生率 薬剤別 pH 浸透圧 末梢静脈カテーテル 多変量解析" (Japanese, A2) → AMOR-VENUS cohort and Yasuda et al. 2025 catheter-level time-dependent multilevel Cox, MISSED by Gate 2; "antibiotics differ in their tendency to cause infusion phlebitis ... drug-specific phlebitis incidence" (A1) → Lanbeck 2002, per-antibiotic ORs over 1,386 catheters, MISSED by Gate 2; "peripheral parenteral nutrition osmolarity thrombophlebitis ... maximum tolerated osmolarity" (A1) → Dugan 2014, an osmolarity cut field-tested against phlebitis/infiltration, MISSED by Gate 2. Ledger duplicate check: INDEX.md read in full, no hits on catheter/infusion/phlebitis/vascular access; nearest entry UQ-20261016-15 (Y-site compatibility reproducibility) is a different object.
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources): P1. Ryder M, Gunther RA, Nishikawa RA, Stranz M, Meyer BM, Spangler TA, Parker AE, Sylvia C. "Investigation of the role of infusate properties related to midline catheter failure in an ovine model." Am J Health-Syst Pharm 2020;77(16):1336–1346, doi 10.1093/ajhp/zxaa175 (opened, scholarworks.montana.edu). Unit: the midline catheter in sheep (20 sheep, 40 catheters, 6 arms). Endpoint: catheter failure plus histopathological vessel-injury score. Comparator: contralateral 0.9% NaCl; test arms chosen to isolate cytotoxicity, pH and osmolarity (Clinimix 675 and 930 mOsm/L). Estimand: arm-level failure and injury rates (95% test vs 60% control (verified 2026-10-18: 19 of 20 test catheters and 12 of 20 control catheters, neither a share of sheep, and the control figure is partly an artefact of pairing because 8 of the 20 controls were removed UNFAILED when their paired test catheter failed); 4 of 6 arms met the injury criterion, the exceptions Clinimix 675 and acyclovir). P2. Yasuda H, Rickard CM, Schults JA, Marsh N, ... Abe T; AMOR-VENUS Study Group. "Impact of Noradrenaline Administration Dosage on the Occurrence of PIVC-Related Venous Phlebitis ... Time-Dependent Multilevel Cox Regression Model." Emerg Med Int 2025;2025:4457109, doi 10.1155/emmi/4457109. COULD NOT READ full text (doi.org CLIENT_ERROR; Wiley page CLIENT_ERROR; PMC12074845 excluded by environment block); citation, abstract and design read at ivteam.com. Unit: the catheter (3,410 PIVCs, 1,351 patients, 23 ICUs). Endpoint: phlebitis. Comparator/exposure: total noradrenaline dose administered via that PIVC, time-dependent. Estimand: adjusted HR, DAG-defined confounders, splines — HR 1.06 (0.93–1.20), post-hoc knee above ~6 mg. P3. Bahl A, Hijazi M, Chen N-W. "Vesicant infusates are not associated with ultrasound-guided PIVC failure." PLoS One 2022;17(1):e0262793, doi 10.1371/journal.pone.0262793 — Gate 2's COULD NOT READ is SUPERSEDED: both adversaries opened the publisher page independently. Unit: the US-guided PIVC in one trial, 257 adults. Endpoint: composite premature failure; extravasation not predefined (10 events). Comparator: pooled INS vesicant/irritant label yes/no, plus dose count. Estimand: time-dependent extended Cox aHR 1.17 (0.76–1.81), p=0.477; no random effects, no variance components, pH never mentioned and osmolarity only once in the Introduction. Also now on the record as priors, and struck from Gate 2's negatives: Lanbeck/Odenholt/Paulsen, Scand J Infect Dis 2002;34(7):512–519 (1,386 catheters, per-antibiotic phlebitis risk ordering (verification 2026-10-18 reached the abstract only, which carries NO per-drug odds ratios — just an overall antibiotic-vs-none OR of 2.34 and a regression-based sorting of named drugs into highest-risk, also-raised and not-raised groups; that ordering is still an empirically derived irritancy ranking from clinical data, so the strike holds, but "ORs" overstates what anyone has seen) — so Gate 2 query 11's "no empirically derived drug irritancy ranking from clinical data" is WRONG for antibiotics and is struck); Dugan/Le/Jew, JPEN 2014;38(7):847–851 (352 paediatric PPN patients, >1000 vs ≤1000 mOsm/L, multivariable OR 1.67). Kia et al., JMIR AI 2023;2:e48628 (pump-log infusion episodes, occlusion alarm, classifier variable importance; medication type below rate and care unit) and Manrique-Rodríguez et al., Drugs in R&D 2021;21:39–64 (307 admixtures, measured pH and osmolarity, no outcome) stand as recorded but were not independently re-verified by either adversary.
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs P1 — same exposure properties asked of the same outcome family, but in sheep not humans, midlines not PIVCs, 6 arms not 307 admixtures, with no cutoff analysis, no calibration, no variance partition, and its 675 mOsm/L arm (just above the incumbent 600 cut) not meeting the injury criterion; it also defeats the record's "the field is silent on the exposure" framing. vs P2 — the candidate's regime proven feasible (catheter-level attribution, time-dependent multilevel survival), but one drug, no physicochemistry, no pH/osmolarity, no reported variance component, VPC or frailty variance, and nothing on the access rule; the model's levels are unread, so absence of a variance component is recorded as unread, not as absent. vs P3 — the nearest approach to limb (b), but it tests a binary INS label as a covariate in one single-site cohort and reports an association, not threshold discrimination, calibration, a variance partition, or the number of decisions that would flip; it cannot support inserter, ward or lot random effects at n=257. Against Lanbeck and Dugan — per-drug ORs and a single osmolarity cut in one drug class, not a decomposition or a calibration of the incumbent rule across admixtures. No prior in any of nine vocabularies computes a variance share for catheter failure with an infusate component, a discrimination/calibration statistic for the pH/osmolarity rule, or a cross-validated competing index.
Novelty confidence: Medium — and only just; adversary 2's "Medium-minus" is accepted. Grounds: 29 queries across the candidate's own field in its own words, hospital pharmacy, standards/practitioner, the method-owning field, and (at Gate 4) preclinical toxicology, Japanese, Chinese, veterinary, neonatal, device-class and pharmacoepidemiology vocabularies; five priors opened with unit/endpoint/comparator/estimand stated; none matches either limb's estimand. Not High and not clean: Gate 2's vocabulary coverage is demonstrably incomplete — four priors (Ryder, Yasuda, Lanbeck, Dugan) were found by adversaries in vocabularies Gate 2 claimed to have swept, two of them in the field's own flagship pharmacy journal and in the candidate's own words. Not Low: no prior's estimand is the candidate's, and the one named demotion condition (a hidden pH/osmolarity secondary analysis in Bahl 2022) was discharged in the candidate's favour by both adversaries on the publisher text.
Significance — consequence: If the infusate share is substantial and the incumbent thresholds discriminate it poorly, the access rule is miscalibrated in a measurable direction and the deliverable is a replacement index with a counted number of decisions flipping both ways — drugs now barred from peripheral veins with little measured failure burden would stop generating central lines (each carrying its own thrombosis and bloodstream-infection hazard), drugs now passed would be flagged. The rule binds 40% of 307 standard adult admixtures, so recalibration moves a large traffic. A small share, or thresholds that already capture what there is, retires a recurring criticism and redirects effort to the patient, inserter and ward components. The negative is live rather than rhetorical: three cohorts (Bahl aHR 1.17; Yasuda HR 1.06; Kia's medication type below rate and care unit) all point weakly.
Significance — audience: Real, in print, and spending money on the question. INS (Standards of Practice, fixed revision cycle, where the thresholds are reproduced), AVA, the MAGIC appropriateness panel, VHP authors, ESPEN, Flebitis Zero and the 29-expert Delphi behind the tiering, hospital P&T committees writing peripheral-versus-central formulary rules, and device vendors publishing threshold-based infusate decision aids. Strongest evidence: Ryder et al. 2020 is a randomised, blinded, controlled animal trial on exactly these infusate properties, in hospital pharmacy's flagship journal, with the threshold rule's own source author (Stranz) on the byline — a community that funds an ovine RCT to probe these properties would read a human calibration.
Significance — fecundity: Opens the rate, concentration and diluent limbs (Kia found rate dominant for pump occlusion; P3's 0.45% NaCl substitution above 450 mOsm/L has no outcome evidence); whether rule-driven PICC use is net-beneficial once displaced central-line risk is counted; whether failure-mode-specific exposures differ, which would split one threshold rule into several; and whether inserter and ward components exceed the infusate component, which would re-point the securement-and-replacement programme.
Significance — anchoring: The MAGIC/VHP PICC-overuse debate; the clinically-indicated-versus-routine-replacement trial literature (outcome measured carefully, exposure unmeasured); the standing one-third-to-one-half failure rate; Bahl's published verdict that the guidelines are "vague" and the evidence "limited"; and the rule's own numeric instability (pH high-risk cut <5 or >9 in some standards, <4 or >9 in P3's tiering) in a rule applied to 40% of admixtures.
Reason for silence: WEAKENED AT GATE 4 and the binding defect of this entry. The record's primary mechanism (data-architecture boundary — the exposure does not exist in hospital records) cannot do explanatory work inside the regime V2 conditions on, because Yasuda et al. 2025 populate exactly that regime at 3,410 catheters across 23 ICUs (of which 91, 2.6%, actually received the drug) (verified 2026-10-18 as the 2025 paper's own cohort, not the Front Med 2022 cohort's 3,429 — but noradrenaline reached only 70 patients, 5.2%, through 91 PIVCs, 2.6%, so the drug-attribution analysis rests on 91 exposed catheters and one drug). The second mechanism (a disciplinary boundary, pharmacy owning the exposure and nursing the outcome, joined only by consensus documents) is contradicted by Ryder et al. 2020 — pharmacy physicochemistry and vascular-access outcomes joined, on data, in a pharmacy journal, in hospital pharmacy's flagship journal (the Gate 4 record added "by the threshold author"; that is withdrawn — see the verification note below). Only the third and weakest survives: an incentive gap, in that a negative retires a rule and sells nothing while vendors publishing threshold-based decision aids benefit from the rule standing — and that is asserted, not evidenced. What remains is that the multi-drug decomposition is next in a queue of post-hoc analyses nobody has reached, which is a restatement of "no one has got to it" — the mechanism Gate 4 explicitly forbids. The method is not available as the reason: nested frailty and VPCs are off-the-shelf.
Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status): Two independent adversaries, fresh contexts, Gate 0–3 record only; A2 did not read A1's log. Disguise floor met by both (A1 9 queries, A2 9 queries, 18 total in vocabularies Gate 2 did not try), so Disguise is VERIFIED, not unverified. Logs verbatim in -adversary-1.md and -adversary-2.md.
1 Triviality | The directional answer is already legible from Bahl (aHR 1.17), Yasuda (HR 1.06), Kia (medication below rate and care unit), Lanbeck (per-drug ORs) and Dugan (>1000 mOsm/L OR 1.67), so the rest is a page of arithmetic | None of those computes a variance share, an interval on one, a discrimination or calibration statistic for the threshold rule, or a cross-validated index; Bahl tests a pooled label, Dugan one cut in one drug class; 29 queries in nine vocabularies found no such quantity | Resolved (A1) / Resolved (A2)
2 Disguise | Renamed, it is asked: "which drugs cause phlebitis" (ID), "maximum tolerated osmolarity" (nutrition), "venous tolerance/local irritation" (toxicology), "PIVIE risk factors" (neonatology), "flebitis química" (Spanish nursing), "extravasation risk score" (oncology), and most damagingly Ryder 2020 asking whether infusate osmolarity, pH and cytotoxicity are risk factors for midline catheter failure, with the threshold rule's own author on it | Each is a real adjacent literature and four priors were missed by Gate 2, so the silence narrative is overstated and the "field is silent on the exposure" claim is false; but no vocabulary yields the candidate's estimand — no variance partition against patient/inserter/ward/lot, no rule discrimination or calibration, no competing index, and Ryder is 20 sheep and midlines with no cutoff analysis. A known gap never operationalised, not a known question renamed | Resolved with mandatory record correction (A1) / Partial, novelty restated Medium-minus and Gate 2 coverage recorded as incomplete (A2)
3 Combinatorial novelty | Pharmacy physicochemistry x nursing outcomes x off-the-shelf frailty models, with only a data join at the interface | The interface problem is sourced: Bahl's own limitation ("it was not always clear what access point was used for the caustic infusion") is the join the candidate requires, and Yasuda needed a DAG, a time-dependent exposure and splines for ONE drug on ~91 catheters and still landed on a null with a post-hoc knee — that is the identification problem in its easiest form; limb (b) is a decision-rule evaluation question no frailty machinery supplies | Resolved (A1) / Resolved (A2)
4 Presupposition failure | (a) no instance of the line-level-attribution regime had been evidenced, and Bahl could not attribute even inside a prospective trial; (b) the operative rule is the INS vesicant/irritant list plus MAGIC compatibility, not the numeric pH/osmolarity pair, so limb (b) may calibrate a straw rule; (c) "reproduced without field calibration" is overstated given Dugan 2014 | (a) now ESTABLISHED in the one regime V2 claims (Yasuda, 3,410 PIVCs, 23 ICUs), though generalisation beyond critical care is unevidenced; (b) corroborated against the severity reframing twice from opened text (Bahl's "based on infusate osmolarity thresholds that increase the likelihood of these complications"; Ryder's "risk factors for midline catheter failure") and the design carries extravasation injury as a co-primary endpoint, so the severity reading is tested rather than assumed — but the mis-aiming is real and fixable only by amendment; (c) Dugan tests a different cut in one drug class with an OR, so the gap narrows and survives | Partial (A1) / Resolved (A2) — worst status taken: Partial, non-fatal
5 Vagueness | A survival "variance share" is estimator-dependent, and the infusate is multiple-membership (one catheter receives many admixtures), not a nesting factor; A2's own arithmetic on Bahl's 10/257 extravasations (3.9%, Wilson 95% CI ~1.8–6.6%, A2's calculation) puts ~79,000 catheters (range ~47,000–171,000) behind 10 events per admixture level at 307 levels under uniform exposure, against AMOR-VENUS's 3,429 — so limb (a) may be answerable for phlebitis and not for extravasation or infection | V2 fixes scale, model class, interval, failure-mode specificity, two endpoints and IECV, and can come out negative; partial pooling via a low-dimensional infusate term (a smooth function of pH, osmolarity and vesicant status) would rescue the rarer modes — but V2 says "a per-admixture infusate term", which is the 307-level version the arithmetic prices, so the response is unevidenced against a sourced objection | Resolved (A1) / Partial (A2) — worst status taken: Partial, non-fatal
6 Significance inflation | The named bodies have reproduced these thresholds for decades without calibrating them, which is weak evidence they would act | Defeated by the same find that damaged attack 2: Ryder 2020 is a randomised blinded ovine RCT on these exact properties in hospital pharmacy's flagship journal with the threshold rule's source author and a vascular-access clinician on the byline; Bahl calls the guidelines "vague" and the evidence "limited"; Dugan says osmolarity support is "limited"; Manrique-Rodríguez says human tolerance "has not been well studied" | Resolved (A1) / Resolved (A2)
7 Reason for silence | The record's mechanisms explain why answering is hard, not why nobody asked — and worse, both mechanisms the record calls demonstrable are contradicted in print by papers Gate 2 missed: Yasuda 2025 populates the line-attribution regime inside a standing programme of post-hoc analyses off one cohort, and Ryder 2020 crosses the pharmacy/vascular-access boundary on data in a pharmacy journal. The weak forms were asked repeatedly (Lanbeck 2002, Dugan 2014, Bahl 2022, Kia 2023, Ryder 2020, Yasuda 2025) | The un-asked part is the estimand (VPC + rule calibration + competing index) while the topic is thoroughly asked; the record itself concedes an "acknowledged-but-never-operationalised gap". But with both evidenced mechanisms gone, the surviving story is an unevidenced incentive gap plus "nobody has reached it yet", which the gate forbids, and per Gate 4's own instruction a missing credible mechanism makes the novelty finding itself suspect | Partial (A1) / UNRESOLVED (A2) — worst status taken: Unresolved on a non-fatal attack, so Provisional is the ceiling
8 Dissolution | "The infusate VPC" may not name one quantity: a catheter receives many admixtures, the exposure is time-varying and multiple-membership, VPCs are defined for grouping factors, and Yasuda's design is the tell (infusate entered as a time-dependent covariate, not a grouping factor), so the answer depends on the exposure summary chosen (ever/never, cumulative mOsm-hours, peak pH deviation, dose) and on the sample's formulary mix | Multiple-membership multilevel models are a named class and would define the quantity with declared membership weights, so it becomes a question with a stated convention rather than dissolving; IECV across systems addresses mix-dependence, and a mix-dependent descriptive quantity still informs the specific decision the rule makes. Both adversaries held themselves to the sourcing standard — A2 could not open a primary source on the model class and declined to press to Unresolved; neither opened evidence that such a VPC is transportable | Partial (A1) / Partial (A2)
Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 3/3
Strongest remaining objection: The reason for silence does not survive Gate 4. Both mechanisms the record called demonstrable are contradicted in print by papers Gate 2 missed — Yasuda et al. 2025 populate the line-level attribution regime at 3,410 catheters across 23 ICUs (of which 91, 2.6%, actually received the drug) with a catheter-level time-dependent multilevel survival model, and Ryder et al. 2020 join pharmacy physicochemistry to vascular-access failure outcomes on data, in hospital pharmacy's flagship journal, and, as Gate 4 had it, "with the threshold rule's own source author on the byline" — WITHDRAWN ON VERIFICATION, 2026-10-18: no author of that paper is shown to have authored the osmolarity threshold, which the paper itself attributes to the 2011 INS standard credited to L. Gorski, not a co-author; Marc Stranz co-authored a different Gorski paper on noncytotoxic vesicants, which is not a standard. The journal and the data join survive; the byline claim does not. What remains is an unevidenced incentive gap and "nobody has reached it yet", which Gate 4 forbids as a mechanism; and because four priors turned up in vocabularies Gate 2 claimed to have swept, the Medium novelty grade rests on a search record now known to be incomplete rather than on a clean negative.
Promotion requires: a re-run Gate 2 that starts from Ryder 2020, Yasuda 2025, Lanbeck 2002 and Dugan 2014 (UPDATED 2026-10-18: Ryder's full text has now been read and NO cutoff analysis is present, so that item is DISCHARGED; Yasuda's full text is still unread after five route attempts across two passes, so whether any variance component is reported remains COULD NOT READ and this item stays open — it needs an interlibrary request or a subscription, not another search, and its abstract adds that noradrenaline reached only 70 patients through 91 PIVCs, so the exposed subgroup is 91 catheters and one drug rather than 3,410) and still grades novelty >= Medium; a reason for silence graded at least Partial on opened evidence despite those two papers; V3 raising well-posedness to 3/3 by declaring the infusate-exposure parameterisation and membership weighting (a low-dimensional pH/osmolarity/vesicant function rather than 307 discrete levels, with VPCs reported only for failure modes with adequate events) and an outcome-ascertainment plan for the phlebitis-grading and reason-less-removal error; and limb (b) amended to test the operative rule (the INS vesicant/irritant list and MAGIC compatibility designation) alongside the numeric thresholds.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): Establish whether the regime exists outside critical care — ask the AMOR-VENUS investigators what level the "multilevel" in their time-dependent Cox model is on and whether per-catheter administration records carry all infusates rather than noradrenaline alone; that single fact decides whether limb (a) is a data pull or a new data-collection programme.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): Not routed — not rejected. The weak form of limb (b) (whether the thresholds rest on evidence) is an acknowledged open gap stated by the field itself, but the candidate's estimand is not asked anywhere searched, so it stays in this ledger as Provisional rather than going to ledger/routed-open-problems.md. If the re-run Gate 2 above demotes novelty to Low, route it then, sourced to Manrique-Rodríguez 2021 and Ryder 2020.

Verification (post-batch, 2026-10-18; full log in batches/2026-10-18-0130/VERIFICATION.md): seven fresh-context readers across two passes. VERDICT UNCHANGED at Provisional. One decoration of the attack-7 kill is FALSE and is withdrawn above; the kill's substance survives on narrower ground.
- THE FALSE CLAIM, withdrawn. This entry said Ryder 2020 joins pharmacy physicochemistry to vascular-access outcomes "with the threshold rule's own source author on the byline". NO AUTHOR of that paper is shown to have authored the osmolarity threshold. The paper itself attributes 600 mOsm/L to the 2011 INS standard, credited to L. Gorski, who is not a co-author, and 900 mOsm/L to INS 2016 and ASPEN 2014. Marc Stranz co-authored a different paper with Gorski on noncytotoxic vesicant medications, which the paper does not describe as a standard. What survives, and is what attack 7 actually needs: pharmacy physicochemistry and vascular-access failure outcomes joined, on data, in hospital pharmacy's flagship journal.
- RYDER 2020 OTHERWISE VERIFIED AT FULL TEXT, with two numbers that need their denominators. 24 sheep enrolled, 4 excluded, 20 ANALYSED, 40 catheters, 6 test arms each paired with a contralateral saline control, randomised by leg, blinded pathologist, animal as a random effect. 95% is 19 of 20 TEST CATHETERS and 60% is 12 of 20 CONTROL CATHETERS — neither is a share of sheep — and the control figure is partly an artefact of the design, because 8 of the 20 controls were removed UNFAILED when their paired test catheter failed, so control failure is tied to the test leg rather than independently observed. Results and Discussion word this differently and give medians of 7 and 8 days. C675 is Clinimix 4.25/5 at 675 mOsm/L and pH 5.65; C930 is 4.25/10 at 930 mOsm/L and pH 5.54, both product-label values. "Four of the 6 arms (all except the C675 and A350 arms)" is verbatim. CONFIRMED as this entry has it: no threshold or cutoff analysis of any kind — no cut-point search, ROC, sensitivity, specificity or regression on osmolarity or pH, the arms being categorical — and no variance components, ICC or R-squared despite the animal random effect. The Discussion asserts pH is an independent risk factor while no analysis in the paper tests it. One fact this entry should carry and does not: THE STUDY WAS FUNDED BY BD, and four of the eight authors declare BD consulting fees or research payments. That bears directly on the incentive mechanism this entry calls asserted-but-unevidenced, and it cuts both ways.
- YASUDA 2025: THE ABSTRACT WAS REACHED ON THE SECOND PASS, and it carries one figure that changes the sentence above. The cohort numbers are the 2025 paper's own and this entry quotes them correctly — 3,410 PIVCs, 1,351 patients, 23 ICUs in Japan, a post hoc analysis of a prospective multicentre cohort, adjusted HR 1.06 (95% CI 0.93-1.20) — and they are NOT the earlier Front Med 2022 cohort's 3,429, which was the risk a reader had flagged. But NORADRENALINE WAS GIVEN TO ONLY 70 PATIENTS (5.2%) THROUGH 91 PIVCs (2.6%): the drug-attribution analysis rests on 91 exposed catheters and one drug, not on 3,410. The regime this entry needs for attack 7 does demonstrably exist, so the data-architecture mechanism is still falsified, but at a far smaller scale than "3,410 catheters" implies, and that is corrected in place above. Two further qualifications: the 6 mg figure comes from an EXPLORATORY SPLINE, not a formal change-point model, and the abstract's conclusion that a dose at or below 6 mg reduces risk rests on that spline rather than on the non-significant primary HR. WHETHER ANY VARIANCE COMPONENT IS REPORTED REMAINS COULD NOT READ after five route attempts across two passes (doi.org, the Wiley article page, the Wiley pdfdirect URL named as the best open-access location, a Wiley mirror, the Griffith Research Online handle and the Griffith repository all failed; PubMed Central is blocked here; the DOAJ record holds no abstract text, only the trial registration UMIN000028019). That is the promotion condition's own first item and it is still open.
- BAHL 2022 VERIFIED AT FULL TEXT, and the demotion condition is properly discharged. pH appears ZERO times in the text, tables and references; osmolarity appears ONCE, in the Introduction, as background on how the INS list was built, with no values. No random effects, frailty terms or clustering. Extravasation was not predefined and its 10 events appear only in the Discussion with no denominator stated, as recorded. Two internal inconsistencies in the source: the ABSTRACT prints the adjusted HR as 1.71, which lies outside its own confidence interval, where the body and Table 3 say 1.17 — this entry uses the body value, correctly — and the paper is inconsistent on whether 257 or 270 were randomised. Supplementary files S1-S3 were not opened, so the pH and osmolarity absence is established for the main text, tables and references rather than the supplements.
- LANBECK 2002 EXISTS; THE PER-DRUG ODDS RATIOS THIS ENTRY RELIES ON ARE UNVERIFIED. Read at abstract level only: 550 patients with 1,386 peripheral catheters, so the 1,386 is real. But the abstract carries NO per-antibiotic odds ratios — only an overall antibiotic-against-no-antibiotic OR of 2.34, and a qualitative sorting of named drugs into highest risk (dicloxacillin, erythromycin), also raised (benzylpenicillin, cefuroxime, cloxacillin) and not raised (ampicillin, imipenem/cilastatin, clindamycin, netilmicin, vancomycin). Two Lund catalogue records disagree on whether the 18.5% and 8.8% are of catheters or of patients. This entry's conclusion stands — a regression-based ordering of named drugs by observed phlebitis IS an empirically derived irritancy ranking from clinical data, so striking Gate 2 query 11's negative was right — but "per-antibiotic phlebitis ORs" overstates what anyone has seen, and is corrected in place above. Note also a later separate paper (Scand J Infect Dis 2003;35:397-400) comparing dicloxacillin with cloxacillin, so no such figure should be credited to the 2002 paper.
- DUGAN 2014 VERIFIED AT ABSTRACT LEVEL. Real title "Maximum Tolerated Osmolarity for Peripheral Administration of Parenteral Nutrition in Pediatric Patients", JPEN 2014;38(7):847-851, doi 10.1177/0148607113495569: a retrospective matched cohort of 352 patients aged 18 or under on peripheral parenteral nutrition, exposure the single dichotomy above against at or below 1,000 mOsm/L, multivariable OR 1.67 (95% CI 1.08-2.52, P = .02) for the composite of phlebitis or infiltration. The unadjusted composite OR is 1.65, nearly identical to the adjusted one and easy to confuse with it. Whether more than one cut point was tested, and whether any calibration, discrimination or reclassification is reported, are NOT FOUND at abstract level only — the methods were not read, so the single-cut claim is not established beyond the abstract.
- MANRIQUE-RODRIGUEZ 2021 VERIFIED AT FULL TEXT, exactly as recorded. pH and osmolarity are genuinely MEASURED — osmolality by freezing-point depression on a Fiske 210 micro-osmometer with three measurements per admixture, density by pycnometer, osmolarity as their product, pH as the mean of three readings on a Crison 2006 meter — and the paper says no label or literature values existed for these admixtures. 307 is the number of distinct admixtures, from 106 drugs at 183 concentrations, with 123 of 307 (40.0%) classed high risk. NO admixture is linked to any clinical outcome: phlebitis appears only as literature background and the vascular-access algorithm is proposed, not validated. The paper adopts risk tiers of under 450, 450-600 and over 600 mOsm/L, attributing the 600 mOsm/L peripheral limit to other authors and noting that the current INS standard uses 900 mOsm/L for central access while an earlier edition used 600 with pH 5-9.

ID: UQ-20261018-06
Date: 2026-10-18
Status: Rejected — Gate 2 (novelty Low: near-duplicate on the consequence-bearing limb). Confirmed fatally at Gate 4: attack 2 (Disguise) Unresolved from BOTH adversaries, each having run its 8 new-vocabulary Disguise queries, so Disguise is verified, not unverified. Well-posedness 2/3 independently blocks Validated.
Domain(s): Other STEM — hydrology, coastal and wind engineering, environmental measurement networks (target field). Method field: extreme-value statistics / non-ignorable missingness (selection models, informative censoring).

Question (canonical): For one measurand per network, over a pre-declared frame of (station, event-window) pairs with exogenous event windows and each pair's realized peak y assigned from evidence independent of that station's instrument (with a declared error model): (a) what is the hazard h(y) that the instrument ceases to report inside the window, in the measurand's own units, with CIs, and is h flat in y; and (b) re-fitting GEV/POT with that censoring modelled explicitly — as a non-ignorable selection model, or by treating a lost peak as interval-censored below by the last recorded value — what is the signed change in the 50- and 100-year return levels against the conventional fit on the published annual-maxima series? (V2, the one Gate 1 reformulation; V1 and the reason for reformulation are in batches/2026-10-18-0352/UQ-20261018-06-record.md.)

Alternative formulations:
- Do stream gauges, tide gauges and anemometers fail because of the events they are measuring, and by how much does the consequent loss of the largest observations depress estimated extreme quantiles?
- Treating instrument survival as an outcome in the units of the measurand, is missingness in extreme-value records ignorable, and what selection model is being assumed when it is treated as such?

Motivating gap: Instrument loss at the peak is reported constantly in passing and never aggregated (USGS estimated/destroyed-gauge flags, NOAA tide gauges dropping out at the surge maximum, anemometers failing before the maximum gust, clipped strong-motion records). The intake's gap statement — that the EVA literature treats record gaps as ignorable and that nobody has estimated the effect of measurand-driven instrument loss on return levels — is FALSE as written and was withdrawn at Gate 2; see "how this differs" below. Adversary 1 withdrew a second leg: limb (a) itself has a coarse 2005 answer for the wind network.

Presuppositions (graded against documents opened; full text in the record):
1. Event-window outages recorded with enough timing/QC detail to distinguish outage from a low reading — CONTESTED (good for USGS estimated-record flags, weaker elsewhere; flag reliability unquantified).
2. Realized peak at a failed station reconstructible independently of that instrument — CONTESTED, the identification crux. A2 tested it against the method's own standard reference (USGS Rantz ch. 9): indirect peak determination is routine, its accuracy stated qualitatively only ("essentially an 'art'"), with no claim that error grows with magnitude. Literature neither establishes nor refutes it.
3. Failure at least partly caused by the measurand — now EVIDENCED for wind, not merely anecdotal (A1: 2005 ACWE attrition fractions rise monotonically with Saffir-Simpson category). USGS disaster-recovery counts (Harvey 20; Irma 126; Maria 84 + 3 USVI; a stated "192 damaged or destroyed" that does not reconcile with the 233 the per-event figures sum to) still carry no denominator.
4. Published series are computed from these records so bias propagates — ESTABLISHED in general, but CONTESTED per network (A1: USGS replaces destroyed-gauge peaks with indirect estimates published under an "estimated" flag, so for that network the published series may contain the peak as measurement error rather than omit it as censoring; A1 could not source this within budget).
5. A hazard on the measurand is well defined — CONTESTED for compound events; V2 contains it by fiat.
6. Enough station-events with both a documented outage and an independent reconstruction — CONTESTED, undeclared either way.

What would count as an answer: h(y) with CIs over the pre-declared frame in the measurand's units, plus the signed change in 50-/100-year quantiles from a refit with censoring modelled explicitly, against the conventional fit. A clean negative settles it too: h flat in y and return levels moving less than a pre-declared tolerance. Gate 1 passes on this criterion (2/3; see Scores).

Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): Gate 2 ran 11 web searches, 5 fetches, 5 documents opened; Gate 4 added 17 new-vocabulary queries and 8 fetches across two independent adversaries (36 queries total). Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources) — plus two added at Gate 4:
P1 Simpson, E. S. & Northrop, P. J., "Accounting for missing data when modelling block maxima", arXiv:2512.15429v1 (UCL; submitted 2025-12-17). Unit: the block with its non-missing count (162 yr Brest surge; 27 yr Plymouth ozone). Endpoint: GEV parameters and r-block return levels. Comparator: naive / discard / McVittie-Murphy weights / unattainable "full". Estimand: bias from within-block missingness and its removal by a block-count adjustment, explicitly under ignorability ("missing completely at random in each block"; missingness "must be non-informative"). Its Discussion poses limb (b) as the field's open need in the candidate's own example ("river flow gauges being damaged by fast-running water, and there is a need to be able to capture such phenomena... one could attempt to explicitly model the missingness mechanism and incorporate this into the GEV model"). Gate 2 read this verbatim on a second targeted fetch; A2 opened the /abs/ record (authors, date and estimand confirmed) but COULD NOT READ the Discussion, so the posing sentence has one reading, not two.
P2 McVittie, J. H. & Murphy, O. A., "Estimating Extreme Wave Surges in the Presence of Missing Data", arXiv:2506.15970v1 (read in full on verification; "companion to arXiv:2506.15964" is this record’s inference, since P2 does not cite that paper, whose own title is "Weighted Parameter Estimators of the Generalized Extreme Value Distribution in the Presence of Missing Observations"). Unit: yearly block maxima of de-tided surge at Saint John, Yarmouth, Port-Aux-Basques. Endpoint: GEV parameters, 20-/50-/100-year return levels. Comparator: the naive observed-data likelihood, plus the ~10-15% block-discard practice. Estimand: return levels with a lost block maximum treated as censored from below — hard, soft-unconditional, soft-conditional, EM — with Little's test rejecting MCAR at every station and the candidate's causal story in the paper's own words ("a failure of the equipment was attributed to the high intensity waves"). Effect reported: EM and conditional soft censoring "predict a 20-year return level almost 1m higher" at Saint John. OPENED AND VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY BY A2, including that the censoring probabilities are imputed from the within-block non-missing proportion, the empirical CDF of observed values, or the fitted GEV CDF inside EM — never estimated from network data.

L., "Regression Analysis with Truncated Samples and Its Application to Ground-Motion Attenuation Studies", BSSA 2004;94(4):1369-1378, doi 10.1785/012003083 (ABSTRACT ONLY; the year, volume, issue and pages are now READ from three agreeing metadata records rather than inferred, but the methods were never opened, so this entry’s claim that the missingness probability is deliberately unmodelled is UNVERIFIED rather than established — see the verification note). Sci. 19(2):432-438, 2021, doi 10.5937/jaes0-28902 (read at PDF level on verification; the perception-threshold CONCEPT is established B17C/HEC-SSP machinery, but using it to represent missing values inside the systematic record is the authors’ OWN PROPOSAL, not operational guidance — see the verification note). Estimand: quantile error when missing peaks are represented as interval data via Bulletin 17C / HEC-SSP perception thresholds, including "a lower perception threshold bound at the value of the highest observed flow in the available series" — the candidate's second named method as operational guidance with a published sensitivity study.

Novelty — how this differs from each:
vs P1: same object, same endpoint, same field; P1 states the candidate's limb (b) as a need, in the candidate's own example. The candidate is not a different question from that need; it is that need plus limb (a). Asked-and-open, not un-asked.
vs P2: the harder prior, because it executes. Unit class, endpoint, comparator, estimation device and named causal mechanism all match limb (b), with MCAR tested and rejected on real station data and a number attached. Differs only in that P2's censoring probability is assumed structurally rather than measured, no y is reconstructed, and no frame of outage-flagged station-events appears. The residue over P2 is "swap an imputed delta-hat for a measured h(y)" — real and narrow, and not what the candidate asked.
vs P3: opposite direction of truncation, different endpoint, missingness probability deliberately unmodelled. Weakens any claim the statistical apparatus is missing; does not occupy the estimand.
vs P4: this is the prior that removes the candidate's last clean limb. Frame, outcome and conditioning variable all match limb (a), for one of the three network types the candidate names, in the target field's own venue, twenty years before the candidate. The candidate's refinements over it are genuine — continuous h(y) with CIs, a declared independent reconstruction, propagation to quantiles — but they are refinements of an asked and coarsely answered question. Weight carried: the abstract only; full text unread.
vs P5: limb (b) method 2 uses established B17C/HEC-SSP perception-threshold machinery, but P5’s application of it to gaps inside the systematic record is the authors’ own proposal, and P5 reports that the B17C-recommended option is not its best-performing choice. So this prior is a published evaluation of a proposal rather than of settled guidance (corrected on verification).

Significance — consequence: If h(y) rises steeply, every published annual-maxima series in the affected networks is a truncated sample of its own tail and the conventional fit is biased low; P2's ~1 m shift at a 20-year surge level shows the correction is not cosmetic. If h(y) is flat, the standing ignorability assumption is licensed empirically for the first time. But after Gate 2 and Gate 4 this is largely P1's, P2's and P4's consequence: the candidate's marginal consequence is the difference between an assumed and an externally estimated censoring probability — which does break P2's self-referentiality (its delta-hat comes from the same GEV being fitted), of unknown magnitude at the 100-year quantile.
Significance — audience: the EVA methodologists are real, active and verified (P1 2025-12-17; P2 a 2025 companion pair) and would consume an h(y). The operator audience is thinner than the record claimed: A1 shows wind engineering already quantified attrition in 2005 and responded by building hardened portable towers, and USGS already encodes destroyed-gauge peaks as estimated/interval data that Bulletin 17C consumes; A2's queries 3, 5 and 8 show operators speak in deployment, recovery and uptime counts, with no sign any would publish magnitude-conditioned outage metadata. Design-value committees (Bulletin 17C, ASCE 7, FEH) remain Partial on UQ-20261017-25's precedent.
Significance — fecundity: whether h(y) differs by network, instrument generation and mounting; whether hardening beats the statistical correction; whether reconstructed-peak error is itself magnitude-dependent, i.e. whether limb (a) is identified; whether the same logic applies to saturation/clipping; whether networks should optimise for tail information rather than record completeness.
Significance — anchoring: the stationarity dispute (a magnitude-dependent censoring bias and a trend push the fitted tail in confounded directions); P1's declared open item; P2's self-referential delta-hat; and UQ-20261017-25, whose realized-exceedance-rate test is biased toward the reassuring null by exactly this mechanism (its own presupposition 6).

Reason for silence: FAILED as offered, which is why the Low grade is not search luck. The record's mechanism was a disciplinary boundary running between the two limbs, bridged from the statistics side only in 2025 — a mechanism that dates its own expiry. A1 killed it: somebody did ask limb (a), in 2005, in wind engineering, with numbers (P4), so the mechanism explains at most why hydrologists and surge statisticians do not read wind-engineering proceedings — a reason the question was answered elsewhere, not a reason it was un-asked. A2 killed the second leg independently: the record claimed the joining measurement "exists only as a reconstruction that the data owner has no reason to compile", but USGS compiles indirect peak determinations as standard practice precisely where the direct record failed (Rantz ch. 9), and publishes them flagged. What survives is the weaker boundary leg (operators compile the peak as a peak, not as the outcome of a survival model; the EVA side inherited missingness as a weighting nuisance) — graded Unresolved by A1 and Partial by A2. Per Gate 4, a failed reason for silence makes the novelty finding suspect and points back to Gate 2, which is where this verdict already sits.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3
Well-posedness 2/3: V2 states the estimand, the frame discipline, the units and a falsifying negative with a pre-declared tolerance, so it is a question and not a thesis. Short of 3/3 on identification — y at a failed station must be reconstructed from a hindcast, a neighbour or a high-water mark whose own error is plausibly magnitude-dependent, so conditioning variable and outcome share an error source; A2 confirmed from Rantz ch. 9 that the literature neither establishes nor refutes this. Presupposition 5 survives only by fiat for landfalling storms, where the instrument is killed by whichever of surge, wind and rainfall arrives first. 2/3 independently blocks Validated.
Significance 2/3: consequence, audience and anchoring are argued from opened sources and the limb-(a) audience holds the data. Not 3/3 because the strongest consequence was demonstrated by P2, and both adversaries graded the operator and committee legs Partial.

Strongest remaining objection: the candidate is a conjunction in which every limb is occupied by someone else's asking. Limb (b) — the limb carrying the entire claim to consequence — is executed at the candidate's own unit, endpoint, comparator and estimand by P2, on real tide-gauge data, with the mechanism named and a number attached (~1 m at the 20-year level), and posed as an explicit open need by P1; its second method is operational Bulletin 17C practice with a published evaluation (P5). Limb (a), which Gate 2 kept as the un-asked residue, was asked and coarsely answered in 2005 for the ASOS/AWOS network in the target field's own venue (P4), in the measurand's own binned units, over an exogenously framed set of station-storm pairs. What is left after both subtractions — replace P2's imputed censoring probability with a continuous, CI'd h(y) estimated from outage flags plus independently reconstructed peaks — is a refinement of two asked questions, not an un-asked question, and it may not be identified, because the reconstruction it depends on is error-prone in a way that plausibly correlates with the very magnitude being conditioned on.

Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): open the full text of P4 (10ACWE 2005; the par.nsf.gov follow-on at /servlets/purl/10282239 is the likely published form) and establish how the experienced wind at a failed station was assigned — independent wind-field analysis or the station's own last reading. That one fact decides whether limb (a) is a refinement of an asked question or a genuinely un-asked one, and so whether any reformulation is worth taking to Gate 0. Any reformulation should be searched first in the biostatistics vocabulary for its missingness class, "self-censoring" (arXiv:2207.08535; Biometrics 10.1111/biom.13916).

Routing (rejected as already-asked, in part): limb (b) is routed to ledger/routed-open-problems.md as asked-but-still-open, on P1's own posing sentence (arXiv:2512.15429v1, Discussion: "there is a need to be able to capture such phenomena.
