Verification (post-batch, 2026-10-18; full log in batches/2026-10-18-0352/VERIFICATION.md): six fresh-context readers on this entry's priors, each given one source and no reviewer reasoning. VERDICT UNCHANGED. All three legs of the kill survive first-hand reading, and the Disguise leg is now stronger than the batch could show.
- P4's AUTHOR IS RECOVERED and all three of its quoted figures are verbatim in the abstract. Collette M. Blessing, with Forrest J. Masters as contributor, Paper No. 102. The HTML record's author field is blank, but the BibTeX export gives "Blessing, Collette M." and the MARC export gives Blessing as author with Masters as contributor. Checked one at a time: "almost 25% of the stations failed to report" (verbatim), "over 90% of the stations ceased to communicate" (verbatim), "All stations that experienced Saffir-Simpson Category 2 wind speeds failed." (verbatim and complete). ONE WORDING CORRECTION that must not propagate: the second figure is AT Saffir-Simpson Category 1, not "above Category 1" — a MARC-based paraphrase said "above", the source says "At". Three qualifications the abstract itself imposes: the denominator "the stations" is never defined; the level of aggregation (per station, per storm, pooled) is not stated; and the count of stations in the Category-2 bin is not given, so "All stations ... failed" may rest on few. Still ABSTRACT ONLY after about fourteen further routes; the record is restricted and its PDF blocks robots, though the MARC export states a PDF is hosted on ITAM Invenio. Untried routes logged for a later pass: AMS 32nd Hurricane Conference paper 293983, the Masters dissertation PDF at fcmp.ce.ufl.edu, Semantic Scholar.
- THE FINDING THAT STRENGTHENS ATTACK 2. A second reader was given the TOPIC with no identifier and told not to search for any title. It surfaced Blessing & Masters on its FIRST try. Disguise asks whether a question is already asked in other words; a paper a subject-first sweep finds immediately is not hidden. Two ancillary sources neither adversary had, both unconditioned and so not priors: NIST/ICAMS slides giving event counts without wind speeds (Irma: 34 of 66 ASOS and C-MAN stations failed; Harvey: the 3 ASOS near Rockport TX failed), and Powell, Houston & Reinhold 1996 (Weather and Forecasting 11:304-327), whose Table 1 lists causes of Hurricane Andrew site failures with no failure rate against wind speed. The stream-gauge and tide-gauge side of the negative is WEAK and is now recorded as such: those searches returned titles only and no USGS document was opened.
- P1's POSING SENTENCE IS VERBATIM AT FULL TEXT, and the paper has since been published: the abs record carries doi 10.1002/env.70075 (Environmetrics), which this record did not have. All four strings found, each checked alone — but "river flow gauges being damaged by fast-running water" and "there is a need to be able to capture such phenomena" are HALVES OF ONE SENTENCE in Section 6, not two independent confirmations, and "missing completely at random in each block" is in Section 3.2, not the Discussion. The paper does NOT model measurand-dependent missingness: "but this is not accounted for in our current approach", with simulations imposing MCAR within each block at a missing proportion drawn from U(0, 0.2). Comparator corrections: there are TWO McVittie-Murphy weighting variants, not one; "unattainable" is not the paper's word for Full (it says Full "is, of course, impossible in practice"); and the applications do not use Full at all.
- P2 EXECUTES LIMB (b) AND ITS CENSORING PROBABILITY IS IMPUTED EXACTLY AS THIS RECORD SAYS, verified at full text. The unconditional soft estimator uses the within-block non-missing proportion and "do not utilize any information from the random variables within each of the blocks"; the conditional soft estimator uses the empirical CDF of observed values raised to the number missing; EM uses the fitted GEV CDF at the observed block maximum, iterated. NO external information about instruments, networks or failure rates enters anywhere, and the realized block maximum is never reconstructed at a failed station. One real demotion: the quote "a failure of the equipment was attributed to the high intensity waves" is verbatim but is the paper's HYPOTHETICAL MNAR scenario III, not a documented failure at a named station. The figure with its denominators: Table 4, Saint John 20-year levels — obs 1.73 m, hard 6.26 m (SE 137.66, unusable), softUC 1.88, softC 2.95, EM 2.65 m; so "almost 1m" fits EM (+0.92 m) better than softC (+1.22 m), and the comparison is against the observed-likelihood estimate, not a true value. Stations and spans: Saint John 1941-2023 (83 years, 60 with missing data), Yarmouth 1965-2023 (59, 45), Port-aux-Basques 1959-2023 (64, 56). The 10-15% discard rule is Beck et al. (2020)'s, which P2's simulations "appear to support" rather than derive.
- P5'S QUOTED STRING IS A PARAPHRASE, AND THE PRIOR IS A PROPOSAL WHERE THIS RECORD CALLED IT GUIDANCE. Checked piece by piece: "highest observed flow" absent, "available series" absent, "highest peak flow in the available" present. The abstract reads "setting a lower perception threshold bound at the value of the highest peak flow in the available - incomplete dataset"; the Conclusion reads "TY,lower is set to value of the largest flood within the remaining (incomplete) data record". The perception-threshold concept is established B17C/HEC-SSP machinery — quoted in the paper as "the perception thresholds do not depend on the actual peak discharges that have occurred" — but its use for missing values inside the systematic record is the authors' own ("introduces the concept of Perception threshold that can be used for missing data representation"; "perception thresholds are primarily intended for unobserved historic flood representation"), and the paper finds the B17C-recommended option (iv in dataset 1A) is NOT its best performer. Design: 15 BASE datasets plus 56 threshold variants, reference the complete 1931-2016 86-year annual-peak record at HS Senta on the Tisza; percentage error mostly within +/-5%, to -8.5% in 2A-iv, 4A-iv and 4B-iv; CI widths are in unreadable image figures. P5 has no magnitude-dependent probability model either — its gaps are magnitude-dependent only by construction.
- P3 IS STILL UNREAD IN ITS METHODS, and this record's characterisation of it is UNVERIFIED rather than established. The year, volume, issue, pages and DOI are now read from Crossref, the OGS repository and the ISC catalogue rather than inferred. But "the missingness probability is deliberately never modelled" is COULD NOT READ: the OGS PDF returned a login page and GeoScienceWorld errored. The abstract makes it MORE open, not settled — it introduces "randomly truncated regression" for thresholds that change over time and says the method "does not need to know which stations did not trigger". The low-end direction of truncation is confirmed only as an inference from how triggering works. This disturbs nothing: P3 grounds no part of the kill and is cited only to show the method family is mature in a sibling field.

ID: UQ-20261018-07
Date: 2026-10-18
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): Other STEM — isotope geochemistry and environmental/analytical chemistry (secondary: chemical metrology; mineral-provenance forensics)

Question (canonical): For a declared window (index case 2010–2025), construct the production-weighted δ7Li of the commercial lithium pool year by year from (a) feedstock-resolved δ7Li domains and (b) measured per-process Δ7Li for the route each feedstock takes to battery- or reagent-grade product, weighted by public annual production by deposit type and by the recycled share, with uncertainty propagated: (i) what is the year-on-year change Δδ7Li_pool and its interval, and (ii) does substituting the year-appropriate pool value for the anthropogenic endmember of a NAMED published apportionment (index case: effluent endmember 14.5 ± 4.3‰, 1σ, n = 6, Choi et al. 2019) move that study's inferred anthropogenic fraction outside its stated interval?
(V1 as intake, and the Gate 1 reformulation that produced the above: batches/2026-10-18-0352/UQ-20261018-07-record.md)

Alternative formulations:
- Is the anthropogenic lithium isotope signature used as a tracer a constant of the anthropogenic pool, or a moving target set by the supply chain that produced it?
- Do dated commercial lithium products, and datable archives downstream of a steady source, record a secular trend in δ7Li analogous to the Suess effect for carbon?

Motivating gap:
Presupposition inversion on the claim that δ7Li discriminates anthropogenic from natural lithium because the anthropogenic endmember is distinct and stable. IUPAC/CIAAW withdrew a single standard atomic weight for lithium because commercial lithium is isotopically fractionated by processing (interval 6.938–6.997; ciaaw.org/lithium.htm, doi 10.1515/pac-2017-1002); Qi et al. 1997 found 7 of 39 shelf reagents outside natural variation (to +3013‰); Desaulty et al. 2022 showed ordinary battery-chain lithium carries feedstock- and process-resolved δ7Li differences of 5–25‰ against ±0.4‰ (2σ) precision. Nobody has indexed that pool by time or carried it into an apportionment.

Presuppositions:
1. δ7Li of commercial products varies by feedstock/process above analytical precision — ESTABLISHED (Desaulty 2022; corroborated independently by Honra et al., Goldschmidt 2025/30726, Δ7Li(SC–Li2CO3) +2.4 to +4.5‰).
2. The product mix changed materially over the window — ESTABLISHED on tonnage; sourcing is economic, so volatile rather than trending.
3. Dated material exists to measure drift directly — CONTESTED; no archive found. V2 avoids needing it.
4. Published apportionments assume a fixed borrowed anthropogenic endmember — FALSIFIED for the index case (Choi et al. 2019 measured its own effluent endmember in the same July 2015 campaign) and unconfirmed anywhere else: two independent citation-direction sweeps found zero studies that borrow a literature anthropogenic δ7Li endmember.
5. Environmental Li derives predominantly from the commercial pool — PLAUSIBLE, UNVERIFIED.
6. Fractionation during use, treatment and transport is small or correctable — CONTESTED; nothing measured downstream of the consumer.
7. Public production statistics can be partitioned by deposit type and recycled share annually with usable uncertainty — PLAUSIBLE, UNVERIFIED; also ambiguous between mine-mouth and refinery-output accounting.
(Full list and gradings: record.)

What would count as an answer:
A production-weighted δ7Li series for the commercial pool with a propagated interval — from route-resolved δ7Li plus annual production by deposit type and recycled share, or measured on manufacture-dated products and a datable downstream archive — plus recomputation of at least one named published apportionment under the year-appropriate endmember, showing whether its anthropogenic fraction moves outside its stated interval. Three outcomes pre-declared: drift exceeds existing endmember uncertainty; null (drift smaller, tracer robust); or drift large on the production side but irrelevant downstream because studies calibrate locally, re-aiming the finding at provenance-forensics reference libraries.

Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result):
Gate 2: 11 queries (at cap), full list in batches/2026-10-18-0352/UQ-20261018-07-record.md. Most informative: "temporal variability of the anthropogenic lithium isotope endmember δ7Li" (mandatory own-field obvious title) → natural-system δ7Li only, nothing on a time-varying anthropogenic endmember; "nuclear forensics lithium isotopic signature provenance attribution commercial lithium materials 6Li/7Li producer" → surfaced Desaulty et al. 2022, the on-point own-field paper the intake query had missed; "temporal change in anthropogenic isotopic endmember source apportionment lead zinc drift environmental forensics" (method-owning field) → the drifting-endmember method is mature for Pb, no Li analogue; "molar mass uncertainty lithium isotopic variability commercial materials atomic weight interval 6.938 6.997 metrology" → IUPAC/CIAAW state the spread, nobody monitors it over time. Quantity check run: the comparator (±4.3‰ endmember uncertainty) and the feedstock-resolved domain IQRs are published; the production-weighted pool value, its change and the propagation are not.
Gate 4: 17 further queries in 17 vocabularies Gate 2 did not try (adversary-1.md queries 1–8 Disguise + 1 target; adversary-2.md queries 1–9). Most informative: boron-tracing vocabulary → "Are boron isotopes a reliable tracer of anthropogenic inputs to rivers over time?" (hal-02118789), the question's template asked for another element — COULD NOT READ (Anubis block on both HAL routes, no DOI obtained); citation-direction search for who borrows Choi's 14.5‰ → no borrower found; recycling-compliance vocabulary → no δ7Li work on recycled feedstock anywhere; "isotopically anomalous commercial lithium ... re-measured" → no re-survey of commercial reagents since Qi 1997; mixing-model methodology (MixSIAR) → time-varying source signatures are a named methodological topic in stable-isotope ecology. Three Goldschmidt abstracts flagged unread at Gate 2 were opened in Gate 4 (2024/23022 deep-time seawater; 2025/30726 Honra; 2025/30615 Vigier) and none time-indexes the pool.

P3. Qi, Coplen, Wang & Wang (1997), "Unnatural isotopic composition of lithium reagents", Anal. Chem. 69(19):4076–4078, doi 10.1021/ac9704669, read at record level only via pubs.usgs.gov/publication/70019577 — unit: a lithium reagent "from several manufacturers", n = 39, of which SEVEN were artificially depleted in 6Li (the paper says "reagents" and "samples", never "bottles"); endpoint: δ7Li −11‰ to +3013‰, a range spanning ordinary and depleted reagents together, plus a MEASURED atomic-weight range of 6.939 to 6.996 (the paper derives no recommended interval; its atomic-weight claim is that a 1993 IUPAC statement of 6.94 to 6.99 "has been found to be incorrect"). The paper does NOT attribute the depletion to industrial enrichment; that attribution comes from secondary sources. All verified on the abstract only; comparator: natural terrestrial variation; estimand: cross-sectional prevalence of unnatural composition on lab shelves at one time.

Novelty — how this differs from each:
vs P1 — same materials, different estimand: no time index, no production weights, no recycled-feedstock measurement, no environmental endmember; P1 states the staleness problem as a maintenance remark ("the database must be active") rather than measuring it. P1 is the candidate's strongest input, which is also its triviality exposure.

Not High: P1 supplies the arithmetic's inputs and names the problem; the generic template is explicitly in print for boron and standard for Pb/Zn/Cu, and the boron paper could not be read on either route, so an element-swap disguise cannot be excluded.)

Significance — consequence:
If drift exceeds existing endmember uncertainty, borrowed-endmember, cross-year and retrospective-archive δ7Li apportionments become year-sensitive, provenance reference libraries acquire a vintage, and the drift becomes a dating handle (a lithium Suess effect). If smaller, borrowed endmembers are licensed and an anomaly the IUPAC withdrawal makes look alarming closes with a number. Deflated by the audit result: the index case measured its own endmember, so a yes retracts nothing; consequence is confined to borrowed, cross-year, retrospective and forensic uses, a population not yet shown to be non-empty.

Significance — audience:
(i) anthropogenic-Li apportionment geochemists (Choi/Vigier, BRGM) — would carry a drift term rather than a single literature value, but currently calibrate locally; (ii) mineral-provenance and traceability groups (BRGM, EU battery-passport due diligence) — would date and re-measure libraries, the one audience with a plausible stake, and P1 already owns the concern as a maintenance task; (iii) chemical metrology (CIAAW, NMIs) — weakened: the 6.938–6.997 interval is set by reagent extremes, not by a pool mean; (iv) water utilities and regulators beginning Li monitoring — real but not yet practising isotopic attribution.

Significance — fecundity:
A measurable lithium Suess effect and Li-horizon dating in sediment; an isotopic tracer of recycled content in a cell (a compliance measurement); auditing declared supply chains against a time series rather than a static library; where the enrichment-derived tail enters the environment; whether within-year dispersion of the pool exceeds between-year drift, changing the estimand from a mean to a dispersion.

Significance — anchoring:
The IUPAC/CIAAW withdrawal of a single Li standard atomic weight with no time-resolved follow-up; P1's explicit open maintenance problem for provenance databases; the spread between anthropogenic endmember values reported in different catchments and years; and the drifting-anthropogenic-endmember problem in isotope forensics — mature for Pb, explicitly posed for B, absent for Li.

Reason for silence:
Offered: a disciplinary boundary with an incentive gap — metrology states an interval with no mandate to time-index it, provenance forensics wants a static library, apportionment geochemists calibrate locally and never need a pool value — plus genuine data newness (post-2017 hard-rock surge, recycling only now, the second epoch of supply-chain Δ7Li appearing in 2025, no commercial-reagent re-survey since 1997). Both adversaries graded this Partial: P1 noticed and discharged the staleness problem rather than leaving it unthought; the same community poses the question for boron in a paper title; and the forensics disincentive is unevidenced and partly contradicted by Honra et al. 2025 and Kropp et al. 2025, who publish process-fractionation data actively. The data-newness leg survives; the mechanism now reads closer to "no customer for a pool mean", which also caps significance.

Verification (post-batch, 2026-10-18; full log in batches/2026-10-18-0352/VERIFICATION.md): five fresh-context readers on this entry's priors, each given one source and no reviewer reasoning. VERDICT UNCHANGED at Rejected — but THE REJECTION NOW RESTS ON ATTACK 4 ALONE. Adversary 1 graded attacks 1 and 4 Unresolved while adversary 2 graded both Partial; attack 1's ground falls on first-hand reading, attack 4's survives verification of its own source. Under the ledger's rule a ground that survives first-hand verification of its own sources has not fallen, so NO LATE GATE 4 IS OWED — but this record must no longer present attack 1 as a second independent fatal ground.
- ATTACK 1'S GROUND FALLS: THE ARITHMETIC IS NOT SHORT, BECAUSE ITS INPUTS ARE NOT A ROUTE TABLE. Both adversaries judged limb (i) "short arithmetic over P1's published domain IQRs and per-process Δ7Li". P1 read at PDF level over three passes publishes exactly five per-process figures, every one a one-off: hydroxide minus spodumene concentrate +5.5‰ from ONE Keliber sample pair; leaching Li+ minus beta-concentrate +0.2 to +0.4‰ from a Rayleigh MODEL estimate; ion-exchange purification over +8‰ at 95% yield from the authors' own LABORATORY experiments; SQM minus Leverton +1.0 to +1.4‰ from measured products; hydroxide minus carbonate +0.4 to +0.8‰, read by the paper as no significant fractionation. THERE IS NO ROUTE-BY-ROUTE TABLE ACROSS THE INDUSTRY. One measured sample pair, one model estimate and one bench result are not per-process fractionation factors for the routes a production-weighted pool mean needs. The deposit domains hold but are thinner than this record implies: both are THIRD QUARTILES and probabilistic cut-offs, not bounds — hard-rock "below +6‰" is the upper quartile of n = 20 spodumenes (IQR −0.3 to +6.0, median +2.8) and brine "over +11.3‰" the upper quartile of n = 103 salar brines (IQR +7.9 to +11.3, median +9.8), with an explicit "unknown origin domain" between them and Chinese Qaidam brines far higher (IQR +16.1 to +31.4).
- ATTACK 4'S GROUND HOLDS AND ITS TIMING DECORATION FALLS. Choi et al. 2019 read at full text. The figure is verbatim — "their δ7Li values are low (14.5 ± 4.3‰, 1σ, n = 6)" — a mean over six WWTP effluent samples with 1σ as the spread across the six, and the effluents are the authors' own: "The wastewater going in (influent) and going out (effluent) of these plants was collected to estimate the impact of water treatment protocols on dissolved Li." Nothing attributes any wastewater value to the literature, so the endmember is LOCALLY MEASURED, which is all attack 4 needs. BUT THE "SAME JULY 2015 CAMPAIGN" IS NOT STATED ANYWHERE IN THE PAPER: the July 2015 sentence covers the river transect only ("We collected 27 samples in July 2015 from 22 sites along a 422 km downstream transect"), no collection date is given for the wastewater, and the paper never says the six effluent samples are among the 27. Withdraw the contemporaneity claim; keep the locality claim. And one finding cuts against this record's framing while strengthening the attack's conclusion: the main text carries NO numeric anthropogenic fraction and no mixing equation — binary mixing is named only qualitatively and the anthropogenic endmember is called "consistent with" wastewater rather than set at 14.5‰ — so Choi is a WEAKER named propagation target than this record describes, which makes limb (ii)'s want of an identified valid target worse, not better. Supplementary Tables were not read.
- THE ELEMENT-SWAP DISGUISE IS NOW A REAL, IDENTIFIED PAPER, AND STILL UNREAD. This record has it as an open risk because neither HAL route opened. It is now fully identified from Crossref: Guinoiseau, D., Louvat, P., Paris, G., Chen, J.-B., Chetelat, B., Rocher, V., Guérin, S. & Gaillardet, J., "Are boron isotopes a reliable tracer of anthropogenic inputs to rivers over time?", Science of the Total Environment 2018;626:1057-1068, doi 10.1016/j.scitotenv.2018.01.159, PMID 29898514. The TITLE alone poses this candidate's question in another element, and that much is verified. ITS CONTENTS ARE NOT: read level RECORD/LANDING PAGE ONLY after seven routes (HAL behind Anubis; doi.org redirects to linkinghub.elsevier.com which returns empty; ScienceDirect robots-disallowed; PubMed errored; Semantic Scholar reports no open-access PDF). The abstract reached the reader only as a summariser's PARAPHRASE of a Semantic Scholar record, and nothing in it — a Seine comparison of 1994-95 against 2006-12, an urban δ11B shift from about −10‰ to +1.5‰, perborate reduction as the attributed cause, urban sources at 60-100% of basin boron — may be quoted or relied on until the full text is read. So the grading moves one step only: from "an open risk" to "a named, dated, peer-reviewed paper whose title poses this question for boron, contents unread". Both adversaries graded attack 2 Resolved without the citation. This reverses nothing, and belongs on the record.
- THE BORROWED-ENDMEMBER ABSENCE: A THIRD SWEEP AGREES, AND ALL THREE ARE THIN. A topic-first reader found no δ7Li apportionment borrowing a literature or industry-average anthropogenic endmember; every study it could open measured locally, including one nobody had — Millot, R. & Desaulty, A.-M., "The impact of waste waters in a small watershed: a view through Lithium isotopes", Goldschmidt 2016 abstract 2085, which sampled the hospital WWTP effluent of l'Egoutier (about 15 km2, Loire basin near Orléans) on site, giving a wastewater endmember of about +4‰ against river water at about −0.5 ± 1‰ (n = 7). But the absence is WEAKLY graded and this record should say so: HAL-BRGM returned Anubis "Access Denied" on both attempts, hiding the Ebro (hal-04077240) and Loire (hal-03113284, hal-01281906) papers — the likeliest places for a borrowed endmember; a coal/CCR lithium-isotope paper (hal-03699877) was seen only as a title; no forward-citation search of Choi 2019 was run; and no compilation of anthropogenic δ7Li endmember values was found that a later study could borrow from. The only literature-borrowed endmembers seen were Li/Ca and Li/Na ratios in Liu-Lu et al. 2022 (Min Jiang, Front. Earth Sci. 10:838867), for NATURAL carbonate and evaporite sources.
- P1's QUOTATION IS A NEAR-MISS and its article number is unconfirmed. The paper says "the database", not "the reference database": "This approach is only possible if robust data on within-deposit variations are available; moreover, the database must be active, as new orebodies of deposit are exploited, new extraction sites are open, and new mining/refining companies enter the market." The article number 4172 was not seen in anything read (the record gives vol. 13(1) with none), and the hydroxide count differs between Methods (10) and the Fig. 4 caption (11). Confirmed and supporting this record: no time index and no production weighting anywhere — the 2020 country production and reserve shares in Fig. 1 are never combined with δ7Li data — and no δ7Li for recycled feedstock.
- P3 VERIFIED ON ITS ABSTRACT, with three qualifications now carried in the prior-art list above: only SEVEN of the 39 reagents were depleted, so the −11 to +3013‰ range mixes ordinary and depleted reagents and this record's "enrichment-contaminated corner of the pool" is right in direction and overstated in degree; the paper reports a MEASURED atomic-weight range rather than deriving an interval; and it does not itself attribute the depletion to industrial enrichment, which matters because this candidate's presupposition narrative leans on enrichment entering the market. The ACS page and the DOI could not be fetched, so the body is unread.

ID: UQ-20261018-08
Date: 2026-10-18
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): Other STEM — fire safety engineering and building-code policy (target field; method from comparative-effectiveness epidemiology / ex-post regulatory evaluation). Source method: cross-field transplant.

Question (canonical): In a jurisdiction holding a retrievable register of performance-based ("alternative solution" / "performance solution" / equivalency) fire-safety approvals joinable to individual buildings, and with frame, covariate set and non-inferiority margin declared before any data pull: (A) for what fraction of buildings in the frame can design pathway be recovered, and how many code-relevant fire incidents accrue to the performance-based stratum, and (B) conditional on (A) clearing a declared power threshold, among buildings in which a fire actually occurred, does the performance-based stratum differ from otherwise-comparable prescriptively designed buildings — matched or weighted on occupancy class, height, construction era and suppression provision — in realized engineering outcomes, with flame and smoke spread beyond the compartment of origin as the primary endpoint and structural damage and casualties secondary?
(V2, the one Gate 1 reformulation. V1, as intaken: "Among buildings in which a fire has actually occurred, do those designed by performance-based fire engineering differ from otherwise-comparable prescriptively designed buildings in realized engineering outcomes — fire and smoke spread beyond the compartment of origin, and structural damage — once occupancy, height, era and suppression provision are matched?" V2 fixes the frame, makes the margin a pre-declaration requirement, and promotes recoverability to limb (A) so the question is answerable whichever way the records fall.)

Alternative formulations:
- Has performance-based fire design ever been evaluated against prescriptive design on field outcomes, rather than on design-stage modelling and cost?
- Treating design pathway as the exposure and the fire incident as the outcome, what is the effect of performance-based design on compartmentation failure in real fires, and can the regime's claim of equivalent safety be tested rather than assumed?

Motivating gap: Performance-based fire design has been permitted for ~30 years on an explicit claim of equivalent safety at lower cost. The question comparative-effectiveness research asks of any alternative regime — does it deliver equivalent outcomes in the population that actually experiences the event? — appears never to have been asked of it with building-level incident data. The field's evidential culture is the verification calculation, the full-scale test and the life-cycle cost model.

Presuppositions:
1. Design pathway is recoverable per building from approval records. CONTESTED — the principal feasibility risk and plausibly the reason for silence. Adversary 2 opened the Victorian BPC/VBA 2024 documentation audit: pathway is recorded per audited permit ("what compliance solution was used, e.g., DtS, performance solution, or a combination of these") but "practitioners are currently not required to lodge this documentation with the VBA" and "the VBA is not a central repository of information". No jurisdiction found with a building-linked queryable register.
2. Incidents linkable to building with spread-extent and damage fields. PARTLY ESTABLISHED — NFIRS and equivalents record spread extent; P1 demonstrates inspector-graded smoke/fire spread collectable at scale.
3. Enough incidents in performance-based buildings to estimate an effect. CONTESTED — hence the power threshold in limb (A).
4. Confounding addressable with recorded covariates. CONTESTED, deepest objection: pathway is chosen BECAUSE the building is atypical (confounding by indication). V2 requires E-value sensitivity analysis; it does not claim identification.
5. A defensible estimand exists. FLAGGED, addressed in V2 by requiring a pre-declared non-inferiority margin.
6. Outcome fields not recorded differentially in performance-based buildings. CONTESTED — large engineered buildings draw investigation teams; needs a measurement-equivalence check or negative-control endpoint.

What would count as an answer: a matched or weighted comparison on a frame and non-inferiority margin declared before any data pull, primary endpoint spread beyond the compartment of origin, with a quantified unmeasured-confounding sensitivity analysis and a measurement-equivalence check; OR a documented demonstration that pathway cannot be recovered for enough buildings to support any comparison — itself an answer, establishing that a thirty-year regime has been unauditable on outcomes by construction, and naming the record-keeping change that would make it auditable.

Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 29 distinct queries — 11 at Gate 2 (full list and 5 fetch attempts in batches/2026-10-18-0352/UQ-20261018-08-record.md), 9 by adversary 1 and 9 by adversary 2 in vocabularies Gate 2 did not try (full lists in UQ-20261018-08-adversary-1.md, -2.md). - "how many buildings approved via performance solutions / share of approvals / register of alternative solutions statistics" (the "how many of X" limb) → NO published count or share in any jurisdiction, and no queryable register; limb (A)'s quantity appears genuinely uncomputed.
- UK: `"fire engineered" buildings "fire strategy" real fire incidents post-fire audit BS 7974` → the Building Safety Regulator Real Fires Investigation Project (opened: 595 incidents 2021-22, 13 investigated in depth, self-described as entailing "reporting bias"); the only mention of fire engineering is a Category 2 escalation criterion, "fire incidents involving 'fire engineered' buildings". Exposure named, never recorded or contrasted. Nearest disguised prior; should be carried as P4.

(The one place a regulator does hold which facilities were approved by equivalency.)

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
P1. Maiworm, Goldner, Mannl & Hammann, "Evaluating 900 Potentially Harming Fires in Germany: Is the Prescriptive Building Code Effective?", Fire Technology 2024;60(3):2041-2065, doi 10.1007/s10694-024-01560-6 — link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10694-024-01560-6 (read at FULL TEXT post-batch). **Cited pre-batch as "Hammann et al." from the portal.fis.tum.de record; that is a mis-citation — the first page prints Björn Maiworm, Moritz Goldner, Kilian Mannl and Claudius Hammann in that order, so Hammann is the LAST author.** Unit: one fire in an existing building, inspected after extinguishing — usually the next day — on a 105-item questionnaire; n=900, 123 fire departments, **24.7%** of the German population (the abstract rounds to about 25%), data August 2016 to July 2022 and ongoing. Endpoint, as the paper names them: smoke spread beyond the unit (about half of fires), fire spread beyond the unit (15.7%, n=141) and to other buildings (3.6%, n=32), injured persons (37.5%, n=807), fatalities (6.6%, n=854), self-rescue before brigade arrival (60.1%, n=898) and **intervention time** (arrival to start of extinguishing, by floor), all per incident. **Two endpoint names in the pre-batch list are wrong: "multiple-casualty risk" is not a named endpoint (the nearest items are a count of simultaneous injuries and an F-N societal-risk curve for Munich), and "response time" is the paper's "intervention time".** Comparator: height and age strata, and the code's own protection objectives. Estimand: descriptive prevalence of protection-objective shortfalls. No performance-based arm; the performance-based code appears only as a forward suggestion — verbatim from the abstract, "authorities could in the future establish a performance-based building code instead of the current prescriptive code." **The central absence is confirmed at full text and with its honest limit: the text records and uses no design-route variable (its variables are use, building class bc 1-5, age, height/storeys, floor of origin, spread and its paths, injuries, fatalities, self-rescue, extinguishing attempts, intervention time; "deviation", "Sonderbau", "approval", "building permit" and "fire protection concept" do not appear), but the 105 questionnaire items are not all listed, so what is established is that the TEXT records and uses no route variable, not that no unlisted item touches it.** One internal inconsistency in the source, single-sourced: the text says Munich contributed 42% of records while Table 1 reportedly lists 481 of 900 (about 53%).
P2. **Chenzhi Ma and Thomas Gernay, "Economic impact of performance-based fire design of composite steel frame structures", Engineering Structures 2025;338:120542, doi 10.1016/j.engstruct.2025.120542** — sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0141029625009332. **Still COULD NOT READ after the verification pass (ScienceDirect robots-disallowed, no open copy); the pre-batch description came from a Johns Hopkins press release and every element of it except the journal and year was wrong.** Cited pre-batch as "Gernay & Ma" because the release lists Gernay first; **Ma is the first author**, and the release gives no title at all. Characterised post-batch from the JHU project pages and an October 2024 project slide deck: unit is modelled prototype buildings with steel-concrete composite floors validated against NIST full-scale tests — **8 typologies across 4 occupancies, office, APARTMENT, HOTEL and hospital, and 130 prototypes** with an 11-storey case study, so the pre-batch "office/hospital/multi-family" is wrong on two of three. **Endpoint: damage states DS1-DS4 from slab deflection ratio, direct/indirect/human losses, CO₂, and 50-year present-value lifetime cost. "Simulated time to failure under a two-hour standard fire" is wrong: time to failure appears only for the physical NIST tests (prescriptive integrity failure at about 90 min; the PBD test reached 120 min and was stopped at 142 min), not as a simulated endpoint, and the analysis is not framed around a two-hour fire as a design endpoint.** Comparator confirmed: Design 1 prescriptive (all beams protected, 60 mm²/m reinforcement), Design 2 (all protected, 230 mm²/m), Design 3 PBD (central beam unprotected, 230 mm²/m, 24% of beams unprotected). Estimand: model-based expected difference in simulated performance and cost. **On the question this entry's exclusion of P2 turns on — whether the paper carries any realized-incident arm — the answer is COULD NOT READ, not NOT FOUND. Nothing contradicts the exclusion and nothing verifies it: the related material's real data are NIST LABORATORY tests used for model validation, and its realized figures are national aggregates used as motivation.** A trap worth naming, because it is how a false discharge of promotion item (ii) would happen: the press release says the model was validated against real NIST fire tests, and those are laboratory experiments, not fires in occupied buildings.
P3. **Johan Lundin, "Safety in Case of Fire — The Effect of Changing Regulations", DOCTORAL THESIS, 446 pages, defended 15 December 2005, Lund University Dept of Fire Safety Engineering and Systems Safety, Report 1032, ISRN LUTVDG/TVBB--1032--SE, ISBN 91-628-6679-6** (supervisor Sven Erik Magnusson, opponent Ben Ale) — vpp.sbuf.se; Boverket confirms the regulatory object. The SBUF 11011 report carries the identical title as its running header, calls itself "this thesis" and has the same summary text, so the two are strongly indicated to be one document, **but that is not confirmed** (the SBUF title page was not seen and the Lund record does not mention SBUF). **Read at PDF level but only PARTIALLY: both PDFs reach the summariser as about 118,500 characters — front matter, summary, contents and early chapters to roughly §2.1.1 — so §4.3.3 "Measures of risk", §5.4.1 and Chapter 10 were never reached, and lup.lub.lu.se is blocked to direct fetching.** Unit confirmed: the building design and design method — documentation from 46 projects, plus an extensive risk analysis of one building class (apparently assembly halls). **Endpoint NOT CONFIRMED: CFAST is certainly used (Appendix B compares it with FDS, Appendix D gives an input file, Appendix E replaces it with a response surface), but §4.3.3 was unread, so "modelled occupant fatality risk", its unit and its denominator must not be treated as established.** Comparator: analytic design vs the risk level implied by prescriptive design, same modelled building. **Estimand correction: what was found is a statement about PRESCRIPTIVE design within one building class — prescriptive design "leads to great variation in risk level within a class of buildings" — not a comparison of variance ACROSS design methods, which is what "level and variance of modelled risk by design method" asserts; those numbers live in the unreachable §5.4.1 and Chapter 10.** The finding this entry leans on IS found, in the Summary: "One dilemma identified is that no unambiguous acceptance criteria have been stated in the building regulations" (probable verbatim; under 125 characters, seen once through a summariser). Realized outcomes appear only as background in §2.1.1 (Swedish Rescue Services Agency statistics, the 1998 Göteborg dance-hall fire and the 2001 WTC fires named as examples, not analysed); no use of them as endpoint or validation was seen, but the analysis chapters were unread, so that absence is not established either.
P4 (added by adversary 1, opened): UK Building Safety Regulator Real Fires Investigation Project — gov.uk/government/collections/real-fires-investigation-project and the 2021-22 summary. Unit: a selected fire incident (13 of 595 in depth). Endpoint: case-by-case building performance including spread beyond the compartment of origin. Comparator: none — the Building Regulations and guidance, judged case by case. Estimand: none; selective case reporting, self-described as entailing reporting bias. Records no design route for any building.

Novelty — how this differs from each: vs P1 — same data layer, same unit, same endpoint family, and no exposure; P1 is the paper that would have stratified by pathway and explicitly did not. vs P2 — same comparator pair, opposite epistemic object: a design on paper with simulated failure time and life-cycle cost, conditioning on no fire having occurred; it supplies the expected-value claim the candidate proposes to test. vs P3 — nearest in intent ("has the regime delivered equivalent safety?"), furthest in method: design documentation and modelled risk dispersion, no realized outcomes, no fired buildings; it establishes that the equivalency claim was never pinned to an acceptance criterion, a precondition of the candidate's margin requirement. vs P4 — same data layer and same regulator audience, and it names the exposure as an escalation trigger, but records no route, has no comparator arm, no estimand and no pooling; it is the strongest evidence that the question is adjacent to live regulatory practice and still unasked in cohort form. Negative recorded in the METHOD-owning vocabularies (ex-post regulatory evaluation, regulatory-policy research, comparative-effectiveness epidemiology, actuarial loss analysis, regulatory economics), not only the data-owning one: those fields name the outcome-data gap programmatically (ICC/Meacham roadmap, WPI research areas) and nothing opened closes it.

Novelty confidence: Medium
(Distinct from all priors on unit, endpoint, comparator and estimand across twelve vocabularies and 29 queries. Held at Medium: P3 asks the same regulatory question in the same field and P4 names the same exposure to the same audience; P2's exclusion rests on an institutional release, not the paper.)

Significance — consequence: If limb (B) runs and non-inferiority holds, a thirty-year regime acquires its first field evidence for a claim it has asserted from models. If non-inferiority fails, a quantified excess in compartmentation failure attaches to a design pathway still being approved. If limb (A) fails, that is not a null but a governance finding: the regime has been unauditable on outcomes by construction, so no incident, inquiry or statistical series since the 1990s could have detected a systematic difference, and the fix is a recorded field rather than a research programme.

Significance — audience: Code bodies with a live decision on pathway scope — ICC, NFPA, ABCB (performance-requirement architecture and the Fire Safety Verification Method), MBIE, the Nordic authorities, and the UK BSR, which already escalates fires in fire-engineered buildings without recording the route. Concretely evidenced rather than invoked: the Victorian regulator is already spending audit resources on this pathway (13 FERs, ~100 performance solutions, 5-10% inadequately developed) with no outcome measure anywhere, and its own non-lodgement finding motivates the cheap action the question names. Also fire services and incident-data custodians, SFPE and the verification-method community (which would gain the acceptance criteria P3 found missing), and insurers, who price engineered buildings with no pathway-stratified loss series.

Significance — fecundity: Once pathway is a joinable exposure: does the design-stage margin in a submitted verification predict realized spread; do particular alternative solutions (atrium smoke exhaust, extended travel distances, ratings traded against suppression) carry distinct field signatures; do real fires in engineered buildings fall inside the design fire scenarios that approved them — the empirical calibration fire safety engineering has never had; does in-service drift from the approved performance basis show up in outcomes; and does the differential-investigation effect bias every existing spread statistic by building size.

Significance — anchoring: The equivalency assumption licensing the whole performance-based regime; P3's finding that no acceptance criteria were ever stated; P1's result that flame spread is controlled while smoke remains the threat, which makes smoke spread the discriminating endpoint; the ICC/Meacham programme to put a risk basis under performance objectives; Shergold-Weir Recs 12 and 14 on a central building-information database and on specifying in occupancy certificates where performance solutions were used; the post-Grenfell question of design-pathway traceability; and ex-post evaluation of performance-based regulation generally, where the NZ weathertightness precedent is the cautionary case.

Reason for silence: A disciplinary boundary reinforced by a records gap and a liability incentive — sharpened by both adversaries, not merely asserted. (a) The exposure field did not exist in approval records: Shergold-Weir Rec 14 (2018) is an instruction to create it, so the cohort form of the question was unaskable. **Post-batch this characterisation is UNVERIFIED: every industry.gov.au copy of the Shergold-Weir report returned ROBOTS_DISALLOWED, Rec 14's text was never obtained, and the one third-party summary opened "confirmed" the phrase by echoing the prompt string back, which is no confirmation at all.** (b) Where regulators do ask about pathway, they ask it as a documentation-quality question ("what compliance solution was used, e.g., DtS, performance solution, or a combination of these") with the records explicitly not lodged centrally, or as selective single-incident escalation (P4, self-described as biased). (c) P3 shows the regime never fixed the quantity that would constitute equivalence, so there is no custodian of the question. (d) The strongest positive evidence of structural silence is P1: a team inspected 900 fires, rendered a verdict on the prescriptive code, and recommended a performance-based code without asking how the buildings already approved that way had fared.

Strongest remaining objection: the two-arm exposure does not exist in the records. **It now rests on ONE of its two legs, which is the stronger one and is confirmed first-hand.** Confirmed leg: the Four readers, each reading the sources this entry cites rather than the adversarial log. **Verdict unchanged at Provisional, and promotion item (ii) is NOT discharged.** What moved underneath it:

Domain(s): Other STEM — planetary science / small-body mission engineering (planetary defence, sample return). Method-owning neighbours: geotechnical blind prediction ("Class A"), calibrated-interval statistics / forecast verification.

Question (canonical): For the small bodies carrying both a dated pre-encounter remote-observable record and a post-encounter in-situ mechanical constraint (Itokawa, 67P, Ryugu, Bennu, Dimorphos), and under a measurand map and reference-standard tier declared per body in advance (A direct measurement, B one-sided bound, C model-inverted): (a) how wide is the narrowest honest prediction interval on near-surface cohesion (and penetration resistance at a declared depth) that a pre-named estimator family — thermal inertia -> particle size -> cohesion, spin-limit cohesion, radar CPR, boulder SFD, slope stability — would have issued from pre-encounter publications only; (b) does that interval contain the post-encounter constraint, per body and probing mode, with the sign of the error recorded; and (c) is it narrower than the gap between the strength regimes that sampling, landing and deflection design distinguish, those thresholds quoted from mission requirement documents rather than assumed to exist? (V1, scored as V2 after the one permitted Gate 1 reformulation; V1's "the in-situ determined near-surface strength" presupposed a single commensurable measurand per body.)

Alternative formulations:
- What is the calibrated uncertainty of remote-sensing-based regolith strength prediction for small bodies, as distinct from its reported qualitative agreement with in-situ results?
- Could a pre-registered blind prediction of near-surface strength from remote data alone be stated with intervals tight enough to be a design input for Hera, Ramses or OSIRIS-APEX, and would it cover?

Motivating gap: In-situ mechanical constraints on small-body surfaces are a seven-year-old class of measurement (Hayabusa2 SCI and MASCOT at Ryugu, the OSIRIS-REx TAG at Bennu, DART at Dimorphos), so whether remote observables predicted them is newly answerable. The only cross-body comparison in print is qualitative: Barnouin's 2024 ISAS curation-symposium abstract S41-3 says the techniques are "successful when compared to assessments of surface interactions" "in many instances", with no error bars, no intervals and no containment statement. Hera arrives at Didymos in 2026-27; Ramses and OSIRIS-APEX must design Apophis operations in 2029 from remote data alone.

Presuppositions: (1) remote and in-situ quantities are comparable measurands — CONTESTED, and the hardest limb; (2) pre-encounter predictions can be reconstructed without hindsight — CONTESTED but checkable; (3) five bodies suffice — CONTESTED, usable n is 2-3 once tiers apply; (4) design distinguishes strength regimes at a stateable numeric resolution — NOT VERIFIED by Gate 2 or by either adversary; (5) in-situ determinations carry characterised uncertainty — PARTLY FALSE (one-sided bounds; Y = 10 to 10^5 Pa as a model input); (6) pre-encounter observables available at comparable quality across the five — CONTESTED (radar CPR, boulder SFD not so for 67P or Dimorphos).

What would count as an answer: a table, per body and probing mode, of the reconstructed pre-encounter prediction with its own uncertainty against the post-encounter constraint tagged by reference tier, giving a signed error in log units and an empirical containment count (not a "rate" over n<=5); plus sealed pre-arrival intervals for Hera at Didymos and Apophis in 2029 so containment is tested prospectively. The informative negative is pre-stated: intervals that contain but are already wider than the named design gap answer in the negative.

Verification (post-batch, fresh-context readers, 2026-10-18):

Five readers, each reading this entry's cited sources rather than the adversarial log. **Verdict unchanged: Rejected, attack 4 Unresolved from adversary 1. The ground survives and is strengthened; three decorations fall and the novelty grade narrows without lifting.**

**The ground holds from three directions.** No containment statement exists in Barnouin et al. 2024 (three targeted prompts), no comparison with any pre-encounter prediction exists in Raducan et al. 2024 (no β prediction, no Stickle 2022 or Raducan 2022 result, no signed error, no ratio; agreement stated qualitatively as "most consistent with observations"), and no signed error, remote-to-in-situ ratio or containment statement exists in Groussin et al. 2019 to the start of §3.3. A topic sweep found **no pooled audit anywhere and no study reporting a containment rate**. Every strength figure in both Didymos papers is confirmed one-sided; two-sided intervals exist only for other quantities (β 2.2-4.9, ejecta mass 1.3-2.2×10⁷ kg, opening angle 115-139°, macroporosity 38±3% and 34±4%), and bulk density is itself an upper bound (<2400 kg/m³).

**What fell, all of it decoration:**
1. **The "~50-500 Pa sliding bound" does not exist** — the largest single correction in this batch. Three distinct figures were described as one sliding bound; the paper attaches no number to the porosity/density dependence, only a direction.
2. **Rivkin is the LAST author of prior 2**, not the first, and the self-disqualification applies to the crater-scaling Y values (1300, 40, 5 Pa), not to the headline <0.9 Pa. The Bennu "good match" is to the Factor-of-Safety method, not to a number.
3. **Three of five quoted strings are paraphrases** (Raducan's "similar to Ryugu and Bennu", Groussin's "about 10 kPa or less", and "less than a few Pa" left unverified), and the MUPUS 2 MPa is a lower bound at one penetration site. **One figure sat on the wrong source**: the "cohesion 1-2 Pa" is Vincent et al. 2017's, not Groussin 2015's (whose own figure is 4-30 Pa).
4. **Prior 3's "side by side" framing is withdrawn**, and its scale-dependence link to the remote-versus-in-situ gap is the adversary's inference, not the paper's.

**Two new priors nobody had**, both formal pre-encounter-versus-in-situ tables in the target field: Lauretta 2019's DRA scorecard and arXiv:2502.14990's Table 2. They narrow the novelty grade and do not remove it, for the reasons set out at Novelty confidence. **And one finding that cuts the candidate's way: on the reader's arithmetic over Lauretta's own table, pole declination AND largest boulder size fall OUTSIDE the pre-encounter 1σ, while the paper's text says the rotation period, obliquity and pole are "within the 1σ uncertainties of the ground-based values" and a footnote says "Most values are well within 1σ". The one existing scorecard misstates its own containment** — which is the gap this candidate points at, found inside its nearest prior. That does not revive the entry, because attack 4 is about the estimand being undefined for mechanical properties, and strength appears in neither scorecard.

Status: Provisional
Domain(s): Other STEM — electrical metrology / power engineering; secondary legal metrology (method owner: sampling inspection in legal metrology)
Question (canonical): For one declared national installed base of static residential electricity meters, taking a probability sample stratified by meter model, firmware revision and build year from a distribution utility's asset register, and applying a pre-declared library of residential load mixes synthesised from a published appliance current-waveform set against a reference instrument whose immunity to those same stimuli is demonstrated rather than assumed: what is the population-weighted distribution of relative registration error per mix (mean with CI, plus lower and upper tail quantiles), and, under a declared national load-composition model, what fraction of billed residential energy does that distribution imply is misregistered? (v2; the one permitted Gate 1 reformulation of v1, which asked the same thing without a sampling frame, a declared mix library, a demonstrated-immune reference, or the conditional status of the billed-energy limb.)
Alternative formulations:
1. Do the waveforms used in meter type approval and periodic sample testing represent the loads meters actually see, and what does the installed base register under realistic household load mixes?
2. Is there any population-level estimate of static-meter over- and under-registration, as opposed to laboratory demonstrations that large errors can occur?
Motivating gap: The field is dense with how-to-answer apparatus (IEC 62052/62053, EN 50470, utility periodic sample testing, verification procedures) and appears empty of the population value. The anomaly is on record — Leferink/Keyer/Melentjev reported -32% to +582% on mixes of common consumer electronics (IEEE EMC Magazine, 2016), disputed, partly replicated by VSL/UTwente, and followed by standards activity — and the party holding the asset register has publicly asserted the null from complaint counts without an estimate.
Presuppositions: P1 effect real, not a 2016 setup artefact — now supported independently of 2016 (VSL/UTwente deck; INRIM 2024 found one of six DUTs between **24.35% and 25.11%** — a range, not "about +25%" — under a LABORATORY REPRODUCTION of a recorded field waveform, and its DUTs are anonymised by class rather than named models; **arXiv 2601.16612 is DEMOTED as support here: it does find discrepancies across three anonymised manufacturers, but its stimulus is a synthesised two-component VOLTAGE signal and its outputs are voltage-based power-quality indicators (P_st flicker, THD, fundamental frequency), with no current-channel or distorted-current test and no crest factor anywhere, so it supports "errors across manufacturers under non-ideal conditions" and NOT error under distorted CURRENT waveforms, which is this candidate's exposure**). P2 error reproducible enough to pre-declare a mix — supported in outline (MeterEMI waveform library and testbed). P3 register supports model/build-year strata — EVIDENCED (Dutch steekproefcontrole; Eversource files lot sizes from installed meter counts per model); firmware strata unevidenced. P4 a demonstrably immune reference exists — established in outline, to be shown per mix. P5 in-service testing uses conditions under which the effect cannot appear — now evidenced twice beyond the Dutch document (Eversource's NH PUC filing states no amperes, power factor or waveform; arXiv 2601.16612: verification is "performed under ideal conditions or with simple signal models", IEC 62053-24 testing "only a 5-th order harmonic") but still by omission. P6 misregistration not already absorbed in loss accounting — UNEXAMINED; a loss-accounting sweep found no decomposition of unaccounted-for energy into a metering component. P7 household composition has shifted — in outline only; no household field-waveform evidence was opened, and the one field waveform tested (INRIM) came from a 50 kW PV site, not a home.
What would count as an answer: an error distribution measured on a probability sample of in-service meters drawn by model/firmware/build-year strata from a real asset register, against a reference with demonstrated immunity, under a pre-declared mix library — population-weighted mean relative error with CIs and tail quantiles per mix, plus a conditional energy-weighted misregistered fraction under a declared composition model. The null (distribution inside the class limit, thin tails) is pre-specified, decisive and publishable, and is what the incumbents already assert.

Significance — consequence: if the distribution has material mass outside the class limit under declared realistic mixes, the in-service sampling regime is measuring under a stimulus that cannot reveal it (so conforming and misregistering populations are indistinguishable under it), the draft waveforms handed to CENELEC/IEC/OIML become calibrated against measured population harm rather than precautionary, and a two-signed error opens a transfer-between-customers problem rather than a net-overcharge one. The null is equally consequential and is the incumbents' own position: it closes a dispute running since 2016 and redirects the work to specific appliance classes.
Significance — audience: NMIs already staffed on this object (VSL, PTB, NPL, METAS, INRIM); verification and market-surveillance authorities with a standing annual decision the answer feeds (RDI's rejected-population lists, UK OPSS/IST, US state PUCs receiving annual meter-testing filings, German/Austrian recertification-extension sampling); the standards bodies named by MeterEMI; DSOs and energy regulators; consumer bodies. They are demonstrably already acting with the estimate missing.
Significance — fecundity: whether registration error is socially patterned (dimmer/LED/heat-pump/EV penetration, income); whether decades of steekproefcontrole and Z1.9 data can be re-analysed as error distributions; the sign distribution and hence cross-subsidy vs loss; how much DSO non-technical loss is misregistration; transfer to gas, water, heat, PV and EV submetering and to the 2-150 kHz band; how to make a mix library auditable so "realistic" is contestable rather than the testing party's choice.
Significance — anchoring: the 2016 Leferink anomaly and its unresolved dispute; the 2-150 kHz supraharmonic emission/immunity gap; the acceptance-sampling-versus-estimation distinction in legal metrology; MID 2014/32/EU and the OIML R46 revision; non-technical-loss accounting.

Promotion item (i) is NOT discharged — but the route is now found and the mechanical cause of six readers' failures is known.** Three supporting legs are demoted, four dates or identities corrected, and one new document supplies what this entry was citing a two-page explainer for.

**The MeterEMI failure has a cause, not a mystery.** Both deliverables are linked from the EURAMET project page and the fetch proxy refuses their URLs for exceeding its maximum fetchable length. That is recorded in promotion item (i) with the untried short-link routes, so the next pass starts there instead of searching again. The project coordinator is NPL, not VSL. **One permission-classifier refusal occurred on this candidate — a request to read the agent proxy's own status page — and was recorded and not retried, not counted as a check that ran.**

**The three demotions:**
1. **arXiv:2601.16612 is a real paper about a different subject.** It is Bracale, Janowicz, Kuwałek & Wiczyński, "Challenges in the Proper Metrological Verification of Smart Energy Meters", and its stimulus is a synthesised two-component VOLTAGE signal with voltage-based power-quality outputs — no current-channel test, no crest factor (its own "fc" is the fundamental frequency in hertz). It supports errors across manufacturers under non-ideal conditions, not error under distorted current waveforms.
2. **The VSL/UTwente deck documents no selection method**, in all 37 slides, so the novelty difference "convenience selection vs probability sample" is an assertion on both sides. It also carries no per-specimen error magnitudes, only signs.
3. **Eversource names no test points at all**, so the "sinusoidal or single-harmonic" parenthetical is withdrawn from that source and re-sourced to the Kiwa load-point scheme (itself an inference) and to IEC 62053-24 as quoted in arXiv 2601.16612.

**What was confirmed and is stronger than described:** INRIM 2024 is fully identified (Cultrera et al., Energies 2024;17(6):1403) and read at full text, with its central contrast verbatim and the figure a RANGE of 24.35-25.11% rather than a point; the Eversource Z1.9 per-lot table exists as described, with the quoted Centron row correct but n = 201 the quantity tested against a plan size of 200; and the Dutch stratification by "soort, type en bouwjaar" is verbatim, with firmware absent, which confirms this entry's "firmware strata unevidenced".

**What weakened the record's own falsification claim:** every estimated percent nonconforming in the Eversource table is ZERO across all six lots, and the report nowhere claims to publish an error distribution. The falsification holds in form — a Z1.9 variables plan does publish moments per lot — and was generous in substance.

**One new document:** Kiwa's "Statistische controle kWh-meters: Populatiebesluit controlejaar 2024" (GT-250023, 25 March 2025), which publishes per-population statistics and the load points this entry wanted, and which never states a waveform.

Four dates or identities were wrong: the Steekproefcontrole document is 6 July 2021 and not 2024, the grid-operators' response is probably 2017 and not 2023, the Eversource docket is DE 18-162 and not IR, and the deck's event is the KIVI EMC-ESD event of 21 November 2023. None of them touches the verdict: the entry is Provisional on well-posedness 2/3, an Unverified attack-2 near-duplicate check and an Unresolved attack 7, and all three survive this pass intact — the near-duplicate check is still Unverified for the same document, now for a known reason.

Domain(s): AI architecture — sparse mixture-of-experts design and MoE inference systems (secondary: multilingual evaluation).
Question (canonical): For released sparse-MoE checkpoints run at inference under a declared drop rule (R1 arrival-order overflow; R2 lowest-gating-score drop) at C>=3 capacity factors on M>=2 checkpoints, with strata pre-declared (language/script, document domain, token-frequency decile, position bucket): (a) does the joint distribution of drop events over strata depart from the marginal input distribution over the same strata under a pre-declared exchangeability/permutation test with per-stratum drop-rate intervals; and (b) in a paired contrast against a capacity-free run on identical inputs, weights and decoding, is each stratum's loss/accuracy delta a positive function of that stratum's drop rate — a slope, against an in-harness evaluation-and-seed noise floor, that lets an operator forecast a capacity factor's incidence before shipping it? (V2, the one permitted Gate 1 reformulation; V1 left the drop rule, the noise floor and the frequency proxy unspecified — see record.)
Alternative formulations: When an MoE discards tokens to meet an expert-capacity limit, who pays — is the reported aggregate degradation spread evenly or is it a tax with an identifiable incidence? / Is MoE token dropping distributionally neutral, or can the per-stratum accuracy penalty be read off the per-stratum drop rate?
Motivating gap: Capacity-Aware Inference (arXiv:2503.05066, ICLR 2026) reports ~30% MoE-layer speedup on OLMoE for "0.9% performance degradation" and +0.2%/1.85x on Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct as single averages; full text read (alphaxiv route) confirms it characterises dropped tokens only by importance score, arrival order and modality, and breaks results down by benchmark/capability — task categories, never token categories. AMENDED at Gate 2: the intake premise that the field holds no characterisation of the dropped set is withdrawn — OpenMoE (arXiv:2402.01739) names and measures the phenomenon ("Drop-towards-the-End"). Live residue: nothing opened measures a per-stratum penalty against a capacity-free run, or any slope of penalty on drop rate.
Presuppositions: (1) capacity-limited dropping is deployed where it matters — CONTESTED and not strengthened (Q10, Adv-1 D6/D3 and Adv-2 q7 all found inference run dropless: DeepSeek-V2 "do not drop any tokens for evaluation"; Huang et al. 2303.06182 capacity factor "usually set at high values during inference"); (2) drop events loggable per token without altering behaviour — ESTABLISHED; (3) strata pre-declarable — ESTABLISHED, frequency must be a declared tokenizer/eval-corpus proxy for closed-corpus checkpoints; (4) a capacity-free reference exists on identical inputs/weights — ESTABLISHED for dropless-trained checkpoints, FLAGGED asymmetric for capacity-trained ones; (5) per-stratum effects near a ~0.9% aggregate are resolvable above evaluation noise — CONTESTED, plausibly binding, but on a different source after verification: Switch's "typically < 1%" is not a rate at a stated capacity factor, while the anchor's own published rates run 2% to 12% by rule and capacity factor; (6) routing is input-dependent in a way correlating with the strata — ESTABLISHED (arXiv:2510.04694; OpenMoE token-ID specialization), which cuts against novelty, not for it; (7) the drop rule is a factor, not a nuisance — ESTABLISHED by the anchor's Order/Score ablation and by Megatron-Core's shipped `moe_token_drop_policy: Literal['probs','position']`.
What would count as an answer: A measured joint distribution of drop events over the pre-declared strata vs the marginal input distribution, with a pre-declared permutation test and per-stratum intervals; plus a paired per-stratum loss/accuracy delta (capacity-limited vs capacity-free, same inputs/weights/decoding) regressed on that stratum's drop rate, crossed over M>=2 checkpoints x C>=3 capacity factors x R=2 rules, the slope judged against an in-harness noise floor. "No" = flat drop rates within intervals and no slope above the floor. "Yes" = a named stratum ordering plus a slope with a usable forecast interval.

No adversary had returned a fatal status on this candidate, so the rejection is the judge's Gate 2 call and no late Gate 4 is owed; the Gate 2 ground was instead re-tested at first hand and survived, narrowed in two places and strengthened in one.
HOLDS. OpenMoE's five quoted strings are all verbatim, including the grammar of "We found that this probably be caused by the token drop of a long sequence"; Fig. 12's caption is "Comparing the ratio of tokens dropped at different position IDs", panel (a) "Different datasets" (RedPajama, TheStack, Multilingual TED, MTBench) and panel (b) before and after supervised fine-tuning, with y = Token Drop Ratio (%) and no numeric drop rate anywhere in the text. So limb (a) is asked, named and descriptively measured for TWO strata only — position ID and dataset category. Language, script and token frequency are NOT measured: the multilingual curve is one aggregate dataset line, the per-language material (Fig. 7, Table 10) is routing and token counts rather than drop rate, and the token-identity claim is the hypothetical newline example. There is no capacity-free arm ("dropless" and "capacity factor" do not appear), no penalty attributed to drops, and no intervals. The layer and the pooling for Fig. 12 are NOT STATED, which the entry did not say. Capacity-Aware Inference's finest accuracy grain is confirmed as the benchmark sub-category (MMBench's six capabilities, SEED-Bench dimensions), with its finest non-accuracy grain the dropped-token percentage per layer, per capacity factor and per dataset (App. G, Figs. 17-20) and its baseline a true gamma = infinity arm; its ICLR 2026 venue is on the PDF running header. So the residue the entry claims is unoccupied is confirmed unoccupied: no source opened, in four independent sweeps, measures a per-stratum penalty against a capacity-free run or any slope of penalty on drop rate.
NARROWED. The Switch Transformer parenthetical is verbatim in Sec. 2.2 but it is not what Gate 5 took it for: "we didn't notice any dependency on the number of experts for the number of tokens dropped (typically < 1%)" states the absence of a dependency on the number of experts, with no capacity factor, model size, step or aggregation attached, and Table 1's capacity factors 2.0/1.25/1.0 report no drop rates at all. It is therefore not a published drop rate, and presupposition 5's "plausibly binding" contest loses that support; the published per-capacity-factor rates are the anchor's instead (2% for Expert Drop against 12% for Token Drop on OLMoE-Instruct, Sec. 5.2, and the per-dataset per-layer curves of App. G). Two further details of Switch cut the candidate's way rather than against it: its Appendix F code keeps only the tokens that fit in arrival order within the core, so the drop rule there is position, not gate score; and its Appendix B No-Token-Left-Behind rerouting of overflow tokens "found no empirical benefits", which is a policy comparison and not a capped-against-uncapped measurement.
STRENGTHENED AGAINST THE CANDIDATE. A by-subject reader found a stratified incidence measure the batch missed entirely: LIMoE (arXiv:2206.02770) reports a per-MODALITY "success rate" — the share of tokens not dropped, image against text, at layer 9 — and compares dispatch orders on validation accuracy (batch-prioritized routing about 70%, shuffled 56%, image-first 42%). That is a third stratum type with an outcome attached, closer to limb (a) than anything the entry credits, though still with no capacity-free comparator (its evaluation uses a high slack factor) and no position or frequency analysis. It makes the Gate 2 rejection firmer, not weaker.
Read levels: OpenMoE FULL TEXT via summariser (HTML v1 and PDF extraction; figure pixels not seen, axis labels from extracted text); Switch Transformer FULL TEXT via summariser, the Sec. 2.2 sentence confirmed on three independent fetches; Capacity-Aware Inference PDF via summariser (whole paper queried); LIMoE PDF via summariser, author line not checked against the first page; 2605.17598 and 2303.06182 read in full and neither mentions capacity or dropping. ID: UQ-20261018-12
Date: 2026-10-18
Status: Rejected
Domain(s): AI architecture — training systems; optimizer implementation and numerics. Neighbour vocabularies reached: numerical analysis (stagnation/absorption/compensated summation), communication-efficient distributed ML, DSP adaptive filtering (stalling), QAT, analog in-memory training, provenance auditing.
Question (canonical): In shipped low-precision training configurations (BF16 parameters with BF16 or block-quantized 8-bit optimizer state, versus FP32 master weights), what fraction of (parameter, step) update attempts leaves the parameter bitwise unchanged ("annihilation") or materially deviant from an FP32-master-weight replay ("distortion"), is that fraction concentrated on identifiable parameter groups (rare-token embedding rows, normalization gains, small-magnitude weights, attention vs MLP), and does it rise as the learning rate decays? (V2, the one permitted Gate 1 reformulation, declares the configuration frame, a bitwise annihilation definition, a pre-declared distortion threshold, the parameter partition and a seed band; full text in batches/2026-10-18-0619/UQ-20261018-12-record.md.)
Alternative formulations: (1) How many of a run's updates never land, and which parameters quietly stop learning before the run ends? (2) Numerical-analysis words: what is the realized stagnation rate of the weight-update recurrence in shipped low-precision optimizers, stratified by operand magnitude? (3) Distributed-systems words: what per-step weight-update sparsity does BF16 absorption induce, and is the pattern structured by module?
Motivating gap: Inverts the presupposition that a computed update changes the parameter it is applied to. The claimed gap was that the ecosystem ships mitigations (Kahan summation in torchao/optimi, stochastic rounding, FP32 master weights by default in Megatron/DeepSpeed, bitsandbytes block-quantized state plus stable-embedding layer) whose necessity has never been quantified in a real LLM run. FALSE AS STATED: the realized rate is published at five scales with the ulp mechanism named (arXiv 2602.03839), independently at seven scales (arXiv 2602.11456), by module group and magnitude decile at the end-checkpoint unit (arXiv 2606.13657), and with matched compensated/FP32-master arms on held-out perplexity at 125M-7B two years earlier (arXiv 2405.03637, COLLAGE, ICML 2024).
Presuppositions: (1) Annihilation measurable per (parameter, step) by bitwise comparison — ESTABLISHED, and operationalised in print (2602.03839 Def. A.2). (2) BF16-master / 8-bit-state configurations carry a stake — contested at intake, frame declared in V2; RL post-training at lr ~1e-6 is inside it. (3) Not already eliminated by default — NOT eliminated: ~99% per step in the RL regime. (4) "Effectively frozen" has a behavioural consequence — contested, and the record's claim that this is the candidate's "one genuinely unmeasured limb" is FALSIFIED by COLLAGE's Option D matched arms. (5) Instrumentation does not alter the update path — satisfied by construction. (6) LR decay drives the rate monotonically — left as a prediction; no schedule-phase study found. (7) Concentration on small-magnitude weights — FALSIFIED IN DIRECTION: ulp scales with |w|, so a fixed update is less likely to be absorbed on a small weight, and 2606.13657 finds visible updates over-represented on the bottom magnitude decile.
What would count as an answer: Measured annihilation and distortion rates per (configuration, parameter group, training-phase bin) from instrumented runs at >= 2 scales in pretraining, SFT and RL, with incidence structure named, plus matched Kahan / stochastic-rounding / FP32-master arms at the same seed and data order giving held-out loss per group. "Nothing here" = rate below ~1e-4 outside the final decay, no group concentration, no matched-arm loss gap.
