That is the group-stratified, schedule-dependent, attempt-level measurement this candidate advertises as missing, with the gradient-shrinkage control arm the candidate treats as its own methodological contribution. Reinforced by arXiv 2607.09800, which supplies the same per-coordinate definition and estimand in transformer pretraining with an attention-against-MLP breakdown. What remains is an unanswered sub-question of an asked question, which is an open problem rather than an un-asked one. Well-posedness and the declared estimand survive intact; novelty does not.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): the residue, not this question — re-run Prior 1's Def. A.2 instrument inside one open pretraining stack across a full cosine schedule with the parameter-group partition declared in advance, and read COLLAGE Figure 3 and Prior 1 Section G.3 (the LR sweep neither adversary's fetch reached) before scoping it.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): Primary limb → already ANSWERED, not routed: arXiv 2602.03839 (per-step bitwise-unchanged fraction ~99%, five models 0.5B-7B), arXiv 2602.11456 (independent, seven models 4B-72B, nonzero ratio 0.93-2.56%), arXiv 2606.13657 (end-checkpoint unchanged fraction by module group, NOT by magnitude decile — see the verification block), arXiv 2010.06192 App. D.3 (per-iteration cancelled-update percentage, embedding against linear, with a constant-LR control arm) and arXiv 2607.09800 (per-step frozen fraction in transformer pretraining, attention against feed-forward, plus a three-seed held-out-loss rounding arm). Residual limbs → asked-but-open, routed to ledger/routed-open-problems.md as one tier-B row: per-group behavioural consequence, LR-schedule-phase dependence in pretraining and SFT, block-quantized 8-bit optimizer state, and embedding-row incidence binned by training-corpus token frequency. The in-batch narrowing that struck the aggregate matched-arm limb because COLLAGE supplies it is WITHDRAWN on verification — COLLAGE's arms are not master-weights-only — but the limb stays struck anyway, because arXiv 2607.09800 Table 5 supplies a three-seed held-out-loss rounding arm in transformer pretraining. What the late pass adds to the routed row: no paper measures the per-step frozen fraction in the frame this candidate declares (BF16 parameters with BF16 or block-quantized 8-bit Adam state) across a full schedule in pretraining at two or more scales, because the one paper that measures it in transformers keeps the optimizer state in fp32 and the one that quantizes the state keeps the weights in BF16.

Verification and late Gate 4 (post-batch, fresh-context agents, 2026-10-18): five readers opened the four cited priors and swept the subject cold; the Gate 2 ground then failed first-hand verification, so Gate 4 ran LATE AND SEPARATELY, two cold adversaries at all eight attacks on the Gate 0-3 record with the Gate 2 grade and the struck verdict declared void; three further readers then checked the late kill's own sources at first hand. VERDICT UNCHANGED, GROUND REPLACED. Both cold adversaries returned attack 2 Unresolved and one returned attack 4 Unresolved, so the fatal rule rejects the candidate again — but on papers neither the batch nor the first verification pass had opened, and none of the three sources the struck verdict rested on survives in the role it was given.
WHAT FELL. (a) Prior 3 does NOT report the bitwise-unchanged fraction by magnitude DECILE: the word decile appears in neither its v2 nor its v3 rendering, its module-group table reports a relative delta NORM rather than a zero fraction, and its per-layer sparsity exists only as an unlabelled figure. The "Table 8" cited above is in neither version (v3's exact-zero column is Table 9, 12 rows, 3.06-84.65; v2's is Table 2 at a 1e-5 tolerance, 10 rows, 3.06-89.50), and the figures 86.50 and 64.13 appear in neither — the 3.06-86.50 range should not have been written. Its nearest magnitude analysis is a bottom-10%-source-magnitude COVERAGE metric, its unit is the end-checkpoint delta in post-training, and its stated direction is the opposite of the candidate's: updates "preferentially occupy coordinates where the source weight was small in magnitude" (App. D.2), 36.68% coverage against a 10% baseline. (b) COLLAGE's Def. 3.3 is NOT a deviation: it is an inner product of the normalised intended update with the effective one, which the paper itself calls "projection of the effective update along the desired update". Its imprecision percentage is pooled "for all model parameters" per iteration with no group breakdown, and nothing in it links imprecision to a frozen group or to LR decay. Its arm A against arm D differs in more than master weights, since D also carries FP32 optimizer states, so it is not the clean matched arm the strongest-objection paragraph claimed. (c) AuroraRL's "0.93-2.56%" is stated as a range nowhere in that paper: it stitches a Table 4 algorithm cell (RLOO on Qwen3-8B, 0.93) to a Figure 3 model cell (Llama3-8B, 2.56), and its rho is the share of elements that CHANGE, not the unchanged share. (d) Prior 1 holds on its own terms — Def. A.2, ~99% per step over 400 steps at five models, step SD 0.2-0.4%, |w|_crit 7.68e-4 at lr 3e-6 — but it is RL fine-tuning only, aggregate-only with no group breakdown, and its Figure 8 is not a matched arm on a held-out metric.
WHAT REPLACED IT, read at first hand. **arXiv:2010.06192 App. D.3 / Figure 9, opened independently by BOTH cold adversaries** after the first pass had it as COULD NOT READ through two truncated ar5iv attempts. Its caption reads "The percentage of weight updates that are non-zero but get canceled in the standard 16-bit-FPU training", in four panels splitting an EMBEDDING layer from a LINEAR layer on two datasets; the text says the percentage "increases as the training progresses" and "can be larger than 80% in the mid-to-late training stage"; and it DECOMPOSES the rise by design, attributing the constant-LR run's rise to shrinking gradient magnitude and the other run's to "the compound effect from decaying gradient magnitude and decaying learning rates". That is the candidate's attempt-level, group-stratified, LR-decay-connected measurement, with a constant-LR control arm, published in 2020. **arXiv:2607.09800** (sole author Zekai Shang, UIUC), which this entry dismissed at abstract level as grounding nothing, is the candidate's definition and estimand almost exactly: Sec. 2.1 Eq. (1) is Q_m(q_i + d_i) = q_i, decoded-grid equality of the stored code before and after one update, with the paper's own phrase "The executable exact event is decoded-grid value equality"; f_t is "the fraction frozen on step t" (computable proxy Eq. 4); it runs nanoGPT GPT-2 124M on OpenWebText at 3,000 and 10,000 steps and two 162.2M decoders, i.e. transformer PRETRAINING from scratch; it stratifies by attention against feed-forward and by a Core/All-2-D scope (Table 7: Core 65.87% and 65.83% never-moved under RNE); and its Table 5 is a three-seed held-out-loss SR-against-RNE arm with 95.6-98.9% gap recovery at 3,000 steps, Table 6 the two-seed 10,000-step version at 89-92%. A third independent reader confirmed every one of those items. Two late findings qualify it and are recorded rather than waived: nearly every number it TABULATES is the cumulative never-moved fraction, which the paper itself distinguishes from f_t; and in all but two studies the low precision is an analytic grid held in fp32 containers with fp32 compute and fp32 optimizer moments, so it measures a write-back quantization event rather than a native low-precision configuration.
WHAT THE LATE PASS DID NOT ESTABLISH. The third reader killed two supporting claims of the second adversary: arXiv:2605.07330 (SparseRL-Sync) does carry "tends to increase over training" verbatim and 99.30-99.40% BF16 sparsity at 30B with at least 98% up to 671B, but it has NO per-tensor or per-group breakdown of sparsity anywhere, and the phrase "learning rate" does not appear in it at all, so it supports the rising-sparsity direction in one sentence with no schedule analysis and no mechanism. And arXiv:2603.16731 (Topollai and Choromanska, C4 pretraining at 60M/100M/350M plus a 1B run) is real with its Definition 3.1 on the optimizer-state unit, but the "0.825-1.000 theoretical range" quoted to the judge splices two tables and two rounding modes (round-to-nearest 0.946-1.000, stochastic rounding 0.825-0.994), the "0.17-0.97 empirical floor" is not an interval but three format endpoints of one measured row, and it carries no stratification by parameter group, decile, normalization gains or token frequency and no link to the learning-rate schedule.
LATE GATE 4 STATUSES (adversary 1 / adversary 2, both cold, 8 and 7 searches, 5 and 6 fetches): 1 Triviality Partial / Partial; 2 Disguise **Unresolved / Unresolved (FATAL, both)**; 3 Combinatorial novelty Resolved / Resolved; 4 Presupposition failure **Unresolved** / Partial (fatal on the worse of the two); 5 Vagueness Resolved / Resolved; 6 Significance inflation Resolved / Resolved; 7 Reason for silence Unresolved / Partial; 8 Dissolution Partial / Partial. Attack 4's legs, each now sourced: the motivating gap's "no reported realized annihilation rate" is false in RL and in transformer pretraining; the small-magnitude concentration is backwards both by the ulp arithmetic and by Prior 3's measured direction; and the normalization-gain limb is closer to moot than open, because the one paper that measures the event in transformers keeps 1-D normalization parameters in fp32, outside the quantized write-back path entirely, so the breakdown could not be formed there even in principle. Attack 3 is worth recording as Resolved for the opposite reason to the one alleged: the interface is crowded, not empty, and the same crowding is what makes attack 2 fatal.
THE RESIDUE THAT SURVIVES, and why it is a routing rather than an entry. No paper measures the per-step frozen fraction in the configuration this candidate actually declares — BF16 parameters with BF16 or block-quantized 8-bit Adam state — across a full cosine schedule, in pretraining, at two or more scales: 2607.09800 keeps the optimizer state in fp32 and mostly emulates the grid in fp32 containers, 2603.16731 is its mirror image and quantizes only the state while the weights stay BF16, 2602.03839 is constant-LR RL, 2605.07330 is RL fine-tuning. No source stratifies by normalization gains, by weight-magnitude decile, or by token-frequency-binned embedding rows. And the LR-schedule link exists only on the DLRM unit. Both adversaries converge on routing that residue, and the row is appended.
Read levels for the late pass: 2010.06192 PDF via summariser including App. D.3, read twice independently, with the Figure 9 panel values COULD NOT READ beyond the axis ranges; 2607.09800 FULL TEXT via the v4 HTML, characters 0-100,000 of 104,782, the tail unread, its PDF returning "[This PDF is empty or contains no machine-readable text]"; 2605.07330 FULL TEXT; 2603.16731 FULL TEXT via the v2 HTML. One identity defect to carry: 2607.09800's title DIFFERS between its abs page ("Auditing Invisible Weight Updates with Reference Traces") and the document's own first page ("Reference Traces for Auditing Invisible Weight Updates and Guiding Exact-Budget Protection"), both current surfaces of v4, and a third-party mirror carries it under a third title; the sole author is the same on both arXiv surfaces. The paper is also candid that its own aggregate forecasts and allocator claims fail their predeclared gates in about twenty places including its conclusion — the parts this kill rests on, the freeze definition, the group breakdown and the rounding-arm loss table, are the parts it reports as working.

Status: Rejected
Domain(s): AI architecture — training-systems experimental methodology (pretraining ablation practice; within-run loss telemetry). Source method: cross-field transplant from time-and-frequency metrology / inertial-sensor characterization (overlapping Allan deviation, noise-type identification, Allan-variance-informed optimal averaging window). Target field deciding novelty: AI architecture.
Question (canonical): For a pre-registered frame of public pretraining runs with step-resolution loss logs (>= 10 runs, >= 3 scales), with detrending pre-declared as one primary estimator plus two sensitivity arms and tau bounded by the overlapping-Allan estimator's CI at that run's length: (i) what is the fitted log-log slope mu of sigma_y(tau) of the detrended residuals per declared phase (warmup/stable/cooldown), which canonical noise type does it identify (white -1/2, flicker 0, random-walk +1/2), and where is the sigma_y minimum; (ii) where the mixture is white-plus-random-walk, what is the Allan-variance-informed optimal window tau*, and how does it compare with the windows published ablation reports use (EMA 0.9/0.99, mean of last k) and the step counts at which they call A-vs-B; (iii) against ground truth from seed-replicated pairs, what are the realized false-decision rates of a tau*-window rule versus the conventional windows? (V0 at intake and V1 after the one permitted Gate 1 reformulation are both in the record.)
Alternative formulations: (1) At what averaging time does smoothing a loss curve stop removing noise and start hiding real drift? (2) Does a training loss curve have a measurable noise floor and a drift regime, and are recipe decisions being made inside the regime where averaging cannot help?
Motivating gap: "Is recipe A better than B" is decided constantly from smoothed loss curves with windows (EMA 0.9/0.99, mean-of-last-k) chosen by convention and never justified; metrology has a standard answer to "how long should I average" (noise-type identification by Allan slope; a closed-form optimal window for white-plus-random-walk, Haeri/Soleimani/Jerath, ACC 2022). Ledger differentiation: UQ-20261017-27 is between-configuration/between-seed variance, UQ-20261017-28 is within-step batch-formation design effect; this claimed the third axis, within-run temporal noise. 155 INDEX entries plus a keyword grep: no duplicate.
Presuppositions: P1 logging cadence regular enough and runs long enough for an overlapping-Allan estimate (CONTESTED; N1 logs on a deliberately non-uniform grid). P2 Allan variance applicable despite a strong deterministic trend if run on detrended residuals (CONTESTED, load-bearing). P3 noise type stable enough within a phase (CONTESTED). P4 step-resolution logs retrievable for >= 10 public runs (unverified). **P5 "two runs differ" is the decision the field actually makes from these windowed curves (graded DEFENSIBLE in the record; FALSIFIED on the opened evidence — see Adversarial log row 4; this is the ground of rejection).** P6 seed-replicated pairs available as ground truth (CONTESTED in availability). P7 the imported theorem assumes white-measurement-noise-plus-random-walk, so limb (ii) is conditional on limb (i) (CONTESTED; verified exactly right against N3 full text by A2).
What would count as an answer: sigma_y(tau) curves with fitted slopes and CIs for >= 10 runs across >= 3 scales under the primary detrending and both arms; identified noise type per phase and the tau at the minimum; where white-plus-random-walk, tau* and its realized false-decision rate against seed-replicated pairs, beside the conventional windows and the step counts at which published reports call the decision; where flicker dominates, an explicit statement that the imported optimality result does not apply plus what does. A negative ("white at every accessible tau, mean-of-last-k already optimal") is pre-registered as a real answer.

Significance — consequence: YES (white-to-drift transition at an accessible tau) — every decision read off an EMA-0.99 or last-k curve has a window that is too short or past the Allan minimum, and the deliverable is three usable numbers (tau*, realized error rate at tau*, realized rate at the window in use) from already-stored logs with no new training compute. Strongest remaining objection: the question's load-bearing presupposition P5 — that the field's A-vs-B call is made from a windowed training-loss series, so that an averaging window is the decision instrument whose optimality is in question — is contradicted by every instance of its own named audience that any adversary opened (modded-nanogpt's p<0.01 over run logs against a fixed FineWeb val target; PRIME Intellect's eight-run fixed-seed mean; gilesthomas's three-SD rule on final test loss), all of which decide on an end-of-run fixed-set evaluation averaged over seeds and none of which smooths a curve or picks a window; and a fixed-set loss lacks the white measurement-noise component that the imported optimality theorem (N3, opened: x_k = x_{k-1} + w_k, y_k = x_k + v_k, no drift term, silent on detrending) requires, so limbs (ii) and (iii) interrogate a decision device the audience does not use. The record has no positive evidence for P5 — it concedes the census that would supply it was never run — so the presupposition is unestablished at the gate, not merely contested. Novelty was not what failed: 38 queries across four agents in 20-odd vocabularies, including three structural twins of sigma_y(tau) in other sciences, found nothing renamed, and the record's one named novelty blocker was opened and cleared.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): before any Allan computation, run the census the record never ran — a sourced audit of how a defined sample of published pretraining ablation reports actually calls A-vs-B (decision variable: training loss or fixed-set held-out loss; smoothing window if any; step count at which the call is made; replication count) — because that census decides whether a within-run averaging-window question has a decision to attach to at all, and if it does not, the surviving object is the within-run noise structure of held-out eval series across LR schedules, which must be re-posed without the averaging-window decision limb.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): none. Not asked-but-open: no source poses this question and leaves it unanswered. The substantive decision question the audience does ask ("is this difference real?") is asked *and answered* in a between-run frame (speedrun p<0.01, PRIME's eight-run mean, gilesthomas's three-SD rule), which per the ledger's definitions is an answered rejection and is not routed; the decision limb's remaining content belongs with UQ-20261017-27/-28.

Verification (post-batch, fresh-context readers, 2026-10-18): seven readers opened the kill's own sources cold, one per source, blind to the adversarial reasoning. THE FATAL GROUND HOLDS AND STRENGTHENS, so no late Gate 4 is owed; the corrections below all fall on decoration, and two of them cut against the entry's own wording rather than for it.
THE P5 COUNTER-INSTANCES, all three confirmed at first hand. modded-nanogpt: the README was read in FULL as raw text (54,932 bytes via curl, no summariser, content running to record 92 of 08/30/26). Rule 2 is "Attain <=3.28 mean val loss. (Due to inter-run variance, submissions must provide enough run logs to attain a statistical significance level of p<0.01 that their mean val loss is <=3.28. ...)" — the significance requirement is on the LOSS axis and is waived outright for pure systems-performance submissions, while rule 4 is only "Run faster than the prior record when baselined on the same hardware" and carries no significance requirement at all. The fixed held-out set is confirmed: the metric is loss on "the first 10,485,760 tokens of the FineWeb valset" (a string that sits in the metric-comment section, not in the numbered rules), rule 1 forbids changing the validation pipeline, and the README states the train and val tokens must be kept fixed. A full-text search for smoothing, EMA, moving average, averaging window and mean-of-last-k returns nothing about a loss curve: the hits are tail weight averaging of WEIGHTS, an EMA wrapper on an optimizer, and sliding-window attention. Evaluation frequency is NOT FOUND in the README. Prime Intellect: "trains the recipe eight times on fixed seeds it can't touch" and "8-trial mean remains the record arbiter" are both present as quoted, in the Harness section and the policy panel of "Measuring Autonomous AI Research" (15 Aug 2026); the acceptance threshold is 3.27859 rather than 3.28, the parser keeps the final-step val_loss, and single runs screen only. One narrowing: the page never says how the validation split is built and never says held-out, so "fixed-set" is the entry's inference there, not the document's word. gilesthomas 32i: the three-SD rule and the seed SDs are confirmed (three experiments of n=3; SDs 0.0154919, 0.008672, 0.012062 on losses near 3.67, with every stated three-SD range exactly three SDs wide), the decision variable is test-set loss, and smooth, moving average, exponential and window are all absent. Narrowing: that absence was checked in parts 32i and 32m only, not across 32a-h and 32j-l, and the post does not say whether the evaluated weights are the final or the best checkpoint.
A FOURTH counter-instance, found by this pass and stronger than any in the entry: Apertus (arXiv:2509.14233) states in its Fig. 3 caption, of its own pretraining curves, "No smoothing is applied to the loss curves" — while the gradient-norm curves in the same figure ARE smoothed with a running window of 500 steps at 70B and 1000 at 8B. Its Sec. 2.4 ablations (1.5B, 100B tokens, about 48,000 steps) then decide between recipes on ONE training-loss number each (baseline about 2.037, AdEMAMix 2.002, xIELU 1.997) whose aggregation — final step, average, smoothed, held out — is never stated, with no seeds and no noise discussion. That narrows the kill's own phrasing in one respect, since this instance decides on an END-OF-RUN TRAINING loss rather than a fixed held-out set averaged over seeds, and strengthens it in the respect that matters: a single unstated end-of-run number is still not a windowed training-loss series, and no source opened in six further searches states a smoothing or averaging window used to DECIDE an ablation. Two further sourced practices in the same direction: a proxy-model paper (2512.24503) ranks on Pile validation loss with "standard errors calculated across 3 random seeds" and mentions no smoothing, and MaP (2510.09295) averages the last N checkpoints' WEIGHTS to reduce parameter noise on benchmark scores while its Appendix G.1 argues against a simple moving average of SCORES, which is checkpoint-weight averaging rather than smoothing of a training-loss series.
THE TRANSPLANT OBSTRUCTION (N3, Haeri, Soleimani and Jerath, ACC 2022, pp. 1646-1651) is confirmed at first hand: the model is a pure random walk plus white measurement noise, Eq. (1) and Eq. (2); there is NO deterministic trend or drift term, "drift" appearing only as the label of the stochastic signal; detrending is not discussed anywhere; and flicker, 1/f and pink are absent, the noise being white Gaussian only. "x1 = 0" is a proof assumption inside Theorem 1, not part of the Sec. II model statement. CORRECTION: the closed form's radical scope is UNRESOLVED, because the text extraction does not show the radical's extent. The reader's own algebra from Eq. (12) gives m^2 = 3 sigma_v^2/sigma_w^2 + 1/2, which would make the estimand sqrt(3 sigma_v^2/sigma_w^2 + 1/2) rather than the form printed in this entry; the paper's "floor" is also described as rounding to whichever adjacent integer has the smaller estimation error, so it may be nearest-by-error rather than a floor; and the paper's claim of LINEAR relationships between each variance and the optimal window (Fig. 1) sits oddly with any square-root form. The entry's m_c expression should be read as unverified in its grouping.
THE ALLAN-IN-ML NEGATIVE IS WEAK, and the entry should not lean on it. Seven searches returned link lists only, with no snippets, and only three ML-adjacent documents were opened; many result pages were never opened, so "no application of Allan variance to an ML training series" is NOT FOUND under limited coverage rather than established absence. What was read: a Koutsoyiannis note relating Allan variance to the climacogram as twice the difference at scales k and 2k, requiring stationarity and silent on trends; and Ashby and Patla on the Hadamard variance, which says that with significant drift the Allan variance at large tau "overestimates the intrinsic noise" and that drift removal can remove long-term random components — an independent statement of exactly the detrending bias adversary 3 raised, from the metrology side. arXiv:2602.02400 is confirmed as "An Empirical Study on Noisy Data and LLM Pretraining Loss Divergence" (Zhang, Garg, Foerster, Chatterji, Malik, Lewis), mentions Allan nowhere and carries no tau statistic, so "opened and cleared" is accurate. The nearest method-side analogue found is an MCMC batch-size paper (1804.05975) that picks a window from the series' own autocorrelation under a stationarity assumption, with nothing on trend.
THE TOOLING CLAIM is confirmed only in part: W&B's smoothing panel does offer time-weighted EMA as its default among four algorithms, with the unsmoothed series drawn faintly behind, and its support page says only that the EMA formula "aligns with the one used in TensorBoard" — but the numeric default is not stated on that page, the page carries no warning about comparing runs, and TensorBoard's own documentation COULD NOT BE READ from here (its README says nothing about smoothing, and the 0.6 default and the debiasing detail are unverified). One practitioner piece argues that uniform smoothing should replace EMA for visualisation (Redding, Aug 2026), is explicit that comparing runs makes this "especially important", and offers no formal method for choosing the width; it is the only such piece found and is not widely cited as far as the reader could establish. Everything read concerns visual inspection, and no documented use of a smoothed value as the basis for a recipe decision was found — which is the kill's point, from the tooling side.
Read levels: modded-nanogpt README FULL TEXT RAW (curl, HTTP 200); Prime Intellect blog FULL TEXT via summariser, both strings relayed twice consistently; gilesthomas 32i FULL TEXT via summariser (32m partial, other parts unread); N3 FULL TEXT via summariser of the NSF PAR copy, with the raw PDF unreachable ("curl: (56) CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403") and the extraction garbled at the formula; Apertus, MaP and the proxy-model paper PDF via summariser; the Smol Training Playbook primary text COULD NOT READ (the Hugging Face Space returned metadata only) and is reported here only through a third-party summary; W&B pages FULL TEXT via summariser; TensorBoard documentation COULD NOT READ.

Domain(s): AI architecture — training-systems optimization; measurement methodology of its public competitive record. Method source: HPC performance-variability characterization, empirical algorithmics (competition re-evaluation), benchmark metrology.
Question (canonical): Over the modded-nanogpt speedrun's record series (8×H100 / FineWeb val-loss ≤3.28), under a pre-declared protocol (≥5 re-timings per record on ≥2 nodes, in two arms — A1 period-correct environments, A2 one common modern environment; a step-down counted as surviving only if the re-timed distributions separate at p<0.01; the surviving share computed log-additively; plus a pre-declared transfer ladder on which each accepted change's retained speedup is reported with a CI), what share of the cumulative recorded wall-clock speedup survives (i) re-timing and (ii) transfer, and how many records no longer run, by failure class? (V2, the one permitted Gate 1 reformulation; V1 intake version retained in the record.)
Alternative formulations: How much of the speedrun's recorded speedup is measurement and how much is method? · Which accepted records in a public optimization ledger are indistinguishable from timing noise, and do the survivors pay off outside the fixed target they were selected on? · (lay) The record fell from 45 minutes to about 90 seconds; if you ran every record five times on two machines, how much of that fall would still be there?
Motivating gap: New-instrument question. A public, dated, append-only competitive record with per-record code and logs, whose acceptance rules were read as putting a p<0.01 test on the loss axis and an unreplicated comparison on the time axis — "the variance control sits on the axis that is not the record." Third parties have made the series load-bearing (METR 2026-04-21 progress note; the Automated LLM Speedrunning Benchmark, arXiv 2506.22419, whose FSR metric divides by per-record step-downs; Prime Intellect's agent environment). **The in-batch Gate 4 struck that motivating premise at attack 4; the late pass RESTORED it, because the premise is what the rules actually say — rule 4 is "Run faster than the prior record when baselined on the same hardware" and imposes no replication at all, while rule 2's p<0.01 sits on the loss axis and is waived outright for pure systems-speed submissions. See the verification block.**

WHAT FELL. (a) ATTACK 4's kill inverted the rules it cited. Rule 2's "submissions must provide enough run logs to attain a statistical significance level of p<0.01" is verbatim, is a claim about mean val loss ≤ 3.28, and ends "For submissions which improve speed by optimizing the systems performance, without touching the ML, this requirement is waived" — so the variance control is conditional, on the loss axis, and waived precisely for the submission class most likely to be noise-sized. The candidate's premise, "the variance control sits on the axis that is not the record", is therefore what the rules say, and the in-batch kill had read the practice of some contributors as a requirement of the rules. THIS LEDGER'S OWN ARITHMETIC, AND A CORRECTION TO IT. The README table was parsed by script from the raw 54,932-byte file: 92 contiguous records, 45.000 min (an external llm.c baseline, 05/28/24) to 0.665 min (08/30/26), total log-speedup 4.2146 = 67.67x — so the record's framing of "77 records, 31x, about 90 seconds" is stale on all three figures. Exactly one step in the series is negative, record 22 (2.933 -> 2.990 min, -1.94%), which is the post-record-21 timing-regime change showing up as an accepted record slower than its predecessor on the old clock. Step-downs under 2% number 54 of 91 and carry 11.15% of the log-speedup. ID: UQ-20261018-15
Date: 2026-10-18
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): AI architecture — pretraining schedule design, the annealing/cooldown data layer; secondary: LLM evaluation methodology (format sensitivity, calibration). Source method: silence mapping.

Question (canonical): For >=2 open pretraining runs with dense cooldown checkpoints and one pinned harness, decompose each benchmark's cooldown-phase score change into (i) a sharpening/format component — the part reproduced on the PRE-cooldown checkpoint by a fixed-weight output transform fitted on held-out items (temperature/entropy rescaling; length-normalised or rank-based option scoring; a label-emission format correction), no weight update — and (ii) a knowledge residual read by a pre-declared probe panel held fixed across checkpoints; report the share per benchmark with uncertainty, a manipulation check, and the re-ranking of >=3 published annealing data mixes under (ii) alone. (V2; the one permitted Gate 1 reformulation, spent. V1 asked the same without an estimator — see record.)

Alternative formulations:
- Does the cooldown teach the model anything, or mostly teach it to answer in the shape the benchmark scores?
- Is the end-of-run benchmark jump a knowledge gain or a calibration/formatting gain — and does the split change which annealing mixes look good?
- (lay) When a training run cools down and test scores jump, has the model learned more, or just learned how to take the test?

Motivating gap: The final decay is engineered everywhere and interrogated nowhere. Two mid-training surveys (arXiv:2510.23081 Sec. 8.1, "the rapid convergence in the LR decay stage is due to the first-order directional derivative diminishing"; arXiv:2510.06826 intro, "lowering the learning rate mitigates gradient variance") explain the decay-stage downstream gain by optimization and token utility alone and never raise format or calibration, while OLMo 2 (arXiv:2501.00656 Sec. 2.4) consumes cooldown-phase dev scores as its annealing-mix selection signal. The gap is real, and it is where the record placed it. The in-batch Gate 4 relocated it onto arXiv:2407.07890; the late pass withdrew that relocation when the paper failed first-hand reading (see the verification block).

Presuppositions: P1 format-free probe family exists — holds (N1 verified; arXiv:2407.07890 Sec. 3.2). P2 knowledge/format separable in a next-token model — contested; arXiv:2609.02015 calls capability "interface-conditioned". P3 dense cooldown checkpoints for >=2 open runs — VERIFIED (adversary 3, GitHub: allenai/OLMo stage-2 checkpoints every 1000 steps, 1B/7B/13B, three ingredient seeds; Marin cooldown phases documented). P4 the jump is real under one pinned harness — unverified by anyone. P5 share reportable — holds via per-benchmark vector. P6 mixes are selected on cooldown-phase score movement — STRENGTHENED beyond the record (Marin model card; Blakeney et al. arXiv:2406.03476; Llama 3 arXiv:2407.21783; Gemma's mixture "determined partially based on downstream benchmark evaluations"). P-implicit, unlisted by the record: that the cooldown gain is either sharpening/format or newly acquired knowledge, so a small format share licenses the practice — FAILS IN PART, and this is the entry's standing defect. Both late adversaries found independently that the two-way partition is not exhaustive on the only run where P3 is sourced: the Dolmino cooldown mix carries the GSM8K train split (2.74M tokens, 17.6K documents) alongside TinyGSM-MIND (6.48B) and FLAN (17.0B), so direct test-task supervision — the channel arXiv:2407.07890 names and measures at a different unit — is absorbed silently into the "knowledge residual". Graded Partial, not fatal: it damages limb (ii)'s interpretation, not the primary estimand.

What would count as an answer: a pre-declared per-benchmark decomposition with estimators, uncertainty and a validated manipulation check on >=2 open runs under one harness, plus the re-ranking of >=3 published annealing mixes under the knowledge component alone. Pre-committed bands: (i) small component and no re-ranking -> practice licensed; (ii) large and re-ranks -> published ablations partly selected format compliance; (iii) large but no re-ranking -> a reporting finding without a curation consequence. Gate 4 shows band (i) does not support the inference attached to it.

Novelty — queries run (query -> one-line result): Gate 2: 11 web searches + 5 fetches (2 empty); full list in batches/2026-10-18-0619/UQ-20261018-15-record.md. Three adversaries ran 8, 9 and 9 further Disguise queries in new vocabularies, plus 12 fetches and 14 GitHub code searches; full lists in UQ-20261018-15-adversary-{1,2,3}.md. No call was refused except export.arxiv.org (proxy CONNECT 403, adversary 3). Most informative:

- "fraction of accuracy gain attributable to output format compliance versus knowledge ... quantified share" [mandatory already-computed query] -> no cooldown share; surfaced arXiv:2609.02015 (SFT phase).
- "during pretraining checkpoints knowledge probe versus task-format ability disentangle" -> N1, the record's close own-field neighbour.
- A3-1 "'training on the test task' annealing OR mid-training OR cooldown benchmark emergence confound" -> the in-batch kill: Dominguez-Olmedo, **Dorner** & Hardt, arXiv:2407.07890 (ICLR 2025 oral), OPENED. Missed by Gate 2 and by adversaries 1-2. **The kill is WITHDRAWN on verification, and the author line the record carried for it was itself wrong — see the verification block.**

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
N1 (the in-batch kill, WITHDRAWN on verification; a neighbour one unit and one mediator over, no longer the nearest). Dominguez-Olmedo, **Dorner** & Hardt (2024), "Training on the Test Task Confounds Evaluation and Emergence", arXiv:2407.07890, ICLR 2025 oral — OPENED (HTML) by adversary 3; read post-batch at first hand (PDF, 100,000 of 101,411 characters, plus the HTML outline and the abs page). Author line as printed on the paper's own first page: Ricardo Dominguez-Olmedo, Florian E. Dorner, Moritz Hardt (MPI-IS Tübingen / Tübingen AI Center / ETH Zürich) — **"Mendler-Dünner" is not an author of it, and Dorner was dropped**; "ICLR 2025 (Oral)" is on the abs page's Comments field and the iclr.cc page, not in the paper's own text. Unit: **56 released base models (70M-70B) split by release before/after Nov 2023 at matched pretraining compute — no within-run checkpoints, and cooldown, annealing and LR decay appear nowhere in the text read**; the only intermediate checkpoints in it are of fine-tuning runs, in the Sec. 5 emergence analysis. Endpoint: MMLU/GSM8K accuracy. Comparator: older vs newer models, before and after fine-tuning each on the same task-relevant data. Instrument: **a weight update (fine-tuning every model on the MMLU auxiliary training set) plus prompt reformulation — not a fixed-weight output transform**; Sec. 3.2's own move is "We then reformulate ARC and HellaSwag as MMLU-style multiple-choice questions". Mediator: **training on the test task in general, not multiple-choice-format ability**; Sec. 3.2's "conflates knowledge-testing with testing a models' ability to answer multiple choice questions" is verbatim, but it is that section's reading of what MMLU tests, not the mediator the mediation estimates. Estimand: **indirect effects in accuracy units, not a share** — Appendix B **Table 3** (there is no Table 2) gives 0.071 for MMLU (SE 0.018, R² 0.530) and 0.168 for GSM8K (SE 0.032, R² 0.503), with Table 4's direct effects at -0.004 and 0.000 and "no evidence of a significant direct effect"; the total effect is absent from the same table, so **no share is formable from the paper**, and the record's "close to the whole gap" was an inference, not a reading. Sec. 2.2's unadjusted gaps are "over 7 accuracy points in MMLU" and **19** accuracy points in GSM8K — **the record's ">17-point GSM8K" figure does not exist in the paper** — and 0.071-against-7 and 0.168-against-19 are different regressions, so neither pair is a share of the other.
N2. Bunn, Wiegreffe & Bogin (2025), "Fine-Tune on the Format: First Improving Multiple-Choice Evaluation for Intermediate LLM Checkpoints", GEM 2025 — aclanthology.org/2025.gem-1.46/ (abstract page opened at Gate 2; existence VERIFIED via ACL Anthology XML; full text COULD NOT READ, fetch caps, all three adversaries). Unit: an intermediate pretraining checkpoint. Endpoint: MCQ accuracy under label emission. Comparator: standard label-emission prompting vs after auxiliary MCQ fine-tuning. Estimand: a format-corrected MCQ level for a checkpoint.
N3. OLMo et al. (2025), "2 OLMo 2 Furious", arXiv:2501.00656 — OPENED (intro, Sec. 2.4); stage-2 configs and checkpoint revisions verified on GitHub. Unit: a candidate annealing mixture. Endpoint: downstream dev scores ("we use 200 examples to inform choices (e.g., choices of annealing mixtures)"). Comparator: other mixtures at matched budget. Estimand: per-mixture efficacy, interpreted as knowledge ("to infuse new knowledge and patch deficiencies").
(Also located and bearing: OLMES arXiv:2406.08446 and DataDecide arXiv:2504.11393, OPENED — AI2 already instruments CF/MCF format ability on intermediate checkpoints and already prefers length-normalised continuous metrics for data decisions; WSM, ICLR 2026 oral, OPENED — "establishes a formal connection between learning rate decay and model merging", an averaging account of the decay gain; arXiv:2609.02015, OPENED — the same confound for SFT data-quality judgments, "a skill that raises accuracy by more than 40 points under the training format can be nearly invisible under every other".)

Novelty — how this differs from each:
vs N1 — it differs on the unit, the mediator, the instrument and the estimand, all four certified at first hand, which is why the in-batch kill is withdrawn. The unit is a within-run cooldown pair, not a cross-vintage cohort of released models; the mediator is a fixed-weight output transform, not task-relevant fine-tuning; and N1 publishes no share of anything, so there is no quantified answer for the candidate to duplicate. What N1 does own is the TEMPLATE — that a benchmark gain can be carried by test-task ability rather than capability — and the in-batch kill mistook owning the template for owning the question. Two of the in-batch objection's own premises survive and are kept as defects rather than as a kill: V2's stage-2 contrast does change learning rate and data together, so it cannot isolate the schedule's contribution; and the cooldown mix of the run it names does contain FLAN and GSM8K-derived data (G2, G13), which is why a third component is now declared necessary. The record's METHOD-OWNING-FIELD NEGATIVE is **partly restored**: mediation has been applied to LLM benchmark gains, but at a cross-cohort unit and never to a training phase — and late adversary 1's mediation-vocabulary sweep returned education, HCI and SLA mediation and did not surface 2407.07890 at all, which is evidence about how far that vocabulary reaches.
vs N2 — the record's distinction (level vs share of a change; no phase; weight-updating instrument) still stands as stated, and N2 alone would have left Medium intact. Open item: whether N2's "intermediate checkpoints" already include OLMo 2 stage-2 checkpoints, in which case the format-corrected cooldown series exists inside it. Unread by every agent.
vs N3 — unchanged: N3 is a user of the quantity, not a study of it. The audit limb is still absent from N3. This is why the candidate's second limb remains a gap, but it is N1's gap re-pointed, not a new one.

The record's own trigger was "if Gate 4 ... finds the phase-gain decomposition stated generally, Medium should fall to Low"; arXiv:2407.07890 does not state it generally, has no share to state, and works at a different unit with a different mediator and a weight-updating instrument, so the trigger was never met and the regrade rested on a reading of the paper rather than on the paper. Medium rather than better because a close neighbour stands unread: Bunn, Wiegreffe & Bogin 2025 already format-correct MCQ scores on intermediate pretraining checkpoints, and no agent has opened its full text across four passes and five routes — COULD NOT READ, not NOT FOUND. Disguise is VERIFIED five times over: the three in-batch adversaries ran 8, 9 and 9 new-vocabulary queries (eval-methodology, data-curation, optimization, Chinese, representation probing, elicitation, knowledge dynamics, data-decision metrics, signal-detection theory, ASR discriminative training, temperature scaling, causal mediation, mixture ranking, stored-vs-extractable knowledge, weight averaging), and the two late adversaries ran 8 each in six further vocabularies (mediation and causal inference, surface-form competition and PMI scoring, in-mix supervision and contamination, item response theory, scoring-rule-drives-the-gain, format-corrected mixture selection, plus a citing-work check on the struck kill), all clean. Not asked-but-open either: no source was found that poses this question and leaves it open — both mid-training surveys account for the decay-stage gain in optimization terms and cite no decomposition — so there is nothing to route.

Significance — consequence: unchanged in kind and not the ground of rejection — if the format share is large, published annealing ablations have partly ranked format compliance and cooldown-phase screening needs a format-corrected endpoint. But the band (i) direction is void: under V2 the residual absorbs in-task training and any averaging/noise-reduction gain, so "sharpening small" licenses exactly the confound N1 identified rather than retiring it.
Significance — audience: real and verified harder than the record claimed — AI2 (microanneals, Sec. 2.4), Marin (cooldown phases named in its model card; GH#898), Blakeney et al. end-of-training domain upsampling, Llama 3, and the format-sensitivity/eval-noise groups. Discount: the field's stated position is that test-task data in pretraining "is not a malpractice" (N1) and OLMo 2 adds FLAN and GSM8K-derived data to the cooldown deliberately, so band (ii) is met with "intended"; and screening endpoints are already moving post-SFT (ICLR 2026 "Pre-training LLM without Learning Rate Decay Enhances Supervised Fine-Tuning"; Marin GH#898).
Significance — fecundity: the live follow-ups (does the share scale with model size, cooldown length or shape; is it benchmark-format-dependent; can a fixed transform substitute for a microanneal) survive the rejection and belong to a successor intake, not to this formulation.
Significance — anchoring: cooldown/WSD dynamics (arXiv:2508.01483; 2405.18392; WSM); both mid-training surveys' decay-stage accounts; the training-on-the-test-task and emergence debate (2407.07890, which now owns the question rather than merely touching it); format-sensitivity and eval noise; the RLVR sharpening-vs-capability programme.

Reason for silence: the record's own mechanism still does not hold up, but the late pass rebuilt one that does, and both late adversaries graded attack 7 RESOLVED. What stays contradicted: the instrument-gap limb — OLMES instrumented CF/MCF format ability across training in 2024, and the AI2 group that built the format-correction instrument on intermediate checkpoints (N2, 2025) is the group releasing stage-2 checkpoints — and, in weakened form, the method-field limb, since mediation did reach LLM benchmark gains in 2024, though at a cohort unit and never at a training phase. What replaces it, dated and triangulated: the phase's owners measure it in loss and geometry, and a SECOND independent mid-training survey (arXiv:2510.06826, opened for the first time by late adversary 1) explains the decay-stage gain as "lowering the learning rate mitigates gradient variance and stabilizes convergence near favorable minima", cites no decomposition, and never mentions format sensitivity, length-normalised scoring, cloze scoring, calibration or temperature scaling in connection with evaluating mid-training; the phase's consumers hold the intuition and have no reason to audit it, and Marin's own retro carries exactly that as an unmeasured aside ("High quality data seems to often lack data that leads to good few-shot performance", alongside harness "systematic failures to follow the strict templates"); and the instrument reached within-run checkpoints only in 2025 (Bunn et al., 10 checkpoints of one OLMo-1B run), the same vintage as the public anneal-stage revisions. The tension is reported rather than hidden: 2407.07890 was an ICLR 2025 Oral that put the gain-confound template in the air in 2024, so the silence has to survive two years of a visible template — its own aim was cross-cohort comparability and emergence, and that is where its follow-through went. Limitation: Section VII (Future Work) of 2510.06826 COULD NOT READ by either late adversary, so neither can certify the question is absent from that survey's open-problem list.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3
Well-posedness returns to the record's 2/3, and not to 3/3. The in-batch 1/3 rested on two grounds and one of them NARROWS: Guo et al. 2017's invariance covers the argmax over a single input's K-class logit vector — exactly label-emission MCQ accuracy, where temperature/entropy rescaling is an exact no-op — but it does not extend to multi-token summed or length-normalised option scoring, to sampling, or to multi-token greedy decoding, and Guo claims it for temperature scaling rather than for vector or matrix scaling. Both late adversaries reached that independently. So component (i)'s sharpening half is dead on one scoring mode rather than identically zero, and the remedy is to restrict the limb, which a successor can do. The second ground HOLDS and is the entry's standing defect: the partition is not exhaustive, because in-mix test-task supervision lands in the "knowledge residual" under every probe in the panel. A presupposition that survives as a restriction, plus a non-exhaustive partition, is 2/3 — which bars Validated under Gate 5. Significance stands at 2/3 and was never the ground of rejection.

Strongest remaining objection: the two-way partition is not exhaustive on the only run where P3 is actually sourced, so the second limb would re-rank mixes partly on how much of each benchmark's own training distribution they carry. The Dolmino cooldown mix contains the GSM8K train split (2.74M tokens, 17.6K documents), TinyGSM-MIND (6.48B tokens) and FLAN (17.0B tokens); direct test-task supervision is a documented third channel, named and measured by arXiv:2407.07890 at a different unit, and under every probe in V2's panel it is absorbed into the "knowledge residual". The candidate's available answer — that the sharpening component is still identified by the fixed-weight transform whatever the residual contains, and that per-probe reporting would expose it — is correct for limb (i), does not repair limb (ii)'s interpretation, and is nowhere stated in the record. Both late adversaries graded it Partial rather than Unresolved, because it damages the mix-re-ranking limb and not the primary estimand. A second standing defect at the same grade: the pre-committed bands turn on "small" against "large" with no numeric threshold and no minimum denominator, and Marin's FLAN arm moved MMLU .653 -> .651, so a per-benchmark ratio can be unstable or sign-flipping where V2 promises a vector of shares.

Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): read Bunn, Wiegreffe & Bogin 2025 in full. It is the nearest prior, no agent has opened it across four passes and five routes, and it settles whether a format-corrected series already exists inside the OLMo 2 stage-2 revisions. Then pin one harness and establish the cooldown-checkpoint cadence for a second open run, since only OLMo 2's stage-2 revisions are sourced ("stage2-ingredientN-stepXXX-tokensYYYB", cadence unstated) while Marin's retro states internal "permanent full checkpoints every 20,000 steps" and does not say cooldown checkpoints are released. The reformulation is spent, so the restrictions a successor needs — the scoring-mode limit on component (i) and the third component for in-mix supervision — go in a V3 intake, not in this entry.

THE STRUCK KILL, CERTIFIED GONE. arXiv:2407.07890 was read post-batch from the PDF (100,000 of 101,411 characters; the last 1,411 unread, probably end matter), the HTML outline, the abs page and the iclr.cc page, one supplied string at a time. Every element the kill rested on is wrong on the paper's own text: the author line is Dominguez-Olmedo, Dorner, Hardt, so "Mendler-Dünner" was an INVENTED author and Dorner a dropped one; the mediator is training on the test task in general, not multiple-choice-format ability; the unit is 56 released base models split by release date at matched pretraining compute, with no within-run checkpoints and with cooldown, annealing and LR decay absent from the text read; the instrument is fine-tuning plus prompt reformulation, not a fixed-weight output transform; NO mediated share exists anywhere in it, because Appendix B Table 3 (there is no Table 2) gives indirect effects in accuracy units with SEs while the total effect is absent from the same table; and ">17 points GSM8K" does not exist — the paper says 19. What DID verify: Sec. 3.2's "conflates knowledge-testing with testing a models' ability to answer multiple choice questions" is verbatim, Sec. 2.2's "over 7 accuracy points in MMLU" is verbatim, the 0.071/0.168 numbers are real in Table 3, and Sec. 3.2's cloze-and-MCQ reformulation is real — which is what P1 was leaning on, so P1's support survives. The lesson is the one this ledger keeps relearning: a paper can be real, correctly identified, accurately quoted in three places, and still not carry the claim, and the author line fails as often as the number.
WHAT THE LATE PASS ADDED. arXiv:2609.02015, which the record itself called "the single most dangerous unread source" with a stated kill condition, was opened (abs page; its PDF returns "[This PDF is empty or contains no machine-readable text]", and a vendor blog supplied the rest, labelled as such). It measures gradient signatures and effective rank across 12 tasks, 4 equivalent output formats and 3 model families at the instruction-tuning stage, reports no share and re-ranks no data ablations: the record's kill condition is NOT met. A second, independent mid-training survey (arXiv:2510.06826) was read for the first time and carries an optimization-only account of the decay-stage gain, which strengthens the silence mechanism rather than the kill. Marin's 8B retro was read in full: two named cooldowns, before/after pairs (GSM8K "from 0.509 to 0.611", MATH "from 0.184 to 0.211", FLAN "MMLU 5-shot (.653->.651)"), microanneal results "described qualitatively, without numbers", and no format-vs-knowledge decomposition. Three further neighbours were opened and ruled non-identical on all four attributes: arXiv:2407.15018 (answer-token logit differences keep growing over training — a mechanism neighbour that supports the premise), arXiv:2504.13837 (RLVR capability boundary in pass@k) and arXiv:2512.07783 (a 100M model, pass@k under process verification).
WHAT THE LATE PASS DID NOT ESTABLISH. The ">=2 open runs" clause is sourced for OLMo 2 only; Marin's cooldown-checkpoint release is unverified and the W&B cooldown-ablation report COULD NOT READ by three routes. Section VII of 2510.06826 COULD NOT READ, so neither adversary can certify the question is absent from that survey's open-problem list. 2609.02015's own text COULD NOT READ. Bunn, Wiegreffe & Bogin 2025 remains unread in full — the single most consequential gap left, and the first item of Promotion requires. arXiv:2406.11813 was left on a budget cap. Three RLVR papers (2504.13837 beyond its abstract, 2507.14843, the ICML 2025 "Limits of RLVR") were NOT ATTEMPTED by late adversary 2.
LATE GATE 4 STATUSES (operative). 1 Triviality Resolved/Resolved — the number exists nowhere; the honest caveat, routed to attack 4, is that Guo makes one named limb an exact no-op in a paragraph, and that the direction is partly foreseeable from Bunn's 34-point SciQ swing. 2 Disguise Resolved/Resolved, non-identity first-hand on all four attributes for both nearest priors, with 16 new-vocabulary queries clean. 3 Combinatorial novelty Resolved/Resolved — the interface carries a live documented problem: OLMo 2 chose its math sources through 19 microanneals scored mainly on MMLU and a 200-question GSM8K dev subset. 4 Presupposition failure Partial/Partial, the two findings now in the Scores and Strongest-objection lines. 5 Vagueness Partial/Partial on the undeclared band thresholds. 6 Significance inflation Resolved/Resolved — the phase gain is 9.4-9.9 average points in OLMo 2's Table 9 and the named audience runs the procedure the answer would change. 7 Reason for silence Resolved/Resolved on the rebuilt mechanism. 8 Dissolution Partial/Partial — the split is operationalisable on frozen weights and non-degenerate (Bunn SciQ 24.6 label against 58.6 sequence), but the share has no instrument-independent value and nobody has shown it is stable across admissible transforms.

But well-posedness is 2/3, which bars Validated on its own; the nearest prior is COULD NOT READ rather than ruled out; and the entry carries two live defects on its face, the non-exhaustive partition and the undeclared band thresholds. ID: UQ-20261018-16
Date: 2026-10-18
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): Biology — microbiology / microbial systematics and biological resource centres; secondary comparative genomics, research-reagent reproducibility. Method-owning neighbour: reference-material metrology (between-unit homogeneity / stability, ISO Guide 35).

Question (canonical): Over a frame of co-held microbial accessions declared before any sequencing — strains linked as "equivalent" across two or more independent collections (ATCC, DSMZ, NCTC, CIP, JCM, NCIMB) by catalogue cross-reference or StrainInfo identifier matching — sequence the material as distributed by each collection (freshly ordered ampoules, primary arm; distributor-provenanced public assemblies, secondary arm) and report (a) the pairwise cross-collection divergence distribution partitioned into SNV / indel / IS / plasmid / prophage classes; (b) the share of accession pairs exceeding a comparator measured inside the same study — the divergence between two independently revived ampoules of one lot from one collection — not a stipulated threshold; (c) the dependence of divergence on transfers-since-deposit and years-since-deposit, under a pre-declared rule separating post-deposit drift from cross-referencing error.
(This is V2, the one Gate 1 reformulation, adopted as canonical. V1, superseded at Gate 1: same question with "a pre-declared within-strain comparator", which was undefined and so answerable by stipulation.)

Alternative formulations:
- (lay) Is "the same strain" one organism across the world's culture collections, or has each collection's freezer grown its own version?
- (metrology) Treating each co-held accession as a reference material issued by two or more producers, what is the between-producer inhomogeneity of the genomic property value versus each producer's within-lot inhomogeneity?

Motivating gap: Divergence between nominally identical holdings of one strain is reported case by case and never aggregated as a population quantity. Desroches et al. 2018 sequenced the ancestral Escherich E. coli strain as held by NCTC, CIP, ATCC and DSMZ — 164/803/878 SNPs and 127/227/230 indels against NCTC86_Dunne, i.e. four collections' holdings are four lineages — and calls for no broader survey. StrainInfo welds 717,337 identifiers / 476,193 deposits onto 314,035 strains, verifying matches by comparing sequence *accessions*, never sequence content. READ LEVEL caveats from the record: prior (B) read as preprint; four PMC-hosted leads unread at Gate 2.

Presuppositions (post-Gate-4 status):
P1 Enough co-held accessions exist (K) — supported by StrainInfo's deposit:strain ratio; exact K unpublished, must be extracted from the frame as step 0.
P2 Each collection's distributed material is obtainable — established for the prospective arm; retrospective arm contested and demoted to secondary.
P3 Divergence well defined under a symmetric reference-free variant/SV protocol — established for bacteria; contested for fungi/protists, to be excluded or stratified.
P4 A comparator exists — repaired by V2's internally measured within-lot replicate baseline; needs an interval, not a point.
P5 Transfers-since-deposit retrievable — WORSE THAN CONTESTED after Gate 4: DSMZ's catalogue History field is defined as history *before* deposit, the wrong side of the event for limb (c); limb (c) stays secondary.
P6 Divergence is post-deposit drift rather than two wrongly linked isolates — contested, load-bearing; reported as a result under the declared separation rule.
P7 One ampoule stands for the accession — contested; lot-to-lot variance needs its own arm.
P8 A cross-reference claims one physical lineage — NOW EVIDENCED, and it cuts the candidate's way: NCIMB's own curator page states it is "generally accepted amongst major collections" that equivalent cultures "will be indistinguishable from one another", that "genetic drift may alter the properties of the strains between collections", and that these are "rare occurrences" — an unquantified rarity claim, which is the candidate's estimand. But DSMZ's field guide defines the field — whose printed name is "Other collection no. or WDCM no.", not "Other collection numbers" as this entry has it at both of its mentions — as nothing more than "Accession numbers in other collections" OR "or number of WDCM Reference Strain Catalogue", a two-limb definition whose second limb is not another collection's accession number at all, so the claim is NOT uniform across the frame (see strongest objection).

What would count as an answer: (i) the frame fixed before any data pull, with K reported; (ii) per accession, assemblies of each collection's distributed material plus the within-lot replicate pairs; (iii) one pre-declared symmetric reference-free variant+SV protocol; (iv) the divergence distribution with class partition; (v) the exceedance share with an interval under pre-committed bands (CONCENTRATED-NEAR-ZERO / MODEST-DRIFT / LINEAGE-DIVERGENT) so a null is informative; (vi) regressions on transfers and years for the subset with retrievable histories, with its coverage fraction; (vii) an explicit mis-cross-reference rate under the declared rule. A distribution tight near zero is equally publishable.

Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 11 at Gate 2 (cap 11; 5 fetches) + 9 per adversary x 3 = 38 documented queries. Full lists: batches/2026-10-18-0945/UQ-20261018-16-record.md and -adversary-1/-2/-3.md. Most informative: "genomic differences between the same bacterial strain distributed by different culture collections" (own-field obvious title) → the single-strain Desroches study, no survey; "what percentage of strains ATCC reference genome disagrees with existing public assembly" (mandatory pre-computed-fraction query) → Yarmosh et al., median 7 SNPs / 8 indels per assembly, but against public assemblies of the same strain *designation*; "microbial reference material between-unit homogeneity genome stability certified reference strain metrology" (method-owning field) → NIST programme, ISO Guide 35, never applied to collection equivalence; adversary queries in germplasm-genebank, laboratory-animal-vendor, model-organism stock-centre, BCG vaccine-substrain, biologics seed-lot, clinical-QC, ring-trial, catalogue-semantics, Japanese, Chinese and German vocabularies → the question's *shape* is routine on non-microbial material (duplicate Brassica accessions in two European genebanks, Plants 9:925; JAX vendor substrain divergence) but no microbial cross-collection divergence survey in any vocabulary tried.

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
(A) Desroches et al., "The Odyssey of the Ancestral Escherich Strain through Culture Collections", mSphere 3(1), 2018, 10.1128/msphere.00553-17 (opened). Unit: one strain, four collection holdings. Endpoint: cgMLST alleles, SNP/indel, MLST, virulence, plasmids, MICs, mouse lethality. Reference: NCTC86_Dunne. Estimand: per-holding counts (4/11/105/446/572 alleles; up to 878 SNPs / 230 indels). Transfers qualitative only.
(B) Yarmosh et al., "Comparative Analysis and Data Provenance for 1,113 Bacterial Genome Assemblies", mSphere 7(3), 2022 (read as bioRxiv 2021.12.14.472616; PubMed 35491842 confirms the journal version). Unit: assembly pairs, 1,113 ATCC reference genomes vs RefSeq assemblies labelled as ATCC strains (708 RefSeq assemblies with an ASRG counterpart, of which the 303 at "complete genome" level are the set actually carrying the variant analysis — corrected on verification, which found no figure of 366 anywhere and established the structure as 1,113 ASRGs / 2,701 RefSeq assemblies / 708 overlapping / 303 analysed, identically in the preprint and the published version). Endpoint: ANI, aligned fraction, dnaDiff SVs, SNPs/indels. Reference: the public assembly of the same strain *designation*. Estimand: medians/counts, no comparator, no exceedance share. Second publication on the same axis found by adversary 2: ATCC poster "The Elephant in the Room" (2021) — 100 strains evaluated, "35 were found to have more than 50 variants", 8 >100 variants, 2 >50 kb (35/100 is the adversary's own arithmetic over a convenience set, no stated uncertainty, not a population estimate).
(C) StrainInfo, Database (OUP) 2025 (opened). Unit: identifiers and deposits (717,337 / 476,193 / 314,035 strains). Endpoint: identifier linkage, "further verified by comparing sequence accessions". Estimand: counts. Divergence between linked deposits never measured.
Also, found by adversary 1 and missed at Gate 2: "Domestication of Campylobacter jejuni NCTC 11168" (bioRxiv 10.1101/591701, opened; PMC6700657 blocked) — 23 nominally identical laboratory stocks of one strain, 10 taken directly from NCTC, "an average of 29 SNP differences", "21 of 23 isolates (91%) ... 32 or fewer", max 281, one isolate losing a 15-gene block, inversions >90 kb. A limb-(a)-shaped answer for single-collection dissemination of one strain.

Novelty — how this differs from each: (A) is the candidate's comparison at n = 1, with no frame, no distribution, an asymmetric reference, no class partition beyond plasmid replicons, no transfer regression, and silence on the general question rather than, as this entry first had it, an explicit refusal to generalise — corrected on verification, which read the whole body including ALL SIX Discussion-and-conclusion paragraphs under an open prompt and found no sentence proposing extension to other strains, collections or isolates and none asking how commonly holdings diverge, the nearest thing being advice on analysis practice ("Therefore, interpretation of WGS data should trigger a thorough analysis of antimutator genes"). Silence is the weaker novelty signal of the two, so the distinction is worth keeping. (B) is population scale on the wrong comparator object — one collection against other laboratories' re-sequencings of the same strain *name*, provenance unverified, collections and cross-references absent, no internal baseline, no IS/plasmid/prophage partition, no passage history; it bounds how surprising (a) can be where public assemblies exist, and it does not pose or defer the cross-collection question. (C) builds the candidate's frame and verifies equivalence against identifiers rather than content — the gap measured. The Campylobacter study varies *laboratories* downstream of one collection, not collections against each other. Plainly: candidate = (A)'s comparison on (C)'s frame at (B)'s scale, with an internal comparator and a transfer-history limb none has. LEDGER duplicate check: nearest are UQ-20261016-29 (plasmid repository, map-vs-material axis), UQ-20261016-57, UQ-20261017-32; no duplicate.

Novelty confidence: Medium. Flanked on two sides by opened work — the cross-collection comparison published at n = 1 with hundreds of SNPs, and divergence distributions for nominally identical strain material published at scale on a one-collection axis, now twice (B plus the ATCC 2021 poster, which already reports a share-above-threshold statistic). Not Low: nothing opened compares two collections' *distributed material* over a declared frame of co-held accessions, reports a share exceeding a measured within-accession baseline, partitions by IS/plasmid/prophage, or regresses on transfers-since-deposit; no opened paper poses it as future work. Not High: the marginal yield over (B) rests on the cross-collection pairing and the comparator, and the transplanted method family is mature in metrology. Unclosed reads bearing on the grade: PMC6544187 "Beware of False 'Type Strain' Genome Sequences" (confirmed at abstract level by adversary 2 via a repository record as a labelling-error object, publisher version never opened by any adversary) and the BCG daughter-strain cross-institute comparative-genomics line (identified by adversaries 1 and 3, Springer HTTP 429 and PMC blocked, never opened).

Significance — consequence: If divergence is concentrated near zero, administrative equivalence is validated as genomic equivalence and cross-reference tables become usable as scientific statements. If a material share exceeds the within-lot baseline — and (A)'s 878 SNPs shows the upper tail is not hypothetical — "the strain" is a collection-specific lineage, and four practices lose a premise: the ICSP type-strain principle, QC-strain-based assay standardisation (CLSI/EUCAST organisms sourced from whichever collection is local), accession-based industrial and probiotic identity claims, and the reproducibility reading of thousands of methods sections. It also bears on whether a genome sequence can stand as nomenclatural type or must be tied to one named holding.
Significance — audience: instrumented and demonstrably acting. Collections and their federations (WFCC/WDCM, ECCO, StrainInfo as the graph's maintainer) — available action: flag or withdraw a cross-reference, publish per-accession diffs; RIKEN JCM already does this one accession at a time by public notice (JCM 12229T, JCM 1633T withdrawn and replaced), which is exactly the case-by-case practice a rate would systematise. ICSP / IJSEM / SeqCode on what a type is. CLSI, EUCAST, ISO/EURL reference-material producers who already run between-unit homogeneity studies for every other property. Reusing laboratories deciding whether to sequence on arrival. Probiotic and biocontrol regulators. Discount recorded: ATCC is already applying authentication pressure without the cross-collection axis.
Significance — fecundity: a drift rate per transfer or per year makes passage budgets computable; makes "how much divergence before MICs shift" answerable; opens whether drift is random or convergent (mutator alleles, IS activation, prophage loss at the same loci across collections would be laboratory domestication, not noise); makes a cross-collection coalescent datable as an archival record; exports to cell-line, antibody, mouse-line and plasmid analogues.
Significance — anchoring: the type-strain-as-physical-object problem and the genome-as-type debate; (A)'s mutator acquisition in collection passage; (B)'s authenticated-vs-crowd-sourced discordance; the pre-genomic "strain degeneration on subculture" literature, never converted into a population estimate; and reference-material metrology's between-unit homogeneity framework.

Reason for silence: Gate 4 re-ordered the record's list and the surviving mechanisms are structural, not "no one thought of it". Strongest, supplied by adversaries 1 and 2: the field holds a consensus answer by assertion — a major collection states in public catalogue guidance that equivalent cultures "will be indistinguishable" and that drift between collections is a matter of "rare occurrences" — plural in the printed text, and the predicate of "these", i.e. of the clerical errors and the genetic drift the sentence has just named, rather than of any single phenomenon — with no study, number or citation behind it, and a quantity everyone treats as already characterised is not asked about. Second: a boundary inside the only institutions that could answer it — the equivalence graph sits in collection informatics, sequencing sits in each collection's own QC, and the comparison is between peer depositories, so no single actor owns the pair. Third: a systematics norm that reads variation as a curation error to fix case by case rather than a distribution to estimate — (A) narrates four non-identical holdings as one strain's "odyssey" and proposes no survey; JCM absorbs each counterexample as a withdrawal notice. STRUCK on adversarial review: the record's lead mechanism ("public metadata names a strain, not a distributor") is a why-answering-is-hard for the secondary arm only, since the record itself concedes ampoules are sold; and the reputational mechanism weakens to "publishing a caveat is cheaper than publishing a measured failure rate about a peer".
