ID: UQ-20261021-01
Date: 2026-10-21
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): Medicine — clinical-trial methodology and chronic-disease therapeutics. Target field (decides novelty, would act): trialists, regulators reading estimands, pharmacometricians. Neighbour vocabularies swept: survey-methodology panel conditioning / measurement reactivity, trial measurement-reaction methodology (MERIT/MRC), causal inference with irregular or informative observation times, pharmacometrics / pharmionics (Urquhart, Vrijens, PAGE/PAGANZ), white-coat adherence in glaucoma, hypertension, HIV, epilepsy and anticoagulation, econometric anticipation effects, event-sequence periodicity, French/German/Spanish terms.

Question (canonical): V2 (Gate 1 reformulation, the one permitted; scored as canonical) — In >=2 independent cohorts or trials holding per-patient time-stamped electronic dosing records over whole inter-visit intervals and a visit-measured biomarker whose pharmacodynamic response time is shorter than that interval (BP, LDL, HIV RNA, IOP, INR), under one pre-declared exposure-response model per biomarker with >=2 model forms as sensitivity: what is the signed difference, per randomised arm and in the arm contrast, between the treatment effect as the visit-measured analysis reports it and the effect predicted when each patient's realised doses are redistributed uniformly across the interval (dose-count-preserving; visit-entrained component removed, total exposure fixed), expressed as a fraction of the observed arm difference against a pre-declared margin, with HbA1c as the pre-specified falsification arm in which the difference must vanish?
V1 (as intaken) differs only in specification, not in object; both texts in batches/2026-10-21-0452/UQ-20261021-01-record.md.

Alternative formulations:
- How much of a drug's measured effect is an artefact of patients taking it more faithfully in the days before the visit at which the effect is measured?
- Treating the visit calendar as a cause of the exposure used to evaluate it, what is the visit-entrainment bias in the ITT estimate, and does it differ between arms?

Motivating gap:
Source method: anomaly mining. The anomaly is established on a primary source read at full text and independently re-read by one adversary: Poleon, Sabbagh & Racette (Front Med 2022;9:867884; 66 POAG patients, MEMS caps, 28 days bracketing one visit) report adherence rising 85.5 -> 88.5% from Pre14-4 to Pre3-1 (p = 0.01) overall and 94.0 -> 97.7% (p = 0.001) in the optimal-adherence subgroup (n = 49), with no pattern in suboptimal adherers (p = 0.69). Two things verification adds. The surge is carried by the already-adherent only BEFORE the visit: after it the full sample falls (87.0 +/- 23.9 -> 84.9 +/- 23.3, p = 0.02) while the optimal subgroup RISES (95.2 +/- 12.0 -> 95.4 +/- 5.7, p = 0.007), and the paper says in terms that "patients with optimal adherence showed an increase in adherence both prior to and after the clinic visit", so no subgroup reproduces the full-sample decline and the suboptimal group's own fall (63.2 -> 54.7, -8.5 pp, p = 0.32) is attributed by the authors to n = 17 and high variability rather than to absence. Separately, an anomaly in the source itself, reproduced not corrected: that +0.2 pp optimal-subgroup post-visit change carries p = 0.007 with the SD more than halving, printed identically in the Abstract, the Results body and Table 2. The SDs matter here: every mean is +/- 21 to 24 points against shifts of 2 to 3 points, and the 88.5-to-84.9 pair across the visit is never tested. The entrainment is owned as a patient trait ("whitecoat adherence") and corrected out of the ADHERENCE estimate; it is not posed as a property of the measurement schedule that biases the EFFICACY estimate. Correction owed to adversary 2's re-read: in the optimal subgroup the post-visit comparison is 95.2 -> 95.4, a slight increase, so the full rise-then-fall cycle is supported only on the pre-visit side in the subgroup carrying the effect — which is the side the bias limb needs. The nearest statement of a consequence in any opened source is one uncited sentence in P1's Introduction about a clinician's bedside inference in glaucoma care, not about an estimated treatment effect.

Presuppositions:
1. One dataset holds time-stamped dosing records AND a fast visit-measured biomarker AND a randomised arm contrast. HALF-ESTABLISHED by Gate 4: Tousset et al. (PAGE 2006) hold MEMS records plus office SBP in a 44-patient trial cohort, but state no arm contrast. Binding feasibility presupposition.
2. Adherence is entrained to visit timing, not merely noisy. ESTABLISHED in one indication (P1, full text); magnitude ~3 pp overall, concentrated in near-ceiling adherers. Unverified in HIV/hypertension.
3. The named biomarkers respond faster than the inter-visit interval. MIS-SPECIFIED, per adversary 3: the mechanism needs the PD time constant to be comparable to the SURGE window (~3 days), not to the inter-visit interval; no time constant was sourced for any named biomarker.
4. Electronic timestamps index ingestion. CONTESTED and sign-bearing: MEMS logs container openings as a dose proxy (stated in P1 itself), and curiosity or tidying openings have no reason to be stationary before an appointment.
5. A counterfactual time-averaged-dosing effect is well defined. RESOLVED BY CONSTRUCTION at V2, at the price of model-dependence; adversary 1 adds that uniform redistribution is a convention, since real non-entrained dosing also clusters (drug holidays).
6. The entrainment is not already cancelled by the comparator arm. CONTESTED; adversary 3 notes cancellation is design-dependent — nil in placebo-controlled designs, partial in active-comparator ones.
7. NEW, unaddressed in the record (adversary 3): the datasets in which the quantity is computable are monitored, so patients can anticipate a cap download; the trials whose estimates are allegedly contaminated have no download to anticipate. Data and target differ on the very variable that could manufacture the surge.

What would count as an answer:
A signed, interval-estimated difference in >=2 independent datasets between the visit-measured effect and the effect re-estimated with the visit-entrained dosing component removed under the dose-count-preserving regime and a pre-declared exposure-response model, reported per arm and as a fraction of the arm difference against a pre-declared margin, plus the HbA1c falsification arm in which it must vanish. Small and margin-compatible everywhere with the falsification arm behaving = a negative answer that retires the question. An interval too wide to separate the answers is declared in advance to be an answer about feasibility, not a null.

Novelty — queries run (query -> one-line result):
38 distinct queries in total: 11 at Gate 2 (record), 9 + 9 + 9 by three independent adversaries, each in vocabularies the record had not tried; 17 pages opened or attempted across all four agents. Full lists with per-query results: batches/2026-10-21-0452/UQ-20261021-01-record.md and -adversary-1.md, -adversary-2.md, -adversary-3.md. The most informative:
- [MANDATORY own-field own-words title query] pre-visit adherence surge overestimates drug efficacy blood pressure measured at clinic visit electronic monitoring quantified -> no such paper; only adherence-measurement trial registrations. The obvious title does not exist in the candidate's own field.
- [MANDATORY "what fraction of X" already-computed query] what proportion of measured treatment effect attributable to visit-related adherence improvement quantified percentage -> NO PUBLISHED FIGURE FOUND; results were registrations, SAPs and adherence-category tables.
- blood pressure measured at clinic visit higher adherence preceding days ... antihypertensive efficacy -> the find of Gate 4: Tousset et al., PAGE 15 (2006) Abstr 1008, opened independently by adversaries 1 and 2.
- Goetghebeur Vrijens "compliance pattern" "treatment effect" randomized electronic monitoring structural model -> Vrijens & Goetghebeur, Controlled Clinical Trials 1997;18:187-203, opened at full abstract (adversary 3, F4).
- PAGANZ "Pharmacodynamic modelling approaches in the setting of suboptimal drug adherence" -> opened twice (adversaries 1 and 3): simulated IV drug, doses missed at RANDOM, bias only of PK parameters. The record's own named residual risk is CLEARED, not inherited.
- "Weisskittel-Compliance" OR "compliance de la blouse blanche" OR "adherencia de bata blanca" -> null; every hit is about physician attire.
COULD NOT READ, with routes that failed, and grounding nothing in either direction: HIV Clinical Trials 2008, doi 10.1310/hct0904-238 (tandfonline CLIENT_ERROR; surfaced in five separate queries across two adversaries; the single most important unread source); Feinstein 1990, Arch Intern Med 150:1377-8 (no publisher URL surfaced); Cramer et al. 1990; the 1980s Kass eyedrop-monitor papers; an AES abstract titled "One month adherence in children with new onset epilepsy: white coat compliance does not occur" (title only).

Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources):
Re-ranked by the judge after Gate 4; the record's MERIT protocol (Miles et al., Trials 2018;19:653, full text) and Kant & Krijthe (arXiv:2501.11449, full text) stay in the record as the method-owning neighbours and were not re-opened by any adversary.
P-a. Vrijens B, Goetghebeur E (1997). "Comparing compliance patterns between randomized treatments." Controlled Clinical Trials 18(3):187-203, doi 10.1016/S0197-2456(96)00235-8 — READ LEVEL: full abstract plus repository record (documentserver.uhasselt.be/handle/1942/3351). Unit: patient-day dosing indicator in a randomised BP trial (self-monitoring vs not), MEMS-timestamped. Endpoint: the dosing indicator itself, not BP. Comparator: randomised groups. Estimand: between-arm comparison of the full pattern of daily dosing; found no difference in average compliance but a treatment x time interaction. NOT found in the abstract: visits, a mapping of pattern to effect, white-coat. Post-batch verification downgrades these from verified absences: the read is ABSTRACT ONLY of a 17-page methods paper, and an abstract cannot evidence absence. ScienceDirect is robots-closed to this environment at host level and no deposited copy exists (the Hasselt record states access closed, no file attached), so resolving them needs a different route entirely rather than more calls at the publisher. Two wording corrections: the paper says "no simple difference in average compliance levels", and dropping "simple" inverts its methodological point, which is that simple summaries miss the structure; and "treatment x time interaction" tightens its "an interesting interaction between treatment and time", for which the abstract gives no estimate, interval or test. Note also that MEMS records a container OPENING, not an ingestion, so no ingestion claim is available from this source, and that this is a methods paper analysing another trial's data whose parent investigators the abstract does not name.
P-b. Tousset E, Figueiredo H, Schneider MP, Bugnon O, Vrijens B (2006). "Relation between patients' variable compliance and office blood pressure in treatment-resistant hypertension." PAGE 15, Abstr 1008 — READ LEVEL: abstract, opened independently by two adversaries. Unit: patient-visit, 44 trial + 45 GP patients. Endpoint: office SBP. Comparator: none; an exposure gradient within one model. Estimand: a sigmoid Emax exposure-response (24 mmHg [11-37] at 100% exposure, half-maximal at 51% [26-76]), exposure defined as correct dosing days in the 10 days BEFORE the BP measurement. Four corrections from post-batch verification, all bearing on how far this curve can be pushed. (i) "95% CI" is NOT in the source: the abstract prints [11-37] and [26-76] unlabelled and nowhere states what the brackets denote, so the uncertainty is a range of unstated type — UNCHECKED, not disproved, the reader having hit its fetch cap before re-reading the Objectives section or the linked poster. (ii) "Correct dosing days" is permissive: the daily indicator is "whether the patient took at least one of the drugs as prescribed by the physician", so in a population on three or more antihypertensives a day on which one of three was taken counts, and "100% drug exposure" is a weaker condition than the short form implies. (iii) Only the 44 are treatment-resistant despite the title; the 45 are "uncontrolled patients followed by general practitioners" with no drug count and no resistance criterion, so the pooled 24 mmHg and 51% are not estimates in a purely resistant population. (iv) Exposure is DEFINED as a number of days out of 10 and REPORTED as a percentage, with no mapping stated in the source. The item is a conference poster abstract with no volume or page numbers; any citation supplying them would be inventing them, and the 10-day window is stated in Results, not Methods.
P-c. Poleon S, Sabbagh N, Racette L (2022). "Whitecoat Adherence in Patients With Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma." Front Med 9:867884 — READ LEVEL: full text, re-read independently by adversary 2 (every figure reproduced). Unit: patient-visit window, 66 POAG patients, one visit each. Endpoint: daily MEMS adherence %. No clinical outcome; IOP never related to the surge. Comparator: within-patient adjacent peri-visit windows. Estimand: within-patient change in mean adherence.

Novelty — how this differs from each:
vs P-a: same two objects and the same arm-contrast frame, but its endpoint IS the dosing pattern, not a biomarker effect; it has no visit node, no exposure-response map and no counterfactual regime, so it cannot bound the efficacy consequence in either direction. It is the strongest evidence against the record's reason for silence and still not a prior formulation of the question.
vs P-b: it fits exactly the exposure-response map V2 says must be declared, in one of the index indications, with exposure already defined on a pre-visit window — but it reports an association and a regimen-relevant Emax, never names entrainment, states no arm contrast, and estimates no schedule-induced bias.
vs P-c: it measures the entrainment and stops; its endpoint is adherence, where the candidate's is a biomarker treatment effect with adherence as the exposure. No arm, no outcome analysed, no exposure-response mapping.

Novelty confidence: Medium
Grounds: 38 distinct queries across the candidate's own field in its own words, the historical term, survey methodology, trial measurement-reaction methodology, irregular-observation-time causal inference, pharmionics/pharmacometrics, four indication vocabularies, econometric anticipation, event-sequence periodicity and three other languages. The mandatory own-field title query returned no such paper; the mandatory fraction query returned no published figure; no source opened by any of four agents asks or answers the question. Not High: two neighbours are genuinely close (P-b holds the exact model on a pre-visit window; P-a holds the exact arm-contrast-on-dosing-patterns frame). Not Low: both miss on the limb that matters — P-a has no outcome mapping, P-b has no arm and no counterfactual, P-c has no outcome at all. Held under explicit suspicion, because Gate 4's attack-7 rule says a failed reason-for-silence makes the novelty finding itself suspect; three independent sweeps nevertheless found no prior that asks it, and one on-term source (doi 10.1310/hct0904-238) remains unread.

Significance — consequence:
If the entrained component is material in fast-biomarker indications, the visit schedule stops being a logistical parameter and becomes an efficacy-relevant design parameter: part of what a registration trial estimates is a property of its own calendar, which no label reproduces. Non-inferiority margins and dose-ranging slopes calibrated on visit-measured effects would be mis-scaled; part of the efficacy-effectiveness gap would be mechanical schedule geometry rather than a fact about patients; and an E9(R1) estimand would have to declare whether it is defined under the trial's visit schedule, for which the five attributes have no slot. If the answer is no, a plausible threat to every fast-biomarker endpoint is retired on evidence instead of by silence. Adversary 3's correction, accepted: the efficacy-effectiveness limb is weaker than the record states, because routine care also has visits, so only the trial-versus-practice difference in visit frequency can enter that gap.

Significance — audience:
(a) Trial methodologists and funders: the MRC commissioned MERIT on exactly this bias family, and MERIT's taxonomy slot A2 (measurement x arm interaction) is empty for this mechanism by verified full-text absence. (b) Regulators reading estimands: a signed magnitude would be the argument for an additional declaration under E9(R1). (c) Pharmacometricians: a visit-locked periodic component is a specification error they can act on — though adversary 2's point stands that the one opened pharmacometric model of a visit-measured biomarker is already visit-locked by construction, which weakens the claim that the field treats dosing histories as exchangeable in time. (d) Clinicians in the index indications, who already act on the idea qualitatively and have no magnitude to discount by.

Significance — fecundity:
Opens: visit spacing as a bias-minimising design problem; whether remote or at-home biomarker capture yields a less entrained estimate; whether scheduling frequency is itself an adherence intervention, making the control arm's calendar part of the control treatment; whether arm-asymmetric entrainment is a signature of functional unblinding; whether the entrained component is a measurable term in an efficacy-effectiveness decomposition.

Significance — anchoring:
The efficacy-effectiveness gap; the white-coat family (white-coat hypertension, white-coat compliance/adherence, pseudoresistance); measurement reactivity in trials (MERIT's unresolved A2); causal inference with informative observation times (Kant & Krijthe's measurement-time-to-treatment arrow); E9(R1) estimand specification; and the standing complaint that electronic adherence data collected in trials is used only for compliance screening.

Reason for silence:
STRUCK, on two independently opened primary sources. The record's mechanism — that neither community held both objects, that a declarable non-ITT exposure-mapped estimand arrived only with E9(R1) in 2019 and the measurement-time causal apparatus later still, and that "before that the question had no sayable form" — fails. Tousset et al. (PAGE 2006) held time-stamped MEMS records, a visit-measured fast biomarker, a trial cohort and an exposure-response model at once, with exposure deliberately defined in the 10 days before the BP measurement, thirteen years before the bridge the record says was needed (adversaries 1 and 2, independently). Vrijens & Goetghebeur (Controlled Clinical Trials 1997) went further and twenty-two years earlier, in a trial-methodology journal, comparing "the full pattern of daily dosing indicators" between randomised groups in a blood-pressure trial (adversary 3). The vocabulary "white-coat compliance" has been in print since 1990. The fallback — that this community's estimand was a slope, or regimen comparison, or protection of PK estimates, rather than an audit of a trial's own estimand — restates the original argument after its factual premise is gone, and the incentive argument runs the wrong way, since a vendor of dosing monitors has every reason to publish that a visit calendar inflates an effect estimate. Two explanations survive: that the insiders who held both objects judged the quantity a priori negligible, which is attack 1 restated and a significance problem rather than a novelty mechanism; or "no one thought of it", which this gate does not accept.

Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status):
Three independent fresh-context adversaries; none was shown another's log, and the third was run as a harder rerun. Disguise EXECUTED by all three: 9 new-vocabulary queries each (27 in total, 8 required), with pages opened in each pass; Disguise is verified as run, not unverified. Verbatim logs: batches/2026-10-21-0452/UQ-20261021-01-adversary-1.md, -adversary-2.md, -adversary-3.md.

Strongest remaining objection:
The reason for silence is weak, and the most likely replacement for it is also the candidate's own likely answer. Vrijens & Goetghebeur (1997) and Tousset et al. If thirty years of silence was a judgement that the effect is negligible, the question is novel chiefly because it is not worth asking, and Gate 4's own rule then turns that silence back on the Medium novelty grade.

Post-batch verification softens this objection without removing it, and the softening is worth stating precisely. The claim that the mechanism "has collapsed on two opened primary sources" overstated the reads behind it: Vrijens & Goetghebeur was read at ABSTRACT level only, so what it establishes is that the paper's abstract does not ask the question, not that its 17 pages do not; and Tousset is a conference poster abstract whose brackets are of unstated type and whose exposure definition counts a day on which one of three or more drugs was taken as prescribed. The arithmetic bound therefore rests on a curve whose top end attaches to a weaker adherence standard than the short form implied, and whose uncertainty cannot be carried as a 95% interval because the source never says that is what the brackets are. The bound is still the right order of magnitude and still the strongest thing said against this candidate; it is one abstract-level read away from being decisive rather than, as Gate 5 had it, already decisive.

Validated requires all five of: Vrijens & Goetghebeur 1997 read at FULL TEXT, since a promotion condition hinging on what a paper does not contain is discharged only by reading the paper and the present read is its abstract (ScienceDirect is robots-closed here, so this needs an interlibrary copy or another deposit, not more publisher calls); a reason-for-silence mechanism that survives that read and Tousset et al. 2006 (or significance re-argued explicitly on the premise that the answer is a small bounded null); well-posedness to 3/3 by separating ingestion from container-opening with an ingestion-evidencing device or validation subsample, sourcing each named biomarker's PD time constant against the ~3-day surge window, and answering the download-reactivity objection with a design that can observe the surge unmonitored; doi 10.1310/hct0904-238 (Podsadecki, HIV Clinical Trials 2008) and Feinstein 1990 read at full text to close Disguise beyond Partial; and a numeric pre-declared margin plus a magnitude check in a steep-exposure-response indication (HIV RNA or INR) that the hypertension envelope does not reach.

## Verification of the load-bearing priors at first hand (post-batch, 2026-10-21)

Three fresh-context readers, each handed one claim and its source and none handed any reviewer's reasoning. The verdict does not move: Provisional, capped by attack 7 Unresolved in all three adversaries and by well-posedness 2/3, neither of which is a claim about a source. What moves is how much weight the capping objection can carry, and the answer is less than Gate 5 gave it.

**Tousset et al. 2006 is real and its numerals are reproduced correctly, and three of the ledger's additions to it are the writer's words rather than the source's.** "95% CI" is the most consequential: the abstract prints its brackets unlabelled, and the reader hit its fetch cap before it could resolve what they denote, so this is recorded as UNCHECKED and not as refuted. "Correct dosing days" conceals a permissive definition — at least one of three or more antihypertensives taken as prescribed — which makes the 24 mmHg Emax attach to a less demanding adherence standard than the entry's short form suggests. And despite the title only 44 of the 89 patients are treatment-resistant. The 10-day exposure window is exact, and the confirmed negative is worth recording as a negative rather than as something unchecked: the abstract reports no randomised comparison and no visit-timing attribution at all.

**Poleon et al. 2022 holds field for field, and the entry's own statement of it was accurate.** Front matter, the 28-day window, the Pre14-4 to Pre3-1 and Post1-3 to Post4-14 comparisons, the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, and the clean negative that intraocular pressure is never measured or analysed, all check out. What verification adds is the post-visit direction: the optimal-adherence subgroup rises after the visit while the full sample falls, so "carried by the already-adherent" is true of the pre-visit surge only. The source also carries an internal anomaly, reproduced above rather than corrected.

**Vrijens & Goetghebeur 1997 is the read that does not support what was asked of it.** Front matter and the endpoint hold at abstract level. The three absences do not: an abstract cannot evidence absence over a 17-page methods paper, and they are downgraded above to "not found in the abstract". The abstract's own hedge was also dropped — "no simple difference in average compliance levels" is not "no difference in average compliance", and the difference between them is the paper's point.

**One correction to this pass's own conduct, and it is the same mistake this ledger has made before.** The brief for the Poleon check was written from the batch runner's structured summary field rather than from the entry or the record, and that field compressed the paper's pre- and post-visit subgroup results into a single "carried by the >=80% subgroup, absent in the <80% subgroup". The reader correctly found that claim directionally wrong — and it is not a claim this entry or its record makes. The record states all four means with their standard deviations, names both window pairs, names the test, gives the optimal subgroup's post-visit figures and the suboptimal group's two p-values. So the Poleon defects that pass turned up belong to the brief, not to the ledger, and are recorded here as mine. Memory already carries this rule from 2026-10-18 — brief a checker from the full citation the ENTRY carries, never from a label in a log or a summary field — and it has now cost a second pass its accuracy on one claim.

## Verification of the kill at first hand (post-batch, 2026-10-21)

Three fresh-context readers, each handed one claim and its source and none handed any reviewer's reasoning. The verdict does not move. The kill's load-bearing leg survives in better shape than it arrived; its two supporting legs fall.

**Leg 1, Ross et al. 2012, holds, and is now the most thoroughly checked claim in this batch.** The front matter matches field for field on two independent records (Sarah Ross, Laura Hamilton, Cristin Ryan, Christine Bond; Postgraduate Medical Journal 88(1043):507-510, September 2012; received 9 November 2011, accepted 8 April 2012; PMID 22582180; issue section "Original Article"). The 61% sentence is verbatim and is the entire Results section of the abstract: both edges fall at sentence boundaries, the page returned an 18-word count for Results that matches the assembled sentence, and 112/183 re-derives to 61.2%. There is no surrounding clause able to change its sense and no dropped hedge. Three things to carry, none of which weakens the kill: the figure is bare, with no interval or p value; its denominator is restricted by the source's own clause to new-medicine prescribing events, so no all-prescriptions rate exists in the abstract; and the design is six wards of one large UK teaching hospital over January to April 2011, with the paper itself calling the estimate an attempt to "provisionally quantify and describe".

**Leg 2, the instrument-misclassification theorem, fails on scope.** Adversary 1 made Disguise Unresolved on three legs — Ross for the rate, Baysari et al. 2011 for the intervention mis-targeting, and Jiang and Ding for the IV consequence being "theoretically pre-answered" — and listed as its own Unverified checks exactly the two things that have now been read: "Jiang & Ding's exact measurement-error assumption text" and "the continuous-instrument case (no primary opened)". Both resolve against the kill. The no-bias result is Theorem 1 for an all-binary model, Z, D and Y each in {0,1}, under randomisation of Z, monotonicity, exclusion and non-differentiality of all three errors. The paper's single encounter with a non-binary instrument runs the other way: dichotomisation at a non-median quantile is a DIFFERENTIAL error, with sections 3 and 4 "not applicable". A provider-level preference-rate instrument whose error is wrong-provider attribution is simply not in the paper; the finding is an ABSENCE, which supports neither direction. Three quotation defects accompany it, each from the catalogue: the recorded "does not bias the estimate" is a mid-sentence slice cut before a comma and stripped of the non-differentiality condition that is its only qualifier in the abstract; the recorded Assumption 2 string is a LABEL LINE ending at a colon, whose substance is three conditional-probability equalities joint over D, Y and Z; and "We do not consider the differential measurement error of Z." was recorded with a full stop the source does not have, cutting the clause ", because the measurement of Z often precedes (D,Y) and its measurement error is unlikely to depend on later variables" — the clause that bears on any setting where Z's error could depend on later variables, which is precisely the candidate's worry. One further correction cuts the other way: it is wrong to read the no-bias result as silence on precision, because section 8.1 gives first-stage attenuation RD_{D|Z'} = r'_Z x RD_{D|Z} and an asymptotic regime in which a weak-instrument problem is possible. The published version, Biometrika 107(1):238-245 (2020), was missing from the entry, and citing the preprint alone also hid its Miscellanea short-paper status.

**Leg 3, the provider-preference-IV methods literature, addresses a different defect.** Güdemann et al.'s within-practice-heterogeneity concern is real and quoted correctly, so the entry's first string stands. But the gap this candidate is about — the clinician named on a prescription not being the clinician who chose the drug — is genuinely absent from the paper and must not be inferred from the practice-aggregation sentence. Two further corrections: the multi-construction recommendation is quoted with its hedge removed, the source reading "If possible, treatment effect estimates from multiple constructions should be derived and their coherence assessed [21]", and it cites Uddin et al. [21], so the paper endorses that proposal rather than originating it. Also recorded against a near-miss: the paper's sentence that "In most routine clinical databases, the reason underlying a treatment decision is not systematically recorded" notes the absence of a DIFFERENT thing — the reason, not the decider's identity — and is not a flag of this candidate's gap. The item is an arXiv preprint with no published version found, and the surname carries an umlaut: Güdemann.

**Why the verdict stands anyway, and what that costs.** Of the three legs under the fatal Disguise objection, the one that survives is the one that matches the candidate's own Alternative Formulation 1, in its own field and its own words, with the number published; the Gate 2 Low grade rested on that same source. A ground whose own source survives first-hand verification is not a withdrawn ground, so no late Gate 4 is owed and none was run. What falls is decoration, and the objection is rewritten above to name only what holds. The honest cost of that rewrite is that limb (c) is restored as un-asked: this entry is rejected because its headline question was answered in 2012, not because every limb of it was.

**One correction to this pass's own conduct.** The brief sent to the theorem reader carried a stray identifier, "arXiv:2501", beside the correct 1906.02030. It was the brief's error, not the entry's — neither the entry nor the record contains that string — and the reader flagged it as a ledger defect. It is recorded here as mine so the ledger does not inherit a defect it never had.

ID: UQ-20261021-03
Date: 2026-10-21
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): Medicine — patient safety, hospital pharmacy and medication systems (target field for novelty). Method-owning neighbours swept: system reliability engineering/PRA (CCF beta, MGL, alpha factors), LOPA/independent-protection-layer, human reliability analysis (THERP dependence assessment), industrial serial-inspection theory, latent-class conditional-dependence biostatistics, human-factors automation bias.
Question (canonical): For each of a pre-declared set of medication-error classes, restricted per class to orders whose barrier-capability set holds >=2 barriers (CPOE alert, pharmacist verification, barcode administration) with per-barrier outcome joinable to the order record: (a) estimate P(barrier k+1 fails | barrier k failed) against the same cohort's marginal P(barrier k+1 fails), with intervals; (b) express the coupling as a CCF beta factor (or alpha-factor set) with an interval; (c) report the ratio of realised all-barrier passage probability to the prediction from that same cohort's own marginals; (d) bound the unobserved "passed every barrier, never detected" stratum with declared assumptions; (e) record whether any of the site's own published barrier/FMEA/business-case analyses states a product of barrier failure probabilities. (V2; V1 and the Gate 1 reformulation rationale are in the record.)
Alternative formulations:
- Are a hospital's successive medication checks statistically independent, and if not, how much does adding another check really reduce the chance an error reaches the patient?
- Estimate the common-cause coupling between CPOE decision support, pharmacy verification and barcode administration for matched error classes, and the error in independence-based barrier calculations that follows.
Motivating gap: Medicine imported defence-in-depth as a qualitative metaphor; the apparatus that makes it quantitative (beta factor, IPL independence criterion, THERP dependence assessment) returns zero healthcare applications, while the field measures only per-barrier marginals. Corrected at Gate 4: the field's own professional literature does state the arithmetic — David U, "Double-checking: does it work?", Can J Hosp Pharm 2003;56(3) (ISMP Canada PDF, opened in full by A1) prints "the checking error rate x the task error rate" and "5% of 5%, or only 0.25%", and in the same column "not all double checks are truly independent" and "there is a high probability that the 2 individuals doing the checking will make the same error". The record's secondhand "ISMP Canada 2005, 1 in 400" is this 2003 column; the product stated is task-error x one check, not a product across barriers.
Presuppositions: (1) each barrier's per-order outcome electronically recorded and joinable — CPOE/BCMA established in principle, pharmacist-verification content granularity CONTESTED and unevidenced either way (leading feasibility risk); (2) a ground-truth error label assignable independently of the barriers — CONTESTED and central; a rule-computed label for CDS-covered classes reuses barrier 1's rule, so only blinded re-review is independent (A3); (3) >=2 barriers nominally capable per class — CONTESTED, and A3's own class analysis finds few classes with three capable barriers; (4) the field's reasoning multiplies barrier failure probabilities — now EVIDENCED at task x one check (CJHP 2003), still imputed across barriers; (5) event counts sufficient for the needed precision — CONTESTED, needs a power statement (Galanter: 32 intercepted wrong-patient errors in 127,320 alerts); (6) fixed barrier order — CONTESTED, order-of-arrival must be modelled.
What would count as an answer: per class, limbs (a)-(e) above with intervals; a beta indistinguishable from zero reported against a stated minimum detectable coupling answers negatively and is substantive. Defect carried forward (A2): limb (a)'s within-cohort marginal is not observable in a filter cascade — every error reaching barrier k+1 is already one barrier k failed to stop, so conditional and marginal coincide; the marginal requires a between-cohort comparator in which the upstream barrier was inactive (rule never configured, pre-implementation period, unit without BCMA). Positive-control injection is not a route for live orders.
Novelty — queries run (query -> one-line result): 37 distinct queries — 11 at Gate 2 (web-search cap; 5 fetches) plus 26 Disguise queries across three adversaries (8 + 9 + 9), full lists in batches/2026-10-21-0452/UQ-20261021-03-record.md and the three adversary files. Most informative: "Are medication safety barriers independent? conditional probability error passes CPOE alert pharmacist verification barcode administration" (own-field, own-words) -> no paper poses it; "probability medication error escapes all checks reaches patient ... published" -> the all-barrier escape probability and independence-excess factor are unpublished; "human reliability analysis dependence between checker and performer ... THERP level of dependence healthcare" -> zero healthcare returns, the method field's own name for the quantity; "layers of protection analysis independent protection layer criterion hospital medication safety" -> 100% process industry; "multiplying barrier failure probabilities overestimates risk reduction correlated safety checks hospital 'independence assumption'" -> the critique is in print in dam safety, process safety and autonomous systems, not medicine; A1 "'independent double check' '1 in 400' 5% error rate ... probability both checkers miss" -> found the CJHP 2003/ISMP primary source; A2 "latent class model conditional dependence between imperfect error detection methods adverse drug event no gold standard" -> machinery mature and medicine-owned, zero application to barriers; A2 "automation bias clinical decision support caused clinicians to miss prescribing errors downstream verifier dependence measured" -> Lyell 2017; A3 "'quality control quantification' radiation oncology QC checks sensitivity ... combinations of checks redundant Ford" -> Ford 2012; A3 Japanese double-check query -> BMJ Qual Saf 29(7):536 conceptual piece. Disguise was executed by all three adversaries (26 queries, min 8 each met); it is not unverified.
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources): (1) Lyell D, Magrabi F, Raban MZ, Pont LG, Baysari MT, Day RO, Coiera E. "Automation bias in electronic prescribing." BMC Med Inform Decis Mak 2017;17(1), doi:10.1186/s12911-017-0425-5 — abstract only via opus.lib.uts.edu.au/handle/10453/123624; 120 final-year medical students, nine simulated scenarios, incorrect CDS increased omission errors by 33.3%/24.5%/26.7% against no CDS. (2) David U. "Double-checking: does it work?" Can J Hosp Pharm 2003;56(3), ismp-canada.org/download/cjhp0306.pdf — full column read; states the product and asserts endogenous/exogenous dependence qualitatively. (3) Ford EC, Terezakis S, Souranis A, Harris K, Gay H, Mutic S. "Quality control quantification (QCQ)." Int J Radiat Oncol Biol Phys 2012;84(3):e263-e269, doi:10.1016/j.ijrobp.2012.04.036 — abstract only, and at one remove via a third-party institutional repository, mostly as paraphrase with two strings verbatim; 63% for physicist plan review holds, but "all individual checks <50% sensitive" is an INFERENCE from a best-at-63% sentence and does not follow — no 50% threshold appeared in anything the post-batch reader could open, and the 4.0 +/- 2.3 versus 2.6 +/- 1.4 figures do not occur in the text available at all, so both are UNCHECKED rather than confirmed. The two recorded strings are also one sentence cut in two ("An effectiveness of 97% was achieved with 7 checks used in combination."), and "effectiveness of 97%" detached from its seven-check qualifier can be read as a single check's effectiveness. Carry the denominator with any of these figures: sensitivity here is over voluntarily reported, non-harming incidents, judged counterfactually as what a check "could have caught", "effectiveness of 97% ... with 7 checks used in combination and was not further improved with more checks"; incidents detectable by 4.0 +/- 2.3 vs 2.6 +/- 1.4 checks. Also on record: White 2010 Qual Saf Health Care 19(6):562-7 (0/30 detection of seeded clinical-decision errors); Radley 2013 and Galanter 2013 JAMIA 20:470-6 / 477-81 (Crossref-verified by A2); Anderson 2003 JAMIA 10:292-3 (combines barriers, states no combination rule); BMJ Qual Saf 2020;29(7):536 — the attribution is now RESOLVED: 536 is a commentary ON the Koyama systematic review, which sits separately at 29(7):595 in the same issue, so these two strings are the commentary's words about the review and must not be put in the review's mouth. Front matter for both is still COULD NOT READ (authors, printed title, article-type label, page range and DOI), so the "commentary" label rests on third-party records and stays provisional until a byline is read — "both people may be affected by the same disturbances in the environment", "full independence cannot be achieved for checks"; Westbrook et al. 2020 double-checking observational study — SECONDHAND via trade coverage only.
Novelty — how this differs from each: vs Lyell — unit is a student prescriber in simulation with CDS present/absent, coupling measured between an automated check and the human who is also the error source; no downstream pharmacist or BCMA barrier, no conditional on operational records, no beta, no escape ratio. vs CJHP 2003 — a qualitative assertion about two human checkers at one step, and a product of task error x one check, with no measurement anywhere; the candidate's estimand is the measured cross-barrier conditional. vs Ford — another specialty, judged capability ("could have detected") on voluntarily reported incidents, combination effectiveness computed as a realised union, not an independence product or a coupling parameter; never-detected stratum absent by construction. vs White/Radley/Galanter — marginal per-barrier detection, barrier-vs-no-barrier attributable reduction, and a descriptive per-alert interception rate respectively; 0/4 of unit, endpoint, comparator and estimand match in each case. vs the method-owning fields — the formalism is parameterised and alive (THERP dependence, CCF beta/MGL/alpha, the IPL independence criterion, serial-inspection and latent-class models) and in 37 queries none was found pointed at a hospital medication barrier chain; the interface problem is real and sharper than the record states (A2's derivation): a barrier chain is a filter cascade, so when barrier k stops the error barrier k+1 never receives a demand, missingness is deterministic in the upstream outcome, and both latent-class estimators and demand-record CCF estimation are inapplicable as written.
Novelty confidence: Medium
Significance — consequence: If beta is materially above zero the realised escape probability exceeds the independence prediction by a computable factor and every "add another check" decision is overvalued by roughly that factor, moving the remedy from a fourth barrier to decorrelating the three that exist (modality, information source, operator, time). If it is indistinguishable from zero at a stated minimum detectable coupling, that is the first quantitative defence of medication defence-in-depth. Discount carried forward (A3): under the capability restriction few classes clearly have three capable barriers, so the headline "add vs decorrelate" decision mostly concerns barrier pairs.
Significance — audience: ISMP and ISMP Canada, whose own 2003 column supplies both the product arithmetic and the qualitative dependence claim without a measurement; hospital P&T and medication-safety committees pricing a proposed extra check; health-IT vendors and CDS/informatics governance configuring alert, verification and scan workflows; HFMEA practitioners whose ordinal detectability scores would become measured conditionals; accreditors setting double-check and scanning requirements. Documented as stuck, not imputed: Koyama's review concludes "There is insufficient evidence that double versus single checking of medication administration is associated with lower rates of MAEs or reduced harm" (abstract read first-hand by A1), and Ford 2012 shows a check-chain quantification was publishable and taken up in a sibling specialty. Caveat: the opened evidence concerns the human double check; the electronic three-barrier chain's audience is argued, not shown.
Significance — fecundity: which barrier pairs are decorrelated by modality, and whether modality diversity rather than barrier count is the design variable; whether automation complacency is estimable as a named alpha-factor cause; whether HFMEA detectability should be re-specified as a measured conditional; whether the same parameter transfers to transfusion bedside checks, surgical counts, specimen labelling and radiotherapy chart checks; whether accreditation should require evidence of a check's independence rather than its existence; and separating detectability frailty from true coupling.
Significance — anchoring: the unresolved double-checking effectiveness question; the Swiss-cheese model's holes, never made quantitative; alert-override and alert-fatigue research, which measures overrides but never the downstream conditional; HFMEA ordinal detectability; LOPA's IPL independence criterion, unapplied in healthcare; Ford 2012's check-chain quantification in radiation oncology; and this ledger's UQ-20261016-62, a structurally identical candidate killed five days ago by own-field prior art its Gate 2 missed.
Reason for silence: Primary (retained) — a disciplinary and committee boundary with no owner of the joined record: CPOE alerting is reported by clinical informatics, verification by pharmacy, scanning by nursing informatics, each as its own marginal indicator; the conditional belongs to no one's required reporting and needs three systems joined. Credible, but asserted rather than evidenced by any opened source. Secondary (STRUCK) — "medicine lacks the vocabulary" is refuted by opened primary sources: CJHP 2003 states the dependence in the field's own words, Lyell 2017 runs an experimental programme under the name automation bias, and BMJ Qual Saf 29(7):536 states the common-cause mechanism. Replacement secondary (A1/A2) — a new-data mechanism (the joined per-order record across CPOE, verification and BCMA exists only at sites with all three electronically, a recent condition) plus a cheaper-substitute mechanism (comparing outcomes with and without the extra check answers the field's decision question adequately, so the harder coupling question never had to be posed). Identification obstacle (unobserved passed-everything stratum) demoted to why-answering-is-hard, as the protocol requires.

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3
Strongest remaining objection: The own-field read record is incomplete at exactly the place a kill would live. Koyama et al.'s BMJ Qual Saf systematic review of double checking is still largely COULD NOT READ after Gate 2, three adversaries and the post-batch pass, though that pass reached enough of it to report one thing on point: on the text it could read, the review reports no conditional probability and no dependence measure between the two checks, only a qualitative Discussion remark that "any level of priming between the two checks can substantially decrease the probability of the checker detecting an error" and a count of three of 13 studies distinguishing independent from primed checking. That is silence on the candidate's estimand, not a denial of it, and the review's front matter is unread, the Westbrook 2020 primary is secondhand via trade coverage, and A3's unexplored lead — the alert-override literature possibly holding a per-alert linkage of prescriber override to pharmacist action with error labels — was not reached within budget. If any of those reports a downstream-barrier conditional on an upstream automated check, limb (a) for the dominant two-barrier class is already measured, novelty falls to Low and this entry becomes a Rejection; the structurally identical UQ-20261016-62 died this way five days ago.
Promotion requires: (i) open Koyama et al. full text at the publisher with its front matter, which the post-batch pass left unread at 29(7):595 after its query budget went on resolving the 536 commentary's attribution, plus the Westbrook 2020 primary, plus the Lyell 2019 follow-up and the Goddard/Roudsari/Wyatt automation-bias review, and confirm none reports a conditional miss probability for a downstream barrier (pharmacist verification or BCMA) given an upstream automated barrier's failure; (ii) search the alert-override literature specifically for per-alert prescriber-override-to-pharmacist-action linkage with error labels, and sweep radiology/cytology double reading on its own for a measured P(both readers miss) against independence — both currently unswept, not checked; (iii) replace limb (a)'s within-cohort marginal with a named between-cohort comparator in which the upstream barrier was inactive, restoring well-posedness to 3/3; (iv) add a frailty-versus-coupling identification step to limb (b) or demote the decorrelation remedy. With (i) and (ii) returning nothing on point, (iii) rewritten and (iv) addressed, novelty holds at Medium with the search record complete and the entry promotes to Validated; a single on-point hit in (i) or (ii) rejects it instead.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): establish feasibility before design — at one site with all three barriers electronically recorded, audit whether pharmacist verification is logged at content granularity rather than as a timestamp only (presupposition 1, the leading feasibility risk), and in the same pass identify a between-cohort stratum in which one barrier was inactive, since limb (a) cannot be estimated without it.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): n/a — not rejected, and no source was found that poses the question, so nothing is routed to the open-questions project.

## Verification of the close neighbours at first hand (post-batch, 2026-10-21)

Two fresh-context readers, each handed one claim and its source and neither handed any reviewer's reasoning. The verdict does not move: Provisional, on Medium novelty with close neighbours plus Gate 4 Partials, with no attack Unresolved from any of the three adversaries. One attribution is resolved in the candidate's favour and one claimed absence turns out to be an unread page.

**The two load-bearing quotations belong to a different article than the entry implied, and the correction matters.** "both people may be affected by the same disturbances in the environment" and "full independence cannot be achieved for checks" are the words of the commentary at BMJ Qual Saf 2020;29(7):536, not of the Koyama systematic review at 29(7):595. They are two articles in the same issue, the first commenting on the second. Attributing them to Koyama et al. would have put the commentary's framework-building claims into the mouth of the review it criticises for not distinguishing checking methods. The entry had them as unattributed, which was honest; they are now attributed, and the attribution is to the commentary. Two cautions carried forward: the second string is cut after "checks" where in place it is a "Therefore..." premise continuing into "and optimising independence works differently:", so quoted bare it reads as a verdict; and front matter for both articles remains COULD NOT READ, which is not NOT FOUND — both bodies were served.

**The decisive methodological question about Ford et al. 2012 could not be reached, and that is a different finding from the paper being silent.** Three publisher routes refused: doi.org returned HTTP 429 with a do-not-retry instruction, ScienceDirect was robots-disallowed, and the journal's own article page returned a client error. So whether its 97% combination figure is a realised union of checks, a product of independent per-check miss probabilities, or a measured conditional dependence is UNRESOLVED, and any claim that the paper contains no coupling or common-cause parameter is currently unsupported. What did hold is the part that bears on how the figure may be used at all: detection was judged counterfactually rather than observed, over voluntarily reported non-harming incidents, so 97% and 63% are conditional on reporting and on a retrospective counterfactual. Two of the entry's figures for this paper are now marked unchecked above rather than carried, and one of its claims — every individual check below 50% — is withdrawn as an inference that does not follow from the sentence it was drawn from.

**Why this does not reject the entry, and what would.** The entry's strongest objection says the own-field read record is incomplete at exactly the place a kill would live, and that is still true: the pass narrowed where the kill could be hiding without reaching it. On what could be read of the Koyama review there is no conditional miss probability for a downstream barrier given an upstream one, which is the finding that would have taken novelty to Low. Promotion condition (i) is rewritten above to name the front matter and page that the pass left unread, since a condition hinging on what a paper does not contain is discharged only by reading the paper.

ID: UQ-20261021-04
Date: 2026-10-21
Status: Provisional
Domain(s): Medicine — health systems, insurance coverage, access to care. Target field: US health-policy measurement (CMS, payers, KFF/trade analysts already ranking payers on the metric; specialty societies). Method-owning neighbours swept: queueing/OR (unobserved balking, silent abandonment), public-economics administrative burden and ordeal/take-up, survey methodology (coverage error, endogenous denominators), fair-lending discouraged-borrower econometrics, disability-insurance allowance-rate stringency.
Question (canonical): For a pre-declared set of payer-by-service cells drawn from the first years of CMS-0057-F public prior-authorization reporting, what fraction of prior-authorization-requiring clinical decisions terminate on the provider side before any request reaches the payer, and does cross-payer variation in the published denial rate predict that pre-submission attrition rate with a negative sign — in what share of cells does adding attrition reverse the ranking of payers by obstruction, against a flip threshold fixed before any data pull? (V2; the one permitted Gate 1 reformulation. V1 and the two factual corrections that forced it are in batches/2026-10-21-0452/UQ-20261021-04-record.md.)
Alternative formulations: (a) Does a low published prior-authorization denial rate mean a payer approves more care, or that fewer requests were ever filed? (b) Treating the new public prior-authorization metrics as an instrument with an endogenous denominator, estimate pre-submission attrition and the bias it induces in the metric as a measure of access to care.
Motivating gap: CMS-0057-F requires payers to publish, from CY2025, percentages approved/denied/overturned on denominators of requests the payer received or adjudicated; response time is measured from payer receipt, not provider send. Every published figure is conditioned on arrival, so care never requested cannot appear in it, while analysts (KFF, 13 Aug 2026; Becker's) are already ranking named payers on those percentages. The field has named denominator-side confounds it can see from payer files (gold carding, case mix, service mix, no counts) and none on the provider side.
Presuppositions: P1 arrival-conditioned denominator — ESTABLISHED, but not uniform ("CMS currently provides suggested denominators", standardisation only proposed in a 2026 rule; DHCS prints "adjudicated" against a narrative "received"). P2 pre-submission terminations identifiable from provider records — CONTESTED, lower bound only. P3 requirement lists matchable to orders — PARTLY ESTABLISHED, needs a sensitivity arm. P4 payers gain from submission friction — CONTESTED, carried as the hypothesis under test. P5 substitution vs abandonment separable — CONTESTED (already executed for drugs: 46.2%/53.8%, Brot-Goldberg et al.). P6 comparable cross-payer/service reporting — WEAKENED (percentages only, no counts, no service breakdown nationally, drugs excluded, inconsistent methods). P7 "public for the first time in 2026" — FALSE as stated; true only as "first nationally, on a uniform federal specification", and even that is qualified by the suggested-denominator finding.
What would count as an answer: Paired cell-level estimates of (i) the printed denial rate and (ii) a provider-side pre-submission attrition rate over PA-requiring decisions identified by a pre-declared matching rule, with the sign and magnitude of their cross-cell association under one primary estimator plus declared sensitivity arms (matching error, substitution-vs-abandonment, received-vs-adjudicated denominator), the post-submission auto-denial share reported separately because it loads the same metric with the opposite sign, and the share of cells whose obstruction ranking flips against a pre-fixed threshold. A null answers it; a negative association of stated size makes it a respecification question. Gate 5 note: on the present protocol the null is NOT yet interpretable (see strongest remaining objection).
Novelty — queries run (query → one-line result): 11 at Gate 2 (at cap) + 8 Disguise (adversary 1, 8/8) + 7 Disguise (adversary 2, 7 of 8 required — one short, self-disclosed) + 9 Disguise (adversary 3) = 35 recorded; full lists in batches/2026-10-21-0452/UQ-20261021-04-record.md and -adversary-1/-2/-3.md. Most informative: "Health Affairs prior authorization denial rates do not measure access unmeasured deterrence" (own field, own words → KFF/Fierce 12–18% denial figures; no paper poses the denominator question); "queue abandonment balking performance measure conditional on arrivals censored demand unobserved lost customers" (queueing → arXiv:2311.16884 et al.; method mature, never transplanted to a regulatory metric); "Brot-Goldberg Burn Layton Vabson Rationing Medicine Through Bureaucracy" (ordeal economics → NBER w30878, the closest prior, missed by Gate 2); "'sentinel effect' utilization review preadmission certification denial rate understates deterrence" (historical UR → Kahan et al. BJCP 2006, ISPOR, RSNA 2009 RBM gatekeeper-effect abstracts); "discouraged borrowers denial rate bias lender ranking HMDA applications never submitted" (fair lending → Boston Fed 1992 etc., same structure, no transplant); "allowance rate stringency not comparable across offices because application rate responds to deterrence" (disability econometrics → same shape, unconnected field); "kff.org prior authorization metrics new insights insurer practices gaps remain" (located the record's demotion condition). Published quantities measuring other objects: 12%–18% market-average denial (KFF via trade; insurer-level ranges are MA 5%–17%, ACA 3%–25%); 7.3% of denials appealed; 12% of Medi-Cal requests auto-denied after non-response; ~13% of oral anticancer prescriptions not received; 26.8%/28.9% utilization reduction and deterrence for Part D restricted drugs.
Novelty — nearest prior formulations (3, with sources): (1) Brot-Goldberg, Burn, Layton & Vabson, "Rationing Medicine Through Bureaucracy: Authorization Restrictions in Medicare", NBER w30878, Jan 2023 (abstract + conference PDF read to mid-Sec. 6 by adversary 3) — unit: Part D low-income beneficiary; endpoint: use of the restricted drug; comparator: random assignment to default plans that DIFFER in restriction status, restricting and non-restricting alike — "unrestricted default plans" misstated the design and is corrected here; estimand: causal effect of a PA restriction on utilization (−26.8%; deterrence 28.9%, which is the simulated share of USERS deterred (0.12 users per capita) and sits on a different unit from the 26.8% utilisation effect rather than being a component of it; 46.2% substitute, 53.8% no drug). (2) Long, Fuglesten Biniek, Lo, Wallace, Raphael, Kim & Pestaina, "Prior Authorization Metrics Provide New Insights into Insurer Practices, but Gaps Remain", KFF issue brief, 13 Aug 2026 (full page read by adversaries 1 and 2; wire copy by adversary 3) — unit: insurer × market; endpoint: published approval/denial shares; comparator: other insurers; estimand: descriptive, drivers explicitly unidentified. (3) Kahan, Chinitz, Waitman & Kahan, "When gatekeepers meet the sentinel", Br J Clin Pharmacol 2006;61(3):341–344, DOI 10.1111/j.1365-2125.2006.02577.x (ABSTRACT LEVEL ONLY; Wiley full text COULD NOT READ, CLIENT_ERROR) — unit: antibiotic prescription in one MCO; endpoint: cefuroxime use (8.0%→1.2% of eligible prescriptions) with an 8.5% rejection rate; estimand: pre/post utilization change attributed, hedged, to a sentinel effect. Record's own P1–P3 (KFF quick-take Apr 2026; Forvis Mazars Aug 2026; Becker's "Payers ranked by prior authorization denial rates") stand in the record file; the volume↔denial inverse relation the record attributed to the Aug 2026 analysis belongs to an earlier KFF Medicare Advantage analysis — STRICKEN as a second-hand error.
Novelty — how this differs from each: (1) Answers the framing limb, and for drugs — which CMS-0057-F excludes, verified post-batch as an express carve-out repeated three times and appearing inside the reporting paragraph itself, "excluding data on drugs as defined in Sec. 422.119(b)(1)(v)," — in a regime where the authors state they have "no data on the steps in the bureaucratic process" and "nor can we compute rejection rates" — carried with the sentence that follows it, because the authors calibrate rejection rates anyway from outside literature (1.5% to 15%, plus 0%), so the fragment quoted bare implies the paper has no rejection-rate numbers when it has calibrated ones; and with a third limitation statement the entry omitted, "The number of requests is also unobserved.", which is the most direct support for the gap this entry claims, and never compare plans by approval or denial rate. The candidate's limb 2 (a provider-side pre-submission rate paired cell-by-cell with the published metric) is the gap w30878 names and cannot fill. (2) Enumerates the metric's gaps exhaustively in payer-file-visible terms and names none on the provider side; care never requested, non-submission, deterrence, chilling and sentinel effects are absent on three independent reads, so the record's declared demotion condition did NOT fire. Its only non-payer input is a patient-reported poll figure, not a measured provider-side rate. (3) Denominator is eligible prescriptions dispensed, not PA-requiring decisions; computes no fraction never submitted; one plan, so nothing published to invert; mechanism hedged and untested.
Novelty confidence: Medium (with a close neighbour — Brot-Goldberg et al. w30878, which Gate 2 missed; the framing limb and limb 1 are occupied for drugs, the cross-payer pairing estimand is not). Not Low: no source opened by Gate 2 or by three adversaries across 24 new-vocabulary Disguise queries measures provider-side attrition or states the candidate's estimand.
Significance — consequence: If attrition is substantial and negatively associated with the printed rate, the metric is partly a gauge of submission friction and a published payer ranking is partly inverted; if small and uncorrelated, the metric survives its sharpest available criticism on the record while the trade press is already ranking payers on it. Either way, what a reader may conclude from an annually published number changes.
Significance — audience: Demonstrated, not assumed: a seven-author KFF issue brief on exactly these files (13 Aug 2026) that says it is "not possible to identify what is driving the differences"; a Becker's cross-payer ranking; same-week trade and advocacy pickup; a Senate HSGAC letter to Humana (14 Jul 2026); a live 2026 CMS proposed rule that "would standardize the denominators". Discounted: the stated lever is misdescribed — payers cannot count requests they never received, and the rulemaking standardises which determinations count, not non-submission, so a provider-side metric would need a different vehicle.
Significance — fecundity: Whether submission friction responds to publication (CY2025 is a clean pre-publication baseline for a Goodhart test); whether the auto-denial-on-non-response category should be reclassified and how much of the reported denial range it is; whether the appeal-side analogue (7.3% appealed) has the same structure; whether an exposure denominator can be built from gold-carding rosters plus requirement lists; whether unobserved-balking estimators transfer to a regulatory metric at all.
Significance — anchoring: The administrative-burden/ordeal claim that denials are produced by burden rather than eligibility (NBER w31239, still unread by anyone in this record; w30878, read); inference under unobserved balking and silent abandonment; the sentinel/gatekeeper-effect literature in drugs and imaging; measured abandonment in pharmacy and oncology (levels, never the metric's invariance); and this ledger's "a CMS measure may not measure what it is read as measuring" family (UQ-20261017-18, now a fifth member — family-level redundancy flag to the curator).
Reason for silence: Measurement-boundary split on an eight-month-old national instrument, in the narrowed form that survived attack. The metric is specified, computed and published entirely from payer holdings; the complementary term exists only in provider EHR/ePA logs, which are only now accumulating under FHIR-based ePA. The analyst community working from payer files reached for exactly the confounds those files show (gold carding, case mix, service mix, counts, format), which is the pattern the mechanism predicts. STRICKEN: the record's claim that the provider side "has no standing to ask" and that neither side owns both terms — health economists asked the deterrence question from outside and estimated it (w30878), provider-organisation UR request data have been studied academically (Kapur, Gresenz & Studdert 2003, ~half a million requests, ABSTRACT ONLY), and ePA intermediaries and integrated payer-providers hold both terms. Why that one party never published remains unexplained.
Adversarial log (8 rows: attack | objection | response | status): Three adversaries, independent fresh contexts, each handed the Gate 0–3 record only; logs verbatim in -adversary-1.md, -adversary-2.md, -adversary-3.md. Status below is the worst across the three.
| 1 Triviality | The framing limb is already answered in the candidate's own field: w30878 finds −26.8% utilization and writes that such effects "refute claims that high prior authorization approval rates mean that prior authorization has little significance for actual utilization"; P5's substitution split is already executed for drugs (46.2%/53.8%). | The asked quantities are not derivable: w30878 covers Part D drugs, which the metric excludes, has no data on the bureaucratic steps and cannot compute rejection rates; KFF can supply no fraction because insurers report percentages only; limb 2 cannot be written down from what exists. | Partial (A1/A2 Resolved, A3 Partial) |
| 2 Disguise | A known question renamed three or four times: sentinel/gatekeeper effect (UR, drugs and imaging), ordeal/hassle cost (w30878), discouraged borrowers (HMDA), allowance-rate stringency (disability insurance). | Proven for the framing limb and limb 1; fails on the cross-payer pairing estimand, which no source under 24 new-vocabulary queries states — the one causal paper that could have says it cannot compute rejection rates and does not compare plans by approval rate. Kahan et al. full text COULD NOT READ (Wiley CLIENT_ERROR), and adversary 2 ran 7 of its 8 required queries, so the sweep is run-but-incomplete, not unverified. | Partial (all three) |
| 3 Combinatorial novelty | Queueing's unobserved balking × a CMS metric; ordeal economics × PA; nothing at the seam, and the queueing bridge is decorative. | A seam-specific defect is evidenced first-hand: the same metric carries two oppositely signed unobserved channels (pre-submission attrition down; auto-denial after non-response, 12% of one real payer's requests, up), the field's own denominators are merely "suggested" pending a proposed rule, and the causal literature names the exact gap. The transplanted object is a published metric's bias, which the queueing estimand (arrival-rate parameters) is not. | Resolved (all three) |

| 5 Vagueness | "Obstruction ranking" has four admitted meanings and is not pre-declared, so the flip-share limb has no object; the true sentinel effect (never ordering at all) leaves no trace in provider logs, so the lower bound is of unknown tightness; a positive sign has no stated interpretation. | Estimator, flip threshold, matching rule, three denominators and sensitivity arms are pre-declarable and the lower-bound status is stated; the sign test is determinate once the component set is fixed. Concession is not repair — the record defers the definition to the design. | Partial (all three) |

Scores: Well-posedness 2/3 · Significance 2/3
Strongest remaining objection: As protocolled, no outcome of the sign test is diagnostic — a negative association is already observed in the field and already attributed to gold-carding exposure, the stringency model predicts a positive one, and the two attrition channels (pre-submission, which lowers the printed rate; auto-denial after non-response, which raises it) are oppositely signed; compounded by a left-hand variable that is not one quantity in year 1 (percentages only, no counts, denominators not defined in the regulatory text at all, which is stronger than the entry's original "merely suggested": 42 CFR 422.122 as codified carries no numerator or denominator definition, no counting unit, no treatment of partial approvals or withdrawn requests and no published volume, so a published percentage cannot be converted back to a count, and whether CMS suggested denominators in the preamble is UNCHECKED because the Federal Register page truncates inside preamble section II.B), so denominator heterogeneity is confounded with the very submission-side friction the design wants to detect and the cell-level flip threshold has no sampling interpretation.
Promotion requires: pre-declaring all three sign outcomes with an explicit stringency-vs-friction decomposition and a gold-carding exposure control so some outcome is diagnostic; fixing "obstruction" among its four meanings and either resolving or dropping the cross-service limb, to reach well-posedness 3/3; and completing Gate 2 — cite w30878 and read Secs. 6–7, open Kahan et al. 2006 in full by a non-Wiley route, open the services-side RBM/sentinel sources (ACR, Radiology Business, RSNA 2009 abstract 8003072) and NBER w31239, and confirm none pairs deterrence with cross-payer published denial rates.
Suggested first step toward an answer (pointer only — do not take it): Read Brot-Goldberg et al. w30878 Secs. 6–7 and the services-side RBM sentinel-effect sources before any data work; then, on one provider organisation's ePA transaction log for a single payer-market pair in CY2025, count transactions begun and never transmitted against orders matched to that payer's published requirement list, and report it as a lower bound alongside that payer's printed denial rate and its auto-denied-after-extension share.
Routing (if rejected as already-asked): None — not rejected; the framing limb is asked and partly answered (a novelty reduction, not an open problem), and the candidate's estimand is unasked.

## Verification of the instrument and the close neighbour at first hand (post-batch, 2026-10-21)

Two fresh-context readers, each handed one claim and its source and neither handed any reviewer's reasoning. The verdict does not move: Provisional, with Validated barred by well-posedness 2/3 and by Medium novelty with a close neighbour. The deciding regulatory claim holds and comes back stronger; several framings around it need correcting.

**The drug carve-out holds, and it is the load-bearing fact.** It is express, repeated three times, and sits inside the reporting paragraph itself as "excluding data on drugs as defined in Sec. 422.119(b)(1)(v),". So the published metrics genuinely cannot see drugs, which is what keeps Brot-Goldberg et al. from occupying this candidate's limb even though it answers the framing question for drugs. One open edge: that cross-reference supplies the definition of "drugs" for all three exclusions and was not read, and the words "pharmacy benefit", "medical benefit" and "pharmacy" are all absent from 422.122, so whether the carve-out tracks the pharmacy/medical benefit split is OPEN and is the single highest-value unread string in this check.

**Two corrections to what the rule requires.** There is NO appeal rate and NO appeal-overturn rate in it: paragraph (c)(4) is "The percentage of standard prior authorization requests that were approved after appeal", which runs against standard requests rather than against appeals or denials, so calling it an overturn rate silently swaps the denominator, and it drops expedited requests entirely. And the metrics are published as percentages aggregated to the MA contract across all items and services, with no volume denominator, which is a sharper version of the entry's own objection and is corrected into it above. Taken with a timeliness clock that starts "between the submission of a request", the published metrics are structurally blind to abandoned requests, to care never requested, to per-service denial patterns, and to everything about drugs — which is the cleanest statement of why this candidate's gap sits where it does.

**Read-level limits on the regulatory check, stated so they are not mistaken for findings.** The rule's own amendatory text is COULD NOT READ: the Federal Register document page yields only 143,134 extractable characters and ends mid-sentence inside preamble section II.B, while the published rule runs 89 FR 8758-8988. The operative requirements above come from the CURRENT codified text at eCFR 42 CFR 422.122, not from the as-published text, which is a routing deviation forced by that truncation. The CMS display copy is the PRE-PUBLICATION version and its dates are placeholders, so no date should be cited from it. The first data year CY2025 is derived from two clauses rather than confirmed against CMS's compliance-date table, which is in the unread preamble. Only one of the rule's parallel payer sections was read; 42 CFR 457.732 and 45 CFR 156.223 are both titled "Prior authorization requirements." and were not opened, so identical wording across payer types is an expectation and not a finding. And the decision timeframes that the auto-denial limb turns on, 42 CFR 422.568(b)(1) and 422.572(a)(1), were not read, so what happens on payer non-response is unresolved and must not be filled in from memory.

**The close neighbour's gap is absent in a strong form, and the entry must not credit the paper with noticing it.** Brot-Goldberg et al. have no request-level data at all, so neither provider-side pre-submission abandonment nor plan-level approval and denial rates could be measured even in principle from their design: plans are compared only on how often they restrict a drug, which is the treatment variable, and the outcome is always a realised fill in claims rather than the fate of a request. That is why this candidate's limb sits outside it. But the paper's section 5 limitation sentences are declarations of its own data's limits for a paperwork-cost calculation, framed from the payer and claims side, not a flag that provider-side attrition is unmeasured — a source noting the absence of a different thing is not a flag of this gap, and the entry is corrected not to claim otherwise. One overstatement also trimmed: the paper does carry medical utilisation as an outcome in its health analysis, so the exact claim is that prior authorization ON medical services or procedures is never studied, not that medical services are absent. Figures recorded second-hand: the table locators in this block come from the paper's own cross-references rather than from tables the reader saw, no uncertainty could be attached to the 26.8%, and no published version was found, though the authors circulate a full PDF that the reader's fetch cap kept it from opening.
